avertissement: Traductions automatiques des résumés français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

puces: The City appoints Pierre Rivard as a commissioner at the Bureau de l'ombudsman, replacing Jacques Ouellet, who resigned.
His term ends on October 1, 2028, the same end date as the other commissioners appointed on October 1, 2025.
He stays in the position until he is replaced or appointed again.
The City adds a rule: when a commissioner's position becomes vacant, the replacement finishes the term already under way rather than starting a new one.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City is appointing Myriam Pellerin as clerk and interim director of the Service du greffe et des archives.
The appointment applies retroactively to August 24, 2026.
Her salary is set at $165,578, according to the senior management salary scale (DS2).
She keeps her current conditions for group insurance, the pension plan and job security.
Until now, she held the position of director of the Division du secrétariat aux instances décisionnelles et à l'accès à l'information.
The funds are already provided for in the budget of the Service du greffe et des archives.
The City is creating a temporary project director position in the Service des finances.
Ginette Lachance is assigned to it until June 30, 2027 at the latest, while keeping her title of assistant treasurer.
Her salary stays at its current level, which is $169,183.
She will lead all the steps leading to the adoption and rollout of the 2027 budget, which is already under way.
She will then have to propose improvements to the budget process and to the preparation of the Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
The necessary funds, including employee benefits, are already provided for in the Service des finances budget.
The Ville de Québec will pay $2,822,917 to QMI Spectacles inc. to cover part of the Centre Vidéotron's 2025 operating deficit.
This payment comes from the lease signed in 2011, which requires the City to cover 50% of the operating deficit, without exceeding the base rent paid by the company.
In 2025, the City collected $2,822,917 in rent, $946,445 in royalties on tickets, and $992,493 in recoverable revenue, mostly related to parking.
The amount of the contribution was confirmed by the audit of QMI Spectacles inc.'s financial statements carried out by Mallette S.E.N.C.R.L.
Representatives of the Service des finances reviewed the company's records on December 16, 2025 and July 28, 2026, under a confidentiality agreement.
The amount is recorded in the City's 2025 financial results and falls under urban agglomeration jurisdiction.
The decision must be made by the urban agglomeration council of Québec, with a target date of September 16, 2026.
The City is adopting a by-law authorizing it to borrow $20,000,000 to buy buildings and land for municipal purposes.
The money will be used to buy back industrial land, since the city's reserve has shrunk considerably, and to acquire strategic land to redevelop certain areas.
The acquisitions can be made by mutual agreement or by expropriation, anywhere on the city's territory.
The budget also covers professional services (studies, land surveying, environment, appraisal, negotiation) and demolition, clearing and decontamination work.
The term of the loan is 5 years and the funds are planned for the years 2027 to 2030 of the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The City is drawing $3,000,000 from its general fund, which is 15% of the expense; this amount will be repaid to the fund when the by-law comes into force.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 4369, rue Jordi-Bonet, in the Des Châtels neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The attached garage of this single-family home is 5.28 metres from the street, while the planning by-law requires 6. The decision makes it compliant.
The request serves to regularize the garage, built in 2021 with a permit.
According to the analysis, the permit had been issued by applying rules meant for a protected non-conforming building, since the 1996 house is today located in a non-conforming way.
The analysis notes that the garage is more than 10 metres from the neighbour on the left and that it is built in a steep-slope area.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on May 27, 2026.
The City of Québec is giving $994,298.09 to the Coopérative d'habitation Les Jardins d'Alchémilles to build a 28-unit social and affordable housing building.
The five-storey building will be located at 545, rue Kirouac, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough.
The housing units are intended for families, single people and self-sufficient seniors.
This grant is in addition to the $900,000 already paid in 2025 to buy the land, for a total municipal contribution of $1,894,298.09.
The payment is made in two parts: $497,149.05 in 2026, taken from the agglomeration operating surplus set aside for social housing, and $497,149.04 in 2027, funded by a loan by-law.
The funding is part of the Programme d'habitation abordable Québec, which requires the City to provide at least 40% of the basic grant from the Société d'habitation du Québec.
City council adopts the Vision Ville-Port 2026-2035, a collaboration agreement between the Ville de Québec and the Port de Québec for the next ten years.
The speed of heavy vehicles will be reduced in the Vieux-Port area.
The City and the Port will share their mobility data and hold consultation activities on port and maritime issues.
The North American representation of the Association internationale Villes et Ports will be based in Québec.
The governance of citizen spaces will be reviewed, with regular public follow-up on the implementation of the Vision.
The two partners commit to agreeing on investments over a 10-year horizon and to developing the city-port interfaces in a way that improves access to the river.
The document does not specify any amount; the financial impacts section contains no sum.
The City is authorizing the construction of a six-storey building with 67 housing units at 2255, boulevard Henri-Bourassa, in the Maizerets neighbourhood.
Following a public consultation held on May 4, 2026, the City is adding one prohibition: the building may not be used for tourist accommodation.

The project departs from the area's planning rules: height of up to 20 metres instead of 13, up to 70 housing units instead of 40, fewer large units than the required percentage, and a wider access lane.
The developer must deliver at least 65 housing units, keep 90% of the parking indoors, provide 72 bicycle spaces and plant at least eight trees in the back yard.
The ground-floor units on the Henri-Bourassa side must have direct access to the outside; a 100-square-metre terrace is required on the fifth floor.
Work must begin within 12 months of the adoption of the resolution, otherwise the authorization lapses.
Breaching the conditions carries a fine of $1,000 for an individual and $2,000 in other cases, doubled for a repeat offence.
The City completed five projects to make intersections near schools safer in 2024 and 2025, at a total cost of $754,468.
The ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable granted $537,784 in financial assistance for this work; $359,887 has already been paid.
The urban agglomeration council takes note of the work and expense reports needed to obtain the second and final payment of the grant.
Work completed: curb extensions at rue de Rigauville and rue Saint-Ambroise ($94,737.93), near école Sacré-Coeur.
Raised intersections: avenue du Bourg-Royal and carré de Tracy Est and Ouest ($182,372.34), rue Jean-Brillant and rue Julien-Green ($159,979).
Also raised intersections: rue de la Galaxie and rue de l'Apogée ($124,268.98) and rue Alexander and rue Triquet ($193,109.90).
The document indicates no financial impact for the City.

The executive committee takes note of the quarterly report on transactions of the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale (Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2026), for October 1 to December 31, 2025.

The Fonds Vision 2018-2025 paid out, among others, $288,000 to Créneau Aliments Santé, $150,000 to Nutra-Fruit, $150,000 to Technologies LiveSnap, $150,000 to Zilia and $140,000 to Technologie Hoola One.

Commercial development corporations received help for neighbourhood projects: $80,000 in Vieux-Québec (winter decorations), $25,000 in Petit Champlain, $25,000 in Vieux-Port, $23,219 in Saint-Sauveur, $15,240 in Faubourg Saint-Jean and $13,108 in Montcalm.
Québec stores and businesses were also supported, including $66,716 to Décembre inc. (urban farm) and $27,725 to Saudade studio floral for premises in Saint-Roch.
Unused balances from earlier projects were returned to the fund, totalling $1,546,205.59, including $500,000 tied to the Centre d'affaires Yarihwa' and $473,274 tied to Québec Capitale Climat.
The balance of the Fonds Vision 2018-2025 stood at $1,029,652.22 as at December 31, 2025; that of the Fonds Vision 2025-2030 was $8,698,231 as at September 30, 2025.
The City wants to obtain a permanent public utility servitude on a piece of land alongside 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The servitude covers about 4.30 square metres of part of lot 1 941 030.
It will be used to move conduits and public utility networks needed for the project.
The City will try to reach an amicable agreement with the owners; otherwise, it will proceed by expropriation.
The owners have been informed of the process, the next steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
If the project no longer needs this servitude, the City may abandon the expropriation proceedings, in whole or in part.
The entire property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $249,000, or $393.18 per square metre; the funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342.
The City is adopting a new code of ethics and professional conduct for municipal elected officials, By-law R.V.Q. 3520, which replaces, without any changes, the one adopted on February 21, 2022.
Quebec law requires every municipality to review its code of ethics before May 1 following a general election.

The code prohibits elected officials from having conflicts of interest, showing favouritism, making disrespectful remarks about other elected officials, employees and citizens, and using the City's resources for personal purposes.
An elected official must declare to the city clerk, within 30 days, any gift or hospitality worth more than $200; these declarations are entered in a public register.
For the 12 months following the end of their term, a former elected official cannot hold a position that would give them an undue advantage because of their past duties.
In the event of a breach, the Commission municipale du Québec can impose a reprimand, training, a reimbursement, a penalty of up to $4,000 or a suspension of no more than 90 days.
An elected official may consult an ethics advisor at the City's expense, as a preventive measure and if the fees are reasonable.
The City is entrusting the Canadien National with the reconstruction of the north portion of the 4e Avenue railway overpass, in the La Cité-Limoilou arrondissement.
The CN informed the City that this portion of the bridge has reached the end of its useful life; the work is to begin as of summer 2026.
The cost of the work is estimated at $25,656,000 (plus GST and QST), and the net expense for the City is estimated at $26,935,593.
The City is paying the bill: an order from the Office des transports du Canada places the maintenance and repair of the bridge at its expense.
The City will be billed according to the costs actually incurred, and the CN will reimburse it for any unused amounts.
The CN will choose the contractor through a call for tenders by invitation; the City must obtain the authorizations and make the necessary acquisitions, at its own expense.
The south bridge, built in 1984, stays in place.
The Ville de Québec will sign a three-year agreement with the organization Communautés Solidaires for its Entraid'aînés program, in the Beauport borough.
The financial support will decrease each year: $6,152 in 2026, $4,060 in 2027 and $2,030 in 2028, for a total of $12,242.
The program offers seniors in Beauport recreational activities, transportation, referrals, accompaniment and home visits.

The City states that this will be the last agreement signed for this program, in particular to ensure fairness between organizations and because the share of Beauport seniors who benefit from it fell from 52% in 2022 to 40% in 2025.
The decreasing support is meant to give the organization time to prepare for the end of the funding; the organization says it agrees.
The organization will have to report each year and mention the City's contribution in its official publications.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of the municipal budgets.
The Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is transferring $10,000 from its operating budget to the Service des relations citoyennes et des communications.
The money will be used to create the Commission consultative pour la mobilité du Vieux-Québec.
This commission aims to improve mobility and quality of life in Vieux-Québec.
The document states that this transfer will have no effect on the borough's activities.
The borough council adopted the decision (resolution CA1-2026-0033) on February 23, 2026.
The City is awarding Les Excavations Lafontaine inc. (Lévis) the contract to build the 8e Avenue bike path, between 1re and 11e Rue, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The contract is worth $6,165,139.50 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $6,472,625.83.

The work includes redeveloping the streets, building sidewalks, replacing pipes, catch basins, manholes, fire hydrants, water valves and service connections, as well as bringing some traffic lights up to standard.
The City is choosing scenario B, which replaces the concrete elements with granite, rather than scenario A ($5,776,996.80), citing greater durability in the face of snow-removal machinery.
Four companies submitted bids; Lafontaine offered the lowest price, 24.1% below the department's estimate ($8,123,684.88).
The funding comes from two loan by-laws: $5,218,346.16 for bike and pedestrian paths, and $1,254,279.67 for local projects.
The contract includes clauses to adjust for asphalt and fuel prices.

The City is sending a division director from the Service du développement économique et des grands projets on an economic mission to Paris, from June 6 to 13, 2026 (or on other dates set by the organizers).
The expense is estimated at $6,500, plus taxes, reimbursed upon presentation of supporting documents: air and ground transportation, accommodation and meals.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets.
The mission is organized by the association Palme Québec, of which the City has been a member since August 2025, and which works on the sustainable development of industrial parks.
On June 10 and 11, the representative will take part in the work of the Association internationale des territoires d'activités durables (AITAD).
On June 10, she will take part in a round table on reducing the climate impact of mobility in sustainable activity areas.
A difference of no more than 10% of the authorized amount will be accepted without further authorization.
The City is maintaining its refusal to demolish the heritage house at 2330, avenue Notre-Dame (maison Drolet-Belleau).
The owner had asked the city council to review the refusal issued on March 26, 2026 by the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation.
The applicant wanted to demolish the house in order to subdivide the lot and build two semi-detached two-family buildings, for a total of four housing units.
The City finds that the building has good heritage value and higher historical value, and that it is part of a group of some forty neoclassical houses in the area.
According to the City, the building is neither beyond saving nor dangerous, and restoring it remains possible; some of the work could be subsidized.
The applicant estimates the renovation work at $119,025; the City considers this cost acceptable compared with demolition and reconstruction.
The house is vacant but heated, and contains one housing unit that is currently unoccupied. No written comments were received from the public.
The City is authorizing a $900,000 expense to redevelop rue de la Faune, funded by a loan repayable over 15 years.
The work covers rue de la Faune between rue Saint-Julien and about 450 metres east of rue Marigot, roughly 2,000 metres, in the Charlesbourg and La Haute-Saint-Charles boroughs.
The redevelopment includes adding two vehicle lanes and a shared bike-and-pedestrian path.
The City will also add a water main network, domestic and storm sewers, and a stormwater management system.
The City may acquire buildings and easements by mutual agreement or by expropriation in order to carry out the work.
The funds are planned for 2026 to 2028; rue de la Faune would be the first "boulevard 2.0" in the Couronne Nord mobility plan.
The City is drawing $90,000 from the general fund, which is 10% of the expense, an amount that will be reimbursed when the by-law comes into force.
The City is paying $375,000 to Créations Hit The Floor, or $125,000 per year, to hold the "Hit The Floor Québec" event in 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The event will take place at the Centre de foires d'ExpoCité from May 14 to 18, 2026, from May 20 to 24, 2027, and from May 18 to 22, 2028.
It is a dance competition with more than 2,000 choreographies; there is an admission fee, except for children under 5.
Free activities are offered to the public: Championnat Breaking Québec, dance battles, talks, morning clinics, a rebroadcast zone and outdoor dance workshops.
The grant represents about 3% of the event's budget, which goes from $3,914,198 in 2026 to $4,253,337 in 2028.
The funding is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners and on approval of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.
In 2025, the City had granted $100,000 to this event.
The City approves the exterior appearance plans for the expansion of a building at 2496, 4e Avenue, in the Lairet neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The project involves changing the exterior cladding to add a third storey; the existing red brick is kept.
The owner will have to change the proposed colour: the cladding of the new storey must be masonry or lightweight cladding in a colour similar to the brick of the first two storeys.

Reason given: the requested grey colour (grey fibre cement) does not exist anywhere else in the neighbourhood as cladding for a storey, and the rear brick expansion that justified this choice in 2023 is no longer being built.
If the owner does not meet this condition, the application is put on hold and the owner will have to submit a new project at a later meeting.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion with this condition on January 27, 2026; the borough council adopted the resolution on February 23, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 955, Grande Allée Ouest, in the Montcalm neighbourhood (La Cité-Limoilou borough).
The space separating the two street accesses may measure 0.2 metres instead of the 7.5 metres required by the planning by-law.
The two accesses in question are the one for the parking lot and the one for the waste containers.
The exemption is part of a project to expand an existing building, which will allow for the construction of 145 housing units.

According to the analysis, the building's heritage character, the protection of the tree cover and the desire to limit the impact on the neighbouring buildings south of avenue Mérici restrict where the accesses can be located.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour; the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec, the Division de la foresterie urbaine and the Service du transport also gave a favourable opinion.
The Arrondissement de Charlesbourg is giving $4,000 to the organization "Loisirs du Trait-Carré" for its activities during Spring Break 2026.
The activities took place from February 28 to March 8, 2026, rain or shine.
On the program: a sports discovery zone and treasure hunts at parc Guillaume-Mathieu, a fair at parc Maria-Goretti, and Vélo Ballado Polaire at parc Maurice-Dorion.
The grant has gone up year after year: $2,012 in 2024, $3,000 in 2025, $4,000 in 2026.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement de Charlesbourg, under the event support component.
City departments, including police and fire protection, said they were in favour of the activities.
The City is authorizing the conversion of the former office building at 1075, chemin Sainte-Foy (Saint-Sacrement neighbourhood) into a residential building, with an extension.
The project provides for 222 social housing units: 148 in the existing 15-storey building and 74 in the extension.

Three exemptions are granted: a height of 54 m for the existing building and 45 m for the extension (instead of 16 m), two parking spaces for people with disabilities in front of the façade on the avenue Joffre side, and underground parking 0 m from the lot line on the chemin Sainte-Foy side.
Conditions imposed: at least 200 social housing units maintained, of which 45% have two or more bedrooms and 15% have three or more bedrooms.

Other conditions: a pale reflective roof, at least 25% glazing on the ground floor on the chemin Sainte-Foy side, and specific exterior cladding requirements (monochrome concrete for the existing building, 70% reddish or paler brick for the extension).
A fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases) applies if the conditions are not met, doubled in the event of a repeat offence.
The process includes a public consultation meeting and three days to submit written comments; the project is not subject to approval by referendum.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 9105, rue Courtois, in the Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf neighbourhood (Arrondissement des Rivières).
The front setback of the detached single-family home is recognized as compliant at 4.5 metres, instead of the 6-metre minimum required by the planning by-law.
The owner wants to expand the house in line with the existing wall, on a corner lot that has two front setbacks.
The planned addition measures about 10 feet by 12 feet and does not increase the encroachment into the setback.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 2, 2026; the 7.5-metre rear setback remains compliant.
According to the analysis, the house was built around 1990, its non-compliant siting is protected, and no complaints have been received from neighbours.
The City is entrusting the Corporation des Loisirs de Vanier with supervising aquatic activities at the indoor pool of the complexe Jean-Paul-Nolin.
The organization will also handle the supervision and specialized maintenance of the outdoor pool Yvette-Cloutier, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The agreement covers 24 months, from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027.
The contract is worth $333,183.41 (plus GST and QST); the net cost to the City is $349,800.94.
The amounts planned for 2027 depend on the approval of that year's budget.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders, as the law allows this with a non-profit organization.
The urban agglomeration council approves $21,256,604 in budget transfers between operating expense items, made from January 1 to April 30, 2026.
These transfers move money that was already budgeted from one department to another; they do not add any new spending.
No additional funds were added on the investment side during this period.
The council takes note of $16,284,049 in transfers between urban agglomeration and local (proximity) responsibilities, in favour of local responsibilities.
The Loisirs, sports et vie communautaire department is by far the most affected by the multi-department transfers ($8,729,545 transferred to it, $5,052,171 coming from it).
The arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou receives $2,627,111 in multi-department transfers.
The City is giving up to $48,750 to the organization Le Diplôme avant la médaille (DAM) for the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
The money is used to support activities that promote the inclusion and participation of young immigrants, using sport as a tool against dropping out of school.

DAM already works in five high schools: Vanier, La Camaradière, Roger-Comtois, Polyvalente de Charlesbourg and Pointe-Lévy, reaching about 900 young people a year, 38% of whom are from immigrant backgrounds.
The grant will make it possible to add a sixth school and reach more than 1,000 young people.

New activities planned: intercultural discussion groups, a project designed by and for young people, and "zone découverte culturelle" (cultural discovery zone) booths at six tournaments in the spring.
The organization will have to report on its activities once a year and mention the contribution of the City and the MIFI in its publications.
The funding covers only one year so that the next three-year agreement will line up with the future agreement with the MIFI in 2027.
The City is appointing four people to represent it on the retirement committee of the Régime de retraite des fonctionnaires de la Ville de Québec.
They are Marie-Josée Drouin and Dominic Stephenson (human resources), France Bilodeau (consultant) and Andrée-Anne Verreault (finance).
Their term runs from February 25, 2026 to February 23, 2029, because the term of the current trustees ends on February 25, 2026.
The City also confirms that Marie-Josée Drouin is replacing Véronique Caron, who has left the Service des ressources humaines, from November 10, 2025 to February 25, 2026.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City is giving $16,000 to the Festival Marocain de Québec to hold an intercultural event in the summer of 2026.
The festival is in its 5th edition and will take place from September 4 to 6, 2026, at parc Roland-Beaudin.
The event features Moroccan music, dance, traditions, food and crafts.
The grant comes from an invitation-only call for projects, a pilot project to add intercultural events in Québec.
The money comes from the Fonds des grands événements et événements spéciaux of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The application form replaces the agreement: no separate contract is attached.
In 2024, the organization received $8,000 from the City for its festival.
The City is banning parking on a section of rue de l'Oasis, in the arrondissement de Beauport, from November 15 to March 31.
The ban applies to the west side of the street, on the outside of the curve in front of 208, rue de l'Oasis.
The affected zone starts 50 metres south of chemin des Eaux-Vives and extends 35 metres to the south.
Three parking spaces are removed during this winter period.
The measure is meant to let snow removal equipment through, which parked vehicles were blocking.
According to the document, the occupancy rate of parking spaces in the area is low.
The City is giving $4,000 to the Tournoi international de basketball de la vieille capitale for the 2026 edition of the event.
The tournament takes place from June 25 to 28, 2026, at the PEPS of Université Laval.
The event welcomes close to 600 young people aged 12 to 15, including six international teams; a Ninja course is added on the Friday and Saturday.
The grant goes from $3,000 in 2024 and 2025 to $4,000 this year, which is 3.5% of the planned budget of $114,800.
The help is conditional on enough funding from the other partners, and the money will be paid in a single payment within 10 days of the signing.
The organization must display the City's logo, take out $5,000,000 in liability insurance and hand in a report with financial statements by the end of September 2026.
Admission is paid, except for children under 5; thousands of tickets are offered to elementary and high school students in the city.
The City is awarding La Compagnie de Parterres Portugais ltée the contract to build sidewalks, curbs and curb extensions for $1,375,590.88 (plus GST and QST).
The work affects the arrondissements of Beauport and Charlesbourg: rues du Villonet and du Parc-Roy, avenues des Diamants and Marcoux, boulevards du Loiret and des Français.

Along with the sidewalks, the project includes removing the existing asphalt, reinforcing the roadway, new layers of asphalt mix, adding or replacing catch basins and manholes, as well as lighting and traffic light work.
Seven companies submitted bids; the one chosen submitted the lowest price, 14.3% below the department's estimate of $1,606,042.80.
The net cost to the City is $1,444,198.49, funded by two loan by-laws and a grant from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The contract includes a bitumen price adjustment clause.
The executive committee gives three managers the power to authorize, by order, the use of a pesticide that is normally banned, or to restrict the application of a permitted pesticide.
These powers go to the director of the Arrondissement de Charlesbourg, the director of the Division de la prévention et du contrôle environnemental, and a section director within that division.
The same people will also be able to sign orders about noise and about restrictions on the use of solid-fuel appliances (wood stoves, for example, according to the by-law concerned).
The City explains that it wants to respond to requests more quickly, in particular because the end of temporary permits for lawn treatment could increase their number.
The by-law comes into force as soon as it is adopted; the executive committee adopted it on April 15, 2026.
The City is entering into a 36-month agreement, starting July 1, 2026, for cloud computing services for the Service de police de la Ville de Québec.
Estimated cost: $2,679,526 (plus GST and QST); the net expense for the urban agglomeration is estimated at $2,756,483.43.
The services cover data processing and storage, security of hosted data, bandwidth and backup copies.

The supplier's identity remains confidential: the City is invoking a provision of the law that allows a contract to be awarded without a call for tenders for confidentiality reasons related to public safety.
The contract goes through the master agreement of the ministère de la Cybersécurité et du Numérique, without a public call for tenders.
An external partner of the Service de police is paying part of the costs; $1,136,520 is recorded under a recoverable project.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 depend on the adoption of the budgets for those years.

The City is authorizing the construction of a mixed-use building of about 80 housing units, four to six storeys high, at 1111, boulevard Pie-XI Nord, in Val-Bélair, even though residential use is not normally allowed in this zone.
Following the public consultation of May 20, 2026, the developer will have to build a pedestrian path on the property, on the rues Émond and de l'Équinoxe side.
The minimum number of parking spaces goes from 95 to 120, in response to residents' concerns about the availability of spaces.
The condition on the location of the terrace is reworded to specify where it must be set up.
The project must include at least 75 housing units, 30% of them with two or more bedrooms and at least three with three or more bedrooms; each unit must have a heat pump.
The ground floor must set aside at least 360 square metres for a store, a service business or a restaurant.
Anyone who breaks the conditions is liable to a fine of $1,000 (individuals) or $2,000 (all other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.
The conseil d'arrondissement des Rivières approves the plans for the construction of a detached residential building at 1750, rue Careau, in Duberger-Les Saules.
The building will have 274 dwelling units on 8 storeys, a height allowed by the zoning currently in force.
This is the first phase of a residential and commercial project that includes moving rue du Marais to the centre of the site.
The wooded area west of the property will be cut down to make room for the street extension and the construction; the trees that are cut will be replaced.
A vegetated screening berm will separate the project from the houses on rue des Impatientes, with no gradual change in height between the two.
The underground parking encroaches on the visual screen, which is the subject of a minor exemption request.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave its opinion on May 4, 2026; the resolution was signed on May 26, 2026.
The City wants to change the zoning at 15971, boulevard de la Colline and at 1275, rue Lepire, in the Lac-Saint-Charles neighbourhood.

The land owned by Groupe SM Tardif is currently split into two zones (61010Ib and 61011Ia); the City is proposing to bring it together into a single zone to make it easier for the business to develop.
In practical terms, zone 61011Ia is enlarged by taking in part of zone 61010Ib, on portions of lots 6 686 504 and 6 686 505.
No changes are planned to the specification grids (the applicable standards) of the zones concerned.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.

The conseil de quartier de Lac-Saint-Charles will be invited to give its opinion and to hold a public consultation meeting; interested people will then have seven days to submit their comments in writing.
City council is to make its decision on September 22, 2026.
The City is removing the parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility in front of 375, rue Bouffard, in La Cité-Limoilou (Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur district).
The space in question is on the east side of rue Bouffard, between avenue des Oblats and rue Napoléon, over 6 metres.
The Service du transport was informed that this reserved space is no longer needed.
No on-street parking space is being removed: the space goes back to being regular parking.
The request came from a citizen; the borough council adopted ordinance O-1548.
The arrondissement des Rivières is giving $200 to the Corporation Jeunesse L'Évasion L'Ormière.
The money comes from the budget of the conseil d'arrondissement des Rivières.
The Maison des jeunes l'Évasion asked for the help to celebrate its 30th anniversary.
The 30th anniversary celebration will take place on July 10, 2026, and the public is invited.
The Maison des jeunes welcomes teenagers aged 12 to 17 from the Neufchâtel area.
The Ville de Québec is authorizing an agreement with Cégep Limoilou to lend it technical documents for teaching purposes.

The documents concern the construction project for the centre de valorisation des surplus de matériaux d'excavation et de traitement des sols contaminés (CVSME), in the arrondissement de Beauport: PDF or CAD drawings, a digital model and related technical documents.
Students in the Technologie du génie civil program will use them in the Estimation et soumission course to carry out topographic surveys and quantity take-offs.
The City keeps all of its intellectual property rights; the licence is non-exclusive, non-transferable and cannot be sublicensed.
Prohibited uses: any commercial use, access by unauthorized persons, public distribution without the City's written consent, and downloading of the model by students (unless agreed to beforehand).
The agreement lasts 5 years, renewable for one-year periods with written notice 30 days before it expires; either party may end it with 30 days' notice.
No financial impact according to the document.
The City is submitting to city council the lists of its contracts of $25,000 and more for the month of December 2025, as required by the Cities and Towns Act.
In December 2025, the City awarded 141 contracts of more than $25,000, for a total value of $57,245,418 (before taxes).
Of these, 40 contracts are over $250,000 and total $49,262,781; 26 contracts are between $100,000 and $250,000 ($4,242,021) and 75 contracts are between $25,000 and $100,000 ($3,740,616).

The director general and the assistant directors general awarded 13 contracts, including sanitary maintenance in Beauport and Charlesbourg ($144,500) and the thawing of water service lines ($207,779).
The director of the Service des approvisionnements renewed 20 contracts, including the supply of hydrated lime ($2,025,257) and the cleaning and inspection of sewer systems ($1,358,037).
Since April 2024, the threshold requiring the City to put a contract out to competition has been set at $33,000; between $10,000 and $33,000, two price requests are required.
The lists also cover contracts transferred to a new supplier, terminated contracts, cancelled calls for tenders and additional expenditures that were authorized.
The Service de protection contre l'incendie de Québec is reorganizing its structure: divisions and sections are being created, renamed or abolished.
The reorganization creates no net positions, but results in a negative budget gap of $74,653.
A position of assistant director, support and advice to management is created; the Direction adjointe aux opérations becomes the Direction adjointe intervention et développement opérationnel.
The Direction adjointe affaires stratégiques et administratives is abolished and replaced by the Direction adjointe soutien organisationnel et relations avec la communauté.

New divisions are being created: operational performance and specialized operations, occupational health and safety and fire training, commissioner's office and prevention, public safety quartermaster, administrative and financial affairs, technological development and compliance, and major projects.
The Division quartier maître sécurité publique will manage, among other things, vehicles, equipment purchases and radio communications for firefighters, police and civil security.
The decision must be made by the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The City is paying $220,000 to the organization EXMURO art public to present a monumental public artwork.
The artwork "Canard de bain" by Dutch artist Florentijn Hofman will be installed on the fleuve Saint-Laurent, in the Vieux-Port de Québec area.
The inflatable sculpture, more than 30 metres high, will be on view for 2 months in the summer of 2027.
The project will unfold in three phases: construction, a river procession, and a contemplative installation.
The artwork was chosen following a call for projects issued to professional cultural organizations.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de la culture et du patrimoine.
The City is giving $22,000 to "Go le grand défi inc." to register two teams of employees in the "1 000 KM" and ten employees in "La Boucle" of the Grand défi Pierre Lavoie in 2026.
The "1 000 KM" takes place from June 11 to 14, 2026 in Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu, on the site of the Collège militaire Royal de Saint-Jean; "La Boucle" (135 km) takes place on June 13.
Each team must raise the rest of its registration cost itself; donations above that amount go to the associated elementary schools, which are still to be confirmed.
The two teams each have five employees, from services such as police, fire, culture and information technology.
The ten participants in "La Boucle" were drawn at random from among the employees who were interested.
The money comes from the City's general expenses, under the "Gérer les subventions" (Manage grants) activity.

The Administration portuaire de Québec (APQ) replaces Le Projet Ex Machina in several obligations under the agreement on the light artwork "Aurores boréales", from the signing of the amendment until September 15, 2027.
The APQ becomes solely responsible for the lighting, the maintenance of the equipment, its operation, its dismantling or disposal, and the resulting costs.
Ex Machina transfers to the APQ, free of charge, the equipment and know-how needed to keep projecting the artwork on the facilities of the port de Québec.
For 2026, the City is paying $109,149 (plus taxes): 75% to Ex Machina by January 31, 2026 at the latest and 25% to the APQ by November 30, 2027 at the latest.
Ex Machina remains the owner of the rights to the artwork and grants the APQ a licence to present and exploit it at the port de Québec until the end of the agreement.
After September 15, 2027, the APQ may keep the equipment for other lighting uses, except for the artwork itself, or dispose of it.
The APQ must hold civil liability insurance of five million dollars per event until September 15, 2027.
The City wants to obtain a permanent easement on a piece of land on boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest (Montcalm neighbourhood, La Cité-Limoilou borough), for the TramCité tramway project.
The easement covers about 3.5 square metres and will be used to move public utility conduits and networks.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement or by expropriation: the Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to begin the proceedings.
Discussions have already taken place with the owner, who received a contractual and monetary offer.
The City may withdraw from the expropriation, in whole or in part, if the project no longer needs the easement.
The land is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $1,070,000, or $490.11 per square metre.
The funds come from the loan by-law related to the structuring public transit network.

The City is giving $67,000 to the Québec Jazz en juin festival for its 2026 edition, and is providing it with free municipal services (police, communications) worth at most $5,000, for a total of $72,000.
The festival's 8th edition runs from June 25 to 28, 2026 in several neighbourhoods: rue Maguire, parc Durocher, faubourg Saint-Jean-Baptiste, Université Laval and Grand Théâtre de Québec.
More than 50 shows are planned, about thirty of them presented free of charge, along with youth workshops and yoga.
The grant covers 18.4% of the event's budget, estimated at $365,030, and remains conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners.
The money is paid in three instalments: $40,200 at the start, $20,100 after the planned activities are held, and $6,700 when the financial statements and the final report are submitted.
The organization must give its complete final report to the City no later than 90 days after the end of the festival.
In 2025, the City had granted $67,000 plus $3,000 in services; in 2024, $95,000 plus $11,000 in services.
The Ville de Québec is submitting four applications for financial assistance totalling $1,941,798 under the ministère des Transports' Véloce III program, for the year 2026-2027.
The eligible cost of the four projects is estimated at $5,546,377 (net of taxes).
Rue Borne: making a railway crossing safer and official, with cycling and pedestrian works ($470,355 in eligible expenses, up to $235,178 in assistance).
Avenue Charles-Huot and the rue Triquet intersection: second phase of the 2025 work on the bike link and the intersections ($2,565,830 in expenses, up to $451,524 in assistance).
Boulevard des Chutes: upgrading of the designated roadway, the bike lanes and the off-road path, plus a new sidewalk ($2,316,678 in expenses, up to $1,158,339 in assistance).

Intersection of boulevard Père-Lelièvre and avenue Godin: extension of the sidewalk on the north side, tactile paving slabs and traffic lights for cyclists ($193,515 in expenses, up to $96,757 in assistance).
The City undertakes to follow the program's rules, failing which the financial assistance will be terminated. The decision summary indicates no financial impact.
The City is granting a variance for 665, rue Margaret-Fraser, in the Beauport industrial park (Saint-Michel neighbourhood).
The owner will be allowed to install four heat pumps 0.7 metres from the neighbouring property line, instead of the 1 metre required by Beauport's planning by-law.
The units, each 0.9 m by 0.9 m, will be placed in the side yard of an industrial building built in 2024 that has five suites.
The applicant says installing them on the roof is impossible because of the structure, and that snow piles up in front of the main façade.
According to the City's analysis, there is no residential building nearby.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the variance on March 26, 2026; the borough council granted it.

The City is amending its agreement with Le Centre résidentiel et communautaire Jacques Cartier, which is receiving a grant of up to $75,000 to launch a mixed-use project at 421, boulevard Langelier (La Cité-Limoilou).
The expenses that can be paid with the grant will now also include an analysis of the potential to build the building out of engineered wood.
The expenses already covered remain the fees for analyzing an eco-efficient mechanical system, such as geothermal energy, and for designing adaptable housing.
The City is extending the agreement by nine more months, to give the organization time to produce its studies and technical opinions.
The agreement will end no later than 21 months after it is signed if all the obligations are not met.
The project provides for 63 housing units for young adults, a total cost of $10,900,000 and a construction start on June 1, 2026.
The City is awarding a $297,860 contract (before taxes) to 9355-5787 Québec inc. (Athom), of Trois-Rivières, to build, transport and install two single-module prefabricated buildings.
The buildings will be added to the écocentre Val-Bélair, in the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough.
One building will be used by employees and will house an emergency shower; the other will be used to greet écocentre users.
Two companies submitted bids; Athom submitted the lowest price, ahead of Gestion A. Santerre inc. ($317,975).
The bids came in under the requesting department's estimate, which was $360,000 before taxes.
The net cost to the City is $312,715.75, paid out of a loan by-law related to the écocentres.
The executive committee was to decide on March 25, 2026.
The City is awarding Les Entreprises MRA Paysagistes inc. a contract worth $2,383,116.21 (before GST and QST) for the écocentre Val-Bélair, in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The contract covers supplying and transporting containers, as well as a wheel loader with an operator, from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2030.
The company must also move the containers, load the materials, clear snow and carry out the other tasks needed to operate the écocentre.
The contract can be renewed three times for 12 months, with a yearly price increase based on the consumer price index.
Three bids were received and found to be compliant; MRA Paysagistes submitted the lowest price, 5.7% below the City's estimate.
The net expense for the urban agglomeration is $2,501,974.13, spread out from 2026 to 2030, subject to the adoption of the budgets for the years 2027 to 2030.
The City is changing the zoning of four areas in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood (arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, district du Plateau).
Detached buildings will be allowed up to three dwelling units instead of two in zones 32006Ha, 32023Ha, 32027Ha and 32040Ha.
Semi-detached buildings will be allowed up to two dwelling units instead of one in zones 32006Ha and 32027Ha.
The two-storey limit is removed in zones 32006Ha, 32027Ha and 32040Ha, but the maximum height stays at 10 or 12 metres.
The parking standards for zones 32023Ha and 32040Ha go from the "general" type to the "structuring corridor A" type.
The change stems from a request concerning 794, rue des Talus, a building that has only one dwelling unit.

The conseil de quartier de la Cité-Universitaire will hold a public consultation meeting; interested people will have seven days after it to submit their comments in writing. The by-law may be subject to approval by referendum.

The City authorizes the company Les Constructions T Ouellet inc. to add water and sewer lines and to upgrade about 105 metres of rue Décarie, between rue des Dauphinelles and avenue de la Montagne Ouest, in Val-Bélair.
The work will allow six housing units to be built: 1 detached single-family home, 1 detached two-family home and 4 semi-detached single-family homes.
Two existing neighbouring homes will be connected to the new water and sewer systems.
The developer pays for everything: about $350,000 in municipal infrastructure, for a total investment of about $3M. The City pays nothing.
The developer will pay into the City's parks fund an amount equal to 10% of the value of the land.
Once the work is accepted, the developer will hand over the infrastructure to the City free of charge.
According to the tax impact analysis, the project would bring in about $3,497 in net revenue per year once all the buildings are built.
The City is buying its motor fuels and heating fuels from two suppliers, from the date the contract is awarded until March 31, 2029.
Les Huiles Desroches inc. will supply clear diesel and gasoline (regular and super), for an estimated amount of $33,277,950 before taxes.
Harnois Énergies inc. will supply light fuel oil (heating oil and coloured diesel), for an estimated amount of $1,144,095 before taxes.
The prices billed will follow, each day, the average of the rack prices of Énergie Valero and Suncor for the Québec region, minus the discounts offered.
The net expense is estimated at $36,138,844.49, paid out of the operating budget of the departments and boroughs.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
Three companies submitted bids; SG Énergie was found non-compliant because it refused to extend the validity of its bid to 90 days.
The City is granting a minor exemption for a planned mixed-use building of 7 to 17 storeys at 220 to 280, rue De Saint-Vallier Est, in the Saint-Roch neighbourhood.
The developer will not have to hide its loading and unloading area behind a screen.
The building's access from rue Sainte-Hélène may be up to 29 metres wide, instead of the maximum of 10 metres set out in the planning by-law.

According to the analysis on file, rue Sainte-Hélène is too narrow to let trucks turn with an access that meets the by-law; the project includes an indoor logistics hub and a loading area parallel to the street.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme said it was in favour by a majority on April 7, 2026, and the La Cité-Limoilou borough council granted the exemption on April 27, 2026.
The City is changing the zoning of zone 62223Mb, in Saint-Émile, located between rue de la Scierie, rue Lafond, avenue Lapierre and rue des Sommeliers.
Housing (group H1) becomes permitted in this zone, where only commercial and public uses were permitted.
After the public consultations, the City is withdrawing the planned height increase to 14 metres: the limit stays at 10 metres.
The maximum number of storeys (two) is removed, and an amenity area of 4 square metres per dwelling becomes required.
The minimum percentages of cladding materials and the maximum distance of 3 metres between the front setback and the façade are removed.
The public consultation and the request for an opinion from the conseil de quartier took place on March 24, 2026, and the written consultation ran until March 31, 2026.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The City is granting a minor exemption to the property at 2836-2840, avenue L'Isle-Dieu, in the Saint-Louis neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The existing building sits 5.81 metres from the street, while the borough's planning by-law requires 6.0. The siting is now deemed to comply.
Without this exemption, the building would have to be partly demolished, according to the analysis on file.
The analysis notes that the situation has existed since 1959 and has no impact on neighbouring buildings.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the request on June 16, 2026; the borough council followed the recommendation.
The executive committee takes note of the quarterly report from the Service des ressources humaines on positions created and abolished from January 1 to March 31, 2026.
Summary for the period: 23 positions created and 11 positions abolished.

The new positions are mainly in the Service de la gestion des équipements motorisés (mechanics, technicians), the Service de police (4 surveillance officers), the Bureau pivot du tramway de Québec and the Service des affaires juridiques (2 lawyers).
Two environment advisor positions are created in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg, for the follow-up of contaminated sites and industries.

The abolished positions are concentrated in the Service de la planification de l'aménagement et de l'environnement (urban planning, urban ecosystems, sustainable mobility, landscape architecture, financial management), in addition to 5 positions abolished after the adoption of the 2026 budget.
The City states that the positions created were already provided for in the 2026 budget.
The City is awarding Les Constructions Bé-Con inc. the work on the site of the municipal garage on chemin de la Canardière, in La Cité-Limoilou, for $8,678,804.93 before taxes.
The contract covers the partial demolition of the municipal garage, the redevelopment of the land and the construction of a new street.
The work includes the water main, the sewer, the roadway, lighting and urban technical networks.
The road alignment of boulevard Henri-Bourassa, next to the work site, will be changed.
A petroleum storage tank will be moved and environmental rehabilitation work is planned.
Four companies submitted bids; the lowest offer is 21.4% below the City's estimate ($11,045,145.26).
The net expense for the City comes to $9,111,660.33, funded by funds tied to the Littoral Est port sector and by a loan by-law.
The City is entrusting the sanitary maintenance of recreational or sports sites and facilities in the arrondissement des Rivières to the organization Loisirs Duberger-Les-Saules inc.
The agreement covers the period from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027, that is, 12 months.
The contract is for $188,785.27 (plus GST and QST); the net cost to the City is $198,200.91.
The funds are split as follows: $132,133.47 in 2026 and $66,067.44 in 2027 (net of taxes).
The 2027 portion depends on the approval of the 2027 budget.
The agreement is entered into without a call for tenders, an option provided for by the Cities and Towns Act for a non-profit organization.
The previous agreement with the organization ends on April 30, 2026.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council grants a minor exemption for 1480, rue Maréchal-Foch, in the Saint-Sacrement neighbourhood.
The parking area built on the property extends 2 metres in front of the house's façade, while the planning by-law allows no such encroachment; the exemption makes it compliant.
The owners demolished the former parking area to the right of the house, replanted it with vegetation, and built a double parking area on the left.
According to the analysis, it was the presence of a mature tree in the front yard that forced part of the parking area to be moved in front of the façade.
The planning advisory committee recommended refusing the request; the council granted it despite this opinion.
The committee was concerned in particular about a knock-on effect on other similar requests in Saint-Sacrement, Montcalm, Saint-Jean-Baptiste and Saint-Sauveur.
The City is entrusting the organization Loisirs de St-Rodrigue inc. with taking charge of and using municipal recreation buildings and equipment in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The agreement covers the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029, replacing the previous agreement, which ended on March 31, 2026.
The City will pay $96,054.03 (plus GST and QST), which represents a net expense of $100,844.73 for the borough.
The amounts break down as follows (net of taxes): $23,530.44 in 2026, $33,614.91 in 2027, $33,614.91 in 2028 and $10,084.47 in 2029.
The amounts will be indexed to the Consumer Price Index starting in the second year.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
The president and the assistant clerk of the arrondissement de Charlesbourg are authorized to sign the agreement.
The City is giving $65,000 to the organization Envol et Macadam to hold the Festival Envol et Macadam in 2026.
It is also providing free municipal services (public works and police) worth a maximum of $5,000, for total support of $70,000.
The festival's 29th edition will take place from September 10 to 12, 2026, at the Agora du Port de Québec, with evening events in three bars in the Saint-Roch or Limoilou neighbourhoods.
Admission is paid, except on Thursday evening, when the shows are free for everyone.
The event's budget is estimated at $853,791; the City's grant accounts for 7.6% of it.
The money is paid in 2026 ($58,500) and in 2027 ($6,500), with the final payment conditional on the submission of the financial statements and the event's final report.
The support is conditional on sufficient funding from the other partners.
The City is awarding the maintenance work on sports and off-street structures and infrastructure across the entire city territory to Système E inc., a Québec-based company.
The contract is estimated at $589,990 before taxes; the net cost to the City is estimated at $619,415.75.
The work runs from the date the contract is awarded until April 30, 2027.
The work includes installing floodlights on poles, pouring concrete bases, excavation, and replacing light fixtures on trails and in sports parks.
Four companies submitted bids; Système E inc. offered the lowest price, 7.5% below the estimate from the requesting department.
Funding for the 2027 amounts depends on the budget being adopted by the appropriate authorities.
The City is awarding concrete repair work (sidewalks, curbs, slabs) throughout its territory to three companies, until November 30, 2026.
Les Entreprises Antonio Barrette inc. is awarded the West sector ($2,259,790) and the Centre sector ($2,085,667), before taxes.
Les Entreprises Gariépy inc. is awarded the East sector ($986,860) and JLE Entrepreneur Général inc. the North-West sector ($946,240), before taxes.
The total net expense is estimated at $6,591,700.03.
The work includes sawing, demolition, granular base, concrete and paving repair, and may take place on City land or on private property.
Four bids were received for lots 1, 3 and 4, and two for lot 2; all were compliant.
The Ville de Québec is buying a 194.3 square metre piece of land along route de l'Église, between chemin Saint-Louis and rue de Valmont, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The agreed price is $128,530, plus applicable taxes, payable when the notarized deed is signed.
The seller is the Centre intégré universitaire de santé et de services sociaux de la Capitale-Nationale (Santé Québec).
This amount includes compensation of $11,950 for claims, damages, costs, interest and lost income.
The purchase is for the project to redevelop route de l'Église, in order to improve mobility conditions.
The City is also authorizing the opening of part of the route de l'Église right-of-way on this land, once the purchase is completed.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3325 on bicycle path and pedestrian path work.
The City is changing the zoning for the area around boulevard Père-Lelièvre and boulevard Central, in the Duberger–Les Saules neighbourhood (Vanier-Duberger district).
It is merging zones to reduce their number and standardize the rules: zone 22323Mb and zone 22332Hc are being eliminated and absorbed into zones 22328Mb and 22330Mc.
The minimum and maximum numbers of dwellings per building are being removed, which makes several buildings compliant, particularly along boulevard Père-Lelièvre.
Retail stores, services and restaurants will be allowed to set up somewhere other than on the ground floor; the 750 m² limit for education and training establishments is being removed.
Front setbacks are set at 6 metres, side setbacks are being reduced for single-family homes and duplexes, and the amenity area is going from 15 to 5 m² per dwelling.
The requirement to cover 50% of the façade in masonry is being removed, the limit of three flags per lot is being eliminated, and pole signs are once again allowed.

The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to a referendum approval process; the conseil de quartier de Duberger–Les Saules will hold the public consultation meeting, followed by seven days to submit written comments.
The City is paying $69,980 to three organizations in the arrondissement des Rivières for summer activities for youth aged 13 to 15.
The amounts: $24,025 to Loisirs Duberger-Les Saules inc., $23,430 to Loisirs Vanier and $22,525 to Loisirs Lebourgneuf inc.
Each organization receives 90% of its grant in a first payment and 10% in a second payment.
The projects offer group activities, an introduction to the role of day camp leader, and preparation for the job market.
The organizations expect 98 registrations in 2026, including 13 in integration; they had welcomed 89 teenagers in the summer of 2025.
A review committee selected fifteen projects in total across the city, including these three in Les Rivières.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement des Rivières; the decision is scheduled for the borough council meeting of April 28, 2026.
The City authorizes an ExpoCité employee, an account manager, to travel to Montréal on September 1, 2026 to run a booth at the Salon Momentum, at the Hôtel Bonaventure.
A total expense of $4,194.78 is authorized, upon submission of supporting documents: registration, booth, car travel, accommodation and per diem.
The money comes from ExpoCité's operating budget.
The goal is to promote ExpoCité as an event venue and to generate business contacts among event organizers.
The trade show brings together more than 600 buyers and more than 150 exhibitors; the booth also includes two months of digital visibility on the Momentum 24/7 platform.
A variance of no more than 10% of the authorized amount will be accepted without further authorization.
The City is banning U-turns on rue de la Promenade-des-Sœurs, in front of école primaire l'Arbrisseau.
The ban starts 35 metres east of rue de la Forêt-de-Vernon and extends 200 metres eastward.
The area affected is the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, district de Cap-Rouge–Laurentien.
Police officers reported frequent U-turns in the school zone, often after a parent dropped off children.
The City says it is aiming for the safety of schoolchildren and smooth traffic flow.
The borough council adopted ordinance O-768 on August 27, 2026.
The City supports the application by Groupe de ressources techniques en arts (GRT-Arts), owner of the Centre Alyne-Lebel, at 310, boulevard Langelier.
GRT-Arts wants to obtain money from the Fonds municipal vert, a program of the Fédération canadienne des municipalités, to pay for a feasibility study.
The study would aim to improve the building's energy performance and reduce its greenhouse gas emissions over the long term.
This support was required by the program, which asks non-municipal applicants for proof of support from the municipality.
The resolution does not commit the City to any expense or obligation, unless the city council decides otherwise at a later date.
The former technical school, converted into an arts production centre in 1995, houses among others the École de danse de Québec, the Théâtre des Confettis and the Théâtre du Gros Mécano.
The Ville de Québec is giving a grant of up to $311,899 to the organization Fonds 2 for its project "Incubateur commercial 2026-2028".
The incubator supports retail businesses that want to set up or strengthen their operations on the commercial streets of the Québec agglomeration.
The organization plans to support 30 businesses per year and create 2 jobs.
The project costs $514,899 in total: $311,899 from the City, $163,000 from Fonds 2 and $40,000 in private sponsorships.
The incubator is located in the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou and follows a pilot project in Saint-Roch that supported more than 20 businesses.
Fonds 2 is a non-profit organization created in 2012 that offers microcredit, support and training.
Follow-up will be done using an economic benefits form.
The Ville de Québec is signing a new lease with Hydro-Québec to rent land next to the Complexe de soccer Chauveau, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The land, about 30,500 square metres, is used for parking, pedestrian walkways and landscaping.
The rent is $56,400 for the first year, plus taxes, and then goes up by 2% each year.
The previous year (October 1, 2024 to September 30, 2025), the rent was $20,119.50 plus taxes; the new amount is based on the market value of the land in December 2025.
The lease covers five years, from October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2030, with the possibility of renewal from year to year.
The City has set aside $119,610.16 net of taxes for the period from October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2027.
The Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire confirmed that these spaces are still needed.
The City is changing the zoning of two industrial parks, Duberger and Jean-Talon Nord, in the Duberger-Les Saules and Saint-Sauveur neighbourhoods (des Saules-Les Méandres district).
The property at 358-370, rue Jackson goes from industrial zone 22617Ip to commercial zone 22620Cb, which allows administrative offices as well as retail sales and services.
The properties at 2200 and 2181-2211, rue Léon-Harmel also leave zone 22617Ip for zone 22628Cc.

Outdoor storage is being standardized: all types become permitted in the industrial park zones, except storage of single-module homes, and except in zones 22624Cc (rue Cyrille-Duquet), 22616Cb and 22620Cb (avenue Saint-Sacrement).
These changes respond to requests made by two owners during the public consultation on the zoning review.

The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; the Duberger-Les Saules and Saint-Sauveur neighbourhood councils will be consulted, with 7 days after the public meeting to send written comments.
The borough council was aiming for adoption on April 28, 2026.
The City is ending the lease of the Fondation Monique Fitz-Back, which rents offices at 320, rue Saint-Joseph Est, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The lease ends on June 30, 2026, and the Fondation must vacate the premises on that date.
The City is paying compensation of $45,000, taxes included: a rent credit of $16,220.76 for March to June 2026 and a cheque for $28,779.24.
The cheque will be issued within 15 days after the last signature on the agreement.
The City is taking back these offices to house administrative units and reduce the space it rents elsewhere.
The City has owned the building since May 30, 2025; the rent from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2026, was $42,324.12 plus taxes.

The City is adopting the 2025 report and the 2026 update of its Plan d'action en accessibilité universelle 2025-2030 (universal accessibility action plan), which it must produce every year under the law.
In 2025, 205 new bus stops were made accessible, for a total of 1,741.
Four more kilometres of sidewalks are now cleared of snow, in addition to the new sidewalks that were added.
In parks, the City installed 9 adapted tables, 47 sets of armrests for benches and 28 adapted portable toilets; 10 parks were assessed.
24 files were handled under the Programme d'adaptation de domicile (home adaptation program), which helps people with disabilities stay in their homes.
18 projects in the Ten-Year Capital Works Program received universal accessibility improvements; 15 departments and 26 people in charge took part in the actions.
The measures planned for 2026 are continuing, and others are starting this year.
The urban agglomeration council of Québec approves the new building maintenance by-law adopted by the Ville de L'Ancienne-Lorette on March 31, 2026 (by-law 403-2026), which replaces by-law 159-2011.
The Ville de Québec considers this by-law to be consistent with its land use planning and development plan; the city clerk therefore issues a certificate of conformity.

The by-law requires property owners in L'Ancienne-Lorette to keep their buildings in good condition and prohibits letting them deteriorate (cracks, hollowed-out mortar joints, unstable stairs, broken windows, mould, etc.).
It prohibits letting snow or ice accumulate in a way that could damage the building or its structure.
For dwellings, it prohibits unsanitary situations: clutter, spoiled matter, accumulation of garbage, dampness, vermin or mould.
In the event of a suspected infestation of vermin or nuisance animals, the owner must immediately call on a person qualified in pest management.
The by-law applies to the entire territory of L'Ancienne-Lorette and also aims to protect heritage buildings.
The City is awarding Pagui inc., of Québec, the contract for outdoor cabling between its buildings for an estimated amount of $3,317,361 (before GST and QST).
The contract covers the installation, finishing, fusion splicing and labelling of optical fibres and copper wires to connect the City's computer and communications equipment.
The contract runs from August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2029, with an option to renew for 12 months.
Prices will be indexed each year based on the Consumer Price Index, starting in the second year.
Three bids were received and found to be compliant: Pagui inc. ($3,317,361), Télécon inc. ($3,562,108.95) and L.E.Q.E.L. ($4,030,695).
The net expenditure is estimated at $3,482,814.38 and depends on the approval of the 2027 to 2029 budgets.
The matter is to be decided by the urban agglomeration council of Québec.

The City supports a request made to the Commission de protection du territoire agricole du Québec (CPTAQ) to use lot 2 163 977, in the Aéroport neighbourhood (Cap-Rouge–Laurentien district), for purposes other than agriculture.
The goal is to build a house on an area of about 834.5 square metres (0.0835 hectare), along the rang Sainte-Anne.
To comply with the regulations, lots 2 163 977 and 2 164 107 will have to be merged, so that the house is on a lot where agriculture is practised.
The applicants say the home would house the family and would eventually be handed over to a child to take over the farm.
The City's analysis concludes there would be little or no impact on farming activities in the area, where there is already a concentration of homes.
The land is served by the water and sewer systems; the decision rests with the city council.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 1090, avenue Moncton, in the Montcalm neighbourhood (La Cité-Limoilou borough).
The exemption allows a height of 10.75 metres for the expansion of the third floor, whereas the planning by-law requires a maximum of 8 metres.
The work consists of changing the slope of part of the roof in order to set up an office in the attic.
According to the analysis, the building already exceeds 8 metres (it reaches 10.44 metres) and the expansion extends the existing roof by reproducing the dormer on the front facade.
The Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec and the comité consultatif d'urbanisme both gave a favourable opinion.
No financial impact is indicated in the document.
In 2024 and 2025, the Ville de Québec completed work to make walking routes safer around 17 schools, at a total cost of $9,953,523.
The ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable has committed up to $3,862,141 in grants for these 17 projects; the City has already received $3,089,713 in first payments.
The urban agglomeration council takes note of the work and expense reports and authorizes sending them to the ministère, which will allow the City to collect the final payment.

The schools involved include Stadacona, Les Sources, de l'Escale and du Plateau, Beausoleil, du Beau-Séjour, de l'Orée-des-Bois, Everest Elementary School and de la Mosaïque, Externat St-Jean-Berchmans, de Château-d'Eau, Collège Stanislas, de l'Harmonie, des Berges, Notre-Dame-des-Neiges, L'Eau-Vive, des Deux-Moulins, du Bourg-Royal-et-du-Châtelet and du Boisé.
The work around the école L'Eau-Vive was postponed because of technical difficulties.
The work includes such things as roadwork, plantings and flashing lights; the document indicates no financial impact for the City.
The City is awarding Hamel Construction inc. the operation of three snow dump sites: Jonquière, Saint-Thomas-d'Aquin (lot 1) and Godin (lot 2).
The snow dump sites are located in the arrondissements of Les Rivières and Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The contract covers five winter seasons, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2031.
The amounts are $6,100,500 for lot 1 and $1,925,375 for lot 2, plus taxes; the net expense comes to $8,426,165.50.
Prices will be indexed each year based on the Consumer Price Index (excluding energy), with adjustments based on the cubic metres of snow dumped and the price of fuel.
Two bids were received; Hamel Construction inc. submitted the lowest annual prices for both lots.
The amounts for 2027 to 2031 remain subject to budget approval by the competent authorities.
The City wants to obtain a permanent servitude (right of use) on a piece of land along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
This servitude will allow the relocation of conduits and public utility networks needed for the project.
The area involved is about 53.30 square metres, on part of lot 1 315 356.
The City will first try to reach a negotiated agreement with the owner; otherwise, it will proceed by expropriation.
The owner has been informed of the process, the next steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
If the project no longer needs the servitude, the City may withdraw from the expropriation proceedings.
The entire piece of land is assessed at $313,000 on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll, or $306.92 per square metre; the funds come from the loan by-law for the structuring network.
The Ville de Québec is granting a maximum subsidy of $511,000 to the organization 2 Degrés, a clean technology business incubator.
The money is for the project "Renforcement et poursuite de l'accompagnement des startups en technologies propres," which will last two years.
The project costs $5,253,289 in total: Québec is contributing $1,007,083, Ottawa $465,000, private partners $2,892,623, with the rest coming from incubation and management revenues.
2 Degrés will support startups through four phases (foundation, exploration, validation, consolidation) in the areas of water, the energy transition and residual materials.
Pilot projects in real-world conditions are planned with partners such as the Port de Québec, H2O Innovation and Recyc-Québec.
The project's head office is in the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou; the record provides for 7 jobs created.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.

The City is setting up a list of suppliers to compost the dewatered sludge from the Centre de biométhanisation de la matière organique (CBMO), when the plant shuts down for maintenance or equipment breakdown.
The contract covers the sludge produced from Monday to Friday (lot 1), from the awarding of the contract until August 31, 2028, with an option to extend for 12 months, indexed to inflation.
Two suppliers were found to be compliant: Environnement Viridis inc. (1st rank, $216,616.80 before taxes) and Biogénie Canada inc. (2nd rank, $283,800.00 before taxes).
The City will call on the suppliers according to their rank and their availability; the supplier must also coordinate with the carrier designated by the City.
The net expense is estimated at $227,422.66, subject to the approval of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.
Lot 2 (sludge produced on weekends) was awarded separately through a delegation of powers.
City council approves $36,626 in budget transfers between departments for current expenses, from September 1 to December 31, 2025.
A transfer of $9,626 goes from the Développement économique department to Loisirs et sports, to renew the agreement with Hydro-Québec on the parking lots at stade Chauveau.
Another transfer of $27,000 stays within the Culture et patrimoine department, to finalize an agreement for archaeological research.
Council also authorizes $321,684 in budget additions for investment activities during the same period.
Council takes note of the 2025 transfers between agglomeration and local (proximity) jurisdictions, totalling $3,919,786 in favour of the local (proximity) jurisdiction.

Three elected officials from the Arrondissement de Beauport will attend the annual convention (Assises annuelles) of the Union des municipalités du Québec (UMQ), from May 13 to 15, 2026, at the Centre des congrès de Québec.
They are President Elisa Verreault, Councillor Mélanie Sauvé and Councillor Éric Courtemanche Baril.
The registration fee is $890, plus applicable taxes.
Other expenses will be reimbursed upon submission of supporting documents.
The money comes from the Arrondissement de Beauport budget, under the activity "Soutenir les conseils d'arrondissement" (Supporting borough councils).
The City is awarding the decarbonization work at the complexe Jean-Paul-Nolin, in the arrondissement des Rivières, to the company Louis Fecteau inc. for $674,978 before taxes.
The work includes dismantling a natural gas boiler, installing two heat pumps, and setting up a heat recovery system on the stale air.
Also included are a rooftop ventilation unit, coils in the ducts, a glycol loop, a new 600 V electrical panel, structural reinforcements, and commissioning.
Nine companies submitted bids; Louis Fecteau inc. submitted the lowest compliant price, ahead of Groupe Symaco inc. at $683,190.
The net expense for the City is $708,642.53, funded by two loan by-laws.
The requesting department had estimated the work at $630,000 before taxes, which is 7.1% less than the lowest compliant bid.
The executive committee was to decide on April 15, 2026.
City council takes note of the lists of contracts and expenditures authorized by City employees in May 2026, without making any new decision.
In May 2026, the City awarded 139 contracts of more than $25,000, for a total of $71,691,511.97.
Employees with delegated authority approved $14,680,178.85 in expenditures during the same month.
The lists filed also cover terminated contracts, calls for tenders cancelled after the bids were opened, and additional expenditures made through change notices.

An employee may amend a contract up to $250,000 (net of taxes) if there was a competitive process, and up to $139,000 if there was not; above those amounts, the authorization comes from the Direction générale.
The list of contracts of $25,000 and over is published on the City's website. The amounts shown exclude taxes.
The City is awarding Sodrox Chemicals Ltd. (Salaberry-de-Valleyfield) a contract to supply bulk 50% liquid caustic soda, from April 27, 2026 to April 26, 2027.
Two lots: $214,625 for the Complexe de valorisation énergétique and $606,000 for the Centre de biométhanisation de la matière organique (before taxes).
Both facilities are located in the borough of La Cité-Limoilou.
The caustic soda is used to treat the boiler water at the Complexe de valorisation énergétique, and to treat wastewater and odours at the Centre de biométhanisation.
The contract can be renewed for two 12-month periods, with prices indexed each year.
Three companies submitted bids; the bid from Univar Solutions Canada was found non-compliant for both lots.
