The net expense is estimated at $861,553.67 and depends on approval of the 2027 budget.

The La Cité-Limoilou borough council is ending the draft by-law that would have allowed goods to be stored on the ground floor of 844, boulevard Champlain (Vieux-Québec–Cap-Blanc–Colline parlementaire neighbourhood).
The owner wanted to renovate the building, which has been vacant for a few years, and store goods there for a business in the area; the zoning only allows housing.
At the June 9, 2025 consultation and the written consultation held from June 10 to 16, 2025, most citizens said they disagreed and wanted to keep a convenience store use.
The conseil de quartier unanimously recommended (8 votes out of 8) that the request be refused.
No zoning change is therefore made for this property; storage remains not allowed there.
The document does not provide for any financial impact.
The City is giving up to $1,019,593 to the Institut canadien de Québec to run activities across the Bibliothèque de Québec network.
Of that amount, $917,593 comes from the Entente de développement culturel with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications, and $102,000 from the Politique culturelle 2025-2030.
The money pays for cultural programming at the city's 26 libraries, which offer more than 2,700 activities a year.
The City is increasing its support to expand activities at the bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy, which reopened in 2024.
An amount of $57,000 comes from an agreement with the ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration for intercultural activities.

Among the funded projects: a pop-up library in a shipping container in Saint-Pie-X (summer and fall 2026), "Contes bilingues" (bilingual storytelling), writing residencies and Indigenous culture activities.
The amounts paid were $883,541 in 2025 and $758,000 in 2024.

The City is granting $165,000 in assistance to La Parade des jouets inc. for the 2026 edition of the event: $100,000 in cash, up to $59,000 in free municipal services, and up to $6,000 in the purchase of goods and services.
The 25th Parade des jouets will take place on the afternoon of November 14, 2026, on 1re Avenue between 50e Rue and rue Boisclerc, finishing at place Jean-Béliveau at ExpoCité.
The event is free, except for the bleachers set up at the finish, which require payment.
The parade includes winter-themed floats and more than 300 costumed participants; a toy drive is planned with the Joujouthèque.
The $100,000 grant covers 21.1% of the event's planned budget, estimated at $473,200.
The City will pay $90,000 in 2026 and $10,000 in 2027, the latter amount depending on the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The assistance is conditional on a sufficient contribution from the other partners; the organization must submit a full report within 90 days after the event.
The Ville de Québec is adopting a by-law that changes the agglomeration's land use planning rules for water environments (shoreline beds, banks, flood zones) and steep-slope areas.

It is removing from the plan the rules on banks and flood zones that have become less strict than the new Government of Québec framework, which came into force on March 1, 2026, and is keeping those on the riverside protection strip and the revegetation of banks where the soil is cultivated.

Recreational trails (mountain biking, downhill skiing) become permitted on steep slopes and the areas next to them, under certain conditions: a report from an engineer on soil stability and a report from a professional on erosion and water flow.
Adding a dwelling in an accessory building is prohibited on steep slopes and the areas next to them, as is converting a non-residential building into a residential building.

The flood zone map is renamed "Zones inondables réglementées en date du 23 juin 2021" and the site planning and architectural integration programs related to work on banks, shoreline beds and watercourse crossings are removed.
Québec, L'Ancienne-Lorette and Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures will have to adjust their urban planning rules if the plan is changed.
A public consultation meeting will be held by the Commission consultative sur le schéma d'aménagement et de développement; no financial impact is expected.
The City wants to obtain a permanent easement on a piece of land bordering rue des Frênes Ouest, in the La Cité-Limoilou arrondissement, for the TramCité tramway project.
This easement will be used to relocate public utility conduits and networks needed for the project.
The area involved is about 2.50 square metres on part of lot 6 324 398.
The City may reach an amicable agreement with the owner or proceed by expropriation; the owner has been informed of the steps and has been given the name of a contact person.
The Service des affaires juridiques may drop the proceedings if the project ends up no longer needing the easement.
The entire piece of land is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $161,000, which is $552.69 per square metre.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 tied to building the structuring public transit network.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 13029, boulevard Henri-Bourassa, in the Orsainville neighbourhood (arrondissement de Charlesbourg).
The existing building will be allowed to cover 8% of the lot instead of the minimum of 15% required by the planning by-law.
In exchange, the owner must set aside 15% of the lot as green space, instead of the usual minimum of 10%.
The exemption allows two lots to be merged in order to enlarge the parking area of a used vehicle sales business, without enlarging the 177-square-metre building.
The merged lot will have an area of 2,292 square metres; the building, built in 1971, will not be modified.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on the request on February 4, 2026.
The City is giving $500 to the Association de soccer de Beauport, a non-profit organization.
The grant supports the game between the Royal Beauport and the FC Supra, held on March 29, 2026 at the Centre sportif Marc-Simoneau.
The game was played to a full house and admission was free.
The event cost the Association de soccer de Beauport more than $4,000.
The money comes from the City's "Frais généraux" (general expenses) budget, under the "Gérer les subventions" (manage grants) activity.
Last year, the City gave $750 to the same association for a game against the Roses de Montréal.
The Ville de Québec is paying $398,199 to Patro de Charlesbourg inc. for the year 2026, to support its recreational and community life activities.
The money will be paid in two parts: 50% within 30 days of signing, and 50% on June 30, 2026.
The agreement covers January 1 to December 31, 2026, and the funds come from the budget of the Arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
This is an indexed renewal of the 2025 grant ($390,391), requested by the 11 federated community recreation centres to avoid an interruption of services.
Discussions are to continue until June 2026 with a view to multi-year agreements.
The program's total funding envelope for the federated centres was indexed by 2% and reaches nearly $3.7M in 2026.
Patro must submit an accountability report form within 120 days after the end of its fiscal year and mention the City's support in its communications.
The City and the Syndicat des employés manuels de la Ville de Québec have reached an agreement (letter of agreement 26-09).
The agreement changes Schedule "F" of the collective agreement, which is in effect until December 31, 2028.
The change concerns how overtime hours are offered and assigned at outdoor pools.
The conseil d'agglomération de Québec takes note of the agreement and authorizes the change.
The document does not state any financial impact.
The Ville de Québec spent $373,091 in 2025 to maintain the des Cheminots and du Littoral bike corridors, which are part of La Route verte.
The executive committee takes note of and approves this expense report, a condition required by the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
This resolution releases a second payment of $17,157, which is 20% of the total grant of $85,783 for 2025.
The City maintains 53.9 of the 69.1 kilometres of the La Route verte network in the Québec urban agglomeration.
The main expense items: repair work ($183,081), building maintenance ($43,651), garbage collection ($39,253) and urban forestry ($35,047).
The funding is capped at 50% of eligible expenses, or at $1,750 per kilometre of bike path, $875 per kilometre of bike lane and $60 per kilometre of designated roadway.
The City is awarding Du-So Pièces d'auto inc. (377, rue Dupuy, Québec) the supply of parts and tools for municipal vehicles.
The contract covers two lots: parts ($312,494.85 before taxes) and tools ($271,542.32 before taxes).
The net expense is estimated at $613,166.02, once the QST refund is taken into account.
The contract runs from the award date until October 1, 2029, with two one-year renewal options and price indexation twice a year.
Only one bid was received for the two lots: it is 32.1% below the estimate for parts and 8.6% above it for tools.
The parts will be kept in inventory in the City's stores to supply the vehicle fleet.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the annual budgets.
The Ville de Québec wants to build a pavilion at Stade Canac.

It is applying for government grants for this project, in particular to the Programme d'aide financière aux infrastructures récréatives, sportives et de plein air (PAFIRSPA), component 1, of the ministère de l'Éducation.
This program can cover up to 66% of eligible costs, with a maximum of $20M per project.
The City agrees to pay its share of the costs, the pavilion's operating costs and any cost overruns.
No contract related to direct costs will be awarded before the minister's announcement letter.
The director of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire is authorized to sign and submit the documents for the financial assistance applications.
The City is giving out up to $100,000 in grants to 34 professional artists from Québec, through the "Le Levier" program.
Of the 62 applications submitted, 58 were eligible and 34 received a positive answer, or 59%.
The refusals are explained by an ineligible applicant, ineligible expenses, a project already supported by the City, or an incomplete application.
The program has three streams: Circuler (max. $1,500), Écrire et Développer (max. $2,500) and Concrétiser (max. $5,000).
Artists can submit an application twice a year, on May 1 and December 1.
The funded projects involve theatre, dance, circus, music, visual arts, ceramics and film, both here and in residencies elsewhere (Îles-de-la-Madeleine, Alberta, Japan, New Brunswick).
The money comes from the loan by-law tied to the implementation of the Politique culturelle 2025-2030.
The Ville de Québec is amending the agreement to sell a piece of land along rue des Moqueurs, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough (lot 5 579 068, 3,210.30 m²).
The buyer is La Bouée, société acheteuse de préservation et de développement de l'habitat communautaire.
The change concerns where the funding comes from: the assistance comes from Fonds fiscalisés recognized by the Société d'habitation du Québec instead of the Programme d'habitation abordable Québec.
The sale price set out in the purchase offer is $2,400,000, with no warranty of quality or of ownership title.
The buyer still plans to build a building with about 90 housing units for families and single people with low or modest incomes, including a common room and offices.
The buyer must start construction within 36 months after the deed is signed; otherwise, it will pay $4,000 per month to the City.
The City is adding a mandatory stop sign on avenue du Colonel-Jones, on the west approach to the intersection with rue Le Pailleur.
The area affected is the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, district de la Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy.
The intersection has three branches in a "Y" shape, and until now only the north approach had a stop sign.
According to the analysis, the shape of the intersection and the slope of the avenue prevent a driver stopped on the north side from seeing vehicles coming from avenue du Colonel-Jones.
The stop sign applies to both drivers and cyclists.
The file stems from a request made by a citizen.
The City is cancelling its August 2025 decision (CA-2025-0572) and replacing it with a new purchase authorization, this time covering the rights of an emphyteutic lessee.
It wants to acquire, by agreement or by expropriation, the real rights on part of lot 1 571 613, along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The area involved is 10.4 square metres; the City is already the bare owner of this property.
The purpose: to widen the 1re Avenue right-of-way for the structuring public transit network (TramCité project).
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings and to withdraw from them if the project no longer needs the land.
The property, land only, is entered on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $865,000, or $445.65 per square metre.
The funding comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 tied to the structuring network.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council approves architectural and site plans for two projects, as required by the borough's planning by-law.
First project: construction of a detached multi-unit residential building at 694 to 704, rue des Saules Est (Maizerets–Lairet district).
Second project: change to the exterior cladding of a detached two-unit building at 1670 and 1680, avenue de la Capricieuse.
These approvals follow the favourable recommendations of the planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme) made at its meeting of April 7, 2026.
Approval of the plans is a necessary step before construction or renovation permits can be issued.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City is awarding Les Systèmes Cyberkar inc., of Terrebonne, a contract of $409,059.76 (before GST and QST) to buy electronic components for police vehicles.
These parts will be used to outfit 87 new Ford Interceptor vehicles, planned for 2026.
The contract includes an option to buy 25 additional units per component, at a cost of $126,201.25 before taxes, to be exercised by October 1, 2026, with delivery before December 31, 2026.
Four companies submitted bids; Cyberkar submitted the lowest compliant price. Two bids were found non-compliant for administrative reasons.
The price selected is 25.7% lower than the estimate from the requesting department, which was $550,555 before taxes.
The net cost for the urban agglomeration is $429,461.62, once the QST refund is taken into account.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council confirms its intention to remove general tourist accommodation (C10 uses) from 12 zones in the Vieux-Québec area and its surroundings.
Until the planning by-law is amended, the City is suspending the issuing of permits and certificates and the approval of plans that do not comply with this intention.
The City says it wants to encourage the creation of housing and the arrival of new residents in Vieux-Québec, where it already sees a large number of tourist accommodation establishments.
The executive committee issued this notice of intention on April 10, 2026; the city council had already ratified the zones under its jurisdiction on April 21, 2026.
Municipal departments must now prepare the corresponding draft by-laws.

The City is granting $782,000 in support to the Communauté Allemande Québec for the 5th edition of the Festival Kaléidoscopes: $500,000 in cash, $139,800 in free municipal services and $142,200 in the purchase of goods and services.
The festival runs from December 27 to 31, 2026 in Vieux-Québec, with free outdoor activities and shows.
New this year: $400,000 of the grant goes to the New Year's celebrations on December 31, with a midnight countdown and fireworks; $100,000 goes to the usual programming.
The activity sites are the gardens and the place de l'Hôtel-de-Ville, the place D'Youville and the place de l'Assemblée-nationale.
The event's total budget is expected to be $1,960,000; the City's support covers 25.5% of it in cash.
The City will pay $450,000 in 2026 and $50,000 in 2027, subject to the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The support is conditional on a sufficient contribution from the other partners.
The City wants to obtain a permanent servitude (right of use) over part of a lane located near boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The area involved is about 27.3 square metres (lot 1 303 401).
This servitude would be used to move public utility conduits and networks for the TramCité tramway project.
The City may acquire the servitude by negotiated agreement or, failing that, by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques may abandon the expropriation proceedings if the project no longer needs the servitude.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the structuring public transit network.
The lane does not appear on the assessment roll, so no value is indicated.
The City is borrowing $9,000,000 to build, renovate and redo buildings, parks and recreational facilities.
The loan will be repaid over 10 years out of the City's general revenues.
The money may be used for the work, for professional and technical services contracts, for hiring staff, for grants, and to buy goods and land.
The projects cover the City's entire territory and run from 2026 to 2028, as part of the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The planned breakdown: $350,000 for universal accessibility, $5,250,000 and $3,400,000 for other components (recreation and other projects).
The City may acquire buildings or easements by agreement or by expropriation in order to carry out the work.
An amount of $900,000 (10%) is being taken from the general fund and will be repaid to it when the by-law comes into force.
The executive committee is amending its by-law on the delegation of powers to bring it in line with the new Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux, adopted in 2025.
For agglomeration contracts awarded without a competitive process, the $100,000 ceiling is replaced by the threshold set out in the law, currently $139,000.
A city employee will be able to authorize additional spending only if it covers minor changes that do not alter the nature of the contract.
An employee other than the director general or an assistant director general cannot authorize additional spending of more than 10% of the contract's original price.

The executive committee must approve the additional spending as soon as the contract total goes over $250,000 (contract with a competitive process) or reaches the threshold set out in the law (contract without a competitive process).
For a contract awarded by the city council or the urban agglomeration council, the additional spending must come from an amendment clause already provided for in the contract.
The Service des approvisionnements must submit to the executive committee the list of authorizations given under this delegation.
The City is lowering the speed limit from 70 km/h to 50 km/h on chemin de la Grande-Ligne, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The change affects a 115-metre section, heading south from the intersection with rue des Aigles-Pêcheurs, at the boundary of Stoneham-et-Tewkesbury.
The new limit applies at all times.
The municipality of Stoneham-et-Tewkesbury had asked the City to look into the matter.
The City is thus aligning its limit with the 50 km/h already in effect on the Stoneham-et-Tewkesbury side.
The Ville de Québec is joining a group purchasing agreement of the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales (CAG) to buy light vehicles.
The agreement applies from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The purchase volume is estimated at $6,640,000 (plus GST and QST).
Taking the QST refund into account, the net expense is estimated at $6,971,170.
The vehicles covered are electric, plug-in hybrid or gasoline-powered: police cars, passenger cars, sport utility vehicles, pickup trucks and vans.
The Service de la gestion des équipements motorisés is the beneficiary; the funds will come from its financing as needs arise.
The director of the Service des approvisionnements is authorized to sign the documents and to confirm the City's participation.
The Ville de Québec is authorizing spending of $17,260,000 to buy vehicles and motorized equipment for the Service de protection contre l'incendie.

The money will be used to replace vehicles that have reached the end of their useful life: pumper trucks, ladder trucks, water supply trucks, pickup trucks, vans, as well as accessories and technological solutions.
The amount also covers professional and technical services contracts and the hiring of the staff needed for the purchases.
The City is borrowing the full amount, repayable over ten years out of its general revenues.
An amount of $1,726,000 (10% of the expenditure) is being taken from the general fund and will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The vehicles will be used throughout the territory of the agglomeration of Québec; the funds are planned from 2026 to 2030 in the capital works program.
The City is paying up to $154,643 to the organization Craque-Bitume to manage 32 community composting sites during the 2026-2027 season.
Two sites are closing in 2026 due to low use: the Ateliers de la Terre and parc Nérée-Tremblay; their users are invited to join other sites.

Craque-Bitume will install 11 composters in 7 community gardens (Sillery, des Franciscains, des Sables, Cité-Verte, la Comtoise, Croque-Soleil, Marchand) and will replace 3 composters that have reached the end of their life.
The bank of support hours for community gardens is going from 80 to a maximum of 200 hours.
The grant is lower than the $168,635 one for 2025-2026, because of the site closures and because there are no video clips this year.
The way the funding is calculated is changing: a flat amount per site based on the number of composters, instead of tonnage estimates.
Managing the composters in the community gardens remains the responsibility of each garden, not Craque-Bitume.
The Ville de Québec is granting a maximum subsidy of $140,000 to the company 3D Coupe (9148-3461 Québec inc.), located in the parc industriel de Charlesbourg.
The money goes to the "Virage numérique" project: robotization of machining, dashboards, artificial intelligence agents, cybersecurity and staff training.
The project costs $350,000 in total: $140,000 from the City, $105,000 from the company and a $105,000 loan from the Banque Nationale.
The company, which does plastics cutting and machining, has 9 employees and plans to create 2 more.
The subsidy comes from the Capitale-Productivité component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, which pays up to $500,000 per project, for a maximum of 40% of eligible expenses.
The program's analysis committee gave a favourable opinion on June 9, 2026; the decision rests with the urban agglomeration council.
The City is awarding Groupe Colas Québec inc. the work to upgrade the networks on rue Montreuil, for $1,375,000 before taxes.
The work affects rue Montreuil, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge arrondissement.
Sanitary and storm sewers will be built to separate the existing combined sewer system over 155 metres, and the water main will be replaced in the work zone.
A sidewalk will be added over about 140 additional metres, outside the underground work zone.
Nine companies submitted bids; Colas offered the lowest price, 1.6% above the City's estimate.
The net expense comes to $1,443,578.12, funded by a loan by-law ($1,192,011.59) and a grant from the ministère des Transports ($251,566.53).
The contract includes a bitumen price adjustment clause.
The City wants to authorize a real estate project at the corner of rue Lee and rue de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres, in the Saint-Roch neighbourhood, alongside autoroute Laurentienne.
The project calls for a mixed-use building with about 375 rental units, half of which would have at least two bedrooms, including two-storey townhouses and three-bedroom units.

A food store would occupy the ground floor on the rue de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres side, and the green roofs would include a market garden greenhouse whose produce could be offered to citizens and organizations in the area.

The project does not comply with the planning rules: a height of about 31 metres instead of the 21-metre maximum, seven to nine storeys, front and side setbacks not respected, underground parking too close to the lot line, a rooftop greenhouse that is not permitted, and a generator in the front yard.
The proposed percentage of large units is below the minimum required by the regulations.
The City must hold a public consultation meeting, then give interested persons three days to send their comments in writing; the project is not subject to approval by referendum.
Anyone who breaches the conditions of the resolution faces a fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.
The City is granting an exemption for a residential project of 303 housing units on eight storeys, at 6351, rue de la Goutte-de-Lait, in Neufchâtel-Lebourgneuf (Arrondissement des Rivières).
The underground parking will be allowed to come within 1.5 metres of the front property line, instead of the 3 metres required by the planning by-law.
Condition imposed: keep at least 1 metre of soil above the underground parking along the entire length of the lot, in order to plant and maintain at least 13 trees in the front yard.
The developer commits to providing 20 cubic metres of space and 1 metre of soil for the survival of large-growing trees in the front yard.
According to the analysis, complying with the 3-metre setback would have meant losing 42 parking spaces, with a risk of overflow onto neighbouring streets.
A watercourse runs along the back of the property, which limits the possibility of moving the building back.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on August 3, 2026, unanimously.
The City is adding one parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility on rue Saint-Germain, in Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur.
The space is on the west side, between rue Boisseau and rue Napoléon, in front of 386, rue Saint-Germain.
It begins 14 metres south of rue Boisseau and extends 6 metres to the south.
Only vehicles displaying a sticker, licence plate or permit provided for in the Code de la sécurité routière will be allowed to park there.
The request came from a resident of 386, rue Saint-Germain, who holds a SAAQ sticker and a valid driver's licence.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council adopted ordinance O-1579 on July 9, 2026.
The arrondissement de Charlesbourg is paying out 12 grants totalling $29,978 to 11 organizations in the area.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget, under the "Soutien aux organismes" (support for organizations) activity.

The largest amounts go to Patro de Charlesbourg ($9,398) for support staff during its activities, Partage des Laurentides ($5,000) and Association de baseball mineur de Charlesbourg ($4,250) for equipment.
Société d'histoire et de généalogie de Charlesbourg receives $3,516 to redo its website, and Club aquatique de Charlesbourg receives $2,306 for swimming support staff.
Other smaller amounts pay for bingo equipment, keyboards, banners, branding and training.
Applications had to be submitted by March 15, 2026 at the latest; some grants correspond to year 2 or 3 of the program supporting operating expenses.
The borough council adopted the decision on May 26, 2026.
The owner of 375, 19e Rue, in the Lairet neighbourhood (Limoilou), wants to change the exterior siding of the house.
The project submitted would have replaced the stone on the ground floor and the red siding on the upper floor with pale grey fibre cement with dark grey accents.

The City approves the project, but with two conditions: put brick on the ground floor of the front facade, and choose a shade of fibre cement for the upper part that is close to the colour of the brick.
Reason given: keep materials similar to those already in place and respect the facade as a whole.
If the owner does not meet these conditions, the application is put on hold and another project will have to be submitted at a later meeting.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion by majority on August 11, 2026.
The City is authorizing the construction of a 36-unit building at 1853, boulevard Bastien, in Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf, whereas the by-law allows only 3 units.
The building may have 4 storeys and be 15 metres high, instead of the 3 storeys and 11 metres allowed, and provide 40 parking spaces instead of 43.
The developer will have to build at least 32 units, including at least 4 with three or more bedrooms, and equip each unit with a heat pump.
Other conditions: a white roof on the 4th storey, 35 trees planted, 10 covered bicycle spaces, a 100-square-metre outdoor common area, and a hedge or fence on the west and east sides.
The building must be set back at least 15 metres from the south boundary of the lot, and the parts above the 3rd storey at least 20 metres.

The project must start within 18 months following the adoption of the resolution, otherwise the authorization lapses; offenders face a fine of $1,000 (individuals) or $2,000 (other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.
The City will hold a public consultation meeting, followed by three days to submit written comments; the project is not subject to a referendum.
The Arrondissement de Charlesbourg is giving $250 to the organization "OBNL de la Rivière Jaune".
The money is being used to organize the Fête de la pêche de Notre-Dame-des-Laurentides.
The event takes place on the weekend of June 6 to 7, 2026.
The document expects between 1,200 and 1,500 people on site: trout fishing enthusiasts and their families.
The funds come from the budget of the conseil d'arrondissement de Charlesbourg (borough council).
A similar grant had already been given to the same organization for the 2024 edition.
The Ville de Québec is giving $8,000 to the Association des travaux publics du Québec for its FièrementTP 2026 campaign.
This amount gives the City major partner status, as it did last year, when the City also gave $8,000.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service des travaux publics: $4,000 from snow removal and maintenance of public roads, $4,000 from maintenance of the water and sewer systems.
The campaign includes a tour by spokesperson Sara Dufour from May 18 to 24, 2026, during the Semaine nationale des travaux publics, with the possibility of hosting her for about two hours.
In exchange, the City gets visibility (logo, mentions on social media) and unlimited posting of its public works job offers.
The organization's total budget for the 2026 campaign is $90,000.
The executive committee adopted resolution CE-2026-0115 on January 28, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 685, avenue Newton, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood (Arrondissement des Rivières).
The one-way access lane will be allowed to be up to 7.5 metres wide, instead of the maximum of 6 metres set out in the planning by-law.
The applicant, Distribution Ste-Foy (a building materials store), wants to add a garage door in the front yard, which will be used only as an exit.
The widening is meant to allow 54-foot trucks to turn from rue Newton; the building is close to the street, which limits manoeuvring.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme recommended the application unanimously on February 2, 2026, and the Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente said it was in favour.
The borough council adopted the decision on February 24, 2026.
The executive committee takes note of the weekly list of additional expenses over $250,000 authorized by employees with delegated authority, for the week of February 8 to 14, 2026.
Only one contract change appears in the report: $336,408.92 before taxes, at the Service de la gestion des immeubles.
It concerns the new pavilion at parc Chauveau, to adjust the civil engineering work because of additional management of contaminated soils.
The contract goes from $6,562,331.20 to $6,898,740.12; its initial value was $6,533,855.19.
The Service des approvisionnements publishes this list every week, with amounts shown before taxes.
The City authorizes spending of $31,600,000 for work to repair and build municipal infrastructure, and is borrowing the same amount, repayable over 15 years.
The work covers roads, water and sewer systems, lighting and traffic lights, public utility networks, engineering structures, and the development of municipal spaces.
The projects can be carried out anywhere in the territory under the city's jurisdiction.
The amount also covers professional and technical services, hiring staff, buying buildings and easements, and paying out grants.
The City may acquire, by agreement or by expropriation, any building or easement needed for the work.
An amount of $3,160,000 (10% of the spending) is being taken from the general fund and will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The funds are planned for the years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 capital works program; the Service de l'ingénierie is leading the file.
The City is banning U-turns on rue des Couventines, in the school zone of the école primaire de la Passerelle (460, rue des Couventines).
The ban covers 295 metres, starting 38 metres east of avenue du Lac-Saint-Charles and going east.
The Service de police had asked for the change after seeing U-turns made by parents dropping their children off at the school.
The measure aims to protect the safety of schoolchildren and keep traffic flowing.
The area affected is the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles, district of Lac-Saint-Charles–Saint-Émile.
The City is selling a 626.1-square-metre lot to the company Prologis inc., in the Val-Bélair industrial park, in the borough of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The price is $53,915, plus taxes, which works out to $86.11 per square metre; the money will go to the Fonds général.
The land must be used for industrial, para-industrial or research purposes.
The added land is meant to solve parking and outdoor storage problems and to make the lot rectangular along with the neighbouring property.
The project does not create any jobs, but it maintains the 15 existing jobs; the total investment is estimated at close to $124,000.
The price matches the rate in effect when the purchase offer was made, not the rate applied since September 16, 2025.
Two conditions differ from the City's policy: the construction deadline starts when the deed is signed, and the right of pre-emption applies only up until the building is constructed.

The Ville de Québec is reaching an agreement with the Canadien National for an estimated amount of $1,056,000 (plus GST and QST) to prepare the plans and specifications and to characterize the soils in view of rebuilding the north portion of the 4e Avenue railway overpass.
The net expense for the City, after recovering the QST, is estimated at $1,108,668.

CN advised the City that the bridge is at the end of its useful life and that the reconstruction work must be done in 2026 and 2027; an order from the Office des transports du Canada places the maintenance and repair costs on the City.
The overall budget for the reconstruction project was assessed at $25,656,000 in the feasibility study by CIMA+, including a 30% contingency.
The detailed design must be completed by June 30, 2026, and the call for tenders for the work is planned for July 2, 2026.
The City pays the costs actually incurred, CN reimburses any unused amounts, and invoices are payable within 15 days.
The agreement is entered into without a call for tenders, as the law allows this for work on a railway right-of-way carried out with its owner.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 2765, rue des Anciens-Combattants, in the Saint-Louis neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough).
The existing house sits 5.89 metres from the street, while the planning by-law requires 6.0 metres. The siting of the building is therefore deemed to comply.
According to the analysis, without this exemption, the building would have to be moved or demolished to meet the rule.
The situation has existed since 1956 and no complaints have been recorded; the analysis concludes there is no impact on neighbours, safety, health or the environment.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on March 10, 2026, and the borough council granted it.
The City is transferring $313,068 from the urban agglomeration contingency account to the budget of the Service des affaires juridiques.
This money is used to pay the bill from the ministère de la Justice for the salaries of the judges of the Cour municipale de Québec in 2026.
The ministère's bill is higher than what the City had budgeted, which was based on the Court's historical data.
The difference comes from changes to the number of sittings requested by the presiding judge, changes that do not match the Court's needs according to the City.
The City has raised the issue and asked for the bill to be reviewed, with no favourable response so far.
The City is paying the bill anyway in order to continue benefiting from the judges' services, and is pursuing its efforts to have it reviewed.
The executive committee adopted the decision on March 4, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0271).
The City is setting up a marked and signed pedestrian crossing on rue Duberger, at the intersection of rue de Côme, in Charlesbourg.
The goal: to make the crossing safer for schoolchildren and pedestrians going to école primaire de l'Ancrage, on rue de la Faune.
Parking becomes prohibited at all times on the west side of rue de Côme, between rue Phydime-Deschênes and rue Duberger.
The parking ban from November 15 to March 31 is removed on the east side of rue de Côme; parking will be allowed there at all times.
Seven parking spaces on rue de Côme are removed at all times.
The request comes from an application filed by a citizen.
The City is filing with council the lists of its contracts of $25,000 and more awarded in January 2026, as required by law.
In January 2026, it awarded 109 contracts of more than $25,000, for a total value of $31,183,891 (before taxes).
Of that number, 31 contracts are over $250,000, for a total of $24,669,054.

The director general and his assistants awarded 16 contracts, including lawn and landscaping work in several neighbourhoods (Val-Bélair, Loretteville, Lac-Saint-Charles, Maizerets, Orsainville and others).
The director of the Service des approvisionnements renewed 7 contracts, including snow removal on certain streets ($776,211) and the supply of polymer to the Centre de biométhanisation ($1,238,198).
Since April 2024, a contract must be opened to competition as soon as it reaches $34,000; between $10,000 and $34,000, two price requests are required.
The lists filed also cover contracts that were transferred or terminated, cancelled calls for tenders, and additional spending that was authorized.
The City is hiring three firms to carry out materials quality control and environmental soil management for its worksites, until March 31, 2027.
Lot 1 (Haute-Ville: La Cité-Limoilou, Charlesbourg and the Service des travaux publics): Laboratoires d'Expertises de Québec ltée, about $1,620,740.00 before taxes.
Lot 2 (Basse-Ville: La Cité-Limoilou and Beauport): Les Services EXP inc., about $1,268,470.00 before taxes.
Lot 3 (Les Rivières, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge and La Haute-Saint-Charles): Englobe Corp., about $1,167,063.44 before taxes.
The services cover street resurfacing work, water main and sewer rehabilitation, engineering structures and street openings, including laboratory testing and reports.
The net cost to the City is estimated at $4,258,580.08, subject to approval of the 2027 budget.
Seven bids were received; firms selected for one lot became ineligible for the following lots.
The City takes note of the decision authorizing the demolition of the maison Drolet-Boiteau, at 1629, boulevard Pie-XI Nord, in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec approved the demolition on March 26, 2026, citing the building's poor overall condition, restoration costs and the lack of any possible grants.
The Commission points out that boulevard Pie-XI Nord is identified as a densification corridor and that the replacement project would increase the supply of housing in the area.
The authorization comes with conditions: the replacement project will have to be adjusted according to the Commission's recommendations and be the subject of a permit application.
No one asked the city council to review the decision within 30 days; the urban agglomeration council confirms that it will not use its power of disallowance and is shortening the 90-day period.
The City will then be able to issue the demolition authorization certificate.
The document indicates that there is no financial impact.

The City is awarding a $657,667 contract (before GST and QST) to Solotech inc., a Québec City company, to buy animation video projectors for the rink at the multipurpose amphitheatre (Centre Vidéotron).
The request comes from ExpoCité and aims to replace the current audiovisual equipment, which has reached the end of its useful life.
Solotech submitted the lowest price among the four compliant bids received, which went as high as $891,725.04.
The chosen price is 21.2% below the requesting department's estimate, which was $834,701.00.
The money comes from the "Pérennité Centre Vidéotron" financial reserve; the expense falls under the urban agglomeration.
Two other lots from the same call for tenders (projectors for the press gallery and lighting for the stairs) have already been awarded through delegation of powers.
The City is refusing a minor exemption request for 3391, rue Hertel, in the Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy neighbourhood (arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The owner wanted to split the lot in two in order to keep the existing house and build a detached two-family building on the new portion.
The proposed lot would have been 13.42 metres wide, while the planning by-law requires 16.0 metres.

Reason for the refusal: the 16.0-metre standard, adopted in 2022, is meant to ensure new buildings fit in and that densification is consistent with the surrounding area; the City concludes that there is no serious harm.
The analysis also notes that allowing this width would set a precedent for similar requests in the area.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the refusal on January 13, 2026; the borough council followed that recommendation (resolution CA3-2026-0020).
The City is changing the zoning at 2800, avenue Saint-Jean-Baptiste, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood, to allow the company Laserax, which specializes in lasers, to set up there.
The building would house Laserax's head office, research and development, assembly and laboratories, in space that is partly vacant.
The change adds the "high-technology industry" use group in zones 22128Cb and 22129Cb, east of avenue Saint-Jean-Baptiste, between rue Michelet, autoroute Henri-IV and boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel.
Data processing or data hosting centres larger than 200 square metres remain prohibited in these zones, as does outdoor storage.
According to the document, the activities would generate no noise or odour noticeable outside the premises.

The by-law contains provisions subject to approval by referendum; the conseil de quartier de Duberger-Les Saules will hold the public consultation meeting, followed by seven days to send in written comments.
Two other nearby zones (22108Cb and 22109Cb) fall under the borough council and are the subject of a separate process.
The City wants to acquire a piece of land and an easement alongside 1re Avenue, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The purchase covers a parcel of about 11.70 square metres, needed to widen the right-of-way of 1re Avenue.
The City also wants to obtain a permanent public utility easement over about 36.80 square metres, in order to move conduits and networks.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement or by expropriation; the Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings.
If the project no longer needs the land or the easement, the City may abandon the expropriation proceedings, in whole or in part.
The owner has been informed of the process and of the name of a contact person at the City.
The money comes from the agglomeration loan by-law for building the structuring public transit network.
The borough of La Cité-Limoilou is giving $500 to the organization "Mères et monde, Centre communautaire et résidentiel par et pour jeunes mères".
The money is meant to support the organization in carrying out its mission.
The request comes from councillor Raymond Poirier.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, under the activity "Soutenir les conseils d'arrondissement".
The organization is located at 727, 8e Avenue, in Québec.
The City is authorizing the demolition of a heritage house located at 1132, boulevard Raymond, in the Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux neighbourhood, in Beauport.
The Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec approved the demolition on March 26, 2026, citing the building's deteriorated condition and the cost of restoring it.
The building in question is the maison Dubreuil-Latulippe, described as one of the oldest houses in the area.
No one asked the city council to review the decision within the 30-day period, and no written comments were received during the publication period.
The urban agglomeration council is waiving its power of disallowance and shortening the 90-day period provided for by law.
The demolition is conditional: the replacement project will have to be adjusted according to the Commission's recommendations before the permits are issued.
The document states that there is no financial impact.
The City is requesting $2,817,530 from the ministère des Transports under the Programme d'aide financière du Fonds de la sécurité routière, which is funded by photo radar fines.
This money would go to 12 road safety projects valued at $3,521,913, to be carried out in 2027; the program covers up to 80% of eligible expenses.

Five school corridors would be built: écoles Beausoleil (rues du Tunis and Vachon), St-Albert-le-Grand (2e Avenue and des Peupliers Est), de la Source (boulevard des Étudiants and Charles-Garnier), Sans-Frontière (rues Blouin, Bélanger and avenue Rousseau) and Guillaume-Mathieu (avenue de Gironde and rue d'Urfé).
New sidewalks would be built on rue Careau, rue De Brugnon, avenue Jules-Verne and boulevard Pie-XI Nord, with traffic lights on De Brugnon.
Avenue Champfleury and the autoroute Félix-Leclerc ramp would be redesigned with curb extensions and traffic lights.
The City would install 100 speed humps in total: 40 in the east sector and 60 in the west sector.
The document does not anticipate any financial impact for the City at this stage; a first payment of no more than 80% of the funding would follow the signing of the agreement.
The City is banning parking on new sections of rue Hugues-Randin, in the Métrobec industrial park (arrondissement des Rivières, district des Saules-Les Méandres).
On the west side, the no-parking-at-any-time zone goes from 30 to 76 metres, which covers the parking entrances at 5005 and 5055, rue Hugues-Randin.
On the east side, parking becomes prohibited at any time over 22 metres, near the entrance at 5000, rue Hugues-Randin.
Five parking spaces are being removed because of these changes.
The goal: to let delivery trucks manoeuvre more easily, following a request from a business in the area.
The City is giving $2,000 to the organization Vivre Grand for the Semaine québécoise de la déficience intellectuelle, from March 15 to 21, 2026.
This amount funds five flagship activities in a program with a total budget of $19,000.

Four activities are free: launch evening at LaScène (March 13), sensory workshop at the Bibliothèque Monique-Corriveau (March 14), inclusive soccer at the Stade Chauveau (March 14) and research evening at the UQTR campus (March 17).
One low-cost activity: the medical schools' hockey tournament at the PEPS on March 21.
Vivre Grand will have to mention the City's contribution in its publications and submit an activity report and a financial report no later than June 30, 2026.
The amount is the same as the one granted in 2025 ($2,000), after $1,000 in 2024.
The City is paying out $20,736 in grants to six organizations in the arrondissement des Rivières, for applications submitted on March 15, 2026.
Boîte à science is receiving $8,895 to enhance its workshops for 12- to 17-year-olds.
La Ruche Vanier is getting $4,250 to redo its website.
Solidarité Familles Duberger - Les Saules is receiving $3,352 for gardening and cooking supplies, and the Club de soccer des Rivières $3,264 for soccer nets.
Le Choeur V'là l'bon Vent ($500) and Groupe Les Relevailles ($475) are receiving money for team-building activities and volunteer recognition.
The money comes from the operating budget of the arrondissement des Rivières, under the "Soutien aux organismes" (support for organizations) line item.
The borough council adopted the decision on May 26, 2026.
The City wants to acquire a piece of land along rue de la Faune, in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles, in order to widen that street.
The land in question is about 2,491.7 square metres and is part of lot 1 398 045.
The purchase will be made by mutual agreement with the owner or, if the discussions fail, by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the acquisition or expropriation proceedings.
The Division de l'arpentage et de la géomatique will prepare the necessary plans, technical descriptions and cadastral operations.
The property, in its full extent, is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $208,000, or $3.56 per square metre.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 related to the redevelopment work on rue de la Faune.
The City wants to allow financial services offices to open in the house at 902, Grande Allée Ouest, in the Sillery neighbourhood, which is currently used as a residence.
The building, built around 1930, was recently purchased in order to set up these offices; its appearance will not be changed.
The property has about six parking spaces, whereas nine would be required: the owner will have to redevelop the parking area or pay a compensation to be exempted.
The borough council is adopting the draft by-law and giving a notice of motion, then asking for the opinion of the conseil de quartier de Sillery, which will hold the public consultation meeting.
Interested people will have seven days after the public meeting to send their comments in writing.
The by-law cannot be the subject of a referendum and no active participation measure is planned, the City noting that the area already has this type of use.
The City is abolishing the Division du vivre-ensemble et de la cohésion sociale, which was part of the Service de la coordination stratégique et des relations internationales.
All of that division's employees were already transferred in February 2026 to the Division du développement social of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The division no longer had any employees, which justifies closing it according to the document.
Social files are therefore brought together in a single division.
The abolition has no budget impact: the funds, including employee benefits, are already provided for in the budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The move is part of the reorganization of the Direction générale adjointe - Citoyen et vitalité urbaine that began in 2025.

The executive committee takes note of the quarterly report on the urban forestry agreements signed with property owners next to the tramway route (TramCité project), for the period from January 1 to March 31, 2026.

The report lists 33 signed agreements, mostly on boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest and Est, as well as on avenue du Parc-Thornhill, avenue des Laurentides, avenue du Cardinal-Rouleau, avenue De Salaberry, avenue Rodolphe-Forget and avenue Moncton.
All of these agreements provide for clearing the right-of-way: cutting down, transplanting, clearance pruning or protecting trees.
Several agreements commit the City to planting trees on the private property after the work, and most commit it to maintaining the private trees near the route in perpetuity.
Six agreements include an offer of final compensation to the owner: $313, $675, $1,935, $2,691, $4,445 and $13,245.
This quarterly filing is required by by-laws R.C.E.V.Q. 160 and R.C.E.V.Q. 172.
City council approves budget transfers of $442,133 made between January 1 and April 30, 2026 in operating activities.
It also authorizes $52,040 in additions to the operating budget and $3,278,571 in additions to the capital budget for the same period.

Among the transfers: $250,000 to pay grants under the program for the removal or replacement of non-certified solid-fuel-burning appliances, and $37,133 for grants related to the fight against the emerald ash borer.
$155,000 is moved to the temporary public spaces (places éphémères) and to the Programme d'animation des espaces publics extérieurs.
The operating additions cover $33,840 for the three-year agreement with the Externat Saint-Jean-Eudes and $18,200 for the partnership agreement with the Club de hockey Les Remparts.
Council takes note of transfers of $16,284,049 moved for the benefit of local jurisdiction, between the agglomeration and local budgets.
The Ville de Québec is lending up to $2,000,000, interest-free, to the non-profit organization Un toit en réserve de Québec inc.
The money will be used to buy the building at 3055 to 3065, 2e Avenue, whose purchase price is $4,000,000.
The organization wants to build a project there of about 251 social housing units.
The loan must be repaid within 18 months, and the organization is giving the City a first-rank mortgage on the building as security.
The loan could be converted into a grant if the project qualifies for a Société d'habitation du Québec program or for a government order; a second agreement would then be required.
The $2,000,000 comes from the agglomeration operating surplus set aside for social and affordable housing.
The organization must insure the building at its own expense and pay the notary fees related to the mortgage.
The Ville de Québec is buying a property at 4264, rue Saint-Félix, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough, for $1,058,000 plus taxes.
The lot is 1,749.2 square metres and includes a building and its outbuildings; it is assessed at $650,000 on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll.
The seller is Mr. Pascal Goudreault; the price includes an incidental indemnity of $83,000, and the property must be delivered free of any lease.
The purchase is meant to allow the redevelopment of the former Anacolor plant lands, already owned by the City, in order to speed up housing construction.
The project must also improve access to the banks of the rivière du Cap-Rouge, redevelop the area and showcase the archaeological site of the Poterie de Cap-Rouge.
The City is authorizing the demolition of the building and its outbuildings; the funds for the demolition will be approved later.
The sale puts an end to the servitude buy-back lawsuit filed by the seller, who will waive any legal proceedings within 30 days of signing.
The Ville de Québec is signing an agreement with the Ville de L'Ancienne-Lorette for the use of its snow dump sites.
For years, L'Ancienne-Lorette has been dumping its snow there and paying a yearly amount, but there was no written agreement.
The agreement sets the rules for using the snow dump sites and the rights and obligations of each city.
It can be renewed up to and including the winter of 2029-2030.
The revenue from the agreement will go into the Ville de Québec's general fund.
The director of the Service des travaux publics is authorized to sign the agreement on behalf of the City.
The City is changing how the traffic lanes are used on boulevard Saint-Jacques, at the intersection with avenue Chauveau, in Arrondissement des Rivières.
On the north side: the left lane is for left turns only, the centre lane is for going straight, and the right lane is for turning right or going straight.
On the south side: the left lane is for left turns only, and the right lane is for turning right or going straight.
The change follows complaints from residents about traffic flow on the north and south approaches to this intersection.
The City's analysis finds that many drivers turn left without having a lane reserved for them, which disrupts traffic.
The districts of Neufchâtel–Lebourgneuf and Les Saules–Les Méandres are affected.
The City authorizes the Service de la culture et du patrimoine to spend up to $50,000 (net of taxes) in 2026 to buy show tickets.
These tickets are for the Guichet Ouvert program, which gives the most disadvantaged residents access to cultural outings.
The Service buys performing arts tickets and gives them to recognized community organizations in the area, which distribute them.
The program also aims to develop audiences and cultural mediation activities.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de la culture et du patrimoine.
Amounts of $50,000 had already been authorized for the same program in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

The City is adding $66,689.27 (plus taxes) to the contract with the Corporation des Loisirs de Vanier for the maintenance and supervision of the recreational and sports facilities and equipment in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The contract therefore goes from $192,597.72 to $259,286.99 (plus taxes), for the period from May 1, 2025 to April 30, 2026.
The additional amount covers 3,016.25 more hours of supervision than planned, at a rate of $22.11 per hour: 10,801.25 actual hours instead of the 7,785 hours estimated.
The City explains this overrun by the increase in bookings at the Centre Fernand-Dufour, the Centre Laurence-Perron and the école secondaire de Vanier, and by an initial estimate that was too low.
The net expense for the arrondissement des Rivières comes to $70,015.40, taken from the operating budget of the community recreation centres.
The City is paying $10,000 per year to the organization T.R.A.I.C. Jeunesse in 2026, 2027 and 2028, for a total of $30,000.
The money pays for street outreach work with young people in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, where three street workers are active.
The 2026 payment comes within 30 days after the agreement takes effect; those for 2027 and 2028 around July 31 of each year.
The 2027 and 2028 amounts depend on the budgets being adopted and on the organization handing in the documents required by the City.
The organization must report each year and mention the City's support in its official publications.

According to the document, street workers in the area reached 1,998 people last year, including 717 direct interventions and 225 ongoing follow-ups; 63% of the people served are between 10 and 29 years old.
Twenty people experiencing homelessness received support, compared with seven the previous year.
The City is easing the planning rules in the parc industriel Armand-Viau, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood (district des Saules-Les Méandres).
Outdoor storage becomes permitted in several zones of the industrial park, including the storage of goods, construction materials, containers, heavy vehicles or bulk materials.
Parking and outdoor storage become allowed in the electricity transmission corridor that crosses the park, or on a vacant lot next to that corridor.
Any outdoor storage area must be surrounded by an opaque fence, and storage remains prohibited in the front yard.
Following the public consultations held from May 12 to 19, 2026, the City is withdrawing its plan to allow outdoor storage in zone 22002Cc, because of a residential neighbourhood nearby to the north.
In zone 22006Ma, general industry becomes permitted and parks are no longer permitted; the minimum building height of 8 metres and the 2-storey requirement are removed.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; adoption was planned for the borough council meeting of June 23, 2026.
The City is giving $150,000 to the organization BLEUFEU to hold the "St-Roch XP" event from August 27 to 29, 2026.

It is also providing free municipal services (staff time and equipment loans from public works, building management and the police) worth no more than $33,500, plus $500 in purchases of goods and services, for total assistance of $184,000.
The grant includes $120,000 in support for the event and $30,000 paid under the plan Saint-Roch.

The event will take place on rue Saint-Joseph, between rue du Pont and rue Saint-Anselme, as well as at the bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy, at Grizzly Fuzz, in the former premises of District St-Joseph and at Impérial Bell.
Most of the program is free: music showcases, street food, family activities on Saturday morning and electronic music evenings; shows at Impérial Bell require paid admission.
The City will pay $135,000 in 2026 and $15,000 in 2027, the latter amount being conditional on the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The assistance also depends on sufficient contributions from the other partners; the event's projected budget is $916,600.
The City is paying $46,750 to the organization Générations Actives for its Inclusion project, from May 2026 to March 2027.
The project offers 40 sports and recreational activities, cooking workshops, a photo exhibition and 5 themed activities.
The activities bring together immigrants, ethnocultural minorities and members of the host society.
The total cost of the project is estimated at $100,700; the City is paying about 46% of it (wages, materials, promotion and management).
The organization will have to mention the contribution of the City and of the ministère de l'Immigration in its publications, and submit a report on the activities and a financial report.
The money comes from the financial assistance agreement between the City and the ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration.
The City is authorizing the demolition of a detached garage located behind the house at 1705, avenue Chauveau, in the Neufchâtel Est - Lebourgneuf neighbourhood (arrondissement Les Rivières).
The building, put up between 1880 and 1910, is recognized as a heritage property and is a reminder of the area's farming past.

The Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec approved the demolition on June 18, 2026, citing structural failures documented by an engineer, a condition considered beyond repair and a possible danger to public safety.
After the demolition, the land will have to be cleaned up, levelled and planted with vegetation; no new construction is planned.
Two written comments were received during the publication period, and no one spoke at the public meeting.

No request for review was filed within the 30-day period; the urban agglomeration council confirms that it will not overturn the decision and is shortening the 90-day period, which clears the way for the authorization certificate to be issued.
The City is hiring Protecta Security inc. (Lévis) to provide security for the temporary sanitary unit at carré Lépine, on rue Saint-Vallier Est, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The contract is worth $260,876 before taxes and runs from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
The contract can be renewed for another 12 months, with a price increase based on the consumer price index.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 depend on those years' budgets being adopted.
Out of 16 bids received, Protecta Security offered the lowest price among the compliant bids; the City's estimated price was $345,976.55 before taxes.
The City is approving eight lists of suppliers authorized to provide professional IT services, valid for three years from the date they are published on the SEAO website.
The eight fields covered: project management and agility, infrastructure, analysis and architecture, geomatics, change management, artificial intelligence, telecommunications and security.
Of the 28 applications received, the companies that scored at least 70% in the evaluation by a selection committee are being retained; a few were found not to meet the administrative requirements.
Among the qualified firms: CGI, Cofomo, Levio, Alithya, Groupe LGS, Fujitsu, Micro Logic, Idexia, Systematix, PricewaterhouseCoopers, Atos and others.
Each time the Service des technologies de l'information has a need, it will invite the qualified suppliers in the relevant field and award the contract to the lowest compliant bid.
The City will publish a new qualification notice each year for the next two years so that other companies can be added to the lists.
The City is filing with the council the lists of contracts and expenses authorized by its employees for the month of June 2026.
In June 2026, 176 contracts of more than $25,000 were awarded, for a total of $123,960,768.11.
Employees holding a delegation of authority approved $26,168,717.89 in expenses during the same month.
The filing also includes the lists of terminated contracts, of calls for tenders cancelled after the opening of bids, and of additional expenses made through change notices.
The amounts shown exclude taxes; the list of contracts of $25,000 and more is published on the City's website.
The City is granting an exemption for a planned apartment building at 200, 62e Rue Ouest, in Charlesbourg (Saint-Rodrigue district).
Three of the building's walls will be allowed to have less masonry than the required minimum of 70%: 40% for two walls and 30% for another.
In exchange, the walls facing 62e Rue Ouest and 1re Avenue will have to have at least 80% masonry.
The project calls for a multi-family building with 203 housing units, between the couvent des Pères Eudistes and a CHSLD (long-term care home).
The building will be set back 6 metres from the lot line on the CHSLD side to allow for planting vegetation.
The borough council is going against the opinion of the comité consultatif d'urbanisme (planning advisory committee), which recommended refusal on the grounds that a compliant project was feasible.
The City wants to monitor air quality across the whole territory of Québec, as part of its 2023-2027 action plan for good outdoor air quality.
It is authorizing a $450,000 expenditure and borrowing the same amount, repayable over five years.
The money will be used to buy sensors, samplers or analyzers, and to map and model air quality.
The amount also covers professional and technical services contracts, the purchase of goods and the hiring of staff.
An amount of $45,000 (10% of the expenditure) is taken from the general fund and will be paid back to it when the by-law comes into force.
The funds are provided for in years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The expenditure is shared between local jurisdiction and urban agglomeration jurisdiction.
The City is giving a grant to the Unité de loisir et de sport de la Capitale-Nationale for the « Mes Premiers Jeux » program in 2026.
The amount is $125 per activity held, up to a maximum of $12,000.
The program introduces young people aged 6 to 12 in the City's day camps to different sports, through workshops given by sports clubs from the area.
The money is used to support the clubs and associations that offer these introductory workshops.
The grant was $20,000 in 2025 (including an $8,000 increase) and $12,000 in 2024 and 2023.
According to the document, the program has got more than 128,000 young people moving since 2002.
The executive committee approved the decision on May 27, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0784).

The executive committee authorizes a third amendment to the financial assistance agreement signed in 2021 between the City, the Réseau de transport de la Capitale (RTC) and the Government of Québec for the TramCité tramway project.
Québec will pay $330,000,000 in cash, in a single payment, after the amendment is signed and no later than March 31, 2026.
The amendment sets out the payment rules for eligible expenses incurred as of April 1, 2026.
The cap on travel expenses rises from $107,000 to $138,000, and this cap does not apply to suppliers.
The amendment confirms that the maximum amount reimbursable to the RTC for planning and preparatory work is $944,379,095, plus fees and interest on long-term loans.
The amounts received will be used to reduce the temporary borrowings tied to the project's loan by-laws.
The City is selling a 5,844.7 m² piece of land in the Val-Bélair industrial park, along rue de l'Industrie, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The buyer is the company 9540-9751 Québec inc., represented by Tommy Ouellet, which is linked to Les Constructions T. Ouellet inc.
The price is $503,300 plus taxes, which works out to $86.11 per square metre; the money will go to the Fonds général.
The buyer has 24 months after the deed is signed to start building a building.
The project calls for a 2,337.8 m² building covering 20% of the land, a total investment of about $3.8M and the creation of 5 jobs.
The price matches the rate in effect when the transaction was concluded, on March 3, 2025, and not the rate applied since September 16, 2025.
The City is changing the development rules for the Chaudière area, in the Cap-Rouge neighbourhood, at the western end of the tramway route.

It is creating a "Corridor structurant" (structuring corridor) zone covering the area bounded roughly by avenue Le Gendre, avenue Blaise-Pascal, boulevard du Versant-Nord, rue William-Wood and boulevard de la Chaudière.

It is creating a "Conservation naturelle" (natural conservation) zone on seven lots covered by environmental compensation agreements, including a wetland, now listed as an area of ecological interest.
It adds specific rules for the Chaudière area concerning noise and nuisances linked to the highway and the railway, and changes the noise zones along the Félix-Leclerc and Duplessis highways.
This by-law replaces another one adopted in 2025, which was found not to comply with government directions in a letter from the Ministère des Affaires municipales dated May 28, 2025.
No public consultation is required, because this is a replacement by-law; final adoption is planned for the next meeting of the urban agglomeration council.
The area is to be covered by a special planning program (plan particulier d'urbanisme) aimed at creating a mixed and dense neighbourhood.
The City is cancelling the agreement signed on June 1, 2023, with Gestion Tremblay Légaré inc. (Canots Légaré).
That agreement provided for a grant of up to $50,000 to create a "Centre de location d'équipements nautiques" (water sports equipment rental centre).
The project never went ahead because the required permits were not obtained, which was a condition for receiving the money.
No money was paid to the company, and the grant will not be given to it.
The $50,000 purchase order is cancelled and the money is reallocated to the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030 fund.
The executive committee adopted the decision on June 10, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0781).
The City is hiring Placement Lavora inc. to temporarily recruit garbage collector helpers for waste collection, for an estimated amount of $448,040.97 (plus GST and QST).
The contract covers the period from October 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028.
These temporary employees will lend a hand during the seasonal collections of yard waste and leaves, in April-May and in October-November.
The net cost for the City is estimated at $470,387.00, spread over 2026 ($104,896.11), 2027 ($180,051.04) and 2028 ($185,439.85).
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 depend on the approval of those years' budgets.
Seven companies submitted bids; two were found to be non-compliant, and Placement Lavora offered the lowest compliant price.

The ministère de l'Environnement will pay up to $5,000,000 to the Ville de Québec to set up a Centre de valorisation des surplus de matériaux d'excavation et de traitement des sols contaminés (a centre for recovering surplus excavation materials and treating contaminated soil).
The centre will be set up at 791, rue Marius-Fortier, the former dépôt à neige Sérénité (snow dump), in the Beauport industrial park.
The site will be used to store, treat and reuse excavated materials, rather than sending them to private sites that are sometimes located outside the agglomeration.
Only materials from work done for the City will be received there, and they will be reused in City projects.
The grant will be paid in a single payment by March 31, 2026, and no later than 30 days after the agreement is signed.
The covered expenses include site preparation, a scale, a crusher, a screening system, storage cells, a retention basin and safety equipment.
The total financial assistance received for this project cannot exceed 80% of the eligible costs.

The City is merging two divisions of the Service des affaires juridiques: the Division du droit public and the Division du soutien aux projets stratégiques become the Division du droit public et des projets stratégiques.
Within this new division, it is creating a Section du soutien aux projets stratégiques, dedicated to supervising the team assigned to the tramway project.
Two division director positions are abolished, including that of director of public law, which becomes vacant on July 1, 2026, after the departure of the person who held it.
Kathy Lévesque is appointed director of the new division, keeping her current conditions.

The reorganization creates no net positions and requires no additional budget; the funds come from the department's operating budget and from the loan by-law for the structuring public transit network.
The executive committee adopted the decision on June 17, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0841).
The arrondissement des Rivières is changing its zoning for zone 22503Cb, south of boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, in the Duberger–Les Saules neighbourhood.
The change allows health care establishments without lodging (group P5), with a limit of 200 square metres of floor space per establishment.
The request comes from the owners of 2365, boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, who want to host professionals offering acupuncture services there.
Before the change, the zone allowed massage therapy but not health care establishments without lodging.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.

The conseil de quartier de Duberger–Les Saules must give its opinion and hold the public consultation meeting; interested people have seven days after that meeting to submit their comments in writing.
The City will not hold an active participation measure, considering that this is the addition of a use limited in area within a commercial setting.
The arrondissement de Beauport is giving out $33,375 in 11 grants to 9 organizations in the area.
The largest amounts go to Patro Le Pivot ($10,000 for the “Parcours patrimonial Montmorency” project and $1,396 for games), Club FADOQ Giffard ($7,782) and Gîte Jeunesse ($6,500).
Expression-Danse de Beauport receives $2,844 to redo its website, the Club de taekwon-do de Beauport $1,381, and the Club de Workout Beauport $965 for sound equipment.
The Conseil beauportois de la culture receives $754 for an outdoor sign; the Escadron 630 Rotary Beauport $753 for banners and a tent, and $500 for a team activity.
The Club de l'âge d'or Notre-Dame-de-l'Espérance receives $500 for a back-to-school party.
The applications had been submitted on June 15, 2026 under the programs of the Cadre de soutien aux organismes reconnus (support framework for recognized organizations).
The money comes from the operating budget of the arrondissement de Beauport.

The City is buying two properties in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge: 1015, boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest (1,635.1 m², from the Club de curling Jacques-Cartier) and 449, rue Curie (4,102.6 m², from the Club de curling Victoria de Québec).
The total consideration is $487,000, plus applicable taxes.

This amount breaks down as follows: up to $188,000 for the René-Lévesque property, up to $54,000 for the Curie property, up to $45,000 in legal fees to merge the two clubs into the Club multifonctionnel de curling de Québec, and $100,000 to each of the two clubs for a commitment to limit their activities.
The René-Lévesque property is being acquired to support the development of social and affordable housing; the Curie property will be added to the City's land reserve.
On the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll, the René-Lévesque property is valued at $1,285,000 and the Curie property at $1,015,000.

The City is setting aside $509,044.75 (net of taxes) for the transaction, including $324,864 through a loan by-law tied to the land reserve for social and affordable housing and $184,180.75 through Ten-Year Capital Works Program allocations.
The decision rests with the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The City is amending the zoning by-law of the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou for a single lot: 1059, avenue La Sarre, in the Vieux-Limoilou neighbourhood.
The owner demolished and rebuilt the rear vestibule of the building without authorization, and it does not respect the required side setback.
The change allows a side setback of at least 0.5 metre instead of 1.5 metres, which spares the owner from redoing the work.
The borough council will then be able to approve the construction plan for the building's enlargement, which aims to create a larger dwelling.
The conseil de quartier du Vieux-Limoilou will be consulted and will hold the public consultation meeting.
Interested persons will have seven days after that meeting to send their comments in writing.
The by-law contains no provision that can be subject to a referendum.
The City is entering into an agreement with Canadien National for the construction of an overpass (grade separation) in the area of rue Mendel, as part of the TramCité project.
The overpass will carry the tramway, a sidewalk and a bike path over a CN railway track, and will connect rue Mendel to boulevard du Versant-Nord.
CN will review the final plans, supervise the work and supply the railway signalling, for an estimated amount of $500,000 (plus GST and QST).
The City must pay CN a $500,000 deposit within 30 days of signing; final billing will be based on the actual costs at the end of the work.
The net expense for the City is estimated at $524,937.50, funded by two loan by-laws ($299,214.38 and $225,723.12).
The City is responsible for the costs of building and maintaining the overpass.
This agreement replaces the one signed with CN in 2023 (estimated at $410,000), which was terminated.
The City authorizes an expenditure of $1,250,000 to buy equipment, machinery and additional accessories for public works.
It is borrowing the same amount, repayable over five years.
The purchases will be used for work on and maintenance of the water and sewer systems as well as the roadways, throughout the city's territory and that of the urban agglomeration.
The City is taking $125,000 (10% of the expenditure) from its general fund, which will be reimbursed when the loan by-law comes into force.
