The amounts are planned from 2026 to 2030, at $250,000 per year, in the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The bill will be shared between local (proximity) jurisdictions and urban agglomeration jurisdictions according to the existing rules on mixed expenditures.
City council takes note of the 2025 annual report on drinking water management, filed as required by the Stratégie québécoise d'économie d'eau potable 2019-2025.

In 2025, the City distributed 84,213,328 m³ of water, including 273,698 m³ exported to Wendake; the rest was used in Québec, L'Ancienne-Lorette, Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures and Saint-Gabriel-de-Valcartier.
The volume distributed has dropped by 16.9% since 2006 (from about 102 to 84 million m³), while the population grew by 104,000 people.
Residential consumption is 204 litres per person per day, below the 220 target; water distributed per person is 363 litres per day, below the 458 target.
The leak index is 3.2 (target of 4.0 or less), compared with a provincial average of 5.4 in 2023.
Operating the water services cost $250,908,723 in 2025, or $2.99/m³; with the investment needs projected over 10 years, the cost rises to $5.11/m³.
The City must continue taking action by September 1, 2027, including raising public awareness and controlling leaks; the report still has to be approved by the ministère des Affaires municipales.

The City is amending the zoning by-law of the arrondissement de Beauport for 24 zones in the Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux and Chutes-Montmorency neighbourhoods, mainly outside the urbanization perimeter.
Zone boundaries are being redrawn to match the general land uses of the Plan directeur d'aménagement et de développement and the urbanization perimeter of the agglomeration's land use plan.
In nine zones (including 51003Fa, 51004Fa, 51005Fa, 51008Fa, 51012Fa, 51017Fa, 51019Fa, 51097Fa and 51104Ha), detached buildings will be allowed only one dwelling unit.
Low-odour livestock raising becomes permitted in zone 51016Aa, west of rue Sorbier, to allow a stable project.
A new mixed-use zone is created at 1620, boulevard Raymond to recognize the sale of used auto parts and accessories, and to allow other car-related uses there.
A new zone is created at 2101, boulevard Louis-XIV to recognize the residential use of the land.

The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; the conseils de quartier of Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux and Chutes-Montmorency will be consulted, with a public meeting and seven days after it to submit written comments.
The City is paying $240,000 to the Coopérative de solidarité en habitation de l'ARC for corrective work on the building at 1745, boulevard Louis-XIV.
The building is part of a 48-unit social and affordable housing project built in 2010 for self-sufficient seniors with low or modest incomes.
Construction defects were found in the first year; the corrective work costs $3,400,000 for the two buildings, including $1,699,985 for the one covered here.
The Coopérative recovered $1.7M from an out-of-court settlement with the contractor, an amount allocated to the other building.
CMHC is paying $359,985 and the Société d'habitation du Québec is granting an interest-free loan of $1.1M over 25 years.
The grant will be paid in a single payment after the work is completed, upon proof of expenses; the Coopérative will have to reimburse the City if it receives other compensation.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1467, tied to Québec's social housing development fund.
The City wants to allow housing to be built ("H1 housing" use) in zone 62223Mb, at 1200, avenue Lapierre, in the Saint-Émile neighbourhood.
The zone is located north of rue des Sommeliers, west of avenue Lapierre, east of rue de la Scierie and south of rue Lafond.
The maximum height of buildings would go up to 14 metres and the two-storey limit would be removed.
The required percentages of cladding materials (front wall and side wall) would be removed, as would the 3-metre limit between the front setback and the front wall.
Each housing unit would have to have 4 square metres of amenity area.
The owner of lot 6 600 532 is behind the request; the lot is affected by an Hydro-Québec easement.

The conseil de quartier de Saint-Émile would be consulted and would hold the public meeting; interested people would have 7 days after the meeting to submit their comments in writing, and the by-law may be subject to approval by referendum.
The Ville de Québec is entering into an agreement with Hydro-Québec to temporarily relocate an underground fibre optic cable at the intersection of rue Mendel and boulevard de la Chaudière.
This relocation is needed because Hydro-Québec's network is in the way of work on the future tramway (the TramCité project).
The City is paying the bill: $243,000 plus GST and QST, for an estimated net expense of $255,119.63.
The work includes engineering, dismantling 1,270 m of existing cable, installing 850 m of underground cable and 335 m of overhead cable, and then putting it into service.
Hydro-Québec is committing to finish this work before the end of November 2026.
The permanent cabling will be done later, after other preliminary work.
The agreement is being entered into without a call for tenders, an exception allowed by law for relocating the facilities of a public utility company.
The executive committee takes note of the report on transactions of the Fonds régions et ruralité (FRR) for the period from July 1 to September 30, 2025.
In total, $346,910 was committed during the quarter, including $150,000 to the Communauté métropolitaine de Québec for local and regional development agreements.
Le Monastère des Augustines receives $55,000 under the local societal projects component.

The VDAAA component distributes $64,480 among 10 organizations, including the Marché de solidarité régionale de Québec and Touski ($10,000 each), the Collectif Fardoche ($7,500), the SDC du Faubourg Saint-Jean ($6,850) and the Marché public de Cap-Rouge ($6,300).
An amount of $77,430 goes to the Collège d'enseignement général et professionnel de Victoriaville (city allocation and management fees).
Under the 2021-2025 agreement, the fund's balance reaches $639,950.05 as of September 30, 2025, notably after a return of $3,888 from the CRAAQ.
The City bought the Saint-Louis-de-Gonzague building, at 980, rue Richelieu (Vieux-Québec–Cap-Blanc–Colline parlementaire), and wants to resell it for a residential project.
In the meantime, the borough council is amending the planning by-law to allow offices to be set up there temporarily, including those of the Loisirs department and of the Jeux du Canada organization.

Other uses become permitted in the building: gathering places, cultural and heritage facilities, artists' studios, art galleries, exhibition halls, commercial parking and a fitness centre of 200 m² or less.
The permission lasts two years from the coming into force of the by-law; the City is aiming for occupancy until the spring of 2028.
Following the public consultation of March 9, 2026, the by-law specifies that no minimum number of parking spaces is required, since the current spaces are used by CHU staff.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to a referendum approval process.
The City is giving $150,469 to 16 organizations to run activities in parks and public squares from June 1 to September 28, 2026.
Of the 19 projects submitted, 16 were selected; the activities will take place in all six arrondissements.
The grants range from $6,000 (Commun'Action 0-5, parc Durocher) to $10,000 for several organizations.
Among the places where activities will be held: Passage Olympia, Place Limouloise, and parcs Jean-Paul-Nolin, Notre-Dame-de-Foy, Bardy, Durocher, Maria-Goretti, Sauvageau and Roger-Lemelin.
The announced activities include yoga, outdoor movies, circus, choral singing, nature workshops, puppets and board games, open to everyone and free of charge.
The organizations receiving support must follow a visibility protocol and submit a report on the activities and a financial report at the end of the project.
Last year, the same program awarded 15 grants totalling $137,055.
The City is giving $50,000 to five organizations to run intercultural activities in community gardens in 2026.
Each organization receives $10,000: Carrefour d'Action Interculturelle, Centre R.I.R.E. 2000, Craque-Bitume, Les Habitations du Centre multiethnique de Québec and R.A.F.A.L.
The projects take place mainly in La Cité-Limoilou (Vieux-Québec, Saint-Roch, Maizerets), with one in La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The funding covers the period from May 1 to November 30, 2026.
The subsidized activities must be offered free of charge and held within the territory of the city of Québec.
The funded organizations must test the City's intercultural activity tools and take part in support meetings.
The money comes from the agreement between the City and the ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration.
The City is appointing five trustees to represent it on the retirement committee of the Régime de retraite des cadres de la Ville de Québec.

The people appointed are Véronique Béland and Dominic Stephenson (human resources), Mario Blanchette (industrial projects and development), France Bilodeau (consultant) and Marie-Michelle Linteau (finance).
The term runs from February 25, 2026 to February 23, 2029.
These appointments replace the current terms, which end on February 25, 2026.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City confirms the June 18, 2026 decision authorizing the demolition of the heritage house at 1421, avenue des Grands-Pins, without adding any condition.
The former tenant had asked to delay the demolition in order to retrieve belongings left inside; the request is found admissible, but it is refused.
The City says it is up to the owner and the former tenant to come to an agreement between themselves about access to the building and the retrieval of personal effects.
The tenant was evacuated on an emergency basis on May 22, 2026 after a report of a dangerous structure, before the end of the lease, which was set for May 31, 2026.
The building, the maison Joseph-Noreau, is classified as being of superior heritage interest; it is now boarded up and the land is fenced off.

The expert assessments differ: the applicant's assessment puts the renovation at $1.59M and recommends demolition, while Tetra Tech's assessment estimates priority structural work at about $152,000 and considers rehabilitation feasible.
The demolition remains conditional on a replacement project, namely the construction of a new single-family home.
The City is refusing the request from the owner of 910-912, côte Bédard, in Notre-Dame-des-Laurentides (Charlesbourg), who wanted to keep the parking area as is.
The parking area extends 10 metres in front of the house's façade, while the Charlesbourg planning by-law allows a maximum of 3 metres.
The request followed an enlargement of the building and the addition of a second dwelling unit.
Reason for the refusal: the by-law does not cause serious harm to the owner, because a compliant parking area can be built without interfering with the enlargement.
According to the analysis, the rectangular lot, more than 31 metres wide, makes it possible to move the parking area to the side yard, which is more than 6 metres wide.
The planning advisory committee had unanimously recommended the refusal on March 4, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is authorizing an employee of the Service de la coordination stratégique et relations internationales to travel to Brussels from March 14 to 18, 2026.
She will represent the City at a meeting of the Steering Committee of the New Urban Project of the Organization of World Heritage Cities, on March 16 and 17.
The Organization of World Heritage Cities is paying for air travel, accommodation, meals and ground transportation.
The City is setting aside $200 for meal and ground transportation costs that are not covered, reimbursed upon submission of receipts (10% variance allowed).
This committee is preparing the New Urban Project, which aims to regenerate historic centres and will be presented at the Marrakech congress in October 2026.
The initial proposal must be reviewed by the Organization's board of directors in April 2026.
The City is amending the planning by-law for the arrondissement des Rivières to allow indoor and outdoor storage at 2156-2162, rue Cyrille-Duquet, in the Saint-Sauveur neighbourhood.
The City itself has been renting this entire building in the parc industriel Jean-Talon for about two years, under a ten-year lease, and has offices there (about 20 employees).

The authorization would bring into compliance the storage already taking place indoors (motorized equipment, furniture, event, audio and lighting equipment) and would allow outdoor storage for the equipment centre of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The outdoor storage would be in the back yard and in part of the side yard, surrounded by an opaque fence 2.0 metres high.
The permission would apply only to this lot (lot 1 737 227) and not to the whole of zone 22624Cc, where several other properties face rue Cyrille-Duquet.
The authorized occupancy would have to begin within two years after the by-law comes into force, otherwise the authorization lapses.
Before final adoption, the conseil de quartier de Saint-Sauveur would give its opinion and hold a public consultation meeting, followed by seven days to send in written comments.
The City is adjusting the pay of France Bilodeau, a consultant who has acted since 2016 as the employer-designated trustee on the City's pension committees.
Her attendance at pension committee meetings goes to $787.41 per half-day as of January 1, 2026, then $811.03 in 2027 and $835.36 in 2028.
This half-day amount also covers preparing for the meetings, her secretarial support and her office expenses (computer, internet, cell phone).
For any other pension-related work requested by Human Resources or Finance, her hourly rate is $112.49 in 2026, $115.86 in 2027 and $119.34 in 2028.
The adjustment is meant to give her the same economic increases as those granted to municipal employees, since her pay had not been adjusted as of January 1, 2026.
The executive committee adopted the decision on May 20, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0655).
The Ville de Québec is hiring Julie Marcotte as assistant director of the Service de police, reporting to the director of the Service de police.
Her annual salary is set at $200,553 (2026 salary scale for managers of the Direction générale and service directors).
The position was filled through internal/external competition CADRR-028-2026; until now she was an inspector with the Service de police de la Ville de Québec.
The contract is for an indefinite term: she must give 4 weeks' notice to leave, and the City must give 3 to 12 months' notice to end the employment.
She must devote all her time to her position and cannot work for anyone else.
The funds, including employee benefits, are provided for in the budget for organizational development and police affairs.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
A resident, Réjean Boivin, is asking the Commission de protection du territoire agricole du Québec (CPTAQ) for permission to use part of lot 6 699 193 for purposes other than agriculture.
The goal: to build a home along the rang Saint-Ange, in the Aéroport neighbourhood (Cap-Rouge–Laurentien district).
The area involved is 600 square metres (0.06 hectare), on a lot partially served by water and sewer services.
The City's analysis concludes that there will be little or no impact on farming activities: several houses are already nearby, and a railway line separates the lot from the land under cultivation.
The City recommends supporting the request before the CPTAQ; the decision rests with city council.
The City is signing an agreement with Camaco inc. for soil decontamination work at 500, rue Saint-François Est, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The contamination goes down to 6 metres and runs under City water and sewer pipes, which will have to be dismantled and then replaced.
Camaco inc. is paying for all the work: the City is not putting in any money.
The company will be allowed to temporarily occupy part of rue Saint-François Est and rue du Roi, next to the building.
The work must start no later than July 15, 2026 and be finished no later than October 15, 2026, unless the City grants an extension.
Camaco inc. must provide a bank guarantee of $150,000.00 and civil liability insurance of at least $3,000,000.00.
The new pipes and equipment will be transferred to the City free of charge, once the work is accepted by the Service de l'ingénierie.
The Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is giving $100 to the Chœur de La Cité, a non-profit amateur vocal ensemble.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, out of the funds set aside to support borough councils.
The request came from councillor Catherine Vallières-Roland.
The choir, active since 2005, is based at the loisirs Saint-Sacrement (1360, boulevard De l'Entente) and brings together about fifty singers.
In its letter, the organization explains that its members' fees cover about two thirds of its annual budget.
The borough council adopted the decision (resolution CA1-2026-0105).
The City is granting a minor exemption for 8805, boulevard Mathieu, in the quartier des Jésuites in Charlesbourg.
The rear setback of the enlarged building may be 4.5 metres instead of the 7.5 metres required by the planning by-law.
The purpose of the enlargement is to adapt the house to the owner's rehabilitation needs, based on the recommendations of their health care professional.
The work provides for larger circulation spaces, indoor stairs and a hallway connecting the garage to the dwelling.
According to the analysis, the enlargement is being done in the rear yard and the planned attached garage complies with the regulations.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on January 7, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is authorizing a $12,550,000 expense to buy vehicles and motorized equipment for the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
It is borrowing the same amount, repayable over 10 years, with general revenues of the urban agglomeration set aside for payment.
The money will also be used to modify and upgrade vehicles, to pay for professional and technical services contracts, and to hire the necessary staff.
The purchases are for additional vehicles, made necessary by the creation of new units and the addition of responsibilities, and to meet the requirements of the Schéma de couverture de risques.
The vehicles covered include electric or hydrocarbon-powered vehicles, utility vehicles, cars, pickup trucks, vans, light and heavy trucks, trailers and accessories.
An amount of $1,255,000 (10% of the expense) is being taken from the general fund, which will be replenished when the by-law comes into force.
The funds are planned from 2026 to 2030 in the 2026-2035 capital works program, and the project covers the entire territory under the city's jurisdiction.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 1131, boulevard Pie-XI Sud, in the Val-Bélair neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The exemption allows the construction of two multi-unit residential buildings as part of an integrated development project, on a small lot.
The building fronting boulevard Pie-XI Sud may be 4.45 m from the right side lot line and 8.12 m from the left side lot line, instead of the required 10 m.
The green area between the parking lot and the building at the back of the lot may be only 1.48 m deep, instead of the required 6 m.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on March 25, 2026.
A right-of-way easement will allow travel through the existing access lane on the neighbouring lot, since the lot cannot be merged with the integrated development project already built.
The City is awarding P.E. Pageau inc. the 2026 repair work on bike paths and pedestrian links, for $350,339.50 (plus GST and QST).

The work involves the bike path on boulevard Lebourgneuf (from autoroute Robert-Bourassa to boulevard Pierre-Bertrand) and the one on rue Clémenceau (from avenue Saint-David to avenue du Bourg-Royal).
It also involves boulevard du Versant-Nord (from avenue Montbray to rue de Port-Royal) and the Rivière Saint-Charles path (from rue des Embarcations to parc Gilles-Lamontagne).
Depending on the area, the roadway, the base and the paving are redone, or the existing paving is removed and new paving is laid.
Five companies submitted bids, all compliant; prices ranged from $350,339.50 to $634,085.00, against a City estimate of $746,041.50.
The net expense for the City comes to $367,812.68, taken from the public works bike path maintenance budget.
The executive committee adopted the decision on June 10, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0779).
ExpoCité will receive up to $85,000 from the Tourism Industry Association of Canada to fund an activity tied to the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
The "Canada Celebrates" activity will take place on Sunday, June 21, 2026, in Québec, as a travelling event caravan tied to the FIFA trophy tour.
The grant is divided into $50,000 for hosting costs and $35,000 for administration, coordination, staff and event production (rental, fencing, portable toilets, etc.).
ExpoCité must include local artists and food vendors, reach out to under-represented groups, and provide signage, promotion and emergency services in French and English.
ExpoCité must have its health, safety and emergency plans approved by local authorities.
The agreement covers the period from March 23, 2026 to March 31, 2027; any amount received above the actual costs will have to be repaid.

The City's executive committee is ratifying the agreement already signed by the chair of ExpoCité's executive committee and its director; the contract is written in English only, since it was entered into outside Québec.
The City wants to obtain a permanent easement over part of a lot bordering 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The easement covers about 59.40 square metres and will be used to move conduits and public utility networks.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement or, failing an agreement, by expropriation; the owner has already been notified of the process.
The Service des affaires juridiques will be able to drop the expropriation proceedings if the project no longer needs the easement.
The entire lot is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $575,000, or $461.25 per square metre.
The money comes from the agglomeration loan by-law for building the structuring public transit network.

The Ville de Québec is joining the insurance program of the Union des municipalités du Québec (UMQ), which protects elected officials and senior officers against defamation, harassment and hateful remarks.
The coverage runs from March 31, 2026 to March 30, 2031, that is, five years.
The City is appointing the UMQ as its agent: the UMQ will issue the public call for tenders and sign the insurance contract on behalf of the group of municipalities.
The insurance covers up to $50,000 per municipality per event, with a $200 deductible per insured person per event.
The insurance is used to put a stop to the targeted actions or remarks (demand letter, injunction, out-of-court settlement); damages are not covered.
The insured person must notify the insurer within 15 days of the alleged facts, and may choose their own lawyer with the insurer's agreement.
The director of the Service des approvisionnements is authorized to sign the contract; the expenses will be approved later.
The City is providing up to $20,311 to the Centre d'action bénévole de Québec for 2026-2027.
The money funds the Gouvernance inclusive project, which aims to make more room for people with an immigrant background on the boards of directors of non-profit organizations.
The project plans to raise awareness among boards of directors and give them tools, and to prepare immigrants to sit on them.
The grant covers the hiring of staff, the creation of tools and the organization of activities, from July 2026 to March 2027.

Half of the funding comes from an agreement with the ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration ($10,000) and half from the budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire ($10,311).
The organization will have to report each year and mention the contribution of the City and the ministère in its publications.
The Ville de Québec is awarding Tétra Tech QI inc. (boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, Québec) professional services for the HydroWeb portal and the CSoft overflow control software.
The contract runs from May 1 to December 31, 2026, for an estimated amount of $213,000 (plus GST and QST); the net expense is estimated at $223,623.38.
The agreement can be renewed twice for 12 months, with an annual adjustment based on the Consumer Price Index.
HydroWeb is used to monitor rain gauges, control the rivière Lorette, track wastewater overflows and make decisions about swimming at the Baie de Beauport and the plage Jacques-Cartier.
The CSoft component deals with the effect of development projects on the wastewater system, the reduction of overflows and the remaining capacity of the interceptor sewers.
No call for tenders was held: the law allows this when the contract stems from existing software, in this case developed by Tétra Tech QI inc.
The contract follows the previous agreement, which ended on December 31, 2025.
The City is tightening its construction rules for steep slopes and the areas next to them, across its entire territory.
Adding a housing unit in an accessory building (such as a garden house) becomes prohibited in any steep slope and any area next to a steep slope.
Recreational trails (mountain biking, downhill skiing) become permitted in these areas, if they are linked to a park, a regional recreational facility or a conservation area.
These trails require a geotechnical expert report on soil stability and a report on erosion and water runoff, plus a certificate of authorization.
The ban on using machinery weighing more than 0.50 tonne is extended to the top of slopes, unless an engineer certifies that the soil is stable.
Fill or excavation of up to 0.30 metre is no longer allowed in a steep slope, only in the areas next to it.
A public consultation meeting must be held; the by-law is not subject to a referendum.
The City is authorizing a firefighter-manager from the Service de protection contre l'incendie to travel to Vancouver from September 19 to 23, 2026.

On the agenda: the annual strategic planning meeting of the Fire Service Women network, a professional development day on leadership for women chiefs and officers, then the Fire Rescue Canada 2026 conference.
The City is paying for transportation and meals, up to $2,000, upon submission of receipts.
Registration fees are paid by the Association canadienne des chefs de pompiers through the WAGE organization; the planning meeting receives support from Femmes et Égalité des genres Canada.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de protection contre l'incendie, under the "Offrir de la formation" activity.
An overrun of no more than 10% of the authorized amount is accepted without further authorization.
The executive committee adopted the decision on August 19, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-1070).
Trudel Innovation inc. is giving the City, free of charge, a 261.0 square metre piece of land (lot 6 697 588) in the îlot Dorchester, in the Saint-Roch neighbourhood.
This transfer is the mandatory contribution for parks and green spaces tied to the subdivision of lot 6 692 672, where the company wants to develop a residential project.
The area transferred is equal to 10% of the land subject to the contribution.
The City says it wants to add greenery to this almost entirely paved-over space and improve the supply of parks in the area.
The transfer is a condition that must be met before the subdivision plan can be approved.
The executive committee was to decide on March 25, 2026.

The City is cancelling the authorization that allowed the Réseau de transport de la Capitale (RTC) to permanently occupy part of the public domain within the right-of-way of boulevard Laurier, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The space involved is 100.6 square metres and was used for a heated Métrobus station.
This station has already been demolished for the preparatory work on the TramCité project, now underway on boulevard Laurier.
The station will not be rebuilt: boulevard Laurier will be served by the tramway.
The City wants the boulevard Laurier right-of-way to be free of any occupancy for the project.
The city clerk will draft the notice of revocation and have the entry struck from the land register.
The owner has been informed of the process and of a contact person at the City.
The City is giving out $87,500 in grants to 27 professional artists through the "Le Levier" program.
Individual amounts range from $1,500 to $4,000, for projects such as exhibitions, albums, films, shows and writing.
Of the 51 applications submitted, 47 were eligible and 27 were selected, or 57%.
Applications were turned down because the applicant was not eligible, the expenses were not eligible, the project was already supported by the City, or the application was incomplete.
The program has an annual budget of $175,000, with application deadlines on May 1 and December 1.
The three streams offer up to $1,500 (Circuler), $2,500 (Écrire and Développer) and $5,000 (Concrétiser).
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3073 tied to the Visions culturelles.
The Ville de Québec is giving out 16 grants totalling a maximum of $61,680 to organizations for the Semaine d'actions contre le racisme et pour l'égalité des chances, from March 19 to 31, 2027.
This is the first time the City is marking this theme week on its territory.
The money comes from the agreement between the City and the ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI), valid from April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2027.
Of the 21 projects submitted in response to the call for projects launched in June 2026, 16 were selected after scoring 50/100 or more on the evaluation grid.
The amounts range from $2,750 to $5,000 per organization, including 24H ChronoSports, Métissage Québec, the Carrefour Jeunesse-Emploi Chauveau and the CLAR 03 ($5,000 each).
The projects involve, among others, La Cité-Limoilou, Beauport, Charlesbourg, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, Vanier, Saint-Roch and Saint-Sauveur.

The organizations must display the contribution of the City and the MIFI, list their activities in the official calendars, and submit a report on their activities and a financial report at the end of the project.
The City is giving $100,000 in grants to two short-film production companies, as part of the call for projects of March 27, 2026.
VF2 Productions inc. receives $50,000 for the fiction short film "Deus ex machina".
Les Productions Unstandard inc. receives $50,000 for the fiction-animation short film "La Mort a déjà valsé".
Six projects were submitted and found eligible; two were selected.
The money comes in equal parts from the City ($50,000) and the ministère de la Culture et des Communications ($50,000).

The companies must start production no later than the calendar year following the grant, display the visibility of the City and the ministère, and submit a report and an audited statement of costs no later than 3 months after completion.
Payments are made in three stages: 50% on signing, 40% at the start of filming, and the balance after the final documents are submitted.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 524, rue Franklin, in the Saint-Sauveur neighbourhood (Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The exemption allows a built lot and a vacant lot to be merged to form the new lot 6 710 979.
The ground floor occupancy percentage is accepted at 17% instead of the 35% required by the borough's planning by-law.
The owner will be able to set up a play area and a vegetable garden; most of the current parking area will be removed and turned back into greenery.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the application on May 26, 2026 (opinion CCU1-2026-039).
An exemption had already been granted on August 18, 2025 for the addition of a storey exceeding the prescribed height.
The executive committee takes note of the report on transactions of the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale (Vision entrepreneuriale) for the period from April 1 to June 30, 2025.

The fund spent $40,712 on City activities: an entrepreneurship event on June 4, 2025, professional fees (Aviseo Conseil, Chambre de commerce et d'industrie de Québec) and the launch of the Vision entrepreneuriale 2030.
Amounts committed to projects that were not carried out or that have been completed are returned to the fund, for a total of $1,606,663.
The largest returns come from the Institut national d'optique ($1,000,000), Solutions zéro déchet Fillgood ($250,000), La Maison Orphée ($118,391) and Automatisation JRT ($95,744).
Balances are also returned by the SDC Montcalm and Saint-Sauveur, the Pharmacie Gélinas and Kimpton du Vieux-Québec, and Québec International.
The fund's balance goes from $1,844,988.30 as at March 31, 2025 to $3,410,939.30 as at June 30, 2025.

The arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge is putting back in place architectural criteria for three zones along avenue Myrand, between chemin Sainte-Foy and boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest (quartier de la Cité-Universitaire, district Saint-Louis–Sillery).
These criteria had been adopted in April 2025, then deleted by mistake in June 2025 during another regulatory change.
To obtain a building permit for a main building in these zones, site planning and architectural integration plans will have to be approved.

The plans will have to, among other things, highlight street corners, fit in with neighbouring buildings, include balconies or setbacks on the façade, and landscape the front margin (greenery for residential use, hard surfaces and vegetation for commercial use).
Applicants will also have to provide a colour image of the proposed building and of the neighbouring buildings.
The scope of the criteria stays the same as before; the conseil de quartier de la Cité-Universitaire will be consulted and will hold the public meeting.
A neighbouring zone (32710Mb) falls under the city council and is covered by a separate by-law.
The City is adding mandatory stop signs on avenue Roland-Beaudin, at the intersection with the north entrance to the Marché public de Sainte-Foy.
Drivers and cyclists will have to stop at the north and south approaches to this intersection.
The area affected is avenue Roland-Beaudin, between chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois and route de l'Église, in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge (district du Plateau).
The measure is meant to allow pedestrians to cross the street to reach the Marché public de Sainte-Foy and the Centre de glaces Intact Assurance, where no crossing facilities existed.
Residents and the conseil de quartier had asked for these stop signs; a traffic count was carried out at the intersection.
According to the document, this change makes the avenue safer until work on the tramway begins.
The City is appointing four trustees to represent it on the pension committee of the Régime de retraite des employés manuels de la Ville de Québec.
The people named are Dominic Stephenson and Marie-Josée Drouin (Service des ressources humaines), France Bilodeau (consultant) and Anne Mainguy (Service des finances).
Their term runs from February 25, 2026 to February 23, 2029.
These appointments replace the previous terms, which ended on February 25, 2026.
The pension plan's by-law requires the City to name four trustees, for terms that are normally three years.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City approves part of the request for a minor exemption for the expansion of a building located at 4137-4141, rue des Martinets, in the Orsainville neighbourhood (Charlesbourg).
Balconies will be allowed to extend 3.2 metres into the front and rear setbacks, instead of the maximum of 2.0 metres set out in the planning by-law.
However, the City refuses to remove the requirement to increase the side setback by 3.0 metres, which would bring the required setback to 7.5 metres instead of the 4.82 metres proposed.
Reasons for the refusal: a project that complies with the rules is still possible, and the exemption could interfere with the neighbours' enjoyment of their property.
The expansion project aims to add six housing units to the building, for a total of 18 units.
The neighbouring house is a one-storey single-family home; two balconies planned in the side yard would be 3.3 metres from the property line.

The City is sending two employees from the Service de la planification de l'aménagement et de l'environnement to the EuroMAB 2026 conference, in Parksville, British Columbia, from September 14 to 19, 2026.
It will reimburse up to $7,460 in total (about $3,730 per person) for airfare, ground transportation, accommodation, meals and registration, upon submission of supporting documents.
A difference of up to 10% of the authorized amount will be accepted without further authorization.
The trip depends on obtaining UNESCO Biosphere Region status, with an answer expected during the week of June 1, 2026; if not, the trip will be cancelled.
The plane tickets and the hotel will be booked before UNESCO's decision, with conditions allowing cancellation.
The City submitted its Biosphere Region application on January 30, 2025; it would become the 20th in Canada and the 5th in Québec.
The arrondissement de Beauport is paying $4,310.92 to three organizations for the activities of the Semaine de relâche 2026 (spring break week), held from February 28 to March 8.
The Groupe d'éducation et d'écosurveillance de l'eau (G3E) receives $1,793.53, Croque ton quartier $517.39 and Patro Le Pivot $2,000.
The G3E held a coureurs des bois olympics and a winter bird-watching hike at the Centre de plein air de Beauport.
Croque ton quartier organized three active walks at the Espace collectif Croque ton quartier on March 3, 4 and 6.
Patro Le Pivot held a winter festival at parc Montmorency and a mini-putt on snow at parc Royal.
The activities have already taken place; the money comes from the arrondissement's operating budget.
Last year, the same three organizations shared $4,400 for the 2025 spring break.
The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing $5,600,000 in architectural work on buildings, plants and water treatment facilities.
The City is borrowing the same amount, repayable over 15 years.
The work covered includes construction, renovation, repair, demolition, decontamination, lighting and landscaping, as well as the purchase of furniture and specialized equipment.
The by-law also allows the City to hire staff, award professional services contracts (surveying, engineering, architecture) and acquire buildings and easements.
The work may take place anywhere in the territory under urban agglomeration jurisdiction.
The City is committing $560,000 from the general fund before the by-law comes into force, which is 10% of the expenditure; this fund will be reimbursed afterwards.
The funds are provided for in years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The City wants to change the zoning at 3500, boulevard Neilson (Saint-Louis neighbourhood, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough) to allow a real estate project.
The owner wants to demolish a single-family house and a 12-unit building in order to build a single 58-unit building of six storeys.
The change raises the maximum height from five to six storeys, reduces the front setback from 8 to 6 metres and the rear setback from 15 to 10 metres.
The storeys above the fourth will have to be set back 5 metres on the northwest side, where the property borders low-density residential zones.
Lot 1 661 931 moves from zone 33003Ha to zone 33008Hb so that the whole project is in the same zone.
The by-law may be subject to approval by referendum; the conseil de quartier de Saint-Louis will hold a public consultation meeting, followed by seven days to send in written comments.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council approves three permit applications assessed on their appearance and how well they fit in with the surrounding area (PIIA).
Green light for the construction of a detached multi-unit building at 1447 to 1461, avenue Bardy.
Green light for changing the exterior siding of a detached single-unit house at 1560, avenue Champfleury.
Green light for the construction of a detached building at 2265, boulevard Henri-Bourassa.
These approvals follow the favourable recommendations made by the comité consultatif d'urbanisme at its meeting of April 28, 2026.
The document does not anticipate any financial impact for the City.
The City is giving $4,500 to the organization Santé Urbanité and providing it with free municipal services worth up to $5,000, for a total of $9,500.
This support is for holding the 5th edition of the "Ça roule Doc!" event, on September 26, 2026, at Université Laval and on the surrounding streets.
The event is free: a 12 km bike ride to the plaines d'Abraham (round trip) and a 3 km walk on the campus, to promote active and public transportation.
The services provided in kind take the form of work time and equipment loans normally billed by the City's Service de police.
The $4,500 grant represents 8.2% of the event's planned budget, estimated at $54,600, and will be paid in a single payment within 10 days after the agreement is signed.

The support is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners; the organization must take out $5,000,000 in civil liability insurance and submit a report before the end of December 2026.
The City is giving $4,000 to the winner of the Prix de la poésie Jean-Noël-Pontbriand 2026. Université Laval is adding $1,000, for a total award of $5,000.
The City is also giving $5,000 to the winner of the Prix reconnaissance de la bande dessinée 2026, awarded together with the organization Québec BD.
Both prizes are for creators from the city of Québec, including Wendake; the comics prize goes to a comic book artist who is still active, for their entire career.
Juries choose the winners, whose names stay secret until the announcement.
The announcement takes place on March 24, 2026, in the presentation hall of the bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy, during the awarding of the Prix littéraire de la Ville de Québec.
The $9,000 comes from the operating budget of the Service de la culture et du patrimoine (activity related to the library network).
The arrondissement de Beauport is amending its planning by-law for zone 52106Ip, at 430, rue Ardouin (quartier 5-2, district de la Chute-Montmorency–Seigneurial).
The change allows a polyethylene sheet or another flexible material to be used as the exterior covering of a storage building.
Hydro-Québec wants to install an 18.28 m by 18.28 m (60 ft by 60 ft) mega-dome in the parking area, on the rue Fichet side.
The dome would shelter a tracked vehicle with an insulated mast, a piece of equipment that cannot stay outside in winter.
Before the amendment, flexible materials were allowed only for the storage of bulk materials (type E), not for this type of equipment.
The by-law contains no provision subject to approval by referendum; a public consultation meeting is planned.
The Ville de Québec will pay a grant of up to $1,400,000 to Québec International for its operations and mission in 2026.
The money will be used to pay the organization's administrative costs, rent and certain support salaries.
The grant is split into two parts: $1,000,000 from Government of Québec funds managed by the City, and $400,000 from the budget of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets.
The project costs a total of $1,773,660; private partners are adding $373,660 in cash.
Québec International works to attract talent, international students and foreign investment, and to support exporting and innovation in the region.
The City will track the project's results using an economic benefits form.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The Ville de Québec is paying out $575,000 in grants to five production companies for films and series shot mainly in the Capitale-Nationale region.

The money goes to Parallaxes ($145,000) for "Farador, la série", Maxel Films ($130,000) for "Ce qui demeure", Taïga Média ($100,000) for "Ulaval, l'histoire continue", Frangine 01 ($100,000) for "Point tournant 2" and Groupe Fovéa ($100,000) for "Chilleurs".
The money comes from three sources: the City ($250,000), the ministère de la Culture et des Communications ($200,000) and the Secrétariat à la Capitale-Nationale ($125,000).
Ten projects were submitted in the call for projects of March 27, 2026; eight were eligible and five were chosen.
On average, the producers expect 90% local labour and $5,935,654 in local spending.
Each company must begin its production no later than the calendar year following the awarding of the grant, and must pay back any unused amount.
The productions must display the visibility of the City and of the two government partners in their communications and in the credits.

The City is hiring Modellium inc. (Québec) to provide support and maintenance for the G+ and V+ software packages, which are used for municipal property assessment (updating and equalizing the assessment roll).
The contract runs from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2030 and is estimated at $2,124,700, plus GST and QST.
The net cost to the agglomeration is estimated at $2,230,669.40, spread over four years: $528,927.02 in 2027, $547,719.79 in 2028, $567,037.48 in 2029 and $586,985.11 in 2030.
The contract is being awarded directly, without a call for tenders, because Modellium designed the software packages and holds an exclusive right to them.
The contract includes an annual bank of 600 hours for work not covered by the support service.
The City can drop the self-declaration module as of January 1, 2029 if it makes a written request before November 1, 2028, which would lower the annual price by 6%.
The amounts remain conditional on the adoption of the 2027 to 2030 budgets.
The Ville de Québec is hiring Dominic Côté as assistant director – operations and operational development for the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
His annual salary is set at $193,620 (2026 scale) and he will report to the director of the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
The contract is for an indefinite term: the employee must give 4 weeks' notice to leave, and the City must give 3 to 12 months' notice depending on seniority.
The City may allow him to use an unmarked vehicle belonging to the Service, given the requirement to respond quickly outside normal working hours.
Until now he held the position of division chief of operations in the same service; the position was filled through internal/external competition CADRR-013-2026.
The funds come from the fire protection budget; the decision falls to the Québec urban agglomeration council.
The Charlesbourg conseil d'arrondissement grants a minor exemption for 5114, rue des Écureuils, in the quartier d'Orsainville.
The house and shed already built on the lot are deemed to comply, even though they do not meet the distances required by the planning by-law.

The following are accepted: a front setback of 3.8 m instead of 5 m, side yards of 6.2 m instead of 7 m, a rear setback of 2.3 m instead of 10 m, a porch and stairs encroaching by 2.9 m instead of 2 m, and a shed at 0.2 m instead of 0.75 m.
The house was built in 1958 or earlier; the discrepancy was discovered during a real estate transaction.
The lot is 205 square metres with a depth of 13.72 metres, which makes it impossible to meet the required setbacks according to the City's analysis.
No complaints were made by neighbours; the comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on January 7, 2026.
The City is authorizing 21 members of city council to attend the Sommet électoral 2026 of the Union des municipalités du Québec, on September 18, 2026, at the Centre des congrès de Québec.
The event deals with municipal issues in the campaign for the provincial elections of October 5, with the leaders of Quebec's political parties.
The City is paying or reimbursing the $150 registration fee (plus taxes) per elected official, for a total of $3,650 taxes included.
It is also reimbursing up to $600 in expenses, including parking, upon presentation of supporting documents.
The total bill comes to $4,250, taken from the city council's operating budget.
An overrun of no more than 10% of the authorized amount is accepted without further authorization.
The Ville de Québec is giving $35,000 to the Maison de Lauberivière to continue its street brigade project in 2026.
The brigade brings together an average of three people who use Lauberivière's services; they clean up around the shelter, pick up garbage and remind people to smoke in the designated areas.
Participants act as volunteers and receive a daily allowance; in 2026, these allowances will be adjusted to line up with other comparable projects in the area.
Participants are supervised by the staff of Lauberivière's day centre, located at 485, rue du Pont.
The grant is higher than in previous years: $25,000 in 2025, $16,500 in 2024, and $25,000 from 2021 to 2023.
The organization will have to mention the City's contribution in its publications and submit a report on its activities and a financial report.
The executive committee adopted the decision on April 1, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0424).
The Ville de Québec will pay up to $75,000 to the non-profit organization Socialim to prepare a social and affordable housing project at 8190-9120, avenue du Zoo.
The planned project includes 64 housing units (phase 3 of the avenue du Zoo area).
The money is for start-up costs: environmental assessments, soil tests, title searches, surveying, land appraisal, architect's sketches and the developer's fees.
Socialim has six months after the agreement is signed to use the grant, and 12 months to submit its project to an assistance program recognized by the City.
Only expenses billed after March 31, 2026 are eligible, and the grant is reduced if the organization receives other assistance for the same costs.
The amount will be deducted from the City's contribution if the project is later accepted into an assistance program.
The City is giving $5,000 to the Regroupement pour l'aide aux itinérants et itinérantes de Québec (RAIIQ) to organize "La nuit des sans-abri."
The event, the 37th edition, will take place on October 16, 2026 in downtown Québec.
The amount is double that of the two previous years, which was $2,500 each time.
The extra money will be used to add entertainment: karaoke and artistic activities.
Community organizations will offer food and warm clothing on site.
The RAIIQ will have to mention the City's contribution in its publications and submit a report on its activities and finances.
The City is transferring $4,000,000 from its unallocated surpluses to a reserve dedicated to buying and taking back land.
This $4,000,000 is then made available to be spent, through the 2026-2035 capital works program (record 32002).
The money will be used to buy land for industrial, municipal and other purposes, and to take back land sold by the City when the buyer did not meet its obligation to build.
The City says it wants to rebuild its reserve of industrial land, otherwise it lacks land to meet demand.
The stated goal: to fund these purchases without borrowing.
The reserve has existed since 2019 and has already been topped up several times ($25M in 2019, $15M in 2020, $5M in 2022, $10M in 2025).
City council adopted the decision on June 16, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is appointing Dominic Gaudreau as director of the Service de police and is approving his employment contract.
His annual salary is set at $235,893, based on the 2026 salary scale for service directors.
Until now, he held the position of assistant director of territorial surveillance at the Service de police.
He was selected following an internal/external competition (CADRR-010-2026) and will report to the Deputy Director General – Aménagement, mobilité et sécurité urbaine.
The contract is for an indefinite term: he may leave with 4 weeks' notice, and the City must give him between 3 and 12 months' notice depending on his years of service.
The contract prohibits him from working for anyone else during his term.
The necessary funds, including employee benefits, are already provided for in the Service de police's budget.
The City is creating a new zone (52122Mb) out of the part of zone 52105Ia located west of rue Fichet, in the parc industriel de Beauport.
In this new zone, administrative services, retail sales and services, as well as gathering places become permitted; the other standards stay the same.
The request comes from the owner of 575, rue Clemenceau (Immeubles Tondreau), who says he has lost value and potential tenants since the zoning review of December 2024.
These same uses had been removed from the zone in December 2024 during the zoning review of the parc industriel de Beauport.
The affected area is in quartier 5-2, district de la Chute-Montmorency–Seigneurial, near rue Seigneuriale.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; a public consultation meeting will be held, followed by seven days to send written comments.

The Ville de Québec is authorizing spending of $22,500,000 for work at the Centre de récupération de la matière organique of the Complexe de valorisation énergétique and at the sludge treatment plant.
The work also involves the incinerator and the steam delivery infrastructure (ducts, tunnels, walkways, pipe supports, electrical equipment).
The City is borrowing the same amount, repayable over 15 years, out of the agglomeration's general revenues.
An amount of $2,250,000 (10% of the spending) is taken from the general fund before the by-law comes into force, and will be paid back to that fund afterwards.
The funds are planned for the years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 capital works program (sheet 46006).
If work reduces treatment capacity, the City will be able to use hauling, transloading or landfilling of the materials.
The division of jurisdictions for sheet 46006 adopted in December 2025 is amended.
The City is banning parking at all times on the east side of rue Francheville, between boulevard des Chutes and avenue du Sous-Bois (Beauport, district de la Chute-Montmorency-Seigneurial).
On that same stretch, it is marking out a safety zone 2 metres wide: a virtual sidewalk outlined by pavement markings.
The parking ban on the west side, between boulevard des Chutes and côte d'Azur, is being removed, which frees up 43 spaces.
Removing parking on the east side means a loss of 109 spaces.
According to the document, the street has no sidewalk at all and the parking occupancy rate there is moderate or low.
These changes are temporary, pending the construction of a real sidewalk.

The executive committee takes note of the quarterly report on real estate transactions from the Service du développement économique et des grands projets, for the period from October 1 to December 31, 2025.
The report lists land purchases, easements and compensation paid to owners, with the date, the lot and the amount of each transaction.
Several transactions relate to the tramway project (TramCité), in particular expropriation compensation on boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, chemin Sainte-Foy and avenue Lavigerie.
Among the amounts listed: $61,343 (avenue des Érables), $44,009 (René-Lévesque Ouest), $21,500 (René-Lévesque Ouest), $9,436 (avenue Lavigerie) and $6,900 (chemin Sainte-Foy).

Other transactions involve easements for Hydro-Québec, Bell Canada and Énergir, a bus shelter slab for the RTC on chemin Sainte-Foy, and an acquisition linked to the enhancement of the rivière du Cap Rouge.
The filing of this report is required by a City by-law.
The Ville de Québec will pay up to $150,000 to the company Bia formations inc., whose head office is in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The money will be used to test the "Bia Assistant," a decision-support tool for health professionals, with Groupes de médecine de famille (GMF).
The project costs $405,000 in total: $150,000 from the City, $55,000 from the company, $100,000 from a line of credit and $100,000 from a funding round.
The grant is a non-repayable contribution, capped at 50% of eligible expenses.
The company has 7 jobs and plans to create 6 new ones.
The funds come from the Capitale-Innovation component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, funded by the gouvernement du Québec.
The decision rests with the urban agglomeration council of Québec; a review committee gave a favourable opinion on March 10, 2026.
The City will pay $858,376 to the organization Capitale Nature to purchase 20 lots totalling 206.5 hectares.
These lots are located in the watersheds of the drinking water intakes of the rivière Saint-Charles, Charlesbourg and Beauport.
The project costs $4.3M in total; the rest comes from other funders.
Capitale Nature will become the owner of the lots and will pay the management and stewardship costs on its own.
The lots must be used only for conservation; any change of use requires the City's written consent.
The agreement provides a right of access to the lots for citizens and for the City.
The money comes from a loan by-law and will be paid in a single payment within 60 days of signing.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 2006, chemin de la Canardière, in the Maizerets neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The exemption allows a 3rd customer parking space to be set up along 18e Rue, as part of the expansion of the building that will house the Centre de pédiatrie sociale de Québec.
Two standards are being relaxed: 3 metres between two parking access lanes instead of 7.5 metres, and 5 metres between the street access and the intersection instead of 6 metres.
According to the City's analysis, the space serves to make it easier for parents with children to reach the clinic, and about 75% of the unregulated on-street parking in the area is already occupied.
A lease for the occupancy of public property will be signed between the City and the clinic for the parking spaces, a play area and the gallery within the street right-of-way.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 7, 2026, and the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec did as well.
The Ville de Québec is awarding 8348871 Canada inc. (Terapro Construction), of Lévis, the repair of its Case brand civil engineering equipment, parts included.
The contract runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028, for an estimated amount of $194,090 (plus GST and QST).
The net expenditure, after the QST refund, is estimated at $203,770.24.
The contract covers the maintenance of a fleet of 16 Case loaders used by the workshops of the Service de la gestion des équipements motorisés.
The agreement sets hourly rates, firm prices for parts and discount percentages.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders, as the law allows this when only one company can provide the service (the manufacturer's dealer).
The amounts remain conditional on the adoption of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.

The Ville de Québec is partnering with the Ville de Lévis and the Communauté métropolitaine de Québec to have the fleuve Saint-Laurent modelled, in order to better understand the movement of water and contaminants near the drinking water intakes.
The $75,000 left over from a 2017 study on the river's salinity will be reassigned to this new project.
The research mandate will be given to the École de technologie supérieure (ÉTS) for $75,000, plus taxes.
Québec and Lévis will each pay $47,310.33 to the Communauté métropolitaine de Québec when the agreement is signed.
The Communauté métropolitaine de Québec manages the contract, but the Ville de Québec becomes the owner of the model and will be able to use it for its operations.
The project aims to protect drinking water sources, including those of the usine de traitement des eaux de Sainte-Foy.
A monitoring committee made up of one representative from each party will oversee the application of the agreement.
The City is awarding the reconstruction work on boulevard Bastien to EBC inc. (L'Ancienne-Lorette), for $2,733,600 before taxes.
The work covers boulevard Bastien between rue Roland and rue Élisabeth-II, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The project completely rebuilds the underground and surface infrastructure, including a sanitary reservoir pipe and overflow structure U448, which is being entirely rebuilt.
Three companies submitted bids; EBC submitted the lowest price, 14.3% below the City's estimate.
The contract provides for price adjustments based on the cost of asphalt and fuel.
The net expense for the City comes to $2,869,938.30, funded by two agglomeration loan by-laws.
The executive committee adopted the decision on June 25, 2026.
The Ville de Québec wants to acquire about 307.8 square metres of land along rue de la Faune, in the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough.
This land would be used to widen rue de la Faune, as part of the project to rebuild that street.
The acquisition would be made by mutual agreement with the owner or, if the discussions fail, by expropriation.
The City points to a critical timeline to justify authorizing the expropriation route right now.
The land in question, at its largest extent, is assessed at $201,000 on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll, which is $2.21 per square metre.
The Service des affaires juridiques would handle the proceedings and the Service de l'ingénierie would prepare the plans and the cadastral operations.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 tied to the redevelopment work on rue de la Faune.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 821, rue Pierre-Maufay, in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough).
The existing house is considered compliant even though it is 4.46 metres from rue Hélène-Boullé instead of the 6 metres required.
Its rear setback of 2.56 metres is also accepted, instead of the 9 metres required by the planning by-law.
According to the analysis, without this exemption the owner would have to move or demolish the building.
The situation has existed since 1960 and no complaints have been recorded.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had come out in favour of the application on May 12, 2026.

The City is awarding the company 9521-3401 Québec inc. (Oïkos Civil) the contract for rebuilding the underground pipes on boulevard Henri-Bourassa, between 64e Rue Est and 65e Rue Est, in Charlesbourg.
The contract is worth $1,616,314.16 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $1,696,927.83.
The work involves the storm sewer, a drinking water pipe and a domestic sewer pipe, new manholes, the replacement of fire hydrants and the relocation of a gas pipe.
Also included are the construction of sidewalks, road work, sodding and the replacement of the traffic lights at one intersection.
Five bids were received and all were found to be compliant; the bid selected is the lowest, at 6.1% below the department's estimate ($1,720,493).
The contract includes clauses for adjusting the prices of asphalt and fuel.
The money comes from two loan by-laws: $1,548,931.15 and $147,996.68 (net of taxes).
The arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles approves the architectural and site plans for two construction projects.
Both projects are detached single-dwelling buildings, at 1176 and 1196, rue de l'Embâcle.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had recommended both applications at its meeting of February 25, 2026.
This approval is a required step before construction permits can be issued in this area.
No financial impact is indicated in the document.
The Ville de Québec is giving a grant of up to $150,000 to the company Odém Solutions inc., a maker of rotomoulded products located in the Charlesbourg industrial park.
The money is used to buy equipment (3D printers, a 3D scanner, rotomoulding machines, a painting robot, a computer system) to increase production.
The project costs $696,000 in total: $150,000 from the City, $13,000 from the company, $185,000 as a loan from Investissement Québec and $348,000 as a loan from Desjardins.
The company, created in 2023, has 40 jobs and plans to create 4 new ones.
The goal is to strengthen the company's presence in the Canadian market outside Quebec.
The grant comes from the Capitale-Productivité component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, which pays out a maximum of $150,000 per project and up to 40% of eligible expenses.
The program's review committee gave a favourable opinion on February 10, 2026; the decision is up to the urban agglomeration council.
The City is banning parking at all times along 29 metres on the south side of rue des Artisans, in the curve between rue Borne and avenue Saint-Sacrement (Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur neighbourhood).
The new zone starts 53 metres west of rue Borne and extends westward.
Five parking spaces will disappear in this commercial area.
The request comes from the company Vanbec, at 225, avenue Saint-Sacrement, which repairs heavy vehicles and trailers.
Vehicles parked in front of its garage doors were interfering with truck manoeuvres, according to the company.
The document states that workers in the area have access to off-street parking.
The decision falls to the La Cité-Limoilou borough council (order O-1549).
The Ville de Québec is terminating the agreement signed on February 10, 2020 with ABB inc., which provided for a maximum grant of $710,000.
This funding was to be used for the project "Consolidation de l'entreprise comme centre d'excellence en mesures et analyses".
No amount was paid to ABB inc. under this agreement.
The City points to the fact that the company did not submit its claim for the second payment within the required time and did not provide all the supporting documents requested.
The project's end date had been pushed back three times, to September 30, 2024, with a final claim due by December 31, 2024.
The purchase order is cancelled and the $710,000 is reallocated to the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030 fund.
The Ville de Québec will pay up to $2,000,000 to the Institut national d'optique (INO), a non-profit organization located at the Parc technologique du Québec métropolitain.
The money will go to the Quantino project, an incubator that supports companies in optics-photonics, advanced technologies, life sciences and dual-use technologies (civilian and defence).
Over two years, the project plans to create a biomedical hub, an accelerator in dual technologies, and to set up wet labs and testing spaces.
The project costs $5,291,000 in total: Québec is contributing $875,250, Ottawa $350,000, private partners $1,280,750, plus $643,000 in incubation revenue and $142,000 in management revenue.
The document states that 4 jobs will be created; INO currently has 200 jobs.
The life sciences incubator planned in the previous phase could not go ahead, due to a lack of available space at the CERVO and IUCPQ research centres; this agreement relaunches the initiative.
The funds come from the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale, as part of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030.
The City is buying a 520.1-square-metre lot along route de l'Église, in the arrondissement of Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The seller is the Centre de services scolaire des Découvreurs; the agreed price is $344,000, plus taxes.
The purchase is for the project to redevelop route de l'Église, between chemin Saint-Louis and rue de Valmont, to improve mobility.
Once the purchase is completed, the City will open part of the route de l'Église right-of-way on this lot.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3325 on bicycle path and pedestrian path work.
The decision is up to city council.
The City is renewing for two years the mandates of Yvon Hamel and Cyril Frazao as its representatives on the board of directors of the Société municipale d'habitation Champlain (SOMHAC).
Their current mandates were set to end on April 17, 2026; they will stay in their positions until replacements are appointed, if needed.
SOMHAC is a non-profit organization that offers housing at prices slightly below market rates to the people of Québec, and that can grant housing subsidies according to its means.
The administration of SOMHAC is entrusted to the Office municipal d'habitation de Québec.
It is the Québec urban agglomeration council that appoints the board members, for two-year mandates.
The document mentions no financial impact.
The Ville de Québec is adopting a by-law authorizing a $287,000 expenditure for work to assess and improve environmental quality.
The amount is borrowed and repaid over five years.

The work includes updating forecasting models for beach water quality, acoustic studies on municipal activities, the environmental and nautical brigade, wetland restoration projects and monitoring the quality of drinking water wells.
The project affects the entire territory of the city.
The City plans to hire staff, purchase goods and equipment, and award professional and technical services contracts.
An amount of $28,700 (10% of the expenditure) is taken from the general fund, which will be reimbursed when the by-law comes into force.
The funds are provided for in the years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The Ville de Québec is entrusting the organization Loisirs Brio with the management and use of municipal recreational buildings and facilities in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The agreement covers the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029 and replaces the previous one, which expired on March 31, 2026.
The City will pay $216,334.35 (plus GST and QST), for a net cost of $227,124.03.
The amounts break down as follows (net of taxes): $52,995.60 in 2026, $75,708.01 in 2027, $75,708.01 in 2028 and $22,712.41 in 2029.
The amounts will be indexed to the Consumer Price Index starting in the second year.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 depend on the approval of the annual budgets by the appropriate authorities.
The president and the assistant clerk of the arrondissement de Charlesbourg are authorized to sign the agreement.
The City approves the 2026 budget of the Société de développement commercial (SDC) de la Grande Allée: $490,988 in revenues and the same amount in expenses.
This budget is based on $105,988 in dues from members of the district, $95,000 in revenues from events and sponsorships, and $290,000 in grants.
Businesses in the Grande Allée district will have to pay dues calculated according to their line of business and the floor area of their premises.
Dues range from $26.60 to $3,191.81: from $797.95 to $3,191.81 for hotels, restaurants and bars, and from $26.60 to $1,595.90 for professionals and other businesses.
Non-profit organizations that are members are exempt from dues for 2026.
GST and QST are added to the dues, which are payable 30 days after the notice is sent; any request to correct the floor area must be made to the Service des finances within 60 days of the bill.
The Service des finances is authorized to collect the dues in the commercial district.
The City is borrowing $1,500,000 over five years to develop and carry out a plan for managing wetlands and bodies of water on its territory.
The money will be used for studies, professional and technical services contracts, grants, hiring staff, and buying goods, buildings and easements.
The work aims to better understand wetlands, fix problems, restore or create new areas, protect sensitive areas, and carry out public awareness and consultation activities.
The City will be able to acquire buildings or easements by agreement or by expropriation in order to carry out the work.
An amount of $150,000 is being taken from the general fund until the by-law comes into force, and will then be repaid.
The funds are planned for 2026 to 2028 in the 2026-2035 capital works program (record 38008).
The City is cancelling two resolutions related to a previous loan by-law (R.A.V.Q. 1807), which was withdrawn because no urban agglomeration expenditure was ultimately incurred.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 255, rue Fraser, in the Montcalm neighbourhood (La Cité-Limoilou borough).
The owner will be able to enlarge the building and add a garage attached to the neighbouring building.
The planning by-law requires that a semi-detached building share a wall over 50% of the building's depth; here, the garage will cover only 35% of it.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended granting the exemption on April 28, 2026.
According to the analysis, the layout of the neighbouring building (built-in balconies) makes it difficult to build a compliant wall without creating health and safety problems for the occupants.
The Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec also gave a favourable opinion on the proposed siting.
The document does not mention any amount of money.
The City is awarding Construction et Pavage Portneuf inc. (Saint-Marc-des-Carrières) the contract for the paving program, for $3,642,391.70 before taxes.
The work affects various streets in Québec: pavement repairs (planing and paving), road marking and replacement of detection loops.
Most of the work is being done as part of the TramCité project.
Three bids were received and found to be compliant; the bid from Portneuf is the lowest, 19.7% below the City's estimate ($4,535,763.38).
Prices may be adjusted based on the cost of asphalt and fuel.
The net expense, after recovery of the QST, comes to $3,824,055.99, funded by three loan by-laws.
The executive committee adopted the decision on May 13, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0614).
The City is banning bus traffic on rue Saint-Louis, in Vieux-Québec, from March 30 to November 30, 2026.
Still allowed without a permit: double-decker tour buses and buses of the Réseau de transport de la Capitale.

With a permit, the following may drive there: school buses for Vieux-Québec and Saint-Jean-Baptiste, buses for a hotel that can only be reached by rue Saint-Louis, and buses carrying groups of cruise ship passengers from the Port de Québec.
The permit must be displayed in the windshield; an offence costs $300, and tourism mobility dispatchers and parking officers can issue tickets.
Other buses will enter Vieux-Québec by rue Saint-Jean and côte du Palais; two temporary drop-off areas will be set up on rue Pierre-Olivier-Chauveau and rue D'Auteuil.
The measure follows the closing of rue De Buade for construction work, from April to November in 2026 and in 2027; the City will review how 2026 went before deciding on the measures for 2027.
A communications plan with variable message signs at the entrance to Vieux-Québec will inform tourism stakeholders; no financial impact is expected.
The City is authorizing the construction of a 61-unit, 5-storey residential building at 135, 60e Rue Est, in district 4-5 (Saint-Rodrigue district, arrondissement de Charlesbourg).
Current zoning limits the property to 25 units and 4 storeys; the City is lifting these limits under section 93 of Bill 31 on housing, citing a rental vacancy rate of 2.2% in Québec.
The project must include at least 55 units, at least half of which must have two or more bedrooms, and 11 ground-floor units with direct access to the outside.
The developer must provide at least 50 indoor or underground parking spaces, one of which reserved for car sharing, a rooftop terrace of at least 180 m², a play module and a picnic area.
Other conditions: 30% green space, at least 32 trees planted or preserved, a vegetation screen on the side of the neighbouring lot and a light-coloured roof over 90% of the roof.
Work must begin before February 21, 2027, otherwise the authorization lapses; a fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases) applies if the conditions are not met.
A public consultation meeting will be held, followed by a three-day period to submit written comments; the project is not subject to a referendum.
The City wants to acquire part of a piece of land at 7000, rue de l'Apogée, in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The parcel involved measures about 126.4 square metres and would be used to widen rue de la Faune.
The purchase will be made by mutual agreement with the owner or, if talks fail, by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the acquisition or expropriation proceedings.
The Division de l'arpentage et de la géomatique will prepare the required plans, technical descriptions and cadastral operations.
The entire piece of land is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $1,810,000, or $201.56 per square metre.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 related to the redevelopment of rue de la Faune.
The City is making a section of rue Gérard-Morisset one-way, in the counter-clockwise direction, between the south limit of 970 and the south limit of 67, rue Gérard-Morisset.
The mandatory stop is being removed at the northeast approach of the intersection of rue Gérard-Morisset with itself.
The street has a 9-metre roadway, traffic runs in both directions and parking is allowed on both sides, which makes it difficult for vehicles to pass each other.

A temporary link will be built between avenue Vimy and rue Gérard-Morisset to maintain access to the area during the closure of the Gérard-Morisset and René-Lévesque intersection related to the tramway work.
The one-way direction is intended to make the new intersection safer and to make it easier to manage access and the junction with the temporary link.
Residents supported the measure at a public consultation held on May 26.
The area affected is the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, district Montcalm-Saint-Sacrement.
The City is entrusting the management and operation of the new Centre multifonctionnel de curling de Québec, at 1020, rue des Rocailles, to the Club multifonctionnel de curling de Québec.
This club is a non-profit organization created from the merger of three clubs in the city: Victoria de Québec, Jacques-Cartier and Les Balais Verts. It has more than 700 active members.
The club will first prepare the centre for the curling tournament of the Jeux du Canada, which will take place from February 27 to March 14, 2027.
The City is paying $314,962.50 (net of taxes) under clause 9.1 of the agreement, from urban agglomeration jurisdiction funds.
The revenues provided for in clauses 9.7 to 9.10 of the agreement will go to the City's general fund.
ExpoCité is a party to the agreement: the centre comes under its authority, in particular to operate commercial activities there for the benefit of the City.
The Centre de curling was added in May 2025 to the list of facilities of collective interest of the agglomération de Québec; its construction began in 2025 on City-owned land.
The City is applying for financial assistance from the ministère de l'Éducation to build mountain bike trails at parc Chauveau.
The application is being made under component 2, "Infrastructures de plein air" (outdoor infrastructure), of a funding program for recreational, sports and outdoor infrastructure.
