The program ends on March 31, 2027.
The City commits to paying its share of the project's eligible costs.
Carolyne Larouche, director of the Beauport, Charlesbourg and La Cité-Limoilou boroughs, is authorized to act on the City's behalf in this matter.
No amount is indicated in the document.
The City will install a new traffic light in Charlesbourg, at the intersection of 4e Avenue Est, 4e Avenue Est and a private access road.
The traffic light is required by the redevelopment project at Galeries Charlesbourg, whose driveway entrance will be aligned with 4e Avenue Est.
The cost of the traffic light will be split fifty-fifty: 50% by the City, 50% by the developer.
The stated goal is to keep traffic flowing smoothly and to ensure the safety of drivers, pedestrians and cyclists.
By-law R.A.V.Q. 1868 amends the agglomeration by-law on traffic and parking by replacing the list of traffic lights (Schedule IX).
An agreement on the municipal work tied to the project will be submitted to city council at a later date.
The City is awarding Alaroy inc. the contract to build a services pavilion and a covered skating rink at parc de Duberger, in the arrondissement des Rivières, for $12,774,747 (before GST and QST).
The project includes a covered, refrigerated outdoor skating rink with boards, glass panels, nets, a scoreboard, audiovisual equipment, swivel basketball hoops and pickleball line markings.
The pavilion will include garages, a multi-purpose room, work spaces, washrooms, technical rooms and an outdoor enclosure for the refrigeration equipment.
The outdoor work includes a roundabout, a drop-off area, a public square, a lit pedestrian path and landscaping.
Alaroy inc. submitted the lowest compliant price among the 10 bids received; the gap with the City's estimate ($12,095,000) is 5.6%.
The net expense comes to $13,411,887.51, funded by four loan by-laws.
The executive committee adopted the decision on June 17, 2026.
The City is paying out two grants of $20,000 each, for a maximum total of $40,000, to remove pavement and add greenery on land it does not own.
Nature Québec receives $20,000 for a project at école Saint-Sacrement.
The Centre de services scolaire des Premières-Seigneuries receives $20,000 for a project at école de la Ribambelle.
The funding covers up to 80% of eligible expenses for non-profit organizations and 50% for for-profit businesses, with a maximum of $20,000 per project.
Only start-up and landscaping costs are paid (soil, compost, fertilizer, plants, labour); communications and maintenance are excluded.
The call for projects launched in the fall of 2025 targets work to be done in the spring, summer and fall of 2026; the application deadline was March 31, 2026.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3055, and the grants are paid out after the accountability report has been verified.
The City confirms that it has completed two active transportation projects funded by the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable (Véloce III program).

At the intersection of rue Louis-Lumière and boulevard du Parc-Technologique, the City reconfigured the intersection and added traffic lights over 150 metres; eligible expenses of $1,005,636.40 (net of taxes).

On rue Monseigneur-Plessis, between rue Beaucage and rue Fleur-de-Lys, the City replaced the bike lanes with a one-way bike path in each direction, added a sidewalk on the east side and planted trees over 870 metres; eligible expenses of $1,790,397.16 (net of taxes).
The Ministry had granted up to $250,000 for Louis-Lumière and $870,000 for Monseigneur-Plessis; the City has already received $200,000 and $696,000 as first payments.
By filing these reports, the City aims to receive the second and final payments of the funding.

If the declared expenses are lower than the amounts used to calculate the funding already paid, the City must repay the excess; failure to follow the program rules results in the cancellation of the funding.
The document states that there is no financial impact.
The City is transferring $380,000 from its unrestricted surplus to the reserve set aside for snow removal operations.
This snow removal reserve must reach a total of $20,000,000, under the accumulated surplus management policy of the Cadre financier 2023-2032.
The breakdown of this target has been revised: $17,980,000 charged to the city and $2,020,000 to the urban agglomeration.
This change stems from a by-law adopted on December 17, 2025 that sets the agglomeration's share of Service des travaux publics spending at 10.1%.
A reverse transfer of $380,000 will be proposed to the urban agglomeration council to balance everything out.
The amounts come from the surpluses as at December 31, 2025; the decision was scheduled for the June 16, 2026 city council meeting.
The Ville de Québec will pay €9,075 to the Association internationale des maires francophones (AIMF) as its membership fee for 2026.
The fee goes from €5,150 in 2025 to €9,075 in 2026.
The AIMF has changed how it calculates membership fees: it is now based on GDP per capita and the population of member cities, with population brackets.
The data used for the calculation will be updated every year, and the fee table will be approved annually by the AIMF's Bureau exécutif.
The money comes from the budget of the Service de la coordination stratégique et des relations internationales and falls under urban agglomeration jurisdiction.
Québec co-founded the AIMF in 1979 with Paris; today the association brings together more than 300 mayors and local elected officials from about fifty countries.
Paris pays the highest fee (€46,350), followed by Montréal (€29,000).
The Ville de Québec is giving the company Bel-Gaufre inc. one more year to complete its project to automate its packaging cell.
The project's end date moves from November 30, 2026 to November 30, 2027.
The company will have to submit its final claim by January 30, 2028, instead of February 28, 2027.
The company explains its delay by unforeseen challenges in building its new plant and installing its new production line, which prevented the packaging project from starting.
The $150,000 grant had been authorized on January 21, 2026 under the Capitale-Productivité component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030.
This component pays up to $150,000 per project, for a maximum of 40% of eligible expenses, with no repayment.
All the other conditions of the March 4, 2026 agreement remain unchanged.
The City is awarding Génio Experts-Conseils inc. (Québec) a professional engineering services contract worth $403,770 before taxes.
The project involves adding a drinking water main and rebuilding surface infrastructure on boulevard Henri-Bourassa and 24e Rue, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough.
The firm will handle the studies, the design, the plans and specifications, the cost estimates and the supervision of the work.
It will also be able to apply, on the City's behalf, for permits and authorizations from government departments and utility network companies, with the agreement of the Service de l'ingénierie.
Six bids were received; four were ranked. Génio obtained the best final score.
The net expense for the City is $423,908.03, funded by two loan by-laws ($353,251.44 and $70,656.59 in net taxes).
The requesting department's initial estimate was $577,632 before taxes.
The City is leasing about 320 m² of land to Vidéotron at the Beauport snow dump site, at 101, rue Clémenceau.
Vidéotron will install a 40-metre telecommunications tower, a shelter and equipment there to improve cellular coverage in the area.
The lease runs for 10 years, with two renewal options of 10 years each, and begins on the first day of the month in which the installation starts.
The base rent is $20,000 per year for the first year, plus $5,500 per additional operator, taxes extra.
The rents will be indexed each year based on the higher of the increase in the Consumer Price Index or 3%.
The Beauport borough council had authorized this use on the condition that Vidéotron plant a screen of trees near the properties on rue Saint-Exupéry.
The amounts collected will go to the City's general fund.
The City is refusing the exemption request from the Canadian Tire located at 5500, boulevard des Gradins, in Neufchâtel-Lebourgneuf (Arrondissement des Rivières).
The business wanted to install a 3.93-metre information sign rather than the permitted maximum of 1 square metre.
It was also asking to increase the total sign area to 90 square metres instead of 87.53 square metres.
The business said it wanted to review its signs in order to comply with a provincial law and increase signage in French.
The City replies that a compliant signage proposal could be submitted and that there is therefore no serious harm.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had unanimously recommended refusal on February 2, 2026.
The City is setting the rules for the financial assistance offered to businesses affected by the work on avenue des Hôtels in 2026.
The infrastructure and redevelopment work on avenue des Hôtels will run approximately from April 1 to December 31, 2026.
A plan sets out the boundaries of the designated area and the area of influence of avenue des Hôtels, which define the territory covered by the program.
The 2026 fiscal year is the one that counts for businesses and establishments located in the designated area.
To be recognized, the work must last at least three consecutive months and seriously obstruct traffic.
The executive committee must enact the ordinance before businesses can apply for the assistance.
The arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles is banning parking on both sides of rue de l'Embâcle, in the Val-Bélair area.
Parking is also now banned all the way around the turnaround at the north end of rue de l'Embâcle, to let snow removal and garbage collection vehicles through.
A mandatory stop is being added on rue de l'Équinoxe, at the intersection with rue de l'Embâcle, for drivers and cyclists coming from the east.
These changes follow the extension of the two streets in 2025, which was done to allow the construction of new residential buildings.
The City notes that visibility at the new intersection was inadequate; the temporary signs put up during the work are becoming permanent.
The City is sending Yasmina Lacasse, architect and team leader at the Service de la gestion des immeubles, to The Best in Heritage conference in Barcelona, from November 11 to 13, 2026.
She will attend as a speaker to present the bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy project, winner of the 2025 IFLA/Baker & Taylor Public Library of the Year Award.
The City will reimburse up to $3,754 in transportation, accommodation and meal expenses, upon submission of receipts.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de la gestion des immeubles.
A variance of no more than 10% of the authorized amount will be accepted without further authorization.
If Ms. Lacasse cannot attend, her replacement is authorized to take part, and the dates may change according to the organizers.
The Ville de Québec is raising the 2026 annual salary for the position of team leader – quartermaster (40 hours) in the fire department: from $101,587 to $111,744.
This new salary is the same as the one paid to lieutenants, lieutenant-instructors and prevention lieutenants (35 hours).
The increase also applies in 2027 and 2028, and retroactively for 2024 and 2025.
The reassessment of this job had been promised when the 2024-2028 collective agreement with the Association des pompiers professionnels de Québec inc. was renewed.
The amounts for 2024-2025 come from the payroll increase budget; those for 2026 to 2028 come from the fire quartermaster management budget.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The City is paying the legal fees of Mayor Bruno Marchand, who is being sued personally before the Superior Court by Vicky Lépine.
The mandate is given to the firm BCF s.e.n.c.r.l., and the executive committee is ratifying it after the fact.
The expected bill is $52,493.75 (net of taxes), taken from the operating budget of the Service des affaires juridiques.
The damages lawsuit, filed on February 3, 2026, concerns an event in January 2025 that occurred while the mayor was carrying out his duties as an elected official.
A formal demand letter had first been sent to the mayor on January 14, 2026 for the same event.
The City points to its legal obligation to protect its elected officials in the exercise of their duties (section 604.6 of the Cities and Towns Act).
The City is lowering the fee for receiving household waste at the complexe de valorisation énergétique from $196 to $160 per metric tonne, a fee charged mainly to waste management companies.
It is also lowering the additional fee for receiving narcotic waste from $196 to $160 per metric tonne, charged mainly to outside police services.
These two reductions correspond to the removal of the $36 in disposal fees provided for by the Loi sur la qualité de l'environnement, which are already added to the fees.

The City is adding to the by-law nine parking zones connected to the building at 320, rue Saint-Joseph Est (TF-12, TP-33 to TP-36, TH-16, TH-18, TH-19, TH-20), which it is taking back over the management of in 2026.
Parking zone TF-12 is priced at $10 for daily access by reservation, for people employed by a business housed in a City building.
It is also correcting the fee schedule for the Centre de glace de Québec to distinguish the hourly rate from the daily rate during international and national sporting events.
The conseil d'agglomération (urban agglomeration council) must adopt the by-law, with a target date of June 3, 2026.
The City is changing the zoning of zone 22031Ha, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood (arrondissement des Rivières), east of rue de Caen.
The maximum number of dwellings allowed in a detached building is going from two to three in this zone.
No minimum parking spaces will be required anymore for dwellings in this zone, which is being changed to the "Axe structurant B" type.
The building standards (maximum height of 10.5 m, two storeys, setbacks) stay the same.
The request comes from an owner at 5560-5564, rue de Caen, who wants to add a dwelling in the basement of her home.
The conseil de quartier de Duberger-Les Saules will be consulted and will hold a public meeting; people will have seven days after that meeting to send in their comments in writing.
The by-law cannot be subject to approval by referendum.

The City is adding the Le Zénith parking lot, at 263, rue Sagard (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou), to the list of parking lots covered by the agglomeration by-law. It has 84 spaces and is operated by the SPAQ.

New rates are being added to the draft by-law before it is adopted: monthly passes for residents (at all times, or evenings and weekends), a daytime rate for workers in the area, and an occasional rate for everyone.
These rates are in addition to the passes already planned for municipal employees.
The City says it set the rates based on an analysis of market costs in the Saint-Roch area and of the practices in place for residents of the central neighbourhoods.
The by-law also updates the information for the Place Jacques-Cartier parking lot: address at 365, rue Dorchester, 308 spaces and new rates.
A notice of motion was given on July 8, 2026; the urban agglomeration council is being asked to adopt the amended by-law.
The arrondissement des Rivières is paying out $23,868 in grants to seven organizations in the area, spread over eight applications filed on December 15, 2025.
Loisirs et sports Neufchâtel is receiving $7,410 for support workers for people living with a disability during spring break and a day camp.
Ressources Parents Vanier is getting two amounts: $1,122 for chairs and games, and $3,230 for a strategic planning project.
Corporation Jeunesse l'Évasion l'Ormière is receiving $3,675 for furniture and games.

Four grants are for visibility: Loisirs Duberger-Les Saules ($2,617), Société d'histoire Les Rivières ($2,882 to redo its website), Maison des Jeunes de St-André de Neufchâtel ($1,939) and Club de soccer des Rivières de Québec ($993).
The money comes from the operating budget of the arrondissement des Rivières.
The City is awarding Veolia Water Technologies & Solutions Canada GP a contract worth $821,755 (before taxes) to supply and deliver filter media.
This granular mineral filter media will be used for the biofiltration floors at the two wastewater treatment plants.
Deliveries are for the station Est (105, chemin de la Baie-de-Beauport, La Cité-Limoilou) and the station Ouest (3825, chemin Sainte-Foy, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
Only one bid was received for public call for tenders 95806; the other suppliers who picked up the documents explained why they did not bid.
After negotiation, the supplier revised its price from $865,003.50 to $821,755, which is 25.9% below the City's estimate of $1,108,310.32.
The net cost to the City is $862,740.03, paid out of the operating budget of the Service du traitement des eaux.
The executive committee adopted the decision on June 10, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0777).
The City is banning parking on the south side of rue Adine-Fafard, in the arrondissement des Rivières, along the whole length of the street (123 metres).
This ban removes 13 on-street parking spaces.
The street is 7 metres wide: when vehicles are parked on both sides, two cars cannot pass each other.
Parking there was very busy at certain times, because of the école primaire Les Prés-Verts and the centre communautaire Lebourgneuf.
According to the City, residents have off-street spaces, but users of the community centre will have to park farther away.
The decision follows a request from a citizen.
The City is refusing a minor exemption request for 707, rue des Talus, in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood (Arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The owner wanted to convert their attached garage into living space, with an extension of 3.45 metres on the side.
They were asking for a side setback of 1.2 metres instead of the required 3.0 metres, and a front parking encroachment of 3.5 metres instead of 3.0 metres.
Reason for the refusal: a project that meets the standards is still possible, so there is no serious harm to the owner.
Another reason: the lot has no special feature that would prevent a compliant project.

According to the analysis, an extension of about 1.5 metres toward the side would be allowed without an exemption, and the conversion at 1.1 metres from the lot line could affect the neighbouring property.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the refusal on January 13, 2026.
The City is creating a list of suppliers for renting motorized equipment for short periods (less than six months), with or without an operator, from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027.
The net expenditure is estimated at $7,349,125, subject to approval of the 2027 budget.

The agreement covers 42 types of equipment (vibrating plates, mechanical street sweepers, hydraulic excavators, aerial lifts, etc.), but excludes snow removal equipment and the rental of light vehicles.
15 bids were received for public call for tenders 94241 and the selected suppliers are considered compliant.
Suppliers are ranked in order based on their hourly rates; if the first one cannot respond, the City calls the next one.
The boroughs and departments concerned (public works, recreation, buildings, residual materials, motorized equipment, water treatment) will be able to use it according to their needs.
The City is awarding Signalisation GardaWorld S.E.N.C. (Montréal) the contract for flaggers, the design of signage layout plans and the supply of road signage.
The contract is worth $1,012,970.15 before taxes and runs from the date it is awarded until April 30, 2028, with an option to extend it by 12 months, indexed to the CPI.
The supplier installs and maintains temporary signage during road work carried out by the Service de la gestion des immeubles, to keep pedestrians, cyclists and workers safe.
The work covered includes street lighting fixtures and lampposts, the signals for the Réseau de transport de la Capitale reserved lanes, signage or lighting cabinets, and traffic lights.
Three bids were received: GardaWorld at $1,012,970.15, Mckinnon at $1,258,203.75 and 9477-7604 Québec inc. at $1,445,346.75, against a City estimate of $1,810,355.00.
The net expense is estimated at $1,063,492.04, subject to approval of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.
The decision falls to the Québec urban agglomeration council.
The City is allowing an outdoor staircase in the front yard at 94-96, rue Germaine-Viger, in the arrondissement de Beauport, even though the planning by-law does not permit it at that location.
The staircase will provide a second exit for the second-floor dwelling, as required by Québec's construction code.
Conditions imposed: at least 1.5 metres between the staircase and the front of the building, a mandatory landing, and a maximum encroachment of 2 metres into the front setback.
The owner will also have to plant a tree in the front yard.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on January 21, 2026; the borough council granted it.
The arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge is changing the planning rules for five zones in the Saint-Louis neighbourhood (Saint-Louis–Sillery and Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy districts).

The front setback will now be measured from the centre line of the street: 18 metres along chemin Saint-Louis (zones 33023Hc, 33704Ha, 33723Hb) and 16 metres along route de l'Église (zones 33701Ha, 33721Hb).
In zones 33701Ha and 33704Ha, a detached building may have up to three dwelling units instead of two.
Zone 33701Ha will allow semi-detached buildings with one dwelling unit, with the side setback increased to 3 metres and a minimum lot width of 16 metres (8 metres for a semi-detached building).
In zone 33023Hc, a non-conforming main building destroyed by a disaster may be rebuilt in the same location.

The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; the conseil de quartier de Saint-Louis will hold the public consultation meeting, followed by seven days to send written comments.
The Ville de Québec is sending two representatives to Woluwé-Saint-Lambert, Belgium, on September 28 and 29, 2026.
This is a meeting of the Commission permanente Villes innovantes, intelligentes et responsables of the Association internationale des maires francophones (AIMF).

The delegates are Raymond Poirier, city councillor and member of the executive committee responsible for information technology, and Tatiana Tinoco, section director at the Service des technologies de l'information.
The City is authorizing an expense of $6,782.20 for mission costs, reimbursed upon submission of receipts, that is $3,391.10 per person.
Part of the costs related to organizing the event is paid by the AIMF organizers.
The meeting will contribute to a guide on innovation and artificial intelligence intended for French-speaking municipalities, which is scheduled to be published in early 2027.
An overrun of no more than 10% of the authorized amount will be accepted without further authorization.
The City is awarding snow removal and winter maintenance for five street zones to three companies, for three winters, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2029.
Les Entreprises MRA Paysagistes inc. is awarded Val-Bélair centre ($3,483,444.36) and Sainte-Foy north of boulevard Laurier, east of autoroute Robert-Bourassa ($3,861,748.32), before taxes.
Groupe GCH inc. is awarded the Des Châtels area north of boulevard Saint-Claude, boulevard Valcartier and route Sainte-Geneviève, for $3,642,358.71 before taxes.

Hamel Construction inc. is awarded the Honoré-Mercier, côte d'Abraham, Dorchester, de la Couronne and René-Lévesque area ($5,252,163.63) as well as Charest and Saint-Sacrement ($1,978,216.95), before taxes.
The total net expenditure comes to $19,126,551.33, spread from 2026 to 2029, subject to the adoption of the 2027 to 2029 budgets.
The contracts include an option to renew for two winters, an annual indexation based on the CPI, and adjustments tied to fuel and snowfall.
The contract for the Beauport nord zone (C0039) is dealt with in a separate file.
The City is giving $75,000 to the Association canadienne de tennis for the second round of the Davis Cup qualifiers.
The event takes place on September 18 and 19, 2026, at the Centre Vidéotron, with Canada against France.
Admission is paid, but a free fan zone is planned at place Jean-Béliveau.
The event's budget is estimated at $1,800,000; the City's grant represents 4.2% of it.
The City is paying $67,500 in 2026 and $7,500 in 2027, this last amount being conditional on the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The funding is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners.
The organization must submit a full report on the event within 90 days after it ends.
The City is granting a minor exemption for the building at 3333, rue du Carrefour, in the Vieux-Moulin neighbourhood in Beauport (Robert-Giffard district).
The project involves expanding and redeveloping part of the shopping centre to add an indoor go-kart centre.
The exemption allows a mezzanine above the second floor with an area of up to just under 25% of the floor it sits above, instead of the maximum of 10% set out in the planning by-law.
This mezzanine will not be counted as a storey and does not increase the height of the building.
The mezzanine will house event rooms and an access point to the rooftop terrace.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme of Beauport voted unanimously in favour of the request on June 11, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is about to sign an agreement with the Office municipal d'habitation de Québec (OMHQ) and the Société d'habitation du Québec (SHQ) to fund work in low-rental housing (HLM).
This agreement makes it possible to pay out the financial assistance from the Programme de rénovation des habitations à loyer modique (PRHLM), set up by the SHQ in May 2023.
The program funds the renovation or reconstruction of HLM buildings, several of which were built in the 1970s.
Under the program's rules, the City must pay about 10% of the expenses recognized by the SHQ for eligible projects.
The City says the agreement does not add any expense this year, because the buildings involved were already in the OMHQ's 2026 budget forecasts, authorized on January 21, 2026.
The expenses covered include the work, professional fees, soil decontamination, the call for tenders and the relocation of tenants.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.

The City is awarding SécuriteQ inc. (Montréal) the security guard surveillance of the temporary sanitary block trailer installed at the bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy, at 350, rue Saint-Joseph (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The contract is worth $648,064.80 before taxes and covers June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2029, with a 12-month renewal option indexed to the Consumer Price Index.
The net cost to the City is $680,387.03, spread over four years: $119,608.56 in 2026, $224,672.56 in 2027, $229,271.02 in 2028 and $106,834.89 in 2029.
The amounts for the years 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets by the competent authorities.
The City received 28 bids; SécuriteQ inc. submitted the lowest price among the compliant bids.
The price chosen is 19.9% lower than the estimate of the requesting department, which was $810,030.36 before taxes.
City council adopted the decision on March 31, 2026.
The City is replacing two of its representatives on the board of delegates responsible for the watercourse that runs along route Grand-Capsa (route 358).
Councillor Marie-Pierre Boucher becomes substitute for Mayor Bruno Marchand, replacing David Weiser.
Gaétan Pageau, mayor of L'Ancienne-Lorette, replaces Councillor Marie-Josée Asselin.
These changes follow the November 2025 municipal elections: the two former representatives no longer sit on the urban agglomeration council.
The board of delegates brings together the Québec agglomeration and the MRC de Portneuf and MRC de La Jacques-Cartier, which share responsibility for this watercourse.
Sainte-Catherine-de-la-Jacques-Cartier has complained about flooding along route Grand-Capsa and took the matter to court; the trial has been held and the judgment is still to come.
The Ville de Sainte-Catherine-de-la-Jacques-Cartier is asking, among other things, that corrective work be ordered.
The City is awarding the contract for transplanting and planting trees to the company B.G. Transplantation inc. (Terrebonne).
The contract is worth $245,612.70 before taxes; the estimated net cost is $257,862.63.
The work runs from the date the contract is awarded until December 31, 2027.
It includes transplanting, transporting, planting and watering deciduous trees and conifers.
The trees will be used for various engineering projects, both planned and unplanned, as well as for the Projet du tramway de Québec.
Three companies submitted bids; the two other offers were $399,000 and $406,775 before taxes.
The request comes from the Arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The City is paying $191,804 to four property-owning organizations for maintenance and accessibility work in their buildings.
Centre ressources pour femmes de Beauport (705, avenue Royale): $80,000 to redo the interior layout and install a platform lift.
Patro de Charlesbourg (7700, 3e Avenue Est): $80,000 to replace the gymnasium floor surface.
Relais La Chaumine (850, 3e Avenue): $28,077 to replace the roof and two balconies.
Création le Pantoum (76, rue Saint-Vallier Ouest): $3,727 to install a fire door.
The program covers up to $80,000 and 80% of eligible costs per project.
Each organization receives 90% of the amount after the executive committee's decision, and 10% when the work is finished, upon submission of supporting documents.
The City is borrowing $5,400,000 to fund the implementation of its Politique culturelle 2025-2030, over the years 2026 to 2028.

The money will go to projects in the performing arts, public art and libraries, to support programs for artists and professional cultural organizations, and to activities, presentation, cultural mediation and exhibitions.
Part of it may also pay for the purchase of specialized equipment, capital works, grants and the salaries of the staff required.
The loan will be repaid over five years, out of the City's general revenues.
The projects covered take in the entire territory under the City's jurisdiction.
The City authorizes itself to acquire, by mutual agreement or by expropriation, any building or easement needed for the work.
An amount of $540,000 (10% of the expense) is taken from the general fund and will be returned to it when the by-law comes into force.
The City is signing an agreement with the Minister of Municipal Affairs to receive up to $237,500 for its project "L'eau de pluie, une ressource à valoriser sur chaque terrain!".
The money comes from the Programme pour la gestion durable des eaux de pluie 2025-2027, which covers 50% of the City's eligible expenses, estimated at $475,000.
The project would cost about $1,000,000: $400,000 paid by participating property owners and $600,000 by the City, with a maximum net cost of $362,500 for the City.
The City will set up a program for private properties (residential, commercial, industrial) to increase vegetated areas and reduce impermeable surfaces.
Property owners who receive help will have their assistance capped at 50% of the costs.
The work must be completed no later than March 31, 2028; the ministry pays 50% of the amount as an advance upon signing and pays the balance after an external audit report.
The City officially designates the boulevard René-Lévesque area, between Université Laval and avenue Holland, as a major construction zone for 2026.
Businesses in this area can therefore apply for the financial assistance provided under the support program tied to the TramCité project's construction sites.
The work covered runs approximately from April 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026.
The 2026 fiscal year is the one that is eligible for businesses and establishments located in the designated area.
A plan attached to the order sets out the boundaries of the designated area and the area of influence.
To be recognized, the work must last at least three consecutive months and significantly obstruct traffic.
The arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge is giving out $208,489 in grants to 45 organizations in its area.
The money is used to pay operating expenses (day-to-day costs) of organizations recognized by the City.
These are the applications submitted on February 20, 2026, as well as payments for year 2 or year 3 of agreements already under way.

The amounts range from $500 to $20,000 per organization: among others, $20,000 to Laura Lémerveil, $15,000 to Camp École Kéno, and $10,000 each to Club de natation région de Québec, Club de patinage de vitesse, Québec Excellence synchro and Mieux-être des immigrants.
The organizations involved work in recreation, sports, culture, seniors (clubs FADOQ), families and community assistance.
The funds come from the borough's operating budget, under the "Soutien aux organismes" (support for organizations) activity.
The owner of the inn at 385, Grande Allée Est wants to add a 14th room to the 13 rooms already there.
The by-law requires 7 parking spaces; 6 are recognized as acquired rights and no new space is planned.
The City is exempting the owner from providing the missing space, in exchange for $500 paid into the "Fonds de stationnement" (parking fund).
The amount must be paid no later than 30 days after the borough council adopts the resolution.
The area (parking permit zone 9) has 477 on-street spaces for residents, while 570 permits have been issued.
The Service du transport points out the public transit service, the large parking lots in the area and the paid parking nearby.
The City wants to obtain a permanent servitude (right of use) on a piece of land along rue Berthiaume, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The servitude covers about 6.30 square metres of part of lot 1 570 417 and will be used to move public utility conduits and networks.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement or by expropriation; the Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings.
The owners have been informed of the process, the next steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
If the project no longer needs the servitude, the City may withdraw from the expropriation proceedings, in whole or in part.
The entire piece of land is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $210,000, which is $452.10 per square metre.
The funds come from urban agglomeration loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342, related to the structuring public transit network.

The City is amending its agreement with Terrain Dev Immobilier inc. for the rue de la Herse project, a new street of about 960 metres running parallel to rue Pincourt, in the Loretteville district (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
An invasive plant, Japanese knotweed, was found in the green strip north of the retention basin, which required weeding, disposal of materials and the repair of sections of sidewalk.
This work costs $42,530.94 (before taxes), while other planned costs (tactile paving slabs and plantings) went down by $18,542.84.
The City is therefore paying the developer an additional $23,988.10, bringing its total contribution for the upgrade to $282,125.10 (before taxes).
The net expense for the City, after recovery of the QST, is $25,184.51, paid out of loan by-law R.V.Q. 3241.
The rest of the development project remains unchanged.
City council adopted the decision on June 16, 2026 (resolution CV-2026-0506).
The City is entering into an agreement with Énergir to move a gas line under the rivière Saint-Charles, in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The work consists of rerouting an NPS 4 plastic line so that it passes under the river by directional drilling.
This relocation is required because the City must demolish and rebuild the pont des Seigneuries, under which the gas network currently runs.
The City is paying 50% of the cost of the work, an amount estimated at $445,963.52 (plus GST and QST), of which $46,744.03 had already been authorized on June 26, 2026.
The total cost of the work is estimated by Énergir at $875,438.99 before taxes; the net expense for the City is estimated at $419,130.56.
Énergir estimates that the work will take about 4 weeks and will invoice the City at the end, payable within 60 days.
The director of the Service des approvisionnements is authorized to sign the agreement.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council adopts a by-law allowing a food store with an associated restaurant to open at 23 and 35, côte du Palais and at 1150, rue Saint-Jean, in Vieux-Québec.
The project provides for a mixed-use building: commercial space on the ground floor and in the basement, 30 new housing units on the upper floors, and several levels of underground parking.
The new building would be connected by an indoor link to the former Banque de Montréal building, and the two lots would be merged.

After the public consultations in September 2025, the City revised the project: on the ground floor, the food store will have to occupy twice as much area as the restaurant (two thirds versus one third), instead of the 51%-49% split initially planned.
Occupancy will have to begin within four years after the by-law comes into force.
The by-law applies only to this property and does not change the zoning of other properties in the area; it contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The City is hiring Frédéric Brie as director of ExpoCité, a position he had already been holding on an interim basis since 2025.
His annual salary is set at $174,393 according to the 2026 salary scale for managers of the Direction générale and service directors.
The contract takes effect on June 21, 2026 and is for an indefinite term.
He reports to the directrice générale adjointe - citoyen et vitalité urbaine, and was selected through an internal competition.
If he leaves, he must give 4 weeks' notice; if the City ends the contract, the notice period ranges from 3 to 12 months (one month per year of service).
He must work exclusively for the City and comply with the by-law on employee ethics.
The necessary funds, including employee benefits, are already provided for in the budget.
The City is giving $715,000 to Festival d'été international de Québec inc. for the 2026 edition of the Festival d'été de Québec.
It is also providing free municipal services (up to $1,366,000) and the purchase of goods and services (up to $61,500), for total support of $2,142,500.
The festival runs from July 9 to 19, 2026, with nearly 200 shows, 40% of which are in French or free.
A pass is required for the plaines d'Abraham, the place George-V and the Manège militaire; the stages at the place de l'Assemblée-Nationale and the place d'Youville are free.
Grande Allée is closed in the evenings and on weekends, between rue Cours du Général-De Montcalm and the porte Saint-Louis, and reopened to cars outside those periods.
The event's planned budget is $55,940,790; the City's grant represents 1.3% of it.
The support is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners.
The City is taking $3,185,000 from the financial reserve created in 2020 for the long-term maintenance of the Centre Vidéotron.

The money will be used to replace equipment that has reached the end of its life or is no longer technologically supported: switches, storage and surveillance servers, projectors, monitors, audio and video control room components, seating, and to pay fees.
The needs for 2026 total $4,515,000, whereas only $2,000,000 had been planned at the outset.
A project to replace switches, worth more than $1.5M and planned for 2025, will be carried out in 2026.
The City is adding $2,515,000 to record 60002 of the 2026-2035 investment plan, under agglomeration jurisdiction.
These expenses stem from the preventive maintenance program approved on June 9, 2021, which gives ExpoCité responsibility for replacing certain equipment.
The reserve, built up over 35 years, can reach $75M; amounts of $2,000,000 and $1,700,000 had already been taken from it.
The Ville de Québec is giving up to $55,000 to the non-profit organization Nos choses ont une deuxième vie for its 2026 year.
The money is used to run a physical reuse centre (735, rue Père-Marquette, in La Cité-Limoilou) and an online platform selling used items at low prices.
The grant goes from $52,000 in 2025 to $55,000, which is $3,000 more.

In return, the organization must increase its offering from 30,000 to 34,000 items for sale, set up at least 2 computer search stations on site, and create at least 6 new partnerships (3 with community organizations, 3 for repairing items).
The organization must also increase its capacity to 35 volunteers and to 45 people doing community work, compensatory work or youth involvement.
The payment is made in two parts: $38,500 at the start, then $16,500 after the final report is accepted.
The agreement takes effect on May 15, 2026, and the funds come from the budget of the agglomeration of Québec.
The City wants to obtain a permanent servitude (easement) on private land along 1re Avenue, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité streetcar project.
The servitude covers about 6.60 square metres of part of lot 1 570 399 and will be used to move public utility conduits and networks.
The agreement could be reached by mutual agreement with the owner or, failing that, through expropriation; the owners have already been informed of the process and of a contact person at the City.
The Service des affaires juridiques may drop the expropriation proceedings if the project ultimately no longer needs the servitude.
The entire property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $189,000, which is $503.33 per square metre.
The money comes from agglomeration loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to building the structuring public transit network.
The owner of 2995, avenue Saint-Léandre (quartier Duberger-Les Saules) wants to split the property into two lots and build a new building on the vacant part.
The new two-storey building would have nine housing units spread over three levels: 3 studios, 3 one-bedroom units (3 ½) and 3 two-bedroom units (4 ½).
Current zoning limits buildings in this zone to six housing units; the City is proposing an occupancy permission that applies only to this lot, without changing the rules for other buildings.
No parking spaces are required for the project, because the zone is classified as "Axe structurant B"; two spaces already exist on the lot.
The borough council is asking for the opinion of the conseil de quartier de Duberger-Les Saules, which will hold the public consultation meeting.
Interested people will have seven days after the public meeting to send their comments in writing; the public participation session with referendum approval is planned for around May 2026.
The La Haute-Saint-Charles borough is giving out $34,695 in seven grants to six organizations in the area.
Agiro receives the largest amount, $17,352, for a strategic planning project.
L'Accueil St-Ambroise de Loretteville receives $6,400 for its operating expenses (year 2) and $4,500 to buy freezers and refrigerators.
The Corporation d'astronomie de Val-Bélair receives $2,880 for a television, and Popote et Multi-Services $2,563 for promotional items (banner flags, banners, tablecloths, tent).
The Chevaliers de Colomb du Lac St-Charles (50th anniversary evening) and the Harmonie de Val-Bélair (volunteers' Christmas party) each receive $500.
The applications had to be submitted by June 15, 2026, at the latest, under the support programs for recognized organizations.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget, under the "Soutien aux organismes" (support for organizations) activity.
The arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles is approving a minor exemption at 9525, rue Georges-Émile-Lapalme, in the quartier Des Châtels.
The owner may expand the house with an attached garage and a livable room on the upper floor.
The front setback is accepted at 5.3 metres instead of the 6 metres required.
The left side setback is accepted at 1.4 metres instead of 2 metres, and the combined width of the side yards at 3.3 metres instead of 5 metres.
According to the analysis, the presence of the ruisseau Sainte-Barbe at the rear and its protection strips prevent any expansion toward the rear.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on March 25, 2026.
The executive committee takes note of the quarterly report on the investments of the financial reserve related to the pension plan deficit of the former Ville de Québec.
The report covers the period from January 1 to March 31, 2026.
The reserve's investments were worth $366.7M as at March 31, 2026, compared with $364,774,611 as at December 31, 2025.
The return for the quarter is 0.65%; the return for the last twelve months is 5.61%.
According to the report, the breakdown of the investments complied with the limits of the investment policy as at March 31, 2026.
The supervisory committee must submit such a report to the executive committee every quarter.
The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for money for four active mobility (walking and cycling) projects, under the TAPU program for the year 2027-2028.
The projects concerned: rue des Ardennes (near the Québec-Gatineau railway crossing) and parc Victoria (multi-purpose link along the rue Caron corridor).
Also concerned: rue de la Faune (phase 2), between rue de l'Apogée and the entrance to the Parc-O-Bus de la Faune, and boulevard du Loiret (phase 3), between rue de Chamonix and boulevard Louis-XIV.
The ministère's call for projects runs from August 31 to October 9, 2026; the amounts of financial assistance will be confirmed later by the minister.
The City commits to carrying out the projects according to the program's rules and acknowledges that the financial assistance would be cancelled if they are not followed.
The work concerned is planned for 2027 and is part of the Vision de la mobilité active 2023-2027.
The City is paying its 2026 membership fee to the Union des municipalités du Québec: $385,188.27 plus taxes, for the period from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The general membership fee ($346,560.27 plus taxes) is calculated at $0.583 per resident, based on a population of 594,443 people (2025 order in council).
An amount of $38,628 plus taxes goes to the "Carrefour du capital humain", calculated on the 2024 payroll of $838,252,562.
This service provides municipalities with information, training and representation in human resources and labour relations.
The total cost in net taxes comes to $404,399.53: $363,844.96 from the Direction générale's budget and $40,554.57 from the Ressources humaines budget.
The membership fee was $372,794.01 plus taxes in 2025, $355,197.75 in 2024 and $344,386.76 in 2023.
The City is awarding Apex Expert Conseil inc. (Lévis) a professional services contract worth $297,724 before taxes; the net expense comes to $312,572.98.
The contract covers the consolidation of the water and sewer systems on avenue Thornhill and in the neighbouring area, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The mandate covers data analysis, the preparatory study, design, plans and specifications, cost estimates and work supervision.
The work also includes rebuilding sidewalks and making geometric adjustments between rue du Père-Vimont, Grande Allée Ouest and boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest.
Seven bids were received and five were ranked; Apex obtained the highest final score with the lowest price.
The winning bid is 56.8% below the City's estimate, which was $689,931 before taxes.
The executive committee adopted the decision on April 15, 2026; the funds come from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3390.
The arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles approves the site planning and architectural integration plans for three residential construction projects.
Two permits concern rue de la Herse (3315 and 3319), in the Loretteville–Les Châtels district: a semi-detached building with one dwelling unit each.
One permit concerns 1226, rue de l'Embâcle, in the Val-Bélair district: a detached building with one dwelling unit.
The approvals follow the favourable recommendations of the comité consultatif d'urbanisme, which met on April 29, 2026.
No financial impact is indicated in the decision summary.
The Ville de Québec is granting a maximum subsidy of $300,000 to the Centre de création Limoilou (Manivelle), a non-profit organization located in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The money goes to the "Déploiement du Centre de création" project, in the église Saint-Charles-de-Limoilou, a classified heritage building.

The work includes a free training area (the jubé and the space in front of the maître-autel), safety mats and corridors, a new rental room, plans for washrooms on the ground floor, and improvements to the heating and electrical systems.
The project costs $373,000 in total: $300,000 from the City, $36,500 from the organization's own funds and $36,500 in services and equipment.
The organization plans to create 3 jobs; it currently has 1.
The subsidy comes from the Soutien aux projets structurants component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, funded by the gouvernement du Québec.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.

The La Cité-Limoilou borough council is ending the draft by-law that would have allowed goods to be stored on the ground floor of 844, boulevard Champlain (Vieux-Québec–Cap-Blanc–Colline parlementaire neighbourhood, Cap-aux-Diamants district).
The owner wanted to renovate the building, which has been vacant for a few years, and store goods there for a local business; the zoning only allows housing.
At the public meeting of June 9, 2025 and during the written consultation from June 10 to 16, 2025, citizens said they mostly disagreed and asked that a convenience store use be kept.
The conseil de quartier voted 8 to 0 to recommend refusing the request.
42 people attended the June 9, 2025 meeting, held at Espace Quatre Cents.
No financial impact is indicated in the file.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council is transferring to City managers the power to authorize the occupation of public property: public land, sidewalks, streets and lanes, both above and below ground.

For temporary occupations, the power goes to the director general, an assistant director general, the director of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets, the director of the Division des activités et de l'expertise immobilières and the section directors of that division.

For permanent occupations, the power goes to the director of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets, the director of the Division des activités et de l'expertise immobilières and the section directors of that division.

These managers set the conditions and the rent themselves, may set rules for the work and the materials, and may revoke an authorization by giving written notice to the owner at least one month in advance.
Permanent occupation authorizations must be reported to the executive committee every quarter, including the nature of the occupation, the name of the beneficiary and the amount of the rent.
The City justifies the change by the rise in requests tied to real estate transactions and the desire to standardize practices across the agglomeration.
The Ville de Québec is adopting a policy that sets the rules for all of its projects and services that use artificial intelligence.
The policy applies to the whole organization, including experiments, proofs of concept and integrations, not just formal projects.
It sets four objectives: complying with the law, managing risks (bias, security, confidentiality), ensuring algorithms are transparent, and guaranteeing ethics.

An AI governance committee will be created, with at least one representative from Technologies de l'information, one from the Service du greffe et des archives (personal information) and one from the units that use AI.
This committee will have to approve AI projects before they are rolled out and monitor risks.
The policy stems from the 2024-2029 strategic vision for information governance adopted in 2023.
The decision summary indicates no financial impact.
The City is paying out $16,900 in grants to eight organizations in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The money answers the applications submitted by June 15, 2026 under the programs of the Cadre de soutien aux organismes reconnus.

The largest amounts go to the Club Fadoq Sainte-Ursule ($5,198, year 2 of operating support), the Maison des jeunes de Cap-Rouge ($4,500, furniture and games) and the Club d'astronomie Cassiopée ($3,118, observation equipment).
Other grants: Ligue navale du Canada Cap-Rouge–St-Augustin $2,347 (shooting equipment), Maison Routhier $612 (weaving loom), Sinfonia $125 (Celtic music workshop).
Loisirs St-Benoît and the Popote roulante Ste-Foy each receive $500 for activities with their volunteers.
The funds come from the arrondissement's operating budget, under the "Soutien aux organismes" item.

The City awards Bouthillette Parizeau inc. a professional services contract in mechanical, electrical and telecommunications engineering worth $248,365 (before taxes), for a net expense of $260,752.20.
The mandate covers the restoration of the centre communautaire Paul-Émile-Beaulieu, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles, following a disaster.

The firm will prepare the plans and specifications and supervise the work: restoration of the basement and the ground floor, redevelopment and new rooms on the upper floor, assessment of the building's systems and verification of the elevator's compliance.
The plans and specifications are expected in October 2026 and delivery of the spaces during 2027.
Four bids were received; three were ranked. Bouthillette Parizeau obtained the highest final score.

The selected price exceeds the requesting department's estimate of $121,800 by 103.9%; the City explains this by the tight schedule, the scarcity of engineering resources and the addition, during the call for tenders, of the redevelopment of the bowling area and the kitchenette (about $40K).
The funds come from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3396.
The City is entrusting the organization Les Loisirs Montcalm inc. with the programming and supervision of free swim periods at the outdoor pool in parc du Musée, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The agreement covers 26 months, from June 18, 2026 to August 20, 2028.
Total cost: $101,694.60, exempt from GST and QST.
The expense is divided into $32,898.60 in 2026, $33,886.44 in 2027 and $34,909.56 in 2028.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
The previous agreement with the organization ended on August 17, 2025.
The borough president and the assistant borough clerk are authorized to sign the agreement.
The City is giving $28,974 to the Ligue de Dodgeball de Québec for its Dodgeball Communauté Accueillante project, from August 2026 to March 2027.
The project aims to bring immigrants and the host society closer together through playing dodgeball.
On the program: 16 introductory activities, 2 sport sessions per week over 2 sessions of 10 weeks, and 6 social activities.
The total cost of the project is estimated at $32,329.33; the grant covers 89.62% of the bill.
The organization is working with Motivaction Jeunesse, the Centre R.I.R.E. 2000 and Accès-Loisirs Québec.
The organization will have to mention the support of the City and of the ministère de l'Immigration, and submit a report on the activities and a financial report.
The money comes from the budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire, as part of the Plan d'action municipal de l'immigration 2024-2026.
The Ville de Québec is giving a grant of up to $120,000 to the Rassemblement pour l'alimentation durable et l'innovation solidaire, a non-profit organization created in 2025.
The money will be used to start up a community food hub at the pavillon Alphonse-Desjardins of Université Laval, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The hub will bring together a community grocery store, a cafeteria, ready-to-eat meals and a catering service for the university community.

The project lasts seven months and costs $220,000 in total: $120,000 from the City, $40,000 from Université Laval, $50,000 from the Caisse Desjardins Université Laval and $10,000 from the organization.
The organization expects to create 14 jobs.
The grant comes from the food system development and promotion component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030; it does not have to be paid back.
The decision must be made by the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The City is awarding the contract for the Employee Assistance Program, for its employees and their families, to GreenShield Santé, of Toronto.
The contract covers January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2029, for an estimated amount of $830,856.20 (plus GST and QST).
The net expense, after recovering the QST, is estimated at $872,276.92.
The option chosen is "extended access", rather than a set number of sessions.
The contract can be renewed four times, for 12-month periods, with an annual adjustment based on the Consumer Price Index.
Four companies submitted bids; GreenShield obtained the best final score and the lowest price.
The amounts remain conditional on the adoption of the 2027 to 2029 budgets.
The City is appointing Pieter Agneessens to the board of directors of the Réseau de transport de la Capitale (RTC), as a public transit user.
His term is four years, starting September 1, 2026, and lasts until he is replaced or appointed again.
He replaces Annie Sanfaçon, whose term was to end on November 17, 2026, but who is leaving at the beginning of September.
The RTC had put out a call for applications for this position; a selection committee chose his application.
According to the document, he is an RTC user and works as a strategic advisor in sustainable mobility, with 25 years of experience with public transit companies.
The RTC board of directors has 12 members appointed by the conseil d'agglomération of Québec.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 1004, boulevard Pie-XI Sud, in the Val-Bélair neighbourhood (Arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The future commercial building may be built 7.39 metres from the rear property line, instead of the 12 metres normally required.
The project is the construction of a veterinary clinic, classified as a retail sales and service establishment.
Condition imposed: the owner must install a fence that is more than 80% opaque along the rear property line, to limit nuisances between the business and residents.
According to the analysis on file, the strict standard limited the depth and floor area of the building and interfered with the interior layout of the clinic.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour on August 12, 2026.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council confirms the City's intention to remove general tourist accommodation establishments (C10 uses) from zone 13003Md, in the Vieux-Québec area and its surroundings.
Until the planning by-law is amended, the City is suspending the approval of construction plans and the issuing of permits or certificates that would go against this intention.
The City explains that it aims to create new housing and bring new residents to Vieux-Québec, an area that already has a large number of tourist accommodation establishments.
The City plans to analyze the neighbourhood's tourist accommodation dynamics before proposing new zoning.
The executive committee's notice of intention, given on June 19, 2026, also covered zone 13035Md, ratified by the city council on July 7, 2026.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City is changing the zoning of a piece of land it owns in the Sillery neighbourhood (Saint-Louis–Sillery district), near rue de la Crête, the railway and impasse des Cageux.
Part of lot 6 735 338 is going from zone 31517Rb to zone 33725Ha, which allows housing on this land.
This change makes it possible to combine three lots to create a buildable piece of land with a potential of three to six housing units.
No siting or height standards are being changed: buildings will have to respect the size already allowed in the zone.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The conseil de quartier de Sillery will give its opinion and hold the public consultation meeting; interested people will have seven days after that meeting to send their comments in writing.
The Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough council was aiming for a decision on August 27, 2026.
The City is changing traffic rules on rue des Acadiens, in Charlesbourg, as it approaches boulevard Henri-Bourassa.
At that intersection, the centre lane will be used only for left turns, and the right lane for going straight ahead and for right turns.
Bike lanes are being added on both sides of rue des Acadiens, between Henri-Bourassa and rue des Amérindiens, reserved for cyclists from May 1 to October 31.
Parking becomes prohibited at all times on both sides of this section of rue des Acadiens.
These changes remove 8 winter parking spaces and 9 spaces available at all times.
More than 20,000 vehicles travel through the intersection of des Acadiens and Henri-Bourassa each day, according to the document.
The City is giving $5,000 to the Fondation Aléo.
The money supports the event "Aux Jeux pour les athlètes," held at the Terminal de Croisière in Québec.
The event, organized with the Société hôtesse des Jeux du Canada 2027, is meant to raise funds for the Games and the Foundation.
The recommendation gives the date of March 26, 2026, while the text also mentions March 26 of this coming year.
The Jeux du Canada will take place in Québec from February 27 to March 14, 2027.
The amount comes entirely from the City's funds, under the grant management activity.
The City is amending its ÉquiMobilité program, the reduced public transit fare for low-income people.
As of July 1, 2026, fares will go from $50 to $51 for the monthly pass and from $2 to $2.05 for the single-ride fare.
Fares will now be indexed every July 1, by the same percentage as the social assistance indexation applied in January.
Eligibility applications will be submitted in person or by mail at the service centres of La Cité-Limoilou, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge and Charlesbourg, which is being added.
Eligibility is confirmed for a period of 2 years; the photo ID may be provided as a copy if the application arrives by mail.
The definition of "sponsor" (répondant) is simplified: a person working for an organization who has known the applicant for at least two years.
The City will no longer cover the cost of issuing smart cards in the calculation of the compensation paid to the Réseau de transport de la Capitale.
Ville de Québec is buying from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable a 22,167.40-square-metre lot located along boulevard Pierre-Bertrand, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The price is $4,230,000, plus applicable taxes, based on an appraisal done by an outside firm.
The lot will be used to widen boulevard Pierre-Bertrand and to protect the water main located there.
The lot is sold without warranty and at the City's risk. The City will have to pay the notary and the costs related to the transaction.
Equipment belonging to Hydro-Québec, Bell Canada and Énergir is located on the lot; no servitude will be granted by the ministère.
The ministère's offer expires if the City does not accept it before October 1, 2026, and the notarial deed must be signed within 180 days.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1836 on municipal infrastructure work.
The City is amending the official list of unionized professional jobs.
Two job titles move from salary class 2 to class 3: event planning advisor, and international relations advisor.
This change follows a decision by the joint job evaluation committee.
The City and the Alliance du personnel professionnel de la Ville de Québec signed a letter of agreement on April 7, 2026 to make these changes official.
The agreement forms an integral part of the collective agreement in force.
The Service des ressources humaines will update all the documents concerned.
No financial impact is stated in the document; the decision falls to the Québec urban agglomeration council.
The borough council of Arrondissement des Rivières is renewing two terms on the planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme), from May 26, 2026 to May 26, 2028.
Suzanne Hénault is reappointed as a member who lives in the borough and is named vice-chair of the committee.
Richard Charpentier is reappointed as a member who lives in the borough.
The two previous terms were ending on May 27, 2026.
The committee has seven members: one to three elected members of the borough council and residents of the area; each term lasts two years.
The document does not provide for any financial impact.
The City is extending the deadlines given to developers taking part in the temporary program to support the construction of rental housing.
The deadline to begin the work set out in the agreement goes from 6 to 18 months after signing.
The deadline to obtain partial acceptance of the work goes from 18 to 36 months after signing.
The program provides a residential tax credit of up to 10 years to cover part of the municipal infrastructure (water mains, sewers, sidewalks, new streets, stormwater management, public square).
To be eligible, the agreement with the developer must be signed between January 1, 2024 and December 31, 2027.
The City states that the changes will not cause the program's maximum budget, set at $35M, to be exceeded.
A developer wants to build an 11-storey commercial building with 85 tourist accommodation units at 304, boulevard Charest Est, in Saint-Roch.
The by-law requires 31 parking spaces; the project provides for 12. The developer is therefore asking to be exempted for the 19 missing spaces.
The City is granting the exemption on the condition that the owner pay $37,500 into the « Fonds de stationnement » (parking fund).
The payment must be made no later than 30 days after the resolution is adopted by the borough council.
The Service du transport notes that the area (permit zone 12) has about 334 spaces for 320 permits issued, with paid parking, large parking lots and very good public transit service nearby.
The City is changing the rules that say who can sign its contracts and documents in place of the mayor.
All the signing rules, which until now were scattered throughout the by-law, are brought together in one place.
Any employee who already holds a delegation of power will be able to sign, on their own, the contracts and documents needed to apply it.
The list of people authorized to sign includes, among others, directors and assistant directors, as well as employees in procurement, a City land surveyor and the directors of certain departments.
Notarized documents (with one exception), by-laws and resolutions will continue to be signed by the mayor and the city clerk.
The mayor keeps the power to disapprove obligations and contracts approved by the council or the executive committee.
The by-law comes into force as soon as it is adopted.
The City is banning parking at all times on both sides of rue Vézina, between avenue Lapierre and rue George-Muir, in the borough of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
About 176 on-street parking spaces will disappear; residents will no longer be able to park their vehicles in this section.
The decision aims to improve the safety of pedestrians and cyclists, who have to travel on unimproved shoulders because there is no sidewalk.
The roadway is 7 metres wide, and the lanes become very narrow when vehicles are parked along the side.
The change follows requests from citizens and an analysis by the Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente.
According to the City's observations, on-street parking is generally little used in this section.

On March 26, 2026, the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec authorized the demolition of the main building located at 3590, rue Raymond-Marie, in the Vieux-Moulin neighbourhood in Beauport.
The urban agglomeration council takes note of this decision and confirms that it will not use its power of disallowance; it also shortens the 90-day period provided for by law.
The City will therefore be able to issue the authorization certificate for the demolition.

The Commission based its decision on an engineer's report dated January 21, 2026, concluding that the building requires major work, notably structural work, and on the fact that it is not eligible for restoration grants.

The demolition is conditional: the replacement project (permit application 20260107-052), which would increase the supply of housing in the area, will have to be adjusted according to the Commission's recommendations.
No written comments and no objections were received, and no one requested a review of the decision within the 30-day period.
The document indicates that there is no financial impact.
The City is hiring two companies to mow the retention basins on its territory, from the awarding of the contract until November 30, 2028.
Gazon 911 inc. is awarded lot 17 (mowing basins without collecting the clippings) for $289,585.50, plus taxes.
Intermodale Paysagement Déneigement inc. is awarded lot 18 (mowing basins with collection of the clippings) for $252,413.46, plus taxes.
The total net expense comes to $569,031.15, split into three portions of $189,677.05 for 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
Eight bids were received for these two lots; the other lots in call for tenders 94928 are dealt with elsewhere.
The City is authorizing the installation of a generator in the front yard of 3666, chemin Royal, on the avenue de la Station side, in the Vieux-Moulin neighbourhood in Beauport.
The Beauport planning by-law normally requires a generator to be placed in a side yard or a back yard.
The property is a corner lot bordered by four streets: it has neither a side yard nor a back yard, which made any compliant installation impossible.
The applicant says the generator is needed for the safety of the occupants and to maintain the building's essential services in the event of a power outage.
A fence and a plant screen will be installed around the generator, which will be used only in an emergency or for periodic testing.
The Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec gave a favourable opinion, on the condition that the landscaping and visual screen requirements are met.
The Beauport planning advisory committee unanimously recommended the exemption on March 26, 2026.

The City is awarding Veolia Water Technologies & Solutions Canada GP the supply and delivery of filter media for the station de traitement des eaux usées Est, at 105, chemin de la Baie-de-Beauport (La Cité-Limoilou).
The contract is worth $292,001.29 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $306,564.85.
Two bids were received: the one from Brault Maxtech inc. ($291,600.00) was found technically non-compliant.
After negotiation, Veolia lowered its price from $299,425.00 to $292,001.29.
The price is 27.5% higher than the $228,947.37 estimate, which the City attributes to the rise in transportation fees and energy costs in early 2026.
The funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1719 on the modernization of water treatment plants.

The City is awarding Consulis environnement de bureau inc. (Québec) the supply and installation of furniture for the future multi-purpose curling centre, at 1020, rue des Rocailles, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The contract is worth $305,500 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $320,736.81.
The furniture must be delivered and installed no later than October 30, 2026.
The contract covers, among other things, chairs, stools, office armchairs, meeting and service tables, outdoor furniture and transport carts.
Two bids were received: the one from MAB Profil inc. ($224,059.35) was found to be technically non-compliant, leaving only one compliant offer.
After negotiation, the supplier lowered its price from $309,714.90 to $305,500; the gap with the City's estimate ($278,600) is 9.7%.
The funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1725 related to the construction of the curling centre.
The City is amending its agreement with Lacodev inc. concerning the maximum grant of $626,000 paid under the Fonds pour soutenir les projets durables en habitation.
The money is going to a mixed-use real estate project located at 401, rue Saint-Paul (373 to 401, rue Saint-Paul and 1020 to 1030, rue des Prairies).
The City is giving up its mortgage guarantee on the building (full release of the mortgage published under number 29 985 643), before the end of the agreement.
This release is requested to allow the project to be financed by Financière CMLS, in accordance with CMHC requirements.
Despite the release, Lacodev inc. remains required to meet its commitments and the City keeps its legal remedies.
The deadlines are pushed back: the second payment of 50% of the grant will be paid no later than March 31, 2027, with the request to be made between September 1 and November 30, 2026.
The decision was adopted by city council on August 25, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is reselling sub-licences for ESRI mapping software to the RTC for three years, from February 15, 2026 to February 14, 2029.
The RTC reimburses the City for all of the costs: $398,952.50 in total, billed each year ($126,667.42, then $132,651.71, then $139,633.37).
The City provides the RTC with a set number of ArcGIS licences per year, as well as one annual pass to the ESRI international user conference.
The agreement is retroactive to February 2026: the previous contract ended on February 14, 2026, and the time needed to finalize the contract with ESRI Canada delayed the approval.
The RTC wants to use the same platform as its partners (Ville de Québec, Communauté métropolitaine de Québec, Société de transport de Lévis) in order to share information.
The City undertakes to comply with the conditions of the contract with ESRI and to take up the RTC's defence in the event of a lawsuit related to these conditions.
The revenue paid by the RTC will go into a recoverable project to be created.
The City of Québec is giving up to $416,000 to the Chambre de commerce et d'industrie de Québec.
The money goes to the ALIAS project, which helps businesses in the Capitale-Nationale region adopt artificial intelligence.
The project includes a digital platform, a process to assess businesses' needs, and a network of AI experts.
"Bons d'accompagnement en IA" (BonIA) vouchers will be rolled out, with support for prototypes and pilot projects.
The project costs $520,300 in total: the City pays $416,000 and the organization contributes $104,300 in services.
The project is expected to create 1 job and maintain 2 jobs; the head office is in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The decision is up to the Québec urban agglomeration council.
The City is applying for financial assistance from the ministère de l'Éducation to install signs in its nature parks (recreational, sports and outdoor infrastructure program, component 2).
The signs will be for hiking trails, cross-country ski trails and mountain bike trails.
Parc Chauveau: new signs for the hiking and cross-country ski trails built in 2026, and for mountain biking in 2027.
Parc naturel du Mont-Bélair: upgrading of signs dating from 2009 and new signs for the trail currently being built and the one linking avenue de la Montagne Ouest to the summit.
Parc linéaire de la Rivière-Saint-Charles: signs upgraded at parc des Saules and parc de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres.
Parc de la Rivière-du-Berger and parc du marais Isabelle: new signs for the hiking trails.
The City commits to paying its share of the eligible costs; the program ends on March 31, 2027.
The registration tax on passenger vehicles goes from $61.10 to $63.00 for the year 2027.
The tax applies to people whose address on file with the SAAQ is located within the territory of the Ville de Québec.
The increase follows the indexation set out in the by-law, based on a 3.1% change in the consumer price index for the Québec region (12 months ending June 30, 2026).
The City must send the new amount to the SAAQ no later than October 1, for it to take effect on January 1, 2027.
The City estimates additional annual revenue of $600,000, after deducting the 2% collection fee charged by the SAAQ.
The money is used to fund the City's share of urban agglomeration spending on public transit.
The La Haute-Saint-Charles borough council approves three permit applications related to the appearance and siting of buildings (PIIA).
All three projects are in the Val-Bélair district; no applications are listed for Lac-Saint-Charles–Saint-Émile or Loretteville–Les Châtels.
At 1516, rue de l'Esquif: construction of a detached single-dwelling building.
At 1225, rue de l'Embâcle: construction of a detached single-dwelling building.
At 1216, rue de l'Embâcle: modification of a parking area in order to build a detached accessory building.
The approvals follow the favourable recommendations of the comité consultatif d'urbanisme, which met on May 27, 2026.
No financial impact is indicated in the decision summary.
A councillor is asking the City to improve traffic flow in Val-Bélair: mark a third lane on boulevard Pie-XI, contact the ministère des Transports, and table a timeline with council.

The City instead recommends adopting an amended, more general text: continue the analysis, design and implementation of the measures already identified for the area. The marking of a third lane and the timeline are therefore no longer being requested as such.
A study commissioned from a consultant led to 32 recommendations in the fall of 2023. It identifies boulevard Pie-XI and the Pie-XI / avenue Industrielle intersection as the main bottlenecks.

Measures already completed: new traffic light programming, an arterial management system on Pie-XI and Industrielle, sidewalks, a school route for école de la Myriade on rue de l'Etna, the redevelopment of rue Jean-Bardot, the Métrobus 804, and the lengthening of a right-turn lane near autoroute Henri-IV.
In preparation: a redevelopment concept for the Pie-XI / Industrielle intersection and a study to create a centre left-turn lane on Pie-XI, between avenue Industrielle and avenue de l'Amiral.

A memorandum of understanding signed with the ministère des Transports, L'Ancienne-Lorette, the Commission de la capitale nationale and the Aéroport de Québec provides for a development concept for the route de l'Aéroport between Wilfrid-Hamel and avenue Notre-Dame; a call for tenders is planned for the fall.
Once a development concept is completed, carrying out the work usually takes two to five years.
The City is adding stop signs on chemin Royal, at the east and west approaches to the intersection with avenue Poulin, in Beauport.
It is also adding stop signs on avenue Royale, at the east and west approaches to the intersection with avenue des Cascades.
