A pedestrian crossing with signs and pavement markings will be set up on chemin Royal, at the intersection with avenue Lortie.
The stops apply to drivers as well as cyclists.
Pavement markings will be adjusted at the three intersections.
The changes aim to improve the safety of pedestrians and road users; residents had filed requests concerning chemin Royal.
These intersections have RTC bus stops and between 6,000 and 7,500 vehicles a day on the main roads.
The City is naming a new street "rue de la Goutte-de-Lait," in the arrondissement des Rivières (district de Neufchâtel-Lebourgneuf).
This street serves a residential project built on former farmland left unused, west of rue de la Griotte, east of boulevard Pierre-Bertrand and north of boulevard Lebourgneuf.
The street starts at the intersection of rue du Griffon and rue de la Griotte; this is phase 1 of the project.
Phase 2, which will come later, would extend the street as far as rue des Groseilles.

The name recalls the Association des gouttes de lait, founded in 1915 by the Société Saint-Vincent-de-Paul and prominent Québec citizens to distribute milk and offer services to children under one year of age, which operated until the 1960s.
The name follows the theme of the area, where street names begin with the letter G; the Commission de toponymie du Québec has confirmed the spelling.
The City is adopting a new Records Management Policy, which replaces the 2008 policy.
The policy applies to all administrative units, as well as to employees, consultants, suppliers and partners who use the City's information.
Each administrative unit becomes responsible for managing its own records and must report to the Direction générale on its records management.
The Service du greffe et des archives oversees records management, produces the guides and keeps up to date the retention schedule approved by Bibliothèque et Archives nationales du Québec.
The Service du greffe et des archives collects and permanently preserves records of heritage value.
The Service des technologies de l'information provides the digital storage space and the means to destroy records within the prescribed time limits.
Working documents, drafts, copies, multiple versions, books and newspapers are not covered by the policy.
The City is authorizing the construction of a 24-classroom elementary school in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The land in question is located east of the rivière du Cap Rouge, south of the autoroute Félix-Leclerc, west of the autoroute Duplessis and north of the boulevard du Versant-Nord.
The by-law allows education and training facility uses as well as gathering place uses on this land.
The maximum height of the main building goes from 9 m to 14 m, and the "public or recreational" signage standards apply.
The planning rules for the other lots in the same zone do not change.
A public consultation meeting must be held on this project.
No financial impact is indicated in the file.
The City is paying $3,000 to the Société du Domaine de Maizerets for activities during the 2026 spring break week "À Québec, on bouge!", from February 28 to March 8, 2026.
The activities were held at the Domaine de Maizerets, in the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou, rain or shine.
On the program: the Mr.Palette sugar shack on February 28, a giant games day on March 6, and Mini-bus 1,2,3 GO! Limoilou on March 7, with free use of the equipment on March 6 and 7.
In 2025, the same organization had received $1,000 for the spring break week.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The executive committee adopted the decision on May 13, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 1400, avenue Joseph-Rousseau, in the Sillery neighbourhood, to allow the construction of an attached garage.
The garage will be allowed to encroach 2.0 metres into the secondary front setback facing rue de Bergerville, which the planning by-law normally prohibits.
The garage will also be allowed to be built 3.5 metres from the sidewalk, instead of the required minimum of 4.0 metres.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme recommended granting the exemption on August 11, 2026, and the borough council adopted the decision on August 27, 2026.
According to the analysis, the irregular shape of the lot, a through corner lot with three front setbacks, limits the places where a compliant garage could be built.
The current garage will be demolished and rebuilt; the document does not anticipate any financial impact for the City.
The Ville de Québec is lending up to $200,000 to the company Alias, ligne de signalement inc., which has its head office in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The money comes from the Fonds local d'investissement, a business loan program entrusted to the City by the Government of Quebec.
The loan will be used to bring ALIAS 3.0+, a complaint management module with artificial intelligence, to market in Canada and Europe (Belgium and Switzerland).
The project costs $500,000 in total: $200,000 as a loan from the City and $300,000 as a loan from a financial institution.
The company expects to keep its 13 current jobs and create 15 new ones within two years.
The project provides for the hiring of specialists (national sales, international development, digital marketing, certifications) and for obtaining certifications.
Two people are acting as joint and several guarantors of the company's obligations; the Fund's review committee gave a favourable opinion on June 25, 2026.
The City is awarding a contract to Ethnoscop inc., of Boucherville, for archaeological digs at the monastère des Ursulines-de-Québec, in Vieux-Québec.
The contract is worth $386,279.50 (plus GST and QST); the net cost to the City is $405,545.19.
The work runs from the signing of the contract until September 30, 2027.
The work has two parts and is meant to support the design of the project to convert the monastery, led by the Fiducie du patrimoine culturel des Ursulines.
The contract is being awarded without a public call for tenders, with the City citing the heritage value of the service required.
The money comes from a loan by-law tied to the Entente de développement culturel 2024-2026 signed with the ministre de la Culture et des Communications.
The Ville de Québec will submit its application for Vélosympathique certification, a program launched in 2015 by Vélo Québec Association.
The certification looks at five areas: bike infrastructure, education, incentives, planning, and fair access to cycling.
The City wants to encourage a shift to cycling during the TramCité project construction work, to reduce car traffic near the work sites.
Being certified would help the City with its applications for financial assistance under the Quebec TAPU program, which now asks whether the municipality is certified.
The City also sees it as support for its bids to host national and international conventions and events.
In 2025, about fifteen Quebec municipalities were certified, including Montréal (Gold), Laval (Silver) and Sherbrooke (Bronze).
The City authorizes an international relations advisor, Sarah-Ève Huot, to accompany the mayor to Belgium (Namur and Brussels) from June 6 to 13, 2026.
It authorizes an expense of $4,670 for airfare, ground transportation and accommodation costs, upon presentation of supporting documents, when the AIMF and the partner cities do not pay them.
The mayor will take part in the work of the Board of the Association internationale des maires francophones (AIMF), of which he is vice-president and of which Québec is a founding city.
Meetings are planned with Namur, Bordeaux, Paris, Nantes, Lausanne and Brussels, partner cities of Québec.
The mayor will also accompany Université Laval in meetings with European partners on sustainable health and compassionate cities.

The funds come from the operating budget of the Service de la coordination stratégique et des relations internationales; a difference of no more than 10% of the amount is accepted without further authorization.
The Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is giving $100 to the "Scouts du district de Québec inc.", also known as the "10e groupe scout Montcalm".
The request comes from councillor Catherine Vallières-Roland.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, under the activity "Soutenir les conseils d'arrondissement" (Supporting borough councils).
According to the analysis, the organization meets the criteria for this type of grant.
The borough council adopted resolution CA1-2026-0085 on April 27, 2026.
A developer wants to build a six-unit building at 2661, boulevard Louis-XIV, in Beauport (Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux district).
The zoning by-law requires seven parking spaces; the project provides six.
The City is exempting the owner from providing the seventh space, in exchange for a payment of $500 to the Fonds de stationnement (parking fund).
The payment must be made no later than 30 days after the borough council adopts the resolution.
According to the City's analysis, the area is well served by public transit and the on-street parking occupancy rate there is low.
Parking is not regulated on this section of boulevard Louis-XIV, but a parking ban could be put in place if vehicles park there.
The City wants to acquire a strip of land of about 15.2 square metres along rue de la Faune, in the borough of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
This land would be used to widen rue de la Faune, as part of the project to rebuild this street.
The purchase would be made by agreement with the owner, or by expropriation if the discussions do not succeed.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the acquisition or expropriation proceedings.
The Division de l'arpentage et de la géomatique will prepare the plans, the technical descriptions and the cadastral operations required.
The entire property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $153,000, or $1.4 per square metre.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 on the work to redevelop rue de la Faune.
The City is exempting the owner of 1965, avenue Maufils (La Cité-Limoilou, Maizerets-Lairet district) from providing the parking space required by the zoning by-law.
In exchange, she must pay $500 to the "Fonds de stationnement" (parking fund), no later than 30 days after the borough council adopts the resolution.
The project involves converting a two-unit building into a tourist accommodation unit.
No parking space can be provided because there is no room on the lot.
The area is part of parking permit zone 27: about 474 on-street spaces for residents and 110 permits issued by the City.
The City notes that the area is well served by public transit.
The Ville de Québec is giving a grant of up to $150,000 to Laboratoires Bodycad inc., a company that makes custom orthopaedic products, located in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The money is for a project to develop markets in Asia and the Middle East: finding distributors, adapting regulatory processes, and taking part in orthopaedic conferences.
The project costs $1,204,750 in total: $729,750 from the shareholders, $300,000 as a loan from Développement économique Canada, $25,000 from Can Export and $150,000 from the City.
The grant does not have to be paid back and covers a maximum of 50% of eligible expenses, according to the rules of the Capitale-Innovation component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030.
The company has 52 jobs and expects to create 3 new ones tied to the project.
The Vision entrepreneuriale analysis committee recommended the project on March 10, 2026; follow-up will be done through an economic benefits form.
The funds come from the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale, which the Government of Québec has delegated to the City.
The City is transferring $10,690,775 from the budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire to its six boroughs to fund the Programme Vacances-Été 2026.
This money will be used to enter into agreements with 21 organizations that run day camps.
Breakdown by borough: La Haute-Saint-Charles $2,396,370, La Cité-Limoilou $2,355,720, Charlesbourg $2,157,705, Les Rivières $1,814,980, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge $1,130,000 and Beauport $836,000.
The support for each organization is calculated using a fixed amount plus an amount per child, estimated based on the previous year's registrations.
Each borough council will then decide on the grants paid to its day camp organizations.
Since the amounts are estimates, a report on the adjustments will be presented later in 2026, after the organizations report back on their spending.
The 2025 ($11,277,868.07) and 2024 ($10,532,937.50) transfers followed the same formula.
The City is awarding Mega Technical Holdings Ltd. (Sainte-Catherine) a contract worth $368,212.22 before taxes for protective components for police vehicles.
These parts will be used to outfit 87 new Ford Interceptor vehicles, planned for 2026.
The contract includes an option for 25 additional units of each component, at a cost of $120,340.25 before taxes.
If the City exercises this option, notice must be given no later than October 1, 2026, and delivery completed before December 31, 2026.
The components include kits that replace the seats to create a holding cell for transporting detainees, as well as push-type bumpers.
Three bids were received and found to be compliant; the lowest is 6.5% below the City's estimate ($393,625 before taxes).
The net expense for the urban agglomeration, after the QST refund, comes to $386,576.80.
The City is transferring $380,000 from the agglomeration reserve set aside for snow removal to the unallocated agglomeration surplus (which can be used freely).
This transfer brings the agglomeration snow removal reserve down to the new target of $2,020,000, instead of $2,400,000.
The total target for snow removal stays at $20,000,000: the split changes, going to $2,020,000 on the agglomeration side and $17,980,000 on the local (proximity) side.
This new split comes from a by-law adopted on December 17, 2025, which sets the agglomeration share of Service des travaux publics expenses at 10.1%.
At the same time, a $380,000 transfer will be proposed to the city council to top up the local (proximity) snow removal reserve.
The urban agglomeration council was to make its decision on June 17, 2026.
The City wants to obtain a temporary easement of about 53.9 m² on a piece of land alongside boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, for the TramCité tramway project.
This construction and access easement would last about 13 months and would be used in particular to set up temporary traffic lanes during the work.
The City may buy the easement by mutual agreement or go through expropriation; discussions with the owners may continue during the proceedings.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to withdraw from the expropriation proceedings if the project no longer needs the easement.
The land in question is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $364,000, or $741.95 per square metre.
The funds come from the urban agglomeration's loan by-law for the structuring public transit network.
The City is buying waterworks and sewer materials (pipes, fittings, valves, manholes, catch basins) to maintain the networks across the whole territory of Québec.
The contracts run from July 2, 2026 to July 1, 2028, with the possibility of a 12-month extension with price indexation.
J.U. Houle ltée is awarded lots 1, 3, 4, 5 and 8, for estimated amounts ranging from $153,799.40 to $799,190.70 (before taxes).
Emco Corporation is awarded lots 6, 7, 9, 14, 17 and 18, including lot 7 estimated at $1,608,891.37 and lot 18 at $1,515,206.17 (before taxes).
Wolseley Canada inc. is awarded lots 11, 12 and 20, including lot 20 estimated at $1,294,311.21 (before taxes); Réal Huot inc. is awarded lot 15 at $198,496.83 (before taxes).
The net expenditure is estimated at $11,326,813.57, subject to the approval of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.
Lots 2, 10, 13, 16, 19 and 21 were awarded elsewhere, under the delegation of powers.
A city councillor, Stéphane Lachance, proposed on July 7, 2026 that the City ask to acquire or receive the statue of Samuel de Champlain owned by the Ville d'Orillia.
The Service de la culture et du patrimoine recommends not proceeding with this proposal.
The City considers that Champlain is already very present on its territory: the monument on the terrasse Dufferin, boulevard Champlain, and the promenade Samuel-De Champlain.
The existing monument on the terrasse Dufferin will require major restoration work estimated at between $2 million and $3 million.
The City prefers to focus its resources on preserving the current monument rather than installing a second one.
The City is authorizing the Société canadienne du cancer to hold a street fundraiser on June 20, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m.
The collection will take place at the intersection of 3e Avenue and 4e Rue, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The activity will be held rain or shine.
The money raised will go to the organization's Relais pour la vie.
The Service de police and the Centre de gestion de la mobilité intelligente will monitor the event for the safety of the collectors.
In previous years, the collection was held elsewhere, notably at the corner of boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest and avenue Cartier.
The City is hiring Patrick Tremblay as assistant director of the Service de police, following internal/external competition CADRR-029-2026.
His annual salary is set at $200,553, according to the salary scale for managers of the Direction générale (2026 scale).
Until now, he held the position of inspector at the Direction adjointe de la surveillance du territoire of the Service de police.
The contract is for an indefinite term; the employee may leave with four weeks' notice and the City must give 3 to 12 months' notice.
He reports to the director of the Service de police and must devote all his time to his position, without working for another employer.
The funds, including employee benefits, come from the territory surveillance budget.
The file is submitted to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 258, rue Laflèche, in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood (Arrondissement de Beauport).
The owner will be allowed to enlarge the parking area, which will extend 7.5 metres in front of the house's façade instead of the maximum of 3 metres set out in the by-law.
Condition imposed: only one access driveway may be built on the property.
The goal is to allow two vehicles to be parked side by side, despite the irregular shape of the lot and the position of the building.
According to the analysis, this layout makes less ground impermeable than a compliant layout with two separate access driveways.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme de Beauport voted unanimously in favour on June 11, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption to the owner of 7044, rue du Brisebois, in Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf (Arrondissement des Rivières).
The owner wants to add a solarium in the backyard, on a concrete slab that is already there.
First exception: the solarium will be allowed to take up as much as 50% of the width of the rear wall within the 7.5-metre setback, instead of the maximum of 40% set out in the by-law.

Second exception: the rear façade and the right side façade will be allowed to be covered with stone or brick at a minimum of 70%, instead of 90%. The project calls for 73% brick at the rear and 85% on the right side.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion by majority on June 1, 2026; the borough council was to make its decision on July 9, 2026.
No amount of money is attached to this decision.
The City is awarding SST Consultants inc. (Québec) the management of health and safety on the work sites of segments TW-01 to TW-06A of the TramCité project.
The contract is estimated at $1,501,500 before taxes, for a net expense of $1,576,387.31.
The mandate runs from the date the contract is awarded until December 31, 2027, with a permanent presence on the work site.
The firm will oversee the safety of workers and of the public on the work sites for the preparatory municipal infrastructure work.
Three bids were received; the other ranked firm was judged non-compliant because it lacked authorization from the Autorité des marchés publics.
The selected price is 26% below the requesting department's estimate of $2,029,125.
The funding comes from two loan by-laws: $1,406,047.52 and $170,339.80 (net of taxes).
The executive committee takes note of the list of additional expenses of more than $250,000 authorized by delegated employees, for the week of February 15 to 21, 2026.
Only one additional expense appears in the report: $380,516.40 (before taxes) for the work site to repair the building envelope and roof of the Bibliothèque Paul-Aimé Paiement.

These added works include a clean strip, the removal of a stump, temporary shoring, changes to the location of the electric charging stations and their access ramp, as well as modifications to the parapet and the dormers of the college.
The contract goes from $6,919,309.20 to $6,538,792.80 according to the report, its initial value being $5,479,157.00.
The expense falls under the Service de la gestion des immeubles.
The City is adding $67,450 (plus taxes) to the contract of lawyer Me Josée Dumoulin, of La Prairie, bringing the total to $154,400 (plus taxes).
This contract is for defending the City in grievances about the use of actuarial gains from its employees' pension plans.
The original contract, awarded in April 2025, covered the period from April 1, 2025 to December 31, 2026 for $86,950 (plus taxes).
The additional money covers five hearing days planned for 2026 and the preparation hours, for grievances related to the actuarial valuation of December 31, 2021.
The net expense is estimated at $70,814.07 and will be paid out of the operating budget of the Service des ressources humaines.
The lawyer is paid by the hour; the contract was awarded without a call for tenders, an option provided for by law for legal services related to a legal proceeding.
The City extended the two-way bike and pedestrian path on the east side of boulevard Raymond, from south of avenue Clemenceau to rue Yves-Prévost.
The work added 321 metres of multi-use path, notably for the crossing over autoroute Félix-Leclerc.
The work began in the summer of 2023 and was completed in the spring of 2025.
The ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable granted funding of up to $298,245; the City has already received $238,596 (80%).
The eligible expenses reported total $661,245.78 (net of taxes); the invoices come from Groupe ABS and Construction et pavage Portneuf.
The urban agglomeration council takes note of the end-of-work report in order to obtain the final payment of the grant.
The document states that there is no financial impact for the City.
The City is buying bulk 12% sodium hypochlorite (a water treatment product) for its water treatment plants, pumping stations and pools.
The contract for lot 1 (deliveries of 30,000 litres) goes to Sodrox Chemicals Ltd., for an estimated amount of $372,360.00 before taxes.
The contract for lot 5 (deliveries of 100 to 2,500 litres) goes to Javel Bois-Francs inc., for an estimated amount of $223,925.70 before taxes.
Both contracts run from the date they are awarded until June 30, 2027, with the possibility of two 12-month renewals and an annual price adjustment for inflation.
The net cost to the City is estimated at $626,025.45, subject to approval of the 2027 budget.
Four companies submitted bids for lot 1 and two for lot 5; lots 3, 4 and 6 were awarded through delegation of powers and lot 2 is being handled separately.

The City wants to allow the construction of a building with about 45 housing units on part of the grounds of the église Saint-Ignace-de-Loyola, at 3325-3327, rue Loyola, in the Vieux-Moulin neighbourhood (arrondissement de Beauport).
The project would be four storeys, while the current zoning does not allow any residential use and limits height to three storeys.
The City is also authorizing exemptions for the rear setbacks (6 m instead of 7.5 m) and the side setback (2 m instead of 3 m), and for an outdoor stairway that encroaches on the front yard.
Conditions imposed: at least 40 housing units, including 14 with two or more bedrooms and 7 with three or more bedrooms.
Other requirements: red or brown clay bricks on 80% of the walls, a white or green roof, 30% green space at ground level, at least 9 trees planted, and 90% of the parking underground.
The authorization is based on a provincial housing act, which applies because the rental housing vacancy rate in Québec is 2.2%.

The project must start within the 12 months following the final resolution; a fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases) applies if the conditions are not met. A public consultation meeting will be held.
The City is selling a property with a building located at 25-27, rue Saint-Stanislas and 1075-1085, rue Saint-Jean, in the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou.
The buyer is the company Beaudoin Picard immobilier inc., for $3,007,000 plus applicable taxes.
The lot is 363.50 square metres; the property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $2,230,000.
The buyer must begin the interior fit-up work needed to make the upper floors habitable within 36 months after the deed is signed, and must carry out the work continuously.
A City sidewalk encroaches on the property: the buyer grants the City a permanent easement of about 1.80 square metres to maintain, repair and use this sidewalk for pedestrian passage.
The sale is made without legal warranty; the buyer assumes, among other things, the environmental risks associated with the land.
The sale amount will be paid into the City's general fund.
The City is authorizing spending of $20,000,000 to help carry out social housing and affordable private housing projects.
It is borrowing the same amount, repayable over five years, from general revenues.
The money will be used to pay grants, hire staff, pay for professional services, acquire buildings or servitudes, and carry out demonstration projects.
The projects covered are those accepted under Société d'habitation du Québec programs or by government order.
The projects may be located anywhere in the territory of the agglomeration of Québec.
The City is first drawing $2,000,000 from its general fund (10% of the spending), an amount that will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The funds are entered in years 2026 and 2027 of the 2026-2035 investment plan.
The City is appointing two employees as information security officers with the Société d'habitation du Québec (SHQ).
They are Alexandre Armstrong, director of the Section de l'habitation, and Natalie Brousseau, director of the Section des subventions aux bâtiments.
These two people will be able to ask the SHQ to grant, change, suspend or withdraw City staff access to the PAH system.
The PAH system is used to process and track files for home improvement programs, with a view to reimbursement by the SHQ.
This change follows staff movements and a reorganization of the teams.
This decision replaces the appointment adopted on June 6, 2023.
The City is awarding Terrassement Portugais inc. (Québec) a contract worth $550,411.82 before taxes to build sidewalks and redevelop the roadway.
The work covers the west approach of avenue Industrielle leading to autoroute 573, in the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough.
The contract includes a road structure, a turning lane, traffic management, signage and pavement markings.
Twelve companies submitted bids; all were compliant and Terrassement Portugais offered the lowest price.
The winning bid is 27.7% below the requesting department's estimate, which was $761,412.31.
The net cost to the City is $577,863.61, funded by loan by-law R.V.Q. 3412.
The contract provides for price adjustments based on the cost of asphalt and fuel.
The arrondissement des Rivières is paying out $56,576 in grants to seven organizations, for applications submitted on June 15, 2026.
Adaptavie inc. receives $30,000 for its operating expenses (third year of the program).
Loisirs et sports Neufchâtel inc. receives $10,000 for a 2nd year of the "Ludothèque" project.
Les Cercles de fermières de Duberger ($4,500) and de Vanier ($3,305) are buying a weaving loom and accessories.
Loisirs Duberger-Les Saules inc. receives $4,500 for aerial yoga equipment, and the Choeur V'là l'Bon Vent $959 for instruments and sound equipment.
Loisirs Lebourgneuf inc. receives $3,312 to redo its website.
The money comes from the operating budget of the arrondissement des Rivières.
The City is settling out of court the expropriation of a piece of land on boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, acquired for the structuring public transit network project (tramway).
The final compensation paid to the expropriated owners is set at $59,458.47, including the capital, interest, the additional compensation and expert appraisal fees.
Since $34,000.00 has already been paid as provisional compensation, the City is paying a balance of $25,458.47.
The City or the project's prime contractor is also taking charge of the work to redevelop the remaining part of the land.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the structuring public transit network.
The City's attorneys, Giasson et associés, are authorized to sign the settlement documents.
The City is appointing four people to represent it on the committee that manages the pension plan for its professional staff.
The people appointed: Dominic Stephenson and Véronique Béland (Service des ressources humaines), France Bilodeau (consultant) and Marie-Michelle Linteau (Service des finances).
Their term begins on February 25, 2026 and ends on February 23, 2029.
This appointment was necessary because the term of the trustees currently in office ended on February 25, 2026.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The Ville de Québec is signing agreements with 10 organizations to help fund the Canadian Urban Forest Conference, to be held at the Centre des congrès de Québec from October 13 to 16, 2026.

Four sponsors are contributing $43,000 in total: Sustainable Forestry Initiative ($10,000), Wildfire Resilience Consortium of Canada ($25,000), Administration portuaire de Québec ($5,500) and Arbre-Évolution Coop de solidarité ($2,500).

Six organizations are renting a booth for a total of $8,000: FilmOrganic, Société internationale d'arboriculture Québec, UBC Faculty of Forestry & Environmental Stewardship, PlanIT Geo, IML North America and Innovex produits techniques.
These agreements bring in $50,259 for the City, net of taxes on the value of the tickets provided.
The City acts as the main party responsible for organizing, running the logistics and funding the event, under its agreement with Arbres Canada.
Sponsors must pay within 30 days of signing their agreement; other agreements could be added in the coming months.
The City is awarding Groupe Colas Québec inc. a contract worth $5,948,217 (before taxes) for surface work on rue Dorchester and autoroute Laurentienne, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The work covers several intersections between rue de la Croix-Rouge and côte d'Abraham, as part of the TramCité project.
The contract also covers rebuilding the sewer pipes at the intersection of rue Sainte-Hélène and rue Dorchester, as well as demolishing the passerelle Adrien-Pouliot.
Only one company submitted a bid; after negotiation, it lowered its price. The gap with the City's estimate ($5,586,391.50) is still 6.5%.
The contract includes clauses to adjust the prices of asphalt and fuel.
The net cost for the City comes to $6,244,884.32, funded by three loan by-laws.
The executive committee approved the decision on May 27, 2026.
The City is awarding the company Réno-Voc inc. the cleaning services for the bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy and its mobile trailer, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The contract is worth $1,684,900 (plus GST and QST) and covers the period from September 1, 2026, to March 31, 2030.
The contract can be renewed for another 12 months, with a price increase tied to the consumer price index.
Four companies submitted bids; Réno-Voc offered the lowest price, 18.6% below the City's estimate ($2,070,964.32).
After tax recovery, the net expense comes to $1,768,934.39, spread out from 2026 to 2030.
The amounts for the years 2027 to 2030 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
The City is giving out $58,614 in grants to three schools to remove asphalt and plant greenery on their grounds.
The amounts: École secondaire Vanier $18,614, École du Domaine $20,000, École Sans-Frontière $20,000.
All three projects are in the Vanier area: boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, rue des Balsamines and avenue Bélanger.
The program pays up to 80% of eligible expenses, with a maximum of $20,000 per non-profit organization.
Only start-up and landscaping costs are covered (soil, compost, plants, labour); maintenance and communications are excluded.
The work must be carried out in the spring, summer or fall of 2026.
Two other projects had already received $40,000 in the same call for projects.
The City is awarding EMS Ingénierie inc. (Québec) a professional services contract in landscape architecture and engineering for $330,514.22 before taxes.
The contract covers the redevelopment of baseball fields and BMX tracks at parc Victorin-Beaucage, parc du Petit-Village and the piste de vélocross du Sous-Bois.
The sites involved are in the arrondissements des Rivières and de Beauport.
The firm will develop the design concepts, prepare the plans and specifications, and supervise the work.
EMS Ingénierie will be able to apply for permits and authorizations on the City's behalf, with the prior approval of the Service de la gestion des immeubles.
The net cost to the City is $346,998.62, funded by a loan by-law ($318,585.09) and the Beauport parks fund ($28,413.53).
Five bids were received; EMS obtained the best final score, and its bid is 33.9% below the requesting department's estimate of $500,000.
The Ville de Québec is submitting six financial assistance applications totalling $1,479,766 to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable's TAPU program for 2026-2027.
The six projects represent estimated eligible expenses of $4,562,838 (net of taxes).
Projects covered: the des Ardennes railway crossing ($271,396 in assistance), the multi-purpose link between parc Victoria and the axe Caron ($237,324), and 3e Avenue Est in Charlesbourg ($78,196).

Other projects: 4e Avenue between 22e Rue and chemin de la Canardière ($169,508), boulevard des Chutes toward Beauport ($93,342), and route de l'Église between chemin Saint-Louis and rue de l'Anse ($630,000).
The work mainly involves adding or connecting cycling and pedestrian facilities in these areas.
The City commits to carrying out the projects according to the program's rules and acknowledges that the assistance will be cancelled if it does not comply with them.
The decision summary states that there is no financial impact for the City.
The Ville de Québec is adopting a Cadre d'intervention en toponymie (place-naming framework), the first written document setting out how the names of streets and public places are chosen.
The framework sets selection criteria, exclusion criteria, rules for changing an existing name, and ways of dealing with place names that are criticized.
It also provides for guiding and encouraging citizen participation in the naming of places.
The City commits to better representing under-represented groups in its place names: women, cultural communities, Indigenous peoples and certain social groups.
The Comité de commémoration et de toponymie continues to make its recommendations to the executive committee, and then to city council, which makes the final decision.
There are more than 5,000 official place names on the territory; adopting the framework is one of the courses of action in the Politique culturelle 2025-2030.
The document states that there is no financial impact for the City.
The Ville de Québec is signing an agreement with the organization Sentier Transcanadien to receive financial assistance of up to $60,000.
The money will be used to redevelop a bike and pedestrian path on rue Abraham-Martin.

This redevelopment replaces a section of the corridor du Littoral that ran on land belonging to the Administration portuaire de Québec, near the bassin Louise, which the Administration took back for its own projects.
The contribution covers 4.04% of the project's eligible expenses, and the agreement ends on December 31, 2026.
Sentier Transcanadien had accepted the City's request for assistance on March 18, 2026.
The City must ask the Gouvernement du Québec for authorization before entering into the agreement.
The Ville de Québec is adopting the framework that will govern the use of the Fonds régions et ruralité from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2028.
The Government of Quebec is delegating to the City the management of this fund of $6,147,735 for the period from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2028.
The money will be used to support social economy businesses and non-profit organizations: a target of 20 files per year, 20 jobs created and 50 jobs maintained.
The framework also provides for 5 structuring projects per year to improve living environments, with at least 3 partners per project.
Some amounts will go to the Plan Commerce, the Plan agroalimentaire, workforce and immigration issues, and relations with the Nation huronne-wendat.
Commercial revitalization will target in particular the Saint-Roch and Bastien-Racine-Wendake areas.
About 20% of the budget of the division in charge will be funded by the fund; results will be compiled each quarter.
The Ville de Québec is giving a grant of up to $75,000 to the organization La Bouée société acheteuse de préservation et de développement de l'habitat communautaire.
The money is used to prepare a project of about 140 housing units at 600, 60e Rue Est, in Québec, called Habitation des Anges.
The grant covers start-up costs: environmental studies, soil tests, surveying, title searches, land appraisal, architect's sketches and developer's fees, with a cap for each spending item.
The organization has six months after signing the agreement to spend the grant.
It must submit its project under an assistance program recognized by the City within 12 months of signing, subject to the project's feasibility.
The costs must have been billed after March 31, 2026, and the grant will be reduced if the organization receives other assistance for the same expenses.
The $75,000 comes from an agglomeration loan by-law tied to the Vision de l'habitation.

The City authorizes the construction of a residential building of about 45 housing units at 3325-3327, rue Loyola, on the site of the église Saint-Ignace-de-Loyola (quartier du Vieux-Moulin, arrondissement de Beauport).

The project is granted exemptions from the planning rules: residential use in a zone where it is not allowed, a height of four storeys instead of three, a rear setback of 6 m instead of 7.5 m, a side setback of 2 m instead of 3 m, and an outdoor staircase encroaching into the front yard.

Following the public meeting of June 4, 2026 and a written consultation, the City is adding a condition about trees: at least four trees along avenue Renouard must be kept and protected during the work.
These trees may only be cut down in the cases provided for in the Beauport planning by-law, and every tree cut down must be replaced.
Anyone who does not comply with the conditions is liable to a fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.
The resolution is not subject to a referendum; it must be approved by the urban agglomeration council in order to obtain a certificate of compliance.
The City is awarding Asplundh Canada ULC (Terrebonne) hourly-rate tree care work for the TramCité tramway project, for an estimated amount of $2,840,827.31 before taxes.
The contract runs from the date it is awarded until December 31, 2027, with the possibility of two 12-month renewals indexed to the CPI.
The work includes pruning, felling and stump removal of trees to clear the right-of-way for CDPQ Infra's work and the City's preparatory work.
Some of the work will be done near Hydro-Québec's medium-voltage network, and the supplier will have to put up the necessary road signs.
Some cutting will also serve to meet the City's commitments under a forestry agreement with a citizen.
Three compliant bids were received; Asplundh submitted the lowest, 4.8% above the requesting department's estimate.
The net expenditure, which falls under the urban agglomeration's jurisdiction, is estimated at $2,982,513.57.
The City is launching a public consultation to prepare its agricultural and agri-food policy for the agglomeration of Québec 2026-2035, which will replace the 2015-2025 vision that has now expired.
The process has three phases: gathering ideas from the public, meetings with stakeholders, and then a consultation on the draft policy.
It began in February 2026 with a questionnaire for the general public and a booth at the Fête des semences et de l'agriculture urbaine de Québec.
The future policy is meant to support farming in urban, peri-urban and agricultural areas, and to encourage local food processing and local sales.
It also aims to improve access to fresh, healthy food and to reduce food waste.
The councillor for the district of Plateau responsible for agriculture, Gabriel Dusablon, is mandated to support the public participation activities.
The results of the consultation will be used by the consultant hired to write the policy.
The City is entrusting the cleaning and sanitation services of a building in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg to Patro de Charlesbourg inc.
The agreement covers the period from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027, that is 12 months.
The City will pay $155,563.68, excluding GST and QST: $51,854.56 in 2026 and $103,709.12 in 2027.
The 2027 portion depends on the approval of the 2027 budget by the appropriate authorities.
The contract is awarded by mutual agreement, a rule that allows a contract to be awarded directly to a non-profit organization.
The agreement follows the previous one, which was ending on August 31, 2026.
The director of the Service des approvisionnements is authorized to sign the agreement.
The executive committee takes note of the quarterly report on positions created or abolished by the Service des ressources humaines between October 1 and December 31, 2025.
The report lists 23 positions created and no positions abolished during this quarter.

The positions created involve, among others, the Service de police, the Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente, the Bureau pivot du tramway de Québec, water treatment and the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
According to the document, all of these positions were included in the budget and were taken into account in the 2026 budget.
The City is entrusting the sanitary maintenance of recreational and sports facilities and sites in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou to Centre des Loisirs St-Sacrement inc.
The agreement covers the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, with an option to renew for 12 months.
The contract is worth $133,718.15 plus GST and QST; the net cost to the City is $140,387.34.
The amounts are split between $105,290.42 in 2026 and $35,096.92 in 2027 (net of taxes).
The 2027 portion depends on the approval of the 2027 budget by the appropriate authorities.
The agreement is being made without a call for tenders, an option allowed by law for contracts with a non-profit organization.
City council is to make its decision on April 21, 2026; the director of the Service des approvisionnements would sign the agreement.
The Ville de Québec will pay a grant of up to $245,000 to the Consortium de coopération des entreprises collectives for the years 2026 to 2028.

The money will be used to offer professional services at reduced prices to business groups in the Québec urban agglomeration: accounting, human resources, legal advice, strategic planning and the shift to digital.
With this help, the groups will pay 30% of the real value of the services.
The project costs $350,000 in total: $245,000 comes from the City and $105,000 from the business groups themselves.
The project sheet provides for the creation of 2 jobs.
The funds come from the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale, in two instalments of $137,936 and $107,064.
The project lasts two years and will be monitored using an economic benefits form.
The City is applying for grants from Québec (Véloce III program, component 2) for street redevelopment and cycling projects, for the 2027-2028 government fiscal year.
The applications will be submitted during the call for projects held from August 31 to October 9, 2026.

Projects covered: three sections of boulevard Pierre-Bertrand (rue Fortin, rue du Marais, rue des Entrepreneurs, rue Samson, boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel) and chemin de la Canardière at the Henri-Bourassa intersection.
Also: avenue Marie-de-l'Incarnation (between Guyart and Charest), rue Sheppard (between Chanoine-Morel and Maguire), and rue Borne near the railway crossing.

Added to these are the viaduc Jean-Marchand, coordinated by the ministère and linking L'Ancienne-Lorette and Québec, and the boulevard Lebourgneuf corridor between 4e Avenue Ouest and rue Jean-Perrin.
The City commits to carrying out the projects according to the program's rules and to obtaining the required authorizations; otherwise, the financial assistance would be terminated.
The amount of the grants is not yet known: it will be confirmed by the minister after the applications are reviewed.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 412, rue Sauriol, in the Vieux-Bourg neighbourhood in Beauport.
The owner will be allowed to demolish the existing garage and build a new one in the front yard, whereas the by-law normally requires the side or rear yard.
The new garage will have to be located at least 7 metres from the front property line.

The parking area, including the access to the street, will have to be reduced by at least 1.5 metres in width over its entire depth on the west side, and that space will have to be planted with vegetation.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on April 23, 2026.
According to the analysis, the river's flood zone and the position of the main building at the back of the lot limit the other possible locations.
The City is extending the employment contract of Gaétan Morin, consulting expert for the project to modernize the water treatment plants.
The contract, which was set to end on June 1, 2026, is extended from June 2, 2026 to May 29, 2027.
The extension responds to the need for support in updating the wastewater treatment plants to meet the new Canada-wide standards.
This update stems from new requirements from the ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs.
The funds, including employee benefits, come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 970 on work related to drinking water and wastewater treatment.
The executive committee approved the decision (resolution CE-2026-0843).
The City is extending by 12 months the deadline given to the Office municipal d'habitation de Québec to claim the rest of a $75,000 grant.
This grant is used to reimburse the start-up costs of the Wilfrid-Hamel housing project, at 7543, boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel.
The Office had 6 months to submit its reimbursement requests; it will now have 18 months from the date the agreement comes into force.
Part of the grant has already been paid out, but some requests could not be made within the original deadline for reasons beyond the Office's control.
The money comes from the Fonds de démarrage pour les projets de logements sociaux et communautaires.
The executive committee adopted the decision on July 8, 2026.
The arrondissement de Charlesbourg is authorizing a temporary overhead power line at 6125, 1re Avenue, in the Saint-Rodrigue neighbourhood.
This line will keep electricity running to the existing building while a residential building of about 200 housing units is built on the neighbouring lot.
The authorization is valid from February 25, 2026 to February 25, 2027, and the overhead line will have to be removed at the end of that period.
The current electrical connection must be removed in favour of a new underground connection that will serve both buildings.
The City is granting this permission because the exact location of the underground service has not yet been determined, even though wires in the area normally have to be underground.
The site is part of the former couvent des Eudistes.
The City is creating a 30-minute maximum parking space on rue Monseigneur-Gauvreau, in Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur.
The space is on the west side, between boulevard Charest Est and rue Saint-Joseph Est.
Parking was prohibited there at all times over 19.5 metres from Charest Est; the prohibition is reduced to 13.5 metres.
The next 6 metres become a space where you can park for a maximum of 30 minutes.
The change responds to a request from the business Bédard et Prévost - Les Encadreurs, at 794, boulevard Charest Est, for its customers.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council is enacting ordinance O-1523 to put this change into effect.
The City is awarding security services for the Cour municipale to Corps canadien des Commissionnaires (division du Québec), of Montréal.
The contract runs from January 1 to December 31, 2027, for an estimated amount of $140,049 before taxes.
Officers will monitor the common areas and the service counters of the Cour municipale.
The contract can be renewed twice for 12 months, with annual price indexing under the Décret sur les agents de sécurité.
Of the 11 bids received, 6 were set aside because the suppliers did not have the five years of experience required.
Corps canadien des Commissionnaires submitted the lowest price among the compliant bids, 17.6% below the requesting department's estimate of $170,000.
The funds depend on the adoption of the 2027 budget by the appropriate authorities.
The City is changing its planning rules for steep-slope land and the areas next to it, following a change adopted by the urban agglomeration council on May 6, 2026.
Adding a dwelling in an accessory building (such as a garden house) becomes prohibited anywhere on a steep slope and anywhere in the area next to a steep slope.
Building recreational trails (mountain biking, downhill skiing) becomes allowed in these areas, if it is tied to a park use, a regional recreational facility or a conservation area.
These trails require a geotechnical expert report on soil stability, a report on erosion and water runoff, and an authorization certificate before the work begins.
The exception allowing fill or excavation of 0.30 metre maximum no longer applies on a steep slope, only in the areas next to it.
Machinery weighing more than 0.5 tonne becomes allowed on a steep slope if an engineer certifies the stability and bearing capacity of the soil.

Before adoption, the City is removing the ban on machinery weighing more than 0.5 tonne that was to apply to the area at the top of the slope, to avoid work that is authorized but impossible to carry out.
The City is paying $12,000 to La Maison Michel-Sarrazin, located at 2101, chemin Saint-Louis, in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
This amount compensates for the maintenance and snow removal of the private street leading to the building, services the City has no longer provided since June 1, 2007.
The compensation covers the period from June 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026.
This payment has been recurring since a city council decision in April 2007; the amount has been $12,000 each year since 2016.
The money comes from the budget of the Direction de l'arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The borough council adopted the decision on August 27, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 1687, avenue de Colmar, in the Orsainville neighbourhood (Arrondissement de Charlesbourg).
The garage attached to the house is 0.2 metres from the property line, while the planning by-law requires 0.5 metres.
With the exemption, this structure is now considered compliant; the request was made as part of a real estate transaction.
Without the exemption, the owner would have had to demolish or move the garage to bring it back to 0.5 metres from the lot line.
The side wall of the garage will have to be modified to meet the fire resistance required by the Code de construction du Québec.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on March 4, 2026.
The City is granting a subsidy of up to $50,000 to the organization Québec Nova Murale.
The money will go to the "Pochoirs et affiches pour la planète" project in the summer 2026 day camps.
Professional artists will lead 45-minute urban art workshops (posters and stencils) on environmental themes, for children aged 5 to 12.
The project is expected to reach 2,000 children and be offered in every arrondissement, including regular, adapted and French-language integration camps.
The project was chosen from among 4 proposals received during the call for cultural projects for day camps.
The funds come from a loan by-law tied to the Entente de développement culturel 2024-2026 signed with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The executive committee adopted the decision on March 11, 2026.
The City is awarding the general contractor work in its parks to the company Teramco inc., of Québec, for an estimated amount of $897,050 (before GST and QST).
The contract runs from April 13, 2026 to April 12, 2027, with an option to renew for 12 months including price indexation.
The work covers parks and off-street public spaces in all boroughs: maintenance, renovation, construction, repairs and modifications.
Six companies submitted bids; Teramco submitted the lowest price among the compliant bids.
The net expense is estimated at $941,790.37 after recovery of the QST.
The requesting department had estimated the work at $840,000, which is 6.8% less than the lowest compliant bid.
The amounts planned for 2027 remain subject to the adoption of that year's budget.
The City is awarding Tétra Tech QI inc. the engineering services to rebuild the retaining wall on côte de la Montagne, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough.
The contract is worth $306,380 (plus GST and QST); the net cost to the City is $321,660.70.
The mandate covers all engineering activities, including supervision of the work.

This retaining wall holds up part of the cliff at parc Montmorency, which is owned by the Government of Canada; the new structure will have to blend in with the park's retaining wall and with the wall at 105, côte de la Montagne.
Only one bid was received; after negotiation, the price went from $356,350 to $306,380, which is 4.2% more than the estimate of $293,541.04.
The firm is authorized to apply, on the City's behalf, for the necessary permits and authorizations from government departments and other authorities.
The funds come from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3390.
The executive committee takes note of the report on transactions of the Fonds régions et ruralité (FRR) for the period from April 1 to June 30, 2025.
No new money was paid out during the quarter: the report contains only returns of unused balances, totalling $181,597.
The returns come notably from Université Laval ($87,996), Théâtre Périscope ($60,000) and Complexe de baseball Victoria ($25,000).

Other smaller amounts are being returned by the Fonds de marchés publics (Beauport, Saint-Augustin), the SDC Faubourg Saint-Jean, the Collectif Rutabaga, les Urbainculteurs, Compétences Québec, La Bouchée généreuse and the Carrefour jeunesse emploi de la Capitale-Nationale.
The Fund's balance goes from $132,076.26 as at March 31, 2025 to $313,673.26 as at June 30, 2025.
The Ville de Québec will pay $555,000 to the Corporation des fêtes historiques de Québec for the Fêtes de la Nouvelle-France in 2026, 2027 and 2028, that is $185,000 per year.
It is also adding free municipal services (public works, police, fire) worth up to $30,000, for total support of $585,000.
The 29th edition will take place from August 6 to 9, 2026 in Vieux-Québec; the following editions will be held from August 5 to 8, 2027 and from August 3 to 6, 2028.
The funding is meant to keep the main outdoor sites free, with the addition of a third site in 2026 (the gardens and place de l'Hôtel-de-Ville, parc Montmorency).
The event's planned budget is $1,813,600 in 2026, $1,846,400 in 2027 and $1,880,700 in 2028; the grant covers about 10% of these budgets.
The funding is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners, and the amounts for 2027 and 2028 depend on the adoption of those years' budgets.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 1486, rue Marie-Rollet, in the Saint-Sacrement neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The exemption allows the construction of a new single-family home with a height of 8.5 metres, while the planning by-law allows 8 metres.

According to the analysis, respecting the 8-metre limit would force the owner to add window wells to the basement windows or to reduce the height of the ground floor, which would change the façade and the size of the windows.
The analysis concludes that the extra half-metre does not affect the neighbours and that the height fits in between the heights on the two neighbouring lots.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 28, 2026, and the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec also recommended approval.
No financial impact is indicated in the file.
The City is granting a minor exemption for the construction of a house at 1225, rue de l'Embâcle, in the Val-Bélair neighbourhood.
The exemption allows a distance of 7.3 metres between the front setback and the main façade, instead of the maximum of 3 metres set out in the borough's planning by-law.
The project is a single-dwelling home with an attached garage.
According to the analysis, the house cannot encroach on the portion of the lot located in another zone, where residential use is not permitted.
The analysis notes that this is the last buildable lot on the street and concludes that there is no impact on the neighbourhood.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on May 27, 2026; the decision rests with the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough council.

The City is awarding Charles-Auguste Fortier inc. the infrastructure work on avenue Blaise-Pascal and rue Mendel, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, for $13,375,688.40 before taxes (net expenditure of $14,042,800.86).
The work is part of the TramCité project and includes realigning rue Mendel as well as relocating the water and sewer pipes.
A new drinking water pipe will be added to loop the area's network by way of avenue Blaise-Pascal.
The work site also provides for enlarging the stormwater management basin on avenue Blaise-Pascal and burying the wires under both streets.
A bike path will be built along part of avenue Blaise-Pascal.
Of the 10 bids received, all compliant, the one chosen is the lowest; the City's estimate was $21,071,735.92 before taxes.
The contract provides for price adjustments based on the cost of asphalt and fuel; the funds come from a loan by-law tied to the structuring public transit network.
The City is entrusting the organization Trip Jeunesse Beauport with carrying out the Liaisons jeunesse program in the arrondissement de Beauport.
Workers will go out to meet young people aged 12 to 25 in the parks and public spaces of Beauport, to encourage people to get along well together.
The agreement covers the period from May 1 to September 30, for the years 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The City will pay $74,515.27 per year, for a total of $223,545.81 (excluding GST and QST).
The 2027 and 2028 amounts will be adjusted according to the minimum wage in effect on May 1 of each year, and depend on the budgets being adopted.
The agreement is made without a call for tenders, which the law allows with a non-profit organization.
The previous agreement with the organization ended on September 30, 2025.
The Ville de Québec is giving $5,000 to the Laboratoire d'agriculture urbaine (AU/LAB) to organize the third edition of the École d'été sur l'agriculture urbaine (urban agriculture summer school).
The event will be held in Québec City on August 25 and 26, 2026, on the theme "L'agriculture urbaine : un élément du droit à l'alimentation" (urban agriculture: part of the right to food).
The program includes talks, panels, workshops and field visits.
In exchange, the City gets visibility in the event's publications and two free admissions, as a SILVER partner.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3140, which covers community gardens and urban agriculture.
The City had given $6,000 for the 2022 and 2024 editions.
The City is banning parking at all times along 16 metres on the north side of rue de l'Aqueduc, starting at rue Dollard and going east, in Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur.
Two parking spaces are being removed in an area where the occupancy rate is high.
The measure aims to improve visibility at the "Y"-shaped intersection of rue de l'Aqueduc, rue Dollard and rue Montmagny.
The Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente carried out the analysis after a request from a driver who felt visibility was inadequate at this intersection.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council is enacting ordinance O-1511 to put this change into effect.
The City is renewing the maintenance of its SAP software licences for one year, from July 31, 2026 to July 30, 2027.
The contract goes to SAP Canada inc., of Toronto, for $209,995.36 before taxes (net expense of $220,468.87).
The cost is spread over two years: $91,862.02 in 2026 and $128,606.85 in 2027, net of taxes.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders, because SAP Canada designed the software and holds the exclusive rights to it.
The City uses this software for its data warehouses, its dashboards and its management reports.
The 2027 portion depends on the approval of that year's budget.
The director of the Service des approvisionnements is authorized to sign the contract documents.

The arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is amending its planning by-law for the building at 212, rue Saint-Jean (210-224, rue Saint-Jean / 203-205, rue D'Aiguillon), the Château des Tourelles, in the Saint-Jean-Baptiste neighbourhood.
The change removes the limit of 11 tourist accommodation units: the borough council will be able to authorize general tourist accommodation use with no cap on the number of units.
The purpose is to correct an error in an amendment adopted in December 2024, in which only one of the two sections concerned had been amended.
The reference to a retail sales and services use is removed, because this type of use is already permitted in zone 13005Mb.
The authorized occupancy must begin within 24 months after the by-law comes into force, otherwise the authorization lapses.
The conseil de quartier de Saint-Jean-Baptiste is asked to give its opinion and to hold the public consultation meeting; the by-law cannot be subject to a referendum.
The by-law was adopted at the first stage on March 23, 2026.
The City wants to obtain rights of way (easements) on a piece of land bordering rue Mendel, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, for the TramCité tramway project.
These easements are temporary, lasting 3 years, and are used to move conduits and public utility networks.
Four parcels are targeted: two underground (12.8 and 17.6 m²), one overhead (878.3 m²) and one for passage (1,816.9 m²).
The City will try to reach a negotiated agreement, but is also starting expropriation proceedings to free up the land in time.
An agreement had already been reached with the owner in July 2025, but operational issues are forcing the City to change its approach.
The entire property is assessed at $26,235,000 on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll.
If the project no longer needs the easements, the City will be able to drop the expropriation proceedings.
The City is amending its planning by-law to allow L'Évasion St-Pie X to install and use a community building at 1900, rue Désilets, in the Maizerets neighbourhood.
The building serves as a community pavilion for teenagers living in the Les Appartements St-Pie X residential complex, to give them a place to meet and get support.
The authorization waives the minimum height of 7.5 metres required in the zone and exempts the building from the architectural integration requirements (PIIA) for exterior cladding.
The building's floor area is limited to 100 square metres.
The authorization is valid for 100 years from the date the by-law comes into force and cannot be transferred to another organization.
The conseil de quartier de Maizerets is asked to give its opinion and to hold the public consultation meeting; the by-law cannot be subject to a referendum.
The building was added by the Office municipal d'habitation de Québec, the owner of the site, on an open space at the end of rue Le Droit used as a neighbourhood park.
The Government of Québec is giving $200,000 to the Ville de Québec under the Programme d'appui aux actions régionales (component 3).
This money is added to the assistance program for businesses whose access is disrupted for more than three months because of major infrastructure work.
The program also supports organizations that promote commercial streets, in particular in the context of the TramCité project.
The program's total budget for 2026 comes to $3,700,000: $3,500,000 from the City and $200,000 from the Government of Québec.
The City must complete the project by March 31, 2028 at the latest and submit an activity report and an audited accounting report within the following four months.
Any amount not used or used for other purposes must be paid back to the government.
The executive committee authorizes the mayor and the city clerk to sign the agreement.
The City will pay up to $2,482,047 to the Fabrique de la paroisse de Saint-Pierre-Julien-Eymard to restore the two steeples of the église du Très-Saint-Sacrement, on chemin Sainte-Foy.
This amount is in addition to the $4,000,000 grant awarded in 2023: the total cost of the project now reaches $6,482,047.
The money comes from the Entente de développement culturel signed with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The cost increase is explained by professional fees, contingencies, taxes, additional expert assessments and the rise in construction costs since 2023.
The Fabrique must begin the work no later than one year after the agreement is signed and complete it within 36 months.
The Fabrique pays any cost overruns and reimburses the City for any amount not used or used for other purposes.
According to the document, this priority work will make it possible to reopen the church to the public safely; other work will still be needed.
The borough of La Cité-Limoilou is amending its planning by-law for zone 18400Mb, located on both sides of the chemin de la Canardière, between the boulevard Henri-Bourassa and the avenue Mailloux.
Administrative services (group C1) will be allowed on all floors, including the ground floor and the basement, whereas they were previously permitted only on the 2nd and 3rd floors.
The change stems from a request concerning 2118-2128, boulevard Sainte-Anne, where the owner wants to open an accounting office without converting one of the 13 dwellings on the upper floors.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The conseil de quartier de Maizerets must give its opinion and hold the public consultation meeting.
Interested persons will have seven days after the public meeting to send their comments in writing.
The Ville de Québec is granting a maximum subsidy of $150,000 to Laboratoire Hygienex inc., a vehicle cleaning products company located in the parc industriel Armand-Viau.

The money will go toward a marketing and advertising campaign to sell in Ontario and the rest of Canada: market studies, a website redesign, an Ontario consulting agency, three industry events and social media advertising.
The project costs $345,400 in total: $150,000 from the City and $195,400 paid by the company itself.
The subsidy comes from the Capitale-Innovation component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, a fund entrusted to the City by the Government of Quebec.
The company, created in 1995, has 30 employees; one of the project's aims was to maintain these 30 jobs.
The Vision entrepreneuriale review committee came out in favour of the project on July 14, 2026; the decision rests with the urban agglomeration council.
The City is authorizing a $115,200,000 expenditure for work to repair and build municipal infrastructure.
It is borrowing the same amount, repayable over fifteen years, and is setting aside a portion of its general revenues to pay the interest and the principal.
The work covers roads, water and sewer systems, lighting and traffic signals, public utility networks, engineering structures and the development of municipal spaces.
The projects may take place anywhere in the territory under the City's jurisdiction.
The expenditure also covers professional and technical services, the hiring of staff, the purchase of buildings and servitudes, and the payment of grants and financial contributions.
The City may acquire buildings or servitudes by mutual agreement or by expropriation in order to carry out this work.
An amount of $11,520,000 (10% of the expenditure) is being taken from the general fund, which will be replenished when the by-law comes into force.
The City is awarding Les services périodiques ThermoPro inc. (Québec) the contract for stationary machine mechanic services in various municipal buildings.
The contract is worth about $420,480 before taxes, from the date it is awarded until May 31, 2029, with two possible 12-month renewals indexed to inflation (CPI).
The work includes monitoring, preventive maintenance and the other tasks required by laws and by-laws.
Six companies submitted bids; ThermoPro offered the lowest price, 45.6% below the City's estimate ($776,694.45).
The net cost to the City is estimated at $441,451.44.
Funding for the years 2027 to 2029 depends on the adoption of the budgets by the appropriate authorities.
This decision falls to the Québec urban agglomeration council.
The Ville de Québec will pay $299,000 to the Institut canadien de Québec over three years to keep social workers at the Gabrielle-Roy library, in Saint-Roch.
The payments break down as follows: $39,000 in 2026, $130,000 in 2027 and $130,000 in 2028, subject to approval of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.
The workers support people who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless, refer them to community resources and provide support to library staff.
The document reports more than 1,500 interventions per year since the project was launched in 2024, and one additional worker hired in 2025.
The organization will have to report back according to the requirements set out in the agreement.
The decision falls under the Québec urban agglomeration council.
The City is renewing its artists' studio grant program for 2026 and is putting up to $55,000 toward it, the same as in 2023, 2024 and 2025.
The grant is for professional artists in visual arts or fine crafts who occupied a studio on the city's territory in 2025, either as tenants or owners.
The amount paid is $13.75 per square metre of studio space occupied in 2025; it is reduced on a pro rata basis if the occupancy lasted less than a year.
An artist who lives in their studio located in a residential co-ownership (condo) receives the grant for only half of the area (50% studio, 50% living space).
The studios at Le Réacteur (lot 1 476 965) are excluded from the program because the City already covers part of their occupancy cost.
Applications must be submitted no later than September 18, 2026; they are processed in the order they are received, until the funds run out.
Each artist must fill out their own form and provide proof of occupancy, and where applicable, proof of principal residence.
The City is giving up its right to obtain a no-access easement along avenue de la Roselière, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
This easement, provided for since a 2018 agreement with Les Développements Aventura inc., would have closed off access to the residential project on avenue de la Roselière.
Access therefore stays open: the company asked that the easement not be applied because residents use it a lot.
The Aventura project has 832 rental units spread over 10 phases, all completed.
The City has never claimed the easement since 2018, and the departments consulted are in favour of dropping it.
The land in question (lots 6 337 286 and 6 392 233) is assessed at $1,880,000 and $2,335,000 on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll.
The City is awarding Trafic Innovation inc. (Saint-Eustache) a contract for a subscription to the Navigate Traffic Cloud platform and for preventive maintenance of its mobile speed display signs.
The contract covers the period from March 31, 2026 to October 31, 2028, for an estimated amount of $140,820 (plus GST and QST).
The net expenditure is estimated at $147,843.42; the amounts for 2027 and 2028 still have to be approved in future budgets.
The platform makes it possible to manage the speed display signs remotely, collect data and locate on a map the equipment installed on Québec's streets.
The contract includes repairing the equipment, processing the data, sending reports and providing annual training for employees.
The bid covers 40 mobile display signs (packages of 35 and of 5) per year, from 2026 to 2028.
No call for tenders was issued: the City states that this supplier is the only manufacturer of its equipment and the only one able to maintain it.

The arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou approves the architectural and site plans for two construction projects, following the recommendations of the comité consultatif d'urbanisme of February 24, 2026.
Both projects are detached multi-unit residential buildings, at 760A-760E and 764A-764E, rue des Saules Est, in the district of Maizerets–Lairet.
In both cases, the approval comes with a condition: the masonry cladding in the colour "Kelowna" must be replaced with a more earthy colour, in reddish tones.
The reason given: white is not a dominant colour in the neighbourhood for the facades of multi-storey apartment buildings.
Building permits can only be issued once these plans are approved.
The City is appointing two city councillors to the Comité de vigilance des activités portuaires: Catherine Vallières-Roland and Marylou Boulianne.
Their term ends on November 4, 2029.
Catherine Vallières-Roland is the council member responsible for port activities.
The committee, created in May 2013, monitors the activities of the Port de Québec and their effects on health and the environment.
The committee is advisory: it makes recommendations, informs the public and reports publicly on its actions.
The committee's internal by-law requires two representatives from the City, including one elected official responsible for matters related to port activities.
The Ville de Québec is entrusting the cleaning and sanitary upkeep of buildings in the arrondissement des Rivières to the organization Loisirs et Sports Neufchâtel inc.
The contract covers 24 months, from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2028.
The planned amount is $219,235.61, plus GST and QST; the net expense is $230,169.97.
The payments break down as follows: $28,024.61 in 2026, $113,591.96 in 2027 and $88,553.40 in 2028 (net of taxes).
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 depend on the approval of those years' budgets.
The agreement replaces the previous one, which ends on September 30, 2026.
City council is to decide on September 15, 2026; the director of the Service des approvisionnements would sign the agreement.
The City wants to acquire a strip of land of about 957.8 square metres along rue de la Faune, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The land would be used to widen rue de la Faune, as part of the project to rebuild that street.
The purchase will be made by mutual agreement with the owner or, if the discussions do not succeed, by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to begin the acquisition or expropriation proceedings.
The Division de l'arpentage et de la géomatique will prepare the plans, technical descriptions and cadastral operations that are needed.
The property, in its largest extent, is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $30,500, which is $1.40 per square metre.
The funds come from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 related to the work to redevelop rue de la Faune.
The arrondissement de Beauport is entrusting Patro Le Pivot with running the day camp for the Programme Vacances-Été 2026.
The City will pay the organization a grant estimated at $774,671.19.
90% of the amount will be paid within 30 days of the signing of the agreement; the balance will be adjusted based on the actual number of registrations as of September 14.
If the final amount is lower than the advance paid, Patro Le Pivot will have to repay the City within 90 days after the end of the program.
In the summer of 2025, Patro Le Pivot welcomed 1,572 children and received $844,891.56.
The organization manages registrations and fees, keeps the registration revenue, and must offer a support service for children with special needs.
The City provides technical and material support and gives access, subject to availability, to play areas and to municipal and school facilities.
The Arrondissement des Rivières is authorizing three elected officials to attend the 2026 annual convention (Assises annuelles) of the Union des municipalités du Québec.
The event takes place at the Centre des congrès de Québec, from May 13 to 15, 2026.
The City is paying or reimbursing the registration fees: $377 plus taxes for Catherine Deschamps and Clément Bourdeau, $890 plus taxes for Maxime Elmaleh.
Other travel-related expenses are reimbursed upon submission of supporting documents.
The money comes from the budget of the Arrondissement des Rivières, under the activity "Soutenir les conseils d'arrondissement" (supporting borough councils).

The executive committee takes note of the 2025 annual report on the leases the City has signed with third parties to rent out its buildings or premises, for terms of more than 1 year and no more than 5 years.
The report lists 21 leases entered into by the Service du développement économique et des grands projets.
The largest rent comes from the Centrale des syndicats du Québec, at 320, rue Saint-Joseph Est: $97,346.51 per month, from June 1, 2025 to November 30, 2026.
Resto RVL (9265-3260 Québec inc.) rents food counters and vending machine spaces in 8 arenas and sports centres, with annual rents ranging from $645 to $19,475.

Other tenants: Pro Sports (sporting goods shops in 2 arenas), Groupe Umac and Mathieu Roussel (vending machines), Synchro inc. (storage at $1,930 per month), Ressources naturelles Canada (storage at $150 per month).
Hydro-Québec pays $18,500 for 36 months to maintain an overhead power transmission line on City land.
