The SDC de Montcalm occupies avenue Cartier between chemin Sainte-Foy and Grande Allée Ouest without paying rent, and the Conseil de quartier Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy pays $10 per year to add greenery to a public space.
The City is granting $87,000 in support to Productions Culturelles Québec for Festibière de Québec 2026: $75,000 in cash and up to $12,000 in free municipal services.
The free services come from building management, public works and the Service de police (work time and equipment loans that are normally billed).
The 15th edition runs from August 12 to 16, 2026: on the Espace 400 docks from August 13 to 16, and the "Club social" component in Saint-Roch on August 12, 13 and 14.
The Club social is moving from place de l'Université du Québec to place Jacques-Cartier, near rue Saint-Joseph, with more entertainment in collaboration with the SDC Saint-Roch.
Access to the site and to the programming is free; tastings are done by buying the edition's glass.
The event's budget is estimated at $1,392,432; the City's grant represents 5.4% of it.
The support is conditional on a sufficient contribution from the other partners. The organization must submit its report to the City no later than 90 days after the event.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 1084, rue des Lazurites, in Charlesbourg (district Louis-XIV).
A shed that has already been built stands about 3 metres from the front lot line, while the planning by-law requires 6 metres.
The decision makes this shed deemed compliant: the owner does not have to move it.
According to the analysis, the non-compliance appeared on the plans for two permits issued in the summer of 2025 (in-ground pool and sunroom), but it was not noticed at that time.
The landscaping work done in the backyard after those permits now makes it impossible to relocate the shed.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on August 12, 2026; the borough council made its decision on August 31, 2026.
The City is awarding Groupe Colas Québec inc. an asphalt work contract worth $3,191,570 (before GST and QST).
The work covers various streets in the boroughs of Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, Beauport and La Haute-Saint-Charles.

Planned work includes: milling the existing asphalt, rebuilding the roadway, new layers of asphalt, adding or replacing curbs and sidewalks, catch basins and manholes, road marking and traffic management.
Five companies submitted bids and all were compliant; Colas offered the lowest price.
The winning bid is 18.7% below the City's estimate, which was $3,923,938.
The net cost to the City, after recovering the QST, comes to $3,350,749.55, paid for through a loan by-law.
The contract provides for price adjustments based on the cost of bitumen and fuel.
As of April 1, 2027, leaves and green waste will have to be dropped off loose or in paper bags: plastic bags will no longer be accepted at the transfer centre.
The rule applies to the entire Québec agglomeration, whose green waste transfer centre at 210, avenue Saint-Sacrement receives the materials.
The City explains that plastic bags contaminate the materials, harm the quality of the compost and cost more to process.

According to the authorization certificate from the ministère de l'Environnement, green waste that is loose or in paper bags can be stored for 3 weeks, compared with 18 hours for green waste in plastic bags.
The by-law also adds a separate definition for grass clippings, which are no longer considered green waste.
The document does not mention any financial impact with figures.

The City is confirming to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable that the cycling and pedestrian development work on avenue du Cénacle and rue de l'Etna is complete, in order to collect the balance of the grants.

On avenue du Cénacle, between rue Seigneuriale and rue Labelle: 1,065 metres of active mobility infrastructure added (790 m of bike path and 275 m of sidewalk), safer intersections and 98 trees planted. Work carried out from summer to fall 2024.
On rue de l'Etna, between route de l'Aéroport and boulevard Pie-XI Nord: 2,000 metres of active mobility infrastructure added, with the widening of sidewalk sections and safer intersections.
Eligible expenses declared: $3,229,670.80 (net of taxes) for avenue du Cénacle and $1,328,609.40 (net of taxes) for rue de l'Etna.
The maximum assistance granted is $875,000 for the Cénacle project and $534,556 for the Etna project; the City has already received $700,000 and $427,645 as first payments.
If the declared expenses turn out to be lower than the amounts used to calculate the assistance already paid, the City would have to repay any amounts received in excess.

The decision summary indicates no financial impact and authorizes the director of the Service de la planification de l'aménagement et de l'environnement to sign the documents intended for the minister.
The City is awarding Pluritec ltée a professional engineering services contract to rebuild the escalier du Faubourg, in the La Cité-Limoilou arrondissement.
The contract is worth $288,797 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $303,200.75.
The firm must prepare the plans and specifications, estimate the cost of the work, and provide on-site supervision during construction.
Pluritec is authorized to apply for the necessary permits and authorizations on the City's behalf, with the agreement of the Service de l'ingénierie.
Four bids were received; Pluritec obtained the best final score and submitted the lowest price, 25% below the City's estimate ($385,094.32).
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3390.
The City is giving up to $2,275 to Patro Le Pivot for a day of intergenerational activities on May 21, 2026, in the arrondissement de Beauport.
The activity takes place in the basement of the église Saint-Ignace-de-Loyola, as part of the Semaine québécoise intergénérationnelle.
The program includes a talk, an exhibitors' fair, choral singing and board games.
More than a hundred seniors are expected, along with Grade 5 and Grade 6 students who will take part in a morning activity.
The event's total budget is $3,875: $2,275 from the City, $1,500 from the Table en développement local de Beauport and $100 in sponsorships.
The organizers will have to submit a report on the activities, a financial report and proof of the visibility given to the City.
The City is giving up to $15,000 to the Carrefour international de théâtre de Québec.
The money will be used to produce and present the show "Les Contes à glacer le sang" as part of the Festival Carrefour's 2026 program.
It is an outdoor show, presented on site, with singer-songwriters from Québec; this is its first presentation before the general public.

The project costs $88,750 in total: $32,000 from the Carrefour, $27,750 in self-generated revenue, $10,000 from the Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec, $4,000 from the company La Vierge folle and $15,000 from the City.
The grant comes from the cultural development agreement (Entente de développement culturel) between the ministère de la Culture et des Communications and the City.
A review committee, which included people from the field, assessed the project favourably.
The arrondissement de Beauport is giving out $500 in grants to two organizations.
Autisme Québec receives $250 to support its mission and its activities.
Ressources familiales la vieille caserne de Montmorency (RE-FA-VIE) receives $250.
The amount granted to RE-FA-VIE will be used in particular to organize a community kitchen that prepares lunch boxes for the organization's frigo-partage (community fridge).
The money comes from the borough's budget, under the activity "Soutenir les conseils d'arrondissement" (Supporting borough councils).
The City is giving $115,720 to six organizations in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou for summer activities for youth aged 13 to 15, in the summer of 2026.
The amounts: Centre des loisirs Saint-Sacrement $27,030, Patro Laval $27,025, Les YMCA du Québec $17,605, Patro Roc-Amadour $18,650, Loisirs du Faubourg $13,290, Centre Mgr Marcoux $12,120.
The organizations expect 207 registrations, including 26 spots for integration.
The grants are paid in two instalments: 90% in the first payment ($104,148) and 10% in the second ($11,572).
The activities include group recreation and, for some youth, an introduction to the job of day camp leader.
The funding goes from $111,220 in 2025 to $115,720 in 2026; more than 212 teenagers took part last summer.
The borough council adopted the decision on April 27, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is giving $15,000 to the organization Mon Art Québec for the 2026 edition of the "Championnat international d'arts martiaux Québec Open".
It is also providing free municipal services (staff time and equipment loans) worth up to $1,500.
The event runs from April 23 to 26, 2026 at the PEPS of Université Laval and brings together close to a thousand karate athletes; admission is paid, except for children 6 and under.
The grant represents 4.5% of the event's projected budget, estimated at $335,500.
The funding is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners.
The money is paid in two parts: $12,000 within 10 days of the signing, then $3,000 when the financial statements and the final report are submitted, expected by the end of July 2026.
The organization must display the City's logo on its promotional materials and hold civil liability insurance of at least $5,000,000.

The City is giving Carrefour Jeunesse Emploi de la Capitale-Nationale the job of carrying out the "Chantier urbain Graff'Cité" project in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, for $208,464 (exempt from GST and QST).
The project runs from May 4 to December 4, 2026, which is 31 weeks.
The project aims to help 8 to 10 young adults who are far from the job market find work.
The young people find and clean up graffiti and raise public awareness about the issue.
In 2025, 19,551 graffiti were spotted on private properties in the borough (162,725 square feet) and 1,803 were cleaned up (17,002 square feet).
The most affected neighbourhoods are Saint-Roch, Vieux-Limoilou, Saint-Jean-Baptiste and Saint-Sauveur.
The agreement was made without a call for tenders, which the law allows with a non-profit organization.
The City is banning parking at all times on the west side of rue Semple, starting at rue Léon-Harmel and going south, over 31 metres.
Five parking spaces are being removed in this industrial area of the arrondissement des Rivières (district des Saules–Les Méandres).
The City explains that vehicles parked near the Léon-Harmel/Semple intersection were blocking visibility and getting in the way of heavy vehicle traffic.
The borough council is issuing order O-602 to put this ban into effect.
The City is authorizing the replacement of the brick siding on a duplex located at 1670 and 1680, avenue de la Capricieuse, in the Maizerets neighbourhood.
The work affects the front facade and the right side wall: the old brick will be replaced with new brick.
The new brick will be in shades of brown rather than orange, a colour found on other buildings in the area.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously supported the project on May 26, 2026, finding that it respects the style of the building.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council is approving the plans, which allows the permit to be issued.
The document does not mention any financial impact for the City.
The executive committee takes note of the quarterly report of the Fonds local d'investissement (FLI) for the period from January 1 to March 31, 2026.
No new loan was approved or paid out during this quarter, either under the FLI or under its emergency assistance program for small and medium-sized businesses (PAUPME).
The FLI took in $115,617.06 in loan repayments and $35,353.39 in interest, bringing its balance to $6,255,637.44 as of March 31, 2026.
The PAUPME component took in more than $1.1M in repayments and interest, bringing its balance to $19,705,607.53 as of March 31, 2026.
The document does not provide for any spending or new financial commitment by the City.
The Ville de Québec is signing an agreement with the Fonds d'action québécois pour le développement durable (FAQDD) to receive up to $50,127.58.
The money will be used to prepare a best-practices guide on the use and maintenance of solid-fuel appliances (such as wood heating).
The grant covers 50% of eligible expenses; the City must pay the other half.
The funding will be paid in three instalments: $12,531.89 on signing, $25,063.79 after the progress reports, and $12,531.89 after the final report.
The City must start the project as soon as the agreement is signed and finish it by August 31, 2027 at the latest.
A progress report is due by November 15, 2026 at the latest, or as soon as 80% of the first instalment has been used.

The project stems from the Plan d'action 2023-2027 pour la qualité de l'air and from a motion of the Commission consultative pour la qualité de l'air aimed at reducing fine particles from wood combustion.
The Ville de Québec is revising the investment policy of the Fonds local d'investissement (FLI), which it has managed since 2015 on behalf of the urban agglomeration.
The revision applies the standard model imposed on all of Quebec's MRCs by the ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie.
Loans from the fund can now run for up to 10 years.
The combined total of government assistance rises to 70% for private businesses and 85% for non-profit organizations.
The list of eligible projects now includes the production of non-controversial weapons.
Pre-start-up, turnaround and business acquisition (except as part of a structured business succession process) are not eligible.
The interest rate table must now appear in the policy.
The City is granting an exemption for a lot to be built on in the Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux neighbourhood, in Beauport.
The proposed lot (6 710 955) will be allowed to be 6.3 metres wide instead of the 16 metres normally required.
Without this exemption, the lots in the middle of the block cannot be built on, because they are not next to a street with water and sewer service.
The developer plans a single access driveway shared with the neighbouring proposed lot (6 710 954).
A second exemption request, concerning the rear setback of the future building, may follow.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on March 26, 2026.
The City is sending two police officers from the Unité des Crimes technologiques of the Service de police de Québec to a training session in Orillia, Ontario, from October 5 to 9, 2026.
The training covers the extraction and analysis of data from vehicle infotainment systems (Berla solution).
The Service de police says it currently has no capacity to carry out this type of expert analysis, even though this data is used in several criminal investigations.
The authorized expense is $20,525.80, of which about $16,500 is registration fees.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de police, under the police training activity.
The Service des finances will reimburse the expenses upon presentation of supporting documents; a difference of no more than 10% of the authorized amount is accepted.
The City is setting the maximum floor area per building at 20,000 square metres for offices and professional services in most of the secteur Chaudière, in the west end of Québec.

This area is located roughly east of the rivière du Cap-Rouge, the avenue Le Gendre and the rue William-Wood, south of the rue du Capitaine-Bernier and the avenue Blaise-Pascal, west of the autoroute Duplessis and north of the boulevard du Versant-Nord.

On seven lots covered by environmental compensation agreements with the provincial government, the permitted density drops to zero square metres: no office or professional service will be allowed there.
Previously, the permitted densities in this territory were 750, 1,500 or 2,500 square metres depending on the lot's designated use.
The City says it is adjusting these rules to address the points of non-compliance raised by the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation in a letter dated May 20, 2025.
No public consultation is planned, since this type of interim control by-law does not require one.
The secteur Chaudière, located at the western end of the tramway route, will be the subject of a special planning program.

The Ville de Québec is adding a new job title to the list of civil servant positions: "Première adjointe administrative ou premier adjoint administratif" (senior administrative assistant), rated as class 6.
This change comes from an agreement signed on February 6, 2026 between the City and the Syndicat des fonctionnaires municipaux de Québec (FISA).
A joint committee agreed on the job title, its evaluation and the employee who performs these duties.
The Service des ressources humaines must write to the employee and the manager concerned and update the relevant documents.
The agreement is part of the collective agreement currently in force; the document does not indicate any financial impact.

The Ville de Québec is entrusting the organization Canards Illimités Canada with preparing the plans and specifications, supervising the work and producing the final report to restore the wetlands at the former auto scrapyard on rue Roussin.
The contract is worth $227,172, an amount exempt from GST and QST because the organization is a charity.
The site is located in the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough.
The project aims to protect the City's main drinking water intake, located downstream on the rivière Saint-Charles, and to improve filtration and the regulation of water levels in a flood zone.
The site will be open to the public, with a small parking lot, trails and information panels.
The money comes from $3M in financial assistance from the ministère de l'Environnement for this restoration project.
The agreement applies from the time it is signed until each party has fulfilled its obligations.
The City is authorizing the construction of a six-storey building with about 67 housing units at 2255, boulevard Henri-Bourassa, in the Maizerets neighbourhood (Maizerets-Lairet district).

The project does not comply with the area's planning rules: height of up to 20 metres instead of 13, up to 70 housing units instead of 40, fewer large units than the required minimum, and a wider access lane.
To do this, the City is using Bill 31 on housing, which allows a non-compliant project to be authorized when the vacancy rate for rental housing is below 3% (it is at 2.2%).

The developer will have to meet certain conditions: at least 65 housing units, underground parking (90% of the spaces inside), 72 bicycle spaces, 20% green space, eight trees in the back yard and a terrace on the fifth floor.
The parts of the building over 13 metres will have to be set back at least 12 metres from the rear property line.
This project is not subject to a referendum, but a public consultation meeting will be held, followed by three days to send in written comments.

The project must start within 12 months after the resolution is adopted, otherwise the authorization lapses; breaking the conditions can lead to a fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.
The City is entrusting C.R.I. Environnement inc., of Coteau-du-Lac, with handling the household hazardous waste (HHW) brought back to its écocentres.
The contract runs from June 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029, for an estimated amount of $2,591,826.58 before GST and QST.
The company supplies the containers at the écocentres, and then handles the transportation, conditioning, recycling, recovery and disposal of the hazardous products.
The contract can be renewed twice for 12 months, with an annual price increase based on the Consumer Price Index.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 depend on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
Five companies submitted bids; one bid was found non-compliant because of missing proof related to the authorization certificates from the ministère de l'Environnement.
The City is refusing the request from the owner of 330, rue Delage, in Lac-Saint-Charles, who wanted to rebuild a detached garage 6.1 metres high.
The planning by-law for the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles limits the height of such a garage to 5 metres.
The original garage, 6.52 metres high, was destroyed by a fire and cannot be renovated.
The analysis concludes that a compliant 5-metre garage can be built and that an accessory building destroyed by a disaster has no acquired right.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had come out in favour of the exemption, but by a split vote of 3 in favour and 3 against.
The City is giving $5,000 to Parasports Québec to hold the "Championnat national junior de basketball en fauteuil roulant" (National Junior Wheelchair Basketball Championship).
The event runs from June 4 to 7, 2026 at Cégep Limoilou and brings together eight national junior teams.
Admission is free and the games will be broadcast on the Wheelchair Basketball Canada YouTube channel.
This is the qualifying tournament for the 2027 Canada Games, which will be held in Québec.
The grant covers 9.1% of the event's $54,808 budget; it depends on the other partners contributing enough.
Payment is made in two steps: $4,500 after signing, then $500 when the financial report is submitted, expected in September 2026.
Parasports Québec must display the City's logo in its promotional materials and take out $5,000,000 in liability insurance.
The City approves the new boundaries of the commercial district of the Société de développement commercial (SDC) de Montcalm.
A property located west of avenue De Bourlamaque is removed from the SDC's territory.
This address was not part of the original territory: it had been added later at the request of the former owner.
No new members are added, so no consultation of the merchants is required.
The change comes from a resolution adopted by the SDC's members at their general meeting of September 24, 2025.
The decision rests with city council.
The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing $11,100,000 in work to repair and upgrade drinking water and wastewater stations.
The City is borrowing the same amount, repayable over 15 years.
The funds are planned for the years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 capital works program.
An amount of $1,110,000 (10% of the expense) is taken from the general fund before the by-law comes into force, and will be paid back to it afterwards.
The amount covers the work, professional and technical services contracts, the hiring of staff, and the acquisition of buildings and servitudes.
The projects may be carried out anywhere in the territory under urban agglomeration jurisdiction.
The City may acquire, by mutual agreement or by expropriation, the buildings or servitudes needed for the work.
The City is signing seven agreements with seven recreation organizations to run the day camps of the Programme Vacances-Été 2026 in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
It will pay them a total of $2,245,184.60 in grants.

The amounts by organization: Patro Roc-Amadour $450,776.15, Centre Mgr Marcoux $415,471.29, Centre des loisirs St-Sacrement $379,757.12, Loisirs du Faubourg $325,426.33, Centre communautaire Jean-Guy Drolet $293,371.94, Patro Laval $286,784.44, Loisirs Montcalm $93,597.33.
Les YMCA du Québec are giving up the management of the day camp in the Saint-Roch sector; Loisirs du Faubourg is taking over and will manage a second site.
The Saint-Roch and centre Lucien-Borne sites are keeping the same capacity as in 2025, when they welcomed 488 children.
The organizations must comply with a set of specifications aimed at a uniform service offer everywhere in the city.
In 2025, eight agreements had been signed for a total of $2,351,096.04.
The City is extending its partnership agreement with the Commission de la capitale nationale du Québec until December 31, 2027. The agreement was signed on July 26, 2023 and covered 2023 to 2025.
The agreement funds promotional, artistic and commemorative projects up to $600,000 plus taxes: $300,000 from the City and $300,000 from the Commission.
The money will go toward a public artwork at place des Canotiers and a commemorative monument at parc de Notre-Dame-de-la-Garde.
Planning and completion delays push some payments into 2026 and 2027, beyond the period originally planned.
The amendment states that both parties' commitments depend on available funds and on the necessary authorizations.
All other conditions of the agreement remain unchanged.
The City is granting a minor exemption to the house at 3455, place du Trianon, in the Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy neighbourhood.
The building's front setback is 4.83 metres, whereas the borough's planning by-law requires 6.0 metres.
This siting is therefore deemed to comply: the owner will not have to move or demolish the building.
According to the analysis, the situation has existed since 1964 and no complaint has been recorded.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended granting the exemption on February 10, 2026.
The Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough council adopted the decision on March 9, 2026.
City council takes note of the lists of contracts and expenditures authorized by City employees for the month of April 2026.
In April 2026, the City awarded 164 contracts of more than $25,000, for a total of $102,018,530.
Employees with delegated authority approved $22,405,277.92 in expenditures during the month.
The lists also cover terminated contracts, calls for tenders cancelled after the opening of bids, and additional expenditures made through change notices.
The amounts shown exclude taxes; for agreements, they are estimates.
The list of contracts of $25,000 and more is published on the Ville de Québec website.
The City is selling four vacant lots along rue Bernard, in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles, with a total area of 2,490 square metres.
The buyer is the company Jeff Beauxséjours inc., for $175,000 plus taxes, or $70.28 per square metre.
This price is $20,000 less than the one approved in July 2025: checks revealed contaminants in the soil and the buyer had withdrawn from the first agreement.
The buyer has 36 months to begin construction of a building on the land.
The buyer grants the City, free of charge, a permanent water main and sewer easement over 104.50 square metres of two of the lots.
The sale is made without any warranty as to the quality of the soil: the risks related to contamination fall to the buyer.
The $175,000 will be paid into the City's general fund.
The City is giving $25,000 to the organization SOIT to offer French workshops to newcomers in the Sainte-Foy area.
The workshops (beginner and intermediate, with conversation practice) will take place two to three times a week, in the evening, in fall 2026, winter 2027 and spring 2027.
The grant covers the period from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027 and represents about 66% of the total cost of the project, estimated at $37,800.
The money will be used for things such as the salary of a part-time project manager, buying materials, premises and promotion.
This is a renewal: the City had granted the same amount the previous year.
In the first year, the organization held 54 workshops and 7 social and cultural activities, reaching close to 50 immigrants and recruiting 20 volunteers.
According to an assessment carried out in April 2024, the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge was home to 33% of Québec's immigrants in 2021.
The City wants to acquire a strip of land of about 261.8 square metres along rue de la Faune, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The land will be used to widen rue de la Faune, as part of the project to rebuild that street.
The purchase will be made by agreement with the owners or, if the discussions fail, by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the acquisition or expropriation proceedings.
The Division de l'arpentage et de la géomatique will prepare the plans, technical descriptions and cadastral operations that are needed.
The property, in its largest extent, is entered on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $99,000, which is $1.4 per square metre.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 related to the redevelopment work on rue de la Faune.
The City is changing the zoning of the property at 3233-3235, chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois, in the Plateau neighbourhood (arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
Zone 34509Cc, which contains only one property, where a gas station is located, is being eliminated and merged into the neighbouring mixed-use zone 34510Mc.
The change sets the front setback at 22.5 metres, measured from the centre line of chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois, for this property.
In the enlarged zone, the uses "gas station" and "car wash" become permitted, and the minimum number of storeys for a main building is removed.
According to the amendment sheet, these changes would notably allow residential use on this lot with a view to possible redevelopment.

The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; the conseil de quartier du Plateau must give its opinion and hold the public consultation meeting, followed by seven days to submit written comments.
The City will not hold an active participation measure, on the grounds that only one property is affected.
The City is paying $2,000 to the Caisse Desjardins du personnel municipal, which manages the Ascension scholarships given to students.
Eight scholarships of $500 each will be awarded to aspiring firefighters, funded in equal parts by the Service de protection contre l'incendie and the Caisse.
The scholarships reward academic results, involvement, perseverance and team spirit.
An eighth "Diversity and Inclusion" scholarship will go to a person from a recognized visible, ethnic or Indigenous minority, or of female gender, who is involved in their community.
This is the second year in a row that these scholarships are being awarded.
The money comes from the budget of the Service de protection contre l'incendie, which falls under agglomeration jurisdiction.
The executive committee adopted the decision on May 13, 2026.

The Ville de Québec is entrusting the organization Loisirs Duberger-Les Saules inc. with the programming, maintenance and supervision of the Sainte-Monique outdoor pool, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The agreement covers the period from June 18, 2026 to August 20, 2028, a total of 27 months.
The City will pay $162,374.15 (plus GST and QST); the net cost to the City is $170,472.57.
The amounts are spread over three years: about $55,155 in 2026, $56,805 in 2027 and $58,512 in 2028 (net of taxes).
The 2027 and 2028 amounts depend on the approval of those years' budgets.
The previous agreement with the organization ended on August 17, 2025.
The City is officially setting the boundaries of the rue De Buade area affected by infrastructure and redevelopment work in 2026.
The work runs approximately from April 1 to December 31, 2026, which is more than three consecutive months.
Businesses in the designated area will be able to apply for financial assistance provided under the support program tied to the TramCité project.
The 2026 fiscal year is the one used to calculate the assistance for businesses and their establishments in the designated area.

A plan attached to the order sets the boundaries of the designated area and the area of influence, in the neighbourhood around rue De Buade (rues Sainte-Anne, des Remparts, du Fort, Côte de la Montagne, etc.).
The executive committee must issue this order for the program to apply to this area.
The City is buying bulletproof vests for the police officers of the Service de police de Québec.
The contract goes to Logistique Unicorp inc., of Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu, for an estimated amount of $405,075 before taxes.
The contract runs from the date it is awarded until December 31, 2026, with the possibility of two 12-month renewals indexed to inflation (CPI).
Three companies submitted bids: Logistique Unicorp's was the lowest among the compliant bids; one bid was found technically non-compliant.
The net expense is estimated at $425,278.12 and will be paid out of the Service de police's operating budget.
The selected price is 15.1% below the requesting department's estimate ($477,275 before taxes).
The City is buying 12 light chassis trucks with extended cabs to replace vehicles that have reached the end of their useful life, for various departments.
The contract goes to P.E. Boisvert Auto ltée, of Boucherville, for $941,976 before taxes.
Three bids were received for public call for tenders 94087 and all of them met the requirements; P.E. Boisvert Auto offered the lowest price.
The City's net expense, after recovering the QST, comes to $988,957.05.
The requesting department had estimated the cost at $1,080,000, which is 12.8% more than the lowest bid.
The money comes from two agglomeration loan by-laws: $906,543.97 from R.A.V.Q. 1655 and $82,413.09 from R.A.V.Q. 1578.
The executive committee adopted the decision on January 28, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0100).
The City is transferring $3,693,688 from the budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire to four boroughs, for 2026.
This money is used to subsidize 11 federated community recreation centres in the boroughs of La Cité-Limoilou, Les Rivières, Charlesbourg and Beauport.

La Cité-Limoilou receives $2,627,111 for 8 centres: YWCA de Québec, Jean-Guy Drolet, Centre des loisirs Saint-Sacrement, Centre Durocher, Centre Mgr Marcoux, Loisirs Montcalm, Patro Laval and Patro Roc-Amadour.
Les Rivières receives $229,689 (Loisirs Lebourgneuf), Charlesbourg $398,199 (Patro de Charlesbourg) and Beauport $438,689 (Patro Le Pivot).
The program's funding envelope is indexed by 2% for 2026, which adds $7,238 to the amount provided for in the budget.
It is the boroughs that will then authorize the payment of the grants, under agreements still to come.
The City is giving an official name to a retention basin that until now was identified by the number S164: "Chasseforêt, bassin de rétention de".
The basin is located in the arrondissement de Beauport, district électoral de Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux.
The name comes from rue de Chasseforêt, located very close to the basin, following the usual practice of naming these facilities after a nearby street.
Retention basins temporarily store water and must be included in any new residential development under municipal requirements.
The Comité de commémoration et de toponymie proposed the name, and the Commission de toponymie du Québec was consulted about the spelling.
The document indicates no financial impact.
The RTC is rolling out a transitional bus network starting March 21, because of the tramway construction sites.
Four streets in the Grand Théâtre area are becoming one-way to let buses through.
One-way streets: avenue Turnbull southbound, rue Jacques-Parizeau westbound, rue de Claire-Fontaine northbound and rue De Senezergues northbound.
A two-way bike lane will be built on the south side of rue Jacques-Parizeau, between avenue Turnbull and rue de l'Amérique-Française.
The changes affect the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The parking rules tied to these changes will be modified gradually by the director of the Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente.
The City is awarding the redevelopment of rue des Alisiers to the company P.E. Pageau inc., for $312,762 before taxes (net expense of $328,361).
The work is taking place in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles and aims in particular to protect lac Saint-Charles.
Planned work includes adding and modifying ditches into grassed swales, a new layer of asphalt, waterproofing of manholes, and related work.
Seven companies submitted bids; P.E. Pageau inc. offered the lowest price, which is 31.8% below the City's estimate ($458,479).
The funding comes from a loan by-law ($71,391.50), financial assistance tied to the protection of lac Saint-Charles ($124,613.23), and City allocations ($132,356.27).
The contract provides for price adjustments based on the cost of bitumen and fuel.
The Ville de Québec is authorizing spending of $46,100,000 for work to rebuild and build municipal infrastructure that falls under urban agglomeration powers.
It is borrowing the same amount, repayable over fifteen years.
The work covers roads, water and sewer systems, lighting and traffic lights, public utility networks, engineering structures, and the development of municipal spaces.
The money will also pay for professional and technical services, hiring staff, buying buildings and easements, as well as grants and financial contributions.
The City may acquire by mutual agreement or by expropriation any building or easement needed for the work.
The projects will take place in the territory that falls under urban agglomeration powers, with no specific list of streets given.
An amount of $4,610,000 (10% of the spending) is being taken from the general fund, which will be reimbursed when the by-law comes into force.
The funds are planned for the years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The Ville de Québec is giving lawyer Vincent Rochette and the firm Norton Rose Fulbright the mandate to defend it in a new application for a class action, before all courts.
The application was received on July 14, 2026 in the case Richardy Henderson Pompe v. Ville de Montréal, Ville de Québec and others.

This class action would cover people who, since July 2, 2023, say they experienced racial profiling during police interventions (being stopped and questioned, recorded in police files, detained, arrested, searched, given a statement of offence, or subjected to use of force) other than the traffic stops already covered by the Guèye case.
The same firm is already defending the Ville de Québec in the case Guèye v. Ville de Québec, authorized in April 2025.
The fees for the joint mandate are estimated at between $150,000 and $200,000 before taxes, up to the decision on authorization of the class action.
The Ville de Québec's share is estimated at between $37,500 and $50,000 before taxes; the costs are shared with Blainville, Châteauguay and Terrebonne, which are represented together.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service des affaires juridiques; the executive committee adopted the decision on July 29, 2026.
The City is authorizing Société de développement Chauveau Est to extend rue John-Simons by about 465 metres, in the Des Châtels neighbourhood (La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The new section will service 11 industrial lots and will connect to the emergency access route leading to boulevard Couture.
The City is paying $216,800 before taxes: $210,000 to enlarge the water and sewer pipes, and $6,800 for the frontage of the retention basin. The net cost is $227,612.90.
The municipal work costs $8,029,479 including taxes, of which $7,789,615.36 is paid by the developer.
The developer will build a retention basin and draining planting beds, which will be handed over to the City free of charge; the Comité de toponymie will have to propose a name for the basin.
The developer has obtained authorization from the ministère de l'Environnement to fill in the wetlands on the site, and is paying in cash the compensation for parks and natural spaces.
According to the City's analysis, the project would attract $450M in private investment and would bring in $13,684,217 in net discounted tax revenue over 15 years.
The City wants to remove general tourist accommodation (C10 uses) from several zones in Vieux-Québec, the Vieux-Port and the cliff sector, to make more room for new housing.
Tourist accommodation establishments already in place will not become non-conforming: the use remains permitted in the blocks where it is already carried on.
The City is removing the limit on the number of restaurants (quota) in the Vieux-Port sector.
Restaurants become permitted in zone 11064Mb, which includes properties fronting on rue Saint-Paul.
The by-law affects 11 zones in the Vieux-Québec–Cap-Blanc–Colline parlementaire neighbourhood, Cap-aux-Diamants district; new zones will be created out of zones 11049Mb and 11021Mb.
A public consultation meeting will be held, the neighbourhood council will be consulted, and interested people will have seven days after the meeting to submit their comments in writing.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; the borough council was aiming for adoption on August 31, 2026.
The City is giving $600,000 to L'Institut canadien de Québec for the Québec en toutes lettres festival, which is $200,000 per edition in 2026, 2027 and 2028.
It is also providing free municipal services (staff and equipment loans) of up to $1,000 per year, for a total of $603,000.
The festival will take place from October 15 to 25, 2026, from October 14 to 24, 2027, and from October 12 to 22, 2028.

The program takes place in outdoor spaces and venues in Limoilou, Montcalm, Saint-Jean-Baptiste, Saint-Roch, Saint-Sauveur, Vieux-Québec and Sillery, including place D'Youville, parc Durocher and the bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy.
The event's planned budget is $692,160 in 2026, $723,660 in 2027 and $745,660 in 2028; the City's support covers 26.8% to 28.9% of the budget.
The support depends on enough money coming from the other partners and on the approval of the 2027, 2028 and 2029 municipal budgets.
The support goes beyond the funding guidelines of the Vision événementielle and is part of a gradual decrease in municipal funding.
The arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles is authorizing three of its elected officials to attend the annual convention (Assises annuelles) of the Union des municipalités du Québec.
The event takes place from May 13 to 15, 2026, at the Centre des congrès de Québec.
The people concerned are president Marc Roussin, councillor Marie-Josée Asselin and councillor Stéphane Lachance.
The City is paying or reimbursing registration fees of $890, plus applicable taxes.
Other expenses will be reimbursed upon presentation of supporting documents, in accordance with the by-law on the expenses of council members.
The money comes from the borough's budget, under the activity "Soutenir les conseils d'arrondissement" (Supporting borough councils).
The City is awarding Construction et Pavage Portneuf inc. the contract for rebuilding work on rue de Soulanges for $786,625.34 (plus GST and QST).
The work includes rebuilding the water main and sanitary sewer systems on rue de Soulanges, between boulevard Hochelaga and rue Jules-Dallaire.
Work is also planned on avenue Fournier: reconfiguring the sewer systems and repairing the roadway.
The work site is in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
Eleven companies submitted bids; Portneuf submitted the lowest price, 0.8% above the City's estimate.
The net cost to the City comes to $825,858.28, paid for through loan by-law R.V.Q. 3390.
The contract provides for price adjustments based on the cost of asphalt and fuel.
The City is paying $33,178 to Adaptavie inc. for the year 2026.
The money supports the offering of leisure and sports activities adapted for people living with functional limitations, within the territory of Québec City.
The same amount was paid in 2024 and in 2025.
At the end of 2026, the organization will have to submit a report on its activities, a financial report and proof of the visibility given to the City.
The funds come from the operating budget of the Arrondissement des Rivières.
Adaptavie inc. is located at 525, boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel Est, in Québec.
The City is entrusting the organization Loisirs des Hauts-Sentiers L.D.H.S. with monitoring the recreational and sports facilities and equipment of the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The contract runs from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027, for $156,344.50 (plus GST and QST).
The net cost to the City is $164,142.18, taken from the borough's operating budget.
The agreement may be renewed three times for 12 months, with the amount adjusted according to the minimum wage in effect on May 1 of 2027, 2028 and 2029.
The 2027 portion ($49,242.65, net of taxes) depends on the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The organization must provide qualified staff and notify the City of any incident and of any service interruption.
The City is banning vehicles from stopping at any time along 25 metres on the west side of rue des Alleghanys, starting at rue Ardouin heading south (arrondissement de Beauport).
RTC buses and passenger vehicles used for on-demand transit may still stop there.
Four parking spaces are being removed in this industrial area.
The request came from the RTC: five bus routes travel on this street and stop at stop 3937, and parked cars were preventing buses from pulling up close to the curb.
The change is meant to make it easier for passengers to get on and off.
The Ville de Québec is signing agreements with 6 organizations to fund the Canadian Urban Forest Conference, which will be held in Québec from October 13 to 16, 2026.
Two sponsorships total $25,500: $5,500 from the Ordre des ingénieurs forestiers du Québec and $20,000 from the Wildfire Resilience Consortium of Canada ($15,000 plus $5,000 with nothing in return).
Four companies are each renting a booth for $1,250: Diamond Head Consulting, Xéos imagerie, Consultants AECOM and Distribution Solida, for a total of $5,000.
In all, the City is taking in $30,055.24 in sponsorships and booth rentals, net of taxes on the value of the tickets provided.

The City is correcting a decision from May 2026: the Wildfire Resilience Consortium of Canada had asked to reduce its contribution from $25,000 to $20,000, so its agreement moves into the new block (9 organizations instead of 10).
The City is acting as the lead party responsible for organizing, running and funding the event, under its agreement with Arbres Canada.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 2355, boulevard Central, in the Duberger–Les Saules neighbourhood (Arrondissement des Rivières).
The detached single-family house will be allowed to keep a rear setback of 4.7 metres, whereas the planning by-law requires 9.
The request comes from the owner, who wants to sell the house and whose rear setback did not comply.
The house was built around 1965 and no complaints have been received about this situation.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on June 1, 2026, unanimously.
The document does not indicate any financial impact.
The City is giving $63,825 to the organization Le Piolet for a second year of its sanitary services project for people experiencing homelessness.
The project takes place at the organization's facilities in the Vanier area, where it mainly targets young adults.
The money is used to maintain a resource that broadens access to showers and laundry; the organization also offers free meals, social activities and psychosocial follow-up.
The first year, funded with $60,450, reached about thirty young people without meeting all the targets that had been set.
Le Piolet must mention the City's contribution in its publications and submit a report on activities and a financial report by December 31, 2026.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The City wants to acquire a lot of about 659.6 m² along rue de la Faune, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The lot would be used to widen rue de la Faune, as part of the project to rebuild this street.
The City will first try to reach a negotiated agreement with the owners; if the discussions do not succeed, it may proceed by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the acquisition or expropriation proceedings.
The Service de l'ingénierie will prepare the plans, technical descriptions and land survey (cadastral) operations that are needed.
The entire property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $81,000, which is $13.50 per square metre.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 related to the redevelopment work on rue de la Faune.
The City is giving $15,000 to the Société canadienne de génie civil, a non-profit organization.
The money will help support the organization's 2026 Annual Conference, on the theme "Tradition à innovation".
The event will take place at the Centre des congrès de Québec from June 3 to 5, 2026, and draws close to 1,000 participants each year.
In return, the City gets Platinum partner status and wants a seat on the organizing committee.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de l'ingénierie.
The executive committee approved the decision (resolution CE-2026-0430).
On June 18, 2026, the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec authorized the demolition of the heritage house at 1421, avenue des Grands-Pins, in the Sillery area.
The building, built between 1916 and 1917, is described as the second-oldest house on the avenue; experts conclude that it is in very poor overall condition and that urgent structural work is needed.
The authorization comes with conditions: the replacement project will have to be adjusted according to the Commission's recommendations and be the subject of a permit application.
Three written comments were received and two people spoke at the public meeting; access to the building has been secured since May 22, 2026.
A request for review was filed to add conditions on retrieving personal belongings left in the building; city council upheld the decision without changes.
The urban agglomeration council takes note of the decision, waives its power of disallowance and shortens the 90-day period.
The City is putting up for sale at public auction the properties whose 2025 taxes or taxes from earlier years remain unpaid.
The auction will be held on Wednesday, November 25, 2026 at 10 a.m., and may continue until Thursday, November 26, 2026 if all the properties are not sold.
The owners concerned are listed in the treasurer's statement attached to the file, as of August 25, 2026, with balances ranging from a few hundred dollars to more than $18,000.
Buyers will become permanent owners if the property is not bought back (redeemed) within the year following the auction; council consents in advance to the deeds of sale.
The City may itself acquire certain properties at the auction, and the city clerk is authorized to sign the deeds in its favour.
The city clerk or the assistant city clerk will carry out all the procedures for the sale.
The City says it cannot estimate the amounts of taxes that will be recovered, since no minimum price is provided for by law.
The City is adding $8,640 (plus taxes) to the contract with the firm CBTEC inc. for mechanical and electrical engineering services at caserne no 1.
The total contract therefore rises to $244,520 (plus taxes), after an initial contract of $86,300 in March 2023 and four amendments totalling $149,580 in 2025.
The project involves repairing the building envelope, interior reconfigurations, ventilation work and modernizing the elevator.
The added amount pays for a value analysis exercise, after the call for tenders was cancelled this winter, in order to reduce the gap between the budget and the bids received.

The firm must also analyze the impact of the Code de construction du Québec 2020, which will apply to work sites starting in October 2027, whereas the project was designed according to the 2015 version.
The net expenditure, after recovery of the QST, is $9,070.92, funded by an agglomeration loan by-law.
The City is awarding Air Liquide Canada inc. the supply of welding gases and specialty gases for the Complexe de valorisation énergétique.
The contracts run from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2031, with the possibility of five one-year renewals and an annual adjustment based on the consumer price index.
The estimated amounts are $59,146.25 for the welding gases and $34,312.14 for the specialty gases, before taxes.
The net expenditure, which falls under agglomeration jurisdiction, is estimated at $98,119.63.
The welding gases are used to repair equipment; the specialty gases are used to calibrate the chimney analyzers, four times a day per furnace.
Two companies submitted bids; Air Liquide offered the lowest price for both lots.
The amounts for 2027 to 2031 remain conditional on the adoption of the annual budgets.

The City is sending two employees of the Service de protection contre l'incendie, a district chief and a lieutenant-instructor, to a New York fire department symposium on fires in high-rise buildings.
The event takes place in New York from October 23 to 25, 2026, or on another date set by the organizers.
The authorized expense is $6,439.24, taken from the training budget of the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
The Service des finances will reimburse the expenses upon presentation of supporting documents, with a tolerated variance of no more than 10% of the authorized amount.
The topics covered include emerging technologies, building safety, energy storage systems and next-generation construction.
Upon their return, the two participants must pass on the knowledge they gained to the officers and the staff concerned.
The Ville de Québec is signing an agreement with Fujitsu Conseil (Canada) inc. to use the GOcité software from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029.
The total cost is $373,841.33 (plus GST and QST), for a net expense of $392,486.69 for the urban agglomeration.
Support and maintenance fees come to $82,816.56 per year from 2026 to 2029, and $61,220.45 goes to redevelopment (ArcGIS Pro migration of the cadastre-matrix module).
GOcité manages the graphic assessment roll of the Service de l'évaluation and meets the requirements of the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation.
The software is owned by five cities (Longueuil, Saint-Eustache, Sherbrooke, Thetford Mines, Victoriaville); Longueuil coordinates its development.
The agreement was awarded without a call for tenders because only one supplier holds the rights to the software.
The agreement will renew automatically under the same conditions if the owner cities renew their contract with Fujitsu, unless Québec gives written notice to the contrary.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the annual budgets.
The City is banning parking at all times in three new zones on rue Marius-Fortier, in the Beauport industrial park (north sector).
The bans apply to the stretch between avenue Nordique and boulevard Armand-Paris: one zone on the east side (86 m) and two zones on the west side (34 m and 26 m).
The zones are located on either side of the entrances to the buildings at 581 and 613, rue Marius-Fortier, and along the inside curve of the street.
The change is meant to make it easier for heavy trucks delivering to these two businesses to manoeuvre.
About 15 parking spaces will disappear in the area; the document states that workers have access to off-street parking.
The Beauport borough council is enacting ordinance O-497 to put these rules into effect.
The City is adding a stop sign on rue des Jardins, at the north approach to the intersection with rue Sainte-Anne.
Until now, only two of the four approaches to this intersection had a stop sign (south and east); vehicles coming from the north did not have to stop.
The area affected is Vieux-Québec, in the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou, district of Cap-aux-Diamants.
The Service du transport cites the heavy tourist traffic and the large number of pedestrians at this intersection.
The change is made through order O-1434, adopted by the borough council.
No financial impact is indicated in the document.
The City wants to obtain rights of way (servitudes) on a piece of land bordering rue Mendel, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, for the TramCité tramway project.
These servitudes will be used to move conduits and public utility networks along the route.
They are temporary, lasting 3 years: two underground (7.9 and 11.4 m²), one overhead (206.2 m²) and one right of way (130 m²).
An agreement with the owner had already been authorized in September 2025, but operational issues are leading the City to start expropriation proceedings in order to clear the rights of way in time.
The Service des affaires juridiques may negotiate by mutual agreement or expropriate, and may withdraw if the project no longer needs the servitudes.
The land in question, as a whole, is assessed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $17,700,000, which is $182.99 per square metre.
The funds come from the loan by-law related to building the structuring public transit network.
The City is requesting $1,047,664 from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for five sidewalk projects near schools, estimated at $2,216,215 in total.
The work is planned for 2027, as part of the Stratégie de sécurité routière 2025-2029.
École Saint-Mathieu: new sidewalk between rue de Bar-de-Duc and rue Gabriel-Dumont ($286,458).
École de la Ribambelle: new sidewalk between the entrance to parc de la Ribambelle and avenue Saint-Michel ($328,747).
École Saint-Bernard: new sidewalk on rue Fenil, between avenue Chauveau and boulevard Bastien ($403,325).
École de l'Arc-en-Ciel: sidewalk between rue Louis-IX and rue Racine ($574,985), then a sidewalk on rue Louis-IX between rue des Mirabilis and rue de l'Hôpital with a raised intersection ($622,699).
If the ministère accepts, the City will sign an agreement and receive up to 80% of the funding in a first payment; the funding would be cancelled if the terms are not met.
The City is amending its 2022 agreement with the Société d'habitation du Québec in order to free up an amount of $108,458 that went unused.
This amount had been paid to the City by the Société d'habitation du Québec, but the original agreement provided for only $10,500,000 in payments to organizations.
The grant for the Inter'elle project, run by the organization Un Toit Juste Pour Elles, goes from $8,200,000 to $8,308,458 for 20 units intended for women at risk of homelessness.
The $2,300,000 grant to the Société immobilière YWCA - Québec for the Résidence Cardinal-Bégin stays the same: 14 units for women and children fleeing domestic violence.
The total of the agreement reaches $10,608,458 for 34 housing units.
Another document will have to follow in order to authorize the payment of the $108,458 to the organization itself.
The conseil d'arrondissement de Beauport is approving two exemptions from the planning by-law for 267, rue Simone-Routier, in the Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux neighbourhood.
The owner will be allowed to build a garage with a lean-to in the front yard, in front of the house, which the by-law normally does not permit.
The parking area will be allowed to be 10.5 metres wide instead of 7.0 metres, partly in front of the front of the house.

Three conditions apply: the accessory building must be more than 5.4 metres from the front property line, the parking area no more than 7.0 metres from that line, and the driveway between the parking area and the house must be no more than 4 metres wide.

The City explains its decision by the irregular shape of the lot, the slope between the street and the house (13 to 17%), the presence of a shoreline and Hydro-Québec power lines, and the house being located on a back lot.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 19, 2026.
The City is obtaining the right to temporarily use a strip of land of about 38 square metres along boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
This construction and passage easement would last about 13 months, notably to set up temporary traffic lanes during the work.
The City will try to reach an amicable agreement with the owners; otherwise, it will proceed by expropriation.
The owners have already been informed of the process, the upcoming steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
If the TramCité project no longer needs the land, the City may abandon the expropriation proceedings, in whole or in part.
The land in question, in its largest extent, is entered on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $505,000, or $663.16 per square metre.
The funds come from the urban agglomeration loan by-law related to the structuring public transit network (TramCité project).
The Ville de Québec is adopting its 2026-2030 Action Plan for Seniors, which replaces the measures for seniors previously included in the 2021-2024 universal accessibility plan.
The plan is built around four areas: a complete living environment, participation and social inclusion, health and safety, and communication and information.
The City is setting up a monitoring committee responsible for implementing and evaluating the plan.
This committee will bring together the elected official in charge of the file, municipal employees, outside partners and citizens who are members of the Conseil des personnes aînées.
The plan was prepared in 2025 based on consultations with municipal departments, citizens and partner organizations.
Québec has been accredited as a Municipalité amie des aînés since 2012, a recognition granted by the Secrétariat aux aînés of the Government of Quebec.

The Ville de Québec is applying for financial assistance from the Fonds régions et ruralité of the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation to carry out a diagnostic and a feasibility study.
The study is to assess the possible forms of cooperation with other municipalities to manage the water of the rivière Saint-Charles watershed, upstream from the Château d'eau water intake.
This watershed is the city's main source of drinking water and supplies 300,000 residents; the document states that the condition of lac Saint-Charles remains a concern.
The program covers 20% of the costs, up to a maximum of $20,000; the City agrees to pay its share and to act as the organization responsible for the project.
François Trudel, director of the Service de la planification de l'aménagement et de l'environnement, is designated to sign the documents related to the application.
The City is cancelling its resolution of April 8, 2026 and replacing it, because the ministère required more details about its commitments.
The new resolution must be sent to the ministère by June 1, 2026; technical specifications will then be prepared in order to launch a call for tenders.
The City wants to acquire a strip of land of about 76.8 square metres at 1617, rue Gagnon, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The goal: to widen rue de la Faune as part of the project to rebuild that street.
If the agreement with the owner falls through, the City can proceed by expropriation; the Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings.
The land, in its largest extent, is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $177,000, or $165.85 per square metre.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 on the redevelopment work on rue de la Faune.
The Division de l'arpentage et de la géomatique will prepare the plans and the cadastral operation required.
The City agrees to push back to May 31, 2026 the deadline to sign the sale of a piece of land on rue de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres to the organization Utile Québec 3.
The land (lot 6 665 145), located in the Écoquartier de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres, is being sold for $800,000 under the purchase offer signed on July 18, 2025.
Utile Québec 3 plans a mixed-use project there with about 285 student housing units, up to 250 m² of commercial space and a maximum of 101 indoor parking spaces.
The delay is requested because the organization is finalizing its financing with partners and cannot purchase the neighbouring building at 124, rue de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres within the deadline.
The buyer must start construction within 12 months after the deed is signed, otherwise it pays the City $3,000 per month.
The sale is made without warranty: the buyer takes on the risks and costs related to the condition of the soil and to the environment.
The land is in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou; the decision is up to city council.
The Ville de Québec is granting a subsidy of up to $75,000 to the non-profit organization Un toit en réserve de Québec inc.
The money will be used to prepare a housing project of 251 social and affordable units at 3055 to 3065, 2e Avenue, in the Saint-Albert-le-Grand area.
The subsidy covers start-up costs: environmental assessments, soil tests, title searches, surveying, land appraisal, architect's sketches and developer's fees, with a cap for each spending item.
The organization has six months after signing the agreement to use the money, and 12 months to submit its project to an assistance program recognized by the City.
Only costs billed after March 31, 2026 are eligible; if the organization receives another subsidy for the same costs, the City's amount will be reduced by that much.
The $75,000 will be deducted from the contribution the City could pay later if the project is selected under an assistance program.
The funds come from an agglomeration loan by-law linked to the Vision de l'habitation.
The City is pushing back to February 21, 2027 the deadline to begin work on a student housing project at 100-124, rue de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres, in Saint-Roch.
The original deadline, set by a resolution dated July 2, 2025, required the organization UTILE to start construction no later than July 1, 2026.
The postponement is due to waiting for funding from the SCHL and to the reconstruction work on rue de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres, which is 90% complete and will continue in the spring and summer of 2026.
The project itself is not changing: about 285 student housing units, two towers of 13 and 11 storeys linked by a 4-storey podium, businesses on the ground floor, 19 trees planted, and indoor parking.
The exemptions remain the same: a height of 43 metres instead of 34, housing units on the ground floor, the front setback, and a generator in the front yard.
The process includes a public consultation meeting, followed by three days to send in written comments.
Breaking the conditions of the resolution leads to a fine of $1,000 for an individual and $2,000 in other cases, doubled for a repeat offence.
The City is reserving a parking space for people with reduced mobility on rue Sainte-Agnès, in La Cité-Limoilou (Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur district).
The space is located in front of 432, rue Sainte-Agnès, on the north side, between rue Renaud and rue Bigaouette.
The space is 7 metres long and starts 35 metres east of rue Renaud.
Only vehicles displaying a sticker, licence plate or permit for people with disabilities will be allowed to park there.
The request came from a resident of the building who holds a SAAQ sticker.
No existing parking space is being removed.
The executive committee takes note of the quarterly report on urban forestry agreements related to the TramCité tramway project, for the period from October 1 to December 31, 2025.
Nine agreements were signed with property owners along the tramway route during this quarter.
The properties affected are located on boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest and Est, avenue Blaise-Pascal and chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois.
All nine agreements provide for the clearing of a right-of-way (tree cutting, transplanting, pruning or protection).
Four agreements include planting by the City on private land, and six provide for the City to maintain the trees in perpetuity.
Only one agreement includes compensation, of $180.00, for 164, boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest.
The Ville de Québec is joining a purchasing agreement with the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales to buy switches and network products for the ExpoCité site.
The agreement applies from March 9, 2026 to March 31, 2028.
The estimated amount is $2,500,000 (plus GST and QST), and the net expense is estimated at $2,624,687.50.
The purchases are meant to supply the Centre Vidéotron with switches, firewalls, routers and wireless equipment.
Orders may go to several selected suppliers, as long as their price is no more than 17% higher than the lowest price.
The 2027 and 2028 expenses remain conditional on the approval of those years' budgets.
Going through the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales makes it possible to enter into this contract without a call for tenders.
The City is adding $190,597.00 (plus taxes) to the contract of the company Upex inc. for urban technical network work related to the TramCité project.
The contract therefore goes from $181,596.30 to $372,193.30 (plus taxes). The net cost to the City is $200,103.03.
The work is being done mainly under chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois and on the grounds of école secondaire De Rochebelle, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The additional amount is due to excavation: conduits and connections had to be built over a longer distance than expected, according to Hydro-Québec's preliminary data.
More materials and more time were needed to complete the work.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 on building the structuring public transit network.
The executive committee adopted resolution CE-2026-0339 on March 18, 2026.
The City is awarding Biogénie Canada inc. the contract to transport and recycle green waste collected in bags (plastic and paper) in the agglomeration of Québec.
The contract covers the spring and fall 2026 collections and starts on April 1, 2026.
The estimated amount is $1,295,400 before taxes; the net cost to the City is estimated at $1,360,008.08.
Only one company submitted a bid; after negotiation, it lowered its price from $1,333,500 to $1,295,400.

The chosen price is 44% higher than the City's estimate ($899,686), mainly because of new regulations on the sale of compost and soil mixes, investments at the Saint-Henri-de-Lévis composting site, and less competition.
The contract can be renewed for one more year, with prices indexed to the consumer price index.
Lot 2 (bulk green waste, fall 2026) was awarded separately through a delegation of powers.
The Ville de Québec wants to borrow $1,275,000 to buy vehicles and motorized equipment for the Service de police.
The purchase covers gas-powered and electric vehicles, pickup trucks, vans, trailers, accessories and the necessary technology solutions.
These vehicles will be added to the Service de police's current fleet, to meet the needs of newly created units and new responsibilities.
The loan will be repaid over five years, out of the City's general revenues.
The City will first take $127,500 (10% of the expense) from its general fund, which will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The expense falls under the urban agglomeration of Québec and is planned for years 2026 and 2027 of the 2026-2035 investment plan.

The City is awarding Ortec Environnement Services inc. (Lévis) the cleaning of the water collection and treatment structures at the Ville de Québec landfill site, at 50, route 138 in Saint-Tite-des-Caps.
The contract runs from June 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028, for an estimated amount of $993,204.45 (plus GST and QST).
The call for tenders provides for two possible 12-month renewals, with an annual indexation based on the Consumer Price Index.
The net expense for the urban agglomeration is estimated at $1,042,740.52, paid out of the operating budget of the Service de la gestion des matières résiduelles et de la valorisation.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 still have to be approved when the budgets for those years are adopted.
Only one bid was received: it is 1.2% higher than the City's estimate ($981,822 before taxes). The other supplier that was approached explained why it did not bid.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 1333, rue Hamann, in the Lac-Saint-Charles neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The existing house is considered compliant even though it is 4.39 metres high, while the planning by-law requires at least 5 metres.

The decision brings into compliance a building that has already been built with a permit: the height was measured at the back, where it meets the requirement, but the sloping land makes the building lower on the street side.
According to the analysis on file, the exemption has no effect on the neighbours, since it involves a minimum height that was not met.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 29, 2026; the borough council adopted resolution CA6-2026-0046.
The City is granting a minor exemption for the vacant lot at 605, boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, in the Vanier neighbourhood (Arrondissement des Rivières).
The developer wants to build a six-storey residential building with 227 housing units there.
The exemption allows a setback angle of 51 degrees instead of the 45 degrees required by the borough's planning by-law.
Without this exemption, the project would have to remove a balcony and a corner of the building on the top floor.
The building must be set back from boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel because of a power transmission line and a wastewater pipe.
The new building would be 25 metres (82 feet) from the existing neighbouring building.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour on February 2, 2026; the borough council made its decision on February 24, 2026.
The City is drawing $2,202,000 from the Fonds réservé aux parcs, terrains de jeux et espaces naturels for work in 2026.
The money will be used to develop and rebuild parks and recreational facilities.
Breakdown by borough: La Haute-Saint-Charles $329,000, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge $187,000, Charlesbourg $182,000, Des Rivières $168,000, Beauport $118,000, La Cité-Limoilou $42,000.
An amount of $1,176,000 is allocated to projects affecting the entire City.
For one of the projects, $516,000 planned for 2026 was to come from a loan by-law: this funding will instead come from the Fonds des parcs.
The amounts are planned for the year 2026 of the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The City wants to acquire about 20.2 square metres of a lot located along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité project (structuring public transit network).
The acquisition will be used to widen the 1re Avenue right-of-way.
The purchase will be made by mutual agreement or, if no agreement is reached, by expropriation; the Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings.
The owner has been informed of the process, the next steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
If the project no longer needs the land, the City may withdraw from the expropriation proceedings, in whole or in part.
The entire lot is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $135,000, or $718.47 per square metre.
The funds come from the agglomeration loan by-law related to the structuring public transit network.
The City is awarding Groupe Colas Québec inc. the contract to redevelop route de l'Église for $5,145,000 (before GST and QST).
The work will replace the water and sewer lines between chemin Saint-Louis and rue de Valmont, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The project adds active mobility features between rue de l'Anse and chemin Saint-Louis, to improve safety for users.
Five companies submitted bids, all of them compliant; Colas submitted the lowest price, 12.7% below the City's estimate ($5,896,250.75).
The net cost to the City is $5,401,606.88, funded by two loan by-laws ($2,356,303.46 and $3,045,303.41).
The contract includes clauses for adjusting asphalt and fuel prices.
The executive committee adopted the decision on May 6, 2026.
The City is awarding a contract for the supply of General Motors parts to Laurier-Station Chevrolet Buick GMC inc., of Laurier-Station.
The contract runs from September 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029 and provides for price indexation.
The estimated amount is $806,009.04 before taxes; the net expense is estimated at $846,208.74.
The parts are for the Service de la gestion des équipements motorisés.
Four bids were received, all compliant; the lowest ($806,009.04) wins, which is 3.5% below the City's estimate ($834,972).
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets by the competent authorities.
The City is authorizing spending of $1,415,000 for land-use planning and environment work.
It is borrowing the same amount, to be repaid over five years.
The money will be used to hire staff, retain professional and technical services firms, buy goods and equipment, and pay out grants or financial contributions.
The activities covered include consultations, collecting and analyzing data, taking part in innovation projects, training, and improving the planning process.
The projects affect the entire territory under the City's jurisdiction.
An amount of $141,500 (10% of the spending) is taken from the general fund, which will be reimbursed when the by-law comes into force.
The funds are planned for 2026 to 2028, and the spending will be shared between the urban agglomeration and local (proximity) jurisdictions.

The centre communautaire Paul-Émile-Beaulieu, in the Lac-Saint-Charles–Saint-Émile district, has remained closed since the fire of August 17, 2025, which affected every floor, part of the exterior walls and the roof.
The City will aim for a reopening in 2027: a call for tenders will be issued for the rebuilding, after which the organizations will have a period to move in and settle into the space.
No partial use of the building is possible for now, because air quality and evacuation cannot be assured; the City is continuing its analyses to see whether a phased opening becomes permitted.
Salvaging the existing ventilation and heating systems could cut 3 to 6 months off the timeline, according to the expert assessments under way.
For the summer 2026 day camps, the City is in discussions with the Centre de services scolaire in order to move the activities to nearby schools.
Since September 2025, the City has relocated the organizations, redone the roof, temporarily sealed the building against water, and ordered an air quality audit.
The Institut canadien de Québec is sorting through the roughly 17,000 documents from the library and testing cleaning methods.
The City is adding a new job title to its list of professional positions: kinesiologist, class 2.
This position meets a need of the Service de police de la Ville de Québec.
The City and the Alliance du personnel professionnel de la Ville de Québec signed an agreement to this effect on May 7, 2026.
A joint job evaluation committee first reviewed the file and set the classification of the new job title.
The Service des ressources humaines will update all the documents concerned, and the agreement is added to the collective agreement in force.
The file was submitted to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The City is transferring $360,000 from its contingency fund to the budget of the Service des affaires juridiques.
This money is used to pay for sending, by certified mail, the statements of offence that police officers refuse to hand out to offenders.
This refusal stems from a union directive sent to police officers in the spring of 2025, as part of pressure tactics by the Service de police de la Ville de Québec.
The amount covers the additional costs expected from May to October 2026.
The sum is divided into $184,320 from the agglomeration contingency fund and $175,680 from the local (proximity) contingency fund.
Some statements of offence continue to be withdrawn under the usual internal rules, for example those issued to people experiencing homelessness.
