The executive committee acknowledges the filing of the lists of additional expenses over $250,000 authorized by delegated employees, for the weeks of May 10 and May 24, 2026.

Avenue Charles-Huot worksite: an additional $688,668.69 for more rock to be excavated by blasting, rebuilding driveways, temporary lighting and the water main. The contract goes from $7,557,295 to $8,245,963.69.

Redevelopment of 4e Avenue (phase II): an additional $651,102.72 for a new traffic light, a modified layout between 41e and 42e Rue, and postponing part of the work to 2026. The contract goes from $11,387,722.19 to $12,038,824.91.
The costs related to postponing the work and to the new layout of 4e Avenue are shared equally between the City and the developer.

Snow removal equipment: an additional $326,508 to the contract with Service d'équipement G.D. inc. for reversible snowplows, replacement spreaders and a trailer hitch. The contract goes from $881,964 to $1,208,472.
The amounts are shown before taxes and total $688,668.69 for the week of May 10 and $977,610.72 for the week of May 24.

The City is expanding parking permit zone 6 to include residents of rue Gérard-Morisset and the future residents of a City-owned lot where it wants to develop a housing project (lots 2 742 051 and 2 768 033). These people will therefore be able to get an on-street parking permit.
In this zone 6, about half of the spaces reserved for permit holders are occupied, according to the document.
Five buildings are being removed from their permit zone: their occupants will not be able to buy an on-street parking permit.
Residential buildings affected: 510, rue de l'Éperon (97 dwellings), 401, rue Saint-Paul (141 dwellings added) and 304, boulevard Charest Est (82 lodging units).
Office buildings affected, because of possible future residential use: 880, chemin Sainte-Foy (project of 300 dwellings) and 710, Place D'Youville (project of 133 dwellings).
Zones 5, 6, 8, 10 and 12 of the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou are having their plans changed. The City says developers were notified that future occupants will not be entitled to a permit.
The City is granting an exemption for 335, rue de Bigorre, in the Notre-Dame-des-Laurentides neighbourhood (Arrondissement de Charlesbourg).
The owner will be allowed to expand the house while leaving 2.0 metres between the building and the neighbouring property line, instead of the 3.0 metres normally required.
The expansion consists of adding an attached garage with a livable room above it.
Only a small front portion of the expansion exceeds the standard; the back will be 4.3 metres from the lot line.
The "pie-slice" shape of the lot, a ventilation outlet and an electrical mast make it impossible to move the expansion further back.
After the work, there will be at least 7.5 metres between the side walls of the house and the neighbour's house.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on April 8, 2026.
The City wants to obtain a permanent servitude (right of use) over a strip of land of about 15.80 square metres along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou (part of lot 6 733 986).
This servitude will be used to move public utility conduits and networks for the TramCité tramway project.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement with the owner or, failing that, by expropriation; discussions will take place during the process.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings and to withdraw them if the project no longer needs the servitude.
The Division de l'arpentage et de la géomatique will prepare the plans and the technical description of the land concerned.
The funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to building the structuring public transit network.
The matter must be decided by the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The owner of 5254, boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel wants to convert a ground-floor commercial unit to add a catering service.
The zoning requires 32 parking spaces, but the project provides 31.
The City is exempting the owner from providing the missing space, if he pays $500 to the “Fonds de stationnement” (parking fund).
The payment must be made no later than 30 days after the borough council adopts the resolution.
The Service du transport notes that the area is served by public transit and that on-street parking there is little used.
The City specifies that a parking ban could be put in place on boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel if vehicles park there.
The building is located in the arrondissement des Rivières, district des Saules-Les Méandres, between rue Flaubert and rue Michel-Fragasso.
The City is buying fire hydrants and spare parts for its Service des travaux publics, from the awarding of the contract until October 1, 2028.
Emco Corporation (Québec) will supply the fire hydrants for an estimated amount of $374,955 before taxes.
Stelem, a division of Emco Corporation (Vaudreuil-Dorion), will supply the fire hydrant parts for an estimated amount of $371,356.75 before taxes.
The net cost to the City is estimated at $783,534.05.
The contract can be renewed twice for 12 months, with an annual price adjustment for inflation.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
Three companies submitted bids for the hydrants and two for the parts; the lowest compliant prices were selected.
The Charlesbourg borough council is giving City managers the power to authorize the occupation of public property, instead of deciding each case itself.
This applies to public land, sidewalks, streets and lanes in the borough, both above and below ground.

For temporary occupations, the decision rests with the director general, an assistant director general, the director of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets, the director of the Division des activités et de l'expertise immobilières, and a section director of that division.

For permanent occupations, only the officials of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets and of the Division des activités et de l'expertise immobilières can grant authorization.

These managers set the conditions and the rent, may require a specific way of carrying out the work and specific materials, and may revoke an authorization after giving the owner written notice one month in advance.
Permanent authorizations must be reported to the executive committee every quarter, including the nature of the occupation, the name of the beneficiary and the amount of the rent.
The City explains that requests related to real estate transactions have increased a lot and that it wants to standardize practices across the agglomeration.

The City supports an application made to the Commission de protection du territoire agricole du Québec (CPTAQ) to use lot 2 162 740, in the Aéroport neighbourhood (Cap-Rouge–Laurentien district), for purposes other than agriculture.
The purpose of the application: to allow the construction of a tourist accommodation establishment, a use already permitted in this zone.
The area concerned is 8,376.3 square metres (0.8376 hectare), along boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel.
The land was already used for commercial purposes: the building that housed a tourist accommodation establishment and a restaurant was demolished there in 2025.
The analysis concludes that there would be little or no impact on farming activities in the area; there is no animal production facility nearby according to the assessment roll.
The land is served only by the water supply system; the final decision rests with the CPTAQ.
The City is appointing four trustees to represent it on the pension committee of the Régime de retraite des policiers et policières de la Ville de Québec.
The people appointed are Véronique Fortier and Jonathan Maheux (Service des ressources humaines), France Bilodeau (consultant) and Andrée-Anne Verreault (Service des finances).
Their term runs from February 25, 2026 to February 23, 2029.
This appointment replaces the trustees whose term ends on February 25, 2026.
The plan's by-law requires the City to appoint four trustees, normally for three years.
The document does not indicate any financial impact.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 1550, avenue Nicolet, in the Maizerets neighbourhood (Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The owner will be allowed to build an extension in the back yard with a height of 4.75 metres, while the planning by-law requires 6 metres.
A solarium will be demolished to make room for the extension.
According to the analysis, requiring 6 metres would force the construction of an extension much taller than the existing house.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted in favour of the request on May 26, 2026, unanimously.
The decision states that the exemption has no impact on neighbouring buildings.
The City is officially setting the boundaries of the chemin Sainte-Foy area affected by infrastructure and redevelopment work in 2026.
Businesses located in this area will be able to apply for financial assistance provided under the support program tied to major work.
The work runs approximately from April 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026.
The 2026 fiscal year is the one that counts for assessing whether businesses in the designated area are eligible.
A plan attached to the order sets the boundaries of the designated area and the area of influence, near autoroute Henri-IV and route de l'Église.
To be recognized, the work must last at least three consecutive months and seriously disrupt traffic.
The City wants to obtain a permanent servitude (right of use) over part of a lane in the Limoilou neighbourhood, between rue des Pins Est and rue des Peupliers Est, near 1re Avenue.
The servitude covers about 251 square metres and will be used to move public utility conduits and networks for the TramCité tramway project.
The City will first try to reach a negotiated agreement with the owner; if that fails, it will proceed by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques will be able to drop the proceedings if the project no longer needs this servitude.
The Division de l'arpentage will prepare the plans and the technical description of the land involved.
The money comes from agglomeration loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the structuring public transit network.
The lane is not listed on the assessment roll, so no value is given in the document.
The City is appointing four people to represent it on the retirement committee of the Régime de retraite des pompiers de la Ville de Québec.
They are Dominic Stephenson and Martin Pelletier (Service des ressources humaines), France Bilodeau (consultant) and Anne Mainguy (Service des finances).
Their term runs from February 25, 2026 to February 23, 2029.
These appointments replace the current terms, which end on February 25, 2026.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City is authorizing five people to accompany the mayor of Québec on a mission to Edmonton and Calgary, from March 16 to 20, 2026 (or on another date set by the organizers).
They are councillors Raymond Poirier and Jean-Luc Lavoie and Ms. Isabelle Dubois, Ms. Joëlle Godbout and Ms. Catherine Labonté, or their replacements.
The City is authorizing an expense of $16,000 for air and ground transportation and accommodation costs, reimbursed upon presentation of supporting documents.

The funding comes from two departments: $12,800 from the Service de la coordination stratégique et relations internationales and $3,200 from the Service des relations citoyennes et des communications.

The purpose of the mission is to observe how Edmonton (Valley Line West) and Calgary (Green Line) manage their structuring transit projects, and to exchange on land use planning, housing, homelessness, urban safety and downtown vitality.
Québec and Calgary have been twin cities since 1956; the trip is meant to lead to an agreement on greater collaboration between the two cities.
A difference of no more than 10% from the authorized amount will be accepted without further authorization.
The City is paying out $79,430 in grants to eight organizations, under the Entente de développement culturel with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.

Seven projects involve showcasing religious heritage: tours, concerts and activities at the cathédrale Holy Trinity ($12,000), the église de Saint-Dominique ($12,000), the Monastère des Augustines ($11,500), the Pôle culturel du Monastère des Ursulines ($8,750), the Basilique-cathédrale Notre-Dame-de-Québec and Notre-Dame-des-Victoires ($7,500), the église unie Chalmers-Wesley ($7,000) and the églises de Saint-Michel-de-Sillery and Saint-Charles-Garnier ($680).
Most of these activities take place from June to September or October 2026; some are free, including the Wednesday noon-hour concerts at Chalmers-Wesley.
The église de Saint-Dominique will also produce a virtual tour available at all times.

The Maison Léon-Provancher is receiving $20,000 to coordinate, in 2026, the network of the 12 heritage houses owned by the City, including the Villa Bagatelle, the Moulin des Jésuites and the îlot des Palais.
The total cost of the supported projects comes to $267,797; the City's share comes from a loan by-law ($20,000) and from culture and heritage transfers ($59,430).
The City is awarding GFL Environmental inc. a contract for the rental of containers and the transport of sand, waste and rags, for an estimated amount of $862,372.17 before taxes.
The contract covers the period from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029, with an option for two 12-month renewals indexed to the Consumer Price Index.
The watertight containers are used to collect sand for delivery to the landfill site and to transport waste and rags to the Complexe de valorisation énergétique or the landfill site.
The net expense for the agglomeration is estimated at $905,382.98 after recovery of the QST.
Only one bid was received; after negotiation, the supplier revised its price downward, to 4.6% below the City's estimate ($903,574.44).
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets by the competent authorities.
The City wants to acquire a strip of land of about 2.70 square metres along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The acquisition will be used to widen the 1re Avenue right-of-way in order to build the public transit service there.
The purchase can be made by mutual agreement with the owner or through expropriation; the owner has already been informed of the process and of a contact person at the City.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings and to withdraw from them if the project no longer needs the land.
The entire property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $224,000, which is $677.97 per square metre.
The funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to building the structuring public transit network.
The decision must be made by the Québec urban agglomeration council.
The Ville de Québec is submitting 11 applications for financial assistance to the Quebec FIERH program, which funds water supply and sewer work tied to housing construction.
The program reimburses 40% of eligible costs, with a possible increase for projects tied to affordable housing.
The call for projects ends on September 18, 2026 and the program ends on December 31, 2032.

Projects submitted: sewer on avenue Thornhill, réservoir Vaillancourt and booster pump (Beauport), sewers on rue De Brugnon and rue Paquin, water main on chemin Sainte-Foy (from route de La Suète to rue Jean-Noël), réservoir and Saint-Félix booster pumping station (Cap-Rouge).

Other projects submitted: mains on boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, storm sewer toward the rivière Saint-Charles (Pierre-Bertrand corridor), main between boulevard Valcartier and Val-Bélair, raw water main at the usine Sainte-Foy, street opening at 1619, chemin Sainte-Foy, and modernization of the East and West wastewater treatment plants.
Submitting the applications has no financial impact; for each project selected, an agreement will have to be signed afterwards.
The City is awarding hourly-paid tree care work to three companies: pruning and routine or emergency work, with labour and equipment included, until April 18, 2027.
Services d'Arbres Dufour et Lapierre inc. (Lac-Beauport) gets the East ($403,510) and West ($403,510) sectors, as well as work related to insects and diseases ($404,660).
Élagage RSA inc. (Stoneham-et-Tewkesbury) gets the Centre sector ($493,421.25), construction sites ($368,465) and areas along waterways and wooded areas ($436,518.75).
7762763 Canada inc. (Saint-Georges) will handle trees near the electricity distribution network for $242,442.70.
The net expense is estimated at $2,889,810.02, subject to approval of the 2027 budget.
The contracts can be renewed twice for 12 months, with a price increase based on the Consumer Price Index.
One bidder was set aside for a missing administrative document; another was disqualified for lot 7 because it had reached its capacity limit.
On May 17, 2026, the director of the Service de police suspended a constable from his duties, with pay, because facts brought to his attention require an investigation.
The executive committee is maintaining this suspension with pay until the City's authorities make a final decision.
The collective agreement allows the director to suspend an employee with pay for a maximum of 30 days, while the employee's file is being reviewed.
The constable cannot be reassigned to other police duties until the investigation is finished or unless no measure is taken against him.
The document does not mention the constable's identity or the nature of the alleged facts.
The City is borrowing $1,400,000 for road safety work on streets that fall under the agglomeration of Québec.

The money will be used in particular to build new sidewalks and curbs, to install intelligent transportation systems, lighting, traffic lights and signage, and to put in place measures to slow down traffic.
The project covers the City's entire territory within its agglomeration powers.
The loan will be repaid over ten years, out of the City's general revenues.
An amount of $140,000 (10% of the expenditure) is taken from the general fund and will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The funds are provided for in years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 capital works program.
Grants from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable may reduce the amount borrowed.
The City of Québec is giving $24,600 to the Maison Michel-Sarrazin, a non-profit palliative and end-of-life care facility located in Québec.
The funding follows a request submitted by the Maison itself.
The money comes from the operating budget of the City's Direction générale, with no federal or provincial contribution.
The Maison Michel-Sarrazin is recognized by the Government of Québec for its care, teaching and research missions, which extend beyond the region.
The City had already granted it $23,700 in 2021 and $24,600 in 2022, 2024 and 2025.
The executive committee approved the decision on March 18, 2026.
The City is giving $5,000 to the organization Projet Intervention Prostitution Québec inc. (PIPQ), located at 535, rue des Oblats.
The money will fund a pilot project providing veterinary care for the animals of people in precarious situations who are supported by the organization.
According to the document, these people cannot afford to have their animal treated, which leaves health problems untreated and can lead to overpopulation.
The project also aims to preserve the bond between the person and their animal, presented as a protective factor for mental health.
The organization will have to mention the City's contribution in its publications and provide an accounting of the funds: activities carried out, financial report and proof of visibility.
First-year needs were estimated based on the demand already observed in the field; other needs (boarding, vaccination) will be assessed during the year.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire, and falls under urban agglomeration jurisdiction.
The City is changing the zoning at 2538, chemin Sainte-Foy, in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood, to allow a medical aesthetic care clinic.
The building currently houses an aesthetics training school; the applicant wants to add a centre for aesthetic and medical aesthetic care.
Zone 32039Hb is changing from a mainly residential designation (Hb) to a mixed neighbourhood designation (Mb).
Health care establishments without lodging are now allowed there, with a maximum of 200 square metres of floor area per establishment.
A personal aesthetic care service becomes a specifically authorized use, without opening the zone to all retail businesses.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; the conseil de quartier de la Cité-Universitaire must hold a public consultation meeting.
Interested persons have seven days after that meeting to submit their comments in writing.
The City is giving the company 14892437 Canada inc. more time to build on a piece of land it sold to the company in the parc industriel de Beauport, secteur nord.
The start of construction, which was supposed to take place within 24 months of the sale, is pushed back to no later than March 12, 2028.
The completion of the work, planned within 30 months, is pushed back to no later than September 12, 2028.
The company explains that it could not start on time, since a large part of its exports go to the United States in a context of a tariff war.
All the buyer's other obligations set out in the deed of sale stay the same.
The company says it still intends to carry out its project; the document does not mention any financial impact.
The City wants to acquire, by agreement or by expropriation, a piece of land and an easement along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The land in question is about 40.40 square metres and will be used to widen the 1re Avenue right-of-way.
The easement, which is permanent, covers about 81.80 square metres and will allow public utility conduits and networks to be moved.
The owner has been notified of the acquisition process and of the next steps, and a City contact person has been assigned to them.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings and to discontinue them if the project no longer needs the land or the easement.
The land as a whole, at its greatest extent, is entered on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $360,000, or $322.87 per square metre.
The funds come from the agglomeration loan by-law related to the Réseau structurant de transport en commun.
The City is approving a list of eight companies deemed qualified to outfit cargo vans (utility vehicles) in its vehicle fleet.

The selected companies: Gaévan Aménagement, Précisions Provençal, Remorques MMG, Drive Products, Fourgons Élite (9081-0060 Québec inc.), Zone Technologie Électronique, P.S. Métal and Les Fourgons Rive-Sud.
These vans are used in particular by Travaux publics, Gestion des immeubles and Traitement des eaux.
With this list, the City will be able to award contracts directly to these suppliers, below the threshold that requires a public call for tenders, rotating among them.
The City explains that past calls for tenders in this field attracted few bidders and that delivery times did not meet its needs.
According to the document, the approach aims to speed up the replacement of vans at the end of their useful life, reduce maintenance costs and increase competition in future calls for tenders.
The decision summary does not indicate any amount or financial impact.
The City of Québec is giving up to $350,000 to the organization Capitale Numérique.
The money will be used to hold the 2026 and 2027 editions of two events: the Rendez-vous numérique (April) and Interface Québec (May).
The project costs $2,113,000 in total: $1,127,500 comes from ticket sales and $635,500 from private partners.
Together, the two events bring in more than 2,500 participants from about 950 businesses and involve more than 200 volunteers each year.
Capitale Numérique, created in 2024 after Québec numérique ceased operations, has its head office in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The grant comes from the Soutien aux organismes d'entrepreneuriat stream of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, funded by the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale.
This decision falls to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The Ville de Québec is paying up to $900,000 to Québec International to fund the operations and mission of the Le CAMP incubator in 2026.
The money comes from the Soutien aux organismes d'entrepreneuriat component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, a fund delegated by the Government of Quebec.
The project costs $1,125,906 in total: $900,000 from the City and $225,906 from private partners.
Le CAMP, located in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough, offers workspaces, support and mentorship to technology start-ups.
Targets for 2026: 140 businesses supported, 4,500 hours of support and 600 jobs created or maintained.
The grant is higher than those of 2025 ($827,000) and 2023 ($320,000) for projects related to Le CAMP.
The organization will have to report back through an activity report.
The City is authorizing the demolition of the heritage house at 12 841, boulevard Valcartier, built between 1929 and 1932.
The Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec made this decision on June 18, 2026, unanimously, following a public meeting.
The Commission notes the building's low heritage interest, its poor construction quality and the many defects identified by experts.
The demolition is conditional: the replacement project (application 20251006-051) will have to be adjusted according to the Commission's recommendations.
The replacement project would add housing units in the area.
No one requested a review within the 30-day period, and the urban agglomeration council is waiving its power to overturn the decision, shortening the 90-day period.
The demolition authorization certificate can then be issued.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 6055, avenue Doucet, in the Saint-Rodrigue district, in Charlesbourg.
The owner may expand their house while leaving a rear setback of 2.10 metres instead of the 7.5 metres normally required.
The exemption also allows part of the outdoor staircase, a spa and a propane tank to be located in the front yard.
Condition to be met: install a fence or plant dense evergreen vegetation, and maintain it, so that the spa and the tank are not visible from the street.
The project includes adding an attached garage and enlarging the living areas; the irregular shape of the lot and of the building justifies the exemption.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour on February 4, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 11125, rue du Foyer, in the Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The shed already built on the property is 2 metres from the front lot line, while the planning by-law requires 6 metres.
The exemption makes this shed deemed compliant, without the owner having to move it.
City staff recommended refusing it, considering that the shed could be placed in the back yard in accordance with the standards.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme instead recommended granting the exemption, unanimously, on February 25, 2026.
The document notes that the shed was built in 2024 and that no complaints from neighbours have been received.
The City is awarding Béton sur mesure inc. the contract to supply, deliver and unload cement concrete, non-shrink backfill concrete and small-quantity concrete for the West sector (lot 1).
The contract is worth $432,075 before taxes, from the award date until March 31, 2027, with two possible 12-month renewals indexed to the CPI.
The concrete will be used for work to repair streets, sidewalks and water and sewer systems at various worksites in the city.
The net expense is estimated at $453,624.74 once the QST refund is taken into account.
Only one bid was received for lot 1: at $432,075 after negotiation, it exceeds the requesting department's estimate ($263,358.90) by 64.1%.
The City explains this gap by the absence of bids from its usual suppliers in a context of high demand and by the bidder's smaller economies of scale.
The contract depends on the approval of the amounts in the 2027 budget; lot 2 (small quantities) was awarded separately through delegation of powers.
The City approves the plans for the construction of a 3-storey, 18-unit building at 2280 and 2290, avenue Bergemont, in the Maizerets neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The approval covers the building's exterior appearance and how it fits in with neighbouring buildings.

One condition is imposed: completely replace the fibre cement siding in the colour "Brume légère" or "Gris nocturne" on the front of the building with Windsor-coloured brick (or the equivalent), already used on the rest of the front.
Reason for the condition: to reduce the number of different sidings and give more space to brick, so the building fits in with the neighbourhood.
If the applicant does not meet this condition, the application will be put on hold and the applicant will have to present another project at a later meeting.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme adopted this recommendation unanimously on April 7, 2026.
The executive committee takes note of the quarterly report on transactions of the Fonds Vision (Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale), for July 1 to September 30, 2025.
The fund's balance was $3,410,939.30 as of June 30, 2025.
Support for entrepreneurship totals $1,064,000: about 40 businesses receive amounts ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 (food, manufacturing, video games, clean technologies, etc.).
Support for growth and productivity totals $712,308, paid to stores, restaurants and hotels, mostly in blocks of $50,000.

The Plan commerce funds activities of commercial development corporations and business people's associations: pedestrian street of Faubourg Saint-Jean ($25,000), Grande Allée (2 x $25,000), Saint-Sauveur ($30,000), rue Notre-Dame in L'Ancienne-Lorette ($76,212), Saint-Sacrement ($12,000), Campanile ($12,164), Québec Table Gourmande ($50,000).
Québec International receives $827,000 to maintain the spaces of the incubator-accelerator Le CAMP in 2025.
Support for innovation totals $181,845: $90,000 to Plastique Multifab and $91,845 to Sabotage Studio.
The Ville de Québec is accepting financial assistance of up to $50,000 from Arbres Canada, the organization that manages Hydro-Québec's Fonds de verdissement.
The money will be used to plant 154 trees in 2026, divided into 11 lots spread across the city's territory.
The plantings will take place in different settings: streets, parks, downtown and suburbs.
The project tests tree species that are little present in the municipal inventory or that come from warmer zones, with follow-up on successes and failures.
The grant can cover up to 100% of the project's eligible costs.
The amount will be recorded under item 74020 of the 2026-2035 investment program.
The City is banning parking on the south side of rue Collin, in the Val-Bélair neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The ban applies over 35 metres starting from boulevard Pie-XI Sud, heading west, on the section that runs to rue des Citronniers.
Two on-street parking spaces are being removed.
The change is meant to make it easier to enter and exit the private driveway of the daycare located at 1155, boulevard Pie-XI Sud.
The file started with a request from a resident; the roadway of rue Collin is 9 metres wide and parking there was not regulated.
The City will acquire, either by agreement or by expropriation, two small pieces of land along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The two parcels are about 3.90 and 1.30 square metres and will be used to widen the 1re Avenue right-of-way.
The City is also acquiring a permanent public utility easement of about 80.90 square metres on the same lot, in order to move conduits and networks.
The owner has been informed of the process, the next steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
The land, in its largest area, is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $1,280,000, or $581.58 per square metre.
The Service des affaires juridiques will handle the proceedings and may withdraw from them if the project no longer needs this land.
The money comes from the agglomeration's loan by-law for the structuring public transit network.

The Ville de Québec is entrusting the management and upkeep of the premises and equipment of the Mycélium food incubator, at the Grand Marché de Québec, to the Réseau des entreprises en nutrition santé du Québec (RENSQ).
The agreement runs from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027, for $406,380 (plus GST and QST).
The premises covered include a 1,500-square-foot kitchen, a storage area and a market-testing area, intended for food processing businesses.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders, as the law allows this with a non-profit organization.

The funding comes from the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale ($172,000 in 2026, $153,104 in 2027) and from the budget of the Service du développement économique ($43,000 in 2026, $38,276 in 2027).
The 2027 portion depends on the approval of that year's budget.
The agreement follows the previous one, which ended on December 31, 2025.
The City is banning parking on rue de la Plage, on both sides, over 20 metres starting from rue Alfred going east (arrondissement de Beauport).
Six parking spaces will be removed.
The request came from a resident who reported safety problems at the intersection of rue de la Plage and rue Alfred.
Parked vehicles made turning difficult: rue de la Plage is 9 metres wide, while rue Alfred is only 6 metres wide.
The City notes that snow removal was also more difficult at this spot in winter.
According to the document, residents in the area have access to private parking.
The conseil d'arrondissement de Beauport adopted ordinance O-521 on August 27, 2026.
The City is approving a minor exemption at 400, 3e Avenue, in Vieux-Limoilou (Limoilou district, La Cité-Limoilou borough).
The ventilation equipment will be allowed to extend up to 1.5 metres instead of the maximum of 0.75 metre set out in the borough's planning by-law.
The request concerns the chimney for a restaurant's range hood, which is needed as part of work to enlarge the building.
According to the analysis in the file, meeting the standard would have required moving exterior walls and redesigning the interior layout of the housing units planned for the upper floors.

The Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec asked that the ventilation equipment not be visible from the public roadway or that it be concealed; the proposed location meets this condition.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on May 26, 2026, and the borough council granted it.
The Ville de Québec will pay a grant of no more than $150,000 to the company Zilux inc., which makes lighting and street furniture in the parc industriel Armand-Viau.
The money will be used to sell Zilux products outside Quebec, first in Canada and North America, then in Europe.
The project costs $750,000 in total: $150,000 from the City, $150,000 from the shareholders, a $300,000 loan from the Banque de développement du Canada and a $150,000 loan from Desjardins.
Zilux plans to create 6 jobs: 2 in sales, 1 in engineering and 3 to 5 in production.

On the schedule: hiring of two salespeople between February and April 2026, a new communications plan in March and April, a promotional tool called « Zilux mobile » in April and May, then trade shows and business development in 2026-2027.
The grant is non-refundable and covers at most half of the eligible expenses, according to the rules of the Capitale-Innovation component.
A review committee recommended the project on December 9, 2025; the decision rests with the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The Ville de Québec is giving $60,000 to Université Laval for archaeology research, for the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
The grant is divided into $30,000 in scholarships and wages for students and $30,000 in technical support for the field-school laboratory.
The City is also providing technical services (fencing, trailer, container, etc.) worth up to $15,000.
The digs will take place in May 2026 at the site of "la ferme de Cadet," at 1460, boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, on a property belonging to the cimetière Saint-Charles, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The cost of the grant is shared equally between the City and the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
Université Laval estimates its own contribution at $95,000, mainly for teaching staff.
The agreement also covers the conservation of the artifacts found and the sharing of the research results.
The City is lowering the speed limit from 50 km/h to 40 km/h on rue Provancher, between rue du Domaine and boulevard de la Chaudière.
The new limit applies at all times, in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge (Cap-Rouge–Laurentien district).
According to the decision summary, the change will apply to all of rue Provancher, from côte de Cap-Rouge to rue du Domaine.
The City explains that the school zone has been extended to rue Augustin-Bourbeau and that the number of housing units has increased since 2021.
The decision is based on an eight-criteria analysis (type of area, number of lanes, road width, density of human activity, etc.).
No financial impact is indicated in the decision summary.

The Ville de Québec will use the rates and tariffs of the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable to have its bulk materials (sand, stone, asphalt, etc.) transported from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
The expense is estimated at $4,172,700 (plus GST and QST); the net expense is estimated at $4,380,813.41.
The Ministère's rates are going up by 0.86% compared with 2025, with an adjustment based on the price of fuel.

The work will go to truckers registered in the Registre du camionnage en vrac, through four brokers: Transporteurs en vrac (Région 03), Chauveau-Québec, Sainte-Foy and the Association des Transporteurs en vrac de Montmorency.
No call for tenders is required: the law allows these contracts to be entered into directly through a holder of a brokerage permit.
Bulk trucking during snow removal is not covered by this decision.
The amounts remain conditional on the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The City is proposing to permanently allow the sale and rental of motorcycles, ATVs, snowmobiles and similar vehicles in the premises at 2350, boulevard Sainte-Anne, in the Maizerets neighbourhood.
The business Gaetan Moto inc. occupies these premises under a temporary permission obtained in 2021, which expires in July 2026.
The new owner of the business wants to continue operating and is considering expanding into the neighbouring premises in the medium term.
According to the document, no complaints have been received about the business since 2021.
The conseil de quartier de Maizerets will be consulted and will hold the public consultation meeting; interested people will have 7 days after the meeting to send their comments in writing.
The by-law contains no provisions that can be subject to a referendum.

The City is appointing the members of two committees that recommend financial support for businesses: the committee of the Fonds local d'investissement and that of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030.
The terms begin on April 1, 2026 and last 24 months, and can be renewed.
On the Fonds local d'investissement committee, the five current members are reappointed, with Line Lacroix as chair and Suzanne Gagnon as substitute chair.
On the Vision entrepreneuriale committee, the membership changes: Jacques Desmeules and Rémy Gauthier stay on, and Martin Larrivée, Olivier Delisle and Patricia Kebbe are added.
The Fonds local d'investissement lends businesses up to $300,000 for start-up, growth and business succession.
The Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030 provides support of up to one million dollars per year; its committee reviews contributions of more than $25,000.
The members were chosen following an online call for applications, assessed on expertise and on equity, diversity and inclusion criteria.

The City is authorizing an employee of the Service des travaux publics to take part in a mission to the Lycée des métiers des travaux publics in Bruay-la-Buissière, France, from September 26 to October 4, 2026.
It is authorizing an expense of $3,782 for this participation, paid out of the operating budget of the Service des travaux publics.
The expenses will be reimbursed upon submission of receipts, with a tolerated difference of no more than 10% of the authorized amount.
The mission is organized by TPQuébec, which is developing a provincial training plan in maintenance and public works; representatives from Montréal are also invited.
On the program: presentation of the Lycée's programs, meetings with its partners, a visit to a construction site and to a public works company.
The City says it wants to improve the training of its manual workers, whom it finds harder to recruit and retain; it created its own training centre (CFTP) in 2023.
The City officially designates the boulevard René-Lévesque area, between avenue Belvédère and avenue Turnbull, as a zone affected by major infrastructure work in 2026.
Businesses located in this area can therefore apply for the financial assistance provided under the support program tied to the TramCité project work sites.
The work runs approximately from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The 2026 fiscal year is the one used to determine whether businesses and their establishments are eligible.
A plan attached to the order sets the boundaries of the designated area and of the area of influence, around boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest.
To be recognized, the work must last at least three consecutive months and seriously disrupt traffic.
The Beauport borough council is ending the process to amend the planning by-law for zone 55119Pa, at 3325-3327, rue Loyola (Vieux-Moulin neighbourhood).
This amendment, adopted as a draft on June 10, 2025, would have allowed housing in the zone and adjusted the height as well as the side and rear setbacks.
It is no longer needed: on May 19, 2026, the city council instead authorized the real estate project by resolution, attaching specific conditions to it, under a Quebec housing act.
The project in question calls for a four-storey residential building with about 45 housing units on part of lot 5 474 646, at 3325-3327, rue Loyola.
A public consultation meeting was held on May 8, 2025, and an online written consultation ran from May 9 to 15, 2025.
The Ville de Québec will receive $30,000 from the organization Sentier Transcanadien for the upkeep of multi-purpose trails in 2025-2026.
The money covers routine and periodic upkeep of the Corridor des Cheminots and part of the Corridor du Littoral, which are part of the Route verte and the Sentier transcanadien.
The contribution matches 16.67% of the upkeep costs paid by the City, up to a maximum of $30,000.
This amount is in addition to the funding from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable (Véloce III program) and does not affect the City's eligibility for that program.
The revenue will be paid into the City's general fund.
The City is asking the Gouvernement du Québec for authorization to enter into the agreement; Mayor Bruno Marchand and city clerk Julien Lefrançois are authorized to sign it.
The agreement ends on March 31, 2026, unless it is extended.

The City is officially setting the boundaries of the section of rue Saint-Vallier Ouest affected by infrastructure and redevelopment work, for the purposes of a financial assistance program for businesses.
The work covered runs from approximately April 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026 inclusively.
Businesses and establishments located in the "designated area" may apply for financial assistance for the 2026 fiscal year.
A plan attached to the order sets the boundaries of the designated area and the area of influence, in the neighbourhood surrounding Saint-Vallier Ouest, Marie-de-l'Incarnation and Charest Ouest.
To be recognized, the work must last at least three consecutive months and cause a major obstruction to traffic.
The program also applies to certain organizations that promote commercial streets, in the context of the TramCité project.
The Commission consultative pour une ville inclusive is changing its name and becomes the "Commission consultative pour le vivre-ensemble".

Its mandate is being revised to align with the Plan d'action en développement social 2025-2030: recommendations on social cohesion, collaboration on carrying out the plan, and follow-up on initiatives under way.
The Commission will go from 10 to 12 citizen members, recruited in particular from the social, community, institutional, health, research and social innovation sectors.
Recruitment will follow principles of diversity, inclusion and parity, local roots, citizen expertise and commitment.
The Service des relations citoyennes et des communications is responsible for relaunching the Commission and recruiting the citizen members, whose appointments will be proposed at a later sitting.
Three elected officials have sat on it since the November 2, 2025 elections: Claude Lavoie (chair), Clément Bourdeau and Marie-Pierre Boucher.
City council adopted the decision on March 10, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption for a future house at 3039, rue William-Stuart, in the Saint-Louis neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The building may be set 4.8 metres back from the front property line (measured at the garage) instead of the 6.0 metres required by the planning by-law.
The front wall of the main building will be 5.7 metres from the front property line.
The closer placement is explained by a sewer pipe in the back yard and a no-build easement, which reduce the buildable area of the lot.
According to the analysis, a front wall at 5.7 metres matches how the other buildings in the area are placed.
The planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme) recommended the application unanimously on March 10, 2026; the borough council granted it (resolution CA3-2026-0052).
The City of Québec is borrowing $85,000,000 by issuing bonds dated March 24, 2026.
The Minister of Finance awarded the contract to BMO Nesbitt Burns inc. on March 12, 2026, the lowest bid among seven received.
The real cost of the loan is 3.88019%, with interest paid twice a year and an average term of 6 years and 1 month.
The principal is repaid from 2027 to 2031, plus one portion in 2036; two refinancings are planned: $22,798,000 in the 5th year and $23,822,000 in the 10th year.
Of this amount, $58,498,100 goes to new work and $26,501,900 is used to refinance earlier loans.
The executive committee takes note of the report filed by the treasurer.
The City is authorizing spending of $800,000 in 2026 to detect and replace lead drinking water service lines, both public and private.
The amount covers the work, professional and technical services contracts, hiring staff, buying buildings and easements, and paying grants to owners.
To pay for this spending, the City is borrowing $800,000, to be repaid over fifteen years out of its general revenues.
The City is taking $80,000 (10% of the total) from its general fund to start before the by-law comes into force; that fund will be repaid afterwards.
The project affects the entire city territory, under its local (proximity) powers.
The City may acquire the land and easements needed for the work by agreement or by expropriation.
The City is refusing the minor exemption request filed for 745, rue Léonard, in the Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy neighbourhood (arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).

The owner wanted to expand the house on the side, leaving a side setback of 2.0 metres instead of the required 4.0 metres, and a parking space extending 4.0 metres into the front instead of 3.0 metres.

Reasons for the refusal: a project that complies with the by-law is still possible, the lot has no particular feature that prevents it, and going from 4.0 to 2.0 metres departs from the standards too much.
According to the analysis, the applicant could expand the building by about 2.0 metres toward the side rather than the 4.0 metres wanted.
The analysis notes that the 4.0-metre setback is not respected by a large percentage of the buildings in the area and suggests reviewing the area's siting standards as part of an overall review.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had recommended the refusal on January 13, 2026; the borough council's decision is signed February 9, 2026.
The City is authorizing spending of $500,000 to protect and enhance natural areas and urban woodlands, as part of its Stratégie en faveur de la biodiversité.
The money will be used to buy land, to carry out planting, reforestation and restoration of natural areas, as well as studies, inventories and analyses.
The amount also covers hiring staff, professional services contracts, equipment, promotional activities and the payment of grants and financial contributions.
The City is borrowing the $500,000 and will repay it over fifteen years; the funds are planned from 2026 to 2028 in the capital works program.
The projects can be carried out anywhere in the territory under the City's jurisdiction.
The City will be able to acquire the necessary land by agreement or by expropriation.
An amount of $50,000 (10% of the spending) is being taken from the general fund and will be repaid to it when the by-law comes into force.
The City is allowing a height of 34 metres instead of the 33-metre maximum for a proposed commercial building at 310, boulevard Charest Est, in Saint-Roch.
The building would be used for tourist accommodation and would replace an outdoor parking lot.
The height is measured from rue Notre-Dame-des-Anges, the lowest street around the property, which explains why the maximum is exceeded.
Exceeding the maximum makes it possible to line the building up with the neighbouring one and to provide ceilings of about 2.44 metres (8 feet) per floor.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme was in favour by a majority, and the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec also gave a favourable opinion.
The decision rests with the La Cité-Limoilou borough council.
The City is awarding Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. (Mont-Saint-Grégoire) the planting of about 2,400 container-grown trees in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The contract is worth $290,970 before taxes; the net expense is estimated at $305,482.13.
The work runs from the date the contract is awarded until December 6, 2026.
The goal is to increase the canopy (tree cover) in Charlesbourg.
The contract covers labour, equipment, vehicles and landscaping materials.
Eight companies submitted bids; the lowest bid is 45.3% below the City's estimate ($532,079.55).
The executive committee adopted the decision on April 29, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0544).
The City is granting a minor exemption for 520, 68e Rue Ouest, in district 4-5 of Charlesbourg (Saint-Rodrigue district).
The combined width of the side yards may be 4.5 metres instead of the 5.5 metres required by the borough's planning by-law.
The owner wants to convert the existing carport into an attached garage and to enlarge the basement of the house underneath this garage.
Without the exemption, the project could not go ahead as proposed: the extension would have to be made smaller, and the roof and structure of the carport would have to be demolished.
According to the analysis, since the extension is underground and in the same location as the carport built in 1977, it adds no constraint for the neighbour.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme was unanimously in favour on August 12, 2026; the decision rests with the borough council on August 31, 2026.

The City is paying an additional $28,676.67 (before GST and QST) to the organization Centre Durocher inc. for supervision of the Centre communautaire Édouard-Lavergne and Parc Durocher, in La Cité-Limoilou.
This addition raises the contract from $78,005.79 to $106,682.46 before taxes.
The money pays for 1,297 additional hours of supervision, at $22.11 an hour: the agreement provided for 3,180 hours, but 4,477 were needed.
The City explains the overrun by an increase in bookings at the Centre Édouard-Lavergne and by an initial estimate of hours that was too low.
The renewed agreement covers the period from May 1, 2025 to April 30, 2026.
The net cost to the City, once the QST is recovered, is $30,106.92, taken from the budget of the Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 5250, avenue du Costebelle, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood (Arrondissement des Rivières).
The detached single-family home will be allowed to keep a rear setback of 8 metres, whereas the planning by-law requires 9.
The owner wants to sell the house and bring this non-compliant rear setback into compliance; the house was built around 1971.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted in favour of the request on August 3, 2026, unanimously.
According to the analysis, no complaints have been received about this property, and the City is looking into the possibility of reducing the setbacks to 7.5 metres in this zone.
The borough council made its decision on August 24, 2026.

The City is granting $170,000 in support to the Rendez-vous naval de Québec for its 2026 edition: $70,000 in cash, up to $95,000 in free municipal services and up to $5,000 in the purchase of goods and services.
The event will be held from July 23 to 26, 2026, on the docks of the Port de Québec, with ship visits and themed activities.
The services provided free of charge come from public works and the Service de police, in the form of work time and equipment loans that are normally billed.
The cash grant represents 6.5% of the event's budget, estimated at $1,080,000.
The support is conditional on a sufficient contribution from the other partners for the event to take place.
Payment is spread over two years: $63,000 in 2026 and $7,000 in 2027, the latter amount depending on the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The organization will have to provide the City with a complete report no later than 90 days after the end of the event.
The City is adopting a by-law that changes its land-use planning rules for shorelines, littoral zones, flood zones and watercourse mobility zones.
These changes follow the coming into force, on March 1, 2026, of the Government of Québec's new regulatory framework, which replaces the transitional regime from 2022.

The City is removing its standards that are less strict than the government's and is keeping complementary rules, in particular the requirement to maintain a vegetated strip when the soil is cultivated in a shoreline area.

The by-law sets rules for the construction, moving, enlargement and rebuilding of buildings in a shoreline area or a shoreline protection strip, and prohibits rebuilding a building that has been destroyed or has become dangerous following a flood, submersion or watercourse mobility.
It also tightens the rules for accessory buildings in flood zones and for swimming pools in flood zones of high or very high class, high-velocity zones, ice-jam zones and short-term mobility zones.

The terms « ligne des hautes eaux » (high-water mark) and « plaine inondable » (floodplain) are being replaced by « limite du littoral » (littoral boundary) and « zone inondable » (flood zone) in the by-laws.
A public consultation meeting must be held; the by-law cannot be subject to a referendum.
The City wants to permanently allow the sale and rental of motorcycles, ATVs, snowmobiles and similar vehicles at 2350, boulevard Sainte-Anne, in the Maizerets neighbourhood.
The business Gaetan Moto inc. has occupied these premises since 2021 under a temporary permission that expires in July 2026.
The City says it has received no complaints about the business since 2021.
The occupancy must begin within three years after the by-law comes into force, otherwise the authorization lapses.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.

The conseil de quartier de Maizerets will be invited to give its opinion and to hold a public consultation meeting; interested persons will have seven days after the meeting to send in their written comments.
No active participation measures are planned, with the City citing the already existing use and the absence of complaints.
The City is authorizing an ExpoCité account manager to travel to Windsor, Ontario, for the annual conference of the Canadian Association of Exposition Management, from June 15 to 17, 2026.
ExpoCité will be there both as a participant and as an exhibitor, with a promotional booth to showcase its facilities.
The authorized expense totals $3,396, reimbursable upon submission of supporting documents.
This amount covers registration, the booth space, the flight, accommodation for the nights of June 14 to 17, and per diems.
The money comes from ExpoCité's operating budget.
A difference of no more than 10% of the authorized amount will be accepted without a new authorization.
The City approves the plans to change the exterior siding of the house at 2363, avenue Maufils, in the Maizerets neighbourhood (Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The white aluminum siding on the ground floor will be replaced with Canexel brand wood fibre siding in a similar colour.
The upper floor and the rear addition are already covered with white Canexel; the existing details on the front of the building are being kept.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on July 14, 2026, adopted unanimously.
The borough council approved the request on August 31, 2026 (resolution CA1-2026-0169).
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City will pay an additional $108,458 to an organization that helps women in difficulty.
This money comes from a federal grant (Rapid Housing Initiative) received by the City through the Société d'habitation du Québec, but which had not been tied to any project until now.
The organization had already received $8,200,000 from the City in 2022 under the same program.
The additional money will go to the organization's real estate reserve.
An order of the Government of Québec from July 2025 made it possible to add this amount to the conditions of the grant.
The decision rests with the urban agglomeration council of Québec; the amendment takes effect when the last party signs.
The City is authorizing two employees to accompany the mayor of Québec on an economic mission to Detroit, Michigan, in May 2026.
Nicolas Roy, director of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets, will be there from May 10 to 14; Catherine Labonté, international relations advisor, from May 10 to 12.
The City is paying $7,000 for flights, ground transportation, accommodation and Mr. Roy's registration at the trade shows, upon presentation of supporting documents.
The amount breaks down into $4,600 for Mr. Roy and $2,400 for Ms. Labonté, taken from the operating budgets of their departments.
The mission accompanies businesses from the region to the Xponential and MDEX trade shows, held from May 11 to 14 in Detroit.
It follows up on the visit of a delegation from Michigan received in Québec from October 4 to 6, 2025, with Québec International and Université Laval.
An overrun of no more than 10% of the authorized amount will be accepted without further authorization.
The City is awarding Brenntag Canada inc. the contract to supply and deliver bulk 12% sodium hypochlorite (lot 2, deliveries of 20,000 litres), for an estimated amount of $334,400 before taxes.
The contract runs from the date it is awarded until June 30, 2027, with an option to renew for two 12-month periods and an annual price adjustment for inflation.
The product is used to supply the City's water treatment plants, pumping stations and swimming pools.
The net expense is estimated at $351,078.20 and will be paid out of the operating budget of the Service du traitement des eaux.
Four companies bid on this lot; Brenntag offered the lowest price, 20.3% below the department's estimate ($419,428.80).
The 2027 funds remain conditional on the adoption of that year's budget.
Lots 1 and 5 are dealt with in another decision summary; lots 3, 4 and 6 were awarded by delegation of powers.
The City is awarding to 9352-7133 Québec inc. (Lévis Ford), in Lévis, the repair of its light and intermediate Ford-brand vehicles, including parts and transportation.
The contract is worth $2,519,051.16 (plus GST and QST) and covers the period from September 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029.
The net cost is estimated at $2,644,688.84, once the QST refund is taken into account.
The contract covers 450 Ford vehicles, including public safety vehicles.
Two bids were received: Lévis Ford at $2,519,051.16 and JL Desjardins Auto Collection inc. at $2,617,195.05; the City's estimate was $2,598,113.00.
The workshops of the Service de la gestion des équipements motorisés will be able to use the contract according to their needs.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets by the appropriate authorities.
The City is authorizing a $5,300,000 expense to repair, restore and redevelop the église de Saint-Jean-Baptiste, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
It is borrowing the same amount, repayable over fifteen years.
The work covers the basement, the nave and the galleries, so the building can be put to mixed use, along with interior and exterior improvements.
The amount also covers studies, professional services (architecture, engineering, environment, etc.), the purchase of goods and the hiring of staff for the project.
The City had purchased the church in November 2024; studies showed that urgent and priority work was needed.
An amount of $530,000 (10% of the expense) is being taken from the general fund and will be repaid to it when the by-law comes into force.
The City is continuing its efforts to find the rest of the funding for the redevelopment project.
The Ville de Québec will be allowed to temporarily occupy part of the parc de l'Amérique-Française, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough, for the TramCité tramway project.

The space will be used as a storage site and for construction facilities, near the planned trench (trémie) on boulevard René-Lévesque Est, connected to the tunnel between the Basse-Ville and the Haute-Ville.
The area involved is about 7,759.80 square metres.
The occupancy will run from July 6, 2026 to July 5, 2033, with the possibility of a two-year renewal.
The land belongs to the Commission de la capitale nationale du Québec, which has reached an agreement with the City.
This authorization comes before a servitude agreement that is still being negotiated between the City and the Commission.
The document does not mention any amount.
The City is awarding the public lighting repair work to Électricité André Langevin inc. (Sainte-Marie) for $393,293 before taxes.
The work involves five arrondissements: Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, Charlesbourg, Beauport, La Haute-Saint-Charles and Les Rivières.
Thirteen streets are affected, including rue Quesnel, avenue Saint-Vincent, boulevard Mathieu, 61e Rue Est and rue Brassens.
The contract covers the removal and installation of streetlights, overhead and underground electrical wiring, electrical service entrances and Hydro-Québec connections.
Four companies submitted bids; the lowest bid is 31.7% below the City's estimate ($575,986 before taxes).
The net cost to the City is $412,908.49, paid through loan by-law R.V.Q. 3390.
The executive committee adopted the decision on June 10, 2026.
The City is entrusting Centre des Loisirs St-Sacrement inc. with the programming, maintenance and supervision of free swim periods at the Saint-Sacrement outdoor pool.
The agreement covers the period from June 12 to August 23, 2026, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
Amount of the agreement: $117,416.94, plus applicable GST and QST.
After the QST refund, the net cost to the City is $123,273.11.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget: $13,117.03 for the operation of outdoor pools and $110,156.08 for outdoor aquatic programming.
The previous agreement with the organization ended on August 24, 2025.
The organization must provide qualified staff, notify the City of any incident and report back according to the requirements set out in the agreement.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 742, rue Seigneuriale, in Beauport (Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux neighbourhood).
The parking area in the front yard may be 18 metres wide instead of the 7 metres allowed by the planning by-law.
Condition imposed: only one access driveway may be built on the property.
The owner wants to reuse the existing driveway and parking area to serve both the attached garage and the detached garage.
According to the analysis, a compliant layout would have required two driveways, more impermeable surface and the cutting down of mature trees.
The main building was rebuilt in 2025 after a fire, with a garage of a different configuration.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on May 21, 2026.
The City is tabling before the council its monthly lists of contracts and expenses for February 2026, as required by the Cities and Towns Act.
In February 2026, the City awarded 138 contracts of more than $25,000, for a total of $40,118,298 (before taxes).
Of that total, 24 contracts are over $250,000 and account for $30,026,601; 42 contracts are between $100,000 and $250,000, for $6,069,026.
47 of the 138 contracts were awarded by mutual agreement, for about $8.2 million.

29 contracts put out to competition were authorized by the director general and the assistant directors general, including several lots for landscaping maintenance and lawn repair in neighbourhoods such as Limoilou, Saint-Roch, Montcalm, Sillery and Cap-Rouge.
The threshold requiring a competitive process is set at $34,000; below that threshold, two price requests are required for purchases between $10,000 and $34,000.
The lists tabled also cover contracts transferred to another supplier, terminated contracts, cancelled calls for tenders and additional expenses authorized.
The Ville de Québec wants to borrow $635,000 to buy vehicles and motorized equipment for the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
The money will also be used for professional and technical services contracts and to hire the staff needed for these purchases.
The loan will be paid back over ten years.
The City is taking $63,500 from its general fund, which is 10% of the expense; this amount will be returned to the fund when the by-law comes into force.
The document states that these added vehicles respond to growing operational needs, the creation of new units and new responsibilities.
The expense is shared between the City and the agglomeration, according to the rules on mixed expenses.
The funds are planned for 2026 and 2027 in the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The City is refusing a minor exemption request for a lot on rue Françoise-Encelin, in Notre-Dame-des-Laurentides (Charlesbourg).
The owner wanted to split the lot in two in order to build a new residential building with up to two housing units.
The new lot would have been 13.89 metres wide, while the planning by-law requires 15 metres.
Reason for the refusal: the request does not meet the objectives of the planning program.
According to the analysis, allowing this division would block a possible street extension between rue Françoise-Encelin and rue Isabelle-Doucinet, which could allow for several residential lots.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had recommended granting the exemption on April 8, 2026; the borough council is going against that opinion.
The City is entrusting the organization La Maison Léon-Provancher with cultural programming at the Maison Hamel-Bruneau, in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The agreement is worth $171,700 (excluding GST and QST) and covers July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2028.
The organization must deliver a program of cultural activities and keep the site open and accessible to the general public.
The contract can be renewed twice, for 12 months each time, with a price increase adjusted to the consumer price index.
The amounts break down as follows: $68,000 in 2026, $86,360 in 2027 and $17,340 in 2028.
The 2027 and 2028 amounts depend on the adoption of those years' budgets.
The contract is awarded by mutual agreement, a rule that allows contracting directly with a non-profit organization.
The City is giving Charles-Auguste Fortier inc. the contract for the complete rebuilding of a section of boulevard Henri-Bourassa, east of rue Pierre-Verret, in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The contract is worth $2,081,716.22 before taxes; the net cost to the City comes to $2,185,541.82.
The work includes rebuilding the water and sewer systems, repairing the roadway, the paving, the curbs and the sidewalks, and then restoring the land.
Six companies submitted bids; Charles-Auguste Fortier inc. submitted the lowest price, 8.9% below the department's estimate ($2,286,290).
The contract allows for price adjustments based on the cost of asphalt and fuel.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3390.
The executive committee adopted the decision on May 13, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0615).
The executive committee authorizes the director of the Bureau de l'ombudsman, Anne-Laure Pelletier, to take the training course "Ombudsmans : notions essentielles et meilleures pratiques".
The training runs between September 11 and September 30, 2026: five days online, then three days at the Longueuil campus of the Université de Sherbrooke.
The City authorizes the trip to Longueuil from September 28 to 30, 2026.
The authorized expense is $5,043.43 and covers registration, travel, accommodation and meals.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Bureau de l'ombudsman; the costs are reimbursed upon submission of receipts.
An overrun of no more than 10% of the authorized amount is accepted without further authorization.
The training is recognized by the Barreau du Québec as mandatory continuing education hours.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council is amending its planning by-law for a single property: 1059, avenue La Sarre, in Vieux-Limoilou.
The owner demolished and rebuilt the rear vestibule of the building without authorization, and the new construction does not respect the required side setback.
The amendment makes the situation compliant so that the owner does not have to redo the work; the side setback may be less than 1.5 metres, but at least 0.5 metre.
The by-law also approves the building expansion plan, which is for a larger dwelling.
The work will have to begin within one year after the by-law comes into force.
The conseil de quartier du Vieux-Limoilou will be consulted and will hold a public meeting; interested persons will have seven days after that meeting to submit their written comments.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The executive committee takes note of the weekly list of additional expenses of more than $250,000 authorized by delegated employees, for the week of March 1 to 7, 2026.
Only one additional expense appears in the report: $451,651.76 (before taxes), for the Service de l'ingénierie.
It concerns the contract for the redevelopment of rue Saint-Vallier Ouest.

The work cost more because of unforeseen circumstances: replacement of unplanned sections of combined sewer and water main, adjustments for accessibility for people with reduced mobility, and the discovery of an Hydro-Québec duct bank.
The value of the contract goes from $29,651,341.27 to $30,102,993.03; its initial value was $28,709,026.88.
The Ville de Québec will pay up to $150,000 to the company Braver inc. as a non-repayable grant.
The money will be used to sell Braver's digital platform outside Québec: finding partners, marketing tools, trade shows.
Braver inc. is developing a secure collaborative platform for health care professionals; its head office is in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The project costs $500,000 in total: $150,000 from the City, $250,000 from investors and a $100,000 loan from Desjardins.
The company has 5 jobs and plans to create 2 new specialized ones.
The grant comes from the Capitale-Innovation component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, which caps assistance at $150,000 and at 50% of eligible expenses per project.
The program's review committee recommended the project on March 10, 2026; the decision rests with the urban agglomeration council.
The City is giving $4,000 to the organization Liratoutâge.
Liratoutâge is a team of volunteers that offers read-aloud sessions to people living in seniors' housing facilities.
The service is adapted to the interests and abilities of each person they meet.
The organization asked the City for this help under its status as a Municipalité amie des aînés (age-friendly municipality).
The money comes from City funds, under the grant management activity.
The executive committee approved the decision on February 25, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0227).
The arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge is authorizing four elected officials to take part in the annual convention of the Union des municipalités du Québec.
The event runs from May 13 to 15, 2026, at the Centre des congrès de Québec.
The elected officials concerned are borough president Jean-Luc Lavoie, councillor Marianne White, and councillors Gabriel Dusablon and Yannick Fauteux.
The City is paying or will reimburse the registration fees: $890 for those aged 36 and over, $377 for those aged 35 and under, plus taxes.
Other expenses will be reimbursed upon presentation of receipts, in accordance with by-law R.C.E.V.Q. 17.
The money comes from the borough's budget, under the "Supporting borough councils" activity.
The City is giving $126,199 in grants to 12 organizations to set up shared gardens in the summer of 2026.
Of the 15 applications received in January 2026, 12 were selected.
The amounts range from $2,456 (CPE La Petite Cour de Mistigri) to $20,000 (Centre multiethnique de Québec), with a maximum of $20,000 per project.
The grant covers up to 80% of expenses for non-profit organizations and institutions, and up to 50% for for-profit businesses.
The money is for setting up the gardens (planters, soil, paths, water outlet, hydroponic equipment), not for buying plants, running activities or maintenance.

Funded projects include: écoles Vanier and des Écrivains, CFP Neufchâtel, Le Pignon Bleu, Centre de Nuit Demi-Lune, CPE La Rigolade, Appartements de Bordeaux, Résidence Calla, Coopérative l'Hirondelle and Société Française de Québec.
Each organization receives 75% of the amount as soon as the resolution is adopted, and up to 25% after reporting on its actual expenses.
City council is transferring to the executive committee the power to appoint the City's representative on the board of directors of a société de développement commercial (SDC).
SDCs are non-profit organizations that represent the merchants of their commercial district and carry out economic development projects.
The designated representative may be an elected official, an officer or an employee of the City, and stays in the position until replaced.
The City says it is aiming for greater continuity and faster appointment of the employees of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets who sit on these boards.
By-law R.V.Q. 3404 comes into force in accordance with the law; no financial impact is indicated.
The City is announcing its intention to change the zoning of five zones in the Myrand sector, north of chemin Sainte-Foy, between avenue du Séminaire and avenue Myrand.
The change would allow the development of residential and commercial buildings along planned mobility routes on land belonging to Université Laval.
The affected sector is in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood, Saint-Louis-Sillery electoral district.
The City will consult the people of the sector, merchants and targeted organizations, in addition to the consultations already required by law.
It plans information, active participation and feedback measures.
Details of the participation measures will be published on the City's website before the first activity begins.
The Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough council was to make a decision on August 27, 2026.
The City is renewing its agreement with the Réseau de transport de la Capitale (RTC) for one year for the ÉquiMobilité program, which offers reduced-fare transit passes.
The program is for individuals and families whose income is below the low-income threshold, as well as for holders of an admission card from the Service de transport adapté de la Capitale.
As of July 1, 2026, the monthly pass will go from $50 to $51 (instead of $102.50 at the regular fare) and the 1-trip pass from $2 to $2.05 (instead of $3.85).
Fares will now be indexed every July 1, by the same percentage as the January indexation of social assistance.
The City is paying the RTC compensation estimated at $4,100,000 to cover the lost revenue; it no longer covers the cost of issuing the smart cards.
The City issues the proof of eligibility; the RTC provides the OPUS ÉquiMobilité card free of charge and sends the City a monthly report.
An advisory committee bringing together nine community organizations and the RTC made recommendations that led to these adjustments.
The City is ratifying an amendment with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications to receive an additional $1,196,460 from the ministère's emergency fund.
This money will be used for priority work on the steeples of the église du Très-Saint-Sacrement, which has been closed to the public since fall 2019 and was classified as a heritage building in 2022.
The project costs $6,482,047 in total: $5,196,460 comes from the Government of Quebec (including $4M already granted in 2022) and $1,285,587 from the City.
The City's share is already included in its investment plan, through the Mesure d'aide aux églises à valeur patrimoniale exceptionnelle.
The work on the steeples is a condition for reopening the church to the public.
The amendment had to be signed by the mayor and the city clerk before March 31, 2026, the end of the Government of Quebec's fiscal year.
The City also commits to supporting the church's owner and to reporting back within 3 months after the work is completed.
The City is refusing the request from the owner of 2570, rue des Malécites, in the Vieux-Bourg neighbourhood (Beauport), who wanted to have his already-built parking area approved.
The parking area extends 4 metres in front of the façade instead of the 3 metres allowed, and is 11 metres wide instead of the 7 metres allowed.
Reason for the refusal: the owner is not suffering serious harm, because a compliant parking area can be built on the lot.
Beauport's comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the refusal on April 23, 2026.
