According to the analysis, a compliant version of the parking area had already been submitted when the building permit for the building was applied for.
The City wants to obtain a permanent underground easement on a piece of land bordering 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The easement covers about 10.30 square metres of part of lot 5 259 660 and will be used to move public utility conduits and networks.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement or, failing an agreement, by expropriation; the owner has already been informed of the process and given a contact person at the City.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings and to withdraw them if the project no longer needs the easement.
The Division de l'arpentage et de la géomatique will prepare the plans and the technical description.
The entire piece of land is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $356,000, or $291.35 per square metre.
The funds come from the urban agglomeration loan by-law on the Réseau structurant de transport en commun (R.A.V.Q. 1342).
The executive committee takes note of the quarterly report on the City's Fonds local d'investissement (FLI), for the period from April 1 to June 30, 2026.

Only one loan was recommended during the quarter: $200,000 to Alias, ligne de signalement inc., to bring ALIAS 3.0+ to market in Canada and Europe (recommended on June 25, 2026, payment still to come).
No loans were paid out during the quarter; the City received $122,889.30 in FLI loan repayments.
The FLI balance went from $6,407,350.15 (March 31, 2026) to $6,255,637.44 (June 30, 2026).
No new loans were approved under the emergency assistance program for small and medium-sized businesses (PAUPME); repayments received totalled $867,789.55 (AREAP and AERAM).
The FLI-PAUPME balance went from $20,591,329.11 to $19,705,607.53.
The City is banning parking on both sides of the intersection of rue Roger-Bontemps and rue de la Détente, in the Lac-Saint-Charles–Saint-Émile neighbourhood.
Residents had complained about poor visibility for drivers coming out of rue de la Détente.
A bus stop zone is being created on the north side of rue Roger-Bontemps, so that RTC buses stop at the curb instead of in the traffic lane.
Four on-street parking spaces are being removed; according to the City, the impact is negligible since residents have private driveways.
On the south side, parking is banned on a stretch running from 46 metres west of avenue du Lac-Saint-Charles up to rue de la Détente, and then for 18 metres west of that street.
The decision falls under the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough council.
The Ville de Québec is buying specialized technical rescue equipment for its Service de protection contre l'incendie, at a cost of $1,256,037.40 (plus GST and QST).

The contract is awarded without a call for tenders to Équipements incendies C.M.P. Mayer inc. (L'Arsenal), of Drummondville: no other supplier came forward after the notice of intention published on SEAO, for which the deadline was June 5, 2026.
The net expense, after the QST refund, comes to $1,318,682.24.
The money comes from the loan by-law tied to the building of the structuring public transit network (TramCité project).
The equipment is used for the operations of the Groupe de sauvetage technique: trenches, heavy lifting, confined spaces, collapses, high-angle rescue, stabilization and extrication.
The contract takes effect on June 10, 2026 and ends on December 31, 2026.
The City justifies the contract without a call for tenders by the compatibility with the Paratech equipment already in use, the training costs avoided and the maintenance done in-house.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 1090, rue Louis-Riel, in the Du Plateau neighbourhood (Arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The existing office building keeps a rear setback of 2.37 metres, while the planning by-law requires 9.0 metres.
Without this exemption, part of the building would have had to be demolished to comply with the by-law.
The situation has existed since 1970 and no complaint has been recorded; the vacant lot next door belongs to Hydro-Québec.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on March 10, 2026, and the borough council followed that recommendation.
The Ville de Québec is providing $365,700 over three years (2026, 2027 and 2028) to three youth organizations in the arrondissement de Beauport.
Each year, $121,900 will be divided as follows: $15,525 to the Maison des jeunes de Beauport Ouest, $36,225 to the Maison des jeunes de Beauport Est and $70,150 to TRIP Jeunesse Beauport.
The money is used to maintain prevention and outreach activities for young people in Beauport, including the five youth centre living environments and the TRIP Jeunesse mobile unit.
The organizations will have to report on their activities each year and mention the City's contribution in their official publications.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 depend on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
The funding keeps the same total amount as the previous three-year agreement (2023-2025).

The City is awarding the company W. Brindamour inc., of Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, the ventilation, heating and air conditioning work at various service points and plants of the Service du traitement des eaux.
The contract is estimated at $462,250 before taxes; the net expense is estimated at $485,304.72.
The work will take place from June 1, 2026 to November 30, 2028, with the possibility of two 12-month extensions indexed to the consumer price index.
The company will supply the labour, tools, parts and new equipment for preventive and corrective maintenance, optimization, bringing up to standard and installation of HVAC systems.
Two companies submitted bids: W. Brindamour inc. at $462,250 and BonairSD inc. at $574,875; both bids comply.
The bid selected is 3.1% below the estimate of the requesting department, which was $476,950.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
The Ville de Québec is adopting a revised version of its Politique d'investissement du Fonds régions et ruralité, which replaces the August 2025 version.
A single project cannot receive more than $500,000 for the duration of the agreement, and a sector-based development agreement cannot receive more than $1,000,000.
Grants can cover up to 100% of the expenses for a project by the City or by an MRC, and up to 80% for co-operatives and social economy non-profit organizations.
Eligible administration fees are set at 5% for organizations and 10% for the City's management of the fund.

Support for social economy businesses is increasing: the new collective entrepreneurship scholarship goes from $25,000 to $30,000, the support voucher from $10,000 to $15,000, the digital shift from $20,000 to $25,000, and Défi-Québec ville entrepreneuriale from $50,000 to $75,000.
A new contribution of $75,000 is created for a project related to the food system of the agglomeration of Québec.
Only one-time, non-recurring projects of limited duration are eligible; organizations' permanent operating costs are excluded.
The City is appointing 17 citizen commissioners to the Commission consultative pour la mobilité dans le Vieux-Québec, which was created in March 2026.
Nine commissioners are appointed for a 3-year term and eight for a 4-year term.
A public call for applications was held from May 25 to June 14, 2026 for 16 positions; more than 30 applications were received.
A 17th seat was set aside for the Comité des citoyens du Vieux-Québec so that it could name a representative.
The commissioners are divided into three groups: 7 for lived experience and local roots, 7 for professional expertise and 3 for the academic and scientific side.
The Commission must define a vision for mobility in Vieux-Québec and draw up a mobility plan for this area.
Three elected officials already sit on the Commission: Mélissa Coulombe-Leduc (chair), Elainie Lepage and Yannick Fauteux, who also made up the selection committee.
The City is banning parking at three spots on rue Pélissier, near the pedestrian crossing at the intersection of rue Palmarolle.
Three parking spaces are being removed on rue Pélissier.
On the north side, the ban applies over 30 metres, starting 166 metres west of rue Trémoy.
On the south side, the ban applies starting 183 metres west of rue Trémoy up to rue Palmarolle.
The City explains that cars parked near the crossing were making it harder to see pedestrians, many of whom are seniors.
The measure affects the arrondissement of Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, district of la Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy.
The City is granting an exemption from the planning rules to build a detached three-unit building on a vacant lot at 11394-11396-11398, boulevard de la Colline.
The lot is located in the Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf neighbourhood, in the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough.
The right side setback may be 2.30 metres instead of the 4 metres normally required.
The combined width of the side yards may be 6.3 metres instead of the 8 metres required.
According to the analysis, the irregular shape of the lot makes it impossible to meet the standard without compromising the feasibility of the project.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on February 25, 2026.
The City is sending councillor Marianne White and employee Olivier Therrien Bergeron to the annual convention of the Fédération canadienne des municipalités, in Edmonton, from June 4 to 7, 2026.
The councillor will travel from June 3 to 8; Mr. Therrien Bergeron is responsible for the FCM file at the Service de la coordination stratégique et des relations internationales.
The City will reimburse their expenses (registration, travel, accommodation, meals) up to a maximum of $10,200 taxes included, upon presentation of supporting documents.
The bill is split between two budgets: $4,982 to the city council and the executive committee, $5,218 to the Service de la coordination stratégique et des relations internationales.
An overrun of no more than 10% of the authorized amount will be accepted without further authorization.
The dates may change if the convention organizers modify them.
The City is buying four six-wheel trucks for the Service des travaux publics, to replace vehicles that have reached the end of their useful life.
The contract for lot 1 (cab-chassis trucks) goes to Camions Globocam Québec et Lévis inc., of Québec, for $588,144 before taxes.
The net expense, after the QST refund, comes to $617,477.68.
Two bids were received for lot 1: $588,144 and $655,744 (Transdiff inc.). The requesting department had estimated the cost at $700,000.
The money comes from two urban agglomeration loan by-laws, for $308,738.84 each.
Lot 2 (extended cab) has already been awarded through delegated powers.
The executive committee signed resolution CE-2026-0275 on March 4, 2026.
The Ville de Québec will pay up to $110,000 to the company Les Logiciels Aukcio inc., whose head office is in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The money will be used to sell the Aukcio platform outside Quebec. The platform auctions used vehicles between individuals and dealerships.
Ontario is the first market targeted, followed by British Columbia and Alberta.
The project costs $223,500 in total: $110,000 from the City, $63,500 from the company and a $50,000 loan from the Banque de développement du Canada.
The company plans to create 5 specialized jobs; it currently has 3 employees.
The grant comes from the Capitale-Innovation component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030 and is non-refundable.
A review committee recommended the project on December 9, 2025; follow-up will be done with an economic benefits form.
The City is granting a minor exemption to the hair salon at 6680, 1re Avenue, at the corner of 67e Rue Est, in Charlesbourg (Saint-Rodrigue district).
The owner may redevelop her parking area and go from five to seven spaces, all located on her private property.
The parking area may stay at 0 metres from the lot line on 67e Rue Est, instead of the 4 metres required.
Vehicles will be able to enter and exit moving forward or in reverse, and the access lane may be up to 19 metres wide instead of 10 metres.
The work consists of removing the raised street curb and extending the existing spaces toward the inside of the property.
According to the analysis, the current encroachments on City land will be removed and the minimum percentage of green space remains respected.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on the request on June 17, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 75, rue Doyon, in the Vieux-Bourg neighbourhood in Beauport.
The setback at the rear of the building is recognized as compliant at 2.5 metres, instead of the 7.5 metres required by the Beauport planning by-law.
The purpose of the process is to legalize the siting of a detached building constructed in 1974 with a permit, when the required setback was 3.05 metres.
Without the exemption, complying with the by-law would require partially demolishing the building.
According to the analysis, the rear setback has not been the subject of any complaint and the lot is not in an area of natural or human-made constraints.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on June 11, 2026; the borough council made the decision (resolution CA5-2026-0067).
The City is paying $21,370 to Sports-Loisirs L'Ormière for summer activities for 13- to 15-year-olds.
The funding comes from the Programme Estival-Ado 2026 and concerns the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The organization will open a second activity site and expects to welcome 38 young people.
Loisirs-Action Val-Bélair chose not to offer activities in 2026; only one organization submitted a project in the borough.
In 2025, 37 teenagers took part in the program in the borough, with $28,925 paid to two organizations.
The activities focus on group recreation, an introduction to the role of day camp leader and preparation for the job market.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget; the decision was made at the borough council meeting of April 20, 2026.
The City wants to obtain a permanent servitude (easement) on a piece of land bordering 1re Avenue, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
This servitude would be used to move public utility conduits and networks along the route.
The area involved is about 672.20 square metres, on part of lot 1 941 055.
The City will try to reach a negotiated agreement with the owner; otherwise, it will proceed by expropriation. The owner has already been informed and has been given the name of a contact person.
If the project no longer needs the servitude, the City may drop the expropriation proceedings, in whole or in part.
The entire property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $1,030,000, which is $141.47 per square metre.
The money comes from agglomeration loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342, related to the structuring public transit network.
The City is pushing back to December 1, 2026 the deadline for signing the deed of sale for a piece of land along rue Dugas, in Beauport.
The buyer is the Coopérative d'Habitation Le Harfang de Beauport, which signed its purchase offer on June 4, 2025.
The co-operative wants to build a 23-unit building there for single people or families with low or modest incomes.
The project must be carried out under the Programme d'habitation abordable Québec.
The co-operative asked for this extension because it is still working to finalize its financing with several government partners.
The sale price for the land set out in the purchase offer is $470,000, and the sale is made without any warranty as to soil quality.
The City is paying out $6,957 in grants to five organizations in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The 132e Groupe Scout Saint-Émile receives $4,250 to update its branding and buy promotional items.
Loisirs-Action Val-Bélair receives $1,475 to buy sound equipment.
La Maison des Jeunes de St-Émile receives $500 for an event highlighting the contribution of young people.
Sports-Loisirs L'Ormière receives $273 for support services during spring break week.
Les Voix de la Haute-Saint-Charles receive $459 for their branding and the purchase of a banner.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget; the applications had to be submitted by December 15, 2025 at the latest.
The City is bringing back the architectural review criteria for the construction of main buildings in the avenue Myrand area, between chemin Sainte-Foy and boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest.
These criteria were introduced in April 2025, then deleted by mistake in June 2025 during another by-law amendment.

To get a building permit in these zones, a developer will have to have its plans approved: highlighting street corners, transition with neighbouring buildings, balconies and setbacks on the façade, and a ground floor connected to the public space.
Residential projects will have to landscape the front yard with grass, plantings and landscaping; commercial projects, with hard surfaces and ornamental vegetation.
Applicants will also have to provide a colour image of the proposed buildings and of the neighbouring buildings.
The scope of the criteria stays the same as it was before they were deleted.
The City is asking for the opinion of the conseil de quartier de la Cité-Universitaire and is putting it in charge of holding the public consultation meeting.
The City is entrusting the sanitary maintenance of certain recreational or sports sites and facilities in the arrondissement des Rivières to the organization Loisirs Lebourgneuf inc.
The contract costs $148,181.17 (plus GST and QST), for a net expense of $155,571.70 for the City.
The agreement covers May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027, with an option to renew for 12 months.
The expense is split into $103,714.38 in 2026 and $51,857.32 in 2027 (net of taxes).
The 2027 portion depends on the approval of the 2027 budget by the competent authorities.
The rule on awarding contracts allows this mandate to be granted directly to a non-profit organization.
The director of the Service des approvisionnements is authorized to sign the contract documents.
The Beauport borough council gives City managers the power to authorize the occupation of public property (public land, sidewalks, streets and lanes), both above and below ground.

For temporary occupations, the power is delegated to the director general, an assistant director general, the director of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets, the director of the Division des activités et de l'expertise immobilières, and a section director of that division.

For permanent occupations, the power is delegated to the director of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets, the director of the Division des activités et de l'expertise immobilières, and a section director of that division.
These people set the conditions and the rent, and may require a specific way of carrying out the work and specific materials to be used.
An authorization may be revoked by written notice to the owner, published at the Bureau de la publicité des droits at least one month beforehand.
Permanent occupations that are authorized must be reported to the executive committee every quarter, with the nature of the occupation, the name of the beneficiary and the amount of the rent.
The City explains the change by the rise in requests related to real estate transactions and the desire to standardize practices across the agglomeration.
The City will pay Canadien National (CN) an estimated $404,203.96 (excluding GST and QST) to maintain the surface of the level crossing on avenue Plante, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
CN will rebuild the level crossing: replacing worn or damaged rails, ties, fasteners, ballast and road surfacing.
This work is part of CN's Programme d'entretien des passages à niveau 2026, under which CN notified the City of the need for rehabilitation.
An order from the Office des transports du Canada (R-38325) places the cost of maintaining the crossing surface on the City.
The City will be billed based on the costs actually incurred, and CN will refund any unused amounts.
The money comes from two loan by-laws: $364,203.96 (R.V.Q. 2751) and $40,000 (R.V.Q. 2828).
The matter was to be decided by city council on August 25, 2026.
The owner of 801, 3e Avenue (Limoilou) wants to convert two dwellings into a tourist accommodation unit.
The by-law would require the owner to provide one parking space, but the available space will be used to build a compliant emergency exit.
The City is exempting the owner from this parking space in exchange for $500 paid into the "Fonds de stationnement" (parking fund).
The payment must be made no later than 30 days after the borough council adopts the resolution.
The building is located in parking permit zone 22: 713 on-street spaces giving priority to residents and 371 permits issued by the City.
The Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente recommends accepting the request.
The City is buying two sidewalk snow-clearing tracked vehicles (chenillettes), to replace equipment that has reached the end of its useful life.
The contract goes to Équipements Plannord ltée, of Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, for $463,861.18 before GST and QST.
The net cost to the City, after the QST refund, is $486,996.26.
This was the only bid received for this lot; the price is 5.4% above the requesting department's estimate of $440,000.
After negotiation, the supplier lowered its price, which had started at $465,036.
The City will be able to buy two more chenillettes at the same price, if the budget allows.
Lot 2, which covers three trailer-mounted spreaders, was awarded separately under delegated authority.
The arrondissement des Rivières is granting a minor exemption for a planned property at 0, rue du Blizzard (quartier Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf).
The fence will be allowed to be up to 2.5 metres high, instead of the maximum of 1.2 metres in the front yard and 2 metres in the other yards.
The company Debertin wants to offer a pharmaceutical storage building there to the company GSK, which requires this type of fence for the security of the material stored.
The fence will be made of black wrought iron, 2.44 metres high, with angles pointing outward at the top rather than barbed wire, and less than 100 mm between the bars.
According to the analysis, the lot is largely bordered by a wooded area, which limits how visible the fence is from the front yard.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on March 2, 2026.

The City is adding $18,000 (plus taxes) to its agreement with the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for the P-13708 bridge project, on boulevard des Chutes over autoroute Félix-Leclerc.
This addition is for installing tactile warning plates and rumble strips on boulevard des Chutes, to meet universal accessibility needs that came up during the project.

The original project, approved in November 2024 for about $361,000, includes a multi-purpose path of about 400 metres and a lighting system, between avenue de l'Obiou and rue des Pionnières-de-Beauport.
The City's financial share of the project rises to about $379,000 (before taxes); the total estimated cost of the project is $4,430,000 (before taxes).
The net additional expense for the City is estimated at $18,897.75, funded by loan by-law R.V.Q. 3325 on cycling and pedestrian paths.
The ministère manages the project and runs the calls for tenders; the City will then take care of maintaining the sidewalks, the lighting and the paths.
The City is amending its planning by-law to allow outdoor storage at 1300, rue du Blizzard, in the Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf neighbourhood.
The authorization covers the side and rear yards of lot 4 575 260: vehicles of 4,500 kg and more, equipment more than 3 metres high, tool vehicles, machinery, goods and materials.

The request comes from the Société québécoise des infrastructures, which is relocating facilities of the ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs.
A fence at least 2 metres high is required around the outdoor storage area.
The occupancy must begin within five years after the by-law comes into force, otherwise the authorization lapses.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; the neighbourhood council will hold a public consultation meeting, followed by seven days to submit written comments.
The permission applies only to this property, and not to the entire 21753Cc zone.
The City is adding $125,425 (plus taxes) to the contract awarded to DLGL Technologies Corporation, of Blainville, to improve its VIP payroll system.
The contract therefore goes from $108,675 to $234,100 (plus taxes) since it was awarded in January 2026.
The contract covers the period from January 16, 2026 to January 15, 2027.
The changes to the system are needed to apply the changes set out in the latest collective agreements, the scope of which was not known at the start.
The net cost, after the QST is recovered, is estimated at $131,680.57.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1759 on technological solutions.
The contract was awarded without a call for tenders, as the law allows this for work related to software already in place.
The City is adding mandatory stop signs on rue Valentin, on the north and south approaches to the intersection with rue Gabrielle-Vallée.
Drivers and cyclists will have to stop there.
Pavement markings go with the new stops (pedestrian crossings, centre lines and stop lines).
The measure affects the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, district de la Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy, in the Quatre-Bourgeois area.
The City says it wants to make the pedestrian crossing safer in a dense area where residents are mostly seniors, and where visibility is lacking on the north side.
The decision comes from the Stratégie de sécurité routière 2025-2029 and takes the form of order O-767.
The City is adopting a guide that sets out the rules for travel, hospitality and activity expenses at Destination Québec cité, the regional tourism organization that is also a City department.
The guide is in addition to the City's policy on travel and hospitality expenses: the policy takes precedence, and the guide spells out how it applies to the tourism sector.
It applies to all Destination Québec cité employees who incur expenses as part of their duties, whether those expenses are reimbursed or paid directly by the organization.
It covers, among other things, meal costs, connectivity costs (wifi and data), clothing laundering costs, hospitality expenses and the rules on alcoholic beverages.
The City's executive committee must approve the annual schedule of activities; any travel not included in the schedule must be authorized in advance by the Direction générale.
The expenses and reimbursement claims of the director of Destination Québec cité must be approved by the chair of the board and the Direction générale.
Each year, the director must report to the board on the activities carried out, their costs and whether the objectives were met.
The City is changing the zoning for the area at 2313, boulevard du Versant-Nord, in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough).
The change allows repair shops (group C36 uses) in zone 32201Cc: vehicle repair and maintenance, and the sale and installation of parts and accessories.
The zone in question is south of autoroute Charest, north of rue Jean-Durand, east of autoroute Robert-Bourassa and west of avenue Nérée-Tremblay.

The request comes from the owner of the "Lave-auto à la main du Vallon Centre Protection", who has been offering windshield replacement and rustproofing for at least 15 years without these activities being allowed under the zoning.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The conseil de quartier de la Cité-Universitaire will be consulted and will hold the public meeting; interested persons will have 7 days after that meeting to send their comments in writing.

The City is awarding Gosselin Tremblay Excavation inc. the construction of a temporary road link between avenue de Vimy and rue Gérard-Morisset, for $383,650 before taxes (net expense of $402,784.54).
This link will be used during the tramway (TramCité) work on boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, in the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou.

The Gérard-Morisset / René-Lévesque Ouest intersection will be closed at certain times; since rue Gérard-Morisset is the only car access to the area, the temporary link will maintain access for residents and emergency services.
The work includes a road structure designed to limit impacts on trees, as well as lighting and traffic lights at both ends for alternating one-way traffic.
The link will be open to all modes of transportation, with cyclists and motorists sharing the roadway.
Six companies submitted bids; the selected offer is the lowest, 2% below the department's estimate of $391,590.53.
The contract provides for price adjustments for asphalt and fuel; the funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the structuring public transit network.
The City is authorizing the construction of three residential buildings of two to seven storeys at 4035-4075, boulevard des Cimes, in the Des Châtels neighbourhood (Loretteville–Les Châtels).
The project provides for at least 290 housing units (about 330 according to the draft resolution), with 90% of the parking indoors.

The City is setting aside several of the area's planning rules: maximum heights of 10 and 15 metres, a maximum of two housing units per building, only one building per lot, and distances between buildings.
The developer must pay for the work to extend a sidewalk on the south side of boulevard des Cimes, up to a maximum of $135,000.
The owner must hand over to the City, free of charge, the space for a 1.4-metre sidewalk (about 101 m) and a 2-metre bike path (about 72 m) on rue Monseigneur-Cooke.
The buildings must have a minimum of 90 housing units (building A) and 140 housing units (building B).
A public consultation meeting will be held, followed by three days to send in written comments; the project is not subject to a referendum.
The Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is giving $100 to the 20e groupe Scouts du Triangle (District de Québec).
The money comes from the borough council's budget, under the activity supporting borough councils.
The request comes from 12 young scouts aged 15 to 17 who are preparing a trip to Morocco in June 2026.
The grant is proposed by the councillor for the Montcalm-Saint-Sacrement district, Catherine Vallières-Roland.
The cheque is made out to the 20e groupe Scouts du Triangle, 1229, av. du Chanoine-Morel, Québec.
The City is paying up to $79,194 to Carrefour jeunesse-emploi Chauveau for 2026-2027.
The money is used to hire and employ an intercultural community-living officer in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles, from May 2026 to March 2027.
The amount covers the person's salary as well as organizing and leading activities.

The funding comes from two sources: $40,000 from the agreement with the ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration and $39,194 from the budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
Community-living officers already exist in Limoilou, Saint-Roch, Sainte-Foy and Vanier; La Haute-Saint-Charles is being added to the list.
The organization must report each year and mention the support of the City and the ministère in its publications.
The project is a pilot that could lead to a three-year agreement.
The City is acquiring a strip of land of about 25.5 square metres along 1re Avenue, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough.
The acquisition will be used to widen the 1re Avenue right-of-way for the TramCité tramway project.
The purchase will be made by mutual agreement with the owner or, failing an agreement, by expropriation.
The owner has been informed of the process, the next steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
The land in question, in its largest extent, is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $175,000, or $465.12 per square metre.
The City may abandon the expropriation if the TramCité project no longer needs the land.
The funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the structuring public transit network.
The City is changing traffic on 76e Rue Est, at the intersection with boulevard Henri-Bourassa, in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
On the west side of the intersection, a left-turn lane is being added for vehicles heading east; one westbound traffic lane is being removed.
On the east side, a right-turn lane is being added; the left lane will be used to turn left or go straight.
The pavement markings will be redone, including moving the centre yellow line, and new signs will be installed on each approach to the intersection.
The City says it is aiming for better safety for road users and smoother traffic flow, notably in response to vehicles passing on the right while heading east.
The decision affects the districts of Saint-Rodrigue and Louis-XIV.
The City authorizes Hervé Chapon, transportation planning advisor, to travel to Bruges (Belgium) and Amsterdam (Netherlands) from April 25 to 30, 2026.
It sets aside $5,072.80 for airfare, ground transportation and accommodation costs, paid on presentation of receipts when the hosts do not cover them.
The purpose of the trip is to look at Amsterdam's plan for tour buses (Touringcar Agenda 2020-2025), the electric shuttles in the historic centre of Bruges and its bus station.
What is learned is intended for Vieux-Québec and the neighbouring areas, where traffic will change in the coming years with upcoming construction work.
Mr. Chapon coordinates a network of twelve cities on three continents led by Québec; the work will be presented at the OVPM world congress in October 2026.
A difference of no more than 10% from the authorized amount is accepted without further authorization.
The City is awarding two engineering services contracts for its industrial facilities, valid until December 31, 2028, with the possibility of two one-year renewals and an indexation based on the CPI.
Norda Stelo inc. is awarded lot 1 (industrial processes, mechanical, electrical, automation) for an estimated amount of $16,224,930.00 before taxes.
Pluritec ltée is awarded lot 2 (mechanical, electrical and building structure) for an estimated amount of $2,131,134.40 before taxes.
The work covers the plants and stations of the Service du traitement des eaux, the Centre de valorisation énergétique, the landfill sites and various industrial equipment.
The firms will produce the plans and specifications, the cost estimates, the construction site supervision, the follow-up on warranties and the quality control of soils and materials.
The net expenditure for the City is estimated at $19,271,573.11, subject to the approval of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.
Seven bids were received; WSP Canada inc. was declared non-compliant because its prices were not in the right envelope.
The Ville de Québec is amending, for the first time, its April 2024 agreement with the Société hôtesse des Jeux du Canada 2027.
The change concerns what will happen to the equipment and property bought to organize the Jeux d'hiver de Québec 2027.
Previously, this property was to be turned over to a fund dedicated to sport development after the Games.
From now on, the City will instead be able to set up a plan to sell, donate or transfer this property, even before the end of the Games.
The Société hôtesse would carry out this plan, which must comply with the Conseil des Jeux du Canada's policy and be approved by the City's executive committee.
The agreement is given new appendices: the property liquidation policy, the benefits and legacy plan, and the Société hôtesse's liquidation plan.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City is giving $64,658 in grants to 12 organizations in the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough to help them pay their operating expenses.
The amounts range from $870 to $10,000 per organization: Maison de la famille St-Ambroise ($10,000), Sports-Loisirs L'Ormière ($9,000), Organisme pour l'intégration sociale Apprenti-loisirs ($7,533).
Receiving $6,500 each: Aide à la communauté et services à domicile, Le Piolet and Servio - Soutien aux personnes TCC.

Receiving less: Centre d'appui Réseau-Aînés ($5,647), Cercle de fermières Loretteville ($5,102), R.A.F.A.L. ($3,176), Groupe Scout de Château-d'Eau ($2,563), École de musique La Symphonie ($1,267), Groupe scout des Laurentides ($870).
The applications had been submitted on February 20, 2026; some grants correspond to the 2nd or 3rd year of the program.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget, under the "Soutien aux organismes" (support for organizations) activity.
The City is applying for financial assistance from the ministère des Affaires municipales (Fonds régions et ruralité) to fund a study on water management in the rivière Saint-Charles watershed.
The program covers 20% of costs, up to a maximum of $20,000.
The study would be used to determine whether it is possible to create a cooperation between the City and neighbouring municipalities (a service agreement or an intermunicipal board).
The services targeted: emptying and inspection of septic systems, water quality monitoring, conservation of natural environments.
Lac Saint-Charles and its watershed supply drinking water to 300,000 people; the document states that the condition of the lake remains a concern.
The application must be submitted during the call for projects open from January 5 to April 17, 2026.
The City then plans to prepare technical specifications in order to launch a call for tenders.
The City is granting an exemption from the planning rules for the expansion of a building at 838, rue Grandjean, in the Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy neighbourhood.
The expansion will create 26 housing units.
The rear yard will be 1.13 metres instead of the 15 metres required.
The parking will be 1.7 metres from the front property line instead of 4 metres, and it will be laid out at the front of the building, which is normally not allowed.
Three street accesses are allowed even though the lot has 149 metres of frontage instead of the 150 metres required.
According to the analysis, the expansion is built partly on the existing outdoor parking lot and keeps the inner courtyard and the green space.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted in favour of the request on June 16, 2026, unanimously.
The Ville de Québec is paying its 2026 membership fee to the Fédération québécoise des municipalités (FQM), where it sits as an associate member.
The approved amount is $21,743.86, plus applicable taxes.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Direction générale, for a net expense of $22,828.34.
The membership fee covers January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The agreement with the FQM, signed in 2014, sets a flat membership fee of $25,000 including taxes and renews automatically.
The FQM brings together more than 1,000 municipalities and MRCs in Québec.
The executive committee takes note of the weekly list of additional expenses of more than $250,000 authorized by employees holding a delegation of powers, for the week of April 4, 2026.
Only one change notice appears in the report: $412,156.34 (before taxes) for the project to repair the building envelope and roof of the bibliothèque Paul-Aimé Paiement.

This amount covers unforeseen site conditions: mitigation of swelling rock, demolition of the slab on grade of the former college, mechanical work related to the replacement of the ventilation unit, and a temporary opening in the basement to bring in a mechanical unit.
The contract value goes from $7,058,122.60 to $7,470,278.94, while its initial value was $5,479,157.00.
The expense falls under the Service de la gestion des immeubles.
The City is giving out $6,350 in grants to 12 athletes and 1 sports club from Québec.
Eight athletes each receive $400 for Canadian competitions held outside Quebec (curling, speed skating, snowboarding, biathlon, judo).
Four athletes each receive $600 for competitions abroad: Estonia, Sweden, the United States and Norway (figure skating, tennis, freestyle skiing, cross-country skiing).
The Commission de ski Nordique Skibec receives $750 for a cross-country skiing competition in Canmore, Alberta.
The competitions covered took place between January and April 2026.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The program accepts applications three times a year: in May, in August and in December.
The City is giving out $1,530 in grants to two organizations in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
"Loisirs Action Val-Bélair" receives $530 and "Loisirs des Hauts-Sentiers" receives $1,000.
The money supports activities held during the Semaine de relâche 2026 (spring break), from February 28 to March 8.
The activities: an outdoor zumba session at the Centre culturel Georges-Dor on February 28, and the Saint-Émile storm day at parc Réal-Cloutier on March 5.
The activities were free and open to everyone, rain or shine.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 401, rue Saint-Paul, in Vieux-Québec, for the expansion of a building.
The project calls for converting and expanding a building of high heritage value to create 141 housing units and several commercial spaces.
The building will be expanded into the existing parking area, and a partial fifth level will be added.
The permitted height goes from 16 metres to 17.75 metres for 25% of the area of the fourth level.
The parking lot's traffic aisles may be 6.0 metres wide instead of 6.5 metres.
Seven parking spaces may measure at least 2.5 m by 4.6 m instead of 2.6 m by 5.5 m, and one parallel space 5.9 m instead of 6.0 m.
The exemption is granted without conditions: the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec and the ministère de la Culture will oversee how the expansion fits in.
The Ville de Québec is entrusting the defence of its case to lawyer Vincent Rochette and the firm Norton Rose Fulbright.
The mandate covers representing the City before all courts and tribunals in the class action Guèye c. Ville de Québec et autres.
The planned fees amount to $104,987.50 (net of taxes), taken from the operating budget of the Service des affaires juridiques.
The class action was authorized by the Superior Court on April 22, 2025; the Court of Appeal refused the cities permission to challenge this authorization on September 11, 2025.

The group covered: any racialized person who was a victim of racial profiling during a traffic stop made without grounds to suspect an offence, by the police of one of the defendant cities or by the Sûreté du Québec, since May 23, 2019.
Eight cities and the Procureur général du Québec are being sued; Norton Rose Fulbright already represents Gatineau, Blainville and Terrebonne in the same case.
The City is changing the job title of a non-unionized professional position: "Aumônier, classe 5" becomes "Responsable du soutien psychologique, classe 5".
The class 5 rating and the salary scale attached to the position stay the same.
According to the attached salary scale, this job title pays between $74,544 and $129,006 in 2026, and up to $136,862 in 2028.
A joint job evaluation committee reviewed the file and agreed on this change.
The decision summary shows no financial impact, and the decision falls to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The City is awarding Inter-Cité Construction ltée the contract for the paving program for $4,093,631.40 (plus GST and QST).
The work includes repaving (milling and paving) and the reconstruction of concrete sidewalks and curbs.
The work is planned on several streets spread across the city's entire territory.
Three companies submitted bids; Inter-Cité submitted the lowest price, ahead of Construction et Pavage Portneuf ($4,109,375.45) and Groupe Colas Québec ($4,190,114.00).
The chosen price is 9.5% below the estimate of the requesting department, which was $4,523,650.12 before taxes.
The contract includes clauses for adjusting asphalt and fuel prices.
The net cost to the City comes to $4,297,801.26, funded through a loan by-law.
The City is banning parking in the four right-angle curves of carré De Tracy Est and carré De Tracy Ouest, in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg (district Louis-XIV).
About 25 parking spaces will disappear.
Reason given: these streets are part of the school corridor for école primaire du Bourg-Royal, the roadway is 7 to 9 metres wide and there are no sidewalks.
On carré De Tracy Est, the ban covers two 41-metre sections, between rue de Dover and avenue du Bourg-Royal.
On carré De Tracy Ouest, the ban covers one 33-metre section and one 41-metre section, between avenue du Bourg-Royal and rue François-Trefflé.
According to the document, the impact will be limited because residents of the area have access to private parking.
The City is awarding Construction Deric inc. the contract to rebuild basins 1 and 2 at the Complexe de valorisation énergétique, in the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou.
The contract is worth $1,765,550 before GST and QST; the net cost to the City is $1,815,918.49.
The work covers civil and structural engineering, mechanical systems, piping, electrical systems and instrumentation.
Its purpose is to maintain and improve the facilities used to treat bottom ash (mâchefers).
Three bids were received and found compliant; Deric submitted the lowest price, ahead of Les Constructions Bé-Con ($2,085,583.82) and Tro-Chaînes ($2,287,053).
The chosen price is 1.3% below the estimate from the requesting department ($1,789,224.25).
The executive committee adopted the decision on August 26, 2026; the money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1843.
The Ville de Québec is signing four agreements with recreation organizations in the Arrondissement des Rivières to run the day camp for the Programme Vacances-Été 2026.
Total grants paid: $1,742,286.14, taken from the borough's operating budget.
Breakdown: Loisirs Duberger-Les Saules $516,455.30, Loisirs Lebourgneuf $424,525.00, Loisirs Vanier $406,604.34, Loisirs et Sports Neufchâtel $394,701.50.
The money covers, among other things, support for children with special needs, supervisory staff, training (DAFA, first aid), transportation and the registration platform.
The organizations must follow a common set of specifications: registration, pricing, schedules and supervision of the children.
In 2025, the four camps had welcomed 2,810 children for $1,795,326.27 in grants.
The City is borrowing $2,500,000 to buy vehicles and motorized equipment to replace those that have reached the end of their useful life.
The loan will be paid back over five years, out of the City's general revenues.
The purchases include hydrocarbon-powered and electric vehicles, cars, vans, light and heavy trucks, tool vehicles, worksite equipment and accessories.
The money will also be used for professional and technical service contracts, hiring the required staff, software and shop equipment.
The City is taking $250,000 (10% of the expense) from its general fund, which will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The vehicles will be used throughout the territory falling under the City's jurisdiction; the funds are planned for 2026 and 2027 in the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is giving $150 to the organization Les Loisirs Montcalm inc., which acts as trustee for Mobilisation Haute-Ville.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, at the request of councillor Mélissa Coulombe-Leduc.
The request was for a sponsorship for the Fête du communautaire, on Saturday, May 23, 2026, at parc Saint-Sacrement (postponed to the 24th in case of rain).
The event introduces people to the community organizations of the Haute-Ville and has drawn about 500 people in previous years.
The cheque will be issued to 265, boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, in Québec.
The Ville de Québec is signing a three-year agreement with the organization Regroupement Action Prévention Jeunesse des Laurentides (R.A.P. Jeunesse).
It will pay the organization $17,500 per year in 2026, 2027 and 2028, for a total of $52,500, taken from the budget of the Arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The money is for street work and the Nomade mobile unit serving vulnerable young people aged 12 to 25 in Charlesbourg.
The organization has seven street workers and one support worker for the mobile unit; it carried out 2,123 interventions last year.

The 2026 payment will be made within 30 days after the agreement comes into force; the 2027 and 2028 payments are planned for around July 31, conditional on the organization reporting on its use of the funds.
The 2027 and 2028 amounts depend on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
The organization must mention the City's contribution in its official publications.
The City is awarding Fernand Gilbert ltée, of Chicoutimi, a contract worth $1,030,387.63 (before GST and QST) to rehabilitate sewer pipes.
The work consists of inserting a liner inside the pipes (light-cured lining) and re-drilling the service connections.
This work may take place anywhere within the territory of the city of Québec.
The company must also provide a report and an inspection video after the lining is installed.
Five companies submitted bids; the lowest bid was rejected because it was intended for the Ville de Trois-Rivières. Fernand Gilbert ltée submitted the lowest compliant price.
The net cost to the City is $1,081,778.21, paid through a loan by-law.
The executive committee adopted the decision on March 25, 2026.
City council adopts a policy setting out how the City's computer network can be accessed and the security rules that must be followed.
The policy sets minimum requirements: identity management, network separation, encryption, logging and monitoring.
It applies to employees, elected officials, police officers, interns, consultants, suppliers and partners who connect to the municipal network.
It covers the administrative network, the infrastructure networks (water, traffic lights, sensors), cameras, internal, guest and public Wi-Fi, telework and cloud computing.
The City justifies the policy by the growing number of computer connections with partners, in particular for the construction of the tramway.
The policy provides for controls, audits, a mechanism for exceptions and penalties in cases of non-compliance.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City is entrusting Carrefour Jeunesse Emploi de la Capitale Nationale with a "Service de nettoyage communautaire" (community cleaning service) for graffiti in 2026.
The cleaning is free and is offered to private properties, both residential and commercial.
The service covers the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou and a few particularly affected streets, with priority given to the Saint-Roch neighbourhood.
The agreement runs from April 6 to November 27, 2026, that is, 34 weeks.
The City is paying an estimated amount of $267,247, exempt from GST and QST.
There was no call for tenders: the law allows contracting directly with a non-profit organization.
The previous agreement with the organization ended on December 19, 2025.
The Ville de Québec is entrusting the Maison des métiers d'art de Québec with restoring ten oculi (circular openings) of the église Saint-Jean-Baptiste.
The contract is worth $172,625.65, exempt from GST and QST.
The work is being done as part of a workshop-school, to train artisans in heritage cabinetmaking.
The contract runs from its signing until September 30, 2027.
Funding comes in equal parts from a City loan by-law ($86,312.83) and financial assistance from the ministère de la Culture et des Communications ($86,312.82).
The contract is awarded by mutual agreement, under a rule that allows this method of awarding for contracts related to the cultural field.
The Charlesbourg borough council is renewing René Cloutier's term on the planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme), as a resident member.
His new term runs from February 27, 2026 to February 26, 2028, that is, two years.
The committee has six to eight members, including at least one and at most two elected officials from the borough council.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City is designating the pavillon Guy-Lafleur, on the ExpoCité site, as a major facility for the 2027 Canada Winter Games.
The pavilion's sign will bear the inscription "Hall des Jeux du Canada Games".
The Games' specifications require the host city to designate at least one major facility that will leave a lasting legacy for the community.
The designation will only hold if the Canada Games Council approves it; it is the body that confirms the facility meets the requirements.
The mayor will send the resolution to the Canada Games Council, after which the designation will be included in the Games' contractual and planning documents.
According to the document, the decision has no direct additional financial impact: the financial commitments have already been authorized.
The City authorizes councillor Catherine Vallières-Roland and Nicolas Roy to travel to Dunkerque, France, from November 1 to 7, 2026.
They will take part in the AIVP's 21st World Conference on Cities and Ports, held from November 3 to 6, 2026.
The City expects to spend $11,718.82 for flights, ground travel, registration and accommodation, reimbursed upon submission of receipts.
A difference of up to 10% of the authorized amount will be accepted without further authorization.
Before the conference, they will visit the North Sea Port in Belgium with representatives of the Port de Québec.
The purpose of the trip is to promote bringing a permanent North American representation of the AIVP to Québec and to publicize the Ville-Port vision adopted for the next 10 years.
The funds come from the operating budget of the Service de la coordination stratégique et relations internationales.
The City is authorizing the construction of a detached garage at 1303, rue Louis-Gauthier, in the Saint-Émile neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The garage will be 44.6 square metres, whereas the planning by-law does not allow a garage larger than 18 square metres to encroach on the secondary front yard.
Condition imposed: the garage must be built at least 10 metres from the front property line.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended granting the exemption on August 12, 2026.
The committee notes that the lot is a corner lot, which limits the possible locations, and that an 18-square-metre garage would be too small to park a car.
The new garage will replace a detached 28-square-metre shed; mature trees separate the property from the neighbour's.
The City is transferring $450,000 from the budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire to the six arrondissements to fund local events in 2026.
Each of the six arrondissements receives $75,000: La Cité-Limoilou, Les Rivières, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, Charlesbourg, Beauport and La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The money will go to the Programme de soutien financier aux événements locaux (local events financial support program).
It is the borough councils that will decide which events receive grants.
The amount is an estimate: a report on the adjustments made during the year will be presented later in 2026.
By comparison, $510,000 was transferred in March 2025 and $90,000 in November 2024.

The City will provide up to $197,191 in grants to recreation organizations for cultural mediation projects, under the Entente de développement culturel with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
Each project can receive a maximum of $15,000, and the grant can cover up to 100% of the project's cost.
To be eligible, organizations must be recognized by the City, submit their project by March 1, 2026 at the latest, and complete it by December 31, 2026 at the latest.
The projects take place in several boroughs: La Cité-Limoilou, Beauport, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge and La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The activities are aimed in particular at young people, seniors, mothers living in HLM housing, immigrants and people with disabilities, with workshops in visual arts, dance, writing or comics.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3367 tied to the Entente de développement culturel 2024-2026.
The Ville de Québec is hiring SÉMER, of Cacouna, to transport and biomethanize the biopulp from the agglomeration's Centre de récupération de la matière organique.
The agreement runs from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2029, for an estimated amount of $348,264 (plus GST and QST).
This service acts as a contingency plan: it is used when the Centre de biométhanisation de la matière organique cannot process all the materials.
The rate is $125.65 per metric tonne (transport and treatment included) for an estimated quantity of 2,700 tonnes; $151.65 per tonne if a second carrier is needed.
Additional fees apply if needed: $135.50 per hour for overtime labour and $365.00 per hour for a vacuum truck. A minimum of 30 tonnes is billed per transport.
The rates are fixed for 12 months, then indexed according to Statistics Canada's consumer price index.
The net agglomeration expense is estimated at $365,633.67, subject to approval of the 2027 to 2029 budgets.
The City is giving out $100,000 in grants to 13 cultural organizations in Québec to host artists in residence or in creation labs.
The amounts range from $5,000 to $10,000 per organization: among others, $10,000 to Groupe Danse Partout and to Productions Les Gros Becs, $9,500 to Coop Spira and to Productions Recto-Verso.
Other recipients: La Chambre blanche, Le Pantoum, Premier Acte, VU, Engramme, Les Éditions Intervention, Théâtre Le Diamant, La Charpente des fauves and Centre de création Limoilou.
About 75 artists from Québec are expected to be directly affected by the supported projects.
Each project must include at least one activity involving the Québec public.
The cap is $5,000 for an application with a single artistic project and $10,000 for several projects, up to 80% of the total cost.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3525 tied to the Politique culturelle 2025-2030.
The City confirms that infrastructure and redevelopment work is taking place on avenue des Hôtels, from about April 1 to December 31, 2026.
Businesses in the designated area may receive financial assistance provided under the support program related to major work, for the 2026 fiscal year.

The new order redraws the area covered so that it no longer overlaps the one for boulevard Laurier, which was defined for the TramCité project work: the two zones become neighbouring without overlapping.
An attached plan sets out the boundaries of the designated area and the area of influence around avenue des Hôtels.
This order replaces the one adopted on April 29, 2026 by the executive committee.
To be eligible, the work must last at least three consecutive months and significantly obstruct traffic.
The City wants to acquire a strip of land of about 17.6 square metres along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement with the owner or, failing that, by expropriation.
The land will be used to widen the right-of-way of 1re Avenue for the TramCité tramway project.
The owner has already been notified of the process, the next steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
The entire targeted property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $176,000, or $460.10 per square metre.
The City may abandon the expropriation if the project no longer needs the land.
The funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the structuring public transit network.
The City is replacing the numbers of three quartiers with their names in the by-law that divides its territory for the conseils de quartier.
Quartier 4-2, in Charlesbourg, becomes quartier d'Orsainville.
Quartier 5-1, in Beauport, becomes quartier de Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux.
Quartier 5-4, in Beauport, becomes quartier du Vieux-Bourg.
The maps and the descriptions of the boundaries of the conseils de quartier are replaced by a version that takes the new names into account.
These names were already in use for the conseils de quartier created in 2022 and 2023.
The City wants to acquire, by agreement or by expropriation, a piece of land and two servitudes along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The land in question is about 64.20 square metres and would be used to widen the 1re Avenue right-of-way.
The two permanent public utility servitudes, of about 98.40 and 43.10 square metres, would be used to relocate conduits and networks.
The owner has already been informed of the process, the upcoming steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings, and to withdraw from them if the project no longer needs this land.
The entire property (land only) is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $303,000, or $348.48 per square metre.
The money comes from the urban agglomeration loan by-law related to the structuring public transit network.
The Ville de Québec is entrusting the organization Loisirs Duberger-Les Saules inc. with the supervision of recreational and sports facilities and equipment in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The agreement covers the period from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027 and replaces the previous one, which ends on April 30, 2026.
The contract amounts to $477,110.84 (plus GST and QST), for a net expense of $500,906.74 for the City.
The funds are used in particular for community recreation centres, parks, outdoor and indoor skating rinks, indoor pools and sports fields.
The money comes from the operating budget of the arrondissement des Rivières; the 2027 portion depends on the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The contract is awarded by mutual agreement, a rule that allows a contract to be awarded directly to a non-profit organization.
The City is changing the rules for the question period at city council: priority will now go to people who live in Québec.
Owners of a building or occupants of a business establishment in Québec also have priority, even if they do not live there.
To benefit from this, a person who is not domiciled in Québec must enter the address of their building or business establishment in the register.
Speaking time is granted in the order of registration in the register, where people write down their name, address, city of residence and the subject of their question.
The chair of the meeting may change the order of speakers in order to group together questions on the same subject.
The by-law comes into force in accordance with the law.
The City is renewing the lease of a space at 2, rue Monseigneur-Marc-Leclerc, in Beauport, which houses the Fernand-Dumont service point of the Bibliothèque de Québec.
The lease runs for five years, from September 1, 2025 to August 31, 2030, with an option to renew for five years.
The rent for the first year is $50,966.40, plus taxes. It was $39,840.72 for the previous year.
The rent will be indexed each year according to the Consumer Price Index plus 1%.
The owner is the company 9266-4812 Québec inc.; the rented space measures 132.94 square metres and janitorial services are included in the rent.
The former lease had expired on August 31, 2025; the new lease applies retroactively as of that date.
For the period from September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2026, the City expects to pay $71,879.55 (net of taxes), of which $20,913.89 has already been paid.
The Ville de Québec is entrusting the organization Loisirs Brio with the cleaning and sanitation of certain recreational or sports facilities and equipment in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The agreement covers the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, that is, 12 months.
The contract amounts to $259,677.50 (plus GST and QST); the net cost to the City is $272,628.92.
The amounts break down as follows: $204,565.76 in 2026 and $68,063.16 in 2027 (net of taxes).
The 2027 portion depends on the approval of the 2027 budget by the competent authorities.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders, an option allowed by law for non-profit organizations.
The previous agreement with Loisirs Brio ended on March 31, 2026.

The City is authorizing the construction of a five-storey building with about 40 housing units and offices at 780, avenue du Brabant (quartier du Plateau), even though the zone prohibits residential use and limits buildings to four storeys.
The project includes underground parking with 39 spaces and 17 outdoor spaces, which is one space per housing unit instead of the 1.2 spaces required.
The project also departs from the minimum front and side setbacks (6 m and 3.5 m) and from the minimum distance of 35 m from the centre line of autoroute Duplessis.

Following the public consultation of June 15, 2026, the City is adding a condition to protect the privacy of neighbours on rue Cavelier: on the rear side of the building, only alcove balconies with no projection are allowed, with frosted or opaque guardrails covering at least 90% of their surface.
Anyone who does not comply with the conditions of the resolution faces a fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.
The urban agglomeration council must approve the resolution as consistent with the land use planning and development plan; this decision cannot be subject to a referendum.
The City is sending an engineer, Eric Taylor, to the Association des transports du Canada convention in Winnipeg, from October 4 to 7, 2026.
The City will reimburse his expenses (registration, travel, accommodation, meals and related costs) up to $3,887, upon presentation of receipts.
Jérôme Nadeau will go in his place if he withdraws.
Québec was selected for the convention's official program to present its experience in rolling out the Corridors VivaCité évolutifs.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de la planification de l'aménagement et de l'environnement.
An overrun of no more than 10% of the authorized amount is accepted without further authorization.
The City is asking the ministère de la Culture et des Communications for $1,196,460 to reinforce the two bell towers of the église du Très-Saint-Sacrement, at 1330, chemin Sainte-Foy.
The project costs $6,482,047 in total: $5,196,460 comes from the Government of Québec (including $4M already granted in 2022) and $1,285,587 from the City.
The City will pay its $1,285,587 share as a grant to the Fabrique de la paroisse de Saint-Pierre-Julien-Eymard, the owner of the church, with no matching amount from the government.
Closed to worship since 2019 and classified as a heritage building in 2022, the church will be able to reopen to the public once the work is done, planned for 2026.
The work on the two bell towers will be carried out at the same time to reduce costs.
The fabrique is working with the community to define options for repurposing the building.
The City is paying $353,154.75 to Environnement Viridis inc. to settle a lawsuit out of court, with neither party admitting liability.
The dispute concerned three contracts awarded in December 2020 to recover value from the biosolid digestates produced at the Centre de biométhanisation des matières organiques (CBMO).
Viridis was claiming $486,156.50 plus taxes: $222,706.50 in lost profits for the months remaining on the contract and $263,450 related to the small quantity of digestates processed at start-up.
The contracts, delayed by the commissioning of the CBMO, began on June 23, 2023; the conflict broke out in the fall of 2023 over the quantity and quality of the digestates.
The settlement depends on Viridis signing a final and general release in favour of the City.
The sum of $320,321.86 (net of taxes) comes from the urban agglomeration jurisdiction budget set aside for lawsuits.
The City's lawyers, Giasson et associés, will sign the agreement documents on behalf of the City.
The arrondissement des Rivières is amending its planning by-law to allow outdoor storage at 1300, rue du Blizzard (lot 4 575 260), in the Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf neighbourhood.

The authorization covers the storage of vehicles weighing 4,500 kilograms or more, equipment more than 3 metres high, tool-vehicles or machinery, as well as goods or materials, in the side and rear yards.

The request comes from the Société québécoise des infrastructures, which is relocating and setting up the facilities of the ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs.
The equipment covered includes trailers, bear cages, trailers for ATVs, snowmobiles and boats, gasoline cabinets and pickup trucks.
A fence at least 2 metres high is required around the outdoor storage area.
The authorization is granted only for this property, in the form of an occupancy permission, and not for the entire commercial zone 21753Cc.

The conseil de quartier de Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf will give its opinion and hold the public consultation meeting; interested people will have seven days after that meeting to submit their written comments. The by-law cannot be subject to a referendum.
The City is adding mandatory stops on chemin du Pavillon, at the exit of parking lot no. 3 of parc de la Plage-Jacques-Cartier (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The stop applies to drivers as well as cyclists.
The road markings will be redone: removal of the right-hand lane heading south, hatching of the no-parking zone, stop lines and a new pedestrian crossing at the intersection.
The change aims to make access to the park's parking lot safer, as requested by the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The section of chemin du Pavillon south of rue Vautelet is only open to traffic during the summer season, when an employee directs drivers to the parking lots.
The City is asking the main provincial political parties to hold at least one leaders' debate on its territory during the fall 2026 provincial election campaign.
The City will also reach out to the broadcasters involved so that this debate takes place.
The proposal comes from councillor Stéphane Lachance, tabled at the city council meeting of June 16, 2026.

The wording of the proposal is amended: the request applies to the territory of the city of Québec, rather than the whole Capitale-Nationale region, and is addressed first to the political parties rather than to the broadcasters.
The City is relying on its status as a national capital, which makes its territory the preferred and priority location for important political meetings.
No amount is associated with this decision.
The City is authorizing an expense of $3,500,000 to provide financial help to businesses affected by major infrastructure work, starting in 2026 and for the following years.
The program applies to businesses whose access is disrupted for more than three months by construction work, and it is expanded to areas located along the route of the TramCité project.
Each eligible business can receive up to $30,000 per year of work.
Organizations authorized to promote the affected commercial streets can also receive up to $30,000 per year of work.
The City is borrowing the $3,500,000 and will pay it back over five years, out of the urban agglomeration's general revenues.
An amount of $350,000 (10% of the expense) is being taken from the general fund and will be paid back when the by-law comes into force.
The City is banning parking on the west side of rue Raymond-Daveluy, between rue Albani and route Sainte-Geneviève, from November 15 to March 31.
The ban covers a 98-metre stretch, starting 40 metres north of rue Albani and going north.
This measure removes 11 parking spaces during the winter period.
The goal: to let snow removal equipment get through, because parked vehicles were getting in the way of winter maintenance.
The area affected is the Arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles, Loretteville-Les Châtels district.
According to the document, the parking occupancy rate in this area is average.
The City is awarding Les Entreprises L.T. ltée the contract to supply ready-mix cement concrete and non-shrink backfill, for an estimated amount of $468,248 (plus taxes).

The concrete will be used to maintain building structures and engineering structures throughout the territory of the city of Québec, as well as in certain areas of L'Ancienne-Lorette and Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures.
The contract runs from the date it is awarded until April 19, 2027.
The net cost to the City is estimated at $491,601, once the QST refund is taken into account.
Only one company submitted a bid; after negotiation, it lowered its price from $470,680 to $468,248.

The selected price is 33% higher than the estimate made by the requesting department ($352,000), an estimate based on 2025 prices that did not take into account the increase in demand for concrete or the rise in oil prices.
The contract remains conditional on the funds being approved when the 2027 budget is adopted.
The executive committee takes note of the quarterly report on the Fonds local d'investissement (FLI) for the period from October 1 to December 31, 2025.
Only one loan was approved during the quarter: $300,000 to RIG Craftor inc., to sell its products outside Quebec.
No loan was approved under the emergency assistance program for small and medium-sized businesses (PAUPME) during the period.
For all of 2025, the FLI granted $1,320,000 in disbursed financing, and the fund's balance stood at $6,104,666.99 as of December 31, 2025.
The PAUPME program received about $5 million in loan repayments in 2025, bringing its balance from $18,566,376.62 down to $12,717,536.98.
This quarterly filing is required by the by-law on the delegation of powers of the executive committee.
The City is tabling before city council the list of its contracts of more than $2,000 that total more than $25,000 with the same supplier, from January 1 to March 31, 2026.
This list covers purchase orders, agreements, card purchases and invoices processed in a decentralized way.
Starting April 1, 2026, with the coming into force of the Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux, the City no longer has to present this list to elected officials each month.
The information will instead be published on the Ville de Québec website.
Council is only taking note of the list: no new spending is authorized here.
The City is authorizing a craft textile printing business at 14794D, boulevard de la Colline, in the Saint-Émile neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The printing activity will take place inside the building only.
According to the analysis, the new use will not increase vehicle traffic on the site, and water management is already provided there.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended approval on May 27, 2026.
The decision falls to the borough council (resolution CA6-2026-0059).
The City is creating a facilities manager position (class 5) at the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The position is attached to the Section Est of the Division des installations et des équipements.
Pay follows the salary scale for management jobs.
The money needed, including employee benefits, is already provided for in the budget tied to operating the community recreation centres.
The creation of the position was authorized by the Direction générale and adopted by the executive committee on August 26, 2026.
The City is closing 26 loan by-laws adopted before 2022, for which the work is now finished.
Authorized spending totalled $188,509,200.00, while the work cost $167,868,694.26: the City is cancelling $20,640,505.74 in spending power.
It is also cancelling $41,314,900.00 in loan balances that were never used, out of an authorized borrowing power of $188,509,200.00.
These closures leave $1,198,076.40 available, which is not assigned to any project for now.
The projects concerned include buildings, industrial parks, land decontamination, the centre de glaces, the écoquartier de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres and the plateau centre de Sainte-Foy.
The City says these closures do not affect the carrying out of the projects planned in the 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
It is asking the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation to adjust its records.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 1195, rue des Citronniers, in the Val-Bélair neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The exemption allows a single-dwelling house to be built on a lot that is currently vacant.
The main façade may be located 8.81 metres from the front setback, whereas the planning by-law sets a maximum of 3 metres.
The lot has an irregular, pointed shape, on the outside of a traffic circle; the project provides for a building with a garden level.
According to the analysis, the exemption does not increase risks to public safety or public health, and the lot is not in a steep-slope area.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended acceptance on May 27, 2026.
The City is paying $2,627,111 in 2026 to the eight federated community recreation centres in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou to support their mission.

The amounts by organization: Patro Roc-Amadour $645,116; YWCA de Québec $381,818; Patro Laval $341,729; Centre Mgr Marcoux $286,224; Centre Jean-Guy Drolet $259,066; Centre Durocher $250,817; Loisirs Saint-Sacrement $239,134; Loisirs Montcalm $223,207.
2026 becomes a transition year: the 2025 grants are renewed and indexed by 2%, rather than calculated using the new grid of 14 indicators.
The eleven federated centres asked for this status quo because the new grid created gaps that could harm the finances of some centres.
Discussions will continue until June 2026 with a view to signing multi-year agreements.
The program's total envelope reaches $3,693,688 for 2026, including the centres in Lebourgneuf, Beauport and Charlesbourg.
The federated centres have 4,107 volunteers, 197,280 volunteer hours, 96,141 activity registrations and 203,133 people reached through drop-in access.
The arrondissement de Charlesbourg is giving out $282,522 in grants to 38 organizations in the area.
The money is used to pay operating expenses (day-to-day costs) of organizations recognized by the City.
The applications had been submitted on February 20, 2026; some grants correspond to the 2nd or 3rd year of support already granted.
The amounts range from $500 (Club d'âge d'or Bourg-Royal) to $18,632 (Vivre Grand); several organizations receive $15,000, including the Patro de Charlesbourg and the Centre Signes d'Espoir.
The organizations supported work with seniors, families, youth, mental health, sports and music.
The money comes from the operating budget of the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The borough council adopted the decision on April 28, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption to the house at 772, rue De Longpré, in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough).
