The house is too close to the street and to the neighbour: 5.5 metres for the front setback instead of the required 6.0 metres, and 1.94 metres for the side setback instead of 2.0 metres.
These distances are now deemed to comply with the borough's planning by-law; the building therefore does not have to be moved or demolished.
According to the analysis, the situation has existed since 1955 and no complaint has been recorded.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on May 12, 2026.

The City is authorizing a business that sells or rents small vehicles and light vehicles at 14310, boulevard de la Colline, in the Saint-Émile neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The authorization goes through the conditional uses mechanism, which allows a use that is not otherwise permitted at that location.
The activities will take place inside the building and outside, on a paved section of the lot.
The analysis notes that the activities are located far from the shore of the watercourse, at the back of the lot.
Vehicle parking will have to meet the standards that apply to the drinking water intake watersheds of the rivières Saint-Charles and Montmorency, for a parking area of more than 150 m².
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the application on May 27, 2026.

The City is awarding Csintrans inc. (Montréal) a contract for the pooling and car-sharing of light vehicles, from April 1, 2026 to September 30, 2032, for an estimated amount of $1,638,332 before taxes.
The contract is divided into two phases: a pilot project from April 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027, then a gradual rollout from October 1, 2027 to September 30, 2032.
The City keeps the right not to go ahead with the rollout, depending on the results of the pilot project.
The solution covers about 700 light vehicles in the City's fleet and includes a booking platform, on-board telemetry, training, technical support and performance reports.
The rollout phase includes an option to renew for two periods of 18 months and an annual increase based on the Consumer Price Index.
The net expense is estimated at $1,720,043.81, subject to approval of the 2027 to 2032 budgets.
Two bids were received: Csintrans inc. ($1,638,332) and Communauto inc. ($1,874,413.92); Csintrans obtained the highest final score, 84.58 out of 100.
The Ville de Québec is giving $10,000 to the organization JeunesExplo - Stages d'un jour for the 2026 edition of the « Jeunes explorateurs d'un jour » program.
The organization sets up one-day workplace internships for young people, tied to staying in school and career guidance.
According to the document, more than 30,000 young people in Québec have done such an internship since 2005, in nearly 3,500 organizations, including several hundred in City departments.
The City says it wants to get young people interested in its jobs early, in a context of labour shortage.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service des ressources humaines.
The City had given $10,000 for the 2025 edition and $7,000 for the 2024 and 2022 editions.
The City will pay $75,000 to the Club de tennis Rouge et Or de l'Université Laval to hold the "Challenger Banque Nationale de Québec" tournament.
The event will take place from August 17 to 23, 2026, at the new Centre de tennis de l'Université Laval.
The men's tennis tournament is sanctioned by the ATP and organized with Tennis Canada and the Service des activités sportives de l'Université Laval.
Tickets are paid, but the first day of qualifying is free; free activities (introductory clinics, meet-and-greets with athletes, family entertainment) will be held outside the Centre de tennis.
The grant represents 4.7% of the event's projected budget, estimated at $1,579,000.

The payment is made in three instalments: $45,000 after signing, $22,500 after the event and $7,500 when the financial statements and the final report are submitted ($7,500 planned in the 2027 budget).
The support is conditional on a sufficient contribution from the other partners for the event to take place.
The Ville de Québec is selling a vacant lot of 3,940.6 m² in the parc industriel de Beauport, in the expanding southern sector, along rue Margaret-Fraser.
The buyer is Gestion immobilière les Renards inc., for $634,450 plus taxes, or $161 per square metre.
The buyer has 24 months to begin construction of a building, and 120 days to carry out its environmental checks.
The lot will be used to relocate and expand Éclat Audiovisuel inc., an audiovisual equipment rental company, which will rent the premises.
The project calls for an 800 m² building, an investment of about $2.5M and the creation of 4 jobs.
The sale is made without legal warranty: the buyer takes on the environmental risks and the condition of the soil.
The $634,450 will be paid into the City's general fund.
The Ville de Québec is authorizing spending of $2,605,000 for work on buildings, parks and recreational facilities, and is borrowing the same amount over 10 years.
The money may be used for professional and technical services contracts, hiring staff, paying out grants, and buying goods, buildings and easements.
The work covered includes construction, renovation, repair, landscaping, lighting, paving and accessibility.
The projects affect the entire territory under the City's jurisdiction, on sites that it owns, rents or manages in partnership.
The funds come from the 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program and are planned for the years 2026 to 2028: $2,500,000 to carry out the projects and $105,000 to study them.
An amount of $260,500 (10% of the spending) is taken from the general fund and will be paid back to it when the by-law comes into force.
The City may acquire, by agreement or by expropriation, any building or easement needed for the work.
The City is awarding the rebuilding of the écocentre Val-Bélair, in the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough, to Groupe FJH Construction inc., of Victoriaville.
The contract is worth $2,845,462.89 before taxes; the net cost to the City comes to $2,987,380.35.
The work includes demolishing the existing facilities, excavation, retaining walls, replacing culverts, sewer, water main and road work, paving and landscaping.
Fourteen companies submitted bids; Groupe FJH submitted the lowest price, and all bids met the requirements.
The department requesting the work had estimated it at $5,379,682.85 before taxes, which is 47.1% more than the winning bid.
The money comes from an agglomeration loan by-law set aside for work in the écocentres.
The executive committee was to decide on March 25, 2026.
The City is banning parking at all times on chemin Saint-Barthélemy, in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles (Loretteville-Les Châtels district).
North side: ban over 20 metres starting from boulevard de la Colline, heading west.
South side: ban over 135 metres starting from boulevard de la Colline, heading west.
About 13 parking spaces are being removed.
The change is meant to let heavy vehicles through to the storage site at 1811, chemin Saint-Barthélemy, where access had been blocked since a business opened at 1785.
The roadway is between 7 and 8.5 metres wide, and parking there had not been regulated until now.
The City is accepting a US$5,000 prize awarded by the Fédération internationale des associations et institutions de bibliothèques (IFLA).
This amount comes with the title of "Public Library of the Year" awarded on August 18, 2025 to the bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy, at the IFLA congress in Astana, Kazakhstan.

The jury highlighted the renovation and expansion of the building, how it fits into the Saint-Roch neighbourhood, its services (MédiaLab, studios, creation rooms) and its approach focused on accessibility and inclusion.
The money will be paid into the City's general fund.
According to the document, accepting this amount does not create any financial commitment for the City.
The City is authorizing the creation of a neighbourhood council (conseil de quartier) in neighbourhood 5-2, in the arrondissement de Beauport.
The new body will be named « Conseil de quartier de Saint-Michel »; the name « des Patriotes » had also been suggested.
The decision follows a request from citizens and a public meeting held on June 3, 2026 at the Centre de loisirs de La Ribambelle (333, rue Perroteau), where about 46 people attended.
In the secret ballot: 45 ballots handed out, 39 in favour of creating the council, 2 against, no ballots rejected or cancelled (4 people did not vote).
No one spoke for or against the creation at the meeting.
The city clerk will send the resolution to the Registraire des entreprises, to the arrondissement de Beauport and to the Service des relations citoyennes et des communications.
An organizational meeting of the neighbourhood council must be held within 60 days of receiving the resolution.
The City is awarding Les Entreprises P.N.P. inc. a $361,442.50 contract (before taxes) to redevelop the pedestrian accesses of the jardins Marie-Charlotte-Bédard.
The site involved is that of the Moulin des Jésuites, at 7960, boulevard Henri-Bourassa, in the Charlesbourg borough.
The work includes stone screening paths, stone paving, concrete surfaces, wooden terraces and fences, sandboxes, path lighting, furniture and landscaping.
The project also includes the recovery and showcasing of a millstone, as well as work for stormwater management.
Seven bids were received; the one selected is the lowest compliant bid, 0.2% below the City's estimate ($362,149.39).
The net expense for the City is $379,469.44, funded through a cultural development agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The City is signing a $2,000,000 contract (plus GST and QST) with ESRI Canada limitée for the use of ESRI products, from February 15, 2026 to February 14, 2029.
This software is used to run the City's geographic information systems, including the interactive map used by employees and citizens.
The contract is meant to allow a new geomatics ecosystem to be rolled out over the coming year, to replace the current one, which is considered to be at the end of its useful life.
No call for tenders was held: the City states that ESRI Canada is the only supplier authorized to offer this type of enterprise licence agreement.
The net expense is $2,099,750, of which $398,952.50 is billed to the Réseau de transport de la Capitale, which has been using ESRI sub-licences since 2011.
The amounts planned for 2027, 2028 and 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
The contract includes registrations for the Esri and Esri Canada user conferences, which the City hands out to its employees.
The City is amending its by-law on elm trees so that it applies to all elm trees, diseased or not, in the territory of the agglomeration of Québec.

Anyone who cuts down an elm tree will have to treat the wood, the debris and the stump using a "compliant process": chipping the logs into wood chips, burying them under at least 15 cm of soil, or removing the bark (including the first centimetre of sapwood) and then chipping or burying the bark residue.
Cutting will have to be done by cutting completely through the trunk, perpendicular to its axis, as close to the ground as possible.
The rules will also apply to elm wood and debris that come off the tree because of wind, the weight of snow or otherwise.

Fines go from a range of $300 to $1,000 to a fixed amount of $1,000 for an individual, and from $500 to $2,000 to a fixed amount of $2,000 for a business. The amounts double in the case of a repeat offence, and each day that an offence continues counts as a separate offence.

Employees of the Division de la foresterie urbaine et de l'horticulture will be able to visit land and buildings at any reasonable hour, take photos, collect samples and require documents; owners, tenants and occupants will have to let them in.
The document states that there is no financial impact for the City.
The City is giving $94,000 to the Alliance Arc-en-ciel de Québec for the "Fierté de Québec" 2026 event, plus free city services worth up to $20,000, for a total of $114,000.
The event runs from September 4 to 6, 2026, mainly at place D'Youville and on rue Saint-Jean, in the Faubourg area.
The outdoor activities (stages, shows, talks, solidarity march) are free for the public.
The grant covers 18% of the event's budget, estimated at $523,000.
The funding depends on other partners contributing enough for the event to take place.
The payment is made in two parts: $84,600 in 2026 and $9,400 in 2027, subject to the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The free services come from building management, public works and the Service de police (work time and equipment loans).

The Ville de Québec is signing a confidentiality agreement with Ciment Québec inc. so that information can be exchanged with a view to buying all or part of a piece of land (lot 1 216 823) owned by the company.
The land in question is located in the area of rue Chabanel, near chemin Royal and boulevard des Chutes.
The City wants to carry out quarry restoration there in order to deposit soils of categories MGR, <A and A-B coming from its worksites.
The agreement sets out how the shared information may be used and the measures to be taken to keep it confidential.
Confidentiality applies for five years after the end of the discussions, and with no time limit for trade secrets.
The agreement does not require the City to buy the land: any purchase would have to be authorized by the City's decision-making bodies.
The document does not mention any amount or financial impact.
The City is refusing a minor exemption request for the Costco located at 3233, avenue Watt, in the arrondissement of Sainte-Foy/Sillery/Cap-Rouge.
The applicant wanted to install signs of 2.2 square metres per side on the roof edge of the gas pump islands, whereas the by-law limits the area to 1 square metre.
The applicant cited the rules of the Office québécois de la langue française, which require the word "Essence" to be twice as large as the name "Costco Wholesale".
The City replies that a sign meeting the 1 square metre limit is still possible and that there is therefore no serious harm.
The City points out that this area limit applies everywhere on the territory of the city of Québec.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had recommended refusal on January 13, 2026; the borough council made its decision on February 9, 2026.
The City is amending its by-law on ethics and rules of conduct for its employees.
The values of "responsibility" and "courage" are being replaced by three new values: being visionary, committed and agile.
This change is part of the ongoing review of the City's mission, vision, values and strategic planning.

The by-law also updates the names of some units: the "Service de la culture et des relations internationales" becomes the "Service de la coordination stratégique et des relations internationales", and the "Division des conditions de travail" becomes the "Division des relations de travail".
Before final adoption by city council, the law requires a notice of motion, a consultation with employees and the publication of a public notice.
The document reports no financial impact.
The City is amending its 2018 agreement with Maison de Lauberivière, which had received a $1,300,000 grant to build a 7-storey building with 131 rooms and 18 housing units at 485, rue du Pont.
As security for this grant, the organization had granted the City a mortgage, published in February 2021.
The City agrees to give up its mortgage rank to the Société d'habitation du Québec, which requires first rank for its loan granted under AccèsLogis.
The agreement also adds the possibility for the City to release its mortgage once all the conditions of the agreement have been met.
In both cases, the organization must not be in default, must pay the fees, and must have the draft deed approved by the City.
Follow-up on the agreement is entrusted to the division du développement des milieux de vie, de l'habitation et de l'immobilier.
The City is hiring David Dionne as assistant director – organizational support and community relations at the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
His annual salary is set at $186,101 (2026 scale), with the raises and pay progression provided for senior managers.
The position was filled through an internal and external competition; he previously held the position of director of the Division du contrôle du milieu.
The contract is for an indefinite term: the employee must give 4 weeks' notice to leave, and the City must give 3 to 12 months' notice.
The City may authorize him to use an unmarked vehicle from the Service de protection contre l'incendie, given the requirement to respond quickly outside regular hours.
The funds, including employee benefits, are already provided for in the fire protection budget.
The urban agglomeration council adopted the decision on July 8, 2026.
The City is amending the planning by-law for the arrondissement de Beauport for several zones in the quartier Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux, mostly located outside the urbanization perimeter.

The zone boundaries are being redrawn to match the land use designations in the Plan directeur d'aménagement et de développement and the urbanization perimeter in the development plan (schéma d'aménagement).
The areas affected are near boulevard Raymond, chemin du Silex, rue de Chasseforêt, boulevard Lloyd-Welch, boulevard Louis-XIV and rue Seigneuriale.

In zone 51032Fb (between boulevard Lloyd-Welch and rue des Trois-Saults), crop farming without livestock and local and regional outdoor recreational facilities become permitted, as well as a trailer for an outdoor recreation use.
Two new zones are being created north of boulevard Louis-XIV, west of rue du Sénégal, where only single-family detached houses will be allowed.
The conseil de quartier de Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux will be consulted and will hold the public meeting; residents will have seven days after that meeting to send their comments in writing.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The City is granting an exemption to the owner of 4030, boulevard des Cimes (Des Châtels district, La Haute-Saint-Charles borough) to install an in-ground pool.
The pool may be built in the front yard, which the planning by-law normally prohibits.
The owner will be allowed to install an opaque 2-metre-high diamond-mesh wire fence around the pool, while the limit in a front yard is 1.2 metres.
Conditions: the pool must be at least 4.5 metres from the sidewalk and the fence at least 3 metres, along boulevard des Cimes and rue John-F.-Kennedy.

According to the analysis, the triangular shape of the lot and the position of the house leave little space in the back yard; the angle of the two streets (134 degrees) means the lot is classified as a corner lot.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme said it was in favour of the request on January 28, 2026.
The City is giving $330,000 to six organizations for adapted day camps in 2026, the same amount as in 2025 and 2024.
The grants go to Laura Lémerveil ($112,100), Autisme Québec ($69,600), Maison des lucioles ($45,650), Adaptavie ($45,000), Le Patro Roc-Amadour ($40,000) and Le Sillage ($17,650).
The camps are for children aged 5 to 12 and, in the case of Laura Lémerveil and the Patro Roc-Amadour, for young people aged 13 to 21 living in Québec.
In 2025, 170 children and 63 teenagers from the city took part in these camps.

Each organization must sign an agreement: the City's support cannot exceed 50% of the project cost, the camps must last at least 7 weeks at 35 hours per week, and spots are held until May 1 for children referred by the City.
The organizations receive 90% of the amount as soon as the grant is approved, and the balance after their accountability report is checked; the report must be submitted before October 12, 2026.
The City is renewing the grants as they are because its review of funding criteria is not finished; 2026 serves as a transition year.
The City is removing the no-parking-at-any-time restriction in front of 130, 54e Rue Est, in Charlesbourg (district Saint-Rodrigue).
The change affects the south side of 54e Rue Est, between 1re Avenue and 3e Avenue Est.
About two on-street parking spaces become available as a result.
The request comes from the new occupants of 130, 54e Rue Est; the restriction had been requested by the former owner.
According to the analysis by the Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente, removing it has no effect on traffic or on safety along this stretch of street.
Another no-parking zone remains on the south side of the street.
The Ville de Québec is authorizing spending of $1,200,000 to continue in 2026 the replacement of lead drinking water service lines, both public and private.

This amount covers the work, professional and technical services contracts, the hiring of staff, the purchase of buildings and easements (by mutual agreement or by expropriation) and the payment of grants to owners.
The City is borrowing the same amount of $1,200,000, repayable over fifteen years, and will apply any grant received to reducing it.
The work may take place anywhere in the territory falling under the city's jurisdiction.
An amount of $120,000 (10% of the expenditure) is taken from the general fund before the by-law comes into force; the fund will be reimbursed afterwards.
The expenditure changes from local jurisdiction to mixed jurisdiction for $300,000, which changes how the costs are shared between the city and the agglomeration.
The arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is transferring $27,000 from its operating budget to the budget for floral maintenance, which is managed by the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The money will be used to add flower basins and planters in the Saint-Roch neighbourhood, as part of the "Saint-Roch centre-ville attractif" project.
The document states that this transfer will have no impact on the activities of the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The borough council adopted the decision (resolution CA1-2026-0032) on February 23, 2026.
The City wants to obtain a permanent public utility servitude on a piece of land along boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, near avenue Cartier, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The area involved is about 3.1 square metres, on part of lot 5 750 207.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement or, if no agreement is reached, by expropriation; the owner has already been informed of the process.
The servitude is used to move public utility conduits and networks for the tramway project (TramCité).
The Service des affaires juridiques may withdraw the proceedings if the project no longer needs the servitude.
The entire property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $575,000, or $1,282.34 per square metre.
The funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the structuring public transit network.
The City is awarding Groupe Colas Québec inc. (Lévis) the contract to rebuild the underground infrastructure on rue des Récollets, for $2,137,000 before taxes.
The work involves rue des Récollets, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The project calls for rebuilding the drinking water pipes and the storm and sanitary sewers, plus installing a temporary water system.
The roadway, signage and urban landscaping will be restored.
Seven companies submitted bids; Colas offered the lowest price, 26.4% below the City's estimate ($2,902,076.75).
The net cost to the City, after recovering the QST, comes to $2,243,582.87, funded through a loan by-law.
The contract includes clauses to adjust for asphalt and fuel prices.
The Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough is giving $500 to the organization "Notre jardin du vivre ensemble".
The grant comes from the borough council's budget, under the activity "Supporting borough councils".
The request came from councillor Gabriel Dusablon.
According to the analysis, the organization meets the criteria for this type of grant and the funds are available.
The borough council adopted resolution CA3-2026-0114 on July 6, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is changing the zoning of seven zones in the Vieux-Bourg neighbourhood, in the arrondissement de Beauport, along avenue Royale.
In six of these zones, commercial tourist accommodation (C10 uses) will only be allowed on the second floor and above, so no longer on the ground floor.
In zone 54093Mb, between rue de la Madone and autoroute Félix-Leclerc, commercial tourist accommodation is removed completely: more than 50% of the dwellings there are single-family homes.
The City says it wants to protect existing housing in a context of a housing crisis; the change responds to recommendations from the neighbourhood council.
The conseil de quartier du Vieux-Bourg will hold the public consultation meeting, and interested people will have seven days after it to submit their comments in writing.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; the borough council was aiming for March 12, 2026 for the next step.
The City is awarding Hamel Construction inc. the infrastructure work on chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois, for $9,870,000 before taxes.
The work is located in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge and is part of the TramCité project.
The work includes: complete reconstruction of the drinking water and sewer systems and of the urban utility networks, and the relocation or bracing of existing services.
Also planned: repairs to the roadway, sidewalks, bike paths and signage.
Eight companies submitted bids, all of them compliant; Hamel Construction offered the lowest price, 24.5% below the City's estimate ($13,080,291).
The net cost to the City comes to $10,362,266.25, funded through loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342.
The contract includes price adjustment clauses for asphalt and fuel.
Québec is extending its agreement with Sherbrooke by 12 months, from January 1 to December 31, 2027, for the management of the RH-PAIE payroll and human resources system (VIP software).
Sherbrooke will pay $12,768.23 per month (plus taxes), at the end of each month in 2027, which represents about $153,218.76 for the year. This rate includes a 3% indexation.
Additional services, such as development support, will be billed at $136.17 per hour (plus taxes).
The costs of shared computer development work will be split as follows: Québec 63%, Sherbrooke 20%, Lévis 17%.
If the licence costs for the data extraction solution (SAP) go up, Québec will be able to bill the increase back to Sherbrooke.
The agreement may be extended a second and final time by 12 months afterwards.
The amounts received will go to the City's general fund, with no administration fees added.
The City is tabling the annual report of the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale, which funds its Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, for the period from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026.
During that period, close to $25.37 million was paid out to 196 projects in the urban agglomeration of Québec.
These projects generated more than $72.66 million in investments and involved more than 1,767 jobs.
The Government of Quebec delegated $154,277,465 to the City from 2018 to 2026, including $19,603,739 for the year 2025-2026.
The money is used for non-repayable contributions: entrepreneurship grants, and support for innovation, productivity, trade, the food system and structuring projects.
Eligible sectors include agri-food, digital, manufacturing, optics-photonics, life sciences, clean technologies, retail trade and food service.
The executive committee is taking note of the report; no new spending is decided here.
Québec is extending its agreement with Lévis for the RH-PAIE payroll and human resources system (VIP software package) by 12 months, from January 1 to December 31, 2027.
Lévis will pay $12,768.23 per month (plus taxes) for the main services, an amount that includes a 3% annual indexation.
Québec will take in about $153,218.76 plus taxes in 2027, with no administration fees; the money will go to the general fund.
Additional services, such as development support, will be billed at $136.17 per hour plus taxes.
The costs of shared computer developments will be split as follows: Québec 63%, Sherbrooke 20%, Lévis 17%.
If the licence costs for the data extraction solution (SAP) go up, Québec will be able to pass the increase on to Lévis.
A second 12-month extension remains possible after this one; Lévis has already agreed to 2027.
The City is applying for financial assistance from the ministère de l'Éducation for a project at the parc naturel du Mont-Bélair.
The project includes a walking trail linking avenue de la Montagne Ouest to the top of the mountain.
It also includes the creation of an additional parking lot at the park.
The City commits to paying its share of the project's eligible costs.
The application is being made through component 2 "Infrastructures de plein air" of a program that ends on March 31, 2027.
Carolyne Larouche, director of three boroughs, is authorized to act on the City's behalf in this matter.
The executive committee adopted the decision on April 15, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0488).
The City is entrusting the redevelopment of parc Girardin, in the arrondissement de Beauport, to the company Paradis aménagement urbain inc.
The contract is for $2,799,800 before taxes; the net expense for the City comes to $2,939,440.02.
The work includes a kiosk, cut stone features, ground surfacing, a performance area, lighting, electrical services and horticultural work.
Four companies submitted bids and all of them met the requirements; Paradis aménagement urbain offered the lowest price.
The winning bid is 9.5% higher than the requesting department's estimate, which was $2,556,675.64.
Funding comes from loan by-laws and cultural development agreements reached with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The executive committee adopted the decision on April 8, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0445).

The City confirms the completion of the cycling and pedestrian development work on rue Caron, rue Lockwell and rue de Claire-Fontaine, in order to collect the balance of the grants from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.

In 2023, Québec obtained funding of up to $342,000 for rue Caron, $122,000 for rue Lockwell and $78,000 for rue de Claire-Fontaine; 80% of these amounts ($273,600, $97,600 and $62,400) have already been paid.

Rue Caron, between avenue Simon-Napoléon-Parent and rue de Sainte-Hélène: 516 metres of infrastructure, a mid-height path, a contraflow bike lane, sidewalks brought up to standard and about sixty trees planted. Eligible expenses: $1,897,124.05.

Rue Lockwell, between avenue Turnbull and rue de Claire-Fontaine: 244 metres, a contraflow bike lane, a designated roadway, sidewalks widened at intersections and trees planted. Eligible expenses: $445,141.98.

Rue de Claire-Fontaine, between rue Lockwell and boulevard René-Lévesque: 156 metres, with work aimed at making students' trips to école primaire Saint-Jean-Baptiste safer. Eligible expenses: $1,247,060.74.
The funding cannot exceed 50% of the eligible expenses or the set maximum; if the declared expenses are lower than the initial calculations, the City must pay back the overpayment.

The document states that there is no financial impact and authorizes the director of the Service de la planification de l'aménagement et de l'environnement to sign the documents intended for the ministère.
The City is giving an official name to two retention basins: "bassin de rétention de l'Oie-Blanche 1" (S068) and "bassin de rétention de l'Oie-Blanche 2" (S069).
Both basins were built as part of the same project and the boundary between the arrondissements of Beauport and La Cité-Limoilou runs through them.
The names come from rue de l'Oie-Blanche, located nearby, following the practice of naming basins after a neighbouring street.
These basins are used to temporarily store rainwater; the City requires them in every new residential development.
The proposal comes from the Comité de commémoration et de toponymie, and the Commission de toponymie du Québec was consulted about the spelling.
No financial impact is indicated in the document.
The urban agglomeration adopts a by-law to allow the complete redevelopment of avenue des Hôtels, in the Saint-Louis neighbourhood, in order to create a corridor reserved for public transit.
Société de transport de Lévis buses will use this corridor to reach the future tramway at the new Sainte-Foy transfer hub, near boulevard Laurier and route de l'Église.
The ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable bought strips of land from neighbouring owners to widen the avenue, and paid cash compensation for the lost parking spaces.
The by-law relaxes planning rules for properties next to the construction site: access driveways longer than 10 metres, parking areas, waste containers, retaining walls, fill, embankments and signs.
It also authorizes the demolition, reconstruction, relocation, filling and excavation work, as well as the tree cutting needed to deal with the constraints created by the construction site.
This work is generally exempt from the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec and from the usual permit process, except for certain heritage buildings.
The by-law contains no provision that can be submitted to a referendum; a public consultation meeting must be held.
The City is awarding the contract to supply mechanical bolts and hardware to Distributions P.R. inc., of Québec.
The contract is worth an estimated $415,718.08 before taxes and runs until May 31, 2031, with an annual price adjustment for inflation.
The net cost, after the QST refund, is estimated at $436,452.02.
The material will be used by the City's various administrative units: items kept in stock in the stores and refilling the bolt cabinets in the mechanical workshops.
Five companies submitted bids; the one from Groupe J.S.V. inc. was found non-compliant because the bid form was incomplete.
The winning bid is 52.5% below the requesting department's estimate, which was $875,000 before taxes.
The amounts for 2027 to 2031 remain conditional on the adoption of the annual budgets.
The City is giving $4,000,000 to the organization UTILE Québec 3 to build housing on rue de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres.
The project calls for 2 buildings with 194 affordable housing units and 69 non-market housing units without public support, at 100 to 124, rue de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The payment is made in three parts: $750,000 in 2026, then the rest in 2027 and 2028.
The Fonds immobilier de solidarité FTQ is contributing $14,500,000 to the project for its part; the City's contribution is equal to 28% of that amount.
UTILE Québec 3 commits to finding elsewhere the missing 12% of the required community contribution (40% in total).
The total cost of the affordable housing portion of the project is $47,056,906.
Starting September 1, 2026, only paper bags will be allowed for the collection of dead leaves and green waste in Québec. Plastic bags will no longer be accepted.
The maximum weight of a bag of leaves goes from 25 kg to 12 kg, contents included.
The bag will have to be made of paper, designed for leaf collection, leak-proof and closed so that it can be picked up at the curb.
Leaf collection will take place every week, but only during the period set by the City.
The City explains that plastic bags leave behind fragments that contaminate the compost; paper bags are compostable and accepted without any extra sorting.
The transfer centre can keep loose waste or waste in paper bags for up to three weeks, compared with 18 hours for waste in plastic bags.
The City expects processing costs to go down thanks to this change.
The City is renting off-road articulated trucks of 28 tonnes or more, with an operator, for less than 6 months.
The contract goes to Les Entreprises Lou-Vil inc., of Québec, the only company that submitted a bid.
Estimated amount: $508,880 before taxes, or $534,260.39 taking into account the QST refund.
The rental is estimated at 2,250 hours to haul heavy materials on hard-to-reach terrain.
The trucks will be used on the TW-03 section worksite of the TramCité project, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The bid is 24.4% below the requesting department's estimate ($672,800 before taxes).
The funds come from the loan by-law related to the structuring public transit network.
The City is banning parking from November 15 to March 31 on the north side of rue Guimont, between avenue du Bourg-Royal and avenue Renouard, in Beauport.
The same winter ban applies on the east side of avenue de Lisieux, between rue Loyola (starting 47 metres north of it) and rue Guimont, in front of 2290, avenue de Lisieux.
These bans remove 20 parking spaces during the winter: 18 on rue Guimont and 2 on avenue de Lisieux.
The goal is to make snow removal easier: parked vehicles were getting in the way of the equipment and could cause service interruptions.
According to the document, the occupancy rate of the spaces is moderate on rue Guimont and low on avenue de Lisieux.
The decision falls to the Beauport borough council, Robert-Giffard district.

The City is adding a $11,000 fee for applications to authorize real estate projects filed under Quebec's 2024 housing law, which allows projects to be authorized even if they don't comply with zoning.

Social or affordable housing projects carried out under programs of the Société d'habitation du Québec, the CMHC, an agreement with Maisons Canada, or designated by the executive committee are exempt from this fee.
A new fee is created for the removal and treatment of garbage produced on construction sites, calculated according to the same rules as roll-off, front-load or rear-load containers.
The City says it can now bill contractors on road construction sites, because its systems record the date, location and volume of each transport of residual materials.

Nine parking zones linked to the building at 320, rue Saint-Joseph Est (TF-12, TP-33 to TP-36, TH-16, TH-18, TH-19, TH-20) are being added to the fee schedule; the City is taking back their management in 2026, previously handled by the CSQ.
For the parking covered by line 49, the maximums are $15 or $21.50 depending on the time period; replacing a permit sticker costs $10 starting with the second one.
City council must adopt the by-law, with a target date of June 2, 2026.
The City is setting aside $10,000,000 from its accumulated surplus as of December 31, 2025 for active mobility projects (walking, cycling, connections to public transit).
Of this amount, $240,000 comes from the agglomeration surplus and $9,760,000 from the local (proximity) surplus.
The urban agglomeration council is creating a reserve dedicated to active mobility and transferring the $240,000 into it.
This $240,000 will fund the implementation of the Vision de la mobilité active et de l'intermodalité 2023-2027 (item 38003 of the 2026-2035 investment plan).
The goal is to fund these facilities without borrowing.
The projects concerned involve cycling and pedestrian networks, connections to public transit and the safety of routes.
The local (proximity) portion ($9,760,000) will be submitted separately to city council.

The executive committee authorizes the Service des approvisionnements to buy computer hardware and software from companies that do not have an establishment in Québec, in Canada or in a European Union country.
These purchases are for the City's Service des technologies de l'information.
Two suppliers are involved: Kahoot (Oslo, Norway) for an interactive online learning platform, and Systor Systems (California, United States) for a USB key duplicator.
Each of the two contracts is between $0 and $33,000 and will be paid by purchasing card.

A Government of Québec regulation adopted on March 6, 2025 requires cities to obtain an authorization before entering into this type of purchase without a call for tenders, with no value limit, including credit card payments.
The regulation also covers medical supplies and equipment, pharmaceutical products and scientific instruments.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough is paying out $500 in total in grants to three organizations.
L'Engrenage Saint-Roch receives $166.67.
The Centre Ozanam de la Société de Saint-Vincent-de-Paul receives $166.67.
Méduse, coopérative de producteurs et diffuseurs artistiques, culturels et communautaires, receives $166.66.
The money comes from the borough council's budget and is used to support these organizations' activities.
The City is banning parking on a portion of boulevard Central, on the west side, in the arrondissement des Rivières (district des Saules-Les Méandres).
The ban applies to a 7.5-metre strip, located 220 metres south of boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, between Wilfrid-Hamel and rue Henri-Letondal.
The change means the loss of one on-street parking space.
The request came from a business at 1395, boulevard Central: parked cars were making it hard for vehicles to exit its parking lot.
The Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente notes a low parking occupancy rate at this location.
The executive committee takes note of a reference framework that brings together the standards and practices of the Bureau des relations internationales et du Protocole.
The document gathers the rules for official welcomes, receptions and protocol meals, flag displays and the lighting of public buildings.
It also includes guidelines for giving out tokens of hospitality and a guide on preparing for emergency situations during missions abroad.
This grouping stems from the transfer of the Protocole to the Bureau des relations internationales in August 2024, which made it necessary to harmonize practices.
Future revisions of these documents will be approved by the director general.
The decision summary indicates no financial impact.
The City is borrowing $1,540,000 to fund climate projects in the territory of the agglomération de Québec, repayable over 10 years.
The money is for projects under the Plan de transition et d'action climatique and the preliminary climate plan that are not covered by the Québec government grant.

The City received $49M from the ministère de l'Environnement in March 2022, but this funding excludes, among other things, urban consolidation, biodiversity, carbon capture, soil permeability and collective mobilization.
The amounts cover professional services contracts, hiring staff, purchasing goods, buildings and servitudes, as well as paying out grants.
Awareness, communication and public consultation activities are planned.
The City is taking $154,000 from its general fund while waiting for the by-law to come into force, an amount that will be repaid afterwards.
The funds are spread over the years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 investment plan.
The City is awarding Avizo Experts-Conseils inc., of Sherbrooke, a professional services contract worth $317,781.21 (plus taxes).
The firm will measure flows in the domestic, combined and storm sewer systems, in certain watercourses and at certain wastewater pumping stations, throughout the city's territory.
The contract runs from the date it is awarded until December 31, 2026, with an option for two 12-month renewals indexed to the consumer price index.
Two companies submitted bids; Avizo received the best score, ahead of Can-Explore inc. ($331,871.66).
The net cost to the City is estimated at $333,630.55, funded through an agglomeration loan by-law.
The executive committee approved the decision on February 4, 2026.
The City is appointing Renée Desormeaux to represent the mayor on the board of directors of L'Institut canadien de Québec.
The term lasts three years and is unpaid.
She replaces Nathalie Roy, whose term has ended.
L'Institut canadien de Québec runs the Bibliothèque de Québec and organizes the Québec en toutes lettres literary festival.
One seat on the organization's board is reserved for the mayor or the person he designates.
The City is authorizing the expansion of a residential building at 3390, rue de la Pérade, in Sainte-Foy, to add about 100 rental housing units.
The building at 3350, rue de la Pérade, will be demolished to make room for the expansion; there are no housing units in it.
Two exemptions are granted: a height of eight storeys instead of six, and a rear setback of 7.5 metres instead of 15 metres.
The developer will have to build at least 90 housing units, including at least 45% with two or more bedrooms, and provide air conditioning in every unit.
An acoustic study will have to show indoor noise of 40 dBA or less, and an indoor common space of at least 90 m² will have to be offered to residents.
A public consultation meeting will be held, followed by three days to submit written comments; the project is not subject to a referendum.
The urban agglomeration council must approve the final resolution; the target date is August 25, 2026.
A breach of the conditions carries a fine of $1,000 for an individual and $2,000 in other cases, doubled for a repeat offence.
The City is banning new hotels and other general tourist accommodation establishments (C10 uses) in two areas of the Saint-Jean-Baptiste neighbourhood.
The areas concerned are east of rue Saint-Augustin, south of côte d'Abraham, west of avenue Honoré-Mercier and north of rue Saint-Joachim.
A new zone (13047Md) is being created for the property at 888, rue Saint-Jean, where general tourist accommodation becomes prohibited.
In zone 13034Md, it becomes prohibited to convert a dwelling to a non-residential use on the floors above the ground floor.
Tourist accommodation establishments already in place do not become non-conforming.

The City will hold a public consultation meeting and will ask for the opinion of the conseil de quartier de Saint-Jean-Baptiste; interested people will have seven days after the meeting to submit their comments in writing.
The by-law contains no provision that can be subject to a referendum; the borough council is aiming for adoption on August 31, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is granting a maximum subsidy of $250,000 to Optonique, the centre of excellence in optics-photonics located at the Parc technologique du Québec métropolitain.
The money will go to the project “Optonique : Propulser l'excellence photonique à Québec 2026-2027,” spread over two years.
The project includes workforce recruitment and training, visibility activities (including a signature event), missions and pavilions abroad, and innovation networking activities.

The total cost of the project is $2,126,650: $1,040,450 from the ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie, $596,200 from the organization, $250,000 from the City and $240,000 from Développement économique Canada.
The City's funds come from the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale, in two instalments of $149,762.47 and $100,237.53.
Optonique has 8 employees and 54 members, including 13 businesses from the Québec agglomeration; the project does not provide for any job creation.
The urban agglomeration council adopted the decision on February 18, 2026.

The City is providing up to $619,500 in grants to Québec cultural organizations under the Rejoindre component of the Entente de développement culturel with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The money funds 36 projects aimed at reaching new audiences: cultural mediation, audience retention and online content creation.

Amounts per project range from $5,000 (podcast by Centrale Alternative) to $35,000 (BIG BANG festival by Les Incomplètes); L'Ampli de Québec receives $25,000 for activities in Saint-Roch, and Radio Basse-Ville $34,000 for a radio project with marginalized people.
Several projects take place in specific neighbourhoods and settings: Saint-Roch, Petit Champlain, Beauport, CHSLDs and community centres, schools and CEGEPs.
A committee made up of people from the sector and professionals from the Service de la culture et du patrimoine reviewed and recommended the projects.
The funding comes from a loan by-law ($86,000) and from transfers tied to the Entente de développement culturel 2024-2026 ($533,500).
The City is creating a loading zone on avenue De La Ronde, west side, over 18 metres starting from chemin de la Canardière, heading north.
Vehicles will be able to stay there for a maximum of 30 minutes.
Two parking spaces are being changed; parking was already banned there from April 1 to November 14.
The change responds to requests from businesses on chemin de la Canardière that were looking for a place for deliveries, since the VivaCité corridor removed on-street parking.
The measure affects the Maizerets-Lairet district, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough.
The City is banning parking on new sections of rue de Belleville, in Charlesbourg (district des Monts).
East side: parking banned starting 40 metres north of avenue de la Rivière-Jaune up to rue Valéda-Auclair.
West side: parking banned starting 53 metres north of avenue de la Rivière-Jaune, over a distance of 86 metres.
Nine parking spaces are being removed; the document states that the occupancy rate there is low.
The request came from a resident; the roadway is less than 7 metres wide and parked cars were making it hard for vehicles to pass each other.
The conseil d'arrondissement de Charlesbourg adopted ordinance O-549 on April 28, 2026.
The City is authorizing the installation of a backup generator in the front yard, on the south side of the building located at 500, rue Fleur-de-Lys, in the Vanier neighbourhood.
The planning by-law of the Arrondissement des Rivières normally requires such equipment to be placed in a side or rear yard.
The generator will be used to supply power to the CHU de Québec's external hemodialysis centre in the event of a power outage.
According to the analysis, the unit cannot be installed indoors because of the load limits of the floors and the roof and because of ventilation needs.
The generator will be surrounded by screen walls to blend it into the architecture and reduce noise.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on June 1, 2026; the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec also gave a favourable opinion.
The City is adding two indoor parking facilities to its agglomeration by-law on parking, both in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.

The Le Zénith parking facility, at 263, rue Sagard, has 84 spaces. Starting in September, they will be used by municipal employees (including those of the Cour municipale), workers in the area and residents.
The rates for municipal employees are those set out in the collective agreements. The rates for neighbourhood workers and residents will be added to the by-law before it is adopted.
The Place Jacques-Cartier parking facility, at 365, rue Dorchester under the bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy complex, is open to the public and has 308 spaces.
The City has acquired three additional floors of Place Jacques-Cartier, on top of the two it already owned. The rules of use and the rates will now apply to the entire parking facility.
The hourly rate that applied to the spaces previously owned by the Centrale des syndicats du Québec will from now on apply to all the spaces.
Both parking facilities are operated by the SPAQ.
The arrondissement de Charlesbourg is granting a minor exemption to the building at 12089, boulevard Henri-Bourassa, in the Orsainville neighbourhood.
The exemption lowers the required amenity area to 13.5 square metres per dwelling instead of 15 square metres.
This will allow the owner to add two parking spaces for the 31-unit building, which currently has only 22.
The two spaces will be built on a grassed strip, as an extension of the existing parking lot; the waste containers will be moved a few metres away.
According to the analysis, the percentage of green space on the lot stays the same and tenants keep their relaxation areas (rooftop terrace and balconies).
The regulations require seven trees to be planted on the property, tied to the issuing of the building permit.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave its unanimous support on February 4, 2026.
The City is settling out of court the expropriation of a piece of land on 1re Avenue (lot 2 228 721), acquired for the TramCité tramway project.
The final compensation paid to the owner is set at $700,000.00 (plus taxes), including principal, interest, additional compensation and expert appraisal fees.
Since $436,000.00 was already paid in January 2026, $264,000.00 remains to be paid.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 tied to the structuring public transit network.
The date for vacating the land moves from September 1, 2026 to February 1, 2027.
The lawyers Giasson et associés are authorized to sign the settlement documents on behalf of the City.
The City is giving up to $400,000 to Québec International to organize NordiQ 2026, an event aimed at attracting venture capital funds to Québec.
The event will take place on October 27, 2026, the day after FresQc, and will bring together startups, large companies and investors.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets.

The grant covers expenses made between January 1 and October 30, 2026: logistics ($210,500), salaries ($70,000), communications and advertising ($75,000), travel and speakers ($35,000), administration ($50,000).
The project costs $440,500 in total; private partners are providing the remaining $40,500.
Québec International will have to submit a report on the event and a statement of expenses no later than November 30, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is submitting its bid to host the annual convention of the Fédération canadienne des municipalités from May 24 to 30, 2032.
The Fédération had invited Canadian cities to submit bids for the 2029 to 2032 conventions.
Marie-France Loiseau, Assistant Director General – Citizen and Urban Vitality, is authorized to sign the bid and the necessary documents.
The document does not anticipate any financial impact for submitting the bid.
By way of comparison, the convention held in Québec in 2019 generated benefits estimated at more than $4.2 million, 6,800 rooms booked and 478 media articles.
The Edmonton convention, in June 2026, brought together more than 2,800 delegates.
City council was to make its decision on July 7, 2026.
The City is awarding Agence Gravel inc., of Québec, the contract to purchase service weapons and accessories for police officers.
The contract runs from the date it is awarded until December 31, 2029, for an estimated amount of $2,648,180 before taxes.
The net expense, which falls under agglomeration jurisdiction, is estimated at $2,780,257.98.
Only two companies were invited to bid, because of confidentiality issues tied to the technical specifications.
The other bid, from Rampart International Corp. (Ottawa), was $2,749,893 before taxes.
The requesting department had estimated the contract at $3,500,000 before taxes, which is 24.3% more than the lowest compliant bid.
The amounts remain conditional on the adoption of the 2027 to 2029 budgets.
The Ville de Québec will pay up to $150,000 to Fumoir Grizzly inc., a seafood processing company based in Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures.
The money will be used to market BacM35, a natural ingredient that fights the Listeria bacteria in food.
The company wants to obtain regulatory approvals abroad and sell its product in Europe, North America and Asia.
The project costs $719,500 in total: $509,500 comes from the company, $60,000 from the ministère de l'Économie et de l'Innovation, and $150,000 from the City.
The company expects to create 4 jobs and maintain its 70 existing jobs.
The grant comes from the Capitale-Innovation component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030 and does not have to be repaid.
A review committee recommended the project on May 12, 2026; the decision rests with the urban agglomeration council.
The Ville de Québec is awarding the repair of its detachable snowblowers, parts included, to the company J.A. Larue inc. (3003, avenue Watt, Québec).
The agreement is estimated at $971,127.50 (plus GST and QST); the net cost to the City is estimated at $1,019,562.48.
The contract runs from the signing of the agreement until March 31, 2028.
The fleet covered includes 60 detachable snowblowers made by Larue, used by the Service de la gestion des équipements motorisés.
No call for tenders was held: the law allows the maintenance of specialized equipment to be awarded directly to the manufacturer or its representative.
The agreement sets out hourly rates, firm prices for parts and discount percentages.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of those years' budgets.
The executive committee takes note of the lists of additional expenses over $250,000 authorized by delegated employees for the weeks of July 5, 12 and 19, 2026.
Waste collection: $544,540 more to add 38,000 recycling pickups in La Haute-Saint-Charles and Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, bringing the 2019 contract to $13,005,065.75.
Flood-control works on the rivière Lorette: $2,973,037.97 more (excavation, backfill, roadwork, contaminated soil, waste materials discovered), bringing the contract to $44,916,055.59.
Boulevard Laurier: $555,074.50 more to install a water main east of autoroute Robert-Bourassa, temporarily supply the CHUL and move buses to boulevard Hochelaga.
D'Estimauville storm sewer collector (phase 2): $2,669,556.45 more, mainly for managing contaminated soil, the pumping station, bicycle signage and lighting; contract now at $26,713,806.35.
All amounts are shown before taxes.
The City is refusing the minor exemption request for 1063, rue Élisabeth-Becker, in the Cap-Rouge neighbourhood (arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The owner wanted to convert their attached garage into a living space, with a side setback of 1.07 metres instead of the 2.0 metres required.
The request also sought to allow the parking area at the front of the building to extend 6.0 metres instead of the 3.0 metres permitted.
Reason for the refusal: the by-law does not cause serious harm to the owner, since a compliant project is still possible.
Another reason: the lot has no particular feature that would prevent a compliant project; there is still buildable space in the back yard.
According to the analysis, a living space 1.07 metres from the lot line could have an impact on the neighbouring property.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had unanimously recommended the refusal on May 12, 2026.
Rue du Court-Métrage becomes one-way westbound, between boulevard Bastien and boulevard Saint-Jacques, in La Haute-Saint-Charles (Loretteville-Les Châtels district).
Ten parking spaces are being removed on the north side of the street, between rue Valvue and boulevard Bastien, where parking will now be prohibited.
The City will add road features and signs at the intersections of boulevard Saint-Jacques, rue Bresseau and rue Valvue to enforce the one-way direction.
The change responds to a petition from residents and to complaints about through traffic, which the City's analysis finds to be higher than on comparable streets.

The RTC plans a temporary facility at the southeast corner of Bastien and du Court-Métrage, while waiting for a future Parc-O-Bus; the one-way direction eliminates conflicts between buses and cars coming out of the street.
The arrondissement des Rivières is easing planning rules in the parc industriel Cardinal, in the Vanier neighbourhood (Vanier-Duberger district).
The area concerned is east of rue des Impatientes and rue de Port-Louis, south of autoroute Félix-Leclerc, west of autoroute Laurentienne and north of boulevard Père-Lelièvre.
Distribution centres (use C40) and general industry (I3) become permitted in zones along boulevard Pierre-Bertrand and boulevard Père-Lelièvre, where they were prohibited.
Mechanical or electronic game rooms are allowed in zone 23008Cb: a pinball machine business at 999, boulevard Pierre-Bertrand will no longer be limited to three machines.
Health clinics without lodging (physiotherapy, acupuncture, etc.) are permitted in zones 23008Cb and 23012Cb, with a limit of 200 square metres per establishment added after the consultations.
Outdoor storage and vehicle parking become permitted in the zones of the Hydro-Québec power transmission corridor, except near residential areas.
The public consultations were held on May 11, 2026, and the written consultation ran until May 18, 2026; the by-law contains provisions subject to approval by referendum.
The Ville de Québec is giving $12,200 to École de musique Amadeus et Cie to help pay its rent in 2026.
The organization rents space at 6350, 3e Avenue Est, in the presbytery of the église Saint-Jérôme de l'Auvergne, which is owned by the Fabrique Saint-Charles-Borromée.
The school offers individual and group music lessons, for all ages and all levels, mainly to residents of Charlesbourg.
The agreement covers January 1 to December 31, 2026; the money must be paid within 30 days after it takes effect.
The organization must mention the City's support in its communications, report each year and take part in a follow-up meeting.
The City may cancel the agreement and ask for the money back if the organization does not meet its obligations.
Similar support had been granted before: $17,680 for July 2024 to December 2025 and $27,153 in 2022.
The Ville de Québec is applying for two grants from the ministère de l'Environnement (OASIS program) to add greenery to the city and reduce the effects of heat waves and heavy rainfall.

Component 1: a planning project with $1,638,914 in eligible expenses, for which the City is requesting $1,309,874 (studies of the territory, a reference framework on green infrastructure, a heat plan).
Component 2: 11 works projects totalling $11,392,817 in eligible expenses, for which the City is requesting $9,114,255.

Five streets will be partially de-paved: îlot Kirouac (Saint-Luc, Kirouac, Christophe-Colomb Ouest), Saint-François Ouest and Laviolette, Lafayette, 64e Rue Est (20 trees) and a new street on the site of the former aréna Gilles-Tremblay.

Three micro-forests are planned: near avenue Giguère, at parc Clérin and at parc Saint-Jean-Baptiste-De La Salle; landscaping work is also planned at the CVSME and at the lieu d'élimination de la neige Raymond.
The City aims to plant 5,000 street trees in the areas considered most vulnerable, out of 25,000 sites identified.

The City commits to paying its share of the costs and authorizes the director of the Service de la planification de l'aménagement et de l'environnement to represent it. Work is planned from 2026 to 2028.
The Ville de Québec is officially opening rue de la Promenade-des-Soeurs, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough, so that it becomes a public street.
The street corresponds to two pieces of land (lots 6 712 003 and 6 712 005) already acquired by the former Ville de Cap-Rouge in 1985 and in 2000 for municipal purposes.
The opening aims to provide access to a neighbouring piece of land belonging to the Compagnie des chemins de fer nationaux du Canada, which currently has no access to a public street.
The executive committee is making the decision and adopted it on April 22, 2026.
The City states that the decision has no direct financial impact.
The City borrowed $81,000,000 by issuing bonds dated July 2, 2026.
The Minister of Finance awarded the issue on June 18, 2026 to Financière Banque Nationale inc., which submitted the most advantageous bid out of seven offers.
The real cost of the loan is 3.66904%, over an average term of 4 years and 11 months, with interest payable twice a year.
The money goes to $36,762,200 in new work paid for by the City and $44,237,800 in refinancing of loans already taken out.
The principal is repaid each year from 2027 to 2031, plus one portion in 2036; two refinancings are planned: $9,037,000 in the 5th year and $15,789,000 in the 10th year.
The executive committee takes note of the report filed by the treasurer (resolution CE-2026-0877).
The City is selling a piece of land taken from the right-of-way of rue des Prairies, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough, to the company Les Immeubles NexPlex inc.
The buyer is adding about 34.6 square metres to its purchase, for a total lot of about 400 square metres.
This extra piece of land costs $31,300, plus taxes, which works out to $900 per square metre.
The total sale price goes from $328,700 to $360,000, plus taxes; the money goes into the City's general fund.
The buyer wants this extra area in order to install a private electrical transformer and hook up its building, without encroaching on the City's land.
The City is closing this part of the street and transferring it to its private domain so that it can be sold.
The City is giving up to $81,880 to the organization La Ruche Vanier for the year 2026-2027.
The money will be used to hire an intercultural community-living officer in the Vanier neighbourhood and to organize activities, from 2026 until March 2027.
The project is a one-year pilot; a three-year agreement could follow.

The cost is split into two equal shares of $40,940: one from the ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration, the other from the operating budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The organization will have to report each year and mention the contribution of the City and the ministère in its publications.
Community-living officers are already in place in Limoilou, Saint-Roch and Sainte-Foy.
According to the document, 15.1% of Vanier's population was born outside Canada in 2021, and the neighbourhood is a priority area according to the social vulnerability index.
The City is removing the requirement to install a single-module home (maison unimodulaire) on screw piles or piers in two zones of the Lac-Saint-Charles neighbourhood.
Property owners in these areas will therefore be able to build another type of foundation, such as a concrete foundation, in order to create a living space there.
The zones concerned are located between the rivière Saint-Charles, rue Jacques-Bédard, rue Beauséjour and rue du Piémont, as well as the area covering numbers 558 to 574, rue de l'Élégance.
These two zones were the only ones in the territory of the city of Québec that still had this requirement, inherited from the former municipality of Lac-Saint-Charles and not changed in 2006.
The conseil de quartier de Lac-Saint-Charles will be consulted and will hold the public consultation meeting.
The by-law contains no provision that could be subject to approval by referendum.
The City is authorizing a $400,000 expense to pay its share of the work planned under agreements with developers (for example, building new streets in subdivision projects).
It is borrowing the same amount, repayable over five years, and each year it sets aside part of its general revenues to pay the principal and interest.
Up to 10% of the expense, or $40,000, will be taken from the general fund to cover amounts already committed; this fund will be reimbursed when the by-law comes into force.
The expense involves infrastructure that falls under both the city and the agglomeration; the cost sharing will follow the rules on mixed expenditures.
The funds are entered in the years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 investment plan.
The City may acquire, by mutual agreement or by expropriation, any building or servitude needed for the work.
Any subsidy or other source of funding received will be used to reduce the loan.
The City wants to obtain a permanent easement on a piece of land bordering boulevard Laurier, in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, for the TramCité tramway project.
This easement will be used to move underground conduits and public utility networks along the route.
Two parcels are involved, of 101.4 and 41.7 square metres, on lots 6 643 391 and 6 643 460.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement or, if no agreement is reached, by expropriation; the Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings.
If the project no longer needs the easement, the City may withdraw the expropriation proceedings, in whole or in part.
The entire piece of land is entered on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $11,317,000, or $1,111.14 per square metre.
The funds come from the loan by-law for building the structuring public transit network.
The City authorizes its Service des approvisionnements to buy computer hardware and software from companies that do not have an establishment in Québec, in Canada or in a European Union country.
These purchases are for the Service des technologies de l'information.
Since a Québec government regulation enacted on March 6, 2025, this type of direct-award contract requires prior authorization, even for purchases made by credit card and with no limit on value.
The regulation covers computer hardware and software, medical supplies and equipment, pharmaceutical products and scientific instruments.
The company listed in the appendix is DigiCert (Lehi, Utah, United States), for a certificate used to authenticate emails, paid by purchasing card.
The value of the contract is between $0 and $33,000.
The City is authorizing, for five years, a retail sales and services business on the ground floor of the building located at 2949, chemin Sainte-Foy, in the Plateau neighbourhood.
The owner, who bought the building in the summer of 2025, wants to move a grocery store there, enlarge it by taking in the attached garage, and set up a café terrace in the front yard.
This temporary permission gets around two standards: the front setback goes from 6 to 5 metres on the rue de Rougemont side, and only one storey is required instead of two.
The owner must create a green space of at least 35 square metres in the front yard near the neighbouring lot, plant one tree per front yard, and hide the garbage bins behind a screen.
After the public consultation on March 24, 2026, the City removed the limit of four parking spaces in front and added the requirement to conceal the waste containers.
The owner plans to demolish the building and carry out a residential project within five years.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The City is awarding Lévesque & Associés Construction inc. a $689,000 contract (before GST and QST) for work in two municipal buildings.

At the pavillon de services Prévert, in the arrondissement des Rivières: roof repairs, insulation of the foundations from the inside, and the addition of an accessible washroom that can be entered from outside.
At the Centre de loisirs du Petit-Village, in the arrondissement de Beauport: the addition of an accessible washroom that can be entered from outside.
The net cost to the City is $723,363.88, funded by two loan by-laws ($449,283.51 and $274,080.37).
Four companies submitted bids; the winning bid is the lowest and is 12.6% below the department's estimate ($788,592).
The executive committee adopted the decision on July 2, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0937).
City council appoints 12 citizens as commissioners of the Commission consultative pour le vivre-ensemble, the body that replaces the Commission consultative pour une ville inclusive.
Eight new members receive a 4-year term; four former commissioners (2022-2025) are reappointed for 2 years.
The call for applications ran from April 3 to May 16, 2026 and received 102 applications for 12 positions.
The selection was made by a committee made up of the three designated elected officials: Claude Lavoie (chair), Clément Bourdeau and Marie-Pierre Boucher.
The Commission is to make recommendations on social cohesion, in connection with the Plan d'action en développement social 2025-2030, and to propose concrete actions.
The Service des relations citoyennes et des communications is responsible for restarting the Commission's activities.
The appointed members come in particular from the community, health, university and rights advocacy sectors.
The City is settling out of court its expropriation dispute with the Syndicat des copropriétaires de Iberville Un, before the Tribunal administratif du Québec.
The case concerns a sidewalk and right-of-way servitude of about 49.7 square metres along avenue Lavigerie, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The final compensation is set at $149,956.25 (principal, interest, additional compensation and expert appraisal fees), plus applicable taxes.
The City had already paid $25,650 in July 2023; it will therefore pay a balance of $124,306.25 plus taxes to close the file.
The money comes from agglomeration loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1450.
The City's attorneys, Giasson et associés, are authorized to sign the settlement documents.
The urban agglomeration council must approve the agreement, with a target date of July 8, 2026.
The City is requesting $1,496,473 from the ministère de la Culture et des Communications for the repurposing of the église Saint-Jean-Baptiste, at 470, rue Saint-Jean.

This amount combines $1M from the Ministry's emergency fund and the transfer to the City of a $496,473 grant from the Conseil du patrimoine religieux, originally awarded to the Fabrique de la paroisse.
The City must contribute an equal amount of $1,496,473, provided for in its 2026-2035 capital works program, bringing the total funding for the work to $2,992,946.
The money will be used to restore the doors, windows and storm windows, to improve the building's weather-tightness and the safety of its entrances.
The City plans to issue a call for tenders for this work as early as the summer of 2026.
The City purchased this church, classified by the gouvernement du Québec, in November 2024; it has been vacant for more than ten years.
The project aims to introduce new community, cultural and event uses there; architectural studies and a business plan are under way.
The City is supporting four sports facility projects so that they can apply for financial assistance from the ministère de l'Éducation.
Collège Champigny: new multi-purpose complex with a double gymnasium of 816 m², multi-purpose rooms, change rooms, storage and bleachers.
Collège Jésus-Marie: expansion of the sports pavilion (single gymnasium of 650 m², multi-purpose room of 150 m², multi-functional room of 370 m²).
Académie Saint-Louis: construction of a double gymnasium of 1156 m².

École secondaire François-Bourrin: sports complex with 10 indoor volleyball courts (or 4 to 5 futsal courts), a running track on a mezzanine and 6 beach volleyball courts covered by a dome heated in winter.
This support does not commit any City money for construction or renovation.

The City will sign use agreements with the selected institutions, on the condition that they offer hours that meet the needs of the City and of recognized organizations, at rates that do not exceed market rates.
The Ville de Québec will continue to collect and treat the wastewater of the Municipalité de Lac-Beauport, a service it has provided since 1994.
The new agreement covers January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2030, with a possible automatic five-year renewal (2031-2035) if neither party objects six months before the expiry date.
The City is reserving for Lac-Beauport a maximum flow of 2,000 m³ of wastewater per day, measured at the intermunicipal manhole at the boundary between the two territories.
The annual volumes to be treated are estimated at 730,000 m³ for each of the years 2026 to 2030.
The City expects revenues of $238,000 per year from 2026 to 2030; Lac-Beauport's contribution is calculated using the method of the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation.
If measurements show discharges repeatedly exceeding the reserved capacity, the two parties will meet to review that capacity and the financial contribution.
The City does not guarantee absolute continuity of service and is not responsible for interruptions or backups, except in the case of fault on its part.
The City is banning parking on rue de Champéry, in Charlesbourg, from November 15 to March 31.
The ban applies to the section between boulevard du Lac and rue Josée: 53 metres on the east side and 43 metres on the west side, starting from boulevard du Lac.
Six parking spaces are removed during this period.
The measure is meant to let snow removal equipment through, as it is blocked by parked vehicles.
According to the document, the impact on residents is low because few people use these spaces.
The City wants to obtain a permanent easement (servitude) over part of a laneway in the boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest area, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The area involved is about 51.4 square metres.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement with the owner or, failing that, by expropriation.
The easement will be used to move public utility conduits and networks needed for the TramCité tramway project.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to begin the proceedings and to discontinue them if the project no longer needs the easement.
The money comes from the urban agglomeration's loan by-law on the Réseau structurant de transport en commun; the laneway is not listed on the assessment roll.
The City approves the plans to redo the exterior cladding of the entrance of an apartment building at 1991, avenue Bardy, in the Maizerets neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The existing red bricks and painted concrete are kept; granite cladding will be added at the base of the entrance wall.
The plans call for a play of contrasting colours on the facade.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on the project on February 24, 2026, unanimously.
The borough council adopted the decision on March 23, 2026, which allows the permit to be issued.
The City is correcting the name of the organization that will receive a $2,900 grant for the "Évasion en fête" event.
The money will go to "Corporation Jeunesse l'Évasion l'Ormière" instead of "L'Évasion St-Pie X", which was entered by mistake.
The grant comes from the Programme de soutien financier à un événement de proximité of the Arrondissement des Rivières.

It was part of a block of $28,200 given to three organizations for events in the summer of 2026: Loisirs et Sports Neufchâtel inc. ($5,000), Loisirs Vanier ($20,300) and Corporation Jeunesse l'Évasion l'Ormière ($2,900).
The $2,900 comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement des Rivières.
The City is approving the Arno project: a five-storey residential building with 97 rental units, on a former parking lot at the corner of rue des Prairies and rue de l'Éperon, in Vieux-Québec.
The developer, Les Immeubles NexPlex inc., is investing about $25.22M, or about $260,000 per unit.
A section of rue des Prairies will become a pedestrian passage with paving, two rain gardens and landscaping; the rue de l'Éperon cul-de-sac will close over about 45 metres.
Rue de l'Éperon will be redeveloped: adding a planting bay, an on-street parking bay, and moving the sidewalk as far as rue De Saint-Vallier Est.
The work on city-owned land is estimated at $640,000 and the City is not providing any financial contribution.
The project could receive a tax credit covering up to 85% of the annual residential property taxes, for a maximum of 10 years.
The developer will transfer the municipal infrastructure it builds to the City free of charge, once the work is accepted.
The City is ending its two by-laws on the emerald ash borer: the one that governed the fight against the spread of the insect and the one that subsidized the felling of ash trees.
