The special rules for managing wood after an ash tree is felled are being eliminated. According to the document, they have no longer been necessary or effective since July 2025.
The subsidy program for felling affected or dead ash trees ends as soon as the by-law is adopted.
Exception: a subsidy application submitted before April 1, 2026 for an ash tree felled no later than December 31, 2025 will still be processed under the old program.
This application must be made no later than 90 days after the tree is felled.
The by-law was adopted by the city council.

The City is correcting an error in a land exchange made with the ministère des Transports on March 24, 2010, after the extension of autoroute Robert-Bourassa between boulevard Lebourgneuf and boulevard Bastien.

Two pieces of land (lots 3 753 898 and 4 356 363) had been transferred to the ministère by mistake: one had already been sold to a third party, and the other is part of the right-of-way of rue de La Havane, a city street.
The correction deed cancels these two transfers, as if they had never taken place.
The ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable agrees with the correction.
No money is exchanged: the correction does not change the value of the original exchange.
The land involved is in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The City is tabling its annual report on the use of the special power granted by the provincial housing act (Bill 31), for the year 2025.
This power, valid until February 21, 2027, allows the City to authorize housing projects of at least 3 units even if they do not comply with urban planning regulations.
In 2025, the city council granted 19 authorizations of this type, allowing the construction of 1,955 additional housing units.

The projects involve, among others, 1re Avenue, rue Samuel-King, boulevard Saint-Claude, rue Charles-Albanel, rue de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres, avenue Maguire, Grande Allée Est and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.
The exemptions granted mainly concern the number of housing units allowed, building height and setbacks.
The report will be sent to the minister responsible for Housing and published on the City's website.
The arrondissement des Rivières is giving $150 to the paroisse Saint-Ambroise de la Jeune Lorette.
The grant follows a request letter and a proposal from councillor Maxime Elmaleh.
According to the analysis, the organization meets the criteria for awarding this type of grant.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, under the activity "Soutenir les conseils d'arrondissements" (Supporting borough councils).
The borough council adopted the decision (resolution CA2-2026-0084).
The City is giving out $67,108 in 26 grants to 21 organizations in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The applications had to be submitted no later than December 15, 2025, under the programs of the Cadre de soutien aux organismes reconnus.
The largest amounts go to Patro Laval ($10,000 for support in inclusive recreation) and to Carrefour des enfants de Saint-Malo ($8,500 for the « Mon Espace 0-5 ans » project).

Other amounts are used to redo websites, buy promotional material or equipment: Centre de prévention du suicide de Québec ($4,250 and $2,459), Scouts du district de Québec ($4,250), Limoilou en vrac ($4,182), Squat Basse-Ville ($4,006).
Five organizations each receive $500 for community-building activities (dinners, volunteer recognition evenings, anniversary talks).
The money comes from the arrondissement's operating budget, under the « Soutien aux organismes » activity.
The City is awarding Charles-Auguste Fortier inc. the snow removal and winter maintenance of streets in zone C0039, the Beauport nord sector.
The contract covers three winter seasons, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2029, for $3,531,365.70 (before GST and QST).
The net expense for the City is $3,707,492.58, spread out from 2026 to 2029.
The contract can be renewed for two more seasons, and prices will be indexed each year according to the Consumer Price Index.
Price adjustments are planned based on the cost of fuel and snow quantities.
Six bids were received for this zone; the one selected is the lowest compliant bid.
The contracts for the five other zones (Val-Bélair, Des Châtels, Honoré-Mercier, Charest and Sainte-Foy nord) are handled separately.
The City wants to obtain a permanent servitude (right of use) on a piece of land bordering 1re Avenue, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
This servitude covers about 17.10 square metres and will be used to move public utility conduits and networks.
The City will try to reach an amicable agreement with the owner; otherwise, it will proceed by expropriation.
The owner has been informed of the process, the next steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
If the project no longer needs the servitude, the Service des affaires juridiques may abandon the expropriation proceedings.
The entire piece of land is entered on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $288,000, or $317.92 per square metre.
The funds come from the agglomeration loan by-law for building the structuring public transit network.
The City is awarding Plasti-Bac inc., of Saint-Raymond, the contract to supply wheeled garbage bins, for $180,810 before taxes.
The contract runs from the award date until March 31, 2030, with the option of renewing it three times for 12 months, each time with an adjustment based on the CPI.
These bins are used to replace residents' bins that wear out each year because of collection operations.
After the QST refund, the net cost to the City comes to $189,827.90.
Two bids were received: Plasti-Bac at $180,810 and USD Global inc. at $180,981.50, both compliant.
The price selected is 11.4% higher than the estimate of the requesting department, which was $162,327.
Funding remains conditional on the adoption of the 2026 to 2030 budgets.
The City is changing the zoning in the Carrefour-du-Commerce industrial area, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood (Les Saules-Les Méandres district).
High-technology businesses will be allowed to set up in zones 22108Cb and 22109Cb, located near boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel and autoroute Henri-IV.
Data processing or data hosting centres with more than 200 square metres of floor area will be banned in all the zones covered.
Outdoor storage of type G, meaning any goods or materials, will be allowed in six zones of the Carrefour-du-Commerce industrial area.
The conseil de quartier de Duberger-Les Saules will give its opinion and hold the public consultation meeting; interested people will then have seven days to submit their comments in writing.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The City will not hold active public participation, considering the impact on the neighbourhood to be limited; information and feedback measures will be added to the mandatory consultations.

The City wants to ban general tourist accommodation establishments (use C10) in two zones of the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou (13003Md and 13035Md), in the Vieux-Québec area and its surroundings.
As soon as the notice of intent is adopted, the City suspends the approval of construction plans and the issuing of permits or certificates that do not comply with this intent.
The City says it wants to encourage the creation of new housing and the arrival of new residents in this area, where it already sees a large number of tourist accommodation establishments.
The planning, land management and legal affairs departments must prepare the draft by-laws that will follow up on the notice.
City council ratifies the notice for zone 13035Md; the borough council will ratify the other zone, which falls under its jurisdiction.
In April 2026, the executive committee had already adopted a similar notice for about fifteen other zones in the same arrondissement.
Québec authorizes the signing of an amendment that reduces the funding from the Government of Québec for its territorial development agreement (Fonds régions et ruralité).
The amount goes from $6,147,735 to $5,147,735 for the period from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2028, which is $1,000,000 less.
The ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation explains the decrease by the government's budget restrictions; it represents $500,000 (24.4%) per year for the next two years.
According to the document, the cut will have an impact on the ability to support social economy projects in the territory.
The funding rate for projects carried out by the City goes from 80% to 100%, and the share the City can put toward its costs of administering the fund goes from 5% to 10%.
The total of public funding is set at 100% for municipal bodies, non-profit organizations and cooperatives.
The payment schedule is adjusted: a payment of up to 45% is added based on how far along the spending is as of March 31, 2026, and the one tied to March 31, 2027 goes from 65% to 75%.
The executive committee takes note of the half-yearly report from the Service du traitement des eaux on work that has been provisionally or finally accepted.

Five work sites receive provisional acceptance, including the replacement of the rapid mixing basin at the Sainte-Foy water treatment plant ($9,854,072.75, Construction Deric inc.) and the redevelopment of the mechanical workshop at the Complexe de valorisation énergétique in La Cité-Limoilou ($1,612,327.14, Beauvais et Verret inc.).

Other provisional acceptances: upgrading of the Saint-Augustin pumping station ($3,161,743.15), work on the mechanical corridor for laboratory gases ($392,615.83) and corrective work for sand build-up at structure A ($378,193.66).

Five work sites receive final acceptance, including the replacement of the screening units at the Saint-Pascal station ($1,750,333.39) and the new analyzer room at the Complexe de valorisation énergétique ($1,282,539.41).

The other final acceptances concern the employee room at the east wastewater treatment plant ($305,702.82), harmonic filters at the biomethanation centre ($183,317.82) and the switch to electricity for the shower water heaters at the water treatment plant ($77,274.70).
The Service du traitement des eaux must produce this report twice a year, no later than June 30 and December 23.
The City is hiring Alain Perreault as a substitute driver and escort at the Cabinet du maire, from March 6 to December 31, 2026.
He will work on call, only when the regular driver and his substitute are not available.
His pay is set at $32.30 per hour, with no employee benefits: no pension plan and no group insurance.
On days when he is scheduled on call, he is guaranteed a minimum of 12 paid hours.
He accumulates 4% of his gross pay as vacation pay, and his meals are reimbursed when he works away from his assigned work location.
The contract ends on December 31, 2026 with no automatic renewal, and the City may end it if the employee loses his driver's licence.
The service vehicle is used for work only and is transferred to city hall, at 2, rue des Jardins.
The Ville de Québec is giving a grant of up to $306,452 to the Fonds d'emprunt économique communautaire (Québec), a non-profit microcredit organization founded in 1997.

The money is used to replenish the fund so it can lend to self-employed workers, businesses with fewer than 5 employees and small retail merchants in the Québec agglomeration who have trouble getting a bank loan.
The loans are aimed at businesses that are starting up, consolidating, growing or being taken over; each loan is decided by a credit committee and confirmed by the board of directors.

The project costs $383,065 in total: the City provides $306,452, and the rest comes from donations and private investors ($10,000), MicroEntreprendre ($18,588) and the Fonds de prêt pour les femmes en entrepreneuriat ($48,025).
In 2025-2026, a similar project made $132,000 in loans to 10 entrepreneurs possible, tied to total investments of $1,185,682.
The City had granted $140,000 in 2025 and $150,000 in 2016 to the same organization; its head office is in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The Ville de Québec is signing a confidentiality agreement with VIA HFR - VIA TGF INC. (ALTO), the federal Crown corporation responsible for the high-speed train project between Québec and Toronto.
This agreement allows the City to obtain non-public technical information about the project in order to plan and analyze its effects on the territory of the Québec urban agglomeration.
The document states that, at this stage, no route or station location has been determined on the territory of the city of Québec.
The City and ALTO agree to keep the information exchanged confidential; it may only be shared with their representatives and with the federal and Quebec public servants who need to know it.
At the request of those public servants, the parties must send them the confidential information within seven days.
The agreement also covers information already exchanged before its coming into force.
The Direction générale must send a copy of the signed agreement to the Minister of Transport and Sustainable Mobility.
The City is granting $40,000 in support to Créations Kurdar for the Nuit des Galeries 2026: $35,000 in cash and up to $5,000 in free municipal services.
The event takes place from September 3 to 6, 2026 in the place Royale, Vieux-Port and Petit-Champlain areas, for its 20th anniversary.
On September 5, about thirty galleries will open within a 1.2 km festive perimeter where drinking alcohol on the street is allowed.
Four festive zones with bars and live music will be set up: place FAO, place Royale, parc Félix-Leclerc and parc de la Cetière.
On September 3, 4 and 6: meetings with the artists (youth and school component), gourmet meals, arts brunch, family workshops and cocktail events in the galleries.
The event's budget is $211,000; the City's grant covers 16.6% of it and depends on sufficient contributions from the other partners.
The City will pay $31,500 in 2026 and $3,500 in 2027, the latter amount being subject to the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 530, rue des Canetons, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood (Arrondissement des Rivières).
A proposed industrial building will be allowed to cover 14% of the lot instead of the minimum of 20% required by the borough's planning by-law.
The owner wants to keep large outdoor areas for the storage and logistics of its industrial activities.
The back of the lot includes a section of the rivière Lorette, its bank, part of a wetland and a wooded area, which will be preserved.
According to the analysis in the file, the exemption has no impact on neighbouring lots or on safety, health or the environment.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on May 4, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is buying the house at 1700, avenue Verlaine, in the arrondissement des Rivières, for $533,000 plus taxes.
The 662.30-square-metre lot will be used to build a pumping station to protect the stormwater system.
The purchase is part of the rivière Lorette redevelopment project, which aims to limit the risks of flooding and overflow.
The City will take possession of the property no later than June 1, 2027; until then, the sellers pay for maintenance, heating, electricity, insurance and snow removal.
The building and its outbuildings will be demolished later; the funds for the demolition will be authorized separately.
The property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $331,000.
The money comes from the loan by-law for the work against flooding of the rivière Lorette.
The City is sending two chiefs from the Service de protection contre l'incendie to a training course on flammable liquids and gases, from September 22 to 24, 2026, in College Station, Texas.
The three-day training is given by the Texas A&M Engineering Extension Service (TEEX) and covers foam firefighting and response tactics.
The City says this training serves to meet its commitments with the Port de Québec and to maintain a minimum number of qualified chiefs for a leak of flammable liquids or gases at the port.
The authorized expense is $8,997.04, taken from the training budget of the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
The expenses will be reimbursed upon submission of supporting documents, with a tolerated variance of no more than 10% of the authorized amount.
Registration had to be made before July 21, 2026.
A similar training had been authorized for two representatives in September 2023.
The City is awarding Groupe Colas Québec inc., of Lévis, a contract for cold planing work and the application of tack coat.
The contract is estimated at $663,860 (before GST and QST); the net cost to the City is estimated at $696,970.02.
The work runs from the date the contract is awarded until November 30, 2026, across the whole territory of the city of Québec.
This is preparatory work: the paving operations will be done later by the crews of the Service des travaux publics.
The work includes signage, traffic management, planing of the pavement, sweeping, application of the tack coat and cleaning of the site.
Only one bid was received, 13.1% above the requesting department's estimate ($586,950).
The contract includes a fuel price adjustment clause.
The City is adding the borough director responsible for prevention and quality of the environment to the list of people authorized to sign agreements about trees located along the tramway route.
These agreements deal with preserving, cutting down, replacing and maintaining trees.
Until now, this power belonged to the Division de la foresterie urbaine et de l'horticulture, whose name is also being corrected in the by-law.
The word "abattage" (cutting down) is being added to the title of the relevant chapter of the by-law on delegation of powers.
The executive committee is aiming for adoption on June 17, 2026; no financial impact is indicated.
The City is awarding the work of repairing, maintaining and rebuilding the roofs of its buildings to Toitures R. Martin, of Québec.
The contract covers two lots: the Centre sector (La Cité-Limoilou, Beauport, Charlesbourg and ExpoCité) and the Ouest sector (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, Les Rivières, La Haute-Saint-Charles).
Each lot is estimated at $979,500 before taxes, for an estimated net expenditure of $2,056,705.12.
The work involves roofs made of cedar shingles, TPO membranes, metal, asphalt shingles and elastomeric membrane.
The contract lasts two years from the awarding, with an option for 12 additional months, indexed according to the Consumer Price Index.
Three bids were received; the lowest was found non-compliant because it failed to show that it had the required workforce.
The amounts depend on the approval of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.
The City is buying bench seats to replace those of the 2,592 Premium seats at the Centre Vidéotron, at 250-B, boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The contract goes to the company Irwin, of Grand Rapids, Michigan, described as the only authorized distributor, so there was no call for tenders.
The cost is US$182,259.86, including shipping and importation, or about CA$254,673.52 at today's exchange rate, plus taxes.
Full delivery is expected in September 2026.

The City will first replace the most deteriorated seats before the Jeux du Canada and the 2027 world women's hockey championship, then the rest depending on the condition of the seats and the events calendar.
The money comes from the "Pérennité Centre Vidéotron" financial reserve.
The City is giving up the mortgage it held on the building at 970-972, rue Saint-Jean, in Vieux-Québec.
This mortgage secured a $6,400,000 grant paid in 2018 to restore the building's exterior envelope (Le Capitole).
The City considers that the restoration work was carried out to its satisfaction.
The request for the discharge comes from 9372-4185 Québec inc., which took over the building and the agreement from Capitole de Québec inc. in 2018.
The $640,000 holdback was paid in part in 2020 and completed on May 6, 2022; the obligation to obtain the City's approval before selling the building runs until May 6, 2027.
Despite the discharge, the City keeps all its other rights and remedies provided for in the agreements.
The owner of 2402, rue de la Faune, in La Haute-Saint-Charles, wants to convert a ground-floor commercial space to add two dwelling units.
The by-law requires 6 parking spaces; the project provides 5.
The City is exempting the owner from providing the missing space, on the condition that he pays $500 to the "Fonds de stationnement" (parking fund).
The payment must be made no later than 30 days after the borough council adopts the resolution.
The analysis notes that the area, between rue William-Marsh and avenue Lapierre, is well served by public transit and that on-street parking occupancy there ranges from low to moderate.
The City wants to obtain a servitude (right of use) on a piece of land along 1re Avenue, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité streetcar project.
The servitude covers about 9 square metres of part of lot 6 727 881 and will be used to move public utility conduits and networks.
It is a real and perpetual servitude: it stays attached to the land permanently.
The City will first try to reach a negotiated agreement with the owners; if that fails, it may expropriate.
The owners have been informed of the process, the next steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
If the project no longer needs this servitude, the City's lawyers will be able to drop the expropriation proceedings.
The money comes from the agglomeration loan by-law related to the structuring public transit network.
The City is correcting a mistake made in 2024 in its planning by-law for 212, rue Saint-Jean (Château des Tourelles), in the Saint-Jean-Baptiste neighbourhood.
In 2024, it wanted to remove the limit of 11 tourist accommodation units at this location, but one of the sections was not changed. The new by-law finishes the job.
The building will be able to be occupied by a use in group C10 "Établissement d'hébergement touristique général" (general tourist accommodation establishment), with no maximum number of units.
The rules on the minimum and maximum number of parking spaces will not apply to this occupancy.
The occupancy must begin within 24 months after the by-law comes into force, otherwise the authorization lapses.
The by-law contains provisions subject to approval by referendum; the conseil de quartier de Saint-Jean-Baptiste will give its opinion and hold the public consultation meeting.
No additional information measures are planned, as the City considers that this is a matter of correcting an omission without changing the substance of the decision already approved.
The Ville de Québec is signing an agreement with the ministère de l'Environnement to receive a $25,500,000 grant.
The money will be used to restore or create wetlands and bodies of water: land purchases, studies, design, work and long-term monitoring.
The agglomeration of Québec aims to restore or create 70 to 90 hectares of these environments by 2033.
The grant will be paid out between 2026 and 2031, including $2,300,000 in 2026-2027, $3,600,000 in 2027-2028 and $9,400,000 in 2028-2029.
The agreement ends on October 31, 2031; the City will have to submit an audit report on spending no later than September 30, 2031.
Two committees will follow up on the agreement: the City is appointing Marie-Line Pedneault, director of the Division de la biodiversité et des changements climatiques, to the steering committee.
The Conseil du trésor still has to authorize the agreement for it to come into force.
The City is awarding Charles-Auguste Fortier inc. the contract to build a centre for managing surplus excavated soil and treating contaminated soil, for $32,042,438.41 before taxes.
The centre will be built in the Beauport borough.
The project includes an administrative building with garages, a storage shelter, scales, a wheel wash and soil treatment equipment.
Five companies submitted bids; Charles-Auguste Fortier inc. offered the lowest price, 12.4% below the City's estimate ($36,576,334).
The net cost to the City is $33,640,555.03, funded by several urban agglomeration loan by-laws.
The contract includes clauses for adjusting bitumen and fuel prices.
The executive committee adopted the decision (resolution CE-2026-0337).
The Ville de Québec will pay up to $130,000 to the Coopérative de solidarité Notre-Dame de Jacques-Cartier, also known as La Nef.

The money will be used to prepare the plans and specifications to restore and redevelop the former Notre-Dame de Jacques-Cartier church, in the Saint-Roch neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The project costs $204,150 in total: $130,000 from the City, $59,150 from the organization and $15,000 from the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The design work runs from February 2026 to May 2027, with the final plans and the cost estimate to be produced in May 2027.
The organization plans to keep its 32 current jobs and create one job.
The grant comes from the Soutien aux projets structurants component of the Fonds régions et ruralité, which can fund up to $300,000 per project.
The decision is up to the Québec urban agglomeration council.
The City is giving $25,000 to the organization 24H ChronoSports for the summer of 2026.
The money will fund a welcome camp in the Saint-Roch neighbourhood for children from newly arrived immigrant families, including refugees.
The camp is for young people aged 7 to 14 and offers sports, outings and daily exposure to French and to Quebec social and cultural norms.
The camp is presented as a complement to the City's Programme Vacances-été and prepares young people to attend a regular day camp the following year.
The organization must mention the City's contribution in its publications, take part in an end-of-project meeting, and submit a report on its activities and a financial report.
The same amount of $25,000 had been granted to 24H ChronoSports in 2025; in 2023 and 2024, $20,000 went to the Centre multiethnique de Québec.
The executive committee adopted the decision (resolution CE-2026-0189) on February 11, 2026.
The City wants to obtain a permanent public utility easement on a piece of land bordering 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The easement covers about 15 square metres of part of lot 1 570 422.
The land can be acquired by agreement with the owner or by expropriation; the owner has been informed of the process and has a contact person at the City.
This easement will be used to move public utility conduits and networks along the route.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings and to withdraw from them if the project no longer needs the easement.
The entire piece of land is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $187,000, which is $512.47 per square metre.
The money comes from urban agglomeration loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 tied to the structuring public transit network.
The City is awarding Intermodale Paysagement Déneigement inc. the work to build trails at parc Chauveau for $659,197.08 (plus GST and QST).
The work involves walking, cross-country skiing and mountain biking trails, in the Arrondissement des Rivières.
The contract also covers wooden footbridges, walkways and stairs with guardrails, culverts and drains.
An observation area will be built near the rivière Saint-Charles, and the new trails will be connected to the existing ones.
The net cost to the City is $692,074.53, funded by a loan by-law ($511,595.53) and a grant from the Communauté métropolitaine de Québec ($180,479.00).
Seven companies submitted bids; the one selected submitted the lowest price, 9% below the estimate of the requesting department.
The City is giving $30,000 to the Grand Prix Cycliste Beauce for the "Étape Québec du Tour de Beauce" in 2026.
It is adding up to $13,000 in free municipal services and up to $3,000 in the purchase of goods and services, for total support of $46,000.
The event takes place on June 13, 2026: an 8 km individual time trial with starts on boulevard Champlain and the finish at the top of the côte de Sillery.
The event's planned budget is $678,000; the City's grant represents 4.4% of it.
The support is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners.
The grant is paid in three instalments ($18,000, $9,000 and $3,000) depending on the conditions met, the last one when the financial statements and the final report are submitted.
The organization must give the City its complete final report no later than 90 days after the event.
The City is paying $134,223.30 (plus taxes) for its annual membership fee to the Fédération canadienne des municipalités.
The membership fee covers the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
The calculation combines a base rate of $5,540 and 23.42¢ per resident, for a population of 549,459 people.
With net taxes, the expense comes to $140,917.70, taken from the operating budget of the Direction générale.
The membership fee is going up compared to previous years: $121,585.74 in 2023-2024, $125,651.74 in 2024-2025 and $129,882.57 in 2025-2026.
City council adopted the decision on February 3, 2026.
The arrondissement de Beauport is giving out 15 grants totalling $53,440 to 12 organizations in the area.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget (the "Soutien aux organismes" activity).

The largest amounts go to Matinée Frimousses ($10,000 for "Le cirque dans ton parc", 2nd year), the Centre ressources pour femmes de Beauport ($8,500 for yoga and meditation workshops) and Expression-Danse de Beauport ($8,500 for classes for children aged 0 to 3).

Several grants are used to buy equipment: a kiln for the Atelier de céramique Saint-Elme ($4,250), training equipment for the Club BMX Beauport ($3,805), and percussion instruments for the École de musique des Cascades ($3,723).
Other amounts pay for the organizations' visibility: branding for the Club BMX ($3,400), a redesign of Re-Fa-Vie's website ($2,931), and a community bulletin board for the CDC de Beauport ($1,567).
The Club FADOQ Beauport and the Regroupement du loisir communautaire de Beauport each receive $500 for an anniversary supper.
Applications had to be submitted by March 15, 2026 at the latest; the decision was intended for the borough council meeting of May 12, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is granting a subsidy of up to $300,000 to Méduse, a cooperative that brings together 12 cultural organizations in the Saint-Roch neighbourhood.
The money will be used for the studies and assessments of Phase II of the METÉA project, which plans the modernization and energy transition of Méduse's nine heritage buildings.
The total cost of this phase comes to $556,623: Méduse is putting in $220,623, Desjardins $20,000, the RISQ $15,000 as a loan and the Assemblée nationale $1,000.
The work being considered for later includes moving Antitube's cinema, new exhibition halls, a terrace and an observatory; the full project is roughly estimated at $25M.
The project sheet provides for 5 jobs created and the retention of the 65 current jobs.
The money comes from the Fonds régions et ruralité, entrusted to the City by the Government of Québec.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The City wants to obtain two servitudes (rights of use) on a lot bordering avenue Moncton, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough, for the TramCité project (structural public transit network).
A permanent servitude of about 23.2 m² would allow public utility conduits and networks to be moved; a second servitude, for passage and construction, would last 3 years over about 11.6 m².

The City is authorizing the acquisition by mutual agreement or by expropriation: an agreement had already been reached with the owners, but operational issues are leading it to start expropriation proceedings.
Discussions with the owners may continue during the expropriation process.
The Service des affaires juridiques may drop the proceedings, in whole or in part, if the project no longer needs the servitudes.
The lot, for the land only, is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $404,000, or $1,092.78 per square metre.
The funds come from urban agglomeration loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the structural network.
The Ville de Québec is changing the zoning of zone 52107Ib, in the parc industriel de Beauport, around 395, boulevard Armand-Paris (quartier 5-2, district de la Chute-Montmorency–Seigneurial).
The change allows administrative services (group C1), up to a maximum of 1,100 square metres of floor area per building.
It also allows the use "hand car wash service", which corresponds to the activities of a tenant of the building.

The owner was also asking for the return of drinking establishments, the sale or rental of small vehicles and light vehicles, car washes in general, and garden centres: these uses are not being added.
These uses had been removed from the zone in December 2024 during the review of the zoning of the parc industriel de Beauport.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; a public consultation meeting is planned, followed by a seven-day period to submit written comments.
The Ville de Québec is approving an employment contract with Denis-H Turcotte as associate director of the Service de police.
The contract ends on June 1, 2026.
His annual salary remains at $293,358 (2026 scale, DS1).
He reports to the Deputy Director General – Aménagement, mobilité et sécurité urbaine.
He is bound by exclusivity: he cannot work for anyone else during the contract.
If he resigns, he must give four weeks' written notice; if the City ends the contract, the notice period ranges from 3 to 12 months.
The funds, including employee benefits, are provided for in the budget of the Police activity.
The City is creating a 10-minute limited parking zone, in effect at all times, on carré Rose-Leclerc, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The zone is on the south side, in front of the main door of 9595, carré Rose-Leclerc, and covers two parking spaces.
The zone begins 8.5 metres west of rue de Martigny and extends 12.5 metres to the east.
Residents of the building had asked for this measure to make it easier to reach the ramp for people with reduced mobility and to allow paratransit vehicles to get through.
No on-street parking space is being removed.
The borough council adopted the decision on June 23, 2026 (order O-593).
The Ville de Québec has reached an out-of-court settlement with Les Immeubles Martin et Martin Inc. to close the expropriation of a piece of land located on boulevard Laurier.
The final expropriation compensation is set at $215,000.00 plus applicable taxes (principal, interest, additional compensation and expert appraisal fees).
Since the City had already paid a provisional compensation of $154,300.00 in March 2023, $60,700.00 remains to be paid to the company by cheque.
This payment fully and definitively settles the case opened before the Tribunal administratif du Québec in September 2022.
The land had been acquired as part of the tramway project of the Réseau structurant de transport en commun.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the Réseau structurant de transport en commun.
The City's attorneys, Giasson et associés, are authorized to sign the necessary documents.
The City is awarding five companies the work of mowing lawns, cutting tall grass and cleaning up land on its territory, from the awarding of the contracts until November 30, 2028.

The contracts cover 10 lots (1 to 5 and 7 to 11), meaning areas such as Loretteville, Val-Bélair, Cap-Rouge, Sillery, Les Saules, Saint-Roch, Vanier, Lebourgneuf, Maizerets, Chutes Montmorency and Orsainville.

Gazon 911 inc. gets lots 3, 7 and 9; Intermodale Paysagement Déneigement inc. gets lots 2, 5 and 8; Le Groupe Essa inc. gets lots 1 and 11; Les Entretiens Titan S.E.N.C. gets lot 4; 9469-9717 Québec inc. (Les Entreprises la Québécoise) gets lot 10.
The amounts per lot range from $291,693.69 (lot 1) to $540,752.34 (lot 8), plus GST and QST.
The total net expense is $4,483,666.67, split into $1,494,555.56 per year for 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
Lots 6 and 12 to 16 were awarded through delegation of powers, and lots 17 and 18 are the subject of another file.
The arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is paying out $61,455 in 20 grants to 15 recreation and community life organizations.
The applications had to be submitted by March 15, 2026 at the latest, under the programs of the Cadre de soutien aux organismes reconnus.
The largest amounts go to Craque-Bitume ($10,000) for a project on caring for oneself and the planet, and to L'Engrenage Saint-Roch ($8,500) for activities against food insecurity in Basse-Ville.

Patro Roc-Amadour receives $6,899 to support people living with a disability during spring break and pedagogical days; Loisirs Montcalm ($1,584) and Centre des loisirs St-Sacrement ($792) also receive help for support services.
Société du domaine Maizerets receives $6,019 and Maîtres Nageurs de la Capitale $1,500 for their operating expenses (year 2 and year 3).
Other amounts are used to buy materials and equipment, to redesign websites and brand images, for anniversary activities and for training.
The Ville de Québec is entrusting the Société du domaine de Maizerets with reception, customer service, room rentals and reservation coordination at the domaine de Maizerets.
The agreement covers January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027.
The City will pay $316,928.49 per year (plus GST and QST), an amount indexed to the consumer price index in 2027.
The organization will pay the City a royalty of 10% on its registration and space rental revenues, up to a maximum of $25,528.10 per year.
The organization keeps the revenues from space rentals in exchange for other tasks, such as setting up the rooms.
Recognized organizations will use the spaces free of charge, and the City will compensate the organization for this lost revenue.
The net expense for the urban agglomeration comes to $665,470.60, with the 2027 portion remaining conditional on the adoption of the budget.
The Ville de Québec will pay up to $1,000,000 to Université Laval for a project supporting student and university entrepreneurship.
The money comes from the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, a fund entrusted to the City by the Government of Québec.

The project lasts 30 months and splits the activities into two parts: the Centre d'entrepreneuriat universitaire (idea development, training) and the Épicentre incubator (technology and science businesses).
Total cost of the project: $4,529,188, also funded by Québec ($1,100,000), Canada ($139,885) and the Université itself ($2,289,303).
The activities take place in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge; 4 jobs would be created.
Announced targets: raise awareness among more than 10,000 people per year, train more than 300 participants, support about 55 businesses, including 35 at Épicentre.
The decision must be made by the Québec urban agglomeration council.
The City is releasing the list of grants paid to nine neighbourhood councils (conseils de quartier) between July 1 and December 31, 2025, for projects the councils themselves proposed.

Air quality: $10,000 to the conseil de quartier de Vanier (Air'Vanier project) and $10,000 to the conseil de quartier de l'Aéroport to install about twenty sensors in the homes of volunteer residents (Primev'Air project).
Public consultations: $9,500 to the conseil de quartier des Jésuites to build an action plan, and $10,000 to Saint-Jean-Baptiste for the strategic plan Vision Faubourg Saint-Jean-Baptiste 2027-2030.

Events and neighbourhood life: $3,500 to Cap-Rouge (Halloween party and Christmas Market), $800 to Lac-Saint-Charles (activity for the volunteers of the Frigo du Lac), $450 to Montcalm (workshop on getting bikes ready for winter).

Other amounts: $1,220.30 to Saint-Émile for five plaques commemorating the neighbourhood's 100th anniversary, and $4,200 to Saint-Sacrement for promotional material using the new visual identity of the neighbourhood councils.
Since 2024, it is the director of the Service des relations citoyennes et des communications who awards these grants, and he must report on them to the executive committee twice a year.
The City is awarding La Compagnie de Parterres Portugais ltée the contract to redevelop the play areas at parc Saint-Denys, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, for $1,938,425 (plus GST and QST).
The work, split into two phases, will take place in 2026 and 2027.
The project will rebuild two play areas (ages 2-5 and 5-12) and a tennis facility with three lit courts, including fencing.
It also adds a skating surface, a lit parking lot, a lit multi-purpose path, a low wall, trails, a small square, furniture, drainage and landscaping.
Five companies submitted bids; the winning bid is the lowest and is 9.6% below the City's estimate.
The net cost to the City is $2,035,103.95, funded through loan by-laws and the parks and playgrounds funds.
The City is awarding Échafaudage Vermeren inc., of Stoneham-et-Tewkesbury, a contract for scaffolding work on various structures.
The contract runs from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2029, for an estimated amount of $1,766,117.70 before taxes.
Two 12-month renewals are possible, with an annual adjustment based on the Consumer Price Index.
The net cost for the agglomeration is estimated at $1,854,202.82, after the QST refund.
The work is requested by the Service de la gestion des matières résiduelles et de la valorisation.

Four companies submitted bids: the lowest bid ($1,515,285.00) was found to be non-compliant, because it lacked employees with the required experience in heavy industrial settings and the required health and safety training.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets by the competent authorities.

The City is authorizing two members of the Service de police de Québec to attend the 121st Annual Summit and Trade Show of the Canadian Association of Chiefs of Police, in Edmonton, from August 16 to 18, 2026.
Director Dominic Gaudreau and specialized services inspector Martin Salesse (or their replacements) will make the trip.
The authorized expense is $7,025.14, taken from the Service de police's operating budget.
The Service des finances will reimburse the expenses upon presentation of receipts.
An overrun of no more than 10% of the authorized amount will be accepted without further authorization.
In 2025, three members attended the summit in Victoria for $9,549.45.
The City is correcting a mapping error: lot 1 696 868, located in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, had been left out of the zoning plan.
The lot, in the Cap-Rouge neighbourhood near rue du Petit-Hunier and the railway, becomes the new zone 37045Ha.

Housing may be built there (detached houses with 1 to 3 dwellings, semi-detached houses with 1 to 2 dwellings, row houses with 2 dwellings, maximum 6 buildings per row) and a park may be laid out there.
Buildings will be limited to 9 metres in height and 30% of the land must remain green space.
A 20-metre wooded strip must be planted along the railway, with at least 50% evergreen trees.
The conseil de quartier du Cap-Rouge will give its opinion and hold a public meeting; people will have 7 days after the meeting to submit written comments.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The City is awarding Terrassement Portugais inc. the contract to redevelop the recreational surfaces at parc Bon-Pasteur, in Charlesbourg, for $1,707,640.89 (plus GST and QST).
The work involves demolishing the existing soccer field, skating rink, pétanque courts, lighting, pathways and furniture.
A new soccer field, volleyball and pétanque courts, gathering areas including one for teenagers, concrete pathways and paving will be built there.
The project also includes slabs, concrete curbs, street furniture and landscaping.
The net expense for the City is $1,792,809.48, funded by a loan by-law ($1,610,810.50) and the Fonds de parcs et terrains de jeux de Charlesbourg ($181,998.98).
Four companies submitted bids; the lowest offer is 12.4% below the department's estimate, which was $1,949,518.18 before taxes.
The City is amending its agreement with the Administration portuaire de Québec for the management of the Saint-André parking lot, on the quai Saint-André, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The parking lot now has 85 spaces in total: 28 belong to the City and 57 to the Administration portuaire, following a redevelopment that eliminated one space.
Net revenues from the parking lot are shared based on the number of spaces: 67.10% for the Administration portuaire and 32.90% for the City, and the City's share goes to the general fund.
The amendment updates the land covered by the agreement, following an exchange of lots completed by notarial deed on December 14, 2022.
The agreement now specifies who builds and maintains the flower beds and trees around the parking lot.
The City paid $11,293, plus taxes, for the greening work carried out jointly in the summer of 2025.
The Government of Quebec authorized these changes through an order issued on February 18, 2026.
The City is amending its agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications for the inventory of buildings constructed before 1940.
The inventory covers nearly 16,500 buildings in the city and in the other municipalities of the agglomeration de Québec.
The City must still have the inventories adopted by the urban agglomeration council before April 1, 2026, as required by the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel.
The Ministère has not yet provided the computer tool for receiving the data: the City will have 18 months after it is put in place to send them.
The City will finish the historical documentation of certain buildings before December 31, 2026 and will submit its final report before March 31, 2027.
The financial assistance remains at a maximum of $1,500,000, covering up to 50% of eligible expenses; the final payment of $125,000 is postponed to the 2026-2027 fiscal year.
All other clauses of the agreement signed on April 24, 2023 remain unchanged.
The City wants to change the zoning of a residential area in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood, north of the intersection of avenue Myrand and chemin Sainte-Foy (Saint-Louis–Sillery district).
The change reduces the required side setbacks from 5 metres to 3.5 metres and the rear setback from 15 metres to 9 metres.
The owner of a vacant lot at 754, avenue Myrand wants to build a four-storey, 16-unit building there; the height already meets the standards, but not the current setbacks.
In this zone, about 14 of 39 buildings already have non-compliant rear setbacks and almost all have non-compliant side setbacks.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The conseil de quartier de la Cité-Universitaire will be consulted and will hold the public meeting; interested people will have seven days after the meeting to send their comments in writing.
The City is awarding P.E. Pageau inc. (Québec) a $4,420,498 contract (before GST and QST) for paving, sidewalk and landscaping work.
The work includes rebuilding sidewalks and roadways, laying asphalt, road markings, permanent signage, lighting and traffic signals.
Five boroughs are affected: Beauport, La Cité-Limoilou, Les Rivières, La Haute-Saint-Charles and Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
Streets involved: boulevard Saint-Jacques, 18e Rue, corridor piétons Vézina, côte du Verger, avenue Turbide, boulevards de l'Ormière and Masson, rue Ernest-Gagnon.
Three companies submitted bids; P.E. Pageau inc. submitted the lowest price, 7.7% below the City's estimate.
The net cost to the City is $4,640,970.34, funded by two agglomeration loan by-laws.
The contract includes price adjustment clauses for asphalt and fuel.
The City is borrowing $12,612,000 to pay its share of the reconstruction of the Canadien National railway bridge that crosses 4e Avenue, between 25e Rue and rue des Bouleaux Est.
The loan will be repaid over five years out of the City's general revenues.
CN informed the City that the bridge, built in 1951, is at the end of its useful life and must be rebuilt in the short term.
A federal order issued at the time of construction makes the City responsible for maintaining and repairing the bridge.
The total cost of the preparatory work and the reconstruction is estimated at about $27,112,000, to be confirmed once the plans and specifications are done.
The City will be able to award contracts of up to 10% of the amount ($1,261,200) before the by-law is approved by the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation.
Two memorandums of understanding will have to be approved later: one for the preparatory work and another for the reconstruction.
The City is borrowing $550,000 to buy vehicles and motorized equipment for the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
The money will be used to replace light vehicles of the Service de protection contre l'incendie that have reached the end of their useful life.
The spending also covers professional and technical services contracts and the hiring of the staff needed for the purchases.
The loan will be repaid over ten years.
The City is taking $55,000 (10% of the expense) from its general fund, which will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The amounts are planned for the years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 capital works program; the expense is shared between the City and the agglomeration.
The vehicles and equipment may be electric or run on hydrocarbons, and they serve the entire territory covered.

The City is entrusting the organization Loisirs Lebourgneuf inc. with the specialized maintenance and supervision of the recreational and sports facilities and equipment in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The contract runs from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2029, that is 36 months, and replaces the agreement that ends on April 30, 2026.
The City will pay $621,157.02 (plus GST and QST); the net expense is estimated at $652,137.24.
The amounts are divided between the maintenance of sports fields, the operation of community recreation centres and the operation of outdoor skating rinks.
The amounts planned for 2027, 2028 and 2029 depend on the approval of the budgets for those years.
The price will be adjusted according to the minimum wage in effect on May 1, 2027 and May 1, 2028.

The Ville de Québec is submitting four financial assistance applications totalling $1,139,679 to the Véloce III program of the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for the year 2026-2027.
The expenses for the four projects are estimated at $2,879,811 (net of taxes).

One project moves part of the corridor du Littoral (Route verte 5) off the Port de Québec's land, along rue Abraham-Martin, with a two-way bike path and a sidewalk separated by a planted median strip (assistance requested: $400,000).

Three projects involve boulevard Pierre-Bertrand: redevelopment of the intersections and U-turns at rue Fortin and rue du Marais ($80,906), at rue des Entrepreneurs and rue Samson ($154,674), and improvement of the cycling facilities between rue Samson and boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel ($504,099).
The City commits to carrying out the projects according to the program's rules and to obtaining the required authorizations; otherwise, the financial assistance will be terminated.
The summary indicates no financial impact for the City.
The City is changing the zoning of zone 23003Cb, an area of rue du Marais located west of boulevard Pierre-Bertrand, in the Vanier neighbourhood.
Medical clinics and psychology, acupuncture or social assistance offices (P5 uses, health care without lodging) will be allowed to set up there, with a maximum of 200 square metres per establishment.
The limit of two fuel pump islands in the zone is being removed: there are already three on site, and the chart is being corrected to reflect the situation.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to a referendum.
The conseil de quartier de Vanier will be consulted and will hold the public consultation meeting; interested people will have seven days after the meeting to send their comments in writing.
The file is covered by the Politique de participation publique: the City will add information and feedback measures.
Target date before the conseil d'arrondissement des Rivières: April 28, 2026.
The City is adding $90,000 (plus taxes) to the contract with the firm Résolys inc., which provides investigators for psychological harassment complaints at the City.
The contract therefore goes from $90,000 to $180,000 before taxes, or $206,955 including taxes.
The net additional expense is estimated at $94,488.75, paid out of the operating budget of the Service des ressources humaines.
The contract covers the period from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2026; the investigators are paid by the hour.
The City justifies the addition by needs for professional support that were higher than expected when the contract was first awarded.
The contract had been awarded without a call for tenders, an option provided for by law for professional services related to a proceeding before a court.
The executive committee approved the change on May 27, 2026.
The City is giving up to $250,000 to the Société de développement commercial Centre-ville de Québec to keep the Brigade propreté Saint-Roch running in 2026.
The Brigade picks up garbage and needles on the street and cleans the entrances of businesses in the Saint-Roch neighbourhood.
The project costs $312,500 in total: the City pays $250,000 (80%) and the SDC puts in $62,500.
The activities run from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The SDC must submit a report on its activities and a financial report by March 31, 2027, and pay back any amount it received in excess within 90 days of a request from the City.
In its first year, the Brigade picked up more than 2,600 bags of garbage and recycling and more than 700 used needles.
To fund the grant, the City is transferring $150,000 from the local contingency account to the budget of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets.
The Ville de Québec is giving $245,000 to Centraide Québec et Chaudière-Appalaches for the 2026 campaign.
The corporate donation goes from $175,000 in 2025 to $190,000 in 2026.
The City is keeping its $30,000 contribution to the Fonds d'impact Essentiel, which supports organizations working in food security, housing and support for people in difficulty.
It is also keeping $25,000 for the Chargés partenaires leadership program, which provides staff to Centraide during the fall campaign.
The total grant was $230,000 in 2024 and in 2025.
The money comes from City funds, under the "Gérer les subventions" budget item.
The Ville de Québec is authorizing spending of $25,100,000 to buy and install computer equipment and software, hire staff and retain professional services.
This money will be used to put into service computer and telecommunications solutions used both by the city and by the agglomeration.
The City is borrowing the same amount, repayable over three years, out of general revenues.
An amount of $2,510,000 (10% of the total) will be spent from the general fund before the by-law comes into force, and then repaid to that fund.
The amounts are provided for in the years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
The project covers the entire territory of the city.
The City is removing the loading zone located in front of 385, rue Victoria, in the Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur neighbourhood.
This removal adds two parking spaces on rue Victoria.
The loading zone was used by a business that has closed; the space has become a dwelling.
The request came from a resident of rue Victoria.
The zone being removed is on the east side, between rue Boisseau and rue Napoléon, over 10 metres.

The City is suing the owner of the building located at 616 to 622, rue Saint-François Est before the Superior Court, to force him to carry out the safety work or, if there is no other solution, to demolish the building.
Since the spring of 2023, the City has been asking the owner to maintain the building, without success; the owner has already received three fines totalling $10,000.
On April 21, 2026, an inspector found a thick layer of ice inside the building, reaching the ceiling in some places, caused by burst pipes.
On April 22, 2026, firefighters cut off the water and electricity, and evacuated and boarded up the building.
A City engineer concludes that there is a risk of partial collapse toward the outside: a safety perimeter has been set up and the street is closed to traffic.
The owner refuses any inspection by the City.
If the owner does not comply with the judgment, the City will be able to demolish the building and restore the land at the owner's expense, with a priority claim and a legal hypothec on the property.
The executive committee takes note of the list of additional expenses over $250,000 authorized by delegated employees, for the week of January 4 to 10, 2026.
Six change notices totalling $3,123,462.19 before taxes: $1,589,812.00 for Gestion des immeubles (2 notices) and $1,533,650.19 for Ingénierie (4 notices).
New police headquarters: $539,812 more for excavation and backfill (revised quantities, fuel, contract extension) and $1,050,000 more for construction management.
Redevelopment of rue Caron: $419,615 more for additional surface and landscaping work (planting pits, greening, archaeological discovery).
Redevelopment of rue Saint-Vallier Ouest: $572,881.89 more, including wider milling and paving on boulevard Charest Ouest and night monitoring of the temporary water main.
Parc Victoria connection zone: $267,153.30 more (cost indexation 2023-2025, lighting and roadway changes requested by the RTC).
Civil works in archaeological support: $274,000 more to reinforce a roof for the winter, heating and extension of the work site.
The City is cancelling its September 2025 decision and authorizing a new industrial park project south of the aéroport Jean-Lesage, in the Cap-Rouge - Laurentien district.
Société en commandite YQC will upgrade about 870 metres of route Jean-Gauvin and create a new 225-metre street, rue Marie-Louise-Hamel.
Phase 1 work is estimated at $19.5M before taxes: the developer pays $11.8M and the City pays $7.7M.
The City is adding $7.8M for a new water main and $7.5M in land purchases, for a total of $34.8M in investments.
The developer is handing over 10% of the land (29,335.9 m²) for park purposes; the City is buying another 173,362.90 m² for $6.5M, for a total of 202,698.80 m² of protected wooded areas and wetlands.
The developer must build a stormwater retention basin at its own expense and limit tree cutting within the street rights-of-way.
Phase 1 provides for about 66,888 m² of buildings, with an estimated property value of close to $225M.
The City is allowing a retail and service business to be set up on the ground floor of the building at 2949, chemin Sainte-Foy, in the Plateau neighbourhood.
This permission lasts five years from the date the by-law comes into force.
The owner bought the building in the summer of 2025 in order to move a grocery store there, expand it into the attached garage, and set up a café-terrace in the front yard.
The by-law relaxes certain standards: a front setback of 5 metres instead of 6 on rue de Rougemont, and a minimum of only one storey instead of two.
The conditions imposed: a maximum of four parking spaces in front of the façade, a green area of at least 50 square metres, and one tree planted in each front yard.
According to the document, the owner is considering demolishing the building and carrying out a residential project there within five years.

The conseil de quartier du Plateau will be consulted and will hold a public meeting; interested people will have seven days after that meeting to submit their comments in writing. The by-law may be subject to approval by referendum.
The City is borrowing $3,715,000 to develop or redevelop public and urban spaces throughout its territory.
The work targets universal accessibility, pedestrian safety, active transportation, gathering places and beautification.
It may include walking paths, plantings, street furniture, green infrastructure, public lighting and the integration of artworks.
The loan will be repaid over 15 years out of the City's general revenues.
The amount also covers hiring staff, professional and technical fees, the acquisition of buildings and easements, and the payment of subsidies.
The City may acquire the land or easements needed for the work by mutual agreement or by expropriation.
The funds are planned from 2026 to 2028 in the 2026-2035 investment plan; $371,500 (10%) is first taken from the general fund.
City council is asking Québec and Ottawa to increase their funding for upgrading the City's infrastructure (roads, water treatment plants, etc.).
The City is calling for an additional $223.3M per year for 20 years, shared equally among the three levels of government: $74.4M per year each, including $74.4M for the City itself.
According to the Bilan des actifs 2025, 15.7% of municipal assets are in poor condition ($4.2B) and the maintenance deficit has reached $2.6B.
Maintaining the assets and catching up on the backlog would require $5.5B over 10 years, while the City is planning only $2.0B: a gap of $3.5B.
For its part, the City plans to add $25M per year for asset maintenance and to put more money into its financial reserve without increasing its debt.
It is also asking that Québec combine all of its infrastructure funding into a single program, the TECQ, whose budget has dropped by 25% compared with the previous period.
New federal and provincial rules on wastewater treatment will apply starting in 2030, with no funding announced for municipalities.
The City is buying the house at 3160, rue de l'Anse-Victoria for $850,000, settling out of court the claim of its owner, Jean Genest.
The City had issued him a renovation and expansion permit on March 31, 2020; major work was done in 2021 in accordance with that permit.
Checks then revealed things that did not comply with the planning by-law and raised a safety issue, and the City revoked the permit, requiring that the building be moved or demolished.
Since there was no way to bring the building into compliance, the City is paying $850,000 in exchange for the property (two lots, including the one with the house).
The sale is made without legal warranty, and both parties fully release each other from anything arising from the permit.
The notarized deed is to be signed around the 60th day after the City's acceptance; the notary fees are paid by the City.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3480 on the acquisition of buildings for municipal purposes.
The City is borrowing $820,000 to install, maintain and restore public art and commemorative works in its collection.
The loan will be repaid over five years, out of the City's general revenues.
The work may take place anywhere in the city's territory, depending on needs.
The funds cover various types of work (repairs, renovation, relocation, lighting, plumbing, demolition) as well as the purchase of furniture and specialized equipment.
The City also plans to hire firms in restoration, engineering and other specialties.
An amount of $82,000 (10% of the expense) is taken from the general fund and will be paid back to it when the by-law comes into force.
The money is planned for 2026 to 2028 in the 2026-2035 capital works program.
The City is granting a minor exemption for a vacant lot on rue Hector-Bédard, in the Notre-Dame-des-Laurentides neighbourhood, in Charlesbourg (Arrondissement de Charlesbourg).

The exemption allows the turnaround built by the City on this private lot to stay, even though it does not meet the planning rules (access driveway and parking in front of the building façade, parking and street access more than 7 metres wide).
Without this exemption, no building could be put on the lot; the decision makes it possible to build a one- or two-dwelling building there.
The turnaround is used for snow removal, waste collection and emergency services access, and it stays in place.
Condition: the exemption applies only to the portion of the existing turnaround. If a building is constructed, the parking layout will have to meet the standards in effect at that time.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on February 4, 2026.

The City is adding mandatory stops on rue A.-R.-Décary, at the east and west approaches to the intersection with rue A.-R.-Décary, in the arrondissement des Rivières (district des Saules-Les Méandres).
The "Cédez le passage" (yield) signs currently in place at these approaches are being removed.
Drivers of road vehicles and bicycles will now have to stop at this location.

The Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente carried out a safety analysis and concluded that no approach to the intersection was controlled by a stop, which posed problems for motorists and for the many truck drivers.
The intersection in question is located a few metres from boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel.
The borough council adopted the decision on March 24, 2026 (resolution CA2-2026-0038).
The City is granting a minor exemption for 226, rue Louis-IX, in the Loretteville neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The building's rear setback is accepted at 5.4 metres, whereas the planning by-law requires 12.
The owner wants to renovate and raise the commercial building in order to set up a private school daycare service throughout the property.
Without the exemption, it would be impossible to add a storey and the stairway required for evacuation.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on June 15, 2026.
According to the analysis on file, the neighbouring buildings at the rear are located higher up, which reduces the impacts on the neighbourhood.
The City is adding mandatory stops on rue de la Faune, at the east and west approaches to the intersection with rue Grand Chef Thonnakona, in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The obligation to stop applies to drivers of road vehicles and to cyclists.
The measure follows the upcoming opening of rue Grand Chef Thonnakona, in Wendake, which will form a "T" intersection with rue de la Faune.
The analysis of projected traffic volumes concluded that stops were needed on each of the approaches of rue de la Faune.
The executive committee adopted ordinance O-330 on April 29, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0551).

The City is applying for government funding for four recreation projects: the outdoor pool in the Des Châtels neighbourhood, the synthetic turf soccer field at parc Victoria, the centre communautaire Charles-Auguste-Savard, and a covered refrigerated skating rink.

The applications are for the Programme d'aide financière aux infrastructures récréatives, sportives et de plein air (PAFIRSPA), component 1, of the ministère de l'Éducation, as well as other current or upcoming programs.
This program could cover up to 66% of eligible costs, up to a maximum of $20M per project.
The City commits to paying its share of eligible costs, ongoing operating expenses, and any cost overruns.
No contract involving direct costs will be awarded before a letter of announcement is received from the Minister.
The director of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire is authorized to sign and submit the application documents.
The City is expanding the area where businesses can claim financial assistance during the work on rue Saint-Vallier Ouest.
The expansion mainly affects the area of influence, west of rue Marie-de-l'Incarnation.
The City explains this change by new information about the work and its effects on customer traffic at businesses.
The infrastructure and redevelopment work runs from about April 1 to December 31, 2026.
The 2026 financial year is the one that counts for businesses located in the designated area.
This order replaces the one adopted by the executive committee on April 22, 2026.
The City is amending its planning program for the colline Parlementaire to limit new hotels and commercial tourist accommodations in Vieux-Québec.
Stated goal: encourage the creation of housing and attract new permanent residents, in a context of a housing crisis.
The use group "general tourist accommodation establishment" is removed in certain zones, particularly those with residential potential (vacant lots, outdoor parking lots, office buildings).
Tourist accommodation establishments already in place do not become non-conforming, and the use remains permitted in the blocks where it is already carried on.
New rules in certain areas: accommodation units only above the ground floor, a maximum of 25% of a building's floors, and a ban on mixing tourist accommodation and housing on the same floor.

Areas affected: Vieux-Québec–Cap-Blanc–colline Parlementaire and Saint-Jean-Baptiste, around rue Richelieu, rue D'Auteuil, rue Saint-Augustin, boulevard René-Lévesque Est and place D'Youville; the maximum permitted heights do not change.
A public consultation meeting will be held, with seven days after it to submit written comments.
The City is refusing the minor exemption request for 1221, avenue Charles-Huot, in the Sillery neighbourhood.
The owner wanted to divide the lot in two in order to build a detached single-family home.
The project called for a lot 4.12 metres wide instead of the required minimum of 16 metres, and a front setback of 3.38 metres instead of 6 metres.
The City points out that the 16-metre standard was adopted in 2022 to control how new buildings fit into the surrounding area.
According to the analysis, the lot cannot be divided in keeping with the standards, but being unable to subdivide it does not amount to serious harm: the owner keeps development potential.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended refusal on February 10, 2026.
The City is changing the rules of the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec (CUCQ), which approves work affecting architecture and built heritage.
The Commission will stop reviewing several smaller-scale types of work: accessory buildings, fences, low walls, mechanical equipment and parking areas, depending on the areas concerned.
In several areas, the Commission will review only the façade of main buildings, unless the owner has applied for a heritage restoration grant.
Buildings with high heritage value will be subject to stricter oversight, while those with more limited value will get simplified treatment.
The parc industriel Saint-Malo is removed from the Commission's scope; the ExpoCité area is brought under the rules that apply to shopping centre sites.
Applications to move or demolish buildings will have to include documents specified by the by-law.
New rules govern the review of demolitions in consolidation areas, favouring housing projects, including social housing.
The arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles approves five construction or expansion projects submitted for architectural review (PIIA).

Four projects involve the construction of detached buildings with several housing units on boulevard Pie-XI Sud, in the district of Val-Bélair (at numbers 1239, 1241A-1241J, 1245, and 1247A-1247F / 1249A-1249F).
One project involves the expansion of an industrial building at 9205, rue John-Simons, in the district of Loretteville/Les Châtels.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme had given a favourable opinion on these applications at its meeting of June 15, 2026.
Approval of the plans allows the permits for this work to be issued.

The City is repealing an agglomeration by-law that is no longer needed, which had exempted certain urban planning by-laws from a review of their compliance with the Schéma d'aménagement de l'agglomération de Québec.
This by-law has served no purpose since the passing, on March 25, 2025, of a provincial law (Bill 79) that amends the Loi sur l'aménagement et l'urbanisme.
Under this law, an urban planning by-law adopted by the city council or the urban agglomeration council is now deemed to comply with the Schéma as soon as it is adopted.
The urban agglomeration council was to make its decision on March 11, 2026; the document does not mention any financial impact.
The owner of 3270, rue Villeroi, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge (district du Plateau), wants to add two dwelling units in the basement, on top of the four units that already exist.
The by-law requires seven parking spaces; the project provides five. The City is therefore exempting the owner from providing the two missing spaces.
In exchange, the owner must pay $1,000 to the "Fonds de stationnement" (parking fund), no later than 30 days after the borough council adopts the resolution.
The City notes that the area, between rue de Strasbourg and avenue de Norvège, is served by public transit and that on-street parking occupancy there ranges from low to moderate.
The Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente recommends approving the request.
The City is granting a minor exemption for the construction of a new commercial building at 8700-8710, boulevard Henri-Bourassa, in Charlesbourg (quartier des Jésuites, district Louis-XIV).
The building may be located 2.2 metres from avenue Villeneuve, instead of the 5.0 metres normally required.
The parking area may be laid out 3.3 metres from the front lot line on the avenue Villeneuve side, instead of 4.0 metres.
According to the analysis, this closer placement makes it possible to add one parking space on the private property.
The exemption is justified by the triangular shape of the lot and by the fact that it faces two streets, which requires it to comply with two front setbacks.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on February 4, 2026.
The City is awarding four road marking contracts (lines, crosswalks and individual markings) valid until November 30, 2027, with an option for two 12-month renewals including price indexation.
Lot 5 (Lairet, Montcalm, Saint-Jean-Baptiste, Saint-Roch, Vieux-Limoilou, Vieux-Québec): 9219-4463 Québec inc. (A1 Lignes Jaunes), $503,731.32 before taxes.
Lot 8 (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge): 9219-4463 Québec inc. (A1 Lignes Jaunes), $394,213.00 before taxes.
Lot 9 (Cité Universitaire, Duberger–Les Saules, Saint-Sacrement): Entreprise Techline inc., $395,925.80 before taxes.
Lot 14 (Jésuites, Vieux-Moulin, Maizerets, districts 4-5 and 4-6): Pro-Marquage de la Capitale inc., $395,813.35 before taxes.
The total net expense comes to $1,773,956.44, that is $883,515.02 in 2026 and $890,441.42 in 2027, the latter amount remaining conditional on the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The 12 other lots in the call for tenders were awarded separately under the delegation of powers.
The Ville de Québec will sign an agreement with the Communauté métropolitaine de Québec to receive financial assistance of up to $180,479.
The money will be used to build hiking, cross-country skiing, mountain biking and fat biking trails at parc Chauveau.
The project calls for about 4 km of new hiking trails, 2.3 km of new cross-country ski trails, and the upgrading of 2.5 km of existing cross-country ski trails for mountain biking in the summer.
It also includes wooden footbridges, boardwalks and stairs, a rest area and a lookout over the rivière Saint-Charles.
Most of the new hiking trails will meet universal accessibility rules.
Work will begin in the spring of 2026 and will be completed no later than August 31, 2026.
The City will pay the rest of the cost, estimated at $570,471 including net taxes, through its loan by-laws.
The City is giving up to $124,180 in grants to professional cultural organizations to bring cultural activities into community centres.
Seven projects were selected in this first year of the call for projects; the entire budget has been allocated.
The projects will take place in 21 community centres, with 18 partner community organizations.
Each project can receive a maximum of $20,000, which can cover up to 100% of its budget.
Example: the Centre de valorisation du patrimoine vivant is receiving $20,000 for nine traditional dance workshops in Beauport, Charlesbourg and Les Rivières, free for the public.
Example: the Musée ambulant is receiving $20,000 for free contemporary art workshops in three community centres (Haute-Saint-Charles, Les Rivières, Beauport).
The money comes from the Entente de développement culturel between the City and the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The City is giving an official name to a new industrial park located south of the aéroport international Jean-Lesage.
The name chosen is « parc industriel du Sud-de-l'Aéroport ».
The area concerned is in the district of Cap-Rouge-Laurentien, in the arrondissement of Sainte-Foy-Sillery-Cap-Rouge.
The Service du développement économique et des grands projets had asked the Comité de commémoration et de toponymie to name this place.
The Comité explains that Québec's industrial parks are usually named after their sector, their arrondissement or the former municipality.
The Commission de toponymie du Québec was consulted to check the spelling of the name.
The document does not provide for any financial impact.
The City is banning U-turns on rue Triquet, between rue Nelles and rue Alexander, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The ban covers 125 metres in the school zone of the école primaire Saint-Yves.
Police officers and residents were reporting frequent U-turns in the school zone, especially by parents after dropping off their child.
The City says it is aiming for the safety of schoolchildren and better traffic flow.
The decision takes the form of ordinance O-763, adopted by the borough council (resolution CA3-2026-0146).
No financial impact is indicated in the file.
The Ville de Québec is signing an agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications to obtain financial assistance for the purchase of documents for the Bibliothèque de Québec in 2026.
The amount is not yet confirmed: the City estimates it at $1,850,000, which is the maximum of 66.7% of eligible expenses, with the City having to pay at least 33.3% of the rest.
The money will be used only to buy books, comic books, digital and audio-digital books, periodicals, sheet music, records, films, video games, periodicals and databases.
Purchases must be made in accredited bookstores in Québec, and it is the Institut canadien de Québec that makes them on behalf of the City.
The City will have to report each year to the ministère (a summary of acquisitions and the libraries' financial report).
The ministère is now asking that the agreement be signed before the file is analyzed; the final amount will be announced later by letter. The program's standard runs until March 31, 2028.
The estimated amount is provided for in year 2026 of the 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.

An owner on rang Sainte-Anne is asking the Commission de protection du territoire agricole du Québec (CPTAQ) for permission to split off part of lot 2 164 107, in the Aéroport neighbourhood (Cap-Rouge–Laurentien district).
The parcel involved is 320 square metres (0.032 hectare) and is already used for residential purposes.
The goal is to attach this piece of land to the residential property at 215, rang Sainte-Anne.
