The land is in an agricultural zone under the land use planning and development plan, and "housing" use is not allowed there; it is served by water and sewer services.
The City's analysis concludes there would be little or no effect on farming activities in the area: small area, already built-up area, soils with low agricultural potential.
The City recommends that city council support the application to the CPTAQ.
The Ville de Québec is entrusting the firm Eckler ltée, of Toronto, with managing the investments of the financial reserve tied to the pension plan deficit of the former Ville de Québec.
The contract is worth $232,991 (plus GST and QST) and covers October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2031.
The net cost to the City comes to $244,611.43, spread out from $7,231.80 in 2026 to about $50,000 per year from 2027 to 2031.
The firm will advise the supervision committee: reviewing the investment policy, tracking performance, selecting managers and quarterly reports.
The contract can be renewed up to five times for 12-month periods, with annual price indexation.
The contract was awarded directly, under a rule that allows this method for financial services contracts.
The amounts from 2027 to 2031 remain conditional on the adoption of the annual budgets.
The City is creating an advisory commission on mobility in the Vieux-Québec (intra-muros area).
The commission must define a "Vision 2036" for mobility and draw up a Mobility Plan 2026-2036 for the neighbourhood.
Three elected officials will sit on it: Councillor Mélissa Coulombe-Leduc (chair), Councillor Elainie Lepage and Councillor Yannick Fauteux.
Up to 16 citizen commissioners and representatives of local stakeholders will be recruited through a selection process.
The commission meets at least once every three months; its mandate ends if it does not sit for six months.
The Service des relations citoyennes et des communications will set up the commission and recruit the commissioners; the appointments will be submitted to a later city council meeting.
The document does not mention any financial impact.

The City is giving up to $282,000 in grants to cultural organizations in Québec, under the Produire component of the cultural development agreement with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The money supports 23 artistic production projects that will be professionally presented in Québec, between the summer of 2026 and the spring of 2027.

The amounts granted range from $3,000 to $18,000 per project; among others, $18,000 each to Centre d'artistes Ahkwayaonhkeh, Jamais Lu Québec, Centre de valorisation du patrimoine vivant and Mon père est mort.

The projects involve theatre, dance, music, storytelling, circus arts, visual arts and literary arts, in venues such as the Périscope, La Bordée, the Trident, the Diamant, the bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy and the Maison de la littérature.
A committee made up of people from the field and professionals from the Service de la culture et du patrimoine assessed the applications before recommending the projects.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3367, for the years 2024, 2025 and 2026.
The executive committee adopted the decision on June 17, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0829).
The City agrees to rank behind a private lender approved by CMHC for the mortgage it holds on the real estate project at 401, rue Saint-Paul.
This mortgage secured the commitments of LACODEV INC. tied to a municipal subsidy of no more than $626,000, granted in May 2025 for a mixed-use housing project.
Until now, lenders approved by CMHC were not on the list of creditors eligible for a transfer of rank; the City is correcting this situation for this project.
The usual conditions apply, except one (item 2 b) of the appendix), from which the developer is exempted.
The executive committee repeals its resolution of June 25, 2026 on the same subject, because it did not provide for this exemption.
The City will acquire a strip of land of about 4.9 square metres at 1609, rue Gagnon, in the borough of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
This land will be used to widen rue de la Faune, as part of the project to rebuild that street.
If the agreement with the owner falls through, the City may proceed by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to begin the acquisition process, either by mutual agreement or by expropriation.
The Division de l'arpentage will prepare the plans, technical descriptions and cadastral operations required.
The owner's land as a whole is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $198,000, or $170.09 per square metre.
The funds come from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 related to the redevelopment work on rue de la Faune.
The City is naming two new streets in Charlesbourg, in the Notre-Dame-des-Laurentides neighbourhood: rue de la Hampe and rue de l'Empennage.
These streets are part of a subdivision project north of rue Dorval, starting from rue de Sherwood, covering about 557 metres in total.
The project develops a vacant lot and will allow the construction of 53 detached single-family homes.
The names come from archery vocabulary, in connection with Club Sherwood, an archery association in the area founded in 1959.
The Comité de commémoration et de toponymie proposed the names, and the Commission de toponymie du Québec was consulted on the spelling.
The Ville de Québec is adopting the Plan Commerce 2026-2029, its fourth action plan to support businesses on commercial streets.
The plan covers three years, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029, and takes over from the current plan, which ends on March 31, 2026.
It applies to the territory of the agglomeration of Québec (Québec, Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, L'Ancienne-Lorette) and to Wendake.
Five directions: bring commercial streets to life, support business groups, support companies, encourage entrepreneurship and lead major projects.
The plan does not include any budget: the actions will be funded based on available funds, through the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale and the ten-year investment plan.
The document mentions impacts on businesses located along the route of the TramCité project, during and after the work.
From 2017 to 2025, the previous plans invested nearly $57 million in commercial streets and supported more than 400 events and projects.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 37, rue de la Migration, in the Vieux-Bourg neighbourhood in Beauport.
The house sits 5.0 metres from rue Christian, while the planning by-law requires 6.0 metres. This distance is now deemed to comply.
The request aims to bring the building's siting into compliance as part of a real estate transaction.
The building was constructed in 1976 with a building permit; complying with the by-law would require a partial demolition.
According to the analysis, no complaints have been made by neighbours to date.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on January 21, 2026.
The City is appointing Jean-Philippe Légaré as director of the Division du budget et de la planification financière, in the Service des finances.
His salary is set at $162,516, based on class 1 (B8) of the management salary scale.
The position became vacant following the retirement of Ginette Lachance.
Until now, he held the position of section head of financial performance and financial systems.
The position was filled through an internal and external competition (CADRR-035-2026).
The necessary funds, including employee benefits, are already included in the Finances budget.
The arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is again entrusting the management of the centre communautaire de Saint-Sacrement to Centre des loisirs St-Sacrement inc.
The organization will coordinate services there and offer recreational and community life activities.
The agreement covers the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2028.
The organization will pay the City a royalty of 10% on its revenues from registrations and room rentals, up to a maximum of $8,889 per year (plus taxes).
This amount will be indexed each year according to the consumer price index for the Québec region.
The amounts collected will go to the City's general funds.
The organization has managed this facility since a first agreement was signed in 2015.
The City is giving an official name to a neighbourhood park located on rue Monty, in the Aéroport neighbourhood, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The park will be called « parc du Petit-Singe ».
The name echoes the neighbouring rue Monty, which recalls the British field marshal Bernard Law Montgomery (1887-1976), nicknamed « Monkey » in his childhood.
The Comité de commémoration et de toponymie proposed this name to link the park's family-oriented purpose to the street's theme.
The Commission de toponymie du Québec was consulted to check the spelling.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The executive committee takes note of the filing of the financial statements and the investment statements of the City's sinking fund as at December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025.
The documents for 2022, 2023 and 2024 had not been filed with the executive committee; the City is filing them at the same time as those for 2025 to correct the situation.
The fund was worth $18,146,113 as at December 31, 2025, and it earned net income of $608,905.52 in 2025.
The fund was created in 2006 to repay a City loan that comes due in November 2026; $20,000,000 will then be available for that repayment.
Management of the fund is entrusted to the ministère des Finances du Québec.
The arrondissement de Beauport is granting minor exemptions at 2383-2387, boulevard Louis-XIV, in the Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux neighbourhood.
The owner wants to add a second storey to the building in order to create additional housing units there.
The side setback may be 2 metres instead of 4.5 metres, and the combined width of the side yards 6 metres instead of 9 metres.
The street access may be 6 metres wide, rather than being the same width as the driveway (3 metres).
Condition imposed: install a fence that is opaque over at least 80% of its surface along the northeast lot line, in the side and rear yard.

According to the analysis, complying with the regulations would require demolishing part of the building that has existed since 1986, and an Hydro-Québec pole prevents the creation of parking that complies with the rules for six housing units.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on the request on June 11, 2026.
The City is giving $68,915 to five recreation organizations to adapt their day camps for young people from immigrant backgrounds, as part of the Programme Vacances-Été 2026.
The amounts: Camp École Kéno inc. $30,265, Loisirs Vanier $18,050, Loisirs de St-Rodrigue inc. $12,025, Loisirs du Faubourg inc. $7,160, Loisirs du Trait-Carré $1,415.
The money is used to hire 10 staff spread over 10 sites, and to cover the salaries of specialized camp leaders, training, activity planning and materials.
More than 285 young people would be reached, in the boroughs of Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, Cité-Limoilou, Charlesbourg and Les Rivières.
The grants are paid in two stages: 80% ($55,132) first, then 20% ($13,783).
The City had given $98,070 to seven organizations in 2025 and $78,375 to four organizations in 2024 for the same type of support.
The City is giving $15,000 to the organization Ambulance Saint-Jean for the year 2026.
The money is to be used to improve the equipment of volunteer members and to fund their training.
The funding also serves to train the next generation of volunteers and to introduce new members to the medical field.
This is the same amount as the funding granted in 2023, 2024 and 2025.
The funds come from the City's budget, under the "Frais généraux" (general expenses) item.
The executive committee adopted the decision on July 8, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0976).
The Ville de Québec is signing an agreement with the Municipalité de Saint-Gabriel-de-Valcartier to supply it with drinking water from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2030.
The agreement formalizes a situation that has been in place since 1988: the City has already been supplying this municipality with water without a formal agreement since December 1997.
The water passes through valve chamber P-759, near 17995, boulevard Valcartier, and consumption is measured continuously by two flow meters.
The City is reserving a maximum flow of 1,200 m³ per day for the municipality, with estimated annual consumption of 438,000 m³ from 2026 to 2030.
If the municipality exceeds this flow significantly and repeatedly, the parties must meet and an overconsumption penalty may apply.
The City expects revenues of $394,000 per year, for each of the years 2026 to 2030.
The agreement renews automatically for five years (2031-2035), unless one party notifies the other at least six months before December 31, 2030.
The City is banning parking at all times on the south side of rue Léo-Lessard, in the arrondissement des Rivières (Neufchâtel-Lebourgneuf district).
The ban applies over 32 metres starting from boulevard des Gradins, heading west.
About three parking spaces will disappear; the document notes that residents of the area have access to private parking.
The measure follows a request from a citizen and an analysis by the Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente.
According to the City, vehicles parked on both sides near the intersection increased the risk of collisions and hindered traffic.
The City is paying an additional $55,787.50 (before taxes) to the firm BGLA inc. to update the preliminary study on rebuilding the Hôtel de Ville parking lot.
With this addition, the contract goes from $100,000 to $155,787.50 before taxes; the extra net cost for the City is $57,355.11.
The original $85,000 contract was awarded in April 2023, then increased by $15,000 in February 2024.
The firm must produce a new report with a revised analysis of the work phasing and an updated estimate of the project cost.
The study is being refocused on the long-term durability of the parking lot structures and includes decarbonization and electrification components.
The update stems from a spending rationalization exercise and a review of needs following the 2024 study.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3045.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 4, impasse de Hongrie, in Val-Bélair, to build an eight-unit building.
The setbacks to be respected are reduced: 3.6 m at the front instead of 6 m, 2.6 m on the left side instead of 8 m, 5.5 m at the rear instead of 12 m.
The seven-space parking area may be placed right up against the front line of the lot (0 m instead of 4 m) and be 18.3 m wide at the street instead of the 7 m maximum.
The spaces may also touch the side line (0 m instead of 0.5 m) and allow vehicles to enter and exit in reverse, which the standard prohibits beyond six spaces.
The owner must replant the shoreline and the riparian strip with native species to stabilize the banks.
The owner must also plant a dense hedge or install a fence along the right side line.
The street, the water main and the sewer are private: the City does not provide maintenance, snow removal or residual materials collection there.
The arrondissement de Charlesbourg is paying out 10 grants totalling $30,724 to 8 recreation and community life organizations.
The largest amounts go to Loisirs du Trait-Carré: $8,500 for the "Nouvelle Ludothèque de Charlesbourg" project (game lending) and $4,109 to buy games.

Four organizations are getting money for equipment: Club de gymnastique Québec Performance ($4,250 for mats), Hockey Charlesbourg ($2,199 for pucks) and the collective garden La tomate joyeuse ($1,250 for a broadfork and insect netting).
Loisirs Brio is receiving $3,520 to support people living with a disability during spring break, and $500 for a recognition evening.
Two grants are aimed at visibility: $4,250 to Maison du cœur pour femmes to redo its website and $1,646 to Maison des jeunes La Marginale for posters.
Vivre Grand (formerly AISQ) is receiving $500 for a brunch bringing together its members, volunteers and employees.
Applications had to be submitted no later than December 15, 2025; the money comes from the arrondissement's operating budget.

The City is tabling before council the lists of its contracts of $25,000 and more awarded in March 2026, as well as contracts transferred, contracts terminated, cancelled calls for tenders and additional expenses that were authorized.
In March 2026, 187 contracts of more than $25,000 were awarded, for a total value of $136,051,933 (excluding taxes).
Of these 187 contracts, 43 were awarded by the director general and the assistant directors general, including 40 after a competitive process.
The threshold for a competitive process (call for tenders by invitation or electronic request for prices) is set at $34,000; between $10,000 and $34,000, two requests for prices are required.
As of April 1, 2026, with the Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux, these detailed lists will no longer be sent to elected officials each month: a simplified version will replace them.
The City is changing Steve Gadoury's contract at the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
He is leaving the position of assistant director of operations to become assistant director – support and advice to management, effective March 11, 2026.
His annual salary is set at $195,441.54, based on the DS3 scale for managers of the Direction générale and service directors.
He reports to the director of the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
The City may authorize him to use an unmarked vehicle belonging to the Service, given the requirement to respond quickly outside normal working hours.
His other working conditions remain the same; the funds are already provided for in the response and prevention budget.
The City is authorizing the construction of a 48-unit residential building at 15, rue Boucher, in the Loretteville neighbourhood.
The project exceeds by 12 units the maximum of 36 units per building allowed in this zone.
Following the public consultation of March 30, 2026, the maximum permitted height goes from 19 to 20 metres, because of the slope of the land.
The building will have 5 storeys, but the 5th storey cannot contain any housing unit; it will serve, among other things, as access to the rooftop terrace.
The developer must provide at least 55 parking spaces, 4 units with 3 or more bedrooms, one heat pump per unit and a white roof covering at least 50% of the roof.
At least 20 bicycle spaces are required: 10 inside the building and 10 outside, covered.

Work must begin within 12 months of the adoption of the resolution, otherwise the authorization lapses; breaking the conditions carries a fine of $1,000 (for an individual) or $2,000 (in other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.

The City is setting aside $10,000,000 from its accumulated surpluses as of December 31, 2025 for active mobility projects: $9,760,000 on the local (proximity) side and $240,000 on the agglomeration side.
City council is creating a reserve dedicated to active mobility and transferring to it the $9,760,000 coming from the unassigned local surplus.
This sum of $9,760,000 will be used to fund the implementation of the Vision de la mobilité active et de l'intermodalité (sheet 38003 of the 2026-2035 investment plan).
The projects covered involve cycling and pedestrian networks, connections between active modes and public transit, as well as the safety and accessibility of routes.
By using its surpluses, the City avoids borrowing to fund these developments.
The agglomeration portion of $240,000 is the subject of a separate file (FN2026-018) submitted to the urban agglomeration council.
The City is adding $221,785.97 (before taxes) to the contract with the company Briquetal ltée for coating work at the Maison Pierre-Rainville, at 589, avenue Royale, in the Beauport borough.
The contract, awarded in March 2026 for $149,500, therefore goes up to $371,285.97 before taxes ($426,886.05 including taxes).

The reason: when the wall near the chimney was opened up, it was found that the core of the wall was much more deteriorated than expected, which makes it impossible to rebuild on the existing structure.
More demolition and rebuilding is therefore needed, along with temporary shoring; the work is extended by 60 days.
The building's other walls will be examined later in a separate expert assessment.
The net expenditure of $232,847.55 is paid for by two loan by-laws tied to the cultural development agreements with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The executive committee approved the expenditure on August 19, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is hiring Samantha McKinley as director of Destination Québec cité, effective March 16, 2026.
Her annual salary is set at $215,000, according to the 2026 pay scale for managers of the Direction générale and service directors.

She was selected following an internal and external competition (CADRR-096-2025) and will report to the assistant city manager for citizen services and urban vitality (directrice générale adjointe citoyen et vitalité urbaine).
The contract is for an indefinite term: she must give 4 weeks' notice to leave, and the City must give 3 to 12 months' notice (or a payment in lieu) to end it.
She gets 25 vacation days per year starting May 1, 2026, the managers' pension plan, group insurance and a performance bonus.
She must work exclusively for the City and comply with the by-law on employee ethics.
The decision falls to the urban agglomeration council of Québec; the funds are already provided for in the budget.

The Québec urban agglomeration finds that Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures' decision to allow a 39-unit residential building at 4927, rue des Landes complies with the land use planning and development plan.
The project exceeds the maximum allowed in zone R-425: 39 units instead of a maximum of between 14 and 23, which is a density of 67.5 units per hectare.
The underground garage may be built 2.3 metres from the left side property line instead of the 4 metres required.

Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures is relying on section 93 of Bill 31, which allows such a project to be authorized until February 21, 2027 when the vacancy rate for rental housing is below 3% (1.2% in October 2025).

Conditions imposed on the developer: plant vegetation on the land above the non-compliant part of the garage without developing it for tenants, comply with the acoustic study and, at the City's request, pay for a new noise study and follow its recommendations.
Once approved, the city clerk issues the certificate of compliance.
The executive committee takes note of the list of additional expenses of more than $250,000 authorized by employees with delegated authority, for the week of May 17 to 23, 2026.
Only one expense appears in the report: $354,777.96 (before taxes) for the construction contract for the multi-purpose curling centre.
This amount is used to add protective measures against the presence of swelling rock and to carry out adjustment work in structure, electromechanics and architecture (27 directives).
The value of the contract goes from $28,848,835.80 to $29,203,613.76, whereas it was $28,497,499.46 at the start.
The document specifies that, despite this change, the curling centre project remains within the total planned cost.
The expense falls under the Service de la gestion des immeubles.
The City is closing part of the right-of-way of rue Landry, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough, covering about 437.10 square metres.
This land moves into the City's private domain, which then allows the City to sell it.
The operation is tied to the TramCité project (structuring public transit network).
It must be completed before the signing of the notarial deed transferring the land to the Société québécoise des infrastructures.
The transfer in question was authorized in October 2025 and covers a total area of about 2,404.10 square metres along rue Landry.
The City is transferring $750,000 from its reserve for unforeseen expenses (contingency account) to the operating budget of the Service des ressources humaines.
The money is used to pay for professional services contracts already under way with actuaries and lawyers.
These contracts cover the extension of negotiations, the drafting of by-laws on pension plans, and expert assistance in complex and contentious files.
The amount is split between $384,000 from the agglomeration contingency and $366,000 from the local (proximity) contingency.
The executive committee adopted the decision on June 10, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0788).
The City wants to acquire a strip of land of about 12.10 square metres along 1re Avenue, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough.
The acquisition is meant to widen the 1re Avenue right-of-way for the TramCité tramway project (Réseau structurant de transport en commun).
The purchase will be made by mutual agreement or, failing an agreement, by expropriation; the owners have already been notified of the process.
The property in question is held in divided co-ownership and has 12 property records.
The land, in its largest extent, is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $628,000, or $853.38 per square metre.
The City may drop the expropriation proceedings if the project no longer needs the land.
The funds come from the agglomeration loan by-law tied to the réseau structurant de transport en commun.
The City wants to acquire a strip of land of about 5.4 square metres along route de l'Église, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The acquisition will be used to widen route de l'Église, as part of the project to redevelop this artery.
The City is already negotiating with the owners and has sent them a money offer; if the agreement fails, it may proceed by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the acquisition or expropriation proceedings.
The complete lot is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $404,000, that is, $509.84 per square metre.
The funds come from a loan by-law covering bicycle path and pedestrian path work.
Réal Pelchat is asking the Commission de protection du territoire agricole du Québec for permission to sell two farm properties (lots 2 163 648 and 2 163 649) to different buyers.
The properties involved cover 333,376.2 square metres (33.3376 hectares) in the quartier de l'Aéroport, district de Cap-Rouge–Laurentien, arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The owner would keep lots 2 163 778 and 2 163 779, located north of avenue Notre-Dame.

The properties, partly cultivated and partly wooded, would remain agricultural: the zoning allows only crop farming without livestock, low-odour livestock farming, forestry activity without outfitting operations, and parks.
The City's analysis concludes that there will be no effect on neighbouring farming activities or on water and soil resources.
The City recommends supporting the application before the Commission; the file goes to city council.
The City is authorizing the operation of a construction business at 14322, boulevard de la Colline, in the Saint-Émile neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
Administrative activities will take place on the upper floor of a new building, and the equipment will be stored inside the existing garage.
According to the analysis, the activity is located far from the bank of the watercourse at the back of the lot and will have no impact on the environment.
Employee parking will have to meet the standards that apply to parking areas of more than 150 m².
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended approval on May 27, 2026; the borough council made the decision (resolution CA6-2026-0058).
The City grants a minor exemption to the house at 1074, avenue de la Châtellenie, in the Sillery neighbourhood.
The house is located 4.29 metres from the street, whereas the borough's planning by-law requires 4.5 metres.
The building's siting is therefore deemed to comply, with no work to be done.
According to the analysis, without this exemption, the owner would have to move or demolish the building.
The situation has existed since 1946 and no complaints have been recorded.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour on August 11, 2026.
The City is allowing a 13-metre-wide access driveway instead of the maximum 10 metres permitted, at 709, rue Kirouac, in Saint-Sauveur.
This driveway will serve the underground parking and the waste containers of a new 202-unit, 8-storey building.
Access will be from rue Kirouac rather than from rue Marie-de-l'Incarnation, because of the steep slope and the trees located in the municipal right-of-way.
According to the analysis, the access faces the blank walls of the neighbouring buildings and allows collection trucks to manoeuvre.

The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the application on April 7, 2026; the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec and the Service du transport also gave a favourable opinion.
The City is adding a mandatory stop sign on avenue le Duc Nord, at the south approach to the intersection with rue de la Souveraine, in Charlesbourg (district des Monts).
This "T" intersection already had stop signs at the east and west approaches, but no control on the south side.
According to the City's analysis, traffic volumes are similar on both streets, which creates confusion for drivers.
The decision follows a request from citizens.
The borough council is enacting ordinance O-579 to make this new stop sign official.
No financial impact is indicated in the document.
The City approves the construction plans for a detached single-dwelling house at 1186, rue de l'Embâcle, in the Val-Bélair neighbourhood.
The lot is located in an area where every new building must have its siting and appearance approved before a permit is issued.

According to the analysis, fill is needed to match the house to the level of the street and of the neighbouring building; the ground-floor level will be 1.2 metres higher than the centre of the street.
The project includes parking for two vehicles in the front yard, embankments and a percolation pit in the back yard for rainwater.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended approval on August 12, 2026.
No financial impact is indicated in the document.
The City is hiring Carrières Québec inc. to store and crush asphalt, concrete, cement and rock waste.
The contract is estimated at $801,900 before taxes and runs until December 31, 2026.
These materials are used for repair work on streets, sidewalks, and water and sewer systems.
Only one bid was received; it is 2.3% below the department's estimate, which was $821,040 before taxes.
The net cost to the City is estimated at $841,894.76, taking into account the recovery of the QST.
The money will come from the operating budget and from funding tied to the Service des travaux publics investment plan.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council adopts a by-law that reviews where commercial tourist accommodation is allowed in Vieux-Limoilou.
General tourist accommodation goes from five zones to two: it is removed from zones 19209Mc, 19215Mb and 19230Cb, and the offer is refocused on 3e Avenue.
Youth hostels are removed from zones 19209Mc and 19215Mb.
On 3e Avenue (zone 19204Mb), tourist accommodation will no longer be allowed on the ground floor, and the protection of existing dwellings is extended to the second floor.
Still in that zone, the limit of five units per accommodation establishment is removed.
A ground-floor business will be able to expand to the second floor despite a protected dwelling, if access is from inside the building.
A dental clinic will be able to set up on the ground floor at 801, 3e Avenue; the maximum floor area for health establishments without accommodation goes from 400 to 800 square metres.
The City is giving $4,350 to "Groupe Plein Air Faune" for its 2026 spring break activities.
The activities took place from February 28 to March 8, 2026, at the base de plein air de Sainte-Foy, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The program included five theme days, from March 2 to 6: Pêche en herbe, De nature sucrée!, Nuit Polaire, Trésor hivernal and Un hiver sur la trotte!.
The activities were open to everyone and were held rain or shine.
The City also provided technical support, depending on available resources.
The grant is higher than the $3,650 given to the same organization for the 2025 spring break.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget (activity "Réaliser et soutenir les événements").
The executive committee takes note of the weekly list of additional expenses of more than $250,000 authorized by employees with delegated powers, for the week of March 8 to 14, 2026.
Only one change notice appears in the report: $235,994 (before taxes) for the purchase and installation of snow removal equipment (lot 4).
This amount is used to buy a second transport box with a spreader, in order to equip a new truck purchased as a replacement.
The contract therefore goes from $235,994 to $471,988.
The expense falls under the Service de la gestion des équipements motorisés.
The City is correcting the financial structure of the Vieux-Québec winter lighting project, carried out from November 2024 to March 2025.
The grant to the Société de développement commercial du Vieux-Québec stays the same: a maximum of $80,000.
The total cost of the project goes from $399,700 to $103,200, because other partners ended up covering some of the expenses.
The grants from Destination Québec cité ($157,015) and the private contribution ($148,935) are removed from the financial structure; the SDC is putting in $23,200 of its own funds.
The City's support therefore represents 78% of the project cost.
The project included lights on trees, lampposts, the gates of the fortifications and above certain streets.
The SDC du Vieux-Québec has received $275,000 in grants from the City since the beginning of 2024.
The City wants to obtain servitudes (rights of use) on a private lot along boulevard Laurier, in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, for the TramCité tramway project.
This involves a permanent servitude for underground infrastructure of about 333.4 square metres and another of about 4 square metres for a fire hydrant.
These servitudes are needed because the project requires moving conduits and public utility networks.
The City will first negotiate with the owner, to whom it will send an offer, but it can also proceed by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques may drop the expropriation proceedings if the project no longer needs the servitudes.
The entire lot is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $6,160,000, or $651.16 per square metre.
The money comes from the urban agglomeration loan by-law tied to the structuring public transit network.
The City is authorizing outdoor storage of types C, D, E and G at 380, rue Desrochers, in the parc industriel Cardinal (quartier de Vanier).
In practical terms, containers, scaffolding, tools, vehicles weighing 4,500 kg or more, granular or organic materials and other goods or materials may be stored outdoors there.
Storage is allowed only in the side and rear yards, and a fence is required around the storage area.
The authorization applies only to this property (lot 1 943 935), and not to all of zone 23009Cb, which remains limited to types A and B along boulevard Pierre-Bertrand.
The property is vacant: the former building was demolished and the new owners want to build an industrial or construction contractor's building there.
The occupancy must begin within 18 months after the by-law comes into force, otherwise the authorization lapses.
The by-law may be subject to approval by referendum; the conseil de quartier de Vanier will hold a public consultation, followed by seven days to send in written comments.
The City is awarding a contract of $4,278,909 (before taxes) to the company P.E. Pageau inc. (Québec) for paving work and various improvements.
The work affects the arrondissements of Beauport, La Cité-Limoilou and Les Rivières.
Streets involved: boulevard Pierre-Bertrand, boulevard des Chutes, 4e Avenue / chemin de la Canardière and boulevard Père-Lelièvre.
Planned work: building sidewalks, raised intersections and concrete slabs, and repaving.
Five companies submitted bids; P.E. Pageau inc. submitted the lowest price, 8.4% above the City's estimate ($3,948,783.78 before taxes).
The net expenditure comes to $4,492,319.59, funded by two agglomeration loan by-laws.
The contract provides for price adjustments based on the cost of asphalt and fuel.
The City is awarding P.E. Pageau inc. the contract to build a bike-and-pedestrian link on rue Abraham-Martin, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough.
The contract is $1,024,233.50 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $1,075,317.15.
The work includes lighting and the creation of tree planting pits.
P.E. Pageau inc. submitted the lowest of the four bids received, all of which were compliant; the others ranged from $1,196,624.08 to $1,385,348.00.
The price chosen is 21.1% lower than the estimate from the department making the request ($1,297,675.00).
The contract allows for price adjustments based on the cost of asphalt and fuel.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1769 on bike paths and sustainable mobility.
The City is changing the zoning of the building at 1170, boulevard Lebourgneuf, in the Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf neighbourhood.
The change allows three new types of uses in the zone: gathering places, education and training establishments, and high-technology industries.
In practical terms, a fitness centre or a boxing studio of more than 200 square metres becomes permitted, which was prohibited before.
The owner wants to fill vacant units and welcome, among others, a training and fitness centre for pregnant women and mothers with babies, as well as high-technology businesses.
The conseil de quartier de Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf will hold a public consultation meeting; people will have seven days after it to send their comments in writing.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The City is giving $15,000 to the Fédération québécoise de handball olympique to hold the "Trophée IHF junior masculin de handball de l'Amérique du Nord et des Caraïbes".
The tournament takes place from October 26 to November 1, 2026 at the PEPS of Université Laval, with up to nine teams and about 200 accredited participants.
Admission is paid, but free for children 12 and under; tickets are offered to students taking part in introductory activities in schools in the region.
The grant represents 4.7% of the event's projected budget, estimated at $316,000.
The payment is made in two parts: $12,000 within 10 days of signing, and $3,000 when the financial statements and the report are submitted.
The organization must submit its report within 90 days after the end of the event and maintain civil liability insurance of $5,000,000.
The funding is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners and on approval of the 2027 budget.

The conseil d'agglomération de Québec (urban agglomeration council) approves the 2025 financial statements of the Société municipale d'habitation Champlain (SOMHAC), for the year ended December 31, 2025.
SOMHAC's board of directors had already approved these financial statements on April 14, 2026.

The 2025 budget forecast a net increase of $1,826,524.00 in the replacement reserve ($2,936,024.00 paid in, $1,109,500.00 used); instead, the financial statements show a contribution of $1,376,254.00.
The difference is due to the fact that SOMHAC has not yet received the CMHC funding for work carried out from 2023 to 2025.
Without this funding, some work was postponed and the reserve was used for the most urgent work; the amounts will be paid into the reserve as soon as CMHC pays.
The financial statements will be sent to the Ville de Québec and to the Société d'habitation du Québec; the audit report was prepared by Mallette.
The City is amending a December 2025 decision in order to enlarge the piece of land it wants to acquire along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité streetcar project.
The area to be acquired goes from 1.2 square metres to about 3.30 square metres, on part of lot 1 943 567.
The City is adding the acquisition of a permanent public utility easement of about 43.30 square metres on the same piece of land, in order to move conduits and networks.
The right-of-way of 1re Avenue must be widened for mobility and safe service.

The acquisition can be made by mutual agreement or by expropriation; the Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings and to withdraw from them if the project no longer needs the land.
The owner was informed of the process, of the next steps and of the name of a contact person at the City.
The entire piece of land is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $234,000, that is $359.06 per square metre; the money comes from the loan by-law for the structuring network.
The arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is giving out $59,600 in grants to five organizations for events in the summer of 2026.
Limoilou en vrac receives $27,200 for "Limoilou en musique et le Grand bazar de Limoilou," on June 5, 6 and 7 on 3e Avenue and chemin de la Canardière.
Mouvement Bouge Québec receives $20,000 for the "Festival Bouge Québec," on June 13 at parc Victoria.
Art Dans La Ville Production receives $7,000 for the "Fête de la musique de Québec," from June 12 to 14 (rue Saint-Jean, the square in front of église Saint-Jean-Baptiste, Passage Olympia).
École de cirque de Québec receives $3,400 for "Jours de cirque," from June 4 to 7; the grant is lower because the programming component is now supported by the Service de la culture et du patrimoine.
Centre des loisirs St-Sacrement receives $2,000 for "Lutte pour la solidarité de quartier," on June 20 at parc Saint-Sacrement, a first request for support.
The City is also providing technical support; the police and fire services are in favour of holding the events.
The City of Québec will take part in the 2026 National Organ and Tissue Donation Awareness Week and in future editions.
The week will run from April 19 to 25, 2026, and aims to encourage people to consent to organ donation and to talk about it with their loved ones.
The City's support could take the form of flag raisings or social media posts.
Police officers from the Service de police de la Ville de Québec transport organs and medical staff on a volunteer basis, outside their working hours.
Since 2025, Transplant Québec has coordinated these transports, a role previously played by the Association canadienne des dons d'organes et de tissus.
Eight police forces in Québec, including the one in Québec City, take part in organ transports; 109 municipalities took part in the campaign last year.
The decision has no financial impact.
The City is granting a minor exemption for a vacant lot at 0, boulevard Pie-XI Sud, in the Val-Bélair neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The exemption allows an accessory building to be built with no green strip at all between the parking area and the building, whereas the by-law requires one of 6 metres.
The planned building will be multi-purpose: storage, a training room, and offices for managing the overall project.

According to the analysis, the presence of a watercourse and a wetland requires a protection strip to be respected, which makes it impossible to move the building farther away from the parking spaces.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme was unanimously in favour on June 15, 2026, and the borough council adopted the decision on July 2, 2026.
No financial impact is indicated in the document.
The City is authorizing spending of $7,100,000 for work to rebuild underground infrastructure, including the sewer and water supply systems.
It is borrowing the same amount, to be repaid over five years.
The work may take place anywhere in the territory under the city's jurisdiction.
The amount also covers hiring staff, buying equipment and machinery, professional and technical services contracts, and acquiring buildings or easements if needed.
The City will be able to acquire the buildings or easements needed for the work by mutual agreement or by expropriation.
An amount of $710,000 (10% of the spending) is being taken from the general fund and will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The funds are provided for in the years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 capital works program.

The developer Trudel Innovation inc. will transform a surface parking lot at the corner of rue De Saint-Vallier Est, rue Dorchester and rue De Sainte-Hélène, in Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).

The mixed-use complex will include 413 housing units, commercial space and a 158-room hotel, with heights of up to 17 storeys on the rue Dorchester side. The private investment is estimated at about $150M.
The work includes redeveloping about 196 metres of rue De Sainte-Hélène, rebuilding about 230 metres of sidewalk on De Saint-Vallier Est, and adding paving stone at the Narcisse-Belleau intersection.

A public mobility passage will be built in the heart of the block, between rue De Sainte-Hélène and rue De Saint-Vallier Est. The Comité de commémoration et de toponymie will have to propose a name for it.
The City is investing $2,499,705 before taxes: $785,205 for the street work and $1,714,500 for the mobility passage. The net expenditure amounts to $2,624,377.79.
The developer will transfer the municipal infrastructure and equipment it builds to the City free of charge, once the work is accepted.
According to the tax impact analysis, the building would be eligible for a tax credit estimated at $3,059,478, and the net tax contribution would remain negative for about 10 years.
The City wants to acquire two parcels of land and an easement along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement or by expropriation if no agreement is reached with the owners.
The land involved is about 17.30 square metres (lot 6 373 547) and 188.20 square metres (lot 1 315 368).
The easement, of about 107 square metres, will allow public utility conduits and networks to be moved underground.
The widening of the 1re Avenue right-of-way is the reason given for these acquisitions.
On the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll, the land of lot 6 373 547 is listed at $75,000 and that of lot 1 315 368 at $1,320,000.
If the project no longer needs this land, the City may abandon the expropriation proceedings.
The City wants to reduce the minimum distance required between a house and the side boundary of the lot: from 4 metres to 2 metres.
The change affects zone 35008Ha, in the Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy neighbourhood, between rues Alain, Chavigneau, François-Tavenas and avenue des Compagnons.
The change stems from a request to enlarge a home to about 2 metres from the side lot line in order to add a dwelling unit for a family member.
According to the analysis, the current standard does not match the reality of the area, where several buildings already have side setbacks that do not comply.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The conseil de quartier de la Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy will be consulted and will hold a public meeting; interested people will have 7 days after that meeting to submit their comments in writing.
The City is awarding the cleaning and maintenance of several buildings to four companies, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2030, with an option to renew for 12 months including a price indexation.
Lot 1: Entretien Costa (José Costa) receives $129,600.00 (plus taxes) for the édifice de la Sécurité civile, 2780, rue de la Faune (La Haute-Saint-Charles).
Lot 2: Placement Lavora inc. receives $514,952.04 (plus taxes) for the édifice De Lestres, 715, avenue De Lestres (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
Lot 8: Réno-Voc inc. receives $225,900.00 (plus taxes) for the Centre de services Canardière, 1252, chemin de la Canardière (La Cité-Limoilou).
Lot 9: 3559840 Canada inc. receives $274,264.54 (plus taxes) for the Pavillon place D'Youville (997, rue Saint-Jean) and the temporary washroom block at carré Lépine, rue Saint-Vallier Est.
The total net expense is $1,201,809.31, spread from 2026 to 2030, subject to the adoption of the budgets for the years 2027 to 2030.
Lot 7 (bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy and its temporary washroom block) is cancelled and will be the subject of a new call for tenders; lots 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10 are dealt with in another file.

The City is sending two chiefs from the Service de protection contre l'incendie, Dave Andrews and Steven Lahaye, to a three-day training course on flammable liquids and gases in College Station, Texas, from September 22 to 24, 2026.
The authorized expense goes from $8,997.04 to $14,156.79, because the planned budget has changed; the July 2026 decision is cancelled and replaced.
The training, given by the Texas A&M Engineering Extension Service, covers foam extinguishing, fluorine-free foams, response tactics and water supply.
The goal is to keep enough qualified chiefs to handle a leak of flammable liquids or gases at the Port de Québec.
The expenses are covered by the funds provided for in the agreement between the City and the Port de Québec, out of the operating budget of the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
An overrun of no more than 10% of the authorized amount will be accepted without a new authorization; reimbursement is made upon submission of supporting documents.

The City is giving the organization Le Pignon Bleu, la maison pour grandir the job of providing meals and food assistance to children at day camps in disadvantaged neighbourhoods of Québec during the summer.
The agreement covers three years, from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028.
The City will pay $65,000 per year (excluding GST and QST), for a total of $195,000.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 will be adjusted based on the Consumer Price Index, and depend on the approval of the budgets for those years.
The agreement is made without a call for tenders, which the Cities and Towns Act allows with a non-profit organization.
The previous agreement with the organization ended on December 31, 2025.
City council was to make a decision on March 31, 2026.
The City is awarding the company 2851-9288 Québec inc. the work to repair and rebuild windows and glazing on its buildings, from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2028.
The work includes replacing windows, thermal panes, interior glazing and exterior seals, including at the ExpoCité site.
Lot 1 (La Cité-Limoilou, Beauport, Charlesbourg and ExpoCité): $515,700 before taxes. Lot 2 (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, Les Rivières, La Haute-Saint-Charles): $625,400 before taxes.
The net cost is estimated at $1,198,012.36, once the QST refund is taken into account.
The contract can be renewed for another 12 months, with a price increase based on the consumer price index.
Only one company bid on the two lots; its prices are about 3% below the City's estimates.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
The City is changing the zoning of the site of the former aréna Gilles-Tremblay, at 1011, avenue Larue, in the quartier des Chutes-Montmorency (Beauport).
The land is going from a recreational use to a small-scale residential use: housing is now permitted there.
Detached houses with one to three dwellings, semi-detached houses with one to two dwellings and row houses with no more than two dwellings may be built there, with a maximum of six buildings per row.
Buildings may have up to three storeys; the 11-metre height limit is removed and the rear setback goes from 7.5 to 7 metres.
Part of the site will be used for housing that helps young families become homeowners (Programme Accès Famille).
Gathering places, restaurants and bars will no longer be allowed in this zone.
A workshop with area residents was held on October 11, 2023; the by-law contains provisions that may be subject to a referendum.
The City's director general, Luc Monty, will be away from February 9 to March 6, 2026.
The City appoints Isabelle Dubois, assistant director general, as interim director general during this period.
The appointed person exercises all the powers and obligations of the director general during her mandate.
The executive committee adopted the decision on February 4, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0151).
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City wants to acquire a strip of land of about 173.6 square metres alongside rue de la Faune, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The land would be used to widen rue de la Faune, as part of the project to rebuild this street.
The acquisition would be made by agreement with the owner or, if the discussions fail, by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to begin the acquisition procedures.
The Service de l'ingénierie will prepare the necessary plans, technical descriptions and cadastral operations.
The complete property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $65,000, or $13.4 per square metre.
The funds come from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 concerning the redevelopment work on rue de la Faune.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 1292, rue du Beaujolais, in the Saint-Émile neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The heat pump installed in the back yard is 0.5 metre from the left side property line, while the planning by-law requires 1 metre.
The exemption legalizes an installation done in 2022, which was discovered when a new location certificate was prepared for the sale of the house.
According to the analysis, moving the heat pump to a compliant location would require changing the connection to the Hydro-Québec network.

The heat pump sits on anti-vibration pads, and a fence and vegetation separate the property from the neighbour on the left; the maximum noise level indicated by the manufacturer is 59 dB and no complaints have been received since the installation.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on August 12, 2026.
The City is correcting a decision made on October 1, 2025 concerning water main and service connection work with the company Immo-Experts S.E.C.
The original decision called for the complete cancellation of an old easement dating from 1976 (inherited from the former Ville de Sainte-Foy) on lot 1 533 018.
In the end, the City is cancelling this easement only in part, because the segments upstream and downstream of the project are still needed to operate, maintain and protect its pipes.
A new easement is being established as a replacement, under an agreement signed with Immo-Experts S.E.C.
The land in question is in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City is naming a new street, about 225 metres long and perpendicular to route Jean-Gauvin, "rue Marie-Louise-Hamel".
The street is located in the future industrial area south of Jean-Lesage airport, in the quartier de L'Aéroport, arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The project also includes upgrading route Jean-Gauvin, which the council decided on earlier.
The name honours Marie-Louise Hamel (1821-1910), who opened a hat and clothing shop and helped found the magasin Paquet on rue Saint-Joseph.
The Comité de commémoration et de toponymie wanted a name connected to business and a better representation of women in street names.
The Commission de toponymie du Québec was consulted about the spelling of the name.
City council adopted resolution CV-2026-0230 on March 31, 2026.
The City is authorizing a real estate project at 15, rue Boucher, in the Loretteville neighbourhood (Loretteville-Les Châtels district).
The project will allow the construction of a building with at least 48 housing units, which is 12 more than the maximum of 36 allowed in the zone.

The City is accepting exemptions: a height of 19 metres instead of 13, parking reduced to 55 spaces instead of 58, a staircase that encroaches further into the front setback, and a retaining wall closer to the lot line.

The developer will have to meet certain conditions: at least 4 housing units with 3 bedrooms or more, one heat pump per unit, an air-to-water heat pump for hot water, a white roof covering at least 50% of the roof, and 20 bicycle spaces (10 indoors, 10 outdoors under cover).
The fifth floor cannot contain any housing unit, and the authorization expires if work does not begin within 12 months.
The City will hold a public consultation meeting, followed by 3 days to submit written comments; the project is not subject to a referendum.
Anyone who does not meet the conditions faces a fine of $1,000 (individuals) or $2,000 (all other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.
The Ville de Québec is paying $9,511.09 to renew its 2026 membership in the Les Arts et la Ville network.
The fee is 1.60 cents per resident for cities of 30,000 residents or more, calculated on a population of 594,443 residents.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de la culture et du patrimoine.
The fees for previous years were $8,904.47 in 2025, $8,396.60 in 2024 and $8,015.34 in 2023.
The City sits on the organization's board of directors, represented by city councillor Marianne White and the director of the Division de la culture et du patrimoine.
Les Arts et la Ville is a charitable organization created in 1987, with its head office in Québec, that brings together more than 500 members from the municipal world and 140 from the cultural world.
The City is banning right turns on a red light on Grande Allée Est, at the east approach to the intersection with avenue Honoré-Mercier.
The ban applies at all times, to drivers as well as cyclists.
Right turns on a red light were already banned at the north approach to this intersection.
The City says it wants to make the pedestrian crossings safer at this intersection, where many vehicles and pedestrians travel.
The intersection is in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, district du Cap-aux-Diamants.
The City wants to obtain a permanent public utility easement on a piece of land bordering 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The easement covers about 22.70 square metres on part of lot 6 730 437.
The City may acquire this easement by agreement or by expropriation; the owner has been informed of the process and the next steps.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings, and to withdraw them if the project no longer needs the easement.
The easement is needed because the project requires moving public utility conduits and networks.
The funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the structuring public transit network.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 3630-3636, rue Palmarolle, in the Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy neighbourhood (arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The exemption allows a rear setback of 1.38 metres instead of the 15 metres required by the borough's planning by-law.
It applies to a new proposed lot (6 736 329) in order to allow the expansion of an existing neighbouring building.
The planned expansion has 26 housing units and would be built partly on the current outdoor parking lot.
According to the analysis, the inner courtyard and the green space are kept, and the views from the existing housing units are not blocked.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on June 16, 2026; the decision rests with the borough council.

The City will pay up to $242,100 in grants to cultural organizations: $232,600 comes from the Entente de développement culturel with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications, and $9,500 from the operating budget of the Service de la culture et du patrimoine.
In all, 23 projects are supported: 22 through the Entente and 1 through the Service's budget.

The "Organiser" component funds equipment purchases and resource sharing, for example $15,000 to Antitube for 65 seats at the Cinéma Beaumont, $15,000 to the Théâtre de la Bordée for sound equipment and $10,000 to À l'est de vos empires for a reception resource in the Méduse hall.

The "Rayonner" component pays for prospecting missions and showcases abroad, including $10,000 to Machine de Cirque in France, $10,000 to Théâtre Rude Ingénierie in Germany and $3,000 to Envol et Macadam in Indonesia.
A $9,000 project at Théâtre Le Diamant will offer two shows with audio description for theatre (théâtrodescription) in 2026-2027 for people with a visual limitation.
The funds come from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3367 ($168,840), from culture transfer funding ($63,760) and from the operating budget ($9,500).
The applications were assessed by a committee of professionals from the Service de la culture et du patrimoine; the executive committee adopted resolution CE-2026-0963 on July 8, 2026.
The City is banning parking at all times on the west side of rue Mercier, in Beauport, along the entire stretch between rue de Tunis and avenue Larue.
Previously, the ban covered only the portion located more than 228 metres north of rue de Tunis.
About 26 parking spaces are being removed.
The City says the change has little impact on residents, who have private parking, and a moderate impact on customers of businesses in the area.
The street is 9 metres wide; according to the City, cars parked on both sides were interfering with traffic flow and safety.
The decision stems from a request by a citizen that was reviewed by the Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente.
The City is granting a minor exemption to the house at 1595, rue Potvin, in Charlesbourg (Louis-XIV district).
The distance between the building and the rear property line, which is 0.54 metres, is declared compliant, even though the planning by-law requires 7.5 metres.
This correction allows the owner to carry out an expansion project that would otherwise be impossible.
The house was built between 1830 and 1880, before Charlesbourg adopted its first planning by-law.
The planned expansion will be located in the front yard, more than 23 metres from rue Potvin; a wooded area borders the rear yard.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on January 7, 2026, and so did the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec.

The Ville de Québec is awarding the company Truelle et Cie inc. (Sainte-Christine-d'Auvergne) the archaeological monitoring work related to the redevelopment of rue De Buade, in the borough of La Cité-Limoilou.
The contract is worth $534,662, before GST and QST; the net cost to the City is $561,328.27.
The contract runs from the date of signing until May 31, 2028.
This is phase 2 of the archaeological work, which has two parts, tied to the project of the Service de l'ingénierie.
The contract was awarded without a public call for tenders, as the law allows this when only one supplier can provide the service because of its heritage value.
The funding comes from two loan by-laws: $309,247.37 (R.V.Q. 3289) and $252,080.90 (R.V.Q. 3417, work in the Vieux-Québec heritage site).
The arrondissement de Charlesbourg is entrusting the organization of the summer 2026 day camps (Programme Vacances-Été) to five recreation organizations.
The five organizations are Les Loisirs Bourassa, Loisirs de St-Rodrigue, the Patro de Charlesbourg, Loisirs du Trait-Carré and Loisirs Brio.
The City is paying out $2,124,707.83 in grants in total for 2026, slightly less than the $2,199,274.37 paid in 2025.
Breakdown: Patro de Charlesbourg $628,392.39, Loisirs de St-Rodrigue $502,674.23, Loisirs Brio $434,806.02, Loisirs du Trait-Carré $421,735.57, Les Loisirs Bourassa $137,099.62.
In the summer of 2025, these organizations welcomed 3,465 children in total in the arrondissement.
The funding covers, among other things, the regular camps (ages 5-12), support for children with special needs, transportation, staff training and family discounts.
The City also provides access to play areas and to municipal and school facilities, depending on availability.
The City is amending its planning by-law to allow more outdoor storage at 380, rue Desrochers, in the Vanier neighbourhood (arrondissement des Rivières).

The lot, located in the parc industriel Cardinal, has been vacant since the former building was demolished; the owners want to build a building there for industrial or construction contractor activities.

In addition to the types of storage already permitted (A and B), types C, D, E and G would be added: for example containers, scaffolding, tools and equipment, vehicles weighing 4,500 kg or more, and granular or organic materials.
Storage would be permitted only in the side and rear yards, and a fence is required around the storage area.
The authorization applies only to this property, and not to all of zone 23009Cb, which runs along boulevard Pierre-Bertrand.
Occupancy must begin within 18 months after the related by-law comes into force; otherwise the authorization lapses.
The conseil de quartier de Vanier will be consulted and will hold a public meeting; interested people will have seven days after that meeting to submit their comments in writing.
The City is creating a position of associate director at the Service des relations citoyennes et des communications, reporting to the Direction générale adjointe citoyen et vitalité urbaine.
Marie-Claude Brousseau is appointed to this position, with a contract taking effect on March 9, 2026 and for an indefinite term.
Her annual salary is set at $186,101 (2026 scale) and she has access to the performance bonus program.
Until now, she held the position of director of the Division des communications en sécurité publique at the Service de police.
If the City ends the contract, it must give 3 to 12 months' notice (one month per year of service) or pay an equivalent amount; the employee must give 4 weeks' notice.
The necessary funds, including employee benefits, are already provided for in the citizen relations and communications budget.
The decision falls to the Québec urban agglomeration council.
The City confirms the completion of work to build a shared bike-and-pedestrian path on boulevard du Loiret, between chemin du Petit-Village and rue Alexandra.
The former bike lanes were replaced by a 364-metre shared bike-and-pedestrian path, usable in all four seasons, which connects the bike network between Beauport and Charlesbourg.
The eligible expenses reported to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable total $1,250,720.25 (net of taxes).
The ministère had granted funding of up to $364,000 in August 2023; the City has already received $291,200, or 80% of that amount.
Taking note of this work completion report is intended to obtain the second and final payment of the grant.
If the program's terms are not met, the financial assistance will be terminated; expenses lower than forecast would require the City to repay the overpayment.
The work began in the summer of 2023 and was completed in the spring of 2025. The City indicates no financial impact.
The City is awarding Protexplo inc., of Mirabel, a contract worth $325,538.46 (before GST and QST) to supply a building used to store hazardous household waste.
The building will go to the new écocentre Val-Bélair, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The contract covers the manufacturing, fitting out, transportation and installation of the building.
Two companies submitted bids; Protexplo offered the lowest price, ahead of Quatrex Environnement inc. ($344,821.50).
The net cost to the City, after the QST is recovered, comes to $341,774.69.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1588 related to work in the écocentres.
The executive committee adopted the decision on July 29, 2026.
The City is appointing Renée Desormeaux to the board of directors of the Fiducie du patrimoine culturel des Augustines, on a volunteer basis.
She represents the people of Québec there, not the City. The appointment does not commit the City to anything.
Her term lasts three years, starting April 1, 2026.
She replaces Line-Sylvie Perron, whose term has ended and who did not wish to renew it.
The Fiducie, created by the Augustines in 2009, protects the heritage of the Augustines and makes it accessible, and supports the Monastère des Augustines and the Centre Catherine-de-Saint-Augustin.
According to the document, Renée Desormeaux is a manager at the Ville de Québec and will soon be leaving for retirement.
The City is changing its zoning in Vieux-Québec and the colline Parlementaire to encourage housing construction and attract permanent residents.
In certain zones, it will no longer be possible to set up new general tourist accommodation establishments (use C10), in particular on vacant lots, outdoor parking lots and office buildings.
Tourist accommodation establishments already in place do not become non-compliant: the use remains permitted in the blocks where it is already carried on.

Around place D'Youville, the City wants tourist accommodation and housing to coexist: tourist units permitted only above the ground floor, a maximum of 25% of a building's floors, and no mixing of tourist and residential uses on the same floor.

The affected zones are located between rue Richelieu, rue D'Auteuil, boulevard René-Lévesque Est and rue Saint-Augustin, as well as an area near rue Saint-Joachim (Vieux-Québec–Cap-Blanc–colline Parlementaire and Saint-Jean-Baptiste neighbourhoods).
The City will hold a public consultation, with information and feedback measures, and a seven-day period after the meeting to receive written comments. The by-law is not subject to a referendum.
City council was aiming for adoption on August 25, 2026; the zones under the boroughs' jurisdiction are dealt with separately.
The City is banning parking at all times on the north side of rue Le Trait-Carré Ouest, in Charlesbourg, across from the entrances to the buildings at 8230 and 8234.
The ban covers a 28-metre section, located 227 metres north of boulevard Louis-XIV.
Four parking spaces are being removed on this street.
The change follows requests from residents who said they could not get into their driveway when vehicles were parked across the street.
The roadway is about 5 metres wide and parking was already banned at all times on the south side.
The decision falls to the council of the Arrondissement de Charlesbourg, district de Louis-XIV.
The City is adding $17,500 (before taxes) to the on-demand cleaning contract for ExpoCité, awarded to Opus Coop, Coopérative de solidarité Nettoieprêt.
The contract goes from $237,800 to $255,300 before taxes for the period from March 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026.
The net cost for the urban agglomeration is estimated at $18,372.81, paid out of ExpoCité's operating budget.
Events added to the 2025-2026 calendar kept ExpoCité employees busy with other tasks, which meant calling on the supplier more often.
The locations involved are the Centre de foires, the Place Jean-Béliveau and the Pavillon Guy-Lafleur.
The executive committee approved the expense on March 4, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0278).

The Ville de Québec will sign a new agreement with the minister responsible for the Capitale-Nationale region to manage part of the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029.
The City will receive $19,603,739 per year, for a total of $58,811,217, which represents 78.41% of the Fund's annual envelope of $25M.

The money is used to support economic development projects in the agglomeration of Québec and in Wendake; the agreement sets out who can apply for assistance, and which projects and expenses are eligible.
The City may keep up to 10% of the envelope for its administrative costs, and its own projects can be funded at 100% of eligible expenses with no repayment.
The annual payment is made in two stages: 80% ($15,682,991) after the accountability reporting and the adoption of an investment policy, then the balance based on actual commitments.
According to the document, the previous agreement (2018-2025) made it possible to support more than 500 businesses and organizations with $154M and to create or maintain more than 13,000 jobs.

The City will set out its investment policy in a separate document; the final version of the agreement is still awaited and the signing must take place quickly because of the provincial election schedule.
The City is borrowing $205,000 for maintenance, repair and construction work on infrastructure that protects water sources and intakes, lakes, rivers and groundwater.
The loan is repayable over fifteen years, out of the City's general revenues.
The money is used for studies, plans and specifications, work supervision, inspection, training, as well as hiring staff and purchasing goods, equipment, buildings and easements.
The projects affect the entire territory under the City's jurisdiction: rivers, lakes, wetlands, plants, wells, septic systems, docks, water intakes and other structures.
The City will be able to acquire the necessary buildings and easements by mutual agreement or by expropriation.
An amount of $20,500 (10% of the expense) is taken from the general fund and will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The funds are planned for 2026 to 2028 and the expense is shared between the agglomeration and local (proximity) jurisdictions.

The executive committee gives the director of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets the power to appoint the City's representative to the board of directors of a société de développement commercial (SDC).
Before, this power belonged to city council, which had delegated it to the executive committee on June 2, 2026.
The law requires the City to appoint a representative to the board of directors of each SDC, the non-profit organizations that represent the merchants of an area.
The City says it is aiming for more flexibility to quickly replace a representative and to reduce administrative steps.
The by-law comes into force as soon as it is adopted.
The City is giving up to $325,000 in grants to 13 artists and 15 cultural organizations in Québec, for 28 projects in total.
Grants to artists and writers total $118,000, with individual amounts ranging from $5,950 to $9,750.
Eco-responsible projects or resource-sharing projects by organizations receive $207,000, with amounts of $12,000 to $15,000 per organization.
The money comes from an agreement with the Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec (CALQ), signed in 2025 for 2025-2028, in which each partner puts in $325,000.
A jury made up of representatives from the sector chose the projects; the City sat on it as an observer only.
Among the organizations supported: Machine de cirque, Théâtre Périscope, EXMURO arts publics, Folie/Culture and the Festival international de poésie de Québec.
The funds come from a loan by-law tied to the work to carry out the Visions culturelles.

The Ville de Québec is awarding a contract of $1,708,980 (plus taxes) to Schneider Electric Systems Canada inc. to modernize the control boards of the Centre de récupération de la matière organique at the Complexe de valorisation énergétique, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The boards in question date back to the start-up of the incinerator in 1974, and replacement parts are no longer available.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders (gré à gré), as the law allows a contract tied to an exclusive right or a warranty to be awarded to a single company.
The City's net expense, after recovery of the QST, comes to $1,757,734.64, funded by an agglomeration loan by-law.

The work will be done in five stages, during planned shutdowns: furnace 3 in March-April 2027, furnace 4 in fall 2027, furnace 1 from November 2027 to January 2028, furnace 2 in early 2028, then the shared equipment in September 2028.
The matter is to be decided by the Québec urban agglomeration council on September 16, 2026.
The City is giving 18 grants totalling a maximum of $73,498 to organizations for the Semaine québécoise des rencontres interculturelles, from November 2 to 8, 2026.
The money comes from an agreement between the City and the ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI), in effect from April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2027.
Of the 31 projects submitted to the call for projects launched in June 2026, 18 scored 50/100 or more and were selected.
The amounts range from $1,750 to $5,000 per organization: among others, 24H ChronoSports, Centre R.I.R.E. 2000, Loisirs BRIO, Loisirs Duberger-Les Saules and Centre Mgr Marcoux each receive $5,000.
The grants will be paid in full after the executive committee's approval.

The organizations will have to display the contribution of the City and the MIFI, list their activities on the MIFI calendar and on the Québec animée page, and then submit an activity report and a financial report.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 1226, rue de l'Embâcle, in the Val-Bélair neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The front of the planned main building may measure 5.21 metres, whereas the borough's planning by-law requires 7.3.
The project is the construction of a single-dwelling house with an attached garage.
According to the analysis, the front of the attached garage is not included in the width calculation, and the rear of the building measures 7.62 metres, above the standard for the zone.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 29, 2026, and the decision rests with the borough council.
The arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge is entrusting Camp École Kéno inc. with running the Programme Vacances-Été 2026 (day camp).
The City will give the organization a grant of $1,128,611.89, calculated based on registrations of Québec children in 2025.

90% of the amount will be paid within 30 days after the agreement is signed; the balance will be adjusted based on the actual number of registrations as of September 14, and any overpayment will have to be repaid.
The organization manages registrations and pricing, keeps the registration revenue, and must offer a support service for children with special needs.
The City provides technical support, promotion and access to municipal and school play areas and facilities, on a non-exclusive basis.
The organization must hold civil liability insurance of at least $5,000,000, including the City as an additional insured.
In 2025, the camp had welcomed 2,542 children and received $1,227,694.46.
The City is refusing the request to enlarge two signs installed on the roof of the pump islands at the gas station at 440, rue Bouvier, in Arrondissement des Rivières.
The owner wanted signs of 2.1 square metres per roof side, while the planning by-law allows a maximum of 1 square metre.
The applicants cited the rules of the Office québécois de la langue française, which require the word "Essence" to be twice as large as the name "Costco Wholesale".
The City replies that a signage proposal respecting 1 square metre is possible and that there is therefore no serious harm.
It adds that the signage limit on pump islands applies everywhere on its territory.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended refusal on February 2, 2026; the borough council made its decision on February 24, 2026.
