The Ville de Québec is authorizing spending of $4,000,000 for work at the organic waste recovery centre of the complexe de valorisation énergétique, including the incinerator, its steam delivery infrastructure and the sludge treatment station.

The work includes modernizing, repairing and improving equipment and buildings, hiring staff, and awarding professional and technical service contracts (architecture, engineering, environmental management).
To pay for this work, the City is borrowing $4,000,000, to be repaid over 15 years out of general revenues.
An amount of $400,000 (10% of the spending) is taken from the general fund before the by-law comes into force, and then repaid to that fund through the loan.
The funds are planned from 2026 to 2028 in the 2026-2035 capital works program (record 46006).
The spending becomes mixed spending: $3,600,000 had been planned as agglomeration spending, but the division of jurisdictions is being changed.
If any work reduces treatment capacity, the City will be able to use transport, transfer or landfill services to divert the residual materials.
The City is providing up to $82,017 in grants to Québec City cultural organizations to offer master classes to emerging artists.
The money is used to pay the fees of the visiting masters as well as their travel and accommodation costs.
The Première Ovation measure is aimed at up-and-coming Québec City artists aged 18 to 35.
Of the 19 applications received during the 2026 call for projects, 15 projects were selected.
The amounts range from $3,200 (Les Amis de l'orgue de Québec) to $9,275 (L'Artère), and include L'Ampli de Québec, Machine de Cirque, the Morrin Centre, Engramme, VU and others.
The funds come from the Entente de développement culturel between the City and the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The owner of 2, rue du Parc-Saint-Laurent, in Beauport, wants to add two dwellings in the basement of a building that already has six.
The by-law requires eight parking spaces; the project provides for six.
The City is exempting the owner from providing the two missing spaces.
In exchange, the owner must pay $1,000 to the "Fonds de stationnement" (parking fund), no later than 30 days after the borough council adopts the resolution.
According to the analysis, the area is served by public transit and on-street parking there is used at a low to moderate level.
The City is giving $30,000 to the Réseau indépendant des diffuseurs d'événements artistiques unis (RIDEAU) for its RIDEAU 2026 event.
The 39th edition of the event takes place in Québec from February 15 to 19, 2026.
Destination Québec cité is adding $12,800, bringing the total municipal contribution to $42,800, which is less than 4% of the event's $1.2M budget.

The 2026 edition is more firmly rooted in the basse-ville, especially the Saint-Roch neighbourhood; showcase performances are being held at the Théâtre Capitole, the Théâtre Petit Champlain, the Grizzly Fuzz, the Impérial Bell, Manivelle and the Grand Théâtre de Québec, among others.
A general public component gives residents free access to activities: more than 1,300 tickets were offered in 2025.
The City had also given $30,000 in 2025, $25,000 in 2024 and $30,000 in 2023.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de la culture et du patrimoine.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough is paying out $610,948 in grants to 80 organizations.
This money goes toward operating expenses of organizations recognized by the City.
The applications covered were submitted on February 20, 2026, in addition to payments for the 2nd or 3rd year of the program.
The amounts vary from one organization to another, for example $706 for the Groupe Vocal Ambitus and $20,000 for the Centre social de la Croix Blanche.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget, under the "Soutien aux organismes" (support for organizations) activity.
The borough council adopted the decision on April 27, 2026 (resolution CA1-2026-0070).
Québec's urban agglomeration council adopts the inventory of heritage buildings in Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures.
The inventory lists and documents 203 buildings constructed before 1940 within the city's territory.
The properties concerned are located mainly on route 138, the 3e and 4e Rangs, the rang des Mines, the chemin du Lac and the chemin de la Butte.
The comité de démolition of Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures will have to take the heritage character of these buildings into account when reviewing demolition applications.
The adoption puts an end to the transitional measure that imposed a three-month waiting period to obtain the ministère's opinion before any demolition of a pre-1940 building.
The City states that permit applications can therefore be processed more quickly.
This inventory requirement stems from the Loi sur le patrimoine culturel, as amended on April 1, 2021.
The City is granting a minor exemption for the property at 356-360, rue Laviolette, in the Saint-Sauveur neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The exemption allows a ground occupancy rate of 10% instead of the 40% required by the borough's planning by-law.
The owner wants to demolish an annex of the building, divide the land into two lots, and build a new eight-unit building on the vacant lot.
According to the documents, ground occupancy would go from 17.3% at the start to 41.4% for the whole site once the new building is built.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion by majority on April 28, 2026; the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec also gave a favourable opinion.
No amount of money is tied to this decision.

On March 26, 2026, the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec authorized the demolition of the house located at 1137, chemin de Bélair, in the Val-Bélair neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The Commission relied on a technical opinion from Tétra Tech engineers dated December 19, 2025, which concludes that the building is no longer safe and that its structure cannot be salvaged.
After the demolition, the land will have to be cleaned up, levelled and planted with vegetation.
No one submitted a written comment or asked the city council to review the decision within the 30-day period.
The urban agglomeration council takes note of the decision, waives its power of disallowance and shortens the 90-day period provided for that purpose.
The City will then be able to issue the authorization certificate required for the demolition.
The document states that there is no financial impact.

The City is awarding Bio-Contrôle Arboricole inc. (Gatineau) a contract worth $354,199.80 before taxes to treat city-owned trees by injecting the biopesticide TreeAzin against the emerald ash borer and other insects.
The contract runs from the date it is awarded until October 1, 2026, at a unit price per centimetre of trunk.
Private property owners in Québec City can have their own trees treated at the same price as the City if they make a request to the company before September 4, 2026.
Residents must contact the company themselves: the City does not handle the planning, the coordination or the billing of these private treatments.
An information campaign will give residents the supplier's contact information and the details, in the weeks following the awarding of the contract.
Three compliant bids were received; the net cost to the City is $371,865.52, paid out of the budget of the Arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The City is amending its planning by-law to allow the non-profit organization Poliquin-Simms2 to occupy part of the building at 199, 2e Avenue, in Vieux-Limoilou.
The organization will be able to create, rehearse and produce its circus shows there, and store its equipment, vehicles and stage trailers. About 15% of the space will be used as offices.
No shows will be presented on site.
The current rule limits this type of artist's studio to 200 square metres; the authorization allows 350 square metres.
The authorization applies only to Poliquin-Simms2, is not transferable and lasts 100 years.
The part of the building involved was partly destroyed by fire in November 2023 and must be rebuilt.
The conseil de quartier du Vieux-Limoilou will give its opinion and hold a public consultation meeting; the by-law is not subject to a referendum.
The Ville de Québec accepts two permits from Hydro-Québec (AG-144252 and 1402-024/420352) to carry out work on the TramCité project in the Pie-XII energy corridor.
The work will take place on land owned by the City, which is subject to easements in favour of Hydro-Québec.
The City will have to design and protect the buried conduits according to the ministère des Transports' design standards for road bridges and culverts (class CL-625 or QS-660 truck).
The conduits must never block the passage of Hydro-Québec trucks and vehicles, in any season, including during the spring thaw.
The City will have to respect the final elevations shown on the plans.
The City will have to produce a coexistence study confirming that the installation can safely coexist with the 735 kV power line, and send a copy of it to Hydro-Québec.
The document states that there is no financial impact.
The Ville de Québec is buying the property at 3, avenue des Sablonnières, in the Beauport borough, for $140,000 plus taxes.
It is using a right of first refusal obtained in 2000, after the owner, Jocelyn Bisson, notified it on July 30, 2026 of his intention to sell.
The lot is 9,265.90 square metres and is located in the flood plain of the rivière Montmorency, an area exposed to flooding.
The building and its outbuildings will be demolished later by the Service de la gestion des immeubles.
The City says it wants to remove a vulnerable use from the risk area and restore the land's ability to hold back flood waters.
The purchase is made without any warranty of quality, at the City's risk; the property is assessed at $75,000 on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3158 on the management of wetlands and bodies of water.
The Service des approvisionnements is submitting its 2025 annual report on the application of the contract management by-laws; city council and the urban agglomeration council are taking note of it.
The report will be published on the City's website.
In 2025, the executive committee authorized 78 businesses located outside Québec (or outside the territory covered by an agreement) to obtain contracts, for a total of CAN$512,234.
The City approved 63,480 purchase orders in 2025, worth $925.89M before taxes, compared with $840.02M in 2024.
The share of contracts awarded to local suppliers rose from 56.32% to 68.22% of the value awarded.
The two contract management by-laws were not amended in 2025.
The Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux comes into force on April 1, 2026, and the City will have to apply it.
The City is changing the zoning of six areas in the Plateau neighbourhood, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge arrondissement (zones 34001Ha, 34004Ha, 34202Ha, 34503Ha, 34702Ha and 34708Ha).
In these zones, a detached building will be allowed to have up to three dwellings instead of two.
In four of these zones (34001Ha, 34004Ha, 34202Ha and 34708Ha), parking changes from the "Général" type to the "Axe structurant A" type: no minimum number of parking spaces is required.
The rules on height and setbacks (the distance between the building and the property lines) are not changing.
The change follows a request to bring three dwellings at 811, avenue Wilfrid-Pelletier into compliance.
The borough council is asking for the opinion of the conseil de quartier du Plateau, which will hold the public consultation meeting.
The by-law contains no provisions that can be subject to a referendum.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 640, boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, in the Vanier neighbourhood (Arrondissement des Rivières).
The planned residential building may be built 2.3 metres from avenue Turcotte and 5 metres from boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, instead of the 6 metres required by the planning by-law.
The restaurant "Chez Gaston", currently on the property, will eventually be demolished to make way for a 30-unit building.
The Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec itself asked that the building be moved closer to the street, so it fits better into the area.
According to the analysis, the sight triangle at the intersection is respected and visibility remains safe.
The planning advisory committee unanimously recommended the exemption on August 3, 2026; the borough council adopted it on August 24, 2026.
The City is granting the "Famille Lachance" a right to partially cut wood and a right of access on about 17.1 hectares of a City-owned property in Saint-Tite-des-Caps, for $100 plus taxes.
The right lasts 20 years from the last signature, with two possible renewals of 5 years each.
The cutting replaces a right granted in 2004 to Donat Lachance; it is moved to a parcel located away from the daily operations of the landfill site.
The family may only cut and access the site from August 1 to November 30, unless the City gives written authorization.
Hunting is prohibited, access through the Hydro-Québec easement is prohibited, and access is by route 138; the family pays for the development and maintenance of the forest roads.
The City cannot revoke the right during the first 10 years (except in case of default), after which it may do so at any time with 6 months' written notice.
The right cannot be transferred, and the family gets a preference to buy the property as long as the cutting right remains in force.
The urban agglomeration council takes note of the 2026-2028 Strategic Plan of Destination Québec cité, the tourism organization that is also a department of the Ville de Québec.
The former plan ended at the end of 2025; the board of directors of Destination Québec cité approved the new one on January 28, 2026.

The plan covers the Québec tourism region: the city, L'Ancienne-Lorette, Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, Wendake and the regional county municipalities (MRC) of Portneuf, La Jacques-Cartier, l'Île d'Orléans and la Côte-de-Beaupré.
It sets three focus areas for 2026-2028: tourism growth, cohesion within the regional industry, and capacity building (data, innovation, digital shift).
The document reports the following for 2025: 4.5M tourists, $2.71B in tourism spending and 38,341 tourism-related jobs.
The plan was prepared following consultations with institutional partners, employees, and members from the attractions and events sectors.
No financial impact is indicated in the decision summary.
The City is hiring the firm Pluritec ltée to provide engineering services for the construction of the escalier des Franciscains, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough.
The contract is worth $275,597 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $289,342.40.
The firm must design the detailed engineering, produce the plans and specifications, estimate the cost of the work, and supervise the work site on-site during construction.
Pluritec is authorized to apply, on the City's behalf, for the permits and authorizations required from government departments, urban technical network companies and other authorities.
Two companies submitted bids: Pluritec ($275,597) and Tétra Tech QI inc. ($465,935). The contract goes to Pluritec, which obtained the best final score.
The selected bid is 20.2% lower than the estimate of the requesting department ($345,481.76).
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3289.
The City is giving up a water and sewer easement it had held since 1975 on land on rue Jean-Durand and avenue Nérée-Tremblay, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The company 9397-4442 Québec inc. (Logisco) had asked for this easement to be dropped so it could carry out a real estate project on its land.
City departments said they were in favour: the pipes in question are no longer used by the City.
The company is paying $100, plus taxes, an amount that will go into the City's general fund.
The company applied for a permit to demolish residential buildings located on lot 1 738 385 in order to build a new project there.
The pipes become private: the company will have to pay for any relocation or removal, install storm and sanitary manholes at the limit of the City's right-of-way, and cover the notary fees.
The City will have no responsibility related to these pipes.
The City is changing the zoning of zone 22031Ha, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood (arrondissement des Rivières), near rue de Caen, avenue du Costebelle and rue du Joybert.
The maximum number of dwellings allowed in a detached building in this zone goes from two to three.
No minimum number of parking spaces will be required for dwellings anymore: the zone is switching to the "Axe structurant B" parking type.
The building standards (maximum height of 10.5 m, two storeys, setbacks) stay the same.
The request comes from an owner at 5560-5564, rue de Caen, who wants to add a dwelling in the basement of her home.
The conseil de quartier de Duberger-Les Saules will be consulted and will hold a public meeting; interested people will have seven days after that meeting to submit their comments in writing.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; the borough council is aiming to adopt it on February 24, 2026.
The City is entrusting the organization Loisirs Lebourgneuf inc. with the programming, maintenance and supervision of the piscine extérieure Lebourgneuf, in the Arrondissement des Rivières.
The agreement covers 27 months, from June 12, 2026 to August 27, 2028.
The contract is for $287,836.05 (plus GST and QST); the net cost to the City is $302,191.88.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement des Rivières, spread over 2026, 2027 and 2028.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
The previous agreement with the same organization ended on August 24, 2025.
The president and the assistant clerk of the Arrondissement des Rivières will sign the agreement.
The City is awarding Pluritec ltée a professional services contract worth $408,560 (before GST and QST) to repair two stairways.

The work involves rebuilding the escalier de la Chapelle, between Côte-d'Abraham and rue Saint-Vallier Est, and reinforcing the escalier Lépine, between rue Saint-Augustin and rue Saint-Vallier Est, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The contract covers all the engineering work, including supervision of the construction.
Pluritec will be allowed to apply, on the City's behalf, for the permits and authorizations needed from government departments, utility network companies and other authorities.
Two bids were received: Pluritec at $408,560 and Tetra Tech QI inc. at $594,056.50; Pluritec obtained the best final score.
The net cost to the City is $428,936.93, funded through loan by-law R.V.Q. 3390.

The City has completed the three projects funded by $26,500,000 in assistance from the Québec government: the trail at the foot of the Sillery cliff, the footbridge between Pointe-aux-Lièvres and Limoilou, and the decontamination of the Pointe-aux-Lièvres and D'Estimauville eco-neighbourhoods.
There is $4M left unspent. The City was supposed to repay it to the government, but the ministry agrees to let it be reused.

This money will be used to decontaminate three sites, in this order of priority: the former Anacolor plant in Vieux-Cap-Rouge (about $2.2M), the Îlot-Saint-Vincent-de-Paul in Vieux-Québec (about $4.1M) and the former Gailuron bakery in Beauport (about $4.5M).

These decontaminations are meant to allow, later on: about 100 housing units and businesses in Cap-Rouge, about 150 social housing units with an 80-space childcare centre (CPE) in Vieux-Québec, and about 75 housing units with a public square in Beauport.
The new work must be completed before December 31, 2029.
Any amount not used at the end will have to be repaid to the government within 30 days.
The City wants to allow indoor and outdoor storage at 2156-2162, rue Cyrille-Duquet, in the parc industriel Jean-Talon (Saint-Sauveur neighbourhood).
The City already leases the entire building for ten years: about 20 employees have offices there and various pieces of equipment are stored inside, which the current zoning does not allow.

The outdoor storage would be used by the equipment depot of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire: containers, crowd-control fencing, mobile stages, trucks, bulk materials, street furniture, etc.
The outdoor storage would be located in the back yard and in part of the side yard, surrounded by an opaque fence 2.0 metres high.
The authorization applies only to this property, not to the whole of zone 22624Cc, which includes several other lots on rue Cyrille-Duquet.
The occupancy must begin within two years after the by-law comes into force, otherwise the authorization lapses.
The by-law may be subject to approval by referendum; the conseil de quartier de Saint-Sauveur will be consulted and will hold a public meeting, followed by seven days for written comments.
The City is banning parking at all times on part of rue de La Havane, east side, between avenue de Porto and rue de Morelia (Arrondissement des Rivières, Neufchâtel-Lebourgneuf district).
The ban covers 22 metres, starting 45 metres south of avenue de Porto.
The measure applies to the 7 metres on each side of the south entrance to the parking lot of the building at 2285, rue de La Havane.
Two parking spaces are being removed.
The request came from a resident; the Service du transport states that vehicles parked near the entrance block the view of drivers exiting the private parking lot.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The arrondissement de Beauport is paying out $42,786 in grants to seven organizations, split across eight applications submitted on December 15, 2025.
Entraide Agapè receives the largest share, $27,647, for a strategic planning project.
Matinée Frimousses receives two grants: $3,201 for chairs, cushions and children's games, and $2,210 for a communications and marketing plan.
L'Harmonie des Cascades de Beauport receives $4,250 to buy a vibraphone, and the Conseil beauportois de la culture receives $2,175 for conference chairs.

Communautés Solidaires receives $1,972 for lettering on a vehicle, the Club de tennis Beauport-Ouest receives $831 for a ball machine, and the Club Radio Amateur de Québec receives $500 for an awards gala marking its 100th anniversary.
The money comes from the arrondissement's operating budget, under the "Soutien aux organismes" (support for organizations) line.
The City is applying for $64,240 from the Fondation de la faune du Québec to plan the restoration of wetlands and bodies of water north of the Beauport area.
The project aims to restore the habitat of the northern dusky salamander, which has been disturbed by off-road vehicles using informal trails alongside the TQ-3 federated snowmobile trail.
It also aims to reduce the amount of sediment flowing into lac John.
The total cost of the project is estimated at $116,279; the grant would cover 55.2%, with the rest coming from in-kind contributions from Canards Illimités Canada and the City.
Council is authorizing the submission of the application and the signing of a financial assistance agreement if the funding is confirmed.
The Fondation is to announce its decision around mid-May 2026; the planning work, including detailed plans and specifications, would take place in 2026.
No financial impact is indicated for the City.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 51, rue des Jardins, in Vieux-Québec, to allow the installation of a fence that does not comply with the planning by-law.
The fence may be up to 2.75 metres high on the building side, instead of the maximum of 2 metres normally allowed.
It may also be 100% opaque and installed directly on the property line, rather than at least 3 metres from a sidewalk.
This screen fence will be used to hide the garbage containers and mechanical equipment that are visible from rue des Jardins.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the application on July 14, 2026, and the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec gave a favourable opinion.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council adopted the decision on August 31, 2026.
The Ville de Québec will pay $25,000 per year to the organization Forces AVENIR for its Galas, in 2026, 2027 and 2028, for a total of $75,000.
Forces AVENIR organizes the Galas Forces AVENIR universitaire, collégial and secondaire, which highlight student involvement.
The 2026 payment is made within 30 days after the signing; those for 2027 and 2028 follow the sending of an invoice after January 1 of the year concerned.
No amount is paid if the Gala does not take place during the year, and any amount paid in advance must be repaid within 30 days.
The organization must give the City 2 tickets per year and provide it with visibility as a host partner.
The City had already paid $25,000 in 2023, 2024 and 2025.
Director general Luc Monty will be away from August 27 (afternoon) to September 4, 2026.
The City appoints Isabelle Dubois, assistant director general, as interim director general for that period.
While serving as interim, she holds all the powers and obligations of the director general.
The decision was made by the executive committee on August 26, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-1089).
The City wants to acquire a strip of land of about 35.10 square metres along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, to widen the street right-of-way.
The acquisition will be made by mutual agreement with the owner or, failing an agreement, by expropriation.
The land is required for the Réseau structurant de transport en commun project, now called TramCité.
The owner has been notified of the process, the next steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
The entire property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $229,000, or $364.48 per square metre.
If the project no longer needs the land, the City may abandon the expropriation proceedings, in whole or in part.
The money comes from the agglomeration loan by-law related to the Réseau structurant de transport en commun.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 2614-2620, 1re Avenue, in the Lairet neighbourhood (Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The enclosed stairwell leading to the basement will be allowed to encroach 3.5 metres into the rear setback, instead of the maximum of 1.5 metre set out in the planning by-law.
The owner is removing the commercial use on the ground floor and in the basement in order to add two dwellings, bringing the building to six dwellings.
The existing rear staircase leading to the basement will be enclosed, in particular to fix water infiltration in the basement.
According to the analysis, the staircase will take up almost the same area as before, and the yard is already fenced with balconies above the staircase.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme was in favour on January 6, 2026, and the Commission d'urbanisme (CUCQ) also gave a favourable opinion.
The City is authorizing Construction C.R.D. inc. to open a new street of about 670 metres, shaped like a "U" and connected to boulevard Louis-XIV, in Beauport (Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux district).

The Domaine Louis-XIV project plans about 182 housing units: 70 semi-detached houses and three 4-storey buildings with about 112 rental units in total; another developer could add a building with at least 60 units.
Total investments are estimated at about $71,000,000, including about $6,000,000 (taxes included) for municipal infrastructure.
The City is paying $127,300 (before taxes) to the developer as a financial contribution, for a net expense of $133,649.09.
The developer is giving the City, free of charge, the street, a retention basin with plantings, and a lot for the start of a street with a bike link; it will pay the parks compensation in cash.

The developer will restore the natural state of the bank of the watercourse to the west, decommission a sanitary sewer pipe, create a wooded strip with a vegetated ditch near the properties on rue George-Sand, and build a bike link.

The City plans a sidewalk on the south side of boulevard Louis-XIV between rue Blanche-Lamontagne and rue Montpellier within about five years; the developer will pay for the 120-metre portion in front of its land.
The City is expanding the Centre-Ville commercial zone by replacing the map attached to the Règlement sur les sociétés de développement commercial.
The new sectors being added are located along rue De Saint-Vallier Est, boulevard Charest Est, rue de la Couronne and rue Dorchester.
This map change is needed so that the Société de développement commercial (SDC) Centre-Ville de Québec can then expand its commercial district.
The SDC's goal was to broaden its membership base, increase its revenues and reflect the commercial activity of the Saint-Roch area.
The decision summary does not mention any financial impact.

On May 21, 2026, the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec authorized the demolition of an accessory building located behind the maison Jules-Latouche, at 2032, avenue Royale, in the quartier des Chutes-Montmorency (arrondissement de Beauport).
The Commission is relying on an expert report concluding that the building, put up between 1875 and 1950, is unstable and dangerous, and that repairing it would amount to rebuilding almost all of it.
After the demolition, the land will have to be cleaned up, levelled and planted with vegetation; no new construction is planned.
No written comments were received during the publication period (May 5 to 15, 2026) and no request for review was filed within the 30-day period.
The urban agglomeration council confirms that it will not overturn the decision and shortens the 90-day period it had to do so.
The file was sent to the ministère de la Culture et des Communications; the work cannot begin before it gives its authorization.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 10055, boulevard de l'Ormière, in the Des Châtels neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The exemption allows a main façade of 13 metres instead of the 18.51 metres required, which is 35% of the lot width instead of 50%.
It paves the way for the construction of a four-storey residential building with about 105 housing units.
Garage doors on the façade will lead to the underground parking; according to the analysis, the narrowness of the lot prevents access through the side yard.
Buildings currently on the land must be demolished.
The land is being enlarged through relotting in order to build an access lane to the waste containers; the developer is adding plantings as compensation.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the application on January 28, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is granting a minor exemption at 7807, rue des Loups-Marins, in the Orsainville neighbourhood (Arrondissement de Charlesbourg).

The exemption makes the following compliant: an in-ground pool and its equipment, a ground-level deck, a shed of no more than 14 square metres, and the extension of a retaining wall, all located in a natural conservation zone where such structures are not allowed.
The elements are located 2.50 metres from the rear property line and 5.50 metres from the west side property line.
The lot borders a 10-metre conservation strip created when the streets in the area were opened, in order to protect the wooded area; construction and tree cutting are prohibited there.
According to the City's analysis, an authorization certificate had been issued in error, which allowed the pool to be built; without the exemption, the owner would have to relocate it.
The City notes that no trees were cut down, as this part of the lot has been cleared since at least 2011.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on June 17, 2026, by majority.

The executive committee authorizes the Service des approvisionnements to purchase computer hardware and software from companies that do not have an establishment in Quebec, Canada or a European Union country, for the Service des technologies de l'information.

Since a Government of Quebec regulation enacted on March 6, 2025, these over-the-counter (mutual agreement) purchases require prior authorization, regardless of the amount, including payments by credit card.
The regulation covers computer hardware and software, medical supplies and equipment, pharmaceutical products and scientific instruments.
The company named in the appendix is Code Dector Pty Ltd, of Brisbane, Australia, for the new version of the Teracopy perpetual licences.
This contract falls within a range of $0 to $33,000 and will be paid by purchasing card.
The decision was made by resolution CE-2026-0691 on May 27, 2026.
The City is authorizing the demolition of a former barn-stable located behind the house at 4335, rue Michelet, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The building, constructed between 1900 and 1930, is recognized as a heritage property; the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec approved the demolition on June 18, 2026.
The decision is based on an engineer's report dated March 18, 2026 concluding that the structure is no longer safe and cannot be salvaged, as well as on the cost of restoring it.
After the demolition, the owner will have to clean, level and replant the land with vegetation; no new building is planned.
No one asked for a review of the decision within 30 days, and no buyer had come forward for the property.
The urban agglomeration council is waiving its power to cancel the decision and is shortening the 90-day time limit, which clears the way for the authorization certificate to be issued.
This matter has no financial impact for the City.
The City is refusing the exemptions requested for a vacant lot on rue Seigneuriale, in the Vieux-Bourg neighbourhood in Beauport (Robert-Giffard district).
The developer wanted to build a detached three-unit building there.

The project did not meet any of the required setbacks: 0.8 m at the front instead of 2.0 m, 0 m on the side instead of 1.2 m, 1.5 m of combined side yards instead of 4.8 m, and 6.1 m at the rear instead of 7.5 m.

According to the analysis, a building 0.91 m from the front lot line would break the alignment of the houses on this section of rue Seigneuriale and would interfere with the enjoyment of neighbouring properties.
The analysis indicates that a smaller building could be built on the lot while meeting the rules in force.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme de Beauport had unanimously recommended refusal on February 19, 2026.
The City is buying a second tilt-cab truck with a van body from Camions Isuzu Lévis, for $141,897 (plus GST and QST).
The total contract for lot 1 therefore goes from $141,897 to $283,794 (plus GST and QST).
The City is exercising a purchase option already included in the October 2025 contract, at the same price as the first unit.
The first truck went to the Service de protection contre l'incendie; the second will go to the Service de la gestion des immeubles.
The truck replaces equipment that has reached the end of its useful life; the City wants to speed up delivery to avoid an interruption in service to residents.
The net expense is $148,974.12, funded by loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1655.
The City is changing the zoning in Vieux-Limoilou to restrict commercial tourist accommodation, following a review begun in the fall of 2024 and in a context of a housing crisis.
General tourist accommodation (C10) is being removed from three zones: 19209Mc, 19215Mb and 19230Cb. Youth hostels (C12) are also being removed from zones 19209Mc and 19215Mb.

The supply is being refocused on the mixed-use zone of 3e Avenue (19204Mb), where tourist accommodation will no longer be allowed on the ground floor, but where the limit of five units per building is being eliminated.
In that same zone, the protection of existing housing will now extend from the second floor up, rather than from the third floor up.

The City is allowing a dental clinic on the ground floor at 801, 3e Avenue by permitting health care establishments without accommodation on that floor and by raising the maximum floor area from 400 to 800 square metres per building.
The conseil de quartier du Vieux-Limoilou will give its opinion and hold a public consultation meeting; interested persons will have seven days after the meeting to submit their comments in writing.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum. The borough council adopted the resolution on May 25, 2026.
The City is awarding the firm Pluritec ltée a professional engineering services contract for the repair of various sewer structures in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The contract is worth $896,011 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $940,699.55.
The mandate covers studies, design, plans and specifications, cost estimates and supervision of the work on site.
Pluritec will be able to apply for permits and authorizations on the City's behalf from government departments and utility network companies, with the prior agreement of the Service de l'ingénierie.
Three bids were received; Pluritec obtained the best score, ahead of WSP Canada inc. ($1,392,720).
The selected price is 28% higher than the requesting department's estimate of $700,000, a gap the City attributes to the complexity of the project.
The funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1450.
The City will pay $378,300 over three years to the organization Jeunes musiciens du monde: $137,700 in 2026, $126,100 in 2027 and $114,500 in 2028.
The money is used to maintain the music lessons and musical expression activities offered free of charge to young people.
The activities target the Saint-Sauveur, Saint-Roch and Vanier neighbourhoods and two other neighbourhoods chosen according to needs, in consultation with the City.
For 2026, the organization wants to reach about 350 young people, half of them from immigrant backgrounds.
The amounts go down each year because the City is gradually reducing the share of management costs it covers: 31% in 2025, 24% at the end of the agreement.
The organization will have to report each year and mention the City's contribution in its official publications.
The 2027 and 2028 payments depend on the City adopting its budgets.
The City is applying for one or more grants from the ministère de l'Environnement (MELCCFP) under the PRRESO program, which targets non-domestic contaminants discharged into sewers.
The money would be used to measure industrial releases of PFAS ("forever chemicals") into the sanitary sewer system and to find ways to reduce them.
The goal: add a PFAS standard to by-law R.A.V.Q. 1124, which governs industrial discharges into the sewer.
Less PFAS in municipal sludge means better digestate at the Centre de biométhanisation de l'agglomération de Québec, making it easier to put to use in agriculture.
The grant can reach $150,000 per project and covers a maximum of 70% of the City's eligible expenses.
The money would go to professional services, laboratory analyses, salaries related to the project, and equipment or materials.
The documents required by the program must be submitted by September 7, 2026.
The City is awarding the televised inspection of the pipes at its landfill site to the firm Can-Explore inc., of Québec.
The contract is estimated at $236,250 before taxes, from the date it is awarded until December 31, 2028.
The work covers three areas: the engineered landfill site in Saint-Joachim, the sanitary landfill site in Saint-Tite-des-Caps, and the leachate treatment plant.
These inspections are part of the preventive maintenance required by the authorizations from the ministère de l'Environnement and deal with the flow of leachate.
The contract can be renewed twice for 12 months, with indexing based on the consumer price index; the estimated total up to 2030 reaches $398,250 before taxes.
Only one firm submitted a bid, at 10% above the City's estimate ($214,732.10).
The net expense for the urban agglomeration is estimated at $248,032.98, subject to the adoption of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.
The Ville de Québec is awarding a contract to Edgenda conseil inc. for a solution architecture consultant for MS Dynamics 365.
The contract is worth $365,472 (plus GST and QST) for 24 months, starting from its signing; the net expense is $383,699.92.
The contract can be renewed for another 12 months, which would bring the maximum total to $548,208 before taxes.
The consultant must prepare the migration of data from the 311 service and from the permits and inspections management system to MS Dynamics 365 in the cloud.
The mandate includes designing the architecture, writing the technical documents and providing advice on information security.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders, through the master agreement of the ministère de la Cybersécurité et du Numérique.
The funds come from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1758 on information technology business solutions.
The City is reorganizing its Service de l'évaluation, which keeps the property assessment rolls up to date for the 190,000 assessment units in the agglomeration of Québec.

Two new divisions replace the former ones: a Division des opérations (day-to-day activities) and a Division de la stratégie et de l'amélioration des pratiques (projects, performance, legislative changes).
All sections will now report to both divisions, with new section names grouped by type of building (residential and land, non-residential and multi-family).
The City is also creating a Direction de l'innovation et de l'intelligence des données.
Management positions and the people holding them are being transferred to the new units; each job will be reviewed again to confirm its salary class.
A vacant property assessment technician position (class 6) becomes a head clerk position (class 5) to strengthen administrative support.
The City states that the change requires no additional budget and no unauthorized increase in staff.
The City is authorizing a $16,600 expense for mission costs (airfare, ground transportation, accommodation), reimbursed upon submission of supporting documents.
Mélissa Coulombe-Leduc, member of the executive committee, and Sarah-Ève Huot, international relations advisor, are accompanying the mayor to Dubrovnik and Madrid from April 21 to 30, 2026.
In Dubrovnik, this is a meeting of the board of directors of the Organization of World Heritage Cities, which Québec currently chairs.
In Madrid, they are taking part in the Bloomberg CityLab summit and a meeting of the OECD Champion Mayors Initiative; Bloomberg CityLab is paying the mayor's costs.
Ms. Coulombe-Leduc is continuing on her own to Amsterdam and Bruges from April 25 to 30 to observe practices in mobility and land use planning.
The City links these learnings to upcoming changes in traffic patterns in Vieux-Québec and surrounding areas.
An overrun of no more than 10% of the authorized amount is accepted without further authorization.
The City is selling a vacant lot of 3,981.1 m² located along boulevard Père-Lelièvre, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The buyer is Les Résidences Populaires de Québec inc., a non-profit organization based on rue de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres.
The price is $1,900,000 plus taxes, or $477.26 per square metre; the lot is assessed at $1,770,000 on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll.
The buyer plans to build a building with about 62 housing units for families and single people with low or modest incomes.
The buyer must start construction within 12 months and obtain final approval of its project under the Programme d'habitation abordable Québec of the Société d'habitation du Québec.
The lot had been acquired in 2021 to preserve the green space and the tree cover; the City is transferring it to the private domain to allow the sale.
The sale is made without warranty: the buyer assumes the environmental and geotechnical risks, and the $1,900,000 in proceeds will go to the general fund.
The City is selling a vacant lot of 3,210.30 m² along rue des Moqueurs, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough, for $2,400,000 plus taxes ($747.59 per square metre).
The buyer is La Bouée société acheteuse de préservation et de développement de l'habitat communautaire, whose head office is at 1199, 4e Avenue in Québec.
The buyer wants to build a building with about 90 housing units (studios and 3 ½ to 6 ½) for families and single people with low or modest incomes, with a common room and offices.
Construction must begin within 36 months after the deed is signed; otherwise, the buyer will have to pay the City $4,000 per month.
The sale depends on the project being selected under the Programme d'habitation abordable Québec of the Société d'habitation du Québec.
The project must meet the requirements of the écoquartier D'Estimauville; the land is sold without warranty and the buyer takes on environmental responsibility.
The land is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $1,695,000; the $2,400,000 will go into the City's general fund.
The City is adding a parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility on avenue Deblois, in front of the bibliothèque du Chemin-Royal (2100, avenue Deblois), in Beauport.
This space replaces the one that was lost when the library's parking lot was redeveloped.
The zone is on the east side of avenue Deblois, 26 metres north of chemin Royal, and is 6 metres long.
Parking will be prohibited there, except for vehicles with a permit or licence plate for people with disabilities.
No amount is indicated in the file.
The executive committee approves a reorganization of the structure of the Service de police de la Ville de Québec (SPVQ), with no net creation of positions and no budget variance.
Patrol at the La Cité and Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge stations, until now led by two inspectors, will report to a single inspector and five captains, one per rotating team.
A new deputy commander role is created to supervise each patrol team; the Unité centre de vigie et de soutien opérationnel is moved under the Section patrouille.

A Direction du développement stratégique is created under the management of the police service, including an inspector in charge, a strategic advisor, professional standards, and occupational health and safety.

The SPVQ is creating a Section analyse stratégique to oversee intelligence, following a 2017 audit by the ministère de la Sécurité publique, as well as a Module triage, contrôle-qualité, service client.

Two other sections are created: Logistique et innovation (technology, projects, buildings, psychological support) and Soutien à la surveillance du territoire (coordination, night team, Unité GRIPP, vehicle fleet).

A Section développement de la performance opérationnelle is created within administrative and financial affairs, with a new Module détection des risques opérationnels to guide and mentor supervisors in the field.
The Ville de Québec is submitting a list of 34 climate projects to the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation to obtain financial assistance, for eligible costs of $55.6M.
The program can cover 80% of the eligible costs of each project; the City commits to paying all non-eligible costs, cost overruns and the maintenance of the subsidized facilities.
The projects concern the agglomeration and the related cities, but not the territory of the city of Québec itself, which is already covered by a $49M agreement signed in March 2022.
The programming includes projects in L'Ancienne-Lorette (greening and de-paving, $747,863) and in Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures (tree planting, $200,000).

Among the projects: decarbonization of ExpoCité and of the fire stations, the VivaCité corridor on boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel ($18M), a park-and-ride lot on rue Roussin, a bike link on boulevard Raymond, and a fund for sustainable housing.
The resolution authorizing the submission must be sent to the ministère no later than February 27, 2026.
If the grant is awarded, the City will have to sign an agreement with the ministère and agreements with each of the related cities.
The City wants to obtain permanent easements on two parts of a lane in the neighbourhood near boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest and rue Crémazie Ouest, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough.
These easements will be used to move public utility conduits and networks for the TramCité tramway project.
The two parcels involved measure about 42.1 and 157.6 square metres.
The City will first try to reach an amicable agreement with the owner; if not, it may proceed by expropriation.
If the project no longer needs these easements, the City may abandon the expropriation proceedings, in whole or in part.
The funds come from the loan by-law tied to the construction of the structuring public transit network.
The lane involved is not listed on the assessment roll.
The City wants to acquire a piece of land of about 449.9 square metres alongside rue de la Faune, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The acquisition will be used to widen rue de la Faune, as part of the project to rebuild this street.
The City will first try to reach an agreement with the owners by mutual consent; if the discussions fail, it may proceed by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the acquisition or expropriation proceedings.
The Division de l'arpentage et de la géomatique will prepare the necessary plans, technical descriptions and cadastral operations.
The property, in its largest extent, is entered on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $53,000, which is $7.75 per square metre.
The funds come from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 on the work to redevelop rue de la Faune.
The Ville de Québec is replacing its school playground development assistance program, adopted in 2021, with a revised version.
A parc-école (school playground) is a space developed together with a school so that it serves both students and local residents.
The program is now open to all school establishments (preschool, elementary, secondary) in the territory, including those that are not under the Centres de services scolaires.
The contribution is simplified: up to $100,000 per application, regardless of the project's budget, without exceeding 50% of eligible expenses.
The former formula granted between $5,000 and $100,000 based on tiers linked to the size of the project.
Applications must be sent by email in a single submission no later than June 15 of each year; incomplete files are not assessed.
Once the work is done, the City does not take on the maintenance or replacement of the equipment, unless there is a prior agreement.
The Ville de Québec will pay $300,000 to the Festival d'opéra de Québec for its 2026 edition.
The festival will run from July 21 to August 2, 2026, in venues such as the Grand Théâtre, La Bordée and the Périscope, and at various outdoor sites.
The program includes 4 productions and 2 paid indoor concerts, plus 3 free outdoor activities, including a new concert called "Sors tes grands airs!" at place Jean-Béliveau.
The grant covers 12.8% of the event's budget, estimated at $2,344,747.
The money will be paid in three instalments: $180,000, then $90,000, then $30,000 when the financial statements are filed ($270,000 in 2026 and $30,000 in 2027).
The funding is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners.
Last year, the City paid $290,000 to the same festival; in 2024, $350,000.
The City is applying for financial assistance from Hydro-Québec under the « Fonds de verdissement », which can cover up to 100% of eligible costs, up to a maximum of $50,000 per project.
The money would be used to plant 154 trees in 2026, divided into 11 lots across the whole territory of the city of Québec.
The plantings will test new species that are not common in the municipal inventory or that come from warmer zones, with follow-up on successes and failures.
The chosen locations represent different settings: street plantings, parks, downtown and suburbs.
Eligible costs cover the purchase of plants, shipping and planting work; a maximum of 25% can go to professional services.
Carolyne Larouche, director of the arrondissements of Beauport, Charlesbourg and La Cité-Limoilou, is authorized to act on behalf of the City for this application.
The executive committee adopted resolution CE-2026-0485 on April 15, 2026.
The City is lowering the speed limit on rue Provancher from 50 km/h to 40 km/h, at all times.
The change affects rue Provancher in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, district de Cap-Rouge–Laurentien.
The order covers the section between boulevard de la Chaudière and côte de Cap-Rouge; the decision summary also states that the change will apply from côte de Cap-Rouge to rue du Domaine.
The limit had been kept at 50 km/h during the 2021 review, but the school zone has since been extended to rue Augustin-Bourbeau and the number of dwellings has increased slightly.
The analysis by the Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente is based on eight criteria, including the type of environment, the density of human activity and the width of the roadway.
No financial impact is indicated in the document.
The City is awarding Béton Provincial ltée two contracts to supply catch basins, manholes, pipes and other precast reinforced concrete items.
The contracts cover the period from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2029, with annual price indexation.
Lot 1 (catch basins): $299,972.00 before taxes. Lot 2 (pipes and manholes): $909,057.99 before taxes.
The net expenditure is estimated at $1,269,330.36, once the QST refund is taken into account.
The prices received are lower than the City's estimates: -21.9% for lot 1 and -27.3% for lot 2.
Only one company submitted a bid; the other supplier that was approached explained to the City why it was not submitting an offer.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
The arrondissement des Rivières is changing the zoning of the building at 1395-1445, boulevard Central, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood.
The change now allows administrative offices (C1) and high-technology industry (I1) in zone 22508Cb.
The amendment also removes the requirement that the building cover at least 20% of the lot area.
The owner, a surveying and geomatics company, wants to expand into a neighbouring space leased until November 2028 and to buy an adjacent piece of land from Hydro-Québec.
The conseil de quartier de Duberger-Les Saules will give its opinion and hold a public consultation meeting.
Interested people will have seven days after the meeting to send in their written comments; the by-law may be subject to approval by referendum.
The Ville de Québec is paying $229,689 to Loisirs Lebourgneuf inc. for 2026, to support its recreation and community life activities in the Arrondissement des Rivières.
The grant is paid in two instalments: 50% within 30 days of signing, and 50% on June 30, 2026. The agreement covers January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The amount is based on the 2025 amount ($225,185) with an indexation, because the 11 federated centres asked for a transition year before the new calculation grid is applied.

The new grid, adopted on October 1, 2025, assesses the centres on 14 indicators grouped into 6 components; applying it for the first time created gaps that were considered risky for the financial health of some centres.
Discussions will continue until June 2026 with a view to multi-year agreements.
The program's total budget for 2026 is indexed by 2% and reaches nearly $3.7M.
To receive the money, the organization must, among other things, submit the "Collecte d'informations" form and meet the City's recognition requirements.

The City is amending its agreement with Industrielle Alliance, Assurance et services financiers inc. concerning land acquired alongside the route de l'Église, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, for the TramCité tramway project.
The original agreement provided that the City would repay part of the cost of building an underground parking facility, in several instalments.
The City has already paid 75% of the costs anticipated at the time the notarial deed was signed, on December 1, 2023.
The initial deadline for the repayments, set at December 31, 2025, was not met: the work was not finished and not all invoices had been compiled.
The remaining instalments are combined into a single final payment, to be made no later than December 31, 2026.
The document does not specify the amount of the repayment.
The arrondissement des Rivières is giving $200 to the Maison des jeunes de Duberger.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, from the "Soutenir les conseils d'arrondissements" activity.
The grant was proposed by the councillor for the Vanier-Duberger district, Clément Bourdeau.
The organization was asking for support for its project « Entendre et contrer les discours haineux et leurs répercussions 2026 ».
The project plans 8 filmed podcasts, one per week starting in the summer of 2026, recorded at the Maison des jeunes with teenagers present.
The themes covered: fatphobia, masculinism, radicalization, drugs and violence, homophobia and transphobia, racism, gun violence in Québec and cyberbullying.
A second part plans group discussions in two neighbourhood schools with selected students.
The City is refusing the request from the owner of 3530, rue Stanley-Cosgrove, in the Cap-Rouge neighbourhood, who wanted to enlarge one of his two parking areas.
The project would have had the parking area encroach 4 metres at the front, while the borough's planning by-law limits this encroachment to 3 metres.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave an unfavourable opinion on August 11, 2026, and the borough council followed this recommendation.
Reason given: the owner does not suffer serious harm, because he can keep his two compliant parking areas with enough space for three spots.
Another reason: accepting the exemption would open the door to repeated requests, which would increase paved surfaces and reduce green spaces in the area.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 2942-2948, chemin Sainte-Foy, in the Du Plateau neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough).
The building's rear setback may be 5.6 metres instead of the 15 metres required by the borough's planning by-law.
The exemption applies to the existing building, its planned expansion into the rear vestibule, and the addition of a porch in the rear yard.
According to the analysis, without the exemption, the building would have to be moved or demolished, and the expansion, the porch and the rear staircase would be impossible.
The analysis indicates that the situation has existed since 1935 and that no complaints have been recorded.
The planning advisory committee unanimously recommended the application on May 12, 2026.
The City is changing a job title in its list of professional positions: "archiviste, classe 1" becomes "conseillère ou conseiller en gestion des documents et des archives, classe 2".
The position therefore moves from class 1 to class 2 in the professional jobs grid.
The change results from a decision by the joint job evaluation committee (comité paritaire d'évaluation des emplois).
The City and the Alliance du personnel professionnel de la Ville de Québec signed a letter of agreement (no. 2026-001) in February and March 2026 to make the change official.
The Service des ressources humaines must update all the documents concerned, and the agreement is added to the collective agreement in force.
The file was submitted to the urban agglomeration council of Québec.

The arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles is entrusting the summer 2026 day camps (Programme Vacances-Été) to three organizations: Sports-Loisirs L'Ormière, Loisirs-Action Val-Bélair and Loisirs des Hauts-Sentiers L.D.H.S.
The City will pay grants estimated at $2,371,952.82 in total: $826,584.57 to Sports-Loisirs L'Ormière, $826,382.82 to Loisirs-Action Val-Bélair and $718,985.43 to Loisirs des Hauts-Sentiers L.D.H.S.
The three organizations must follow a set of specifications: registration, pricing, schedules, supervision of children, staff training and safety rules.
The money covers, among other things, the regular camp, support for children with special needs, transportation for swimming, family discounts and the online registration platform.
The City is committing to provide technical and material support and to give access, subject to availability, to play areas and municipal and school facilities.
In summer 2025, these camps welcomed 1,276 children (L'Ormière), 1,359 (Val-Bélair) and 1,120 (Hauts-Sentiers).
The borough council adopted the decision on April 20, 2026 (resolution CA6-2026-0036).
The City wants to acquire a lot of about 1,495.7 square metres along rue de la Faune, in the arrondissement of La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The purpose of the acquisition is to widen rue de la Faune as part of the project to rebuild that street.
The purchase will be made by mutual agreement with the owners or, if the discussions do not succeed, by expropriation.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the acquisition or expropriation proceedings.
The Service de l'ingénierie will prepare the necessary plans, technical descriptions and cadastral operations.
The property, in its largest area, is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $73,000, or $7.88 per square metre.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3449 on the work to redevelop rue de la Faune.
The City is creating a temporary position of associate director of administrative affairs at Destination Québec cité, attached to the Direction générale adjointe citoyen et vitalité urbaine.
The position is created to support the Destination Québec cité team during the changes currently underway.
Sonia Pomerleau, currently division director for talent attraction and management, is assigned to it for two years, starting February 23, 2026.
Her salary is set at $173,912 according to the salary scale for managers of the Direction générale and for service and borough directors.
Her other working conditions remain those of the Association du personnel de direction de la Ville de Québec.
The funds, including employee benefits, are already provided for in the City's budget.
The City is adopting the final versions of four plans to protect its drinking water sources, for the Québec, Beauport, Charlesbourg and Sainte-Foy treatment plants, covering six water intakes.
It is authorizing the filing of these plans with the Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs.

Some plans were prepared with Stoneham-et-Tewkesbury, Lac-Delage and Sainte-Brigitte-de-Laval, with support from the watershed organizations Organisme des bassins versants de la Capitale and Organisme des bassins versants Charlevoix-Montmorency.
The measures will be carried out over ten years, with a monitoring committee and annual reports on the indicators.

Compared with the preliminary 2025 versions, the final plans change some timelines for measures, replace one threat concerning the Lac-Delage wells, and adjust threats in the Sainte-Foy plan based on comments from the Port de Québec.
A public information session was held on March 26, 2025, followed by a two-week written consultation with citizens.
The City is giving a $500 grant to the Fondation partage chrétien St-Ambroise.
The proposal comes from Councillor Marie-Josée Asselin.
The money comes from the budget of the conseil d'arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The review confirms that the organization meets the criteria for this type of grant.
The borough council adopted the decision (resolution CA6-2026-0039).
The urban agglomeration council approves an RTC loan by-law of no more than $9,037,000 to buy 29 minibuses.
These vehicles will be used to integrate the "Flexibus" on-demand transit service into the RTC's operations.
The loan will be repaid over five years: $9,037,000 in principal and $1,112,800 in interest, for a total of $10,149,800.
The cost breaks down as follows: $6,967,000 for the vehicles ($240,250 each), $300,000 for equipment and fees, $1,090,000 for contingencies, $417,000 in net taxes and $263,000 in financing costs.
Any grant or contribution received will reduce the amount borrowed, and the RTC may pay part of it in cash out of its operating budget.
By-law no. 455 was adopted by the RTC's board of directors on September 9, 2026 and must also be approved by the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing.
The City is giving $2,974 to Patro Roc-Amadour for its Semaine de relâche 2026 activities, “À Québec, on bouge!”
The activities took place from February 28 to March 8, 2026, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, rain or shine.
On the program: La Grande Quête on March 3, the Festival des neiges on March 5, and volleyball and dance on March 6.
The activities were open to the whole public.
The City also provided technical support, depending on available resources.
The money comes from the operating budget of the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, through the financial support program for a local event.
The borough council adopted the decision on May 25, 2026.
The City's director general, Luc Monty, will be away from July 13 to 31, 2026.
Marie-France Loiseau, assistant director general, will serve as interim director general from July 13 to 19, 2026.
Carl Desharnais, assistant director general, will take over from July 20 to 31, 2026.
The designated person exercises all the powers and obligations of the director general during this period.
No financial impact is indicated in the document.
The City agrees to move its mortgage down in priority on the building at 401, rue Saint-Paul, in favour of any private lender approved by CMHC.
This mortgage secures a maximum grant of $626,000 given to LACODEV INC. in May 2025 for a mixed-use project at that address.
The grant comes from the « Fonds pour soutenir les projets durables en habitation » (component B, assistance for carrying out the project).
Until now, the list of creditors that could obtain a transfer of priority did not include lenders approved by CMHC.
The transfer is made under the same conditions as those already set out for the other eligible creditors.
City council must approve the decision.
The City is entrusting the organization Loisirs du Trait-Carré with the sanitary maintenance of certain recreational or sports facilities and sites in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The agreement covers the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, that is, 12 months.
The amount provided for is $168,806.78, plus GST and QST; the net cost to the City comes to $177,226.03.
The amount is split between $132,919.20 in 2026 and $44,306.83 in 2027 (net of taxes).
The 2027 portion depends on the approval of that year's budget.
The agreement replaces the previous one, which ends on March 31, 2026.
There was no call for tenders: the law allows the City to contract directly with a non-profit organization for this type of service.
The City is giving $80,000 to Théâtre Périscope to install a temporary outdoor public artwork.
The work by the duo Cooke-Sasseville will be installed on the theatre's grounds, at the corner of rue Crémazie and avenue De Salaberry.
It will be on view from June 1 to October 31, 2026.
The artwork shows a trio of cows propelled into the air by the jet of their milk, tied to the theatre's annual theme "libérer l'impossible".
The project was chosen following a call for projects issued to professional cultural organizations.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de la culture et du patrimoine.
The City is awarding the company Villéco inc. the door-to-door collection and transport of garbage and yard waste in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.

The contract is worth $6,273,400 (before GST and QST) and runs from the date it is awarded until September 29, 2030, with the possibility of three 12-month renewals and an annual price adjustment for inflation.
Collection by the new supplier starts on May 31, 2027, according to the collection schedule in the tender specifications.
The net cost to the City comes to $6,586,285.79, spread from 2027 to 2030 and conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
Four bids were received: the one from Villéco inc. was the only one that was compliant and ranked, with the highest final score; after negotiation, the company revised its price downward.

Two bids were set aside for administrative non-compliance: Centre Mécanique AGH inc. (no authorization to contract from the Autorité des marchés publics) and GFL Environmental inc. (prices not presented in the required form).
The price selected is 3.1% higher than the estimate from the requesting department, which was $6,087,007.55 before taxes.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 428-434, 46e Rue Ouest, in Charlesbourg (Saint-Rodrigue district).
The exemption allows part of the parking area to extend 0.4 metres in front of the building's façade, whereas the by-law requires 0 metres.
The owner is converting the building from one dwelling to four dwellings; for four dwellings or more, no encroachment is normally allowed in front of the façade.
The encroachment being kept (0.28 metres according to the plan) is used to keep one parking space that meets the minimum width of 2.6 metres.
The building would have three parking spaces in total, and the encroachment on the left side will be removed completely.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the application on August 12, 2026; the borough council made its decision on August 31, 2026.
The City is banning parking on the north side of rue des Pâquerettes, in Charlesbourg, over 48 metres starting from avenue des Œillets, heading east.
Four parking spaces are being removed.
The measure responds to requests from residents and to a lack of visibility caused by the slope of the street and an embankment, which creates a surprise effect for drivers heading west.
According to the document, the risk being targeted is that of head-on collisions and sideswipes with parked cars.
The cleared area will also make it easier for Réseau de transport de la Capitale buses to stop, as they have a stop at this location.
The document states that the impact on residents is limited, since they have off-street parking.
The City approves the list of companies authorized to bid on technical services for the maintenance and development of its computer systems.
Two new suppliers are being added to the list: Cofomo Québec and TechnoConseil TC.
Eight other companies remain qualified, including CGI, Idexia, Levio, Micrologic, Compugen, Alithya, G.D.G. Informatique and ITI Placement de ressources.
Six qualification applications were received; a company had to score at least 70% with a selection committee to be chosen.
The list stays valid for two years from the date it is published on the SEAO website.
A final call for qualification will be published next year so that other companies can join the list.
Each specific need of the Service des technologies de l'information will be the subject of a call for tenders by invitation among these suppliers, awarded to the lowest compliant bidder.
The City is settling out of court two expropriation cases before the Tribunal administratif du Québec involving Emco Corporation.
The land in question is located at 250 and 202, 4e Rue, expropriated for the TramCITÉ tramway project.
The final compensation is set at $5,279,000.00, including principal, interest, additional compensation and expert appraisal fees, plus applicable taxes.
The City had already paid $3,279,000.00 in provisional compensation in December 2022; $2,000,000.00 remains to be paid.
The money comes from the urban agglomeration's loan by-law for the structuring public transit network.
The City's attorneys, Giasson et associés, are authorized to sign the settlement documents.
The City has owned the two pieces of land since April 4, 2024.

The City is giving the Association Y.W.C.A. de Québec the job of programming and supervising open swim periods at the YWCA indoor pool, at 855, avenue Holland, in the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou.
The agreement covers June 11, 2026 to December 31, 2028, that is 31 months, and replaces the previous agreement, which ends on June 10, 2026.
The City will pay $101,623.53 (excluding GST and QST): $21,429.78 in 2026, $39,500.56 in 2027 and $40,693.19 in 2028.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 depend on the approval of those years' budgets.
The organization must provide qualified staff, report any service interruption or any incident, and comply with labour laws.
The chair and the assistant clerk of the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou are authorized to sign the agreement.
The City of Québec is giving $750,000 to Québecor, Sports et Divertissement inc. to host the Women's World Ice Hockey Championship in 2027.
The tournament will take place from November 3 to 14, 2027, at the Centre Vidéotron and the Pavillon Guy-Lafleur: 31 games, 8 to 10 teams and close to 250 players.
The games are ticketed, but a fan zone with free activities is planned at place Jean-Béliveau.
The grant covers 11% of the event's budget, estimated at $6,845,142, and the funding depends on sufficient contributions from the other partners.
The payment is spread out: $450,000 in 2026, $225,000 in 2027 and $75,000 in 2028, subject to the adoption of upcoming budgets.
The organizer must obtain the licence from the Fédération internationale de hockey sur glace six months before the event and provide a full report to the City within 90 days after the tournament.
The document mentions estimated economic benefits of about $10 million, based on previous editions.
The City is awarding Électricité MC2 inc. (Québec) the electrical work in its buildings, until April 30, 2029.

The contract covers two lots: the Ouest sector (La Haute-Saint-Charles, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, Les Rivières, L'Ancienne-Lorette, Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures) for $1,486,200, and the Centre and ExpoCité sector (La Cité-Limoilou, Charlesbourg, Beauport) for $3,431,500, before taxes.
The net expenditure is estimated at $5,162,970.29.
The contract can be renewed twice for 12 months, with indexation based on the Consumer Price Index.
Five companies submitted bids and all were compliant; Électricité MC2 submitted the lowest prices in both lots.
The prices selected are 24.6% (lot 1) and 25.6% (lot 2) lower than the estimate from the requesting department.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets.
The City is adding $51,738.54 (plus taxes) to the contract to rehabilitate a pressurized sewer pipe on rue de la Rive, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The contract with the company Les Excavations Lafontaine inc., of Lévis, therefore goes from $215,386.15 to $267,124.69 (plus taxes).
The work consists of lining about 300 metres of pipe between station U352, on rue de la Rive, and a manhole on boulevard de la Chaudière.

The additional costs are used in particular to dig two exploration shafts to locate the pipe, to redo a corroded section in the pumping station, to buy a 150 mm liner and to use one more vacuum truck for safety.
These changes add 12 days to the work site.
The net expense for the City is $54,319, funded by loan by-law R.V.Q. 3390.
The executive committee was to decide on February 11, 2026.
City council authorizes the creation of the Conseil de quartier du Vieux-Moulin, in the arrondissement de Beauport.
The name chosen is "Conseil de quartier du Vieux-Moulin", the only one suggested by citizens.
The process began with a request from citizens, followed by a public meeting held on June 8 at the Centre sportif Marc-Simoneau (3500, rue Cambronne).
About 51 people took part; in the secret ballot, 50 ballots were cast in favour of the creation and none against.
Citizens' questions dealt with the representation of the various sectors of the neighbourhood and with the protection of historic sites.
The neighbourhood boundaries will be those already set out in the by-law on the division of the territory into neighbourhoods.
An organizational meeting of the new neighbourhood council must be held within 60 days after the arrondissement de Beauport receives the resolution.
A business owner, Marie-Josée Texeira, wants to use two lots along boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, in the Aéroport neighbourhood (Cap-Rouge-Laurentien district), for purposes other than agriculture.
The project aims to enlarge the main building and to store materials and machinery outdoors, for a business that has gone from being a garden centre to providing landscaping services.
The area covered is 13,101.2 square metres (1.3101 hectare).
The City recommends supporting this application before the Commission de protection du territoire agricole du Québec (CPTAQ), which will make the final decision.
The analysis concludes that the lots, which are already commercial and are hemmed in by the railway, homes and the boulevard, have little potential for agricultural use.
According to the City, the project would have little or no impact on farming activities in the area, or on water and soils.
The arrondissement de Beauport is appointing Julie Faucher and Réjean Thériault to the comité consultatif d'urbanisme (planning advisory committee), as members who live in the area.
Their term runs from August 27, 2026 to August 27, 2028, which is two years.
They replace Léah Fay Hayes, whose term ended on April 30, 2026, and Claude Provencher, whose term ended on July 3, 2026.
Both positions were vacant, and the candidates were selected following a call for applications in 2026.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City is awarding Filtrum inc. (Québec) the work to install the new ultraviolet reactors at the station de traitement des eaux Est, at 105, chemin de la Baie-de-Beauport, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The contract is worth $5,570,200 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $5,848,013.72.
The work includes upgrading existing infrastructure, installing equipment that has already been purchased, repairing channels and structures, and adapting the fire safety systems.
Filtrum submitted the lowest compliant price among five bids, which ranged from $5,570,200 to $6,580,776 before taxes.
The selected price is 22.3% lower than the estimate from the requesting department, which was $7,171,250 before taxes.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1719 on the modernization of wastewater treatment plants.
The executive committee adopted the decision on April 8, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0444).
The City is buying Red Hat Enterprise Linux subscriptions to run its virtual data centres, from July 24, 2026 to July 23, 2027.
The contract goes to Softchoice LP, of Toronto, through the group purchasing program of the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales.
The contract amount is $201,426.75, plus applicable taxes.
The net cost to the City is $211,472.91, made up of $88,113.71 in 2026 and $123,359.20 in 2027.
The 2027 portion depends on the approval of that year's budget.
The subscriptions cover 45 socket pairs and allow unlimited deployment of virtualized servers, with the Satellite and Ansible management tools.
The director of the Service des approvisionnements is authorized to sign the contract documents.
The City is awarding Les Excavations Lafontaine inc. (Lévis) the contract for infrastructure work on montée Mendel, for $20,301,261.74 before taxes.
