The work includes an embankment ramp connecting boulevard de la Chaudière and boulevard du Versant-Nord, and an overpass above the CN railway line.
Part of boulevard du Versant-Nord will be raised and rebuilt, and a storm sewer system with basin management before discharge will be built.
The work is taking place in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough, as part of the TramCité project.
The net expense comes to $21,313,787.17, funded by two loan by-laws: $12,441,231.43 on the agglomeration side (tramway) and $8,872,555.74 on the City side.
Nine compliant bids were received; the lowest is 33.6% below the requesting department's estimate of $30,589,914.80.
The contract includes price adjustment clauses for asphalt and fuel.

The Ville de Québec is submitting its application to the Mérite municipal competition of the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation, in the "Municipalité et développement durable" category.
The application is about the Stratégie en faveur de la biodiversité 2025-2040, adopted in 2025 and developed since 2023.
This strategy aims in particular to place 40% of the territory under conservation by 2040, to add more vegetation throughout the city and to fight invasive species.
It provides for a call for projects aimed at the conseils de quartier to support citizen initiatives in favour of biodiversity.
It includes differentiated lawn management, which reduces how often lawns are mowed.
The document states that there is no financial impact.
The winners of the competition will be announced on April 23, 2026, in Québec.
The Ville de Québec will pay CN an estimated $453,062.81 (excluding GST and QST) to bring the boulevard Père-Lelièvre level crossing up to standard, in the Arrondissement des Rivières.
CN will rebuild the crossing structure: worn or damaged rails, ties, fasteners, track ballast and road surfacing.
This work is part of CN's 2026 Level Crossing Maintenance Program, under which CN considers a rehabilitation necessary for the safety of road users and trains.
Under an agreement reached in 2018, the City covers 38% of the maintenance costs for this level crossing.
The City will be billed based on actual costs, and CN will refund any unused amounts.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3389 on road and transportation work.
City council was to make a decision on August 25, 2026; CN's estimate is valid until December 31, 2026.
The City is paying up to $60,000 to artist Guillaume D. Cyr for a new mural on the CHSLD Notre-Dame-de-Lourdes, in Saint-Sauveur.
The project "105, rue Hermine, portraits de quartier" replaces the mural installed in 2022 on the south wall, which has to be taken down.
The new work will be made up of a multitude of portraits: an overall texture when seen from a distance, recognizable faces up close.
Residents of the CHSLD, their families, staff, volunteers, neighbourhood residents, a CPE and two schools will take part in creating it.
The money comes from the mural and video projection program, which is part of the Entente de développement culturel with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
A committee made up of three professional artists and representatives of the City and the Ministry recommended the project.
The City is giving $6,000 to Les Œuvres de la Maison Dauphine inc. to continue its street brigade project.
The brigade cleans the area around the organization's building and makes its users aware of positive ways to use the space; on average, three young people take part each week.
The project takes place in the Haute-Ville de Québec area, from July 2026 to June 2027.
It is aimed at young people who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless and who use the organization, located at 31, rue D'Auteuil.
The organization must mention the City's contribution in its publications and provide an accounting report (activity report, financial report, copies of the publications).
A $6,000 grant had already been awarded in 2025 for the pilot project.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 1095, avenue De Rochebelle, in the Saint-Louis neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge), on the site of école secondaire De Rochebelle.
The exemption allows a parking area to be redesigned with a two-way access lane 15 metres wide, instead of the maximum of 10 metres set out in the planning by-law.
It also allows the street access to be wider than the access lane it leads to.
The new vehicle entrance will be built a few metres south of the current entrance, with an entry lane running diagonally toward the south.

According to the document, the goal is to make it easier for school buses to turn, to keep them from encroaching on the exit lane, and to protect pedestrians walking on the sidewalk on the south side.
The access is used at peak hours by school buses, parents and vehicles heading to the Centre de formation professionnelle Marie-Rollet and the piscine Sylvie-Bernier.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on May 12, 2026.
The Ville de Québec agrees to receive $5,790 from the Société d'histoire de la Haute-Saint-Charles.
This amount comes from the Corporation du Parc de la Falaise et de la Chute Kabir Kouba, which was dissolved on May 27, 2025 for lack of resources to keep up its activities.
The money was first paid to the Société d'histoire on April 1, 2025, but that transfer did not comply with Canada Revenue Agency rules, because the organization did not have charitable status.
The Société d'histoire is therefore handing the amount over to the City, which is an eligible recipient, in order to correct the situation.
The City says it will reinvest the money in support of recognized organizations.
The transaction does not create any additional financial commitment for the City.
The City wants to obtain a permanent servitude (right of use) on a piece of land along 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The servitude covers about 23.30 square metres of part of lot 6 460 865 and will be used to move public utility conduits and networks.
The land will be acquired by agreement with the owner or, failing that, by expropriation; the owner has been informed of the steps and of a contact person at the City.
The Service des affaires juridiques is authorized to start the proceedings and to withdraw from them if the project no longer needs the servitude.
The entire property is listed on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $218,000, which is $435.30 per square metre.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the Réseau structurant de transport en commun.
The decision must be made by the urban agglomeration council of Québec.
The Ville de Québec is accepting sixteen works of art as gifts from four donors, to add to its collection.
Natacha Martin is donating four sculptures by her sister Paryse Martin, valued at $17,000.
Artist Paul Béliveau is donating two paintings ($32,200) and eight prints ($9,900), for a total of $42,100.
Alain Desrosiers is donating a framed painting by Francesco Iacurto, valued at $12,250.
Olivier Dubois is donating a framed painting by his father André Du Bois, valued at $650.
The treasurer will be able to give each donor a tax receipt for these amounts, if the tax authorities accept the values.
The City is paying the notary and publication fees for the four deeds of gift; the donors paid for the appraisals.
The City is adding a new job title to its list of professional positions: "Conseillère ou conseiller en gestion du cadre administratif et normatif", class 2.
This position is being created to meet a need of the Service des finances.
The Ville de Québec and the Alliance du personnel professionnel signed an agreement to this effect on June 22, 2026.
The change is being incorporated into the collective agreement now in force, and the Service des ressources humaines will update the documents concerned.
The decision summary does not indicate any financial impact.
The City is postponing to September the start-up meetings of the two new conseils de quartier in Beauport: Saint-Michel and Vieux-Moulin.
The Saint-Michel conseil de quartier meeting will be held on September 16, 2026, and the Vieux-Moulin one on September 22, 2026.
These dates go beyond the 60-day time limit normally set after the creation of a conseil de quartier; the executive committee is authorizing this delay.
The City explains this postponement by the summer period and the desire to encourage citizen participation.
The Service des relations citoyennes et des communications will call the residents of the two neighbourhoods to these meetings.
Residents will elect the members of the boards of directors there, which will officially launch the activities of the two councils.
The City wants to obtain a permanent public utility servitude over a small part of a piece of land bordering avenue De Salaberry, in La Cité-Limoilou.
This servitude affects about 1.3 square metres of lot 4 915 057.
The acquisition will be made by agreement with the owner or, failing that, by expropriation.
The servitude is used to move public utility conduits and networks needed for the TramCité project (structuring public transit network).
The entire piece of land is entered on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $310,000, which is $1,096.57 per square metre.
The City may abandon the proceedings if the project no longer needs this servitude.
The funds come from the agglomeration loan by-law on the structuring public transit network.
The City is revising the zoning of six zones in the southern part of the Parc technologique du Québec métropolitain, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood.
The new rules make industrial construction more flexible: minimum heights and minimum building widths are removed, and maximum heights are increased (except for 13 metres near residential areas).
The minimum percentage of green space on a lot goes from 10% to 15%, and cutting down trees in side and rear yards is more restricted.

New uses tied to high technology are allowed (laboratories, research centres, manufacturing of medical or electrical equipment); restaurants become possible in an industrial building, under certain conditions.
Elementary and high schools are no longer allowed, except for vocational training centres; the "park" use is removed from the zoning charts.
Outdoor storage remains prohibited in the Parc technologique, unlike in the city's other industrial parks.

The conseil de quartier de Duberger-Les Saules will hold a public consultation meeting; interested people will have seven days after it to send their comments in writing. The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The City wants to remove the possibility of operating a general tourist accommodation establishment (C10 uses) in 15 zones of Vieux-Québec and the areas nearby.
The stated goal: encourage the creation of housing and the arrival of new residents in Vieux-Québec, where there is already a lot of tourist accommodation.
As soon as the notice of intent is adopted, the City suspends the approval of construction plans and the issuing of permits or certificates that would not comply with this notice.
The urban planning and legal affairs departments must now prepare the draft by-laws that will follow up on the notice.
City council ratifies the notice for zones 11104Md, 11017Md and 13008Mb; the La Cité-Limoilou borough council will do the same for the zones under its authority.
The City plans to analyze the tourist accommodation dynamics of the neighbourhood before proposing the new zoning.
The Ville de Québec is giving a grant of up to $300,000 to the organization Touski, a non-profit organization created in 2011.
The money will be used to open a neighbourhood solidarity grocery store in the Saint-Sauveur neighbourhood, in a building that used to house a grocery store.
The project costs $1,967,750 in total; it is also funded by Investissement Québec ($500,000), the CIUSSS-CN ($47,616), Hydro-Québec ($45,000), donations and private loans.
The planned work includes bringing the building up to code, buying equipment and start-up inventory, and recruiting volunteers.
Touski plans to keep its 6 current jobs and create 6 new ones.
The organization aims to serve 1,800 households a year, with adjusted prices and social pricing for vulnerable people, with no registration criteria.
The money comes from the Fonds régions et ruralité, under the component Soutien aux projets structurants pour améliorer les milieux de vie.
The City is lowering the speed limit to 30 km/h on a section of rue Louis-IX, in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The current limit on this short section is 40 km/h.
The new limit applies Monday to Friday, from September to June.
It covers 150 metres in total, on each side (east and west) of the school crossing.
The street is part of the school corridor for école de l'Arc-en-Ciel; a path behind the school leads to this crossing, which is watched by a crossing guard.
The City bought the Saint-Louis-de-Gonzague building, at 980, rue Richelieu, in Vieux-Québec, in order to resell it for a residential project.
In the meantime, it wants to temporarily set up there the offices of the recreation teams and of the teams organizing the Jeux du Canada.
The planning by-law does not allow offices in this zone: the City is amending it to authorize this temporary use.
Other uses would be allowed on the vacant floors: gathering places, cultural facilities, art galleries, exhibition halls, artists' studios, commercial parking and a fitness centre of 200 m² or less.
The authorization is valid for two years from the coming into force of the by-law, for occupancy until spring 2028.

The conseil de quartier du Vieux-Québec–Cap-Blanc–Colline parlementaire will give its opinion and hold a public consultation meeting; people will have seven days afterwards to submit their written comments.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.

The City is sending the director of the Service du traitement des eaux, Valérie Tremblay (or her replacement), to the annual conference of the Canadian Association of Municipal Administrators in Whistler, British Columbia, from May 26 to 28, 2026.

The Centre de biométhanisation de la matière organique de l'agglomération de Québec (CBAQ) project is nominated for the environmental leadership and sustainability award, in the category of municipalities with more than 100,000 residents.
The winners will be announced during the conference, in May 2026.
The City will reimburse up to $3,210 in travel, lodging and meal expenses, upon presentation of receipts.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service du traitement des eaux.
A difference of no more than 10% from the authorized amount is accepted without further authorization; the dates may change.
The arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles is giving a $500 grant to the organization Maison l'Accalmie.
The request comes from councillor Marc Roussin, who is proposing to support the organization.
Maison l'Accalmie is a therapy house located on rue du Beau Site and supports people dealing with addiction problems.
The organization says it wants to use the help for work, buying equipment, improving its facilities and developing a program.
The money comes from the borough council's budget (City funds).
The borough council adopted resolution CA6-2026-0067 on June 15, 2026.
The City is accepting a second donation of archives from Gino Gariépy, free of charge.
The donation includes 2,408 documents: 1,376 photographs (postcards, stereograms, paper prints, slides, glass plates, negatives), 17 tourist brochures, 3 offprints and 9 reels of family film.
Also included are archives from the Sommet des Amériques held in Québec in April 2001: 384 negatives with their paper prints and 235 colour slides.
The documents date mostly from 1860 to 1970 and mainly show the city of Québec and surrounding regions.
These archives are added to the Collection Gino Gariépy, already given to the City in 2021 (more than 2,000 items).
The City agrees to give the donor a tax receipt and to make the documents available to anyone who asks for them, for private study or research.
The City may sort and weed out the documents and keep only those with historical or research value.
The Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough council is giving out $34,203 in 13 grants to 12 organizations in the area.
These grants answer the applications submitted by March 15, 2026 under the programs of the Cadre de soutien aux organismes reconnus.
The largest amounts go to La Courtepointe ($7,365 for an organizational analysis) and to T.R.A.I.C. Jeunesse ($5,809 for strategic planning).
Entraide Sainte-Foy receives $4,250 (website and promotional items) and La Société scoute de Sainte-Ursule receives $4,216 (new brand image).
The Club de plongeon ARO de Québec gets two grants: $3,439 for training equipment and $3,720 for promotional items.
Three organizations (Ensemble Polyphonia, Maison l'Éclaircie, SACQ) each receive $500 for community-building activities and volunteer recognition.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget, under the "Soutien aux organismes" (support for organizations) item.
The City is awarding the plumbing and heating work in its buildings to the company Boucher Lortie inc., from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2028.
The work covers the maintenance, repair, modification, installation and replacement of equipment.
Lot 1 – Centre sector (La Cité-Limoilou, Beauport, Charlesbourg and the ExpoCité site): estimated amount of $1,848,325 before taxes.
Lot 2 – Ouest sector (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, Les Rivières, La Haute-Saint-Charles): estimated amount of $1,256,375 before taxes.
The net expense for the City is estimated at $3,259,546.91, subject to the approval of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.
The contract can be renewed three times for 12 months, with an annual indexation based on the Consumer Price Index.
Two companies submitted bids; Boucher Lortie inc. offered the lowest price for both lots.
The City is awarding Edgar Blondeau inc., of Québec, the repair of lines and suspensions on heavy vehicles and trailers of 5,000 kg and over (lot 1).
The contract runs for 12 months from the date it is awarded.
The estimated amount is $554,827.56 before taxes; the estimated net expenditure is $582,499.58.
Two companies bid on this lot; the second one, Suspensions et ressorts Michel Jeffrey inc., asked for $555,977.70.
Lots 2 (light vehicles under 5,000 kg) and 3 (trailers under 5,000 kg) were awarded elsewhere, through a delegation of powers.
The funds depend on the 2027 budget being approved by the appropriate authorities.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 1407, rue Hamon, in the Val-Bélair neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The exemption allows the owner to build a garage attached to their house.
The width of the main building will be 3.64 metres, while the planning by-law requires a minimum of 7.3 metres.
According to the analysis, the real front of the house, with the main door, is perpendicular to the street, which makes the garage non-compliant even though the actual width is 9.93 metres.
The analysis concludes that the garage cannot be placed anywhere else on the property and that the neighbourhood is not affected, since the lot is wooded and landlocked.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on August 12, 2026.
The City is entrusting the organization Loisirs du Trait-Carré with the management and use of municipal recreation buildings and equipment in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The agreement covers the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029 and replaces the previous one, which ended on March 31, 2026.
The contract amounts to $212,900.43 (plus GST and QST); the net cost to the City is $223,518.84.
The amounts break down as follows: $52,154.40 in 2026, $74,506.28 in 2027, $74,506.28 in 2028 and $22,351.88 in 2029 (net of taxes).
The amounts will be indexed to the Consumer Price Index starting in the second year.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 depend on the approval of the budgets for those years.
The organization is located at 8815, avenue Jean-Paquin, in Québec.
The City is awarding Groupe Solexco inc. the contract to redevelop the tennis courts at parc Victoria, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough, for $3,311,431.19 (plus GST and QST).
The work includes demolishing the current facilities and building new asphalt surfaces with acrylic paint.
The centre court will be converted into three pickleball courts.
The project also includes reworking the drainage, painting the exterior siding of the pavilion, and rebuilding a larger storage space for the Club social Victoria and the tennis club.
Furniture, a relaxation area and universal accessibility measures will be added.
Seven companies submitted bids; Solexco submitted the lowest price, 11.8% below the requesting department's estimate of $3,754,990.
The net cost to the City is $3,476,588.82, funded by loan by-law R.V.Q. 3402.
The City is giving $123,267 to Patro Roc-Amadour (1978) inc., a one-time, non-renewable form of assistance following the fire of September 23, 2025.
The money covers expenses not reimbursed by Patro's insurance: lost operating revenue, additional promotion costs, and construction and code-compliance work.

The amount comes from two sources: $83,267 from the Service des loisirs operating budget (after a transfer from the local contingency account) and $40,000 from a loan by-law for work on buildings and recreational facilities.

Patro Roc-Amadour is a community recreation centre that has been open since 1948: a day centre for seniors living with an intellectual disability, a day centre for autistic adults, food distribution, a thrift shop, and youth programming.
The organization has 65 regular employees, more than 200 seasonal employees and 450 volunteers who contributed 35,601 hours in the past year.
The executive committee and city council adopted the decision in early July 2026.
The Ville de Québec will pay $175,000 per year to Moisson Québec, from 2026 to 2029, for a total of $700,000.
The money funds the Programme de récupération en supermarchés, which collects unsold food from retailers.
The grant covers about one third of the program's operating costs.
Each year's payment depends on the program continuing, on the number of participating retailers being maintained or increased, and on the filing of an annual report.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 remain conditional on the budgets being approved by the authorities.
According to the document, the program serves 82 establishments in the region and diverted close to 1,360 tonnes of food from disposal in 2025.
The agreement takes effect on February 16, 2026 and ends on February 2, 2030.
The City is paying $6,560 to two organizations for Semaine de relâche 2026 (spring break) activities, from February 28 to March 8, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
Loisirs Vanier receives $5,000 and Loisirs Duberger-Les Saules inc. receives $1,560.
Loisirs Vanier held activities at parc Jean-Paul-Nolin from March 2 to 6: snowy mini-putt, entertainment at the cabin, a snow castle contest, bubble soccer and challenges.
Loisirs Duberger-Les Saules offered a roller disco skate at parc Saint-François-Xavier on February 28 and the activity "L'hiver, c'est fait pour jouer!" at the Maison O'Neill on March 4.
The activities were free and open to everyone, rain or shine.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement des Rivières.
In 2025, the same organizations had received $3,600 in total for spring break.
The City is buying a boiler pump and its accessories for the Complexe de valorisation énergétique, located in the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou.
This pump replaces equipment that is out of service and cannot be repaired.
The contract goes to 1221807 Ontario inc. (Saint-Laurent) for $590,000 before taxes; the net expense is $606,831.81.
Four companies submitted bids, but only one was compliant; after negotiation, it lowered its price to $590,000.
The selected price is 19% lower than the requesting department's estimate of $728,000.
The funds come from an agglomeration loan by-law tied to work on the incinerator and the sludge treatment plant.
The executive committee adopted resolution CE-2026-1059 on August 19, 2026.
The City is providing up to $215,114 in grants to cultural organizations in Québec, under the Entente de développement culturel with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.

The money funds 26 projects in three streams: Organiser (buying specialized equipment and sharing resources), Rayonner (scouting missions, showcases and exchanges abroad) and Rejoindre (growing and retaining audiences).
The largest grants, $15,000 each, go to Centre de création Limoilou (Manivelle), Productions Recto-Verso, VU (centre de photographie), Théâtre Sortie de Secours and Création Le Pantoum.

Other recipients include: Machine de Cirque, Musée ambulant, Radio Basse-Ville (CKIA FM), Théâtre Périscope, Théâtre Le Diamant, Coop Spira, Les Gros Becs and the Pôle culturel du Monastère des Ursulines.
The smallest grant is $950, given to the Literary and Historical Society of Quebec for a conference.
The funding comes from two sources: $155,114 from a loan by-law and $60,000 from culture and heritage transfers.
A committee of professionals from the Service de la culture et du patrimoine checked that each application met the requirements.
The City is awarding Automatisation D2E inc. (Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures) the contract to replace the automation system at the Limoilou pumping station, for $242,000 before taxes.
The station is located in the La Cité-Limoilou borough.
The work includes installing two control panels and a console-type junction box in the control room, along with changes to the floor.
The contract also includes temporary UPS power cabling, communication cabling, dismantling one panel, and transferring cables under the floor.
Four bids were received, all compliant; D2E offered the lowest price, 33.3% below the department's estimate of $363,000.
The net cost to the City is $254,069.75, funded through an agglomeration loan by-law.
The executive committee adopted the decision on August 19, 2026.
The City is awarding Construction Pierre Blouin inc. the major repair and redevelopment of the centre communautaire Ferland, in La Cité-Limoilou, for $20,633,643 (before GST and QST).
The work involves the pool basin, the change rooms and the gymnasium, which will be completely renovated.
The roof will be redone and the electromechanical equipment on it will be replaced.
The upper floor will be entirely redeveloped, in addition to various related work.
Six companies submitted bids; Construction Pierre Blouin inc. submitted the lowest price, which is 0.9% above the department's estimate.
The net expense for the City comes to $21,662,745.94, funded by several loan by-laws.
The executive committee was to decide on March 25, 2026; resolution CE-2026-0406 is dated March 27, 2026.
The arrondissement de Charlesbourg is paying $35,705 to two organizations for summer activities for youth aged 13 to 15.
Le Patro de Charlesbourg inc. receives $30,000 and les Loisirs du Trait-Carré, $5,705.
Both projects focus on training future day camp leaders and are to welcome 80 teenagers in total, including 13 integration spots.
The grants are paid in two instalments: 90% up front ($32,134.50) and 10% afterwards ($3,570.50).
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The City's review committee selected 15 projects in total, including these two for Charlesbourg.
In 2025, the same program had paid $35,850 to two organizations in the arrondissement.
The City is awarding Les Entreprises P.N.P. inc. (Québec) the landscaping redevelopment of the Villa Bagatelle, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough, for $415,676 before taxes.
The work includes demolishing existing features, a parking area made of stone screenings with granite curbs, a terrace and sidewalks made of limestone, and the redevelopment of pathways.

A stormwater system will be installed (catch basins, drainage trenches, connection to the existing network) and the current water basin will be demolished and replaced by an ornamental basin supplied with water and electricity.
The wooden fence, screen, wooden stairs and street furniture will be replaced; the site will be levelled and sodded.
The net expense for the City comes to $436,407.84, funded by loan by-law R.V.Q. 3367 tied to the 2024-2026 cultural development agreement.
Three compliant bids were received, ranging from $415,676 to $522,702; the City's estimate was $593,050.44.
The executive committee adopted the decision on April 29, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0545).
The City is banning parking at all times on the west side of rue Mercier, in Beauport, over 85 metres starting from avenue Royale and going north.
On the next 60 metres, the ban stays seasonal, from November 15 to March 31.
Before this, the seasonal ban applied over 145 metres.
The change removes about 14 parking spaces during the summer.
The document states that the roadway narrows to 5.5 metres near avenue Royale and that parked vehicles prevent two-way traffic.
The document mentions that residents in the area have access to private parking spaces.
The change follows a request from a citizen.

The City is authorizing the construction of a five-storey building at 780, avenue du Brabant (quartier du Plateau, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge), with about 40 housing units and offices on the ground floor.

The current zoning prohibits housing and limits buildings to four storeys: the City is setting aside these rules, as well as the minimum setbacks and the number of required parking spaces (1 space per housing unit instead of 1.2).
The project includes underground parking with 39 spaces and a maximum of 17 outdoor spaces, at least 25 bicycle spaces and at least 2 charging stations.

Conditions imposed: at least 34 housing units, including 8 with two or more bedrooms, a workout room of at least 20 m², a rooftop terrace of 130 to 160 m², air conditioning in each unit, and ENERGY STAR windows.
Greening required: at least 19% of the lot as green space, at least 10 trees planted, and a 1.5 m evergreen hedge along the entire southwest boundary.
The City is relying on the 2024 Quebec housing legislation, as the vacancy rate for rental housing is 2.2%.

The project is not subject to a referendum; a public consultation meeting will be held, followed by three days to submit written comments. A fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases) applies if the conditions are not met.
The City is giving a grant of no more than $1,500 to Université Laval for a community forum on aging.
The forum "Vieillir en diversité et en équité" will take place on May 11, 2026 and will bring together seniors and organizations from the area.
The event is organized by the Institut sur le vieillissement et la participation sociale des aînés (IVPSA), which will share the results of its research on seniors from diverse backgrounds.
In return, the City gets visibility in the event's communication materials.
The money comes from the budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The City is closing 29 agglomeration loan by-laws adopted before 2022, for which the work is now finished.
The authorized spending totalled $266,985,500.00, while the work cost $257,685,069.25: the City is cancelling $9,300,430.75 in spending power.
It is also cancelling $136,136,071.00 in remaining borrowing power balances, since only $130,849,429.00 was actually borrowed.

Total financing comes to $263,507,635.87, including $132,658,206.87 from other sources: $43,119,152.87 in grants and third-party contributions, and $89,539,054.00 taken directly from the 2008 to 2025 operating budgets.
There is $5,822,566.62 still available, which the City is not assigning to anything for now.

Among the by-laws being closed: the centre de glaces de Québec ($65,369,420.25 in actual costs), the Pavillon du commerce at ExpoCité, the welcome pavilion at the base de plein air de Sainte-Foy, and the redevelopment of part of the route de l'Église.
The City is asking the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation to update its records; the urban agglomeration council is to decide on July 8, 2026.
The City is allowing the company 9222-9293 Québec inc. to permanently occupy part of the public underground area, beneath rue de l'Amérique-Française and Grande Allée Est, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The occupation is for underground support structures covering about 53.1 square metres.
These structures are for a 20-storey mixed-use building project at 530, Grande Allée Est, with about 200 housing units, a daycare and one commercial space.
The company is paying a one-time rent of $50,000, plus taxes, paid into the City's general fund when the agreement is signed.
The company is covering the surveying costs as well as the drafting and publication of the notarized deed.
The company must remove or level the structures no later than the end of the work and pay the City for the paving and sidewalk repairs, at actual cost plus 15% in administrative fees.
The company may end the permission if it does not obtain the authorizations from the City or from the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
The City wants to allow up to eight dwellings per detached building in zone 32228Mc, instead of the four currently allowed.
The area concerned is in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood: north of rue Hélène-Boullé and rue Louis-Jolliet, south of rue Richer, between rue Paradis and avenue Painchaud.

The owner of 2059, chemin Sainte-Foy wants to convert the garage and the basement storage space into three dwellings and divide one ground-floor dwelling into two, for a total of seven dwellings, without changing the outside of the building.
Three other buildings in the zone that already have more than four dwellings could be brought into compliance.
No rules on height or siting are changing: the new dwellings must respect the building size already allowed.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to a referendum; the conseil de quartier de la Cité-Universitaire will hold the public consultation meeting and give its opinion.
After the public meeting, interested people will have seven days to send their comments in writing.
The City is changing the planning rules for a zone in the quartier du Plateau, located between avenue Wilfrid-Pelletier, rue Jacques-Amyot, autoroute Henri-IV and chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois.
Buildings will now be allowed up to four storeys, instead of three.
The requirement of a minimum of 8 dwelling units per building for the "H1 Logement" use is removed.
The depth of the front yard setback will be measured from the centre line of chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois and set at 22.5 metres.
The conseil de quartier du Plateau will be consulted and will hold a public meeting; interested people will have seven days after that meeting to submit their comments in writing.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to a referendum approval process.

The Ville de Québec is entrusting the Centre communautaire Jean-Guy Drolet (16, rue Royal-Roussillon) with the use of a municipal recreation facility and the provision of services in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The agreement covers the period from June 1, 2026 to September 2, 2028, with two renewal options of one month each (September 3 to 30, 2028 and October 1 to 28, 2028).
The City will pay $679,950 (exempt from GST and QST), broken down as $195,080 in 2026, $368,770 in 2027 and $116,100 in 2028.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 depend on the approval of those years' budgets.
The organization will pay the City a royalty of 10% on its revenues from activity registrations and space rentals, up to a maximum of $35,368 (plus taxes).
The organization will be compensated for revenues lost when recognized organizations use the spaces free of charge.
The previous agreement ended on May 30, 2026; the funds come from the operating budget of the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 2310, rue Chateaubriand, in the quartier de l'Aéroport (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The house sits 5.1 metres from the street, while the planning by-law requires 6.0 metres. The exemption makes this situation compliant.
The building has been located this way since it was built in 1974.
Thanks to this regularization, the owner will be able to add a staircase in the front yard to serve a dwelling planned for the basement.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the application on January 13, 2026; the borough council granted it (resolution CA3-2026-0018).
According to the City's analysis, the exemption has no significant impact on neighbouring properties.
The City is giving $10,500 to the Association régionale de soccer de Québec.
The grant pays for 800 tickets for young soccer players from the region.
They will attend a Première Ligue canadienne game on June 6, 2026, at the Stade Telus at Université Laval.
The game will pit FC Supra, a new Québec club, against Pacific FC of Langford, British Columbia.
Last year, the City gave $15,000 to the same association for a game held on May 31, 2025.
The money comes from the City's "Frais généraux" (general expenses) budget item.
The City is awarding Toitures R. Martin (Québec) the work to redo and repair the roof of the garage de la Canardière, at 1252, chemin de la Canardière, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The contract, based on an hourly rate, is estimated at $3,144,000 before GST and QST; the net expense is estimated at $3,300,807.
It applies from the date the contract is awarded until December 31, 2027, with the possibility of a 12-month renewal indexed to the Consumer Price Index.
The company provides the labour, materials and equipment and manages the work: replacing roof coverings, metal roofing, flashing and mouldings on multi-layer flat roofs.
Four companies submitted bids; Toitures R. Martin got 91.75 points out of 100, the highest score. One bid was found to be non-compliant.
The funds will come from the financing of the Programme de développement des immeubles of the Service de la gestion des immeubles, as needed.
The executive committee adopted the decision on June 25, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0870).
The City is changing the ÉquiMobilité program, which gives a reduced public transit fare to low-income people, starting July 1, 2026.
For fares used in paratransit (STAC), the City will reimburse the RTC 45% of the difference with the regular fare and 55% of the difference with the reduced fare, for both monthly passes and tickets.
For RTC fares, the compensation stays at 70% / 30% for monthly passes and goes to 61% / 39% for tickets.
ÉquiMobilité fares will now be set and indexed each year by the RTC's board of directors.

Eligibility for the program is confirmed for a period of 2 years; the application is submitted on paper or by mail at the service centres of La Cité-Limoilou, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge or Charlesbourg.
A person without photo identification can provide a declaration signed by a sponsor who has known them for at least two years.
The City is amending its agreement with Immeubles Marc Simard inc. concerning a maximum subsidy of $623,000 for a housing project at 2510 and 2518 to 2520, chemin Sainte-Foy.
The subsidy comes from the Fonds pour soutenir les projets durables en habitation and is used to cover the extra costs linked to innovative and sustainable components.

The developer created a horizontal co-ownership on the building; the City accepts the cadastral operation, which replaces lots 1 533 948 and 6 267 144 (3,921.4 m²) with lot 6 701 288 (2,730.2 m²) and a common area.
The deadline to pay out the entire subsidy is moved from March 31, 2026 to September 30, 2026.
The developer must meet the conditions for the first payment (50%) by June 19, 2026 at the latest and submit its complete application for the second payment by July 31, 2026 at the latest.
The document states that the cadastral operation changes nothing about the developer's obligations regarding the project's innovative components.
The City is transferring $680 from a reserve dedicated to protecting and increasing the tree canopy to its general reserve (local unassigned surplus).
This amount is what remains of a $3,500,000 reserve created in 2022 for tree-related developments.
The City states that the objectives tied to this reserve have been met, making the assignment of the balance unnecessary.
A separate transfer of $159,320 will be proposed to the urban agglomeration council for the balance of the agglomeration reserve created for the same purpose ($1,500,000 at the outset).
City council adopted the decision on June 16, 2026.
The City is setting aside $5,000,000 from its agglomeration surplus as of December 31, 2025 for work at the complexe de valorisation énergétique.
This amount will be used to fund item 46006 of the 2026-2035 investment plan, which relates to this work.
The City is choosing to fund this through surplus rather than taking on debt.
The work aims to modify the equipment, the building and the processes in order to maintain treatment capacity and meet environmental requirements.
The complex treats 260,000 tonnes of residual materials per year; about two thirds of the steam produced is sold externally.
A first transfer of $10,000,000 had already been made from the surplus as of December 31, 2024.
The urban agglomeration council was to make its decision on June 17, 2026.
The City is paying $5,000 to the Festival international Juste pour rire Québec.
The money is used to buy 10 tickets to the 2nd edition of the Juste pour aider event.
The comedy evening takes place on April 22, 2026, at the salle Le Diamant.
The funds raised at the event will go to two organizations: the Fonds Antoine and Laura Lémerveil.
These organizations support young people and people living with multiple disabilities, as well as their loved ones.
The amount comes from the City's "Frais généraux" (general expenses) budget.
The City is allowing an exception to the planning rules for a lot at 2108, avenue Chapdelaine, in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough).
The future building will be allowed to be built 4.5 metres from the street instead of the 6.0 metres normally required.
The project is a planned residential building with 20 housing units.

Part of the lot is within the 20-metre protection strip along the top of a steep slope, which reduces the buildable space; moving the building forward by about 1.5 metres makes it possible to build outside that zone.
The 5.0-metre side setback will be respected, no trees will be cut down, and the existing plant screen on the side of the neighbouring lot will be kept.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on April 14, 2026; the borough council granted the exemption.
The City is tabling the lists of contracts and expenses authorized by employees for the month of July 2026.
In July 2026, 126 contracts of more than $25,000 were awarded, for a total of $41,208,558.81.
An amount of $26,237,056.20 was authorized by employees who hold delegated spending authority.
The lists also include cancelled contracts, calls for tenders cancelled after the opening of bids, and additional expenses through change notices.
The amounts shown exclude taxes; the list of contracts of $25,000 and more is published on the City's website.
The City is approving a minor exemption for 6672, rue de Triton, in the Saint-Émile neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The owner will be allowed to build an enclosed sunroom on the existing patio, in the backyard.
The rear setback will be 6.1 metres instead of the 9.0 metres required by the borough's planning by-law.
According to the analysis, the sunroom encroaches 2.48 metres into the rear setback, while the standard allows 1.5 metres.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended granting the exemption on August 12, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption for a lot to be built on in the Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux neighbourhood, in Beauport.
Proposed lot 6 710 954 will be allowed a width of 6.3 metres instead of the 16 metres normally required by the borough's planning by-law.
The exemption makes it possible to subdivide a lot located in the middle of a residential block in order to build a dwelling there.
Without this exemption, the lots in question cannot be built on, because they are not next to a street served by the water main and the sanitary sewer.
The developer plans a single access driveway shared with the neighbouring proposed lot 6 710 955.
Another exemption, concerning the building's rear setback, could be requested later.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the application on March 26, 2026.
The City is increasing the reimbursement paid to council members who use their personal vehicle for travel outside the city limits.
The rate goes from $0.61 to $0.62 per kilometre travelled.
The new rate applies as of May 1, 2026.
This rate is aligned with the one that applies to City staff.
The executive committee adopted the by-law on April 15, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0482).
The document indicates no financial impact.
The City is entrusting Patro Le Pivot with the cleaning and sanitary upkeep of municipal recreational and sports facilities and equipment in the arrondissement de Beauport.
The agreement runs from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027, a period of 12 months, and replaces the one ending August 31, 2026.
The City will pay $245,401.71 to the organization, an amount exempt from GST and QST.
The payment is split into $81,800.52 in 2026 and $163,601.19 in 2027.
The 2027 portion depends on the approval of the 2027 budget by the competent authorities.
The contract is awarded by mutual agreement, which the regulations allow for a non-profit organization.
City council adopted the resolution on August 25, 2026, and the director of the Service des approvisionnements is signing the agreement.
The City is entrusting the organization Exmuro arts publics with creating and presenting two outdoor art trails, for $190,498.87 (plus GST and QST).
Works by the duo Cooke-Sasseville will be installed at the base de plein air de Sainte-Foy, and those by Giorgia Volpe at parc des Saules.
The trails will be open from June 20 to October 12, 2026.
Exmuro is responsible for setting up, taking down, transporting, securing and maintaining the works, and must return the sites to their original condition.
The City is paying in three instalments: 60% on signing, 35% on receipt of the final concept, and 5% after the final report.
The City will also provide services to Exmuro up to a maximum of $5,000.
The net cost to the City is $200,000, funded by a loan by-law tied to the Politique culturelle 2025-2030.
The City approves $16,658,136 in budget transfers made between September 1 and December 31, 2025, for operating expenses under the urban agglomeration council's responsibility.
It takes note of an amount of $3,919,786 transferred for the benefit of local (proximity) jurisdiction for the 2025 fiscal year.
The transfers affect 439 budget lines spread across the various city departments, including $7,219,499 in multi-department transfers.
The departments most affected include Travaux publics ($4,563,053 received), Police ($2,094,886 received) and Entretien des voies de circulation ($2,123,919 paid out).
Examples given include added surveillance hours for the sanitary facility in front of the bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy and the payment of an accommodation invoice from the Croix-Rouge.
The file is to be presented to the urban agglomeration council on March 11, 2026.

The City is amending its by-law on municipal works agreements, which requires a developer to reach an agreement with the City before obtaining a construction or subdivision permit when the project requires infrastructure work.
The developer now pays the full cost of supervising the work, quality control of materials and contaminated soils, stormwater management, traffic control and street cleaning.
The bank guarantee required for the final plans (TQC) goes from $10,000 to $25,000.
The by-law sets maximum pipe diameters paid for by the developer: 300 mm for water mains, 375 mm for domestic sewers, and 750 mm or 1,200 mm for storm sewers depending on the type of system.
The City no longer pays the cost of a median that it requires; cost-sharing rules are added for parks, public squares and engineering structures.
The developer must now provide more documents: a geotechnical and hydrogeological study, the names of the professionals and subcontractors, and plans and specifications at 40% and then at 100%.
New areas are now subject to the by-law, notably in La Cité-Limoilou, Les Rivières and Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.

The City is changing the planning rules for the parc industriel Armand-Viau, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood (arrondissement des Rivières), between autoroute Henri-IV, boulevard de l'Auvergne, boulevard de l'Ormière and autoroute Félix-Leclerc.

Vehicle parking and outdoor storage will now be allowed in the electricity transmission corridor that crosses the industrial park, or on a vacant lot next to that corridor (zones 22013Ip, 22014Ip, 22019Ip, 22020Ip, 22026Ip and 22040Mb).

Outdoor storage of types A to E (merchandise, construction materials, containers, scaffolding, tool vehicles, bulk goods) is being added in zones 22002Cc, 22006Ma, 22026Ip, 22040Mb, 22041Mb and 22042Mb.
Outdoor storage of a good or material (type G) is allowed in all the zones covered.

In zone 22006Ma, general industry (I3) is being added to the permitted uses and the park use (R1) is being removed; the requirements of a minimum height of 8 metres and 2 storeys for a building are being removed.
Outdoor storage areas must be surrounded by an opaque fence, and storage remains prohibited in the front yard.

The conseil de quartier de Duberger-Les Saules will be consulted and will hold the public meeting; interested people will have seven days after the meeting to send their comments in writing. Adoption is planned at the borough council on March 24, 2026.
The arrondissement des Rivières is granting a minor exemption for 840, rue Bouvier, in the Neufchâtel Est–Lebourgneuf neighbourhood.
The exemption allows the construction of a 92-room hotel and a multi-level parking structure shared between the hotel and the restaurants of the Halte Bouffe.
The property will have 179 parking spaces, which complies with the regulations.
The accepted deviations concern the side setback (6 m instead of 7.5 m), the combined width of the side yards (12 m instead of 15 m) and the lot width for the courtesy lane (38 m instead of 40 m).
The green area along the front lot line may be 2.5 m deep instead of 4 m, and the courtesy lane 6.5 m wide instead of 6 m.
The new building will be connected to the existing building by a walkway; on-street parking remains prohibited on rue Bouvier and rue des Rocailles.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on the application on February 2, 2026.
The executive committee takes note of the weekly list of additional expenses authorized by employees who hold delegated authority, for the week of April 19 to 25, 2026.
Only one change notice appears in the report: $235,994 (before taxes) for the Service de la gestion des équipements motorisés.
This amount is used to buy a third dump body with a spreader for snow removal operations, which will be installed on a truck the City already owns.
The City is thereby exercising purchase options already provided for in the contract for the purchase and installation of snow removal equipment (lot 4), for which prices are firm for 2025 and 2026.
The value of the contract goes from $881,964 to $645,970 after this change notice, according to the report; its initial value was $235,994.
The City is awarding Créations Borderline inc. (artist Philippe Allard) the creation and installation of the public artwork "Embâcles", for $426,179.60 plus GST and QST.
The artwork will be installed at the place des Canotiers, at 40, rue Dalhousie, in the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou.
It is a sculptural installation of 10 elements in white granite, with a total height of 5 metres, on the theme of northernness and the ice jams of the fleuve Saint-Laurent.
The installation must be completed no later than February 5, 2027.
The company will have to provide an anti-graffiti coating and give the City a maintenance specification for the artwork upon delivery.

The artwork was chosen from among three finalist proposals by a jury of seven people, including an elected official, a representative of the Commission de la capitale nationale du Québec and a representative of the conseil de quartier du Vieux-Québec–Cap-Blanc–colline Parlementaire.
The contract was awarded without a call for tenders, as the law allows this for contracts in the artistic or cultural field. The net expense for the City is $447,435.31.

The executive committee notes the filing of the performance report as at December 31, 2025, and the annual report of the committee that oversees the financial reserve related to the pension plan deficit of the former Ville de Québec.
The investments in this reserve were worth $364.8M as at December 31, 2025.
The return was 0.49% in the last quarter of 2025 and 6.67% over the last twelve months.
The committee met four times in 2025 (February, May, August and December) to monitor investment performance, the managers and the investment strategy.
After the municipal elections of November 2, 2025, Maxime Elmaleh and Jean-Luc Lavoie were appointed to the committee on November 18, 2025.
As at December 31, 2025, the breakdown of the investments complied with the limits set out in the investment policy.
The City is adding two mandatory stops on rue du Domaine, at the east and west approaches to the intersection with rue de la Poterie.
The stop applies to drivers as well as to cyclists.
Until now, the "T" intersection had a stop only at the south approach.
The steep slope of rue du Domaine prevents a driver stopped on the south side from seeing a vehicle coming from the east.
The change affects the Cap-Rouge-Laurentien neighbourhood, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The request came from a citizen; the executive committee adopted the decision on July 8, 2026.
The City is awarding Groupe Relief inc. (Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures) the contract to build the skateboard park at the Patro de Charlesbourg, in the Charlesbourg borough.
The contract is worth $818,739.84 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $859,574.49.
The work includes rebuilding the skateboard park and the surrounding surfaces, plus adding street lights.
Also planned are demolition, grading, granular foundations, landscaping, lighting, furniture and accessories.
Four bids were received; Groupe Relief inc. submitted the lowest price, 25.7% below the requesting department's estimate of $1,102,580.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3402 covering work on buildings, parks and recreational facilities.
The executive committee adopted the decision on April 22, 2026.
The City is hiring the firm Tetra Tech QI inc. to inspect its structures: bridges, overpasses, culverts, stairways, lookouts and footbridges.
The contract is worth $269,995.72 before taxes, which is a net cost of $283,461.76 for the City.
The inspection work runs from the date the contract is awarded until December 31, 2026.
The contract can be renewed for another 12 months, with a price increase tied to the consumer price index.
Five bids were received; Tetra Tech got the best final score, even though Les Services EXP inc. asked for less ($260,030).
The Service de l'ingénierie estimated the cost at $303,151.79 before taxes.
The money comes from an urban agglomeration loan by-law on municipal infrastructure.
The Ville de Québec is borrowing $1,340,000 to improve the layout of streets and commercial arteries during major rebuilding work.
The money can be used for universal accessibility, active transportation, traffic calming, plantings, street furniture, lighting and the integration of works of art.
The work may take place anywhere in the territory under the City's jurisdiction.
The loan is repayable over 15 years, and the amounts are planned from 2026 to 2028 in the capital works program.
The City is taking $134,000 from the general fund (10% of the expense), which will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The City may acquire, by mutual agreement or by expropriation, the land and servitudes needed for the work.
The City is paying $37,800 to Club social Victoria inc. for the year 2026.
The grant is mainly used to pay the club's rent, at 170, rue du Cardinal-Maurice-Roy, in a building owned by the City.
The amount matches the property, school and waste taxes for the premises.
The non-profit club has more than 2,450 members among City employees.
Previous grants were $31,500 in 2023, $32,800 in 2024 and $37,700 in 2025.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service du développement économique et des grands projets.
The Ville de Québec is paying out $213,000 in grants to six production companies to start up audiovisual projects in 2026.

The amounts awarded: $40,000 to Coop Touski Animation, $40,000 to Chaos Harmonique, $38,000 to Productions Ciné-Scène, $38,000 to Du Coup Studio Production, $37,000 to 9401-1095 Québec (MÖ Films 2) and $20,000 to 10e Ave Productions.
Fourteen projects were submitted during the call for projects of March 27, 2026; thirteen were eligible and six were selected.

The money comes from the City ($75,000), the ministère de la Culture et des Communications ($50,000) and the Secrétariat à la Capitale-Nationale ($75,000); the repayment of an unused grant brings the total to $213,000.
Each grant covers a maximum of 75% of the project's eligible costs.
The six projects plan on an average of 96% local labour and 91% of the work being done in the Capitale-Nationale region.
The companies must submit a summary report and a cost report no later than three months after the development stage.
The Ville de Québec is giving $100,500 to the organization Jeunes musiciens du monde to expand its school at 684, rue Saint-Vallier Ouest.
The money comes from the Fonds immobilier communautaire and covers about 12.7% of the project's total cost, estimated at $792,000.
The work will create a soundproofed space: two classrooms that can host up to 100 new students per week, a multi-purpose room, storage areas and offices.
The rest of the funding comes from the organization ($150,000), Desjardins ($200,000), IA Groupe financier ($100,000), the Government of Québec ($75,000) and other partners ($166,500).
The organization must finish the work within 12 months after the agreement is signed.
It must also keep activities related to its mission in the building for 10 years after the payment.
The amount is paid in a single payment, after the payment request and the required documents are submitted.
The City is borrowing $1,850,000 to buy vehicles and motorized equipment for the Service de police de Québec.

The purchase covers, among other things, utility vehicles, cars, pickup trucks, vans, light and heavy trucks and trailers, electric or fuel-powered, as well as accessories and technological solutions.
These vehicles will be added to the police service's current fleet, to meet growing operational needs, the creation of new units and new responsibilities.
The loan will be repaid over five years, out of the City's general revenues.
The City is drawing $185,000 from the general fund, which is 10% of the expense; this amount will be repaid to the fund when the by-law comes into force.
The expense is shared between local (proximity) jurisdictions and urban agglomeration jurisdictions, and the funds are planned for 2026 and 2027 in the capital works program.
The City of Québec is hiring Philippe LeBlanc as director of the Service de la gestion des immeubles.
His annual salary is set at $186,101 (2026 pay scale for service directors).
The contract starts on July 12, 2026 and has no fixed end date.
Until now, he was director of the Division de l'exploitation et de l'entretien in the same service, a position he had held since 2019.
He will report to the assistant city manager for sustainable infrastructure (directeur général adjoint des infrastructures durables).
If he leaves, he must give four weeks' notice; if the City ends the contract, the notice period ranges from 3 to 12 months depending on years of service.
The position was filled through an internal/external competition; the funds are already included in the budget of the Service de la gestion des immeubles.
The City is awarding Stantec experts-conseils ltée a professional services contract worth $357,000 (plus GST and QST) to prepare and supervise water main work in the area of 8e avenue de l'Aéroport.
The firm will carry out the preliminary study, the engineering, the drafting of the call for tenders for the work, and full-time on-site supervision.
The work covered: building a main drinking water pipe and repairing culverts in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
This is the first phase (about 3.0 km) of a 4.5 km loop of the water supply network between the route de l'Aéroport and the route Jean-Gauvin, south of Autoroute 40.
This phase will provide drinking water and fire protection to a development project planned in the short term at the northeast corner of route Jean-Gauvin and boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel.
Seven bids were received; Stantec obtained the highest final score. The net expense is $374,805.38, funded by loan by-law R.V.Q. 3390.
Stantec will be able to apply, on the City's behalf, for the necessary permits and authorizations from government departments and other authorities, with the agreement of the Service de l'ingénierie.
The City has selected the public artwork "Haut lieu" by artist Laurent Gagnon for parc Girardin, in the Beauport heritage site.
An amount of $47,836.49 (plus taxes) has been set aside for the artwork as part of the park's redevelopment.
The sculpture will be installed alongside the path leading to the entrance of maison Girardin, at 600, avenue Royale.
Made of aluminum, stone, steel and bronze, the artwork measures 1575 x 695 mm and its base suggests a barrel bearing a miniaturized landscape.
A committee of seven people (one elected official, one user representative, two City employees and three artists) chose the artwork on January 30, 2026 from among three proposals.
The Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec gave a favourable opinion on the installation.
The unveiling is planned for spring 2027.
The City is awarding 141273 Canada inc. (Monette Express), of Québec, the contract for moving and installing office furniture, until April 30, 2028.
The contract covers three lots: $563,570 for a regular installation crew, $245,610 for space layout projects, and $114,650 for moves related to recreation and other services (before taxes).
The net cost to the City is estimated at $969,906.02.
The regular crew must carry out about forty jobs per week, five days a week, all year long.
The services cover moving employees' furniture and specialized transfers (records and archives office, museum storage collection, among others).
The contract can be renewed for another 12 months, with a price increase based on the Consumer Price Index.
Seven bids were received for lots 1 and 2, and six for lot 3; Monette Express offered the lowest price in all three cases.
The Ville de Québec is obtaining a permanent easement on a piece of land bordering route de l'Aéroport, in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The easement covers about 637.1 m² for a sanitary sewer pipe and 0.4 m² for a fire hydrant.
The City will pay $125,000, plus taxes, to the company 9521-2544 Québec inc., the owner of the land.
Of that amount, $27,000 is compensation for claims, damages, inconvenience and lost revenue.
The situation came to light through a permit application: a City sewer pipe crosses the land without any easement ever having been registered.
The owner wants to build an industrial building on this land, which is assessed at $494,000 on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3390, and payment will be made after the deed is published in the Registre foncier (land registry).
The arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is giving $500 to the organization Gris-Québec to support its mission.
The request comes from councillor Marylou Boulianne.
The money comes from the borough council's budget, under the activity "Soutenir les conseils d'arrondissement" (Supporting the borough councils).
The cheque is issued to Gris-Québec, at 225-1900, avenue Mailloux, in Québec.
The borough council adopted resolution CA1-2026-0155 on July 9, 2026.
The City is adding one parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility on rue Saint-Germain, in Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur.
The space is on the east side of the street, between avenue des Oblats and rue Boisseau, over 10 metres starting from avenue des Oblats.
Only vehicles with a sticker, a licence plate or a permit provided for in the Highway Safety Code will be allowed to park there.
The request comes from a resident of 455, avenue des Oblats, who holds a SAAQ sticker.
No existing parking space is being removed to create this space.
The City approves the plans to change the exterior cladding of the building located at 121, rue des Peupliers Est, in the Lairet neighbourhood (Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The grey and black stone-look stucco on the ground floor will be replaced with ochre-coloured Canexel, like on the upper floors.
According to the analysis, the new cladding fits in with the façade and with neighbouring buildings, and is better suited to the residential use planned for the ground floor.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the project on August 11, 2026.
The plans must be approved before the permit can be issued.
The City is reorganizing its Bureau de la sécurité civile into three units: a Section opérations, an Équipe interventions et rétablissement, and an Équipe gestion des risques.
The Section opérations will coordinate on-the-ground responses, training, reference documents, citizen preparedness and the continuity of municipal services.
The Équipe interventions et rétablissement will support emergency services in helping disaster victims and will coordinate the return to normal after a disaster.
The Équipe gestion des risques will document disaster risks across the territory and will lead the regional resilience plan required by Quebec's new civil protection act.
A position of director of civil protection operations is created; it was already included in the 2026 budget of the Bureau de la sécurité civile.
A project director position becomes director of civil protection risk management, and a coordinating chief is transferred to the new response team, with no change to their conditions.
The City states that the reorganization creates no position that was not already budgeted.
The City is releasing $159,320 left in an agglomeration reserve set aside for protecting and increasing the tree canopy, and is returning it to the general agglomeration surplus.
This reserve was created in 2022 with $1,500,000; $1,340,680 has already been used to fund a project in the 2023-2032 capital works program.
According to the document, the objectives tied to this reserve have been met, so the money no longer needs to be set aside.
A similar transfer of $680 will be proposed to the city council for the equivalent reserve on the local (proximity) side (of which $3,499,320 out of $3,500,000 has been spent).
The urban agglomeration council adopted the decision on June 17, 2026.
The City is closing eight agglomeration loan by-laws for mixed expenditures, for which the work is now finished.
The authorized expenditures totalled $82,585,800.00, while the work cost $75,121,746.14.
The spending authority is reduced by $7,464,053.86, and the remaining borrowing authority balances of $66,743,900.00 are cancelled.
These closures free up an available balance of $2,694,080.04, which the City is not reallocating for now.
The by-laws involved covered intelligent transportation systems, sustainable mobility projects, buildings, vehicles and information technology solutions.
The City says these closures do not affect the carrying out of the projects planned in the 2026-2035 Ten-Year Capital Works Program.
It is asking the ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation to adjust its records.
The City is naming a new street and a retention basin located south of boulevard Louis-XIV, in Beauport (district de Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux), Phillis-Wheatley.
The U-shaped street is part of a subdivision project that includes higher-density housing near the boulevard and low-density homes to the south.
The retention basin, which temporarily stores rainwater, has the same name as the nearest street, in keeping with the City's practice.
The Comité de commémoration et de toponymie chose this name to extend the area's literary theme by broadening it to the Americas.
Phillis Wheatley (around 1753-1784) is recognized as the first author of African descent in North America to publish a collection of poetry.
The Commission de toponymie du Québec was consulted to confirm the spelling of the name.
The City is adding mandatory stops on boulevard de Monaco, at the north and south approaches, at the intersection with rue Careau.
It is removing the mandatory stops on boulevard de Monaco, at the north and south approaches, at the intersection with rue Sociale.
The stops apply to drivers of road vehicles and to cyclists.
The change affects the Vanier-Duberger district, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The decision follows a request from a citizen; the analysis concludes that traffic volumes justify the stop at rue Careau.

The removal at rue Sociale is explained by the distance of less than 150 metres between the two intersections, which is below the standard of the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, and by traffic volumes below the thresholds.
The Ville de Québec is giving a grant of up to $150,000 to the company Biotix inc., which decontaminates soil.
The money will be used to test, under real-world conditions, a biodegradable cleaning solution that cleans soil polluted with hydrocarbons directly on site, without digging it up.
The project costs $301,867 in total: the City pays $150,000 and the company pays $151,867.
The tests will run over 14 months, from July 8, 2026 to August 31, 2027, at three clients located within the territory of the Ville de Québec.
The company, whose head office is in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, expects to keep its 19 jobs and create 3 new ones.
The grant comes from the Capitale-Innovation component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030 and must be approved by the urban agglomeration council.
The Ville de Québec is signing an amendment with the Government of Quebec to extend its Fonds local d'investissement, which lends money to businesses in the area.
The initial loan of $9,545,557, granted in 2002 and interest-free, will have its repayment postponed: the payments will be spread out from 2029 to 2039.
The new rules apply from February 17, 2026 to December 31, 2028; assistance to businesses can be approved up to that date.
About $5,000,000 remains available to be lent to business projects, and some thirty loans are currently active.
Assistance to a business is capped at $150,000 per year, but the agglomeration de Québec has been authorized since 2017 to go up to $300,000.
The City will have to produce quarterly and annual reports to the government, submit its investment policy no later than June 1, 2026, and mention the contribution of the Government of Quebec.
The City will allow the Centre culturel Islamique Luqman de Québec to use the building at 5485, boulevard de l'Ormière as a place of worship ("religious facility" use).
The property is located in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood, east of the parc industriel Armand-Viau, in a mixed-use zone where religious use was not permitted.
The organization has occupied the building since May 1, 2025, and offers social and cultural activities, support for newcomers, Arabic classes and classes on the Quran.
The authorization is personal, cannot be transferred to another occupant, and is valid for one hundred years from the date the by-law comes into force.
The conseil de quartier de Duberger-Les Saules must give its opinion and hold a public consultation meeting.
The by-law contains no provision that can be subject to a referendum.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 2510, boulevard Louis-XIV, in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, in Beauport.
The existing detached building will be allowed to keep a side setback of 2 metres, while the borough's planning by-law requires 3.
The step regularizes the siting of the main building, built in 1983; the location certificate shows a setback of 2.08 metres.
According to the analysis, applying the by-law would require demolishing part of the building.
The analysis notes that the neighbouring building is about 5 metres from the lot line and that a hedge and a fence separate the two properties.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on May 21, 2026.
The City is renting 10 wheel loaders for the Service des travaux publics, from the awarding of the contract until April 30, 2029.
The contract goes to Toromont Cat, a division of Industries Toromont ltée, of Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, for $1,834,860 before taxes.
The machines will be used in particular to clear snow from roadways, according to the operating budget concerned.
The total net expense comes to $1,926,373.61, spread over four years: $208,442.20 in 2026, $631,583.80 in 2027, $648,381.71 in 2028 and $437,965.90 in 2029.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 depend on the budgets being approved by the appropriate authorities.
Six bids were received; Toromont Cat offered the lowest price, which is 15.1% below the department's estimate of $2,160,000.
The City is authorizing the installation of a temporary overhead power line at 755, boulevard des Chutes, in Beauport.
The Centre de services scolaire des Premières-Seigneuries is expanding the building to set up a vocational training centre of about 2,650 square metres.
The current pad-mounted transformer has to be removed to make room for the expansion, which is why a temporary power supply is needed.
The authorization covers the period from April 22, 2026 to October 22, 2027.
The overhead line will have to be removed at the end of this period, and the installation and removal costs must be paid.
The usual rule requires underground wiring for a public building of 2,000 square metres or more.

The City is applying for financial assistance from the ministère de l'Éducation to rebuild the wooden footbridges and boardwalks on the walking trails of the parc linéaire de la Rivière-Saint-Charles.

The application is being made under component 2, "Infrastructures de plein air" (outdoor infrastructure), of the Programme d'aide financière aux infrastructures récréatives, sportives et de plein air.
The program ends on March 31, 2027.
The City commits to paying its share of the project's eligible costs.
Carolyne Larouche, director of the Beauport, Charlesbourg and La Cité-Limoilou boroughs, is authorized to act on the City's behalf in this matter.
No amount is given in the document.
The City is awarding Les Couvre-Planchers Orléans inc. the contract for repair and replacement work on floor coverings in its buildings, from May 1, 2026, to April 30, 2028.

Two lots are covered: the Centre sector (La Cité-Limoilou, Beauport, Charlesbourg, including ExpoCité) and the Ouest sector (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, Les Rivières, La Haute-Saint-Charles, Val-Bélair).
Each lot is estimated at $472,400 before taxes; the net expense is estimated at $991,921.90.
The contract may be renewed for another 12 months, with an indexation based on the Consumer Price Index.
Two companies submitted bids; Orléans submitted the lowest price, 6.4% below the City's estimate.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
The City is borrowing $2,430,000 to buy vehicles and motorized equipment for the Service de police de Québec.
These purchases are to replace Service de police vehicles that have reached the end of their useful life.
The loan will be repaid over five years, out of the City's general revenues.
The spending also covers professional and technical services contracts and the hiring of the staff needed for the purchases.
The vehicles covered include electric or fuel-powered models: utility vehicles, cars, pickup trucks, vans, trucks, trailers and accessories.
The City is taking $243,000 from its general fund (10% of the spending), an amount that will be paid back when the by-law comes into force.
The bill is shared between the urban agglomeration and the City's local (proximity) responsibilities.
The City is changing the zoning for zone 63369Mb, at the corner of boulevard de l'Ormière and rue Racine, in the Loretteville neighbourhood.
Restaurants (use group C20) become permitted in this zone, with a dining area of no more than 3,300 square metres.
The owner of the building at 579 and 581, rue Racine wants to have a restaurant there with a café-terrace and a soft-shell shelter in the back yard.
The by-law allows the café-terrace in the back yard and a soft, rigid or semi-rigid shelter above it.
Two construction plan by-laws adopted in 2014-2015 are repealed; certain standards are transferred to the zoning grid.
The minimum lot width of 30 metres, the minimum building height of 9 metres and the requirement for a pedestal sign are removed.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; the conseil de quartier de Loretteville will hold a public meeting, followed by seven days to submit written comments.
The Ville de Québec is extending its agreement with Université Laval by two years to rent sports facilities at the PEPS, from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2028, under the same conditions.
The facilities covered are the indoor Stade Telus-Université Laval, the Olympic pool and the diving facilities, used by the City and its accredited organizations.
The City pays only for the time slots it reserves, at the hourly rates set each year by the Université and indexed to the Consumer Price Index for the Québec region.
A 15% surcharge is added to the rates for priority of use and related services (offices, storage, parking, lifeguards).
The renewal depends on the approval of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.

The arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge is changing its planning by-law for four zones in the quartier de la Cité-Universitaire (district du Plateau), located between chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois, boulevard du Versant-Nord, autoroute Robert-Bourassa and autoroute Henri-IV.
The maximum number of dwellings goes from two to three in detached buildings in zones 32006Ha, 32023Ha, 32027Ha and 32040Ha.
In semi-detached buildings, the maximum goes from one to two dwellings (zones 32006Ha and 32027Ha).
The change stems from an application for 794, rue des Talus, a building that currently has only one dwelling.
In zones 32023Ha and 32040Ha, the parking standards become those of the "axe structurant A" type.
