After the public consultation of May 6, 2026, where the conseil de quartier voted mostly unfavourably, the City withdrew the removal of the two-storey limit: this maximum is maintained.
The by-law contains no provision that could be subject to a referendum approval.
The City accepts financial assistance of up to $1,496,470 from the ministère de la Culture et des Communications to repair the église Saint-Jean-Baptiste, at 470, rue Saint-Jean.
The money will be used for urgent work on the exterior doors, windows and storm windows, as well as patching the masonry around the openings, where asbestos and lead are present.

The church, which is classified by the gouvernement du Québec and was purchased by the City in November 2024, has been closed to the public for more than ten years and its openings are badly deteriorated.
The grant covers a maximum of 50% of eligible expenses: 80% will be paid when the agreement is signed and 20% at the end of the project.
The City must complete the work within 24 months of the minister's announcement, unless a different deadline is authorized.
The City must provide progress reports twice a year and a report on the use of the assistance within three months after the work is finished.
The funds will be available in 2026 and 2027 under the 2026-2035 investment plan.

The City is awarding Wolseley Canada inc., of Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, the contract to supply water main and sewer materials for section TW-03 of the TramCité project, in the arrondissement of Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The contract is worth $283,687.77 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $297,836.70.
Three companies submitted bids and all were compliant: Wolseley ($283,687.77), Emco ($286,336.82) and Réal Huot ($353,304.12). Wolseley had the lowest price.
The requesting department had estimated the costs at $430,000 before taxes, which is 34% more than the winning bid.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 on building the structuring public transit network.
The executive committee adopted the decision on March 11, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0306).
The Ville de Québec is joining an agreement of the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales (CAG) to obtain print press review services and media monitoring services (radio and television).
The contract covers the period from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2029, with the possibility of two 12-month renewals with no price increase.
The purchase volume is estimated at $240,000 (plus GST and QST) for the three years; the net expense is estimated at $251,970.
The services covered are the Service des relations citoyennes et des communications as well as the Division des communications en sécurité publique - Police.
The amounts remain conditional on the adoption of the 2027 to 2029 budgets.
The director of the Service des approvisionnements is authorized to sign the documents and to confirm the membership in the agreement.
The City is amending its assistance program for businesses harmed by major construction sites to include the work of the TramCité project.
An eligible business can receive up to $30,000 per year of work, if it demonstrates a loss of gross profit of more than 5% compared to comparable years.
A business located in a designated area can obtain an interim payment of no more than $7,500, which is then deducted from the final assistance.
New: in the areas affected by TramCité, an organization that promotes a commercial street can receive up to $30,000 per year of work.
The work must last at least three consecutive months; the assistance covers the work area and its zone of influence.
Businesses must submit an application to the Service du développement économique et des grands projets, which verifies eligibility.
The executive committee will continue to designate the targeted areas as the construction sites are planned.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 2324, boulevard du Parc-Technologique, in the Duberger-Les Saules neighbourhood (Arrondissement des Rivières).
The exemption allows a ground occupancy rate of 2.2% instead of the 15% required by the borough's planning by-law.
Goal: merge two lots (4 598 425 and 6 412 186) to bring into compliance a parking area located on a lot separate from the building it serves.
This parking area had been authorized in 2006 by a temporary special by-law.
The parking area's redevelopment provides for more green space, a retention basin, vegetated swales and the planting of 26 trees.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on May 4, 2026.
The City is officially designating the chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois area, between boulevard Pie-XII and autoroute Duplessis, as a major construction zone for 2026.
Businesses located in this area will be able to apply for financial assistance under the support program tied to the TramCité project construction sites.
The work runs approximately from April 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026.
The 2026 fiscal year is the one recognized for calculating the assistance to businesses in the designated area.
A plan attached to the order sets out the designated area and the area of influence.
To be recognized, the work must last at least three consecutive months and seriously disrupt traffic.
The City is giving $438,689 to Patro Le Pivot in 2026 to support its recreation and community life activities in the arrondissement de Beauport.
The amount is paid in two equal parts: 50% within 30 days after the agreement is signed, and 50% on June 30, 2026.
The agreement covers January 1 to December 31, 2026, and requires the organization to submit an information collection form before any payment.
The 11 federated community recreation centres asked to renew the 2025 grants (indexed by 2%) so that 2026 would be a transition year.
Talks about multi-year agreements are to continue until June 2026.
The program's total budget reaches $3,693,688 for 2026, compared with $3,621,261 in 2025.
The Ville de Québec is giving $150,000 to the Association canadienne de volleyball to hold the FIVB Volleyball Nations League in 2026.
The event takes place from June 3 to 7, 2026: the matches are held at the Centre Vidéotron (admission by ticket) and a free zone for festival-goers is set up on the place Jean-Béliveau.
Six of the world's best women's teams, including the Canadian team, compete there.
The promoter is organizing a school morning on the Wednesday for thousands of schoolchildren and is handing out tickets to disadvantaged groups.
The grant represents 6.7% of the event's planned budget, estimated at $2,240,000.
The payment is spread over two years: $135,000 in 2026 and $15,000 in 2027, the latter amount being conditional on the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The funding is conditional on a sufficient contribution from the other partners for the event to take place.
The City approves the plans for a new detached multi-unit building at 1930-1966, rue Sir-Mathias-Tellier, in the Maizerets neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The approval is conditional on three changes to the facade materials: the brick must extend up to the third level.
The "Conestoga" coloured brick must be replaced with a more reddish brick, similar to the one at 2639, rue Bardy.
The "Étain vieilli" coloured fibre cement cladding must be replaced with a paler, lighter colour.
These changes are intended to harmonize the facade with neighbouring buildings and to reduce the visual impact of the building's height.
If the developer does not meet these conditions, the application will be put on hold and the developer will have to present another project at a later sitting.
The Ville de Québec is joining a purchasing agreement of the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales (CAG) to buy switches and network products.
The agreement runs from March 9, 2026 to March 31, 2028.
The estimated amount is $5,100,000 (plus GST and QST); the net expense is estimated at $5,354,362.50.
The purchases cover switches, firewalls, routers and wireless equipment (access points, controllers, accessories).
Orders will be placed with several selected suppliers whose price is no more than 17% above the lowest price; prices and products are updated every three months.
Going through the CAG makes it possible to enter into the contract without a call for tenders, under the Loi sur les cités et villes.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets by the competent authorities.
The Ville de Québec is giving up to $120,000 to the non-profit organization Le Reflet Entraide: $60,000 in 2026 and $60,000 in 2027 (the 2027 amount depends on budget approval).
The money supports a program that collects unsold or unused hygiene products and cosmetics that are still in good condition, and gives them away for free.
The products go to organizations that help people experiencing homelessness, women who are victims of violence, low-income families, isolated seniors and youth in difficulty.
In return, the organization must collect and redistribute each year products with a market value of at least $800,000 (about 80,000 products) and find at least 5 new partners.
The agreement takes effect on May 15, 2026 and ends on January 31, 2028; the 2027 payment is scheduled for March 1, 2027.
Since 2018, the organization says it has redistributed more than 700,000 products with an estimated value of $5.8 million, with 111 partner organizations in 2025.
The City is adding two mandatory stops on rue de l'Escarboucle, at the north and south approaches to the intersection with rue des Almandins, in Charlesbourg.
The stop already in place at the west approach on rue des Almandins stays: the "T" intersection will therefore have stops on all three of its branches.
Drivers and cyclists will have to stop at these new signs.
The road markings at the intersection will be adjusted accordingly.
The Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente carried out a safety study following a request from citizens; it concludes that the stops will make it easier for pedestrians to cross.
The intersection gives access to parc du Bourg-Royal and to the recreational facilities of école primaire du Bourg-Royal.
The City is authorizing spending of $2,500,000 to pay out homeownership credits under the Accès Famille program, starting in 2026 and for the years that follow.
The Accès Famille program lends families the minimum down payment they need to buy a main residence in a recognized project, within the territory of the city of Québec.
According to the document, this amount should allow about 80 families to become homeowners.
The City is borrowing the same amount of $2,500,000, repayable over five years, out of general revenues.
An amount of $250,000 (10% of the spending) is taken from the general fund and will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The funds are planned for the years 2026 to 2028 of the 2026-2035 investment plan.
The Beauport borough council approves the plans for the construction of a detached multi-unit residential building at 55-75, rue des Pionnières-de-Beauport, in the Chutes-Montmorency neighbourhood.
The building completes an overall project located north of rue des Pionnières-de-Beauport and west of rue Jeanne-Langlois.
The approval is conditional on one change: creating a gentle, gradual slope between the building and the street, with the bottom of the embankment as close as possible to the front property line.
The City justifies this condition by the fact that the existing embankment on the street side is prominent.
If the developer does not meet this condition, the application will be put on hold and the developer will have to present another project at a later meeting.
The project includes a flat roof, light-coloured masonry with black metal accents, and the planting of several trees in front of the building and in the open spaces.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 1201-1211, 4e Avenue, in Vieux-Limoilou (district de Limoilou, arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
It allows a side setback of 0.1 metre, whereas the planning by-law requires either no setback at all or one of at least 1.5 metres.
The exemption legalizes the position of a wall that already exists, as part of the conversion of an attached garage into a two-bedroom dwelling.
According to the analysis, meeting the standard would force the owner to redo the garage's exterior cladding in order to thicken the wall.
The wall in question is blind (it has no openings), which limits the impact on the neighbouring property.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on April 28, 2026; the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec also issued a favourable recommendation.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 2470, avenue Renouard, in the Vieux-Moulin neighbourhood in Beauport (Robert-Giffard district).
The building's side setback is deemed compliant at 1 metre, instead of the 1.2 metres required by the borough's planning by-law.
The owner wants to set up a third dwelling in the basement and convert the attached garage into a liveable room to give the dwelling an outside exit.
Without this exemption, part of the building, built in 1945, would have had to be demolished to meet the 1.2-metre setback.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on January 21, 2026; no complaints have been recorded about the garage.
The City is entrusting the organization Loisirs Brio with the specialized maintenance and supervision of the recreational and sports facilities and equipment of the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The contract amounts to $302,725.43 (plus GST and QST), for a net expenditure of $317,823.87.
The agreement covers the period from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027, with a 12-month renewal option adjusted according to the minimum wage in effect on May 1, 2027.
The amounts are used in particular for outdoor skating rinks ($145,516.53), parks ($112,697.18), sports fields ($50,031.07) and community recreation centres ($9,579.09).
The funds come from the operating budget of the arrondissement de Charlesbourg; the 2027 portion depends on the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The agreement follows the previous one, which ended on April 30, 2026.
The City can award this contract directly, without a call for tenders, because Loisirs Brio is a non-profit organization.
The City wants to obtain a permanent easement on a piece of land bordering 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The easement covers about 21.20 square metres and will be used to move public utility conduits and networks.
The City will try to reach an agreement by mutual consent with the owner; otherwise, it will proceed by expropriation.
The owner has been informed of the process, the next steps and the name of a contact person at the City.
The entire property is assessed at $210,000 on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll, which works out to $452.10 per square metre.
If the project no longer needs the easement, the City may abandon the expropriation proceedings.
The money comes from the agglomeration loan by-law on the structuring public transit network.
The City is awarding Noxe inc., of Québec, a contract for work on the security systems in its buildings (lot 1), for an estimated amount of $1,261,100.70 before taxes.
The contract runs from the date it is awarded until February 15, 2028, with a 12-month renewal option indexed to the Consumer Price Index.

The work covers access control systems (Kantech or Genetec), intrusion alarms (DSC) and video surveillance (Genetec): installation, replacement, configuration, connection, troubleshooting and removal of old components.
Four companies submitted bids for lot 1; Noxe inc. submitted the lowest price, ahead of Logic-Contrôle ($1,274,953.96), Garda ($1,277,913.18) and Sécurmax ($1,354,261.78).
The selected bid is 9.7% higher than the estimate of the requesting department, which was $1,150,000.
The net expense is estimated at $1,323,998.10, subject to approval of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.
Lot 2, which covers buildings under agglomeration jurisdiction, including those in Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures and L'Ancienne-Lorette, is awarded separately through a delegation of powers.
The City is entrusting the security of the hôtel de ville, in the Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, to the company Groupe de sécurité Garda SENC.
The contract is worth $1,251,972.90 before taxes, for the period from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2029.
The service covers daytime, evening and weekend security.
The contract can be renewed three times, for 12 months each time, with an indexation provided for by the Décret sur les agents de sécurité du Québec.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 depend on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
Eight bids were received; Garda obtained the highest final score, ahead of Trudel Sécurité inc.
The City is changing its by-law to allow a wider garage entrance (driveway) at the future fire station in the Vieux-Moulin neighbourhood, in Beauport.
The maximum width goes from 10 metres to 23.5 metres for this two-way driveway.
The land involved is located south of avenue Saint-Clément, west of avenue Langlois, north of rue Anne-Mayrand and east of avenue D'Estimauville.

According to the City, the widening is meant to reduce response time and improve pedestrian safety when trucks are leaving, since vehicles will be able to drive out in a straight line with better visibility.
The Sainte-Odile fire station, on rue des Pins Ouest, will be relocated to this new facility.
The by-law contains no provisions that can be subject to a referendum; a public consultation meeting is planned.
Adoption is targeted at the urban agglomeration council of September 16, 2026.
The Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough council wants to allow the house at 902, Grande Allée Ouest, in the Sillery neighbourhood, to house financial services offices instead of a residential use.
The building cannot be enlarged, either in floor area or in height, and a hedge must be maintained along Grande Allée Ouest.
The new use must begin within five years after the by-law comes into force, otherwise the authorization lapses.
The property has about six parking spaces, whereas nine would be required: the owner will have to redesign the parking area or pay a compensation to be exempted.
The conseil de quartier de Sillery will be consulted, will hold the public consultation meeting, and interested people will have seven days after the meeting to submit their comments in writing.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The City will not hold an active participation process, because the area already has this type of use and the building's appearance will not change.
L'Église Adventiste du Septième Jour – Fédération du Québec will be allowed to use the building at 33, avenue Ruel (lot 1 988 967) as a place of worship, in the quartier des Chutes-Montmorency.
The current zoning for zone 53141Mb does not allow religious facilities, so the City is amending its planning by-law to create a personal authorization.
This authorization is valid for 100 years from the date the by-law comes into force and cannot be transferred to another organization.
The Église says it also wants to offer community services there: health training, activities to help immigrants integrate, French-language courses, a donation site and a daycare service.
The conseil de quartier des Chutes-Montmorency is asked to give its opinion and to hold the public consultation meeting.
The by-law contains no provisions that can be subject to a referendum.
The City is settling out of court a grievance filed by the Association des pompiers professionnels de Québec inc. in November 2021.
The grievance challenged the way the City calculated firefighters' annual vacation pay.
The City will pay $424,176.53 in principal, interest and costs, plus applicable employee benefits.
The money will be paid to all unionized employees who are in the same situation.
The money comes from the litigation budget of Affaires juridiques and falls under the urban agglomeration's jurisdiction.
The City's lawyers, Giasson et Associés, will sign the release and the necessary documents.
The executive committee adopted the decision on April 29, 2026.
The Ville de Québec will pay a grant of up to $150,000 to the company Groupe Conseil Cogismaq inc., in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The money will be used to market the Genius ERP software in the United Kingdom: reviewing marketing content, trade shows, hiring two sales subcontractors and adapting the software.
The project costs $503,742 in total; the company is investing $353,742 of its own funds in it.
The grant comes from the Capitale-Innovation component of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, which grants a maximum of $150,000 per project and up to 50% of eligible expenses.
The company plans to create two specialized business development positions.
The review committee of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030 gave a favourable opinion on April 14, 2026; follow-up will be done with an economic benefits form.
The City is granting a minor exemption for the house at 2655A-2655B, rue de la Faune, in the Saint-Émile neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The exemption makes the basement entrance compliant with a rear setback of 7.2 metres, whereas the planning by-law requires 9.0 metres.
This decision regularizes the building's siting following renovation work carried out under a permit issued in 2019.

The building was already non-compliant before the work; the basement entrance, adapted to the level of the foundations, now takes up 47% of the rear wall instead of the maximum of 40% allowed for a projection.
According to the analysis in the file, no complaints from neighbours have been received since the construction, 6 years ago.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on August 12, 2026, and the borough council granted it.
The City is reaching an out-of-court settlement with Les Immeubles B. Dupont Ltée to close the expropriation of a piece of land (lot 1 940 421) located on 1re Avenue.
The land is being acquired as part of the structuring public transit network project (TramCité).
The final compensation is set at $1,200,000 plus taxes, including principal, interest, additional compensation and expert assessment fees.
The City had already paid $915,000 in January 2026, so $285,000 remains to be paid.
The money comes from the urban agglomeration's loan by-law for the structuring public transit network.
The date the land must be vacated is moved from September 1, 2026 to February 1, 2027, in line with the work schedule of Infra CITÉ.
The City's attorneys, Giasson et associés, are authorized to sign the settlement documents.
The City is allowing the owner of 4, impasse de Hongrie, in the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough, not to provide 2 parking spaces.
The owner wants to build an 8-unit residential building; the by-law requires 10 spaces and the project provides 8.
In exchange, the owner must pay $1,000 to the « Fonds de stationnement », no later than 30 days after the borough council adopts the resolution.
The City notes that the area is well served by public transit and that on-street parking there is lightly used.
The building will be built on a private street, impasse de Hongrie, in the Val-Bélair district.
The arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is giving out 25 grants totalling $109,910 to 23 organizations in the area.
The applications had been submitted on June 15, 2026, under the programs of the Cadre de soutien aux organismes reconnus.

Seven organizations are each receiving $10,000 for projects: support for youth in distress (Centre de prévention du suicide), food distribution in Maizerets, French-language learning for immigrant families, bicycle delivery of food aid in Limoilou, a children's club in St-Roch, and the « Vers l'autonomie » project.
Amounts of $500 are going to eight organizations for community-building activities, such as back-to-school parties and anniversary celebrations.
Other grants cover the purchase of equipment (balls, furniture and bedding, an oboe, a projector, towels and pyjamas), the redesign of a website, and promotional videos.
Les Scouts du district de Québec is receiving $6,500 and Le Touski $4,222 for year 2 of support for operating expenses.
The money comes from the arrondissement's operating budget, under the « Soutien aux organismes » activity.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 255, rue du Roi, in the Saint-Roch neighbourhood, to build a new 3-unit building (two 2-bedroom units and one 3-bedroom unit).
The front of the building may measure 5.70 metres instead of the required minimum of 6 metres.
The rear setback may be 1.9 metres rather than zero or at least 3.5 metres, and an outdoor staircase may extend all the way to the rear lot line.
A green roof may count for up to 66% of the minimum required green space percentage, instead of 25%.
The lot measures 86.5 m²; with the exemption, the total green space reaches 17.2 m² (20% of the lot) instead of 10.9 m² (12%).
The building will replace a paved parking area.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the application on April 7, 2026, and the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec gave a favourable opinion.
The City is transferring $461,005 from a reserve set aside for snow dump sites to a reserve of money that can be used freely (unallocated local operating surplus).
This amount was what remained of a $5,000,000 envelope included in the 2020-2024 and 2021-2025 capital works programs to expand the capacity of certain snow dump sites and to purchase land.
The City states that the objectives tied to this reserve have been met, so the money no longer needs to be set aside for that purpose.
City council was scheduled to decide on this on June 16, 2026.
The City is settling out of court an expropriation dispute concerning servitudes on a property at 1092, rue du Parc-Thornhill, alongside boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest.
These servitudes were taken as part of the Réseau structurant de transport en commun (TramCité) project, in the arrondissement of Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The final compensation is set at $39,000, which includes the capital, interest, the additional compensation and expert appraisal fees.
The City had already paid $13,700 in 2025; it will therefore pay a remaining balance of $25,300 to the owners.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 tied to the Réseau structurant de transport en commun.
The firm Giasson et associés is authorized to sign the settlement documents on the City's behalf.
The City of Québec is giving up to $150,000 to the organization Entrepreneuriat Think Tank for its "Relancer" program (formerly Persévérance entrepreneuriale).
The program supports entrepreneurs in difficulty for about six months: coaching, meetings with other entrepreneurs, and training sessions given by experts.
Entrepreneurs whose business is located in the Québec urban agglomeration or in Wendake will pay reduced registration fees.
The project costs $300,000 in total: $150,000 from the City and $150,000 from the participating businesses.
The organization aims to support 60 entrepreneurs over two years and to put 75% of them back on the path to entrepreneurship.
The money comes from the Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale, as part of the Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030.
The City had already given $72,860 to this organization for the same project in 2024.
The City is refusing a minor exemption request for the property at 1331-1333, avenue Lavigerie, in the Saint-Louis neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The owners wanted to have a green area of 25% approved instead of the 30% required, and a space of 4.2 metres instead of 6 metres between two driveways or parking areas.
The two-family building was built differently from the plans approved in 2018; the request was meant to make the situation legal.
Reason for the refusal: granting the exemption would set a precedent and lead to repeated similar requests.
Another reason: the City considers it possible to build a parking area that complies with the rules and to respect the green area percentage, so there is no serious harm to the owner.
The owners will therefore have to remove part of the outdoor landscaping and add the planted strips provided for in the permit.
The borough council had already refused a similar request for the neighbouring building in 2021.

The Ville de Québec is entrusting the organization Le centre récréatif St-François-d'Assise inc. with supervising and programming open swim periods at the indoor pool of the Centre communautaire Ferland, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The agreement is worth $175,070.81, exempt from GST and QST.
The contract covers the period from January 1 to December 31, 2026.
The City may end the agreement before December 31, 2026 if renovation work on the Centre communautaire Ferland is confirmed; the closing date will be communicated to the organization.
The agreement was reached without a call for tenders, which the Cities and Towns Act allows with a non-profit organization.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou, under the activity "Réaliser la programmation aquatique" (Deliver aquatic programming).
The arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles is authorizing a conditional use at 14521, boulevard de la Colline, in the Loretteville neighbourhood (Lac-Saint-Charles–Saint-Émile district).
The property will be able to host a construction and landscaping business.
Outdoor storage or parking of vehicles weighing 3,000 kg or more, of tool vehicles and of motorized machinery is allowed there.
Outdoor storage of soil, sand, stone or other granular or organic materials is also allowed there, if it is linked to a construction, landscaping or snow removal business.
According to the analysis, runoff water from the parking area where the vehicles are already stored is directed to existing retention ponds.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the application on March 25, 2026; the use had already been granted in 2021 on the original lot.
The City is authorizing an exemption for the property at 750-760, rue de la Sorbonne, in the quartier des Jésuites in Charlesbourg (the Arpidrome arena).
The owner will be allowed to build a new exit stairway that will encroach up to 3.6 metres into the side setback, whereas the planning by-law limits this encroachment to 2.0 metres.
According to the analysis, this stairway is required to allow the building to be evacuated in compliance with the rules and to ensure the safety of arena users.
The stairway will be built in the side yard, on the side of a parking lot used by users of the Arpidrome and of the high school.

The analysis indicates that the chosen location is the only possible option given the building's architecture, and that the width of the stairway matches the minimum required by the National Building Code.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on June 17, 2026; the decision rests with the borough council.
The City is giving $25,000 to Centre Mgr Marcoux inc. for its project Ateliers d'intégration en français.
The project offers French classes to newcomers, in small groups paired with trained volunteers.
Activities are held mainly at the centre communautaire Monseigneur-Marcoux, Monday to Thursday, during the day and in the evening, over four sessions a year (40 weeks of classes).
The grant covers the period from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027.
The project costs $90,640 in total; the City is funding about 28% of it.
In 2025-2026, 231 people used these services and 77 volunteers take part in them.
A grant of the same amount had already been given to the organization for this project.
The executive committee approves a new administrative structure for Destination Québec cité, the City's tourism organization.
The City is creating a Division tourisme d'affaires et commercialisation, which takes over the Section commercialisation internationale.
The Unité soutien de l'administration et des relations avec l'industrie and the Section développement de la destination durable are abolished.
A Section expérience visiteurs et soutien aux membres is created; the Division développement des affaires et de la destination is renamed Division développement et expérience à destination.
The two managers whose positions are abolished are reassigned and keep the same conditions and benefits.
The reorganization creates no net positions: the new director position is funded by abolishing a vacant tourism development advisor position.
The costs are covered out of Destination Québec cité's operating budget.

The City is changing the planning rules for the parc industriel Cardinal, in the Vanier neighbourhood (Vanier-Duberger district), for 15 zones located between boulevard Pierre-Bertrand, boulevard Père-Lelièvre and autoroute Laurentienne.
Distribution centres and general industry become permitted in zones bordering boulevard Pierre-Bertrand and boulevard Père-Lelièvre, where they were prohibited until now.
Mechanical or electronic game rooms are allowed in the zone at 999, boulevard Pierre-Bertrand, which lifts the current limit of three pinball machines per establishment.
Outdoor storage and vehicle parking become permitted in the zones of the Hydro-Québec power transmission corridor, except near residential areas.
Health clinics without lodging (physiotherapy, acupuncture, etc.) are permitted in two zones fronting Pierre-Bertrand and Père-Lelièvre.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to a referendum; the conseil de quartier de Vanier will hold a public consultation meeting, followed by seven days to submit written comments.
The City is authorizing its Service des approvisionnements to buy computer hardware and software from companies that do not have an establishment in Québec, in Canada or in a European Union country.
These purchases are for the Service des technologies de l'information.
Two American suppliers are involved: Lightburn Software (Dover, Delaware) for a licence update, and Digi-Key Corporation (Thief River Falls, Minnesota).
Each of the two contracts falls within a range of $0 to $33,000: one paid by purchase requisition, the other by purchasing card.
This authorization stems from a regulation of the Government of Québec enacted on March 6, 2025, which requires prior approval for this type of by-mutual-agreement contract, with no value limit.
The regulation also covers medical supplies and equipment, pharmaceutical products and scientific instruments, including purchases made by credit card.
The City is awarding Groupe Colas Québec inc. the contract to redevelop rue de la Faune, for $18,935,000 before taxes (net expense of $19,877,654.96).
The work affects the arrondissements of Charlesbourg and La Haute-Saint-Charles.
The project includes complete resurfacing, a new geometric layout, curbs, roadwork and a bike path.
It also provides for a drinking water system, stormwater management, a lighting system and overhead signage work.
A watercourse will be redeveloped and work will be carried out in the shoreline strip.
Five bids were received; Colas submitted the lowest price, 14.7% below the City's estimate ($22,198,879.45).
The contract provides for price adjustments based on the cost of bitumen and fuel.
The City is lowering the speed limit from 40 km/h to 30 km/h on rue de Bar-le-Duc, between avenue Duchesneau and rue du Grand-Voyer.
The same change applies on rue du Grand-Voyer, between rue de Bar-le-Duc and avenue Wilfrid-Pelletier.
The new limits apply at all times, to road vehicles.
These streets are in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, district du Plateau.
The Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente justifies the reduction by the low traffic in the area and the presence of a school corridor.
In 2021, these limits had been changed from 50 to 40 km/h; in 2023, the west access to rue du Grand-Voyer from avenue Wilfrid-Pelletier was closed to limit through traffic.
The City is creating a secretarial agent position, class 3, in the Division de la culture et du patrimoine of the Service de la culture et du patrimoine.
The request comes from the management of the Service de la culture et du patrimoine and was authorized by the Direction générale.
The position is governed by the collective agreement between the City and the Syndicat des fonctionnaires municipaux de Québec (FISA).
The money needed, including employee benefits, is already provided for in the budget of the Culture et patrimoine activity.
The executive committee adopted the decision on February 18, 2026.
The City is extending the contract of Delphine Micouleau, expert consultant at the Bureau de la sécurité civile, until December 31, 2026.
Her mandate covers the process of developing risk management.
Her hourly rate stays at $54.17.
No hours are added for the period from July 1 to December 31, 2026: she will use up the remaining hours from her initial bank of 750 hours.
The funds, including employee benefits, are already provided for in the budget of the Bureau de la sécurité civile.
The City is banning parking on both sides of rue Duplessis, near the intersection with boulevard des Chutes, in the arrondissement de Beauport.
The ban covers 18 metres on the east side and 17 metres on the west side, going south from boulevard des Chutes.
Four parking spaces are being removed.
The City says that vehicles parked near the intersection were compromising the safety of road users and getting in the way of snow removal vehicles.
The move follows requests from citizens; according to the City, the impact on residents is low because they have enough off-street spaces.
The decision falls under the Beauport borough council (district de La Chute-Montmorency-Seigneurial).
The City is allowing a new detached single-family house at 1981, rue Sheppard, in Sillery, to be built 2.8 metres from the street instead of the 4.5 metres required by the planning by-law.
This decision corrects an exemption granted in November 2025, which set the front setback at 3.49 metres: that figure did not match the actual location of the planned cantilever.
The reference to the 3.49-metre front setback is removed from the earlier resolution.
According to the analysis, the neighbouring houses are already located about 2.7 and 3.0 metres from the street, and the current house on the lot, which will be demolished, is also non-compliant.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on January 13, 2026.
The document reports no financial impact.
The City is changing the planning rules for zone 21543Ha, located at 8720, rue Colette-Samson, in the Neufchâtel Est–Lebourgneuf neighbourhood.
It is removing the 2-metre visual screen required in the back yard, along the western edge of the rue Colette-Samson lots, which is next to a piece of land owned by Hydro-Québec.
This screen prevented any construction (shed, garage, pool) over 2 metres and required the planting of a row of evergreen trees.
It is reducing the required rear setback from 9 metres to 6 metres, which leaves more room to arrange back yards.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.
The conseil de quartier de Neufchâtel Est–Lebourgneuf is being asked to give its opinion and to hold the public consultation meeting.
Interested people will have seven days after this meeting to send in their comments in writing.
The City is awarding Entreprises G.N.P. inc., of Victoriaville, the contract to rebuild the ponceau Seigneuriale (culvert), in the Beauport borough, for $2,651,064 (plus GST and QST).
The work includes demolishing the culvert and the neighbouring building, then installing a prefabricated culvert.
The contractor will also replace the water main, sanitary sewer and storm sewer pipes in the area.
The roadway, curbs, sidewalks and driveway entrances will be rebuilt, and the banks stabilized.
Traffic management measures and environmental measures will be put in place during the work.
Six companies submitted bids; G.N.P. offered the lowest price, 43.6% below the City's estimate ($4,703,090).
The net cost to the City is $2,783,285.82, financed by a loan by-law.
The arrondissement des Rivières is paying $164,812 to 25 organizations in its territory to help them cover their operating costs.
The grants range from $566 (Le Reflet) to $16,683 (Association régionale de loisir pour personnes handicapées de la Capitale-Nationale), with several organizations receiving $10,000.
The organizations covered are recreation, sport and mutual aid organizations in the Vanier, Duberger-Les Saules, Neufchâtel and Lebourgneuf sectors.
The money comes from the arrondissement's operating budget, under the "Soutien aux organismes" (support for organizations) line.
The applications had been filed on February 20, 2026; some payments correspond to year 1, 2 or 3 of support already under way.
The amount granted depends on the organization's recognition category, its priority clienteles and its rental situation.
The executive committee takes note of the list of budget transfers made by the Service des finances between September 1 and December 31, 2025.
These transfers move money from one spending item to another within the operating budget, without adding any new money.
The total of the transfers affecting operating activities comes to $12,814,101.
Transfers involving more than one department total $306,206, spread over 34 lines (public works, culture, recreation, water supply and sewers, city management, etc.).
No transfer between two chapters of the same loan by-law was made during this period.

The City is authorizing the demolition of an accessory building located behind the maison Marie-Verret, at 23, rue Parent, in the Loretteville neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The building, erected between 1917 and 1948, is identified as a heritage property; the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec issued its decision on May 21, 2026.
The Commission cites the structural and building envelope failures documented by an expert assessment, as well as the cost of repairs.
After the demolition, the owner will have to clean up, level and plant vegetation on the lot.
No one asked for a review of the decision within the 30-day period, and no written comments were received during the publication period.
The urban agglomeration council is waiving its power to cancel the decision and is shortening the 90-day period, which clears the way for the authorization certificate to be issued.
The City is authorizing a mixed-use real estate project of about 80 housing units at 1111, boulevard Pie-XI Nord, in the Val-Bélair neighbourhood, where residential use was not allowed.
The building will have four to six storeys and must include at least 75 housing units, 30% of which will have two or more bedrooms and three of which will have at least three bedrooms.

The developer will be allowed to build closer to the property lines (2.9 m instead of 6 m for the front setback, 3 m instead of 4.5 m for the side setback) and to provide 95 parking spaces instead of the 124 required.
The ground floor must set aside at least 360 m² for shops, services or a restaurant.
The project requires a green roof of at least 400 m², a 130 m² terrace for residents, one heat pump per housing unit, 9 charging stations and 20 bicycle spaces.
The process takes place in two steps: a public consultation meeting, then three days to submit written comments, before the final resolution. The project is not subject to a referendum.
Failure to comply with the conditions carries a fine of $1,000 for an individual and $2,000 in other cases, doubled for a repeat offence.
The Commission de la capitale nationale du Québec wants to set up a food service area on the ground floor of 40, rue Dalhousie, in Vieux-Québec.
The space faces the Place des Canotiers; the City says the project aims to increase the number of people using this public space, especially in the summer.
The City declares the project consistent with the objectives of its land use planning and development plan, which allows the CCNQ to move forward.
The land is in a low-current zone of the fleuve Saint-Laurent, and therefore at risk of flooding, but changes of use are allowed there.
The site is in a Centre-ville land use area, where retail businesses and personal services are permitted with no density limit.
The notice will be sent to the minister responsible for the Capitale-Nationale region.
Québec is adopting a revised version of its Politique d'investissement de la Vision entrepreneuriale Québec 2030, which sets the rules for money given to businesses and organizations.
The Gouvernement du Québec has given the City responsibility for managing close to $59M for 2026-2027 to 2028-2029 through the Entente de délégation du Fonds de la région de la Capitale-Nationale.

Grant amounts are going up: Bourse entrepreneuriale and Bon d'accompagnement go from $25,000 to $30,000, Défi-Québec from $50,000 to $75,000, Capitale-Innovation and Capitale-Productivité from $150,000 to $500,000, and Capitale-Commerce from $25,000 to $35,000.
The restaurant sector is no longer eligible under the Capitale-Commerce component.
Three new components are being added: sector-based agreements, projects led by the Ville de Québec (which can be funded up to 100%), and projects eligible under the Fonds régions et ruralité.
An application must now seek a contribution of at least $35,000 (instead of $25,000) to be brought before the Comité d'analyse et de recommandation.
The City explains that the higher amounts take into account the rising costs of the projects submitted.
The City is once again renting the parking lot north of the église Saint-Félix-de-Cap-Rouge, at 1460-1462, rue Provancher, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The parking lot is used by people visiting the area, in particular people going to the plage Jacques-Cartier.
The lease runs from January 24, 2026 to January 23, 2031, with a five-year renewal option.
The rent is $12,190 for the first year (excluding GST and QST), then goes up by 2% per year. Last year's rent was $11,950.93.

The City is renting from the Fabrique de la paroisse de La-Transfiguration-du-Seigneur, which since 2019 has brought together the parishes of Saint-Augustin, Saint-Félix-de-Cap-Rouge and Sainte-Catherine.
The parish keeps priority use of the parking lot for its activities and must give the City at least 48 hours' notice if access is restricted.
Use of the parking lot is limited to 12 hours a day, between 6 a.m. and midnight; overnight use is prohibited.
The City is expanding the list of people who can issue statements of offence to those who occupy the roadway without a permit or who do not meet the conditions of their permit.
Until now, only police officers and one lawyer from the Service des affaires juridiques could issue these statements of offence.

The following people will now be able to issue them: the director of the Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente, the director of the Division de l'exploitation et de la mobilité intelligente, the director of the Section de la gestion des réseaux de transport, an engineer from that section, a technician and an officer in traffic and transportation, a parking officer, as well as a person hired by the council for this purpose.
The measure applies to streets in the arterial network under the responsibility of the city council and to those for which the boroughs are responsible.
The City says it will first focus on raising awareness among contractors at fault, and will issue a statement of offence only if they refuse to comply.
The document indicates no financial impact.
The city council adopted the by-law on August 25, 2026, after the notice of motion of July 7, 2026.

The City is paying out $115,000 in grants to two cultural organizations, as part of the Entente de développement culturel (cultural development agreement) with the ministère de la Culture et des Communications.
La Charpente des fauves (Théâtre Astronaute) is receiving $60,000 for the 8th edition of "Théâtre en quartiers": $50,000 for presenting the shows and $10,000 for a creative residency.
This project will offer about a dozen free performances of an original creation in parks and day camps (Programme Vacances-Été) in Québec, reaching about 3,000 children.
The project is being carried out in collaboration with the Conservatoire d'art dramatique de Québec and includes several graduating students.

Culture Capitale-Nationale et Chaudière-Appalaches (Conseil de la culture de la région de Québec) is receiving $55,000 for the 40th edition of the Prix d'excellence des arts et de la culture and for activities promoting its sector-based committees (tables sectorielles).
The funding comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3367 ($105,000) and from a transfer in culture and heritage ($10,000).
The City approves the plans for a house extension at 2995, avenue Dumas, in the Lairet neighbourhood (Limoilou).
The extension will be built on the side of the building, inside the existing carport.
The proposed exterior siding is vinyl similar to the siding already in place.
The City's analysts noted that the extension does not reuse the stone, which covers about half of the current building, and suggested adding stone at the bottom of the siding.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended approving the plans, without including this condition.
The conseil d'arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou (borough council) adopted the decision on March 23, 2026.

The executive committee authorizes replacing two lots (lots 1 738 378 and 1 738 379) with three new lots, at the intersection of avenue Nérée-Tremblay and avenue Chapdelaine, in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood (Saint-Louis-Sillery district).
The addresses affected are 2314 to 2330 and 2334 to 2340, avenue Chapdelaine, as well as 791 to 799, avenue Nérée-Tremblay.
The eight current residential buildings, owned by Fiducie André Bilodeau, will be demolished and replaced by new residential buildings.
The project provides for 391 housing units in total.
The new lots will measure 3,598, 4,025.4 and 8,172.1 square metres; two of them will be used for phases 3 and 4 of the project, and the division prevents any lot from being landlocked.
Since projects with several buildings on a single lot are not allowed in this zone, the executive committee's approval was required to change the division.
Next step: the Office municipal d'habitation will file an application for a construction permit.

The Ville de Québec is supporting the Marathon de Québec 2026 for a total of $432,500: $120,000 in cash, up to $261,000 in free municipal services and up to $51,500 in the purchase of goods and services.
The event runs from October 2 to 4, 2026 and is aiming for more than 20,000 runners and walkers, with five races: 2 km, 5 km, 10 km, 21.1 km and 42.2 km.
Starts and finishes take place in the ExpoCité area, except for the 2 km youth race, which starts from parc Cartier-Brébeuf; nine neighbourhoods are crossed.
Free activities are also being added: the Expo Je Cours Qc on October 2 and 3 at the Centre de foires ExpoCité, and the Semaine Go from September 28 to October 2.
The free municipal services come mainly from building management, public works, police, fire protection and communications.
The $120,000 grant is spread over two years: $108,000 in 2026 and $12,000 in 2027, subject to the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The support is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners; the event's total planned budget is $4,529,661.
The City is asking the Banque Nationale du Canada for an irrevocable letter of guarantee of $721,219 for its incinerator, the Complexe de valorisation énergétique.
This guarantee is required by the ministère de l'Environnement from any operator of an incinerator or a landfill site; the Ministry asked for it on September 5, 2025.
The amount corresponds to 1% of the capital cost of the facility, assessed at $72,121,856 on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll.
The guarantee is valid for one year and must be renewed for as long as the incinerator is in operation.
It costs the City $3,606.10 per year (0.5% of its value), an amount taken from the operating budget of the Service de la gestion des matières résiduelles.
The $500,000 guarantee for the landfill site remains valid and is not changed; its annual cost is $2,500.
The City is changing the zoning of six zones in the Notre-Dame-des-Laurentides neighbourhood, in the Charlesbourg borough (district des Monts).
The areas affected are located around boulevard du Lac, côte Bédard, rue Saint-Alexandre and rue de Dublin.
The boundaries of the residential zones and of forest zone 41065Fb are being redrawn: some residential zones are shrinking in favour of the forest zone, while others are getting bigger.
These changes are meant to align the zoning with the new urbanization perimeter and with the land uses set out in the revised development plan, in force since February 7, 2020.
The City is asking for the opinion of the conseil de quartier de Notre-Dame-des-Laurentides and is entrusting it with holding the public consultation meeting.
The by-law contains no provision that can be subject to a referendum. City council was aiming for adoption on May 5, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is giving up to $167,000 to Centre R.I.R.E. 2000, a non-profit organization in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The money funds the "Passerelle emploi immigration 2.0" project, which helps immigrants find a job and helps businesses meet their labour needs.
The project targets sectors such as health care, hotels, restaurants, services and construction, using the Moovejob platform from Patrimoine RH.
Stated goals: support at least 50 immigrants, place 25 of them in their field of expertise and help 50 businesses; 2 jobs would be created.

The project costs $209,674 in total: $167,000 from the City, $20,674 from the organization, $12,000 from the ministère de l'Immigration, $5,000 from Patrimoine RH and $5,000 from the Fondation Akelius.
The money comes from the Fonds régions et ruralité, structuring projects component, which allows up to $300,000 per project.
The City will track the results using an economic benefits form.
The City is adding mandatory stops on avenue Montpetit, on the east and west approaches, at the intersection with avenue Louis-Jobin.
It is doing the same at the intersection of avenue Montpetit and rue de Dijon.
Both intersections therefore go from a single stop on the secondary approach to stops on all approaches.
The requirement applies to drivers of road vehicles as well as to cyclists.
The Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente explains that avenue Montpetit has a school corridor along its entire length, used every day by pupils from the école primaire Coeur-Vaillant.
The decision concerns the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, district of La Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy.
The City is changing its planning rules (the harmonization by-law and the borough by-laws) on a series of points covering 13 amendment sheets.

Construction sites will be able to set up worker parking, material storage and a trailer on a lot other than the one where the work is taking place, without an authorization certificate, as long as no tree is cut down and everything is removed once the work is finished.
A wall-mounted air conditioner or heat pump will have to be concealed only if it is on a façade more than 1.5 metres above the ground, and must stay at least 1 metre from a property line.
Other changes concern how the number of storeys is calculated on a sloped lot, terraces attached to a building, prohibited exterior cladding materials, wall murals and parking in front of a façade.
The minimum and maximum number of parking spaces is changing for administrative services (group C1).
In one area shown on the by-law's plan, sidewalk cafés will be allowed in side and rear yards for a two-year period, subject to certain standards.
An authorization certificate will now be required to cut down an elm tree, no matter where it is located.
The City is adopting the 2025 activity report of its Service de protection contre l'incendie and sending it to the ministère de la Sécurité publique, as the Fire Safety Act requires every year.
The Service had 597 employees in 2025, compared with 562 the year before, and its operating budget reached $77.6M, an increase of about $6.7M.
Firefighters responded to more than 15,000 calls, meeting the Ministry's response times in 91% of interventions.
The Service carried out more than 63,500 home prevention visits and more than 46,000 hours of training.
The area covered includes Québec, L'Ancienne-Lorette, Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures and Wendake, with at least 100 firefighters on duty at all times in 16 fire stations.
Workplace accidents dropped by 12.5%, a third yearly decrease in a row, and 99.8% of the property value of buildings hit by a fire was preserved.
The decision has no financial impact.

The City is amending the framework agreement signed with Mission Unitaînés and the Office municipal d'habitation de Québec (OMHQ) for the construction of a 100-unit social and affordable housing building at 9165, boulevard Saint-Jacques.
The agreement provided for a financial contribution from the City of $4,861,124.68, authorized in September 2025.
The housing units are intended for self-sufficient seniors with low or modest incomes.
The amendment removes the clause that allowed the OMHQ to transfer its right to acquire the project and the land to another organization, such as the Société municipale d'habitation Champlain.
The OMHQ will therefore be the one to acquire the building and the land, which the City says it wants to clarify to avoid any ambiguity.
The matter must be decided by the urban agglomeration council of Québec, with a target date of September 16, 2026.
The City is transferring $5,000,000 from its unallocated agglomeration surplus as at December 31, 2025 to a reserve dedicated to social and affordable housing.
It is immediately using this $5,000,000 to fund the social, affordable and community housing program (item 38033 of the 2026-2035 investment plan).
The existing reserve, until now set aside for "social housing," is being renamed to also include "affordable housing."
The City says it wants to avoid borrowing to fund its share of these projects.
Goal restated in the document: 500 social and affordable housing units started per year.
The City contributes about 40% of what its financial partners pay (Société d'habitation du Québec, Desjardins, Fonds de solidarité FTQ, Maisons Canada).
Decision adopted by the urban agglomeration council on June 17, 2026.
The Ville de Québec is paying US$11,600 to renew its 2026 membership in the Organization of World Heritage Cities (OWHC).
The membership fee is going from US$10,800 in 2025 to US$11,600 in 2026; it was US$10,000 from 2021 to 2024.
The increase comes from a new calculation adopted by the OWHC, based on population and gross national income per capita, with a 20% cap on increases applied gradually in 2025 and 2026.
Membership fees will be indexed to inflation starting in 2027 and recalculated every 5 years.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de la coordination stratégique et relations internationales and falls under urban agglomeration jurisdiction.
The OWHC brings together more than 200 cities that have a site on the UNESCO World Heritage List; its head office is in Québec, in space lent by the City.
Mayor Bruno Marchand chairs the OWHC's board of directors, having been re-elected in Cordoba in September 2024.
The City is changing the planning rules for zone 22322Mb, located south of rue Lemieux, east of boulevard de Monaco, north of boulevard Père-Lelièvre and west of rue Darveau, in Duberger–Les Saules.
The maximum number of dwellings per building is removed; buildings are still limited to 3 storeys and the minimum and maximum heights are removed.

The front setback goes to 6 metres and the side and rear setbacks are adjusted according to the type of building, which makes several currently non-compliant buildings compliant and makes it easier to enlarge single-family homes and duplexes.
Retail stores, services and restaurants will be allowed on all floors, and the 750 m² limit for education and training establishments is removed.
Group projects (several main buildings on the same lot) are no longer allowed in the zone.
New requirement: provide an amenity area of 5 square metres per dwelling. Fibre cement panel is removed from the list of mandatory masonry materials.

For signs, the limit of three flags per lot and the requirement to install the sign on a base are removed. The conseil de quartier de Duberger–Les Saules will be consulted and the by-law may be subject to approval by referendum.
The Ville de Québec will pay $4,157,186 to the Communauté métropolitaine de Québec as its share for 2026.
The payment is made in three instalments: $1,385,728.66 on April 18, 2026, then $1,385,728.67 on July 1 and October 1, 2026.
In 2025, this share was $4,071,302.
The money comes from the general expenses budget, under the activity "Contribution à la Communauté métropolitaine de Québec".
City council adopted the decision on March 31, 2026.
The City is moving the stop sign at the intersection of rue Graham-Bell and avenue Branly, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The stop sign is being removed on avenue Branly, at the east approach to the intersection.
A new stop sign is being added on rue Graham-Bell, at the north approach to the intersection. It applies to drivers as well as cyclists.
The no-parking zone on the east side of rue Graham-Bell, starting at rue Frank-Carrel and going south, goes from 15 to 33 metres.
A second no-parking zone stays the same: 22 metres, starting 73 metres south of rue Frank-Carrel.
The Service du transport explains that the change follows the standards of the ministère des Transports, which place the stop sign on the secondary street at a "T" intersection.
The Ville de Québec is signing two agreements with Service national des sauveteurs inc. to receive money to reimburse registration fees for water safety training.
The amounts provided are $161,300 for 2024-2025 and $73,360 for 2025-2026.
The money comes from the ministère de l'Éducation program that makes training free for lifeguards and aquatic instructors.
The actual funding for 2024-2025 should have been $88,080, because there were fewer registrations than expected; the 2025-2026 amount was adjusted downward accordingly.
The 2024-2025 agreement had not been submitted to the executive committee at the time; the City is correcting the situation.
For 2025-2026, the City must carry out the activities no later than March 31, 2026, and submit its accountability documents no later than June 15, 2026.
The amounts received will be paid into the City's general fund.
The arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is authorizing five elected officials to attend the annual convention (Assises annuelles) of the Union des municipalités du Québec.
The event takes place from May 13 to 15, 2026, at the Centre des congrès de Québec.
The people authorized are chair Elainie Lepage, councillors Mélissa Coulombe-Leduc, Catherine Vallières-Rolland and Marylou Boulianne, as well as councillor Raymond Poirrier.
Registration fees are $890, plus applicable taxes.
Other expenses will be reimbursed upon submission of supporting documents, if they comply with by-law R.C.E.V.Q. 17.
The money comes from the borough's budget, under the activity "Soutenir les conseils d'arrondissement" (Supporting borough councils).
The City is granting a minor exemption for 3821, rue Le Corbusier, in the Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The vehicle entrance may be built right at the point where the front lines of the property meet, whereas the by-law requires a distance of 6 metres.
This exemption allows a single-family home to be built on the property.
Condition imposed: no tree or shrub may be planted in the visibility triangle, for safety reasons.

According to the analysis, the slope of the land toward the south and the irregular shape of the lot make the proposed location preferable; the Section de la mobilité et de la sécurité routière is in favour.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on February 10, 2026.
The City is adopting a loan by-law of $700,000 to create and enhance ecological corridors and the infrastructure that goes with them.
The loan is repayable over ten years, and the expense is shared between the urban agglomeration and local (proximity) jurisdictions.
The work aims to connect biodiversity cores through green spaces, bike corridors, hydroelectric rights-of-way, wooded areas, wetlands and waterways.
The planned work includes planting trees, shrubs and perennials, creating meadows and restoring natural environments.
The projects can take place anywhere in the territory under the City's jurisdictions.
The City will be able to acquire, by mutual agreement or by expropriation, the buildings and easements needed for the work.
An amount of $70,000 (10% of the expense) is being taken from the general fund and will be repaid when the by-law comes into force.
The City wants to allow up to three dwelling units per detached building in zone 31275Ha, in Sillery, instead of two at present.
The zone affected is located north of boulevard Laurier, south and east of boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, and west of rue du Parc-Gomin.
The change follows a request to bring into compliance a three-unit building at 2149-2155, boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, where the third unit has existed for a few years.
No work is planned on the building, and the other standards, including siting and height, stay the same.
The conseil de quartier de Sillery will be consulted and will hold the public consultation meeting.
The by-law contains no provision that can be subject to a referendum; adoption is targeted for September 15, 2026 at the city council.
The executive committee takes note of the report on real estate transactions from the Service du développement économique et des grands projets for the period from January 1 to March 31, 2026.
The report lists purchases of land and easements, sales, and temporary occupancies of public property, with the amounts and owners involved.

Several transactions are initial provisional compensation payments made as part of the tramway project (TramCité), notably on 1re Avenue: $915,000, $535,000, $436,000, $276,000, $150,900 and smaller amounts.
The City is buying parts of land to add sidewalks on rue de Rosewood ($3,000) and avenue Marcoux ($5,200), and for the rebuilding of rue de la Faune ($1,100).
The City is acquiring a piece of land (lot 1 045 195) for $590 in the context of conserving natural areas and wetlands.
The City is closing part of rue Triquet and selling it for $39,600 to private individuals in order to regularize the layout of their land.
The conseils de quartier de la Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy and du Plateau are each granted a temporary occupancy of public property for $10 for the citizen greening project "Jardins d'habitat".
The City wants to allow a business on the 2nd floor of 1061, route de l'Église, in the Saint-Louis neighbourhood (arrondissement Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge).
The unit in question is 62 square metres; the permitted uses would be administrative services (C1) or retail sales and services (C2).
This permission would be temporary: five years from the coming into force of the by-law.
Currently, the 2nd floor of buildings in this zone must be used only for housing; a hair salon left the unit in November 2025 and the owner considers that it does not convert well into housing.
The conseil de quartier de Saint-Louis will be consulted and will hold the public consultation meeting.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum; no additional public participation measures are planned.
The City indicates that a review of certain standards of the Programme particulier d'urbanisme du Plateau centre de Sainte-Foy will be carried out later.
The executive committee takes note of the list of additional expenses of over $250,000 authorized by delegated employees during the week of March 22 to 28, 2026.
Two change notices appear on it, for a total of $5,432,622 before taxes.

Culture and heritage: $5,162,622 for the 2026 indexation of the management contract with L'Institut Canadien de Québec for the Bibliothèque de Québec, from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028. The contract goes from $92,071,330.76 to $97,233,952.76.
Engineering: $270,000 to extend support to the contractor during the archaeology work on rue De Buade, after the discovery of new burial sites. The contract goes from $1,652,696.58 to $1,922,696.58.
The Service des approvisionnements publishes this list every week, taxes excluded.
The executive committee approves the dismissal of a detective sergeant from the Service de police de la Ville de Québec.
The dismissal is based on section 119 of the Loi sur la police.
The police officer appeared before a committee to answer for the facts alleged against him in the notice of summons.
The committee members heard his explanations before making a decision.
The director of the Service de police will have to send a letter to the employee to inform him of the decision.
The document does not name the person concerned or the alleged facts.
The City is awarding Services d'Infrastructures Vortex inc. (Boucherville) a contract worth $2,083,931.29 before taxes to rehabilitate drinking water pipes.
The work covers ten streets spread across five arrondissements, including avenue O'Neil, rue d'Hibernia, rue de Bercy, place des Noyers and avenue du Colonel-Jones.
The contract includes excavation, preparation, cleaning, video inspections of the pipes and restoring the sites to their original condition.
Two companies submitted bids; Vortex offered the lowest price, ahead of CoreAqua at $2,252,014.
The net cost to the City is $2,187,867.36, paid out of a loan by-law.
A clause allows the price to be adjusted based on the cost of fuel.
The City is putting ExpoCité in charge of managing the Centre multifonctionnel de curling de Québec, located at 1020, rue des Rocailles.
ExpoCité will be able to exercise there the powers set out in the City's Charter, including commercial operation.
The authorization also covers the landscaped grounds around the building.
Construction of the centre began in 2025 on land owned by the City, in preparation for the Canada Games of February 2027.
The building includes commercial spaces whose revenues are meant to reduce operating costs for the City after the 2027 Games.
The project had been added in May 2025 to the list of facilities of collective interest of the Québec urban agglomeration.
The Ville de Québec is signing an agreement with the minister responsible for the Capitale-Nationale region to receive $7M from the Government of Québec for its 2025 fiscal year.
This amount will go into the City's general fund.
The 2009 agreement provided for $12M per year starting in 2009, but the City has been receiving $7M per year since 2018.
Since April 2024, the government has required a new agreement to be signed each year before each payment.
The City states that signing this agreement does not mean it is giving up the amounts provided for in the 2009 agreement, and it is continuing its efforts to obtain these amounts in the coming years.
The City must submit an accountability report within four months after the end of its fiscal year and repay any unused portion.
The City is removing a parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility on rue De Rigauville, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The space is located in front of 166, rue De Rigauville, on the west side, between rue Chênevert and rue Saint-Ambroise.
A resident reported that this space was no longer being used; the City's checks confirmed this.
Parking along these 6 metres is therefore no longer reserved for vehicles with a disabled parking permit.
The conseil d'arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou adopted ordinance O-1587 on July 9, 2026.
The City is authorizing the construction of a building with about 36 housing units at 1853, boulevard Bastien, in Neufchâtel Est-Lebourgneuf, even though the zoning allows only three.
The building may have four storeys and a height of 15 metres, instead of three storeys and 11 metres, with 40 parking spaces instead of 43.

Following the public consultation of May 7, 2026, the City is adding one condition: the balcony railings on the east side will have to be frosted or opaque over at least 90% of their surface, to address neighbours' concerns about their privacy.
The deadline to start the project goes from 18 to 12 months after the resolution is adopted; otherwise the authorization lapses.

Other conditions imposed: at least 32 housing units, four units with three bedrooms or more, one heat pump per unit, a white roof on the 4th floor, 10 covered bicycle parking spaces, a 100-square-metre outdoor common area and 35 trees planted.
A dense 1.5-metre hedge or a fence that is 80% opaque must be installed along the west and east boundaries of the lot; the building must remain 15 metres from the south boundary.
Anyone who breaches the conditions faces a fine of $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (other cases), doubled for a repeat offence.

The City is authorizing phase 3 of the Etna-Nord project, in the Val-Bélair district (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles): extension of rue de l'Eldorado and rue des Éloges and the opening of a new street, over about 913 metres.
The project covers 115 new lots for 127 housing units: 21 detached single-family homes, 28 semi-detached homes, 60 townhouses and 6 lots for three-unit townhouse buildings.
The developer Investissements Val-Bélair inc. is carrying out the work; the total investment is more than $41M and the municipal infrastructure is estimated at $7.5M.

The City is investing $649,356.49 before taxes, namely $58,810 for the lot frontage intended for a park and a multi-purpose link, and $590,546.49 for channelling a ditch toward the bassin de rétention Émond. The net expenditure is $681,743.15.

The developer is transferring to the City free of charge the streets, a pedestrian walkway, land for a retention basin at the end of rue de l'Emblée (rue de l'Embargo: end of rue de l'Emblée), spaces to enlarge the park already transferred, as well as water main and sewer easements.
The Comité de commémoration et de toponymie will have to propose a name for the new street and for the retention basin.
City council adopted the decision on August 25, 2026 (resolution CV-2026-0689).

The City authorizes two document and archives management advisors, Marceline Daigle and Albane Pélisson, to attend the iPRES conference on digital preservation in Copenhagen, Denmark, from September 21 to 25, 2026.
Their mandate on site: to promote the iPRES 2027 conference and Québec as a tourist destination, notably with a booth and a handover at the closing ceremony.
Québec was chosen in November 2025 to host the iPRES 2027 conference, at Université Laval, from October 4 to 8, 2027.

The non-profit organization Congrès iPRES 2027 received a $21,500 grant from the Fonds pour soutenir le tourisme d'affaires international for the transportation, accommodation and registration of four directors, as well as a video and promotional items.
The transportation, accommodation and registration costs of the two employees will be paid by the organization Congrès iPRES 2027, upon presentation of supporting documents.
The document states that there is no financial impact for the Ville de Québec.
The council adopts a motion on sewer backups in the Chauveau area (Neufchâtel-Lebourgneuf district), which was hit by two such events during heavy rain since 2013.
The City has finished documenting the events (calls to 311 and claims) and the one-time work done: correcting a low-lying spot, disconnecting catch basins, video inspections and flow measurements.
A hydraulic study of the area is being finalized to diagnose the network and determine the improvements needed.
Upgrade work could follow; the City generally expects 3 to 5 years for this type of adjustment, subject to approvals and budget.
The City will continue to monitor the situation when heavy rain is forecast, with preventive measures such as installing temporary pumps.
The City commits to helping residents check that their backflow valves meet requirements; owners remain responsible for equipping and maintaining their homes.
Grant programs exist for backflow prevention devices and sump pumps.
The arrondissement de Charlesbourg is authorizing three elected officials to take part in the Assises annuelles of the Union des municipalités du Québec.
The event takes place from May 13 to 15, 2026, at the Centre des congrès de Québec.
The people concerned are chair Claude Lavoie, councillor Marie-Pierre Boucher and councillor Raphaël Lebailly.
The registration fee is $890, plus applicable taxes.
Other expenses will be reimbursed upon submission of receipts.
The money comes from the budget of the arrondissement de Charlesbourg, activity "Soutenir les conseils d'arrondissement" (Supporting borough councils).

The City is entrusting the organization Loisirs de St-Rodrigue inc. with the specialized maintenance and supervision of recreational and sports facilities and equipment in the Charlesbourg and Beauport boroughs.
The contract covers the period from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027, for $256,566.36 (plus GST and QST).
The agreement can be renewed twice for 12 months, with an annual price indexation.
The services cover outdoor skating rinks, sports fields and parks.
Charlesbourg is paying $200,218.16 and Beauport $69,144.45 (net of taxes) out of their operating budgets.
The contract was awarded without a call for tenders, under a provision of the Cities and Towns Act that allows this with a non-profit organization.
The amounts planned for 2027 depend on the adoption of that year's budget.
The City agrees to widen a pedestrian right-of-way servitude on a piece of land it owns in the arrondissement de Beauport (lot 1 739 464).
The Centre de services scolaire des Premières-Seigneuries built a pedestrian path that is wider than the 30 inches provided for since 1985.
The servitude will now cover the whole lot, that is 221.2 square metres, and this passage must remain free of any obstacle.
The path was built for student safety, as part of the construction of the new école des Grands-Bâtisseurs.
The passage will end if the school service centre sells its land or if the École secondaire de La Seigneurie loses its status as a recognized school.
The school service centre pays the notary, the publication fees and the municipal management fees; the City covers the review of the draft deed.
The servitude cannot be bought back for 30 years.
The City is granting a minor exemption for the commercial building at 5260-5266, boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, in Duberger-Les Saules (Arrondissement des Rivières).
The building will be allowed to cover 17% of the land instead of the minimum of 20% required by the borough's planning by-law.
This exemption makes it possible to split the current lot into two new lots (6 705 261 and 6 705 262).
According to the analysis, a refusal would have blocked the real estate transaction planned between the parties.
