The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on June 1, 2026; the new lots will be partly planted with vegetation in order to reach the minimum of 10% green space.
The City is adopting a new code of ethics and professional conduct for staff in political offices (employees appointed by the mayor or by a designated councillor).
This code replaces, without changes, the one adopted on February 21, 2022; the law requires the City to review its code before May 1 following a general election.
Political office staff cannot have an interest in a contract with the City, must declare their financial interests at a meeting, and must refrain from influencing the decision.
Any gift or hospitality worth more than $200 must be declared in writing to the city clerk within 30 days; the clerk keeps a public register.
Gifts from a supplier are prohibited, regardless of their value, as is the use of City resources for personal purposes.
For the 12 months following the end of their term, a political office staff member cannot hold a job that would give them an undue advantage related to their former duties.
The Commission municipale du Québec can impose a reprimand, training, the return of gifts or profits, or a penalty of up to $4,000, and can recommend a suspension of no more than 90 days.
The City of Québec is entrusting the organization Loisirs de St-Rodrigue inc. with carrying out the Liaisons jeunesse program in the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The program places community outreach workers with young people aged 12 to 25 in the parks and public spaces of districts 4-3 and 4-6, to encourage harmonious coexistence.
The agreement covers the period from May 1 to October 31, for 2026 and 2027.
The City will pay $52,952.69 per year (before GST and QST), an amount that will be adjusted according to the minimum wage in effect on May 1, 2027.
The total net expense is $111,187.42, taken from the operating budget of the arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The 2027 funding depends on the adoption of that year's budget.
The agreement was reached without a call for tenders, which the law allows with a non-profit organization; the previous agreement ended on October 31, 2025.
The City is paying $78,648 to three non-profit organizations for work on their buildings.
L'Autonhommie, Centre de ressources sur la condition masculine, is receiving $23,068 to convert offices into a multi-purpose room.
Le Café rencontre du centre-ville is receiving $15,580 to repair a damaged pipe.
Le Verger, Centre communautaire en santé mentale, is receiving $40,000 to redo the inside and outside of its building and improve universal accessibility.
The program can cover up to 80% of eligible costs, to a maximum of $80,000 per project.
Each organization receives 90% of the amount after the executive committee's decision, and 10% when the work is finished, upon submission of supporting documents.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3261, which covers work on buildings, parks and recreational facilities.
The City wants to obtain a permanent public utility easement on a piece of land bordering 1re Avenue, in the arrondissement of La Cité-Limoilou.
The easement covers about 31.70 square metres of part of lot 1 943 535.
It will be used to move public utility conduits and networks for the TramCité tramway project.
The City will try to reach an amicable agreement with the owner; otherwise, it will proceed by expropriation. The owner has already been informed and has been given the name of a resource person.
The Service des affaires juridiques will be able to drop the proceedings if the project no longer needs the easement.
The entire piece of land is assessed at $224,000 on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll, which works out to $297.32 per square metre.
The money comes from the agglomeration loan by-law for the Réseau structurant de transport en commun.
The City is obtaining from Université Laval the right to cross the campus in order to build, then operate and maintain the tramway (TramCité project), in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
Three rights are granted: a temporary servitude for the work, a perpetual servitude for operation, and a right of use to build and keep equipment there.
The City will pay $10,000,000 to Université Laval when the notarial deed is signed.
The pedestrian tunnel planned in the 2022 agreement is being dropped: the Université no longer wants it, and the related clauses are being removed.
Work on the campus can begin as early as 2026, and the parties are aiming for completion by the end of 2033 at the latest.
The notarial deeds establishing the servitudes and rights of use must be signed no later than December 31, 2026.
The City and Université Laval will share the notary and publication fees equally.
The City is awarding Environnement Routier NRJ inc. (Lachine) the contract for mechanized pothole repair on the territory of the city of Québec for spring 2026.
The contract covers the rental of five trucks with operators, starting on the date the contract is awarded.
The estimated amount of the contract is $281,000 (plus GST and QST); the net expense is estimated at $295,014.87.
The contract may be renewed for two additional years, with an annual price indexation.
Only one bid was received for public call for tenders 94737; it is 4.8% below the department's estimate ($295,050).
The funds come from the operating budget of the Service des travaux publics, roadway maintenance and repair activity.
The City is awarding Pavage S.M. inc. the contract to build paved speed humps for $864,960.40 before taxes.
The work covers 29 streets spread across the City's various arrondissements.
It includes milling and paving, road marking, traffic management during the work, permanent signage and surface repairs.
One of the humps, on rue Lockwell, is being built as part of the TramCité project.
The net cost to the City is $908,100.30, of which $888,150.30 comes from a grant from the ministère des Transports and $19,950 from the loan by-law tied to the tramway.
Three companies submitted bids; Pavage S.M. inc. submitted the lowest price, ahead of Pavage F&F inc. ($942,404) and P.E. Pageau inc. ($960,702).
The contract provides for price adjustments based on the cost of asphalt and fuel.
The City is bringing back temporary permits allowing the application of pesticides that are normally banned, after the transitional rules end on December 31, 2025.
These permits cover only infestations that threaten human or animal health, safety, the integrity of buildings, or the survival of trees, shrubs and hedges.
Temporary permits to treat lawns will no longer be granted, since they were mainly used for aesthetic reasons; in the event of a major infestation, the City may adopt an ordinance.
The permit is free, valid for a maximum of three months, and must be displayed in a visible way while the work is being done; at least seven days must separate each application.
Any accidental spill of a pest control product on an impermeable surface (street, private driveway) must be cleaned up without delay so it does not reach sewers, ditches and natural environments.
Contractors must keep their record of applications in the form of a digital database and send it by email no later than November 30 each year.
The City will refuse to issue the registration certificate to a contractor who already holds one and has not submitted all of their records.

The City is changing the planning rules for three zones in the Cité-Universitaire neighbourhood (district du Plateau), located south of chemin Sainte-Foy, east of autoroute Henri-IV and north of chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois.
In all three zones, the front setback for buildings will from now on be measured from the centre line of route de l'Église, with a depth of 14 metres.
The City justifies the 14 metres (rather than 16 as elsewhere along this route) by the narrower right-of-way of the road and the shallow depth of some lots.
In zone 32020Ha, the side setback goes from 2 to 3 metres and the specific standards for buildings with 4 or more dwelling units are removed; the rear setback becomes 7.5 metres for all.
The by-law contains provisions that may be subject to approval by referendum.

The conseil de quartier de la Cité-Universitaire is asked to give its opinion and to hold the public consultation meeting; citizens will have 7 days after that meeting to send in their comments in writing.
The arrondissement de Beauport is giving out $129,600 in grants to 23 organizations in its territory.
The money goes toward operating expenses of organizations recognized by the City.
The applications had been filed on February 20, 2026; some grants are the 2nd or 3rd year of support already under way.
The amounts range from $583 (Yoseikan budo Beauport) to $20,000 (Autisme Québec).
Among the organizations supported: Patro Le Pivot, Entraide Agapè, the Groupe d'éducation et d'écosurveillance de l'eau and the École de musique des Cascades de Beauport each receive $10,000.
The money comes from the operating budget of the arrondissement de Beauport.
The borough council adopted the decision on May 12, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 860, avenue de Gassicourt, in the quartier des Jésuites in Charlesbourg.
The house sits 5.93 metres from the front property line, while the planning by-law requires 6.0 metres: the 7-centimetre difference is now deemed to comply.
The request aims to regularize the situation as part of a sale of the property.
The difference dates back to an extension authorized by permit in 1992 and was noted during a surveyor's survey in 2020.
Without the exemption, part of the front of the house would have had to be demolished to meet the required setback.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme was unanimously in favour on August 12, 2026; no complaints from neighbours were reported.
The City is adding two mandatory stop signs on rue Évangéline, at the east and west approaches to the intersection with rue de la Sagouine, in Beauport.
Drivers and cyclists will now have to stop at these two approaches.
The stop sign already in place on rue de la Sagouine (south approach) stays in service: the "T" intersection will therefore be controlled in all directions.
Road markings at the intersection will be adjusted accordingly.
The City says it aims to make it easier for pedestrians to cross and to make travel in the area safer.
Rue Évangéline links avenue D'Estimauville to boulevard Monseigneur-Gosselin and is used by regular Réseau de transport de la Capitale routes.
The City is transferring the management of on-street parking permits: the urban agglomeration council will no longer approve the conditions for granting permits or the boundaries of permit zones.
Permits for residents, recreational vehicles, merchants, artists and car sharing will now fall under the borough councils.
Parking permits for workers will fall under the city council.
The urban agglomeration council keeps the responsibility of approving parking rules on the streets of the agglomeration network, including streets where permit or sticker holders have special rules.
The by-law sets a $60 fine for anyone who breaks the provisions of this section.
The appendices that identified the parking permit zones (XV and XV.0.1) are repealed.
The City is banning parking on rue du Printemps, rue de l'Ondée and rue de la Barrière, on the side of the central islands (green spaces), from November 15 to March 31.
On rue de la Barrière, the ban also applies to the east and west sides, starting about 90 metres north of avenue de Gaudarville up to the north end.
These three streets are located in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, district de Cap-Rouge–Laurentien.
The measure removes 51 parking spaces during the winter, or 17 per street.
The Service des travaux publics asked for the change because parked vehicles get in the way of snow removal equipment.
According to the document, the occupancy rate of parking spaces in this area is low.
The City is allowing an above-ground pool and an access platform in the front yard at 1805, côte du Verger, in the Sillery neighbourhood.
Normally, the zoning by-law of the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge arrondissement prohibits this kind of installation in a front yard.
The owner will have to comply with the standards on steep slopes and the areas around them for the location of accessory structures.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on August 11, 2026.
According to the analysis, the lot has an unusual shape: a steep slope, a right-of-way easement and a house set back from the street, which limits the other possible locations.
The analysis concludes that there is no significant impact on the neighbours, since an existing hedge in the front yard reduces the view of the pool.
The City is setting up a new pedestrian crossing on rue De Saurel, 77 metres north of rue Rochambeau, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The crossing will link the church parking lot to the main entrance of the école primaire d'éducation internationale Filteau.
Access to the church parking lot from this point will be reserved for pedestrians only.
The City says it wants to address the irregular manoeuvres seen near the school: double parking stops, U-turns and parking in no-parking areas.
The school's administration already encourages the use of the church parking lot as a drop-off area, with the church's agreement.
The decision falls under the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough council, La Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy district.
The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for $85,783 to maintain the Route verte on its territory in 2026-2027.
The maintenance project is estimated at $225,000, taxes included; the City covers the rest of the bill.
The Route verte has 69.1 km within the Québec agglomeration, 53.9 km of which are maintained by the City.
The funding cannot exceed 50% of eligible expenses, with maximums of $1,750 per km of bike path, $875 per km of bike lane or paved shoulder, and $60 per km of designated roadway.
The City commits to following the program's rules; otherwise, the financial assistance will be cancelled.
The Director of Public Works, Patrick Bastien, is authorized to sign the application and the agreement, co-signed by the city clerk.
If the project is accepted, a first payment of no more than 80% of the assistance will be made after the agreement is signed.
The City is sending three employees of the Service de la culture et du patrimoine on a mission to Bordeaux, France, from September 23 to 29, 2026.
The executive committee is authorizing an expense of $10,329 for travel and accommodation costs, reimbursable upon submission of receipts.
The ministère des Relations internationales et de la Francophonie is covering $6,450 of this amount; the rest comes from the City's operating budgets.
The mission is part of the "Faire culture ensemble" project between Bordeaux and Québec, funded up to $12,750 by the Fonds franco-québécois de coopération décentralisée.
The program of visits covers culture and urban transformation, social accessibility, resources, audience development (including youth) and environmental responsibility.
A cultural delegation from Bordeaux was welcomed in Québec in October 2025 as part of the same project.
A difference of no more than 10% from the authorized amount will be accepted without further authorization.
The City is reorganizing the Service de la gestion des équipements motorisés, which is responsible for buying and maintaining the municipal vehicle fleet.

It is abolishing the Division du soutien administratif et de l'efficacité opérationnelle and creating in its place a Direction en soutien aux affaires administratives, reporting to the service's management.
This new directorate will take charge of the service's budget and financial processes, as well as its information technology governance.
Administrative staff, currently spread across different units, will be brought together in the new directorate.
A vacant division director position is abolished and converted into a position of director in support of administrative affairs (class 3), which will be filled.
Two positions are being moved: an occupational health and safety technician to the Division de la maintenance véhiculaire, and an engineer to the service's management.
According to the document, these changes require no additional budget and no additional staff; the funds come from the service's operating budget.
The City is giving $21,000 to Patro Le Pivot for summer activities for youth aged 13 to 15, in the arrondissement de Beauport.
The money comes from the Programme Estival-Ado 2026, which funds recreational activities adapted for teenagers.
The program also lets some young people get a first taste of working as a day camp leader.
In 2025, 24 teenagers from Beauport took part; Patro Le Pivot is aiming for more than 24 in 2026, including two who need support.
The grant was $24,025 in 2025 and $25,500 in 2024.
Fifteen projects were selected across the city, including one in Beauport.
The funds come from the operating budget of the arrondissement de Beauport.
The City wants to obtain a permanent easement on a piece of land bordering 1re Avenue, in La Cité-Limoilou, for the TramCité tramway project.
The easement covers about 39.20 square metres of part of lot 1 943 429 and will be used to move public utility conduits and networks.
The City will negotiate with the owner, but may proceed by expropriation if no agreement is reached; the owner has already been informed and has a contact person.
The Service des affaires juridiques will handle the proceedings and may withdraw them if the project no longer needs the easement.
The Division de l'arpentage et de la géomatique will prepare the plans and the technical description.
The land is entered on the 2025-2026-2027 assessment roll at $228,000, or $231.07 per square metre.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the Réseau structurant de transport en commun.
The City is refusing to allow the demolition of the heritage house at 1737, rue William-Marsh, in the Saint-Émile village core.
The decision confirms the refusal issued on December 18, 2025 by the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec.
The owner and the firm Blanc Urbain Architecture had asked city council to review this refusal.
After the public notice, the City had received 7 objections to the demolition and 1 statement of support.
According to the second opinion paid for by the City, the building is not beyond saving and is not at risk of immediate collapse; its restoration is considered technically possible.
The project planned in its place, a traffic lane to make it easier for trucks to reach the neighbouring plant, is considered to have no value for the development of the area.
An estimate by the architect hired by the owner puts the restoration work at $1,092,000 before taxes; the firm doing the review mentioned about $900,000.

The Ville de Québec and the Association des pompiers professionnels de Québec inc. have agreed to change the schedule of the lieutenant-instructors working in training at the Service de protection contre l'incendie.
The new fixed schedule has been in effect since April 26, 2026, with workdays spread from Monday to Thursday or from Tuesday to Friday, depending on the team.
The instructors are divided into two teams (A and B) by the division chief, and no one may trade their schedule.
The City says it found that the previous schedule, a four-day rotation, did not meet the needs of the Division de la formation, recherche et développement.
The agreement is added to the collective agreement currently in force; the document mentions no financial impact.
The City approves the plans for a three-storey extension to the building at 2364-2380, avenue De Vitré, in the Maizerets neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The extension will be built in the side and rear yards of the building.
For the front part of the extension, the owner must use a pale beige fibre cement that matches the colour of the transom windows or the foundations of the existing building.
This condition is meant to blend in with the neighbouring buildings and to avoid too strong a contrast with the current building.
If the applicant does not meet this condition, the application is put on hold and the applicant will have to present another project at a later meeting.
The existing red brick front wall is kept; the comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on August 11, 2026.
The Arrondissement de Sainte-Foy/Sillery/Cap-Rouge is renewing the terms of two members of its planning advisory committee (comité consultatif d'urbanisme).
Jean-Louis Chamard and Serge Rousseau are reappointed as resident members of the borough.
Their terms run from April 8, 2026 to April 7, 2028, that is, two years.
No financial impact is indicated in the document.
The City is awarding two contracts for security and usher-signallers at events held at the ExpoCé site, from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2028.
Lot 1 (building guarding and security): Services de sécurité spécialisée S3-K9 inc., for an estimated amount of $724,485 before taxes.
Lot 2 (usher-signallers and security): 9300-4901 Québec inc. (Mckinnon), for an estimated amount of $887,750 before taxes.
The net expenditure is estimated at $1,612,235 and will be paid out of ExpoCé's operating budget.
The contract includes an option to renew for two 12-month periods, with annual price indexation.
Three bids were received for lot 1 and only one for lot 2; after negotiation, that supplier lowered its price from $914,000 to $887,750.
The amounts for 2027 and 2028 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets by the competent authorities.
The City is giving out $5,459 in grants to three organizations in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles.
Au jardin des Iris de Val-Bélair receives $309 to buy gardening equipment (wheelbarrow, pruning shears, hose and spray nozzle).
La Corporation d'astronomie de Val-Bélair receives $900 for its operating expenses (second year of the program).
L'Harmonie de Loretteville inc. receives $4,250 to buy a set of tubular bells.
The applications had to be submitted no later than March 15, 2026 under the Cadre de soutien aux organismes reconnus (support framework for recognized organizations).
The money comes from the borough's operating budget, under the "Soutien aux organismes" (support for organizations) line.

The executive committee authorizes the Service des approvisionnements to buy computer hardware and software from companies that do not have an establishment in Québec, Canada or a European Union country, for the Service des technologies de l'information.
Since a Government of Québec regulation enacted on March 6, 2025, this type of direct-award purchase requires prior authorization, no matter the amount, and even if it is paid by credit card.

Three companies are involved: SimsUshare (Illinois, United States) for the SimsUshare CTC Starter software, Cubic ITS (Texas, United States) for Synchro SIM Traffic, and Isla Collective Ltd (London) for a web platform that calculates greenhouse gases.
Each of the three contracts is between $0 and $33,000.
The reasons given are too short a time frame before a call for tenders for the first two contracts, and a single supplier for the third.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 6125, rue de l'Embellie, in the Saint-Émile neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The owner will be allowed to expand their semi-detached house to a depth of 14.2 metres, whereas the by-law limits it to 12.32 metres.
The project involves expanding the basement at the back to add a bedroom, with a covered patio on the ground floor.
According to the analysis, the current standard is suited to detached houses but leaves little flexibility for the area's semi-detached buildings.
The document states that the neighbour has already been informed of the project and that the opaque fence will be put back in place after the work.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme unanimously recommended the exemption on August 12, 2026.

The City is awarding the cleaning and sanitation of several municipal buildings to three companies, from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2030, with the possibility of a 12-month renewal and price indexation.

Conciergerie McKinnon inc. is awarded the Centre communautaire de la Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy ($266,368.83) and four libraries in La Cité-Limoilou: Collège-des-Jésuites, Saint-Albert, Saint-Charles and Marie-Claire-Blais ($489,621.72).

3559840 Canada inc. is awarded the Centre communautaire Claude-Allard ($276,781.83) and buildings in La Haute-Saint-Charles, including the Centre communautaire Saint-Émile and facilities in parc Réal-Cloutier ($433,787.43).
Entretien Costa (José Costa) is awarded the washroom building and the chapel in parc Victoria for $108,000.00.
The amounts are before GST and QST; the total net expense is $1,653,090.96, spread from 2026 to 2030.
The amounts from 2027 to 2030 depend on the adoption of the budgets for those years.
Lot 7 (bibliothèque Gabrielle-Roy and its temporary washroom building) is cancelled and will go back out to tender.
The Ville de Québec is paying $8,000 to the Institut d'administration publique du Québec (IAPQ) for 2026.
Of this amount, $3,000 is a contribution as an associate partner in the 2026-2027 program of activities.
The remaining $5,000 funds the organization of the Prix d'excellence de l'administration publique du Québec 2026.
The awards ceremony will take place on November 26, 2026, at the Centre des congrès de Québec.
The partnership agreement runs until March 31, 2027; the City pays within 30 days of receiving the IAPQ's invoice.
The City agrees to promote the awards on social media and to appoint a representative 60 days before the event to present an award.
The IAPQ must submit a report on the use of the grants no later than January 31 following the ceremony.
The City is awarding pavement repair work at various locations on its territory, until December 30, 2026.
Gilles Audet Excavation inc. is awarded the West sector ($787,712.50) and the Centre sector ($896,365.00), before taxes.
Groupe Colas Québec inc. is awarded the East sector ($903,455.00), before taxes.
The net cost to the City is estimated at $2,716,585.68.
Five bids were received for the West and Centre lots, and six for the East lot.
The amounts are estimates based on unit prices; the money will come from the public works operating budget and the PDI (Ten-Year Capital Works Program).
The executive committee takes note of the report on disciplinary measures and employment terminations imposed by the Service des ressources humaines between October 1, 2025 and March 31, 2026.
The report lists 26 measures in total, including one dismissal (manual worker, Loisirs, sports et vie communautaire) and one demotion (office employee, Finances).
The other measures are suspensions ranging from 1 to 20 days.
Manual workers account for 19 of the 26 measures, mainly at Travaux publics and Gestion des équipements motorisés.
Other areas are also affected: crossing guards, ExpoCité parking, firefighters, Affaires juridiques and Gestion du territoire.
The director of human resources may impose these measures under a delegation of powers and must report on them to the executive committee twice a year.
The City is awarding a contract to Béton préfabriqué Fortier inc., of Saint-Henri, to supply catch basins, manholes and other precast reinforced concrete parts.
The contract is worth $792,855.68 before taxes; the net cost to the City is $832,399.36.
The materials will be used for work on segment TW-03, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough, as part of the TramCité project.
Two companies submitted bids: Fortier ($792,855.68) and Béton Provincial ltée ($943,665.21). Both bids met the requirements.
The winning price is 24.5% below the City's estimate, which was $1,050,000.
The money comes from the loan by-law tied to the structuring public transit network.
The executive committee adopted the decision on March 11, 2026.
On July 17, 2026, the City submitted four applications for financial assistance to the Government of Canada, under the Fonds pour bâtir des collectivités plus fortes (direct delivery stream).

The projects submitted: the rebuilding of the municipal stadium, the « Le Boisé des voisins » project, a covered refrigerated skating rink with a service building at parc Duberger, and the rebuilding of the barrage Joseph-Samson.

The executive committee is confirming these submissions after the fact, since they were made before it gave its authorization because of the tight deadlines of the call for projects launched on June 26, 2026.
The submission deadline, first set for July 15, had been pushed back to July 20, 2026.
No immediate financial impact: submitting the applications does not commit the City to anything.
If any assistance is granted, it will reduce the share paid by the City; any funding agreement will have to be approved by the governing bodies.
The City is sending two employees to the "Velo-City" international cycling conference in Rimini, Italy, from June 15 to 19, 2026.
The trip also includes the June 15 exchange day of the Cities and Regions for Cyclists group, of which the City has been a member since 2026.
The City will reimburse up to $15,712.30 in expenses (registration, travel, accommodation, meals), which is $7,856.12 per person, upon submission of receipts.
The designated participants are Jean-Baptiste Maur and Thomas Harvey-Gasse; if they withdraw, David O'Brien and Jean-François Martel-Castonguay may replace them.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service de la planification de l'aménagement et de l'environnement.
Going over the authorized amount by up to 10% is accepted without further authorization.
The City also took part in the 2024 (Ghent) and 2025 (Gdansk) editions of this conference.
The City is authorizing Trudel Innovation inc. to carry out phase 1 of the redevelopment of the Les Galeries Charlesbourg site, in the Saint-Rodrigue district in Charlesbourg.
The developer will extend 42e Rue Est and 2e Avenue Est by about 255 metres.

The overall project calls for 6 new buildings, about 1,500 rental units and 20,000 square metres of non-residential space; phase 1 provides services for 583 rental units and 4,554 square metres of commercial space.
Private investment in phase 1 is estimated at $175M, and the City is not contributing any funding to it.
The developer will receive an annual tax credit for its infrastructure expenses, estimated at $3,110,000 before taxes; the credit is valued at $2,647,000 before taxes.
The City will receive the streets, infrastructure and easements free of charge once the work is accepted; the transfer of land for a park will come in the following phases.
Construction of the overall project is to extend until 2035.
The executive committee takes note of the twice-yearly reports from the Service de la gestion des immeubles on work accepted on a provisional or final basis.
These reports are required twice a year, by June 30 and by December 23 at the latest, because the power to accept the work is delegated to the managers of the Service.

The June 2026 report lists provisional acceptances, including the covered skating rink and the services pavilion at parc Victoria ($7,910,994.43) and the covered skating rink at parc Bon-Pasteur ($6,917,979.69).
It also lists final acceptances, including the rebuilding of the parking lot at place Jacques-Cartier ($11,463,860.20) and several work packages for the new police headquarters.
The work covered involves swimming pools, community centres, libraries, parks and fire stations in several arrondissements.
No new spending is authorized: the document only takes note of work already under contract.
The Ville de Québec is entering into agreements with three organizations to help fund the 2026 Canadian Urban Forest Conference.
The Fédération canadienne des municipalités (Fonds municipal vert) and Université Laval are each contributing $10,000 in sponsorship (Pillar package).
Collectif Canopée is renting a single booth for $1,250, plus taxes.
The city is collecting a total of $20,953.50, after taxes on the value of the tickets provided.
The conference takes place from October 13 to 16, 2026, at the Centre des congrès de Québec.
The city is responsible for organizing, running the logistics of, and funding the event, under its agreement with Arbres Canada.
Other sponsorship agreements could be signed in the following weeks.
The Ville de Québec is giving up to $150,000 to Théâtre Périscope to set up the Centre SAS (services aux artisans de la scène).
The Centre SAS will pool resources, equipment and specialized services for Québec City's creators, workers and cultural organizations.

The project costs $220,522 in total: $150,000 from the City, $50,122 from the organization, $15,000 from the Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec and $5,400 from Culture Capitale-Nationale et Chaudière-Appalaches.
The project is planned in two phases: a pilot project from July 2026 to June 2027, then a growth phase from July 2027 to June 2028.
The project's home base is in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou; the record indicates 3 jobs created, in addition to the 11 current jobs.
The money comes from the Fonds régions et ruralité, under the Soutien aux projets structurants pour améliorer les milieux de vie component.
The City is awarding Conseils Aliova inc., of Montréal, a professional services contract worth $844,580 (before GST and QST).
The contract runs from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2030, with an option for two 12-month renewals and an annual adjustment based on the Consumer Price Index.
The firm is to support the City in implementing infrastructure data modelling (BIM) for the design, construction and maintenance of civil infrastructure.
The required team includes a senior BIM expert as project lead, two BIM managers, a coordinator/modeller and an information management specialist.
The net expense, after the QST refund, is estimated at $886,703.43; including the two option years, the estimated amount before taxes reaches $1,266,870.
Only one bid was received; its price is 5.6% above the $800,000 estimate from the requesting department, after being negotiated downward.
The amounts for the years 2027 to 2030 remain conditional on the adoption of the budgets by the appropriate authorities.
The City is adding two mandatory stops on rue Teillet, at the north and south approaches to the intersection with rue Roméo-Vachon.
The requirement applies to drivers as well as cyclists.
Until now, only the west approach to this "T" intersection had a stop.
The analysis concludes that the shape of the intersection and the slope of rue Teillet prevent a driver stopped on the west side from seeing a vehicle coming from the north.
The change affects the Saint-Louis-Sillery district, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The process began with a request from a resident; the borough council adopted ordinance O-784 on August 27, 2026.
The City is granting a minor exemption for a future building at 3037, rue William-Stuart, in the Saint-Louis neighbourhood (Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough).

The building may be built 4.8 metres from the front property line (measured at the garage) instead of the 6.0 metres required by the planning by-law; the front wall of the main building will be 5.7 metres away.
A sewer pipe in the back yard and an easement that prohibits building over it reduce the buildable area of the lot, which is why the building is being moved closer to the street.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme said it was in favour of the request on March 10, 2026, unanimously.
According to the analysis, the 5.7-metre distance matches how the other buildings in the area are set out.
No financial impact is indicated in the file.
The City is awarding a contract of $332,500 (before taxes) to L.S.M. Son et Lumières inc., of Québec, for a new audio distribution system at the Centre Vidéotron (multipurpose amphitheatre).
The contract includes supplying the equipment, installing it, configuring it and putting it into service.
The system replaces the current one, which has reached the end of its useful life, and will be used to manage and broadcast sound in the targeted areas of the amphitheatre.
The request came from ExpoCité; four companies submitted bids and all four bids were compliant.
L.S.M. submitted the lowest price, 18.4% below the department's estimate of $407,716; the other bids ranged from $391,700 to $479,136.17.
The money comes from the "Pérennité Centre Vidéotron" financial reserve; the expense falls under the urban agglomeration and the taxes are 100% recoverable.
The executive committee adopted the decision on August 26, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-1082).
The Ville de Québec is granting a total of $310,000 in support to S-QUAD Sports International for the 2026 "Challenge Cap Québec" triathlon.
This support breaks down into an $80,000 cash grant, free municipal services of up to $205,000, and the purchase of goods and services of up to $25,000.

The event will take place from June 26 to 28, 2026, with swimming in the bassin Louise, cycling on the autoroute Dufferin-Montmorency and the corridor du Littoral, and running in the parc linéaire de la Rivière-Saint-Charles.
Four courses are offered this year instead of three: a new R226 course is being added (3.8 km swim, 180 km bike, 42.2 km run), which can be completed as a team.
Athletes pay to take part; free activities are offered to families and visitors on the docks at Espace 400.
The $80,000 grant will be paid in two instalments: $72,000 in 2026 and $8,000 in 2027, subject to the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The support is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners; the event's total planned budget is $1,201,000. In 2024 and 2025, the support had been $100,000 each year.
The Ville de Québec is signing an agreement with the municipality of Sainte-Pétronille to give young people aged 21 and under who live there access to its arenas.
The sports covered: figure skating, speed skating, ringuette and broomball, in the arenas of the six arrondissements or an affiliated arena.

Sainte-Pétronille pays the City based on the number of young people registered: $926 per person aged 5 to 21 for a full season ($463 for a half-season) and $460 for those under 5 ($230 for a half-season).
The municipality has 60 days to pay the invoices, which are sent no later than the 3rd Friday of October (fall) and the 3rd Friday of February (winter).
The agreement lasts nine months, from August 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027, and renews automatically unless written notice is given at least 3 months before it ends.
If spots are limited, young people living in Québec come before those from Sainte-Pétronille.
The City may review the rates each year; any increase applies on the August 1 following the notice to the municipality.
LS2026-005.pdf.montantPrincipal: $926 plus taxes, if applicable, per person

puces: The executive committee takes note of the Service de l'ingénierie's semi-annual report on work accepted, provisionally or definitively, between two periods of the year.

The June 2026 report lists 21 work sites accepted provisionally, including the redevelopment of rue Saint-Vallier Ouest ($24,685,469.11), the D'Estimauville storm sewer collector – Phase 2 ($30,045,000.05) and the redevelopment of 4e Avenue – Phase II ($10,981,972.90).
It also lists 13 work sites accepted definitively, including the redevelopment of place de l'Hôtel-de-Ville ($17,931,551.27) and the rebuilding of the infrastructure on 18e Rue ($6,286,891.49).
The contractors involved include Charles-Auguste Fortier, Les Excavations Lafontaine, Groupe Colas Québec, Construction et Pavage Portneuf and P.E. Pageau.
Holdbacks are indicated for some contracts, for example $45,990 for the relocation of the networks on 4e Avenue.
The decision has no financial impact; the power to accept this work is already delegated to the Service de l'ingénierie, which must report on it no later than June 30 and December 23.

The City authorizes its Service des approvisionnements to buy computer hardware and software from companies that have no place of business in Quebec, Canada or the European Union, for the Service des technologies de l'information.

A Government of Quebec regulation enacted on March 6, 2025 requires cities to obtain prior authorization from the city council for this type of by-mutual-agreement contract, with no value limit, including purchases made by credit card.
The regulation covers computer hardware and software, medical supplies and equipment, pharmaceutical products and scientific instruments.
The company covered by this authorization is Dropbox, Inc., based in San Francisco in the United States, for a computing and hosting service.
The contract with Dropbox is valued at between $0 and $33,000 and will be paid by purchasing card.
The reason given: replacing the current solution would require a long-term project.
The City is designating the boulevard Laurier area, between route de l'Église and Université Laval, as a major construction zone for 2026.
Businesses in this area will be able to apply for financial assistance provided under the support program tied to the TramCité project work.
The work covered runs approximately from April 1, 2026, to December 31, 2026.
The 2026 fiscal year is the one that qualifies businesses located in the designated area for the assistance.
A plan attached to the order sets out the boundaries of the designated area and the area of influence.
To be recognized, the work must last at least three consecutive months and seriously disrupt traffic.
The Ville de Québec is receiving $2,152,744 from the federal government to enforce the rules on short-term rentals.
The money covers the years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027; the federal program went from three years to two years, which forced the City to revise its budget.
The grant will be used to hire additional staff to better control illegal tourist accommodation on its territory.
The executive committee is ratifying the agreement signed on March 19, 2026 by councillor Marie-Josée Asselin (replacing the mayor) and the city clerk Julien Lefrançois.
The director of the Division du contrôle du milieu, David Dionne, is authorized to sign the reports to be submitted to the federal Minister of Infrastructure and Communities.
The Gouvernement du Québec authorized the signing of the agreement by order in council on March 11, 2026.
The City is refusing a request for minor exemptions for 3270, rue Saint-Victorien, in Beauport (Vieux-Moulin neighbourhood, Robert-Giffard district).
The owner wanted to build a garage attached to the house and expand the building above it.
The owner was asking for a side setback of 0.9 metre instead of the required 1.2 metres, and a combined side yard width of 4.1 metres instead of 4.8 metres.
Reason for the refusal: the by-law does not cause serious harm to the owner.
Another reason: the house can be expanded while complying with the current regulations.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme of Beauport had unanimously recommended the refusal on February 19, 2026.
The Ville de Québec wants to borrow $3,400,000 to replace end-of-life vehicles of the Service de police.
The money will be used to buy and modify vehicles (gas-powered and electric), trailers, specialized equipment and accessories, as well as the necessary software and systems.
The amount also covers professional and technical services contracts and the hiring of the staff needed for these purchases.
The loan will be paid back over five years, out of the City's general revenues.
Up to $340,000 (10% of the expense) will be taken from the general fund, then paid back when the by-law comes into force.
The expense falls under the agglomeration of Québec and is planned from 2026 to 2030 in the 2026-2035 capital works program.

The City is entrusting Centre Musical Québec Plus inc. with organizing at least eight concerts in the summer of 2026, on the stage at parc Roland-Beaudin, in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The contract is worth $130,000 (plus GST and QST) and covers the period from February 1 to November 30, 2026.
Taking into account the QST refund, the net cost to the City is estimated at $139,633.38.
The organization takes care of the programming, artists' fees, technical production, stage setup, rentals, promotion and evaluation of the concerts.
The programming will be developed with the Service de la culture et du patrimoine, taking into account citizens' comments, artists' availability and the budget, then submitted to the borough council.
No call for tenders was issued: the law allows this type of contract to be awarded directly, without a call for tenders, in the artistic or cultural field.
The City is granting a minor exemption for 803, rue des Noisetiers, in the Lac-Saint-Charles neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The decision makes a deck compliant even though it sits 0.29 metres from the left side property line, while the by-law requires 0.50 metres.
It also makes a spa compliant even though it sits 0.70 metres from that same line, instead of the minimum of one metre.
The deck and the spa already exist: the request serves to make their location official.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a favourable opinion on the request on April 29, 2026, noting that the gap from the standards is small and that the spa is surrounded by a privacy screen.
The document specifies that a deck and a spa do not require a permit, and that the spa, which holds less than 2,000 litres, is not covered by the provincial regulations on swimming pools.
The City will pay $404,423.78 to Collectif Canopée to plant and maintain 1,800 trees on private (non-municipal) land in Québec.
This amount covers half the cost of the project, estimated at $808,847.55; the property owners who benefit will also have to contribute financially.
The money will be paid in four instalments: $202,211.89 at the start, then $101,105.95, $80,884.76 and $20,221.18 after the reports are accepted.
Collectif Canopée must submit a progress report on July 31, 2026 and a final report no later than December 31, 2026.
The City was aiming to plant 130,000 trees by 2029; since 75% of the territory is not municipal, it is going through this organization.
Collectif Canopée, created in 2022 by AF2R, CRE Capitale-Nationale and Agiro, had planted 2,300 trees in 2023 and 4,300 trees in 2024-2025 with the City's support.
The funds come from a loan by-law tied to the climate transition and action plan.
The City is granting a minor exemption at 6857, rue du Chénas, in the Saint-Émile neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The owner may build a solarium in the back yard, on the existing porch, without meeting the siding requirement.
The planning by-law normally requires that at least 40% of the secondary front façade be covered with a prescribed material; this requirement will not apply here.
The lot is on a street corner, which means the solarium is located in the secondary front façade.
The vinyl siding on the building and on most of the neighbouring houses is grandfathered.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme voted unanimously in favour of the request on August 12, 2026.
The City is extending Marc De Koninck's contract as a consulting expert with the Direction générale until June 30, 2027.
His hourly rate stays at $59.54.
He is granted a bank of up to 1,000 hours for the period from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
He will advise teams on files related to the Plan d'urbanisme et de mobilité, the environment, biodiversity and housing.
The funds, including employee benefits, come from the land use planning and coordination budget.
The executive committee adopted the decision on July 2, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0944).
The Ville de Québec is buying a piece of land of about 137 square metres alongside route de l'Église, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The agreed price is $94,400, plus taxes, paid to Eddy Gaudreault and to the company Les Immeubles Lambert Dubé s.e.n.c.
This amount includes compensation of $8,800 for claims, damages, inconveniences, costs and interest.
The purchase is for the redevelopment of route de l'Église, between chemin Saint-Louis and rue de Valmont, to improve mobility.
Once the purchase is completed, the City will open part of the right-of-way of route de l'Église and chemin Saint-Louis on this land.
The money comes from loan by-law R.V.Q. 3325 covering bicycle path and pedestrian path work.
The City will be able to inspect the land (soil, water, wetlands) within 120 days after the promise to sell is accepted.

The City is authorizing a civil engineering technician from the Service de l'ingénierie to attend the Association des transports du Canada conference and exhibition in Winnipeg, from October 4 to 7, 2026.
The trip is authorized for an expense of $3,555.50, taken from the operating budget of the Service de l'ingénierie.
The Service des finances will reimburse the expenses upon submission of supporting documents, with a tolerated variance of no more than 10% of the authorized amount.
Ville de Québec has been named the winner of the Association's 2026 Technology Achievement Award for its project identifying frost heaves using 3D surveys (LiDAR).
The award will be presented at a ceremony on October 4 in Winnipeg; the City must confirm its attendance by August 4 at the latest.
The Arrondissement des Rivières is granting a minor exemption for 1750, rue Careau (quartier Duberger–Les Saules), for the construction of an 8-storey residential building with underground parking.
The exemption reduces the depth of the visual screen to 4 metres instead of 15 metres and allows a ground coverage rate of 10% instead of the minimum of 20%.
The underground parking will extend below ground level into the visual screen; according to the developer, a clay layer of about 15 m and a high water table prevent traditional foundations.

Condition: build a vegetated mound at least 2 metres high within the visual screen, planted with trees, along the neighbouring residential lots, according to the plans by Stantec experts-conseils ltée dated March 24, 2026.
Condition: plant at least 73 of the 108 required trees before the phase 1 permit expires.
The minimum ground coverage rate would be reached during a 2nd phase of expansion of the building.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme gave a unanimous favourable opinion on May 4, 2026.
The City will pay $108,500, plus taxes, to Santé Québec (CIUSSS de la Capitale-Nationale) for an easement on its land on boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest.
This permanent easement covers about 1,091.7 square metres and will be used for the power and telecommunication lines of Hydro-Québec, Vidéotron and Bell.
Moving these networks is required in order to build the tramway (TramCité project) in this area.
Since the relocations are done at its request, the City pays the costs and compensates the owners, under the framework agreement with Hydro-Québec.
Once the notarized deeds are signed, the City will drop the expropriation process it had started for this land.
The money comes from loan by-law R.A.V.Q. 1342 related to the structuring public transit network.
The City is buying LED light fixtures to light streets and public parking lots.
The contract goes to Lumen, division de Sonepar Canada inc., located on avenue Watt in Québec.
The estimated value of the contract is $247,453.50 before taxes; the net expense is estimated at $259,795.24.
Three companies submitted bids and all three were compliant: Lumen ($247,453.50), Franklin Empire ($250,500) and Lumisolution ($254,059.50).
Lumen offered the lowest price, 2.0% below the requesting department's estimate ($242,500).
The executive committee approved the decision on April 15, 2026 (resolution CE-2026-0481).
The City is officially closing part of the right-of-way of avenue Turcotte, namely the start of rue Laperrière, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
The land involved measures 464.5 square metres (part of lot 1 944 133).
For more than 10 years, this section has served as a pedestrian link between the residential neighbourhood and the businesses on rue Soumande.
In practice, it is neither cleared of snow nor open to car traffic; the decision legally confirms this situation.
The land is not listed on the assessment roll, since it is part of a street right-of-way lot.
The plan and technical description were prepared by land surveyor Éric Demeule on December 15, 2025.
The Ville de Québec is paying $950,000 (plus taxes) to the Centre de services scolaire de la Capitale for the multi-sport artificial turf field at École secondaire de Neufchâtel.
In exchange, the City gets 800 hours of use per year for 12 years, for a total of 9,600 hours.
The City will be able to book the artificial turf field two weekday evenings (6:30 p.m. to 11 p.m.), on Saturdays and Sundays during the school year, and as a priority during the summer.
Three beach volleyball courts will also be made available to residents, with the same use priorities.
Municipal activities at the site are to begin in the spring of 2026, after the agreement is signed.
The field, in use since September 2024, cost $5.3M: $2.9M from the Gouvernement du Québec, $1M from the school service centre and $0.35M from Desjardins.
The payment is made in 2026, but the expense is spread over 12 years at $83,115.10 per year, subject to approval of the 2027 to 2037 budgets.
The arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles is allowing three organizations to hold street fundraising drives in the fall of 2026.
October 3, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.: Chevaliers de Colomb du conseil du Lac St-Charles, at the intersection of rue Jacques-Bédard and avenue du Lac-Saint-Charles.
October 17, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.: Comité paroissial de St-Émile, at the intersection of avenue Lapierre and rue de la Faune.
October 24, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.: Chevaliers de Colomb du conseil de Montcalm, at the intersection of boulevard de L'Ormière and rue Blain.
The fundraising drives will take place rain or shine.
The money raised will go towards Christmas baskets and food assistance in the Lac-Saint-Charles, Saint-Émile and Loretteville areas.
The Service de police and the Centre de gestion de la mobilité intelligente will provide monitoring on the days of the fundraising drives.
The City is awarding a $137,780 contract (plus GST and QST) for a specialized technology service, requested by the Service des technologies de l'information together with the Service de police.
The contract lasts 36 months, from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2029.
The service includes technical phone support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, as well as software and system updates.
The supplier's identity and the nature of the agreement remain confidential: the City cites public safety and the Loi sur les contrats des organismes municipaux to avoid an open call for tenders.
The amounts for 2027 to 2029 depend on the adoption of those years' budgets.
The director of the Service des approvisionnements is authorized to sign the contract documents.
The City is banning parking along 10 metres on the south side of rue du Roi, just east of boulevard Langelier, from November 15 to March 31.
The goal: to let snow removal equipment through, as its passage was being blocked by parked vehicles.
One 60-minute parking space (9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday) is being removed, including for holders of the zone 14 permit during the winter.
The rest of the stretch, between these 10 metres and rue Saint-Anselme, keeps the 60-minute limit on weekdays, except for vehicles with a zone 14 permit.
The request came from the Service des travaux publics; the change affects the Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur neighbourhood, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The City is extending the no-parking-at-any-time zone on the north side of rue Bourdages, in the arrondissement des Rivières (district Vanier-Duberger).
The at-any-time ban will now start 397 m west of rue Isabelle-Aubert, instead of 452 m, and run to boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel.
The zone where only recreational vehicles are banned between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m. goes from 210 m to 155 m.
About eight parking spaces will be removed.
The change is intended to improve visibility in the curve across from 1215, rue Bourdages, which residents raised at a street workshop held last September.
The problem affects in particular vehicles leaving the parking lot at 597, boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel by way of the rue Bourdages access.
The City is giving $500 to each of five organizations, for a maximum total of $2,500, so they can offer free activities on Monday, May 18, 2026, the day of the Journée nationale des patriotes.
Centre Mgr Marcoux inc. is offering zumba, yoga, soccer and psychomotor activities for ages 0-5, from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m., at the Centre communautaire Monseigneur-Marcoux.
Groupe Plein Air Faune inc. is offering archery and an activity about fur-bearing animals, from 12:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m., at the Base de plein air de Sainte-Foy.
Loisirs Duberger-Les Saules inc. is holding zumba, trampoline, cardio-weight training and yoga, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., at the J.-B.-Lafrance and Duberger community centres.

Loisirs du Faubourg inc. is organizing a motor skills course, badminton, pickleball, soccer, basketball, cardio-cycling, yoga, fencing and a treasure hunt, from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., at the Centre communautaire Lucien-Borne.
Patro Le Pivot is presenting storytelling and interactive theatre, a historical treasure hunt, music and traditional dance, from 12 p.m. to 3 p.m., at the Centre de loisirs Pavillon Royal.
The activities and schedules may change before they take place, depending on the organizations' constraints.

The Ville de Québec is paying $2,100,000 to Carrefour international de théâtre de Québec inc. to produce and present the play "Où tu vas quand tu dors en marchant...?" in 2026 and 2027, that is $1,050,000 per year.
The agreement covers January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027, with an option to renew for 24 months.
The free, walking-tour show will be presented in the Saint-Sauveur neighbourhood in both years.
In 2026, there will be nine performances: May 28, 29, 30 and 31, then June 4, 5, 6 and 7. Six in the evening (9 p.m. to 11 p.m.) and three during the day (3 p.m. to 5 p.m.).
The 2027 dates will be set no later than October 31, 2026.
At least 75% of the artists and staff must live in Québec.
The contract is awarded without a call for tenders, which the law allows for contracts in the artistic or cultural field. The 2027 amounts still have to be approved in the budget.
The City is creating a loading zone on rue du Cuivre, in Charlesbourg (district des Monts), on the west side, between rue de l'Argon and the north end of the street.
The loading zone is reserved for road vehicles from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday.
The zone begins 27 metres north of rue de l'Argon and extends for 25 metres.
Four on-street parking spaces disappear during these hours.
The change follows a request from a manager at the company Concetti Design inc., at 660, rue de l'Argon, who says that parked vehicles interfere with the delivery and receiving of goods.
The City is giving $7,000 in grants to two organizations in the La Cité-Limoilou borough for winter 2026 events.
Centre Mgr Marcoux inc. receives $3,000 for its "Fête hivernale," on Saturday, January 31, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. at parc Bardy (indoors in case of bad weather).
On the program: introduction to skating and snowshoeing, a choir, a youth show, eisstock, a sugar shack, a snack bar, hot chocolate and coffee.

Limoilou en vrac receives $4,000 for "Le loup, le lièvre et la tortue," formerly "Festi-glisse": on February 7 from noon to 5 p.m. at Place Limouloise, and on February 8 from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. at parc de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres, rain or shine.
On February 7, family activities come before the Carnaval de Québec parade starting at 5:30 p.m.; on February 8, tube sliding, snow sculpture, fat biking, a fire pit and a food truck.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget; the City is also providing technical support depending on available resources.
The City is giving $2,500 to the organization L'Engrenage Saint-Roch to organize the "Cabane à sucre de Saint-Roch".
The event takes place on Tuesday, April 14, 2026, from 11:30 a.m. to 2 p.m., on the forecourt of the église Saint-Roch and on rue Saint-François Est, in La Cité-Limoilou.
In case of bad weather, the activity moves inside the church.
On the program: maple taffy on snow, traditional music, dancing, a spoon-playing workshop, food, games and social activities.
The grant goes from $2,000 in 2025 to $2,500 in 2026, because of the rise in the cost of maple products.
The City is also providing technical support, depending on available resources; police and firefighters are in favour of holding the event.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The City is banning right turns on a red light on 57e Rue Ouest, west approach, at the intersection of boulevard de l'Atrium, from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.
On avenue De Gaulle, north approach, at the intersection of rue de Nemours, the ban on right turns on a red light changes from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. to a ban at all times.
These changes affect the arrondissement de Charlesbourg, district de Saint-Rodrigue.
The bans protect pedestrian crossings equipped with audible signals for people with a visual impairment.
At the Atrium intersection, the audible signal is a first-generation model (7 a.m. to 10 p.m.); at De Gaulle, the device has been replaced with a model that works at all times.
The missing signs will be added at the Atrium intersection and changed at the De Gaulle intersection.
The City is giving out $7,500 in grants to three Charlesbourg organizations for neighbourhood festivals in the fall of 2026.
Patro de Charlesbourg inc. receives $2,500 for the "Grande fête du Patro," on Saturday, September 5, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at the Patro de Charlesbourg.
Loisirs de St-Rodrigue inc. (Loisirs Flambo) receives $3,000 for the "Fête des récoltes Bourg-Royal," on Saturday, September 12, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at parc du Bourg-Royal.
Les Loisirs Bourassa inc. receives $2,000 for the "Fête de quartier Loisirs Bourassa," on Saturday, September 12, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. at parc de la Terrasse-du-Bon-Air.
All three events offer free family activities: inflatable games, a fair, face painting, entertainment, shows, a corn roast and food.
The City is also providing technical support, depending on available resources; the police and fire departments are in favour of the events being held.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The arrondissement de Beauport is banning trucks and tool-vehicles from the streets of the Vieux-Bourg neighbourhood at all times, except for local deliveries.
The area covered is bounded by rue Seigneuriale, avenue Royale and autoroute Félix-Leclerc (A-40), in the district de Robert-Giffard.

Before, the rules varied from street to street: traffic was allowed on most streets, banned on avenue du Cénacle, rue Deauville and rue Langevin, and banned from 6 p.m. to 7:30 a.m. Monday to Friday on rue Labelle.
The City is making the rules uniform because the differences between streets were causing confusion among truck drivers and among the people who enforce the regulations.
The borough council is adopting ordinances O-474 and O-475, which amend Schedule X of the Beauport by-law on traffic and parking.
The arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge is officially banning right turns on a red light on avenue Notre-Dame, on the east and west approaches to the intersection with route de l'Aéroport.
The ban applies from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, to drivers as well as cyclists.
The intersection is in the school corridor of école primaire Trois-Saisons, where a crossing guard helps schoolchildren cross.
The signs have already been in place for several years, but they had never been approved by the borough council.
The decision brings the situation into line by adding the ban to the borough's traffic and parking by-law.
The City is authorizing five fundraising drives on public roads in 2026, at specific intersections approved by the municipal departments.
Fondation Mira: September 19, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., to fund the training of assistance dogs ($35,000 per dog).
Club Kiwanis de Québec: September 26, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., to provide winter clothing for 1,000 elementary school children.
Société de Saint-Vincent de Paul ("Noël des enfants"): November 5, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m., with funds shared among the elementary and high schools in the area.
Moisson Québec ("Guignolée des médias"): December 3, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m., to buy food that is redistributed to organizations in the region.
Centre de pédiatrie sociale de Québec: December 12, 2026, from 11:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., to follow up with more children and develop support services.
The City is covering $13,250 in municipal services: $500 for Mira, $750 for Saint-Vincent de Paul, and $4,000 each for Kiwanis, Moisson Québec and the Centre de pédiatrie sociale.
The City is changing the parking rules on rue Charles-Henri-Dorval, in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge (district du Plateau).
The RTC has changed the route of bus line 13: buses now travel on Charles-Henri-Dorval instead of rue Toussaint-Dussault.
A bus stop has been added on each side of the street, near avenue du Chanoine-Scott.

On the north side, over 28 metres starting from avenue du Chanoine-Scott, and on the south side over 20 metres, stopping becomes prohibited at all times, except for buses and RTC on-demand transit vehicles.
Further west, alternating parking remains: prohibited from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays on the north side, and on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays on the south side.
Five parking spaces are being removed on this street.
The arrondissement de Charlesbourg is giving out $15,400 in grants to four organizations for neighbourhood events in the summer of 2026.
“Quartier en fête” receives $3,100: on June 6, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., at the Maison des jeunes L'Intégrale, with free food, inflatable games and shows.
The “Fête du voisinage Loisirs du Trait-Carré” receives $3,300: on June 6, from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m., at parc Maurice-Dorion.
The “Fête de la Saint-Jean-Baptiste St-Rodrigue” receives $4,000: on June 23, from 5 p.m. to 9:15 p.m., at parc Henri-Casault, with fireworks.
The “Fête nationale au Moulin des Jésuites” receives $5,000: on June 24, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., at the Jardins Marie-Charlotte-Bédard, rain or shine.
Except for the Moulin des Jésuites, the other three events are postponed to the next day in case of bad weather.
The City will also provide technical support; the police and fire departments are in favour of holding the events.
The City is authorizing the setup of a café-terrace at 541-547, rue Saint-Jean, in the Saint-Jean-Baptiste neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
The terrace may be located in the building's inner courtyard, whereas the planning by-law normally requires it to be in the front yard.
The terrace will serve the restaurant Baloney Sandwicherie, located in that inner courtyard.
The exemption applies only to the current business.
The comité consultatif d'urbanisme is also requesting a document proving the agreement of the building's owner and tenants before the authorization certificate is issued.
According to the analysis on file, no sound system is planned and the kitchen will close around 8 p.m.
The Ville de Québec is granting $400,000 to the organization Les Créations Pyro to hold the Grands Feux Loto-Québec in 2026.
It is also providing municipal services free of charge (public works, police, fire) up to a maximum of $140,000, bringing the total support to $540,000.
The event features eight pyromusical evenings from August 4 to 22, 2026, with the fireworks at 10 p.m. lasting about twenty minutes.
Activities start at 6 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and at 12 p.m. on Saturdays, on the docks of the Port de Québec and at the quai Paquet in Lévis.
All programming is free for the public.
The event's planned budget is $3,704,262; the City's grant covers 10.8% of it.
The grant is paid in two instalments: $360,000 in 2026 and $40,000 in 2027, and it is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners.
The Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough is giving out $12,000 in grants to three organizations for four neighbourhood festivals in the summer of 2026.
Breakdown: $1,500 to La Corporation des loisirs de St-Louis-de-France, $4,500 to Loisirs Ressources de Québec, and $6,000 to Loisirs St-Benoît inc. ($3,500 + $2,500).
Fête nationale at parc Saint-Louis-de-France on June 24, from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m., rain or shine.
Fête nationale at parc Sainte-Geneviève on June 24, from 12 p.m. to 11 p.m., moved indoors if it rains: games, bingo, a singer and fireworks.
Two events at parc Saint-Benoît: Fête nationale on June 24 (12 p.m. to 10 p.m.) and Canada Day on July 1 (5 p.m. to 10 p.m.), cancelled in case of bad weather.
The City is also providing technical support depending on available resources; the police and fire departments are in favour of holding the events.
In 2025, the same types of events received $13,400 split among four organizations.
The City is changing the parking rules on rue De Saurel and rue Rochambeau, around the école primaire d'éducation internationale Filteau, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
Stated goal: improve traffic flow and user safety, especially when classes start and end.
New drop-off zones for school transportation are being set up on both streets, in order to reduce pressure on rue De Saurel and on the parking lot of the neighbouring church.

On rue De Saurel (west side, between chemin Sainte-Foy and rue Rochambeau): parking limited to 10 minutes from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday during the school period, on certain sections, and stopping prohibited on others.

On rue Rochambeau (north side, west of rue Maur): several sections change to a maximum of 10 minutes of parking, Monday to Friday during the school period, with sections where stopping is prohibited except for buses.
On rue Rochambeau (south side, from rue Maur to the west end): parking prohibited from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, during the school period.
The borough council enacts ordinances O-778 and O-779 to put these changes into effect.
The City is giving $100,000 to Juste pour divertir diffusion to hold the SuperFrancoFête from August 17 to 25, 2026, at the Agora de Québec.
It is also adding free municipal services (staff time and equipment loans from public works and the police) worth up to $4,000, for total support of $104,000.
The money supports the August 17, 2026 show, for which tickets will be free for everyone.
The program includes 5 outdoor music shows, with activities required to end no later than 11 p.m.
The grant is paid in two instalments of $50,000, in 2026 and in 2027, with the 2027 instalment remaining subject to the adoption of the budget.
The support depends on sufficient contributions from the other partners and will not be renewed for the 2027 edition.
The event's planned budget is $16,392,060; the City's grant represents 0.6% of it.
The City is giving $7,300 to three Charlesbourg organizations for 2026 winter festivals.

Loisirs du Trait-Carré receives $3,000 for the "Plaisirs d'hiver du Trait-Carré" at parc Guillaume-Mathieu: a family day on January 31 (10 a.m. to 4 p.m.) and a skating disco on February 7 (6 p.m. to 9 p.m.).
Loisirs de St-Rodrigue inc. receives $2,800 for the "Carnaval polaire" on February 7, from 1 p.m. to 4:30 p.m., at parc Maurice-Lortie.
Les Loisirs Bourassa inc. receives $1,500 for the "Fête hivernale" on February 21, from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m., at parc de la Terrasse-du-Bon-Air.
In case of bad weather, the January 31 activity is postponed to February 7 and the Carnaval polaire to the next day; the Loisirs Bourassa festival takes place rain or shine.
The City is also providing technical support for the events, depending on available resources.
Last year, the same three events received $6,250 in total.
The City is giving $90,000 to the Fédération canadienne de snowboard to hold the "Le Grind – Ville de Québec" event on April 3 and 4, 2026.
It is also providing free municipal services (public works and police) worth up to $2,000.
The event, a snowboard competition (Rail Jam), takes place at the Agora du Port de Québec and is free for everyone.
Qualifying rounds on Friday, April 3, from 12 p.m. to 3 p.m., open to local snowboarders; final on Saturday, April 4, in the evening between 4 p.m. and 9 p.m.
The grant covers 19.1% of the event budget, estimated at $472,000, and depends on enough funding coming from the other partners.
The money is paid in instalments ($54,000, then $27,000) based on conditions the organization must meet.
The Fédération must give the City a full report within 90 days after the event.
The City is adding a $11,000 fee for applications to authorize real estate projects that do not comply with the rules, under sections 145.45 to 145.49 of the Loi sur l'aménagement et l'urbanisme.

Social or affordable housing projects recognized by the Société d'habitation du Québec, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation or Maisons Canada, or designated by the executive committee, do not pay this fee.
It is also creating a fee for the removal and treatment of garbage produced on construction sites, calculated using the same rules as for the City's containers.
It is revising the schedule of parking fees: for example, up to $15 for an evening or weekend period, and up to $21.50 for a day from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. in certain parking lots.
Replacing a parking permit sticker is free the first time, then costs $10 each time after that.
A long-term parking subscription can only be refunded between October 15 and 25 of the year of purchase, minus 15% in administrative fees.
Before it was adopted, the by-law was corrected to replace a reference to a repealed law, without changing the scope of the rules.
The City is changing the parking rules on rue Boisseau, in front of école primaire Marguerite-Bourgeoys, in Saint-Roch/Saint-Sauveur.
The 10-minute limit applied at all times, all year round; it will now apply only from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, during the school year.
The affected zone is 18 metres long, on the north side, starting 56 metres west of rue Victoria.
Three parking spaces become available for long-term parking outside these hours and outside the school year.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council is enacting ordinance O-1562 to put this change into effect.
The City is giving $15,000 in grants to three organizations in the arrondissement de Beauport for music events in the summer of 2026 — $5,000 each.

The École de musique des Cascades de Beauport is organizing "Les balcons s'animent dans Montmorency": concerts every Tuesday in July, from 7 p.m. to 8:30 p.m., on avenue Ruel between 113e and 103e Rue.
The Groupe vocal Atmosphère is presenting the 24th "Fin de semaine chantante" from June 18 to 21, at the Centre de loisirs Monseigneur-De Laval, with choir performances.
L'Harmonie des Cascades de Beauport is holding "Québec en harmonies" on June 19, 20 and 21, exceptionally at parc Roland-Beaudin; the event is free.
All three events take place rain or shine.
The money comes from the operating budget of the arrondissement de Beauport, under the activity supporting cultural and heritage activities.
The borough council adopted the decision on April 14, 2026 (resolution CA5-2026-0032).
The City is changing the parking rules on the north side of rue du Général-Tremblay, between avenue Sasseville and rue Richard-Turner, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
For the first 49 metres from avenue Sasseville, parking is limited to 60 minutes from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., Monday to Friday, except for holders of a zone A3-14 permit.
Along 16 metres in front of the semi-buried bins, parking becomes prohibited from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday.
Bus parking remains prohibited at all times along the first 65 metres.
The former ban on parking on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. is removed.
The change results in the partial loss of two parking spaces.
The purpose: to allow the crane truck to pick up the residual materials from 2712, rue du Général-Tremblay from the street, instead of encroaching on the sidewalk and the roadway.
The City is giving $50,000 to Expérience Saint-Laurent to hold "L'Oasis du Port de Québec" in 2026.
It is also providing free municipal services (staff time and loaned equipment) worth up to $1,500.
The event takes place in the bassin Louise, at the Port de Québec, from June 19 to August 30, 2026.
Swimming and the activities (music, comedy, workshops) are free; the site is open 7 days a week until 10 p.m., and until 11 p.m. on Fridays.
Swimming is available from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. on weekdays and from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. on weekends.
The event's total budget is $606,000; the City's grant covers 8.3% of it and is conditional on enough funding from the other partners.
The City is paying $45,000 in 2026 and $5,000 in 2027, subject to the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The City is tightening its rules for reimbursing its employees' travel and hospitality expenses; the executive committee adopted the amended policy on January 28, 2026.
Accommodation is reimbursed only if the trip is more than 225 km from the home base and if the activity starts before 9 a.m. the next day or ends after 7 p.m.
Accommodation limits per day: $275 in Canada, $365 elsewhere in the Americas, $410 in the rest of the world. Extras billed on the hotel bill (meals, refreshments, services) are no longer paid.
No alcohol is reimbursed in travel expenses; the conditions for reimbursing alcohol as a hospitality expense are tightened.

Breakfast is paid only if departure is before 6:30 a.m., supper only if the return is after 6:30 p.m.; no meals for a half-day within the City's territory, nor for work sessions, meals between employees, arrivals, departures or celebrations.
New out-of-Québec stay allowance: $20 per day in Canada, $26 elsewhere in the Americas, $30 in the rest of the world, only one per 24 hours.
Hospitality expenses are allowed only to generate new economic benefits; the rules are also harmonized for Destination Québec cité employees.
The City is changing the parking rules on the west side of boulevard Montmorency, between chemin de la Canardière and avenue De Vitré, in La Cité-Limoilou (Maizerets-Lairet district).
Goal: allow waste collection trucks to wait near the scale at the Complexe de valorisation énergétique, at 1202, boulevard Montmorency.
Two new zones ban parking from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday, near 1202, boulevard Montmorency.
A new no-parking-at-any-time zone is added near the intersection with chemin de la Canardière.
The no-parking zones from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. are removed, as is the 90-minute limited parking zone (9 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
Nine parking spaces are affected by these changes, in an industrial area.
The City is changing the parking rules on chemin de la Canardière, on the west side, between 3e Avenue and 4e Avenue, in Limoilou.
One space goes from a 60-minute limit to a 30-minute limit, from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., every day.
