The remaining 60-minute spaces apply Monday to Friday, from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., except for vehicles with a zone 21 parking permit.
No on-street parking spaces are being removed.
The change responds to a request from local businesses in the area and from the owner of 399, chemin de la Canardière, for customers and deliveries.
The City is creating a 10-minute limited parking zone on avenue Louis-Fréchette, east side, near Collège Saint-Charles-Garnier (Montcalm-Saint-Sacrement).
The limit applies from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday, during the school period only.
The zone starts 7 metres from rue De Callières and extends 30 metres to the north.
The goal: set aside space for parents to drop off students and improve safety in the school zone.
Five parking spaces are removed during the school period; parking on both sides remains possible outside those hours.
The request comes from the fact that the expansion of the college reduced the space available at the school's turnaround loop.
The City is banning parking at all times on the north side of 66e Rue Ouest, in Charlesbourg (Saint-Rodrigue district).
The ban applies between 1re Avenue and avenue Pierre-Chamarre, over 158 metres to the west.
Before, you could park there outside the hours of 7 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday to Friday.
Four parking spaces are being removed.
The City explains that parked cars were getting in the way of traffic, road maintenance and safety, on a stretch less than six metres wide.

The City is changing the parking rules on rue René-Chaloult and rue Adélard-Godbout, near école primaire de la Chaumière (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles, district de Loretteville-Les Châtels).
On several sections of the two streets, parking becomes prohibited from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, during the school year.

Other sections become no-parking zones at all times, and certain portions of rue Adélard-Godbout will allow parking for a maximum of 10 minutes from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, during the school year.
The change follows requests from citizens and aims to ensure the safety of schoolchildren and the smooth flow of traffic.
According to the document, these changes will have very little impact on the number of parking spaces available on the streets.
The City is banning parking along 14 metres on the west side of boulevard Valcartier, across from 11 001, from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday.
The purpose: to allow waste collection, which is blocked by cars parked in front of the two semi-buried bins of the new building.
The two parking spaces limited to 90 minutes (8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday) are being moved into the space of the former vehicle entrance, which is now closed.
The change means the partial removal of two parking spaces.
The area affected is the section between rue Racine and rue du Frère-Élisée, in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles (Loretteville–Les Châtels district).

The City is extending the no-parking-at-any-time zone on the west side of rue Sherbrooke, between rue des Franciscains and chemin Sainte-Foy (Cap-aux-Diamants neighbourhood, La Cité-Limoilou borough).
One parking space is being removed. The stretch where parking was prohibited only from 7:30 a.m. to 9 a.m. becomes prohibited at any time.
The zone reserved for zone 3 permit holders (90 minutes maximum, from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m., Monday to Friday) goes from 26 to 17 metres.
Reason given: a car parked south of the driveway entrance at 770, rue Sherbrooke prevented drivers from using the right-turn lane toward chemin Sainte-Foy.
According to the document, this blockage also prevented residents of 770, rue Sherbrooke from entering and leaving their private accesses.
The Service du transport et de la mobilité intelligente states that the parking occupancy rate on this street is moderate.
The decision falls to the borough council, through order O-1513.
The City is giving $7,400 to Société du Domaine Maizerets inc. to organize two series of events in the summer of 2026.
The "Matinées musicales" ($1,400) take place on Sundays, July 19, August 2, 16 and 30, from 11 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., at parc du Domaine de Maizerets.
The "Jeudis cover" ($6,000) offer 5 concerts on Thursdays, July 9 and 23, August 6 and 20, and September 3, from 7 p.m. to 8:30 p.m., at the same park.
Both events are held rain or shine; a coffee stand, a street food truck and a microbrewery stand are planned on site.
The grant is lower than the $8,925 given in 2024, because the entertainment surrounding the shows has been removed.
The City is also providing technical support based on available resources; the police and fire services are in favour.
The City is moving two loading zones on rue Saint-Vallier Ouest, between rue Bagot and rue Père-Grenier, in Saint-Sauveur.
In front of 129 and 139, as well as in front of 217, the loading zone (8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday) becomes parking limited to 90 minutes, from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., Monday to Friday.
In front of 165 and 227, the 90-minute parking (9 a.m. to 9 p.m., Monday to Friday) becomes a loading zone from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday.
The change comes from a request by the Société de développement commercial de Saint-Sauveur, for business owners who want to set up sidewalk cafés in the summer.
No on-street parking space is being removed.
The La Cité-Limoilou borough council is enacting ordinance O-1498 to apply these rules.
Rue des Embarcations, in Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur, officially becomes a shared street following the work carried out in 2025.
The speed limit goes from 30 km/h down to 20 km/h on the street, starting at rue du Chalutier.
About 31 parking spaces are being removed in the turnaround circle, where right-angle parking is no longer possible.
New no-parking zones are being created so that vehicles can pass each other in the narrowed lane.
A 20 m section remains reserved for vehicles with a sticker or permit, and a 13 m section is limited to 60 minutes, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday.
A mandatory stop is being added on the west approach of the new intersection created on the street.
The City is banning parking at all times on an 8-metre section of the east side of rue Sagard, in the Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur neighbourhood.
This section is located in front of the entrance to the underground parking and in front of the lowered curb leading to the garbage container room.
The change removes about one parking space.
The 60-minute limited parking zone (9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, except zone 12 permits) is reduced accordingly.

The request came from the department in charge of residual materials: parked vehicles were blocking the handling of the containers at the new Office municipal d'habitation de Québec building, Le Zénith.
The City is giving $28,900 in grants to three organizations in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough for summer 2026 events.

$1,300 goes to Organisme paroissiale de loisirs St-Jean-Baptiste-De-La Salle inc. for the Fête de quartier SJBDLS, on June 6, 2026 at parc Saint-Jean-Baptiste-De La Salle (inflatable games, entertainment, street food, picnic).
$16,100 goes to Société arts & culture de Cap-Rouge for the Festival Découvr'Arts, on June 6 and 7, 2026 at parc Provancher, parc nautique de Cap-Rouge, parc de la Forge and under the Tracel.
$11,500 goes to Club FADOQ Cap-Rouge inc. for the Journée Plein Air des Aînés, on June 10, 2026 from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. at the Base de plein air de Sainte-Foy (34th edition).
The increase in the grant for the Journée Plein Air des Aînés is because the organization is taking on items usually managed and paid for by the City.
The City will also provide technical support for the three events, within the limits of its resources; the police and fire services are in favour.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget (activity "Réaliser et soutenir les événements").
The City is changing parking around the elementary school école primaire de l'Orée-des-Bois, in the Val-Bélair area (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
Parking is being removed from the north side of rue Collin and concentrated on the south side, where a sidewalk has just been built.
New 10-minute parking spaces are being created on rue Collin, rue du Cristal and rue Castel, from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday during the school year.
The stated goal: to fix the shortage of spaces for the school drop-off area on rue des Camarades and to make student travel safer.
In all, 20 parking spaces are being removed and 24 new spaces reserved for the drop-off area and school transportation are being created.
On rue Collin, a parking ban from November 15 to March 31 applies to certain sections.
The City is officially banning right turns on a red light on route de l'Aéroport, at the intersection with avenue Notre-Dame, in Cap-Rouge–Laurentien.
On the south side, the ban applies at all times, because of the layout of the intersection and very limited visibility.
On the north side, it applies from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, because a school crossing guard helps children cross there.
The intersection is part of the school corridor for école primaire Trois-Saisons.
The signs had already been in place for several years, but had never been approved by the executive committee: the decision makes the situation official.
The ban applies to drivers as well as cyclists.
The City is banning parking on rue de Dakar, between boulevard Johnny-Parent and rue de Kyoto, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
East side: parking banned from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday, over 28 metres on the outside of the curve.
West side: parking banned at all times over 31 metres on the inside of the curve.
About six parking spaces will be removed.
The change is meant to let waste collection trucks get through for the new building at 9960, rue de Dakar, whose bins are located in the curve.
The Arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge is moving the borough council meeting scheduled for November 9, 2026.
The meeting will instead be held on November 16, 2026, at 5:30 p.m.
The rest of the 2026 schedule of regular meetings, adopted on November 24, 2025, stays the same.
No financial impact is indicated.
On March 25, 2026, residents of the Vieux-Moulin neighbourhood, in Beauport, filed a petition to create a neighbourhood council (conseil de quartier).
The city clerk's office checked the petition: it has more than 300 signatories with the required standing, and it meets the rules.
The executive committee is calling a public meeting on June 8, 2026, at 7 p.m., in room 105 ABC of the Centre sportif Marc-Simoneau, 3500, rue Cambronne.
At this meeting, the City will explain the mission and the workings of a neighbourhood council, answer questions, and then hold a vote.

People who may vote are those of full age living in the neighbourhood who have been domiciled in Québec for at least 12 months as of the date the petition was filed, as well as representatives of commercial, industrial, institutional or community establishments in the neighbourhood.
If the vote is favourable, city council may authorize the creation of the neighbourhood council and give it a name, before an organizational meeting is held.
The neighbourhood concerned straddles the electoral districts of Robert-Giffard and La Chute-Montmorency-Seigneurial.
The City is creating parking zones with a 10-minute maximum near the Sainte-Odile and des Quatre-Saisons elementary schools, in Limoilou.
These zones apply from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, during the school year.
Three streets are affected: avenue Valmont-Martin (east side), rue des Chênes Ouest (north side) and rue du Curé-Couture (west side).
On rue du Curé-Couture, the no-parking rule from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. is removed and replaced by the 10-minute limit.
About thirteen parking spaces disappear from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, during the school year.
The goal: provide drop-off spots for parents accompanying their children and improve safety in the school zone.
The bus-only stopping zones on rue du Curé-Couture and rue des Chênes Ouest are maintained.
The City is creating a 20-minute maximum parking space in front of the garderie Les Génies, at 2502, avenue Montbray, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
This 13-metre space will be limited to 20 minutes from Monday to Friday, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., so parents can drop off and pick up their children.

Elsewhere on the stretch between rue des Vignes and boulevard du Versant-Nord, the current rules stay the same: no parking on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and a 120-minute maximum on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
The change responds to a request from the owner of the daycare, which takes in 60 children aged 0 to 5.
According to the document, no parking spaces are lost on the street.
The arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge is changing the parking rules on avenue Montpetit and rue de Dijon, in the district de la Pointe-de-Sainte-Foy.
The goal: to clear the line of sight between pedestrians and drivers near intersections, along the school corridor of école primaire Coeurs-Vaillants.
The changes affect avenue Montpetit at the approaches to rue de Dijon, rue Boisverdure, avenue de Liège and avenue Louis-Jobin.
About 15 parking spaces will be removed; the City says it has observed generally low parking use on this stretch.
On part of avenue Montpetit, parking becomes prohibited from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday during the school year, and some zones change to a maximum of 10 minutes.
On rue de Dijon, new sections become no-parking at all times, in addition to the restrictions already in place from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. between November 15 and March 31.
The City is moving up the start of the no-stopping rule on avenue Brown, east side: from 8 a.m. to 7:30 a.m., Monday to Friday during the school year.
The ban applies to two sections on the east side, between chemin Sainte-Foy and rue Père-Marquette, near école primaire Anne-Hébert.
School buses are still allowed to stop in these zones; the ban still ends at 4 p.m.
No parking spaces are being removed on the street.
The change targets parents who were parking in the zone reserved for buses, which made it harder for schoolchildren to get off.
The request came from the management of école Anne-Hébert; the La Cité-Limoilou borough council is enacting order O-1571.
The City is paying $30,000 to Productions Logico inc. and providing free municipal services (staff time and equipment loans) up to a maximum of $2,000, for a total of $32,000.
This money supports the "Fête du Canada à Québec" on July 1, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m.
The program is free: official ceremonies in the morning on the terrasse Dufferin, family activities and ongoing shows on the plaines d'Abraham in the afternoon and evening.
The grant goes from $25,000 in 2025 to $30,000 in 2026, in particular to strengthen the intercultural component and improve universal accessibility.
The event has a planned budget of $345,000; the City's support covers 8.7% of it.
The support is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners.
Among other things, the organizer must provide one toilet per 600 people, accessibility measures and a short emergency response plan.
The City is giving $2,000 to four organizations to run free activities during the Easter break, under the theme « À Québec, on bouge! ».
Each organization receives $500: Centre Mgr Marcoux, Groupe Plein Air Faune, Loisirs du Faubourg and Patro Le Pivot.

On Friday, April 3, 2026: pickleball, cardio-weight training, zumba and psychomotor activities for ages 0-5 at the Centre communautaire Monseigneur-Marcoux (9 a.m. to 2:50 p.m.), and an Easter egg hunt at the Base plein air Sainte-Foy (9 a.m. to noon).

On Monday, April 6, 2026: a motor skills course, badminton, pickleball, soccer, basketball, cardio-cycling, yoga, storytelling and an Easter egg hunt at the Centre communautaire Lucien-Borne (9 a.m. to noon).
Also on April 6: soccer, cosom hockey and basketball at the Centre communautaire des Chutes (10 a.m. to 3 p.m.).
The activities are free and open to everyone, in various arrondissements.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
The City is giving $1,500 to the organization « Loisirs Ressources de Québec » to hold the « Fête d'hiver LRQ ».
The event takes place on Saturday, February 14, 2026, from 12 p.m. to 8 p.m., at parc Sainte-Geneviève, in the arrondissement de Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
On the program: snow sculptures, maple taffy, music and dancing, face painting, a circus show; the activities are free.
In case of bad weather, the party will be held indoors.
The grant goes from $1,000 in 2025 to $1,500 this year.
The money comes from the borough's operating budget; the City will also provide technical support depending on available resources.
The borough council adopted the decision on January 26, 2026.
The City is giving $4,000 to the "Loisirs du Trait-Carré" to organize the Fête de quartier du Trait-Carré.
The event takes place on Saturday, August 22, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., at parc Guillaume-Mathieu, in Charlesbourg; it is postponed to the next day in case of bad weather.
On the program: flea market, canteen, DJ, inflatable games, fair games, mini-farm, arcades and roaming entertainment.
The grant goes from $3,000 in 2025 to $4,000 in 2026 because the organization is adding activities for teenagers.
The City also provides technical support for the event, depending on available resources.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The City is banning parking at all times on the west side of rue de l'Aster, between boulevard Lebourgneuf and the north end of the street.
The ban covers 84 metres starting from a point located 184 metres north of boulevard Lebourgneuf.
Two parking spaces are being removed, in an area where the occupancy rate is described as moderate.
The old rule (no parking from midnight to 6 a.m., on Tuesdays and Thursdays, from November 15 to March 31) is replaced by the permanent ban.
The Service des travaux publics had reported repeated water accumulation near 6305, rue de l'Aster, caused by the shape of the roadway and the location of the catch basin.
Vehicles parked near the catch basin interfered with its maintenance, which increased the risk of water accumulation during rainfalls or thaws.
The decision affects the arrondissement des Rivières, district des Saules–Les Méandres.
The City is changing the parking rules around the école primaire des Jeunes-du-Monde, in the Maizerets-Lairet neighbourhood (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).

On rue Georgette-Lavallée, parking becomes prohibited at all times near avenue Champfleury and near avenue Bardy, and new 10-minute parking zones are created from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, during the school period.
The school bus zone on Georgette-Lavallée is shortened, since only one bus goes to the school.
On avenue Champfleury, a parking zone with a 10-minute maximum is being added (7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, during the school period) and parking becomes prohibited at all times near 25e Rue.
U-turns become prohibited on avenue Champfleury, between rue Georgette-Lavallée and 25e Rue.
In total: 2 parking spaces removed at all times on Georgette-Lavallée, plus 14 spaces during the school period, and 8 spaces on Champfleury during the school period.
The City says residents will be able to park on both sides of the roadway outside the school period.
The City is giving $1,300 to the organization "Loisirs et Sports Neufchâtel inc." to organize the "Fête du voisinage LSN".
The event takes place on Saturday, June 6, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., at parc Robert-Légaré, in the arrondissement des Rivières.
On the program: a family bazaar during the day, then children's activities, a picnic, activity presentations and booths from local organizations in the afternoon.
The event takes place rain or shine.
The City is also providing technical support, depending on available resources; the police and fire services are in favour.
This is the organization's first request for financial support for this event.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement des Rivières.
The City is giving $1,300 to Club Rabaska (canot-camping) inc. to organize the "Festival Vagues-en-ville".
The event takes place on Saturday, April 18, 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 7 p.m., at parc Chauveau, in the arrondissement des Rivières.

On the program: a friendly whitewater race on the rivière Saint-Charles, guided descents open to the public, booths on safety and sharing the river, a DJ, and introductory canoeing workshops if the water flow allows.
If the river's high water level is not adequate, the festival is postponed by one week.
A new promoter is taking charge of the 2026 edition of the event.
The City is also providing technical support, depending on available resources; the police and fire services are in favour.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement des Rivières.
The City is redeveloping route de l'Église between chemin Saint-Louis and rue de l'Anse, in Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge (Saint-Louis–Sillery district).
The work adds raised bike paths, bike lanes, curb extensions and new sidewalks, as well as raised intersections at rues Montarville and Valcourt.
Two orders (O-773 and O-774) change the parking rules on route de l'Église and on rue du Sieur-D'Argenteuil.
On the east side of route de l'Église, parking becomes prohibited at all times from chemin Saint-Louis to rue de l'Anse.
On the west side, parking is prohibited on several sections, with stopping zones reserved for buses and spaces limited to 10 minutes from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. on school days.
The drop-off zones for école primaire Saint-Louis-de-France are adjusted on route de l'Église and on rue du Sieur-D'Argenteuil.
The borough council adopted the decision on August 27, 2026 (resolution CA3-2026-0144).
The City is changing the parking and traffic rules on rue Bertrand, near the école primaire de la Farandole, in Beauport (Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux district).
On the east side of the street, stopping vehicles becomes prohibited along an 82-metre section, between 99 and 181 metres from rue Geneviève-Harnois.
On the west side, stopping becomes prohibited along 38 metres, on both sides of the entrances to the off-street drop-off area.
The parking zones for parents go from 20 to 10 minutes, from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday to Friday during the school period, on two sections on the west side.
U-turns become prohibited on rue Bertrand, along 160 metres starting 50 metres from rue Geneviève-Harnois.
These changes remove five on-street parking spaces at all times.
The City is creating a 15-minute limited parking zone on rue Georgette-Lavallée, in La Cité-Limoilou (Maizerets-Lairet district).
This 15-minute limit applies from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, on the south side of the street, starting 155 metres east of avenue Bardy up to avenue Monseigneur-Gosselin.
For the first 155 metres from avenue Bardy, the current rule stays in place: a maximum of 90 minutes from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday, except with a zone 28 permit.
The change follows a request from the company Hébergement les 2 frères inc., at 2445, avenue Monseigneur-Gosselin, which provides housing, support and care to vulnerable people.
No on-street parking spaces are being removed.
The City is changing the parking rules on the east side of rue Sainte-Marie, between rue Saint-Olivier and rue Richelieu, in La Cité-Limoilou.
The 30-minute limited parking zone is being removed: it served a business (a shoe store) that has closed.
Along the whole section, parking becomes prohibited from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m., Monday to Friday, except for vehicles with a zone 1 permit.
The change makes two more spaces available to parking permit holders.
The change comes from requests by residents of rue Sainte-Marie.
The borough council adopted the decision on March 23, 2026 (resolution CA1-2026-0050).
The arrondissement de Beauport is authorizing the Chevaliers de Colomb du Conseil de La Nativité de Notre-Dame de Beauport (no. 10017) to hold a fundraising collection in the street.
The collection will take place on September 12, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., rain or shine.
Two intersections are involved: Seigneuriale and Clemenceau, as well as boulevard Louis-XIV and rue Seigneuriale.
All of the money collected will be given to the organization Laura Lémerveil, which helps, among others, children in Québec living with multiple disabilities.
The Service de police and the Centre de gestion de la mobilité intelligente will monitor the situation during the day of the collection.
The City is giving $12,200 to three organizations in the arrondissement des Rivières for summer 2026 events.
Loisirs Lebourgneuf inc. receives $3,200 for the "Fête champêtre Loisirs Lebourgneuf," on August 14, 2026, from 3 p.m. to 10 p.m. at parc Jean-Marc-Gauthier (indoors if it rains).
Loisirs et Sports Neufchâtel inc. receives $2,900 for the "Festi-Parc," from August 21 to 23, 2026, at parc Robert-Légaré, rain or shine.

La Société culturelle de Vanier receives $6,100 for "Rendez-vous dans l'parking," on August 22, 2026, from 1 p.m. to 10 p.m. at parc Louis-Latulippe and in the parking lot of the Centre d'art La Chapelle (postponed to the next day if it rains).
The Festi-Parc grant goes from $5,600 in 2025 to $2,900, because of lower eligible expenses and the financial results of the previous edition.
The City will also provide technical support for the three events, depending on available resources; the police and fire departments say they are in favour.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement des Rivières.
The City is changing traffic rules to let the RTC launch its transition network starting March 21, during the tramway construction work.

Four new bus-only reserved lanes: autoroute Robert-Bourassa southbound (from Hochelaga to the traffic light at 2450, boulevard Laurier), boulevard Laurier and Grande Allée Ouest westbound (from des Gouverneurs to Belvédère) and eastbound (from des Gouverneurs to De Laune), from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m., Monday to Friday.
A reserved lane is being added on Grande Allée Ouest eastbound, between rue De Laune and avenue de Bougainville, from 6 a.m. to 10 a.m., Monday to Friday.
Two existing reserved lanes (Robert-Bourassa southbound and boulevard Laurier westbound) change from 7 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. to 6 a.m. to 9 p.m., Monday to Friday.

New mandatory lane directions at three intersections: Grande Allée Ouest and avenue Holland (right turn, except for buses), Grande Allée Ouest and avenue Thornhill, and boulevard Laurier and chemin Saint-Louis (left turn).
Left turns become prohibited on the eastbound approach to the intersection of Grande Allée Est and avenue Taché.
The changes affect the arrondissements of La Cité-Limoilou and Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge; streets in the city's arterial road network will be covered by a separate decision.
The City is banning right turns on red at all times on avenue du Cénacle, at the east and west approaches to rue Seigneuriale, in Beauport.
Until now, this ban applied only from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.
Audible signals for people with a visual impairment will be installed at this intersection during 2026, to make the south and east crossings safer.
The new audible signals operate at all times, unlike the old ones, which is why the ban is being extended.
The two existing signs (7 a.m. to 10 p.m.) will be replaced at the traffic lights.
The decision falls to the Beauport borough council (Robert-Giffard district).
The City is banning right turns on red at all times at four intersections, because new audible signals for blind pedestrians will be installed there.
Beauport: rue Seigneuriale at avenue du Cénacle, south approach — the ban from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. becomes permanent.
La Haute-Saint-Charles: boulevard Valcartier at boulevard des Étudiants, north approach — the ban from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. becomes permanent.
La Haute-Saint-Charles: boulevard de la Colline at rue Pacifique, south approach — the ban from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, becomes permanent.
Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge: route Jean-Gauvin at the entrance to the IGA des Sources, north approach — right turns on red, allowed until now, become banned at all times.
The new audible signals work at all times, unlike the old ones they are gradually replacing.
Intersections on the local networks and on the agglomeration network will be handled separately by the borough councils and the urban agglomeration council.
The City is giving $8,700 to two organizations in the La Cité-Limoilou borough for three neighbourhood festivals in the fall of 2026.
Centre Mgr Marcoux inc. receives $3,000 for the "Fête des moissons Mgr Marcoux," on Saturday, September 12, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. at parc Bardy (inside the community centre if it rains).
Centre récréatif St-François D'Assise inc. receives $2,900 for the "Fête de la rentrée CCJGD," on Saturday, September 12, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on rue Royal-Roussillon and avenue La Sarre.
The same organization receives $2,800 for "Lairet en fête," on Saturday, October 3, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. at parc Sainte-Odile. This is a first request for this event.
The two outdoor events would be postponed to the next day in case of bad weather.
On the program: inflatable games, face painting, shows, organization booths, a flea market and food, depending on the event.
The City will also provide technical support, within the limits of its resources; the police and fire departments are in favour.
The City is creating one short-term parking space on avenue Marconi, on the east side, between rue Faraday and rue Lavoisier (Arrondissement des Rivières, district des Saules-Les Méandres).
Parking there will be limited to 10 minutes, from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday.
The zone covers 6 metres, starting 215 metres east of rue Faraday.
The change comes from a request by the business Le Croquignolet, at 415, avenue Marconi, for its customers.
No on-street parking space is being removed.
The City is amending its by-law to allow rooms to be built in a social housing project at 1300, rue de la Pointe-aux-Lièvres, in Vieux-Limoilou.
The project goes from 20 housing units (May 2025 version) to 8 housing units and 32 rooms, with no change to the height or the number of storeys.
The change adds the use "rooming and boarding house" and removes the requirement to set aside at least 50% of the floor area for housing units.
The organization Maison Marie-Frédéric will house young adults aged 16 and over who are experiencing difficulties, with psychosocial workers on site 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
A social reintegration program and support for finding and keeping housing will be offered.
The final construction project will still have to be approved by the Commission d'urbanisme et de conservation de Québec.
The by-law contains no provision that can be subject to a referendum and changes nothing for the other lots in the zone.

The City is now banning right turns on red at all times at the intersection of boulevard Henri-Bourassa and 83e Rue Est (north approach), in Charlesbourg, where new traffic lights were installed last fall.
There is also a new all-times ban at the south approach of boulevard de l'Ormière and avenue Chauveau, to reduce congestion on avenue Chauveau heading east.
There is a new ban from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. at the north approach of boulevard de l'Atrium and 57e Rue Ouest, where an audible signal for people with a visual impairment is in place.
Five intersections are going from a ban from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. to an all-times ban, because their audible signals will be replaced by devices that work 24 hours a day.

The intersections affected by this change: 1re Avenue and 41e Rue Est/Ouest, boulevard Masson and rue Michelet, boulevard Laurier and avenue de Germain-des-Prés, chemin Sainte-Foy and avenue du Séminaire, rue de Nemours and avenue De Gaulle.
The traffic light at Henri-Bourassa and 83e Rue Est comes from the action plan of the Stratégie de sécurité routière 2020-2024, which identified 140 accident-prone locations.
The City is giving $130,000 to the Salon international du livre de Québec for its 2026 edition.
Of that amount, $115,000 goes toward holding the event and $15,000 funds the bursary for the Prix de création littéraire de la Ville de Québec et du SILQ.
The City is also providing free municipal services (public works and police) worth up to $2,000.
The Salon will be held from April 8 to 12, 2026, at the Centre des congrès de Québec, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. on April 8, 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. from April 9 to 11, and 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on April 12.
The grant for the event is going from $110,000 in 2025 to $115,000 in 2026, because of the return of the Auteur.e Studio component, which was suspended in 2025.
The funding depends on the other partners contributing enough; the event's planned budget is $1,550,925.
In 2025, the Salon welcomed more than 77,000 visitors over 5 days, including 18,104 schoolchildren.
The City is awarding the IT maintenance of public safety vehicles to the company Gestion d'Objets Distants CMO, of Terrebonne.
The contract is worth $466,536 before taxes and covers 24 months starting from its award.
The service includes emergency support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, for vehicles equipped with IT infrastructure.
The contract can be renewed twice for 12 months, with an annual price increase tied to the consumer price index.
Two companies submitted bids; the one selected offered the lowest price, compared with $697,680 for the other.
The net cost to the City is estimated at $489,804.48, subject to the adoption of the 2027 and 2028 budgets.
The City is changing the parking rules on rue Caron, between rue Sainte-Hélène and avenue Simon-Napoléon-Parent, in Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur.
These changes follow the addition of bike lanes and the rebuilding of this section of rue Caron.
The traffic lane was narrowed, sidewalks were widened and green spaces were added.
New parking bans apply on both sides of the street (east and west).
About 44 parking spaces are being removed compared with the situation before the work.
Some sections keep 60-minute parking, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday.
Order O-1518 was adopted by the La Cité-Limoilou borough council.
The City is giving $190,000 to the Festival international Juste pour rire Québec and is providing it with free municipal services worth a maximum of $5,000, for total support of $195,000.
The Festival Juste pour rire Québec will be held from July 22 to August 9, 2026, with ticketed indoor shows at several locations in the city.
Free outdoor shows will take place at place George-V from 7 p.m. to 11 p.m. on July 30 and 31, then on August 1, 6, 7 and 8, 2026.
The free services take the form of work time and equipment loans from building management, public works and the Service de police.
The grant represents 1% of the event's projected budget, estimated at $19,783,500.
The money will be paid in two stages: $171,000 in 2026 and $19,000 in 2027, this last amount depending on the adoption of the 2027 budget.
The support is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners; the organization must submit a complete report within 90 days after the event.
The City is giving out $28,200 in grants to three organizations in the arrondissement des Rivières for neighbourhood events in the summer of 2026.
Loisirs et Sports Neufchâtel inc. receives $5,000 for the "Fête nationale LSN", on June 24, 2026 from 12 p.m. to 11 p.m. at parc Robert-Légaré (rain or shine).
Loisirs Vanier receives $20,300 for "Vanier en fête s'éclate", on June 26 and 27, 2026 at parc Jean-Paul-Nolin and in the parking lot (rain or shine).
L'Évasion St-Pie X receives $2,900 for "Évasion en fête", on July 10, 2026 from 2 p.m. to 8 p.m. in the parking lot of the Centre communautaire Michel-Labadie; cancelled in case of bad weather.
On the program: shows, fireworks, inflatable games, a petting farm, a flea market, street food trucks and activities for all ages.
The City will also provide technical support for these events, depending on available resources; the police and fire departments are in favour.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement des Rivières.
The Ville de Québec is giving $275,000 to Télé-Québec to hold the "Grand spectacle de la Fête nationale dans la Capitale" in 2026.
It is also providing free municipal services (public works, police, fire) valued at a maximum of $60,000, for total support of $335,000.
The show takes place on June 23, 2026, from 7 p.m. to 11 p.m., on the plaines d'Abraham, and admission is free.
The show is broadcast live on Télé-Québec and later on TV5 Monde.
The event's total budget is estimated at $3,400,659; the City's grant covers 8.1% of it.
The funding is conditional on sufficient contributions from the other partners; it is paid in two instalments: $247,500 in 2026 and $27,500 in 2027.
Télé-Québec must provide the City with a complete report within 90 days after the event.
The arrondissement de Beauport is giving $9,200 to two organizations for events planned for the summer of 2026.
École de musique des Cascades de Beauport inc. is receiving $5,000 for "Les balcons s'animent dans Montmorency".
Groupe d'éducation et d'écosurveillance de l'eau (G3E) is receiving $4,200 for the "Festival de la rivière Beauport".
The Festival de la rivière Beauport takes place on Saturday, June 6, 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., at parc de la rivière Beauport, rain or shine.
"Les balcons s'animent dans Montmorency" takes place on the four Tuesdays in July, from 7 p.m. to 8:30 p.m., on avenue Ruel between 113e Rue and 105e Rue.
The City closes the street on each day of the "balcons" activity and provides technical support for both events.
The City is removing the reserved taxi stand in effect from 10 p.m. to 4 a.m. on rue Saint-Jean, south side, between côte Sainte-Geneviève and rue Saint-Augustin, in front of parc Saint-Matthew.
Five on-street parking spaces become available again to everyone, including customers of businesses in the area.
The Société de développement commercial du quartier Saint-Jean-Baptiste had asked for this removal, since the taxi zone was little used or not used at all.
The change affects the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou and is made through ordinance O-385, enacted by the executive committee.
The document does not mention any financial impact.
The City is paying $131,100 in grants to two organizations in the arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles for summer 2026 events.
Loisirs-Action Val-Bélair is receiving $58,000 for "Bel air de fête 2026," on Saturday, June 20, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 11 p.m. at parc de La Chanterelle.
Loisirs des Hauts-Sentiers L.D.H.S. is receiving $73,100 for the "Fêtes de la famille de Saint-Émile," from July 23 to 26, 2026, at parc Réal-Cloutier.
Both events will be cancelled in case of bad weather; food and alcohol will be sold there.
The program includes inflatable games, family activities, fireworks at Val-Bélair, and shows (Marie-Mai, Jérôme 50, Sara Dufour, LBA Band, DJ Champion) at Saint-Émile.
The City is also providing technical support, depending on available resources; the police and the Service de protection contre l'incendie are in favour.
The money comes from the arrondissement's operating budget; the Saint-Émile grant was adjusted for the event's growth and for the withdrawal of certain municipal services.
The City is giving $2,600 to the organization "Initiative 1, 2, 3 Go! Limoilou" to organize the "Fête Les Petits Trésors".
The event takes place on Saturday, May 16, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., at parc de l'Anse-à-Cartier, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The event is for children aged 0 to 5 and their families, and features community organizations that work with this group.
The event will be held rain or shine.
The City is also providing technical support, depending on available resources; the police and fire protection services are in favour of holding the event.
In 2025, the same event received $3,800.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The City is changing parking on rue des Alleghanys, on the west side, between avenue des Cordillères and rue Ardouin, in the arrondissement de Beauport.
It is expanding the loading zone to 40 metres, reserved for deliveries from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday.
It is removing the 60-minute limited parking zone (8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday) in front of the commercial building at 434, rue Alleghanys.
The request came from the building's owner and from the merchants, who say that vehicles parked out front interfere with their operations.
According to the document, no on-street parking space is removed by this change.
The borough council is enacting ordinance O-518 to apply these rules.
The City is authorizing Opération Enfant Soleil to hold a street fundraiser on Saturday, May 30, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.
The fundraiser will take place at the approved intersections listed in the appendix, in six boroughs (Cité-Limoilou, Les Rivières, Sainte-Foy, Charlesbourg, Beauport and La Haute-Saint-Charles).
The City agrees to spend up to $5,000 on municipal services to oversee the activity, using existing operating budgets.
All the money collected goes to Opération Enfant Soleil, which funds pediatric care in Québec hospitals.
Municipal services approved the intersections, issued recommendations and will be on site to monitor how the activity unfolds.
The appendix sets a minimum number of supervisors and volunteers per approach at each intersection.
The arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou is changing the parking rules around the new residential building La Cour (159 units), at 155, rue du Prince-Édouard, in Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur.
In front of the building's main entrance, a 10-metre zone becomes a 10-minute maximum stopping area, for paratransit, deliveries and other similar uses.

On rue Saint-Anselme, between rue du Prince-Édouard and rue des Commissaires Est (east side), parking goes from 60 minutes between 9 a.m. and 9 p.m. to 60 minutes between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, except for holders of a zone 14 permit.
On rue du Prince-Édouard, between Saint-Anselme and Caron, a section where parking was banned becomes usable, with limits of 60 minutes between 9 a.m. and 9 p.m., Monday to Friday.
According to the document, no on-street parking space is lost; the changes aim to favour residents who hold a permit while keeping access for visitors and services.
The City is creating two new bus-only lanes in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
On boulevard Hochelaga, in both directions, between route de l'Église and autoroute Robert-Bourassa.
On chemin Saint-Louis, northbound, between avenue James-LeMoine and boulevard Laurier.
These lanes are reserved for city buses from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m., Monday to Friday.
The change serves the RTC's transition network, which starts on March 21, during the tramway construction work.
Changes affecting the agglomeration's arterial road network will be the subject of a separate decision.
Rue du Parc-Roy becomes one-way northbound, between boulevard François-Xavier and boulevard des Français.
The City is adding a sidewalk on the west side of rue du Parc-Roy and another on the south side of boulevard des Français, near école primaire du Parc, in Beauport.
Parking is banned at all times on the east side of rue du Parc-Roy, which removes eight spaces.

On the west side, parking is limited to 10 minutes between 7 a.m. and 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, during the school year, with a drop-off area for schoolchildren: seven fewer spaces during the school year.
The stop sign on rue du Parc-Roy, at the north approach to boulevard François-Xavier, is removed.
U-turns are banned on boulevard des Français, from boulevard du Coteau up to 150 metres to the east.
The City is changing the parking rules on 2e Avenue, between 13e Rue and boulevard Benoît-XV, in Limoilou.

The change responds to a request from the Centre de services scolaire de la Capitale for the école primaire de la Grande-Hermine, which will receive two more school buses for the start of the 2026-2027 school year.
The zone where stopping is prohibited from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday during the school year, except for buses, is being lengthened.
New no-parking-at-any-time zones are being added near the intersections.
Parking limited to 60 minutes (9 a.m. to 12 p.m. and 1:30 p.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, except zone 22 permits) is moving from the west side to the east side of the street.
Three parking spaces are being removed on the west side during the school year, and four spaces are being removed at all times on the east side.
The City is changing the parking and traffic rules on avenue Saint-Samuel and avenue Gaspard, around école primaire Marie-Renouard, in Beauport (Robert-Giffard district).
It will build a turnaround at the south end of avenue Saint-Samuel and a sidewalk on the west side, between chemin du Petit-Village and the south end of the street.

On Saint-Samuel: parking banned at all times near chemin du Petit-Village and in the turnaround, and a new 10-minute zone on the west side, from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, during the school period.
These changes remove 8 parking spaces at all times and 10 more during the school period on Saint-Samuel.

On Gaspard: parking banned at all times on the east side near chemin du Petit-Village, and the zone reserved for school buses is made bigger; 2 spaces are lost at all times and 1 during the school period.
U-turns are banned in the school zone on Saint-Samuel and on Gaspard, between the south end of each street and chemin du Petit-Village.
The work is part of the Stratégie de sécurité routière 2025-2029.
The City is giving $33,000 to two organizations to hold intercultural events in the summer of 2026, at ExpoCité.
The organization Croquée is receiving $25,000 for "Tuktuk, marché de nuit," from July 30 to August 1, 2026: street food and Asian cultural discoveries.
Access to the night market site and its cultural programming is free; only the food is paid.
The Centre culturel et sportif is receiving $8,000 for "25 ans Capoeira à Québec," on August 15, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m.: workshops, meet-ups and a festive evening.
The money comes from the Fonds des grands événements et événements spéciaux in the operating budget of the Service des loisirs, des sports et de la vie communautaire.
This is a pilot project aimed at bringing the host society closer to people from immigrant backgrounds or ethnocultural communities.
The City is giving $11,800 to three organizations for summer 2026 events in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
Simplement Tout'Art receives $5,700 for the Festival Simplement Tout'Art, on July 4 and 5, 2026 at the Domaine de Maizerets (music, artisan booths, food service and alcohol sales).

Le Centre Durocher inc. receives $1,100 for the Cinéma en plein air Durocher, on Tuesdays July 7, 14, 21 and 28, 2026 from 8 p.m. to 11 p.m. at the parc Durocher, free and postponed to the next day in case of rain.
Les Loisirs Montcalm inc. receive $5,000 for Montcalm en fête, on Saturday, August 29, 2026 from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at the parc du Musée, free and cancelled in case of bad weather.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The City will also provide technical support for the events, depending on available resources; police and firefighters said they were in favour.
The City is setting aside a parking space for people with reduced mobility in front of 63, rue D'Auteuil, in Vieux-Québec (arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou).
This space replaces a paid parking spot in effect from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.; no parking spaces are removed overall.
The request came from a resident of the building who holds a SAAQ permit and can only walk short distances.
In front of 1055, rue Louis-Alexandre-Taschereau, a paid parking spot (9 a.m. to 9 p.m.) becomes a no-parking zone at all times.
This change concerns a pedestrian crossing where parking had been allowed by mistake, to prevent vehicles from stopping there.
Both changes are made through ordinances O-1533 and O-1536 of the conseil d'arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
The City is banning parking from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Friday, on a 5-metre section of the south side of rue Desroches, in La Cité-Limoilou.
This zone is located in front of the former vehicle entrance east of the building at 1880, rue Desroches, between avenue Champfleury and avenue Bardy.
The change removes one parking space.
The rest of the section keeps the 90-minute limit, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday to Friday, except for vehicles with a zone 28 permit.
The measure responds to a request from the waste management service: parked cars were getting in the way of handling the containers during collections.
The City is removing parking fees in on-street spaces reserved for electric vehicle charging: only the charging rate applies.
Drivers previously had to pay both for parking (from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.) and for charging, which created confusion and discouraged use of the charging stations.

12 spaces are affected, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou: in front of 633 and 823, rue Saint-Joseph Est (2 charging stations each), 600, rue Jacques-Parizeau (4 charging stations) and 650, avenue Wilfrid-Laurier (4 charging stations).
In these spaces, parking becomes prohibited at all times, except for an electric or plug-in hybrid vehicle connected to a charging station.
The change is part of the review of charging station rates in effect since June 1, 2026.
No parking space is removed; the borough council adopts ordinances O-1580, O-1581 and O-1582.

The Ville de Québec is extending its agreements with the MRC de Bellechasse and the MRC de La Nouvelle-Beauce until December 31, 2029, to receive their purple bags of food waste. The agreements were set to end on December 31, 2027.
The two MRCs asked for this postponement because the installation of their robotic sorting equipment is behind schedule.
The purple bags from the two MRCs should start arriving in Québec around the end of 2027 or the beginning of 2028, rather than in 2026.
The MRCs are now aiming for 2029, instead of 2027, to open their own composting site. Its opening will end the agreements.
Deliveries remain limited to two trucks per day, with access to the Complexe de valorisation énergétique from 7 a.m. to 8:30 a.m. and from 4 p.m. to 5 p.m.
The purple bags and the accepted food waste must be the same as those of the Ville de Québec.
The City bills based on the actual tonnage received at the Complexe de valorisation énergétique; the money goes into the general fund.
Residents of the "5-2" neighbourhood, in Beauport, are asking for a neighbourhood council to be created; the request was filed on March 25, 2026 by Amélie Carignan.
The city clerk's office checked the request: it has more than 300 signatories who meet the required conditions, and it follows the rules.
The executive committee is calling a public meeting on June 3, 2026 at 7 p.m., at the Centre de loisirs de La Ribambelle, 333, rue Perroteau (room RC08).
At this meeting, the City will explain the mission, powers and workings of a neighbourhood council, answer questions, and then hold a vote.

People who may vote are those of full age who have lived in Québec for at least 12 months and who reside in the neighbourhood, as well as representatives of commercial, industrial, institutional or community establishments in the neighbourhood.
If the vote is favourable, the city council may authorize the creation of the neighbourhood council, give it a name and call an organizing meeting to appoint its board of directors.
The "5-2" neighbourhood covers part of the Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux and La Chute-Montmorency-Seigneurial districts.
The City is adding a signed and painted pedestrian crossing on avenue De Vitré, in the arrondissement de La Cité-Limoilou.
Parking becomes prohibited on the east side of avenue De Vitré, over 20 metres starting from rue De Fondville going north and over 20 metres starting from rue De Grandville going north.
Parking is also prohibited on the section located between 87 metres from rue De Fondville and rue De Grandville.
On the remaining segments, parking stays limited to 60 minutes, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday to Friday, except for vehicles with a zone 27 permit.
These changes remove four parking spaces, while the parking occupancy rate on the avenue is high.
The change comes from a request by a citizen; the City says that parked cars were blocking visibility for drivers and pedestrians.

The City is removing from its municipal regulations two bans on right turns on a red light: at the intersection of boulevard Masson / rue Michelet / private access (east approach) and at the intersection of chemin Sainte-Foy / avenue du Séminaire / private access (north and south approaches).
These bans applied from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., for drivers as well as for cyclists.
Nothing changes on the ground: the signs stay the same, because the urban agglomeration council must adopt the same ban on its side at the same time.
The change is meant to have these bans approved by the same body as the one that manages the street the vehicle is turning onto, under a procedure revised in 2025.
The areas affected are the boroughs of Les Rivières and Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge.
The City is giving $3,600 to Loisirs de St-Rodrigue inc. to organize the "Fête de la famille St-Rodrigue".
The event takes place on Saturday, May 23, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., at parc Henri-Casault, in Charlesbourg (postponed to the next day in case of bad weather).
On the program: Katag, inflatable games, Woodooliparc, iSaute, bungee, balloon sculpting, a rally, bike-powered smoothies and face painting, with food service and the presence of local organizations.
The grant goes from $3,000 in 2025 to $3,600 in 2026, which the City links to the increase in the event's budget.
The City will also provide technical support, within the limits of available resources; police and fire services are in favour of holding the event.
The money comes from the operating budget of the Arrondissement de Charlesbourg.
The City is creating a 10-minute maximum parking zone on rue Juchereau-Duchesnay, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
The 10-minute limit applies from 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., on the west side of the street, over 9 metres starting 14 metres south of rue Blanchette.
The zone takes up two parking spaces, in front of the building's main entrance.
The change comes from a request by a resident of 1388, rue Juchereau-Duchesnay, to make it easier to get on and off paratransit vehicles.
No on-street parking spaces are being removed.
The City is signing a 10-year agreement with GAG Développement inc., owner of the Colisée de Loretteville (86, boulevard des Étudiants), from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2036, with no renewal.
The City commits to renting at least 1,640 hours of ice time per year, at $496 an hour in the first year, with an annual increase based on the CPI for the Québec region or 2%, whichever is higher.
The City also pays for access to the washroom facilities in the summer: about 1,836 hours from May 1 to September 30, at $32.50 an hour plus taxes.
The owner must keep the arena's washrooms open to the public from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. from October 1 to April 30, and from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. from May 1 to September 30.
The bleachers, the common area, and the rink's dressing rooms, showers and equipment are included; spectator access to the bleachers is free.
The hours reserved for the City are Monday to Friday from 5 p.m. to 10 p.m., Friday from 10:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m., and weekends from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m., over 32 weeks.
Estimated net cost for the City: $9,166,560 over 10 years, that is $916,656 per year from 2027 to 2035, subject to budget approvals.
The City is giving $8,300 to École de musique des Cascades de Beauport inc. to organize the "Jazz'Art" event.
The event takes place from July 24 to 26, 2026 in the parking lot of the centre sportif Marcel-Bédard, in Beauport: July 24 from 7 p.m. to 9:30 p.m., and July 25 and 26 from 1:30 p.m. to 9:30 p.m.
On the program: six free shows with musical groups from Québec, plus entertainment on July 25 at the Marché public de Beauport, at place du Vieux-Bourg.
In case of bad weather, the event moves indoors to the centre de loisirs Monseigneur-de-Laval.
The usual site, the agora of parc Girardin, is under construction: the grant was temporarily increased to pay for renting a stage at the replacement site.
In 2025, the organization had received $5,000 for the same event.
The City is also providing technical support, depending on available resources; the police and the fire department are in favour of holding the event.
The City is adding a parking space reserved for people with reduced mobility on rue Hermine, in front of number 316, in Saint-Roch–Saint-Sauveur.
The space replaces a spot where parking was limited to 90 minutes, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday to Friday, except for holders of a zone 16 permit.
The reserved space is 8 metres long and is located on the north side, 13 metres west of rue Victoria.
The rest of the stretch between Victoria and Durocher keeps the 90-minute rule, with the exception for zone 16.
Overall, the change does not remove any parking spaces.
The request came from a resident of 316, rue Hermine, who holds a SAAQ parking permit.
The City is tightening the rules on rue des Camarades, near the école primaire à l'Orée-des-Bois, in Val-Bélair (arrondissement de La Haute-Saint-Charles).
Areas where parking was prohibited are becoming no-stopping zones: you can no longer bring a vehicle to a stop there, even for a few seconds.
On the east side, between rue du Cristal and rue Castel: no stopping along the first 23 metres south of du Cristal, then from 59 metres up to rue Castel.
On the west side, between rue Collin and rue de Cabourg: no stopping for 120 metres, starting 52 metres south of rue Collin.
The drop-off zone stays the same: parking limited to 10 minutes, from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday during the school year, along 36 metres on the east side.
The change follows a request from the police service, which found that parents were parking in the prohibited zones to drop off their children.
